“I agree. I’m much more a woman of *action*.” She reaches out like she’s going to place a hand on Zuko’s arm, and Zuko is barely halfway into a pre-emptive flinch when Mai smacks her hand down with a sharp slap.

Zuko freezes, holding his breath as faces start to turn toward them, his shoulders tightening as the crowd realizes that something interesting might be happening. Fuck. Zuko feels the attention like maggot slugs over his exposed skin. He *hates* it, just like he hates the expectation from both of them that they hold some claim to him just by virtue of wanting one.

Can Zuko just blast a hole in the wall and escape? How high were the stilts the house was on, anyway? Is this the beach side or the jagged rocks side?

“Watch yourself,” the girl warns, smacked hand slowly curling into a fist. “We don’t know you here.”

Mai looks thoroughly unimpressed by the attempt at a threat, because that one cuts both ways. “Good.”

The girl’s eyes narrow. “I suggest you back off.” The lanterns lighting their corner of the room suddenly pull toward her, a much more blatant threat, and now the crowd is really watching.

“Don’t,” Zuko warns, straightening at the threat of bending coming into this, and Mai’s eyes flick over quick and surprised, maybe that he's saying anything at all, or maybe at the hoarse, tight anger even he can hear in the word.

The girl glances at him, looking almost taken aback that he would participate in the conversation, the firelight shifting again to her will, and Zuko doesn’t know if that's supposed to be a threat for him too but he doesn’t have the patience left to find out. He holds her eyes and stretches out his fire sense, wrapping it around the flame over top of hers and then *pulling* the fire from her grip.

The flames come easily to his hold and she gasps, stumbling like she’s been hit. She jerks to look back at the lanterns, stiff and clumsy, before whirling back toward him with wide eyes. Her expression twists with surprise and something like fear, and Zuko thinks that it should probably be an ugly thing that his inner flame curls in satisfaction to see it. Clearly, no one has ever played power games with fire with her before. Foolish of her to start one, then.

“Don’t,” Zuko repeats, low, letting a single spark carry with the word.

She stares, eyes darting between him and Mai, mouth working silently as her face goes even paler. Then she gathers herself back into a haughty condescension worthy of any Upper Ring noble and spins on her heel, stalking away with a toss of her hair and a liquid stride that says ‘fuck you’ more loudly than any words ever could right now. Especially considering he apparently hit her breath control so hard she’s speechless.

Zuko watches her go, making sure she isn’t feinting before he lets the lanterns loose with an annoyed flick. He slumps back against the wall, pointedly ignoring the eyes still staring, the whispers as people speculate on what just happened. To anyone watching there would have been barely even a flicker, just fire swaying in a sudden draft. Thank Agni and anything else listening that Azula wasn’t in the room. She wouldn’t be able to resist a display of dominance like that, no matter how much she wants to try her hand at being normal. Whatever she thinks *that* means.

Zuko isn’t exactly unused to people hitting on him—even without Sokka’s love of a cheesy come on, Jet could barely breathe without flirting, and people were friendly at Jin’s dances before they learned to recognize him and that he always said no. But he absolutely loathes feeling cornered like that. It brings back too many shades of things best left in the past and Agni’s balls, Zuko suddenly, desperately wants to get out of here. Dealing with this, thinking about that even in passing, has him edgy and restless and sharply lonely in a way that he doesn’t—can’t—let himself feel.

Fuck, Zuko is abruptly grateful that Gao is back in Caldera. Feeling like this with that blatant, perfectly constructed trap so close...He itches to reach out, to even just for a moment let himself believe that he isn't doing this all alone, which is the kind of stupid, dangerous hoping that leads to mistakes. Agni, even without that temptation Zuko can feel the suddenly thin edge of his control, the way it presses thinner and thinner against the ache of loneliness that's just growing bigger and bigger now that he's acknowledged it. It wouldn't be all that difficult to find someone here to chase away the feeling with. And that Zuko's even aware of that fact, when even the idea of letting any of these people close that way makes his skin crawl, has his inner flame twisting and biting to be cut loose.

He doesn't want any of that and he can't let himself think about what he does want, and when Mai's hand suddenly touches his arm, gentle and familiar, Zuko shrugs her off on instinct, sharp and violent, because he doesn’t want to be looked at or fought over or *touched*. Not by anyone here, at least.

Mai snatches her hand back like it’s been burned, eyes going fractionally wider in shock before narrowing into a glare. “What is *with* you tonight?”

“Nothing,” Zuko snaps, automatically glowering back and trying to wrestle his thoughts back to the places they're supposed to be.

“Agni, you’re so—after all that, you’re going to—ugh.” She blows out a sharp breath, and Zuko distantly observes that he can count on one hand the number of times he’s seen Mai pushed so visibly to the edge of her patience. “Why are you like this, why can’t you for once just be—”

“What?” Zuko challenges when she doesn’t finish. “What, Mai?”

She’s never one to back down from one of those, not when it really matters to her. “*Normal*.”

Zuko can feel the way his scar pulls as his eyes narrow, tugging into the lines of a familiar-again glare. “If you want normal then go back to talking to Ruon-Jian.”

“How about *you* talk to Ruon-Jian,” Mai hisses, and Zuko’s hand slices through the air between them.

“Don’t.” Not here, not now, not when they’re both getting angry about things they can’t change.

Mai is frustrated and prickly like she rarely lets herself be, though, which means she doesn’t know like Zuko does how to pull it back in. “Why are you—all I asked—why can’t you just —”

“I *told* you how this was going to be.”

“Well maybe that isn’t enough for me anymore.”

“Fine.”

“Maybe I want more,” Mai pushes, and Zuko folds his arms over his chest, because what the fuck is he supposed to do about it. "Maybe I want you to do better."

“I guess you’re shit out of luck, then,” he snaps, his frustration bleeding out in jagged bursts. What more does she *want* from him?

“You won’t even *try*.”

“Agni’s burning tits, Mai, you *agreed. Y*ou’re right I won’t even—"

“Hey, everything okay over here?” A forcibly upbeat voice suddenly asks as Ruon-Jian of all fucking people steps over. “Things seem a little tense after Zolai—”

“We’re fine,” Mai says flatly.

Zuko transfers his glare to Ruon-Jian, gratified to see him blanching beneath his tan, which isn’t even the right fucking *shade*. “Fuck off,” he growls, jerking back in surprise when Mai suddenly rounds on him.

“You know what?” She shifts as if she’s putting herself between Ruon-Jian and Zuko. Or maybe beside Ruon-Jian, against Zuko. “If you’re going to be like this, then just go.”

Zuko blinks, suddenly unsure, inner fire turning in on itself. “What?”

“Just leave. Just…You don’t even want to be here, Zuko. So go. Stop *pretending*," she says, with enough bite to the word that Zuko wonders if he's supposed to take it to mean more than just this.

Zuko clenches his jaw, clawing his frustration and what wants to be anger back into something manageable before it truly breaks free. “Fine.” Fucking fine. There’s no point in staying with the larger part of him now primed for a fight. And he’s so far beyond being done with people right now, anyway, and all their fucking emotions that make no sense, and their demands that try to take and take and take, more than Zuko ever wanted to give them.

&#45;-

Azula finds him in their old beach house what can’t be more than thirty degrees later, which is…well, Zuko doesn’t know what he expected. She would know to look for him here, but it’s a bit early for the party to be done.

He’s looking at a painting of what used to be their family when he hears her distinctive step crunching through years of debris and somehow managing to convey distaste with just the cadence of her stride. It's a skill, that. He doesn't turn to look for her, though, studying the frame barely clinging to the wall in what used to be their parents’ sitting room, the gold of it gleaming dully in the moonlight beneath the layers of dust and salt-air grime.

She snorts as she finally comes into the room and sees him. “Could you be any more dramatic, Zuzu?”

“What do you want?” He isn’t in the mood right now to hear about drama from Azula of all people.

“Come to the beach.”

“Why.” He doesn’t feel like being a captive audience for her right now, just—is already feeling too many things.

“Because we’re lighting shit on fire to make ourselves feel better.” She pauses on her way back out of the room. “Bring some good kindling.”

&#45;-

Zuko is surprised that ‘we’ meant more than just him and Azula, but Mai and Ty Lee are there, dragging driftwood to use as seats around the small bonfire Azula already has going. Azula appears as unbothered as she ever is, but Mai is still looking vaguely annoyed—so pissed—and Ty Lee shockingly glum.

“…What happened?” Zuko slows as he approaches, trying to feel out the mood he’s walking into. Not that he’s feeling settled himself enough to turn anyone's mood around—not that he ever is—but if this is going to be worse then he can always retreat back to brooding dramatically in the remains of his former life over where, exactly, everything first went wrong.

“We got kicked out of the party,” Ty Lee mutters, dropping down onto her seat.

“…Why?”

Ty Lee is the one to brave the silence again, sighing when no one else speaks up. “Azula scared the host and then Mai broke a vase over someone’s head.”

Zuko can’t stop his surprised glance toward Mai, who is determinedly looking sullen and bored and like she doesn’t care. At least she didn’t use her knives. “Oh.”

“The fire,” Azula prompts, tone annoyed in a way that means they’re getting close to talking about something that someone could, theoretically, consider a failure of hers if they were brave enough to suggest it.

Zuko doesn’t feel like being brave tonight, and doesn’t feel particularly inclined toward prying, not when that means someone might pry back. He shrugs, throwing himself down onto the sand and tossing the family portrait into the flames.

Azula snorts, taking her seat neatly on a piece of driftwood as the fire begins to warp the brittle canvas. “At least *try* for a little subtlety, Zuzu, even if it’s beyond you.”

Mai lets out an annoyed huff as the paint really catches and begins to send acrid smoke into the air. “You would need to think that throwing away the past matters to care enough to be subtle about it.”

Fuck that. “I know it’s hard for you to believe, Mai, but not everything is about you.”

Her glare is quick and sharp from beneath her bangs. “Yes, Agni forbid that I forget that nothing is about me. We all know what *you* care about these days.”

Zuko’s simmering anger sparks as she jabs at things he refuses to leave undefended. “Mind your own fucking business about things you choose not to understand.”

“*You* shut up about things *you* don’t understand,” Ty Lee says, words clipped.

“Stay out of it, Ty Lee,” Zuko growls, never taking his eyes off Mai.

“Don’t *tell me* what to do,” Ty Lee shoves back, her sudden hot anger drawing Zuko’s attention. “You think you know so much? You think you’re different now? You’re not the only one who’s seen the world, Zuko,” she says, words dripping with mockery. “Don’t act all high and mighty like we don’t all know all about you.”

Zuko narrows his eyes at the idea that she would presume to know anything. “Forgive me if I don’t give much weight to your time as a circus freak,” Zuko bites out, feeling savage and overfull of all the things he can never give voice to that they still insist on prowling along the edges of. “I think I saw a bit of a different world than you.”

Mai sucks in a hard breath, but Azula’s single shout of laughter cuts out ahead of anything Mai might have said. The sound rings through the air for a trembling, shocked moment alongside the echo of Zuko’s words, hanging together until Ty Lee suddenly bursts into abrupt, angry tears.

“Fuck you, Zuko,” she snaps, scrubbing at her face with clenched fists. “Like you would know anything about what it’s like trying to make your own life for yourself.”

Zuko stares, incredulous. *“Excuse me?”*

“Do you have any idea what it was like to grow up and be completely interchangeable with your siblings?” Azula lets out another sound of amusement that has Ty Lee’s cheeks flushing with mottled upset. “My parents don’t even remember my birthday, because to do that they would need to know which one I was! So call me a freak all you want,” she says, glaring at him through wet lashes. “I’m *proud* to be different and stand out. Some of us don’t want to hide in our family’s shadow our whole lives.”

Zuko stiffens, hands curling into fists against the sand. “Don’t talk to me about being on your own, don’t—”

“Right,” Ty Lee cuts in. “All that alone time I forgot about! Boo hoo, you were so alone when you were hiding behind your mom, or your sister, or your uncle, or your—”

“Or your bottomless need for the spotlight?” Mai finishes, voice harsh with annoyance. “Get off your high ostrich horse, Ty Lee. You aren’t any more noble than the rest of us, no matter who your family is.” She meets Ty Lee’s glare with an unimpressed stare. “All you want is attention, attention, attention. It’s embarrassing, the way you act to get it.”

“Well at least I’m willing to admit to wanting something. You act like nothing matters to you and you know what? All it’s done is left your aura dingy and pasty and gray!”

Mai flicks a chunk of hair over her shoulder. “That would be unfortunate, if I actually believed in any of the stupid aura shit you’re always prattling about.”

Zuko scoffs around something too sharp to be amusement. “That might matter more if you actually believed in anything in the first place.”

She sits back, crossing her arms and glaring at all of them. “Sorry if I don't live my life to be as self-righteous and noble and insane as the rest of you. Some of us grew up with expectations.”

Zuko and Azula let out dual barks of laughter, Zuko falling back onto his elbows from the force of the black, dark thing that might be humor, which only pisses Mai off more.

“You had expectations to *shine*, Child of Agni,” she spits. “Mine were to sit down and shut up and disappear.”

“Oh, poor little you,” Azula rolls her eyes. “A big important father who wanted to do big important things and didn’t want his kids to get in the way.”

“Really one of a kind, there,” Zuko says, mocking.

Azula hums her agreement, making a show of examining her nails. “How unique.”

Mai’s jaw is clenched, her words coming gritted past her teeth. “We all know how much *you* care about uniqueness. How many other kids did you drive away again? How long did it take until there wasn’t anyone left in the palace to get in the way? Until it was just me and Ty Lee?”

Azula leans back on braced arms, crossing her legs out in front of her with enough forced casualness to be insulting. “Yes, yes, I never learned to share and now I’m a spoiled princess whose daddy never told me no, is that it? And sad little Mai had to resign herself to being happy with nothing and now you don’t have a healthy relationship with your own emotions.” She rolls her eyes. “Woe.”

“At least I *have* emotions.”

Zuko laughs, incredulous. “Maybe you should learn to express them, then.”

“Oh, that’s *rich*, coming from *you*.”

“Trust me,” Ty Lee says, waving her hands in front of her and scowling at them all, “There’s plenty of emotion right now.” She wrinkles her nose. “All this negative energy is bad for the skin, can we just *stop*?”

“Oh, is it?” Mai scoffs.

“My bad,” Zuko adds, glaring. “I don’t really worry about my skin anymore after my dad taught me a permanent lesson in standing out and shutting up on my *face*.”

“Aw, Zuzu,” Azula says, all gentle, mocking concern. “Are you mad about it? I had no idea!”

“Fuck you, Azula,” Zuko growls, too much already out there for him to be careful with her. “Not all of us get to be the golden child at the Fire Lord’s right hand.”

“Well maybe,” Ty Lee says with false brightness. “If you weren’t so *pissy* and *angry* about *everything*, *all* the time, you’d have a better shot at it.”

“Wow, it’s almost like I might have multiple things to be angry about in my life!”

“Like what, Zuko,” Mai says, crossing her arms. “Please, do tell. Why are you so angry? Enlighten us, since you're clearly *angry* we don't already know.”

Three pairs of eyes suddenly on him, glittering and expectant, and Zuko tenses under the mix of semi-hostile curiosity. “What does it matter? Like you're going to fix me or something?" He’s fully aware that no one ever cares *why*, they just want him to *stop*. "Heal me through the power of *listening?*”

Ty Lee scrunches up her face in annoyance. “You make a big enough deal about it all the time, it’s not like you’re *subtle*. So tell us. You clearly want people to know.”

“I just am.”

“Come on, Zuzu, you can’t hold everyone else to account and refuse to play the game yourself.”

Zuko transfers his scowl to Azula, resisting the urge to straighten from his sprawl back on his elbows, to so visibly reveal how close they are to things that could hurt. “Not everything is a game, Azula.”

She raises an eyebrow. “Isn’t it?”

“Wow,” Mai says, shaking her head, disgusted. “You’re really going to just dodge it like that, huh? You’re going to just avoid it like you avoid everything you find inconvenient. Nice. Real nice.”

“Yeah, I am, Mai,” Zuko lashes back, stung, the words boiling out of his throat because *fuck* *her* for judging what he’s had to do to *survive*, like she’s never fucking stepped foot in Caldera. “Because the world is fucked up and terrible and I’m a fucked up terrible part of it, so forgive me for not wanting to *chat* about all the ways that it sucks when I already have to live with it all in my head.”

Ty Lee sniffs, unmoved. “Like that makes you special. Don’t want to hate yourself? Then stop doing hateful things.”

“Oh, because it’s that simple? Like there’s any difference between right and wrong anymore when defending the nation means—” He swallows the words with a snarl, voice ragged with anger as he continues. “You can justify *anything* with a bit of noble intent, so don’t sit there and act like it’s fucking *easy*.”

“Cry me a river, Zuko,” Azula scoffs. “Get over yourself. Right, wrong, hateful, who cares. Just be a monster and own it. Then it won’t matter what your friends or family or anyone has to say about you.” She settles her necklace to best catch the light. “It will be true, and guess what? It won’t matter because you made it that way.”

“Some of us don’t want to be monsters, Azula.”

Her tawny eyes are suddenly hard on his. “Some of us aren’t willing to make the hard choices, Zuko, and do what needs to be done. Some of us could learn to start tak—”

“If you tell me to take my place in the world,” Zuko warns, “I am going to light this whole fucking beach on fire.”

“Hm. That does sound nice, doesn’t it?”

“It would be more interesting than this,” Mai mutters, kicking at the sand. “And bitching about our *places* in life. Ugh.”

There's a long stretch of silence broken only by the sound of the dying fire and the waves, then Ty Lee shifts, words half-tentative, half-thoughtful. “…Chan was pretty rude earlier, wasn’t he?”

Azula stares before a slow smile curves her lips. “Almost like he doesn’t know his place in the world, don’t you think?”

Mai flicks her shawl straight, sitting upright. “Like maybe someone should show him.”

Zuko finds himself pinned again by three pairs of eyes, curious and semi-hostile and expectant, and after a moment he shrugs. Why the fuck not.

&#45;-

“…Guys,” Ty Lee says from on top of a shattered couch, feet slowly kicking in the air as she surveys the room from her handstand. “Did we just become best friends again?

Azula hums, taking in the torn paper screens and broken furniture and smashed vases. The sound of Chan’s distressed wailing can still be heard if Zuko strains hard. “Property destruction and dishing out some little terror *does* have a way of bringing a group together. Right, Brother?”

Zuko shrugs, balancing on half of a broken table and considering whether it’s worth kicking any more breakable things into the walls. “I don’t know, I only burned down one village, and Uncle was pretty mad at me for it.” He pauses, playing his words back over his memories of the past few months. “And destroyed an abbey, I guess. The island sinking wasn’t really my fault. Though I guess the watchtower was, even though I didn’t mean to. And things kind of got out of hand with these pirates…”

“And you did that all on your own?” Azula shakes her head, tsking. “What you needed was a *team*, Zuko, that was your mistake.”

“Oh, *that* was my mistake?”

“See, this?” Mai says, taking a bite of a fried dough thing and waving a shuriken between them. “This is why you two aren’t allowed to be on the same team anymore.”

“Or—” Zuko hops off the table. “—Is it because you always lost?”

Ty Lee huffs, flipping onto her feet. “Is it winning if the game is destroyed?”

“Well,” Azula says reasonably, “Did the other person *not* win?”

“Let’s hold that thought,” Mai suggests, turning a slow circle in the wreckage. “This was supposed to be a house party, right? Where do you think Chan was hiding the alcohol?”

“I heard he has a room,” Zuko offers dryly, “That is *very* private. Or not.”

“If you like that kind of thing,” Mai simpers, rolling her eyes.

“Race to see who can find it first?” Ty Lee suggests, because she’s a girl who knows how to motivate the two people in the room most likely to find it. Zuko can feel himself falling for it.

“We probably only have five or ten minutes before someone comes back with an adult,” Zuko warns, already taking note of door placement and hallways and considering that against the exterior shape of the house.

“A *‘minute,’* Zuzu? What are you, some Earth Kingdom drudge?”

“I know it’s not firebending,” Zuko says as he sets off for the back of the house, “But even you can do that math.”

“So spicy, Brother.” Azula sounds positively tickled by it. “Let’s see if you still feel that way when I beat you.”

&#45;-

They giggle—because it *is* giggling, even if nothing they do will get him to admit it out loud, no matter how hard they try—around a different fire later, passing around a bottle of stolen… something.

“Payment for our emotional distress,” Mai says archly, surprising a snort of laughter out of Ty Lee.

“Homebrew rotgut,” Zuko says when he tastes it.

“What the *fuck*,” Azula wheezes around her first inadvisably large gulp. “This is *trash*. I thought Chan’s parents were Admirals!”

“This is good stuff at sea,” Zuko shrugs, taking the bottle back and grinning at her noise of outrage when he doesn’t even flinch around another mouthful. It’s like fire over his tongue, down his throat, in his stomach, and Zuko’s spit enough sparks in his life to know how to welcome the feeling.

“…You know a lot about rotgut these days?” Ty Lee asks, and Zuko gives her the bottle and proceeds to scandalize them all with his knowledge of low-quality moonshine across the three remaining nations. He didn’t grow up on a ship and in ports and spend months in the Lower Ring and walk away with nothing. Lieutenant Jee had been quite the connoisseur, when he didn’t realize Zuko was around, of all the ways to make paint stripper palatable.

And then Azula shocks them all with her delightfully low tolerance, barely lasting fifteen *degrees*—because fuck you, Zuko can do the math backwards and forwards—before she’s snoring on the far side of the cheery little fire, cheek pillowed against the sand and face almost soft with sleep. It’s all remarkably peaceful, considering how it started, and Zuko can finally feel himself doing something close to basking for the first time since stepping foot on Ember Island.

“What are you making?” Mai asks, words quiet with curiosity.

“Huh?” Zuko asks intelligently when he realizes she’s talking to him.

“Whatever's always in your pocket that you fiddle with,” Ty Lee murmurs, half-leaning on Mai to keep from falling off her driftwood seat. “What is it?”

“Why do I have to be making something,” Zuko hedges, aware that the hand in his pocket has gone conspicuously still.

“Because you have no capacity for idleness and you don’t know how to relax,” Mai says, which…is fair. “What is it?”

Zuko wavers for a moment longer, but it’s not like there’s anything inherently incriminating about it. And even if there was, they did all just engage in some petty vandalism—petty by their standards, at least. “It’s not really anything,” he says, pulling out the little metal…thing that he might say is starting to take shape if he had any idea what he wanted it to be yet.

Mai squints, head tilting like that will make it become something recognizable. “Is that…my dessert spoon?”

“The *palace’s* dessert spoon,” Zuko corrects, because that seems like an important distinction for reasons that will be clearer to him in the morning.

“But the ones that go with my—Whatever. Why?”

Zuko shrugs, tucking it away safe again and folding his hands over his stomach. It feels weird to work on now with both of them watching. That will maybe be clearer to him in the morning, too.

“Oh, oh.” Ty Lee nearly falls backward in her excitement, arms going wide and foot kicking up for balance. “Is it for looooove?”

It would just take a little nudge to tip her over. Just a tiny one. Mai would probably get mad again, though. “Like anyone in my family would know what *that* feels like,” he mutters, and hopefully they’re too tipsy to notice the conspicuous lack of a direct answer. Thank Agni that Azula is still dead to the world.

Ty Lee steadies herself against Mai. “Love feels like…shiny.”

Mai raises an eyebrow. “Really, Ty Lee?”

She huffs, straightening as if to prove something. “It’s shiny and bright auras and lady flies in your chest every time you look at them and wanting to be with them and hear them talk and knowing you’d do anything to see them smile and knowing that there’s always someone to keep you warm no matter what.” She finishes with a little hiccup and her eyes narrowed in determination across the fire, and Zuko can see what Mai can’t from her angle, that Ty Lee’s eyes are far more on Azula than Zuko, and far too fixed for it to be a distant stare.

“…That’s going to be hard,” Zuko says softly, going serious. There’s a distinct possibility that Ty Lee is barking up the wrong tree, there.

Ty Lee just shrugs, though, and smiles a sad little smile before resting her head on Mai’s shoulder, so maybe Zuko isn’t giving her enough credit. “I know.”

“You know all about hard things, Zuko,” Mai says, and neither her nor Ty Lee’s expressions change so Zuko’s just going to assume that wasn't meant to be a jab. “Are they worth it?”

Zuko shifts, turning the mostly empty bottle idly in his hands as his mind helpfully trips through half-formed memories of cool fingers curled absently around Zuko’s ankle and a sleep-soft body tucked under his own and bright laughter across a spread of takeout containers. “I hope so.” Agni, but it feels dangerous to hope for anything, let alone to admit to it out loud.

“Well, he’s cute, at least,” Ty Lee says, helpfully lightening the mood. “So *I think* it’s worth it.”

Mai rolls her eyes, all fond exasperation. “Some of us have other things on our mind than ogling everyone we come across.”

“Like what?” Ty Lee asks, grin sudden turning just a little bit sharp. “Ogling Zuko’s freakishly strong legs?”

Mai flushes absolutely scarlet and Zuko chokes on his own breath, letting out a noise alarmingly close to a squeak and hiding behind his shaggy hair as Mai falls backward off her driftwood seat in embarrassment and Ty Lee collapses into delighted giggles on top of her.

&#45;-

Mai and Ty Lee are still curled around each other where they fell, so deep into the night that it’s on the edge of morning, when Azula speaks from across the fire, eyes slitted to nothing more than a thin slash of reflected flame. “Sometimes things are hard for a reason.”

Zuko waits, because she’s pitching her voice not to wake the others, and because if she’s been waiting this long to say something then a little more time won’t hurt.

“Sometimes it’s a warning. That it’s something you shouldn’t do.”

Zuko looks up, mostly-sober at this point, holding her eyes before looking back into the fire. “We can’t all be like you, Azula,” he says quietly.

She snorts. “You could at least *try* to be. I’m serious, Zuko,” she adds when he rolls his eyes, her tone turning disapproving. “You’re making yourself weak with this. You’re making yourself vulnerable on purpose.”

“I’m not trying to,” Zuko sighs, more than aware of all the ways it’s made him question when he’s needed to be sure, of all the little moments when he could have been decisive and strong and instead he hesitated.

“But you aren’t trying to stop.”

“…No,” Zuko admits, because she deserves to know even if he were capable of dodging a question that direct. “I’m not.”

“Agni, you—” She growls in the back of her throat, throwing an angry handful of sand into the fire. They ran out of truly flammable things a long time ago. “—you absolute *dumb* *dumb*.”

Zuko hums in reply, feeling his lips twitch into a lopsided smile. “Maybe,” he allows, for once not particularly bothered by it. She isn’t saying anything he hasn’t already thought himself.

Azula shakes her head, refusing to share in his levity. “You can’t afford to be weak, Zuko. Not now. You’re going to get yourself killed.”

Zuko taps his fingernail against the bottle, watching the twist and dance of the flames. “Maybe.” Or maybe he can keep grounding himself on the fact that someone as amazing and extraordinary as Sokka could want him, and never have to face the fact that it might not be true anymore. Maybe Zuko can hold onto the knowledge of being wanted—not just wanted. Cherished, valued, sought out, touched and held and admired like *Zuko* was the extraordinary thing—and the truth that must follow, then, that some part of Zuko must be worth all that wanting. Even if it’s hard in the halls of the palace to remember what that part might be. Maybe Zuko will make himself strong, for once, with this fragile thing, and find a way to walk this path without it hurting every step of the way.

### Text

Zuko is awake and thinking of Sokka like he usually doesn’t allow himself—it does…non-meditative things to his morning meditation—when he hears footsteps pause in the hallway outside his rooms. He stills, wary. It’s not the noise that usually accompanies a guard, or a servant readying for the day. It could be the woman who tends to his rooms in the morning— she is absolutely determined to help Zuko in the mornings and absolutely unaware that he doesn’t sleep enough for her to ever beat him to waking—but even with her arriving nearly with the sun these days, Zuko should have a few degrees left.

He glances up from where he’s sitting in front of the hearth, as if he can see the lightening sky through the ceiling, before eyeing the door with a healthy degree of caution. Azula wouldn’t let herself be heard, and there’s no one else he can think of who would slip a piece of paper beneath the door under the cover of darkness and scurry off without announcing themselves.

Zuko suspects that if he checks the hallway, he’ll find that this little visit has been timed with the few moments when the shift change and the guard rotations overlap to leave the hallway briefly unoccupied. Which is the other reason Zuko will always be ready for the day before the servants arrive.

Zuko slowly rises to his feet, straining his senses for any more stray noises or shifting shadows beneath the door that could suggest someone lingering out of sight. He can’t feel anything big enough to be a body with his heat sense, but Zuko is acutely aware that his heat isn’t faultless against someone who knows how to conceal themselves.

He warily approaches the doors, eyeing the seemingly ordinary scroll half-shoved into the room. After a moment he stretches out a slipper-clad foot to tug it the rest of the way in, briefly running through the likelihood of contact poisons and deciding that they might not be Azula’s style, but they definitely fit at least a quarter of the Inner Council.

Zuko kicks both slippers into the fire—he can’t have the poor servant, whose name he’s never going to fucking know because he’s never going to work up the nerve to ask, looking for the missing half of the pair all day—and pads on quiet feet to snatch a letter opener and one of his more useless little knives and a polishing rag from his bedroom.

Zuko delicately transfers the scroll onto his desk, avoiding skin contact as he pins it open by the corners into the wood. Satisfied, he tosses the rag into the fire on top of the smoldering pieces of slipper, encouraging the hearth fire to burn with a little more hunger and calling a flame into his hand to light the darkness, reluctantly curious about what someone wanted to tell him with such secrecy.

Zuko needs to read the scroll a few times to make sure he’s understanding it, the characters swimming across the page as his anger builds, the edges of his flame going unsteady, the air around him going dangerously dry and hot. The note is fucking…*commanding* him. To investigate his great-grandfather’s death. In order to understand his own *destiny*, and Zuko almost lights the scroll on fire on principle, damage to the wooden desk by damned, because he’s so fucking *done* with this shit.

Zuko’s breath hisses from between his teeth as he snatches up the scroll, heedless of the blades still buried in the desk surface. He shoves it into his pocket because there’s no place he can fucking put it where it can’t be found. He should just burn it. Agni’s dripping cock, he doesn’t have time for this, not this close to the eclipse, even if he *were* interested in stirring up some viper rat’s nest of trouble and risking turning himself into even more of a political target than he already is.

Investigate Sozin’s death? Why doesn’t he just investigate Azulon’s too, while he’s at it, and maybe then he can start asking if anyone is sure exactly how Lu Ten got deployed that day, onto the front lines where he had no business being and with raw recruits instead of his usual Guard.

Investigate his great grandfather’s death. Like Zuko's an Agni-burned idiot.

…Fuck.

&#45;-

Sokka is never going to understand how—but he *will* chalk it up to his amazing planning— but somehow they actually manage to arrive at the Black Cliffs, exactly at the rendezvous point, four days ahead of the invasion.

“See, Sokka?” Katara tosses a sleeping roll at him with a grin and maybe a tad more force than is strictly necessary. “I told you it would be fine. We had plenty of time.”

“Four days,” he reminds her, catching the next bag with a grunt.

“All the time in the world!”

“Four. Days,” Sokka repeats, gently transferring Momo off their supplies and onto his shoulder. If Toph and Aang were going to run off to explore they could have at least brought Momo with them. Sokka only has so many eyes and hands for catching bags and defending food. “That’s three sleeps.”

“We’ve toppled governments with less time than that,” Katara points out as she starts undoing the harness of Appa’s saddle.

“And more time never hurt to prepare to topple this one,” Sokka says, refusing to budge as he catches the straps she tosses down so they won’t smack against Appa’s sides.

“I still think we could have stopped for—”

“Nope! Definitely not!”

Katara sticks out her tongue as she slides off Appa’s back, the saddle slipping off into the grass on Appa’s other side. “Spoilsport.”

“Sorry for wanting to be on time for my own invasion,” Sokka says, rolling his eyes as he begins sorting out Appa’s grooming supplies.

“*Our* invasion.”

“The *team’s* invasion,” Toph says, wandering back over, looking freshly dust- and grass-covered like she just took a good roll around on the ground. She probably did.

“Fine,” Sokka says, rolling his eyes and absently making note of where Aang is still doing his exploring thing across the wide clearing. “Well now *we* can all be happy that *we* are on time for *our* invasion.”

Toph seems to consider for a moment, then shrugs. “Sokka does know a lot about being on time for Fire Nation invasions.”

“Thank you, I—wait, what?”

“Oh, *ew*,” Katara says, glaring at Sokka like he was the one who said it.

“*Guys*,” Sokka protests, feeling his face turning scarlet despite himself. That didn’t even make *sense.* “Why do you—Spirits, you read into *every*—” He stops himself, glowering at Toph and then pointedly turning back to Appa’s brushes. There's no point in continuing when Katara is making a production of pretending to gag while Toph cackles loud enough to make it clear that she got just the reaction she was looking for.

“You’re too easy, the both of you,” Toph grins, looking entirely self-satisfied.

Sokka scowls, muttering to himself about how *some* people need to get their minds out of the *gutter* and should be *grateful* that he’s taking the *high road* where at least he has Momo who doesn’t judge him. “Where’s Aang?” he grumbles, really hoping they can just…change the subject, immediately.

“Still exploring. He said something about getting in some extra reps.”

“He could at least help set up camp first,” Sokka complains without too much real heat. The three of them can get it done fast enough.

Katara perks up, eyes going straight to the nice river near the tree line. “Oh, extra reps!”

Toph grins, positively evil as she takes a step back from all the bags. “It wouldn’t hurt to give the ol’ muscles a nice workout,” she says, slapping her own thighs.

“Since we have so much extra time, of course,” Katara agrees, giving Sokka her sunniest smile.

*“Four days*,” Sokka says as they both begin edging away. It’s *not* that much time. It isn’t!

“Who knows,” Katara says, mock-serious, “Maybe Aang will spontaneously master firebending with all that time. Four whole days!”

“You know what, *you* do the schedule next time,” Sokka calls to the empty air as Katara and Toph both dash off to do bending things. He huffs, restating the urge to cross his arms in annoyance because he’s fully aware that if he hasn’t moved Katara on the topic after nearly fifteen years, it certainly isn’t going to happen now.

Fine.

“I guess it’s just you and me, Momo,” Sokka says, surveying the packs and grooming supplies and bedrolls scattered around the grass. Momo cocks his head, then takes a springboard leap off Sokka’s face to scamper after them, the little traitor. Appa sighs like he wouldn’t mind joining the others too, dropping down on his belly in a cloud of shedding fur.

“Fine,” Sokka sighs as he tries to remember where he packed Appa’s toe brush. “Good thing we have so much time.”

Zuko does his best to spend his day ignoring that stupid scroll. If only he could bring himself to burn it. If only burning it meant that he could burn the characters from his mind too, but Zuko knows that’s not how it works with him. Not anymore, at least.

He can’t stop thinking about the scroll during training, which is a distraction he can’t afford, or as he’s exercising Gao, which is a distraction that isn’t appreciated, and the Council isn’t meeting until tomorrow, so he doesn’t even have that gauntlet to force himself to focus on. Instead, Zuko has a wholly open afternoon, and it’s only so long before he finds himself standing in the portrait gallery again, for once looking at paintings that feature families other than his own.

He isn’t exactly hiding here, but it’s close enough to draw Azula like a lodestone. “Brother, if I knew you had such a taste for immolating family artwork…”

“Do you remember how great-grandfather Sozin died?” Zuko ignores, for now, the question of just how much of this place he would burn to the ground if he could.

Zuko can *feel* her eye roll. “Really, Zuzu, did your brain just turn to complete mush out there? Tell me, did you forget your entire education immediately, or did it at least take a few months? He died peacefully in his sleep.”

Zuko looks at her askance. “…Sure.”

Azula shrugs, unbothered by his skepticism. “That’s what all the textbooks and teachers and schools will tell you.”

Textbooks and teachers and schools. Azula doesn’t choose her words idly, and she just carved out a very specific Minister of Education approved space. So rule out the publicly accessible libraries, then, because this would be about controlling the flow of information. Which makes it firmly the type of secret that Azula can’t keep her hands off of, as long as there’s anything there to actually know.

“Right,” Zuko says slowly, continuing to stare blindly at the painting in front of him as he sorts through the less welcoming archives and private collections in the city and lands on the Fire Sage’s archives beneath the Temple of Agni. The ones that preserve the deeds of Agni’s blood on earth, the ones that no one is supposed to know about without having gone through the proper rites and initiations, first.

This seems like just the kind of thing that would be neatly indexed and organized down there, assuming it’s not an elaborate trap to catch Zuko where he most definitely is not supposed to be.

Zuko gives her a little nod, pausing as he turns to begin a meandering path back toward his rooms that will conveniently let him scope out what the gardens on the west side of the palace look like these days, and if they still grow all the way up to the perimeter walls. “Have you found out why they wanted us at Ember Island?”

Azula is briefly, visibly annoyed. “Father says that he will tell us in the Council meeting tomorrow.”

“…Are you going to wait for that?”

“Really, Brother,” Azula scoffs, flicking a stray hair back into place. “Do at least *try* not to be stupid.”

&#45;-

Sokka is working on putting a nice edge on all his weapons after dinner, trying not to listen too hard or think too much as Katara tries to rope Aang into post-dinner cleanup. He isn’t sure if it’s because she wants another waterbender around still, or if it’s because she’s also noticed that if anyone has ever needed a distraction…

“Does Aang seem a little…”

“Panicky?” Toph finishes.

“…Yeah,” Sokka says. “That.”

“Oh yeah,” she mutters, her feet shifting on the ground and making Sokka wonder what she’s picking up from all of them, because Sokka has been shooting between pre-battle calm and explosive nerves most of the day, himself.

Sokka fiddles with his whetstone. “I thought he just wanted to get in a few extra reps…”

Toph snorts. “I think he might have a loose definition of ‘a few.’”

“Well,” Sokka says, trying to reach for some good morale. “At least he’ll be tired enough to sleep well.”

“Let’s all be grateful for that,” she says.

Sokka tests the edge on his boomerang, nodding to himself when it easily parts a blade of grass before sneaking a look at Toph, some instinct urging him to be subtle about it even though she can’t see. “How are you doing?”

She tilts her face in his direction, expression bland as she makes a show of relaxing back onto her elbows and propping a leg on her bent knee. “Fine.”

Sokka nods—he’s used to hearing all different versions of that word, and hers is believable enough—spending some more time with his polishing cloth now that he has the blade in good shape. “Do you remember what you—”

“Yes.” Her voice is hard. “And you better not make me do anything about it.”

“I’ll do my best,” Sokka promises, voice wry even as he can’t help wondering if parts of himself have already been compromised in ways that she wouldn’t think to look out for, in moments when she wasn’t around. If maybe it happened not with Zuko’s hands on his skin and smile pressed against his mouth, but in days spend researching in Ba Sing Se libraries and sitting by ponds sketching out plans in soft sand, in the quiet nights together when all of them say with their own thoughts and Sokka slowly pulled the pieces together one by one.

Because Sokka isn’t quite sure if there’s any other explanation for how he could have gone through the raids of his home, through everything in the North—Yue dying and days spent hauling bodies out of the water, not knowing if it would be worse to find a familiar one or to never know—and still turn around now and invite more of his friends into battle.

He knows he didn’t technically *ask* any of the true kids to come, but…can Sokka really say he’ll be surprised to see Teo and the others after asking the Mechanist for help? Or that he thinks the earthbender resistance near Omashu will show up without Haru—if Haru even counts as a kid, when Sokka doesn’t? Or Spirits, that it would even occur to what’s left of Jet’s Freedom Fighters to leave any of their number behind?

Fuck, a *twelve-year-old* is their rallying cry, their hope and their vanguard in battle. And Sokka’s been training the children back home for years. Can he really sit here now and be that shocked, that bothered by the fact that it turns out he’s the kind of person who can plan an invasion and maybe not have places *held* for the kids and the other’s they’ve met along the way, not entirely, but who definitely has spots ready for when they show up.

Sokka feels like he’s tarnishing what’s left of their childhoods—setting aside the fact of risking their lives, as if that’s something to just be set aside—even as a part of him still marvels that any of them can still view this fight as anything except struggle and anguish, as anything they want to be a part of if it can be avoided. But then, they’re all involved in their own way already, even if they shouldn’t be, and Sokka learned a long time ago that war doesn’t leave space for innocents.

What worth can Sokka place in innocence preserved against the value of another earthbender, another sword, no matter how small the person wielding it? What kind of calculus can be wrapped around the means of achieving an end that could be faster, cleaner? How many dreams of grandeur and noble heroism is he willing to sacrifice to the dirty reality of battle— how much more than just dreams—if it means something like the North never happens again?

Sokka wonders if it’s even worth asking, when he’s already set it all into motion. But Spirits, he thinks it’s going to be hard for him to be proud of the person who brings twelve-year-olds to war, no matter how talented and vital they are, no matter how much they want to be there and how important the outcome of the fight. And fuck, what does it say about everyone else involved that Sokka is able to do it in the first place? That he *needs* to?

Soon, he reminds himself, trying to take a page from Toph’s book and just enjoy the moment of peace while they have it. Three nights, and one day, and then one way or another it will be over. And one way or another, Sokka will have his answers on whether what he gains will be worth the price.
