Zuko looks at the unguarded doors and considers, briefly, that Azula has known all along and is helpfully paving the path to his destruction, rather than forcing him to do it himself. Then he snorts, rolling his eyes before setting his face back into its habitual scowl. As if Azula would be helpful.

He checks that his swords are settled, that his topknot is neat and tidy—wouldn’t do to look disheveled—and then shoves the doors open with maybe more force and melodramatic flair than is strictly necessary. But then, this isn’t a conversation to be *subtle*. And Zuko’s been itching to cut himself loose for…months, really.

The Fire Lord seems as unimpressed by his son’s dramatics as he’s ever been, watching without any real surprise as Zuko strides over the red- and gold-inlaid floor. “Prince Zuko,” he says, with the distant distaste of someone noticing a hair in someone else’s dinner. “You have decided you have more important things to do than fulfill your duties?”

“I’ve come to tell you the truth,” Zuko says, deliberately stoking his anger along with his resolve because he can feel the edges of his inner fire suddenly starting to flicker, waver, and he’s going to need some parody of warmth in his chest to get himself through this.

Ozai raises an eyebrow. “A son comes to tell truths to his father during—”

He pauses, and it’s only because Zuko is already tense in every way he could be that he doesn’t flinch when his inner fire abruptly *snaps,* extinguished, leaving behind a cold, sucking, yawning emptiness behind his lungs, in the center of his stomach.

“—the dark of an eclipse,” Ozai finishes, words even and disinterested like he doesn’t feel the chill at all. “How…dramatic. Guards—outside.”

Zuko doesn’t watch as the guards leave, eyes fixed on the Fire Lord. His other senses strain for any sudden movements or drawn weapons and he nearly sways when he instinctively tries to reach out with a heat sense that just isn’t there. Zuko forces himself to steadiness, forces his breathing to be as quiet as possible in his ears, because he wouldn’t put it past Ozai to call for a surprise attack from Zuko’s back if he found it expedient. Though Zuko supposes that then the Fire Lord would need to kill all the witnesses, and that’s messier to do without his fire.

Still, Zuko openly has his swords, and his ability to use them has long been a point of mockery within the family. It’s a show of arrogance, to send the guards away, a multi-person lesson in how little consideration Zuko is worth.

Or maybe a sign that the truths Zuko could tell could hurt the Fire Lord, if Zuko found the right words and said them in front of the right people. Maybe it’s both. After all, Azula always criticizes his inefficiency in doing anything for just one reason, and she didn’t learn to do that from *Zuko*.

Ozai gives him a faintly annoyed look before sweeping a bored hand around the empty room, Zuko instinctively tensing despite the distance between them and the lack of flame. “The stage is yours, *Prince*.”

Zuko ignores the mockery and dives in with his usual blunt impatience. “The Avatar is still alive.”

“…Is he.”

“He’s leading the invasion right now,” Zuko says, carefully watching for any twitch in his father’s expression and ignoring the part of himself that tightens with unease at the thought of the Avatar’s distinctive brand of damage being unleashed on Caldera.

“And why should I believe you,” Ozai finally asks, eyes flicking over Zuko’s lack of armor, the clothes that are of good quality but plain, sturdy, nothing like a Crown Prince should wear.

“Ask any of the soldiers outside.” Or take a look from the roofs. There’s only one person left these days who can glide like that.

Ozai’s voice is soft in that dangerous way that Zuko takes all of Zuko’s willpower not to skitter away from, the way that’s a single invitation to immediately reconsider whatever it is you’re doing. “You would accuse your sister of lying to me?”

Zuko forces himself to meet the Fire Lord’s eyes and fight through a lifetime's worth of instincts as he plays the only card Azula has left for him. “Yes.”

“To what end?” Ozai asks, eyes narrowed, words still soft, soft, soft. “Why would Azula lie about that?”

Zuko snorts, reaching for anger to help shore up his resolve and keep him from visibly wavering, because it’s not enough to just plant the seed, he needs to make sure it has time to take root. “Azula is a fourteen-year-old girl on her first trip off the islands. What she doesn’t know could fill the library three times over.”

“And you know these things? Is that it?” Ozai’s face twists with contempt. “Your attempts to undermine your sister in my eyes are transparent and disgraceful. Even more of a sign of your weakness and incompetence than your pathetic firebending,” he spits, leaning forward with the force of it. “Get out of my sight. You disgust me.”

Zuko knew, intellectually, that his father hadn’t truly changed his opinion. Azula had made that clear. But Zuko still has to work to keep his breathing steady as if the open confirmation doesn’t take him like a knife to the chest. “No.”

“Excuse me?” Ozai’s hands twitch, like maybe he reached for fire and found only emptiness. “Your Fire Lord has spoken.”

“You don’t deserve the title of Fire Lord,” Zuko growls, the worst bursting free without an inner flame to burn them away. “The Fire Lord is meant to embody Agni’s protection of her people! All you’ve done is sacrifice this Nation in a question for your own glory.” Now that he’s started it’s like he can’t stop himself, with is dangerous, dangerous. Zuko is here to speak truths, but not too many. “You sit on your throne and talk about grand purposes, but there's nothing honorable about this war! All it’s ever done is bring fear and despair, to our enemies and our own people.”

“Careful, Prince Zuko,” Ozai snarls before forcing himself back toward some facsimile of calm that Zuko knows covers the hard-enough-to-bruise kind of quiet rage. “If I don’t deserve the crown then that makes your succession to the Dragon Throne rather impossible.” “You *would* care about succession while the world burns,” Zuko bites back, painfully aware that their whole fucking family would.

“It sounds like my brother got to you with his drivel,” Ozai says, yellow eyes raking Zuko with a look of open disdain.

Zuko bares his teeth, anger igniting even without his inner fire to spark it. “Uncle was more of a parent than you ever were.”

“And that is where you fail yet again, *Zuko*,” Ozai hisses, the absent ‘Prince’ as loud as a shout. “Nothing could ever stay in your head, could it?. Dragons do not have parents.”

“As I understand it,” Zuko says, body braced, “Dragons kill them.”

Ozai’s composure breaks for a few lightning-fast heartbeats, his nostrils flaring as his eyes flick to the swords on Zuko’s back. “Is that what you’re here for? With *swords* and not fire? To try to prove that you’re a dragon and not some sniveling koala sheep?”

“No,” Zuko says, something savage in him twisting in satisfaction to see that hint of fear on his father’s face. Will Azula appreciate that Zuko is still playing his part, in a way? ven if it’s not the one she meant for him today? Even if he’s forcing her hand in every way he can? “I’m here to tell you that I’m joining the Avatar, and that I’m going to work with him to take you down.” Agni, it feels good to finally say the words, to let it be heard outside his own thoughts. To finally, finally have it be intention and not just wanting.

“Why go through the trouble?” The Fire Lord’s disdain is firmly back in place. “If you are going to admit that you’ve always been a traitor, the Fire Lord is in front of you right now. And powerless, isn’t that the point in waiting for now for all these dramatics? To do away with fire since you’re useless at it?”

Zuko touches the hilts of his blades but doesn’t draw them, grounding himself in their weight as he breathes through the insult that shouldn’t hurt. He distantly wonders if it would land quite so deeply in different circumstances, or if it’s just the absence of his inner flaming moving in sync or contra that's making his emotions feel so big, so unbalanced.

“Some things should be done under Agni’s light,” Zuko manages to sneer, heart fluttering when he sees his own insult land. And even if the sun were high in the sky, this isn’t Zuko’s job, not like this. He might be throwing basically everything into chaos, but the core of it all hasn’t changed.

But Agni, these questions are starting to turn toward things that are risky to even think about in front of the Fire Lord, let alone dance around saying. Zuko should go, before he says too much and gives something away. Before he misjudges the difference between forcing a hand and showing it entirely.

Besides, Zuko doesn’t want to spend another second in Ozai’s company. Doesn’t want to look at him and contend with the clawing, infuriating fact that Zuko, too, has done things now that should never happen under Agni’s judging eyes.

Zuko takes one slow step back, then another, finally letting hatred slide onto his face as he turns his back to the Fire Lord like no one would dare to do if they weren’t prepared to find themselves facing down an Agni Kai. It’s a deliberate provocation that’s probably going to give him nightmares later, one that he would probably never consider if he weren’t so numb with anger that he feels detached, pushed far beyond his fear.

“So you will be a coward then, on top of being without honor,” Ozai calls to his back, tone conveying that Zuko is only confirming things that everyone knows.

Zuko’s stride hitches, just a little, but he keeps going.

“A true descendant of Agni’s line would have the courage to face me.”

Zuko can feel his scar twisting under the force of his snarl, but he keeps moving. He won’t run, he won’t give Ozai that. But Agni’s tits, the door seems three times as far away now as it was when Zuko came in.

“But then, blood will tell. I should have known, after what happened to your mother.” Zuko goes still, the icy cold washing over him without his fire to beat it back. He turns back toward the Fire Lord, slowly, almost like he isn’t in his own body anymore, a distant corner of his mind screaming and screaming for him to keep walking. “What do you mean,” he demands, voice low. Is Ozai really admitting--but it shouldn’t matter either way, not to Zuko. He doesn’t have *time* for it to matter, he knows it, and his mother is just as dead regardless of how Ozai did it.

Still, Zuko can’t bring himself to tear his eyes away from the Fire Lord’s smirk.

“That night,” Ozai starts, almost conversationally, and Zuko doesn’t need to ask which one. “Your mother did vicious, treasonous things. Things that have consequences.” He pauses, eyes tracking Zuko’s every twitching reaction. “For her betrayal and the violence she committed against Agni’s blood, she was banished.”

Zuko can’t breathe. “…Banished.”

“Yes,” the Fire Lord said, mouth curving like he’s recalling a fond memory even as his yellow eyes stay flat and dead on Zuko. “It was a merciful penalty, for a treason such as hers. But I couldn’t disregard that she gave me a worthy heir.” They both know he doesn’t mean Zuko, and the space where his inner fire would be is yawning wide, filling his core with cold dark. “I learned a valuable lesson since then. Do you know what it is?”

Zuko stares, his whole world trying to realign around the possibility his father is dangling in front of him.

“I learned that a Fire Lord has no room for mercy.”

Ozai’s attack catches Zuko stunned, wrong-footed, his own inner flame roaring back to life and rocking him dangerously off-balance as Ozai stabs his fingers forward. Lightning roars across the room and Zuko doesn’t have time to do anything but set his feet and instinctively raise his hands before it strikes.

The cold fire immediately overwhelms him, crackling and angry and malignant as it lances down his arm, his spine, coiling in his stomach and raging against the confines of the furiously burning wall Zuko’s inner fire has become. Zuko clenches against the feeling, wanting it *out*, and then the lightning is moving again, back up the ladder of his ribs, crackling down his arm as Zuko flows into half-remembered muscle memory, lightning screaming off his fingers to explode against the wall next to Ozai’s head.

Shards of rock burst across the room, laying open small cuts across Ozai’s exposed skin, the only visible signs of violence except for the smell of ozone and singed things, and the Fire Lord’s wide-eyed shock.

Zuko wasn’t lying that some things need to happen under Agni’s light. Their fire might be back, but there is none of Agni’s sight down here.

Zuko holds Ozai’s stare for a moment, glad that his habitual rage covers his own surprise over the fact that he managed to miss his timing and not get killed for it. Then he turns, striding away, refusing to be here a moment longer, the slow trickle of blood over Ozai’s left cheek saying far more than any words Zuko could muster.

Zuko lets the doors slam closed behind him, his hands cooling back to more normal temperatures when he notes the absence of guards in the hallway. The fighting must be back on in earnest now to call the guards away, especially with fire back in play. Zuko feels a quick, sharp stab of fear for Sokka. He must be at the heart of the bunker by now, since Azula hasn’t made an appearance yet. Which means he's with her, and Agni, it’s far too early to let himself feel anything like relief yet.

Zuko takes a bracing breath, shoving strength back into his knees and setting out in a ground-eating job for the surface. He firmly pushes away for later the edges of adrenaline-crash weakness that he can’t afford to indulge right now, and useless wonderings over whether he will ever be forgiven for this, or if Zuko is just trading one piece of his family that sees him as a betrayer for another.

&#45;-

Sokka has practiced paying attention to the passage of time. Riding on Appa’s back, counting Aang’s weak heartbeats back on the stolen Fire Nation ship, during training and evening storytime. Sokka knows by now how to have one corner of his mind calmly ticking away the seconds while the rest of him does something entirely different.

So Sokka knows that the eclipse starts bare seconds before they burst into the grand, sprawling underground throne room, Aang leading the way with Toph and Sokka guarding his flanks to find—

“So good of you all to finally join. I was starting to wonder if you were going to stand me up.”

—Azula. Which is *not* good. It’s not what they want, not at all, but—they can work with this. At least, they can work with an Azula alone in a giant cave with no firebending more than they can work with the big empty hall they burst into a few minutes ago.

Azula scans her eyes over them without rising from her slouch against the throne, legs crossed and foot kicking idly in the air. Her gaze lands on Aang and she smirks, unsurprised. “I had a feeling you wouldn’t stay down. But no peasant girl? A shame. But no matter.” Her eyes settle on Sokka, bright and unsettlingly familiar even across the room. “I suppose we don’t *really* need her, do we.”

“Where’s the Fire Lord!” Aang demands, staff whistling through the air as he steps forward with a warning slash.

“So *rude*,” Azula murmurs, nose wrinkling like an Upper Ring merchant catching sight of a Lower Ring urchin. “Manners, manners. Are you really trying to rush through everything? And after I spent *months* preparing for you?” She shifts her gaze back to Sokka and grins, all teeth. “A little messenger hawk whispered such interesting things in my ear about your little —group.”

Sokka feels the implication rattle through him, eyes that should be trained on Azula suddenly tracking the way Aang’s knuckles tighten on his staff and noting how Toph grounds herself a little deeper. The walls he’s built around the fragile ember of his faith hold, but they shudder, because Sokka can’t ignore the niggling awareness that he hasn’t seen Zuko yet. Hasn’t seen him with them or against them or anywhere, and Sokka can’t help but feel his absence like a constant bruise at the back of his mind. Zuko speaks with his actions. So why isn’t he *acting*, if he’s here. And if he isn’t…

“Tell us where the Fire Lord is,” Sokka orders, shaking himself back into the present. He can’t afford that kind of distraction with Azula, he knows that.

“What, am I not good enough for you?” She says, pouting. “Careful, you’re going to hurt my feelings. And here I thought you *liked* firebenders,” she adds with a sudden twist of acid in her voice.

Sokka shifts his grip on his sword, taken aback by the abrupt hostility breaking through her affected unconcern, the note of animosity that felt…genuine. Personal. “Stop wasting our time and give us the information,” he says, trying to rally.

“You mean you don’t *know*?” Azula sits upright, looking openly delighted. “You got all the way here and you still don’t know? And you’re supposed to be the *planner*?”

“You’re in no position to refuse with the eclipse on,” Aang jumps in, the determined threat in his voice pulling Azula’s attention off Sokka. “Tell us!”

“Hm,” Azula hums, examining her red-lacquered nails. “No, I don’t think I will.”

“We’ll make you if we have to,” Toph says, voice hard and earth creaking with intent.

“Will you,” Azula grins, tossing her head as if a strand of her perfect hair would dare be out of place. “Tell me more about how. Because somehow I don’t think your *usual* strategies will work on me.” She’s looking at Sokka again, implying things, and Sokka feels his battle-calm shudder again. Does Zuko think—is that what—he knows that Zuko *said* that, once, that Zuko used to—but does he still—Sokka thought they—did he not believe—

“All we have to do is ask,” Toph drawls, matching Azula’s nonchalance even as the ground shivers under Sokka’s feet, a localized earthquake telling him to get his shit together. “I’ll be able to tell if you lie.”

“Oh? How *interesting*.” She props her chin on her fist, eyes sharp on Toph. “Let’s try— what’s the game, two lies and a truth?” She starts ticking off on her fingers, almost sing-songing, “I could kill you all. I a-*dore* my dear brother. I am a mere novice firebender.” She pauses, considering, then turns to Toph with a sharp smile. “How’d I do?”

Sokka and Aang both glance toward Toph, who stands completely still, conspicuously silent.

“Maybe some more?” Azula suggests, sounding genuinely amused, which is enough to make Sokka’s skin crawl. “Or maybe you need more time? Okay, how about…” She sits upright again, straight-backed and chin lifted, clasping her hands flat in front of her diaphragm like some kind of choral singer. “The Fire Nation should stretch from the ocean in the east to the sea in the west. I am a six-foot-tall purple platypus bear. I don’t need my fire to hurt you.” She abruptly relaxes back again, looking at Toph expectantly.

“…Okay. She’s good.”

Fuck. That just took out…most of Sokka’s remaining plans, really, if Toph can’t discern the truth…And shit, is it only Azula it doesn’t work against? Firebenders? The entire Imperial family? Spirits…

“So a physiological response then, hm? *Fascinating*.” She cocks her head, and Sokka suddenly can’t stop thinking of a bird of prey about to dive for its prey. “But this must be something that only you figured out? Or the Beifongs? Otherwise, the Earth King would be using it.”

Sokka reaches for some bravado, because when all else fails he always has that. “How do you know he isn’t?”

“Oh,” Azula murmurs, almost to herself if the words weren’t so loud, eyes fixed on Sokka as her lips curl into a little smirk. “I do see why he decided on you. You make things so *easy*.”

Sokka blinks. What?

“Let’s find out,” she says, suddenly brisk. “Shall we?”

Azula snaps her fingers and with the now-familiar rumbling grind of stone on stone, two figures drop from the *ceiling* like fucking *spider snakes.* Dai Li agents, Sokka quickly realizes as he and Toph and Aang automatically shift into a defensive formation. He thought they were done with the Dai Li, what the—how—he didn’t *plan* for—

His eyes dart to Azula, who is smiling like a tiger shark scenting blood in the water as she watches him. “Let’s find out what the Earth Kingdom’s best know how to do.”

The Dai Li surge forward, arms punching, and Toph and Aang both move to counter them with earth just like they drilled back in Ba Sing Se. Okay, this isn’t ideal, and nowhere in any of Sokka’s plans, but three against two aren’t the worst odds. Especially when they already know how the Dai Li operate and the agents are confined to a—

Azula explodes off the throne into a leaping lunge that covers far more ground with far more force than it should, her boot taking fucking *chips* off the stone wall as she narrowly misses Toph—with a *grin*, fuck, how did Zuko grow up with this—and only because Aang fell back to launch a last-second blast of air to knock her off course.

And apparently the Dai Li will *not* be fighting on the defensive to protect their temporary non-bender. How unexpectedly, inconveniently egalitarian. Sokka might theoretically appreciate the sentiment if it didn’t mean that Azula is now fucking flipping all over the confined space, smiling and smirking like a Spirits-damned circus performer.

Fuck, they can’t focus on eliminating the benders because of Azula, and the Dai Li are smart enough not to let either Toph or Aang focus on her. Which leaves Sokka, and he will be wholly up for the challenge as soon as he can fucking *catch* her. A game of cat and mouse might normally not be a big deal—let them wear themselves out trying to be cute—but the clock is ticking and enemy earthbenders underground mean that—

A support column collapses with a crash that shakes the entire room, Azula sliding down the steep angle like she’s *penguin sledding* as another column topples *much* closer to Sokka. He scrambles out of the way, throwing himself against the wall as it falls bare inches from his face. Then he’s hauling himself back up, chest already tight even before he confirms that it’s punched a hole in the wall. *Fuck*.

Enemy earthebenders underground mean that any space is only confined for as long as they want it to be.

He whirls to see Azula already sprinting toward him, and all Sokka can do is flinch back, losing his balance on the dusty curve of the pillar as she launches forward, not *at him*, what the—*over* him, an absolutely ridiculous, showy front flip that has her face passing inches above his own. Her expression is set in a taunting smirk, eyes boring into him, and for a second all Sokka can think, totally inanely as he continues to fall back, is *huh, guess the* *flippy leapy stuff runs in the family.*

Sokka’s back barely hits the stone before he’s up again, jumping most of the way to his feet and hauling himself toward the new hole in the wall to see Azula standing in the room on the other side. It’s the room they cleared first, fuck, at least Sokka knows vaguely where this is. She’s standing at the doors, almost like she was waiting for him, an unsettlingly expectant look on her face that doesn’t match her disconcertingly flat, hostile eyes.

“I know my brother is useless,” she drawls, seeing that she has his attention. “But he wasted enough time on you that I had dared to hope for better.” She scrapes him with a scathing look. “Really.”

Sokka doesn’t dare take his eyes off her. “Aang! Toph!”

There’s an explosion of earth and jagged, dark stone and then a Dai Li agent is flying across the room to roll to a stop at Azula’s feet in a tangle of limp limbs that don’t look like they’re entirely fitting together the way they’re supposed to anymore.

“On it,” Toph growls.

Azula wrinkles her nose and flicks the fresh layer of dust off her shoulder. Then the other Dai Li agent is riding a wave of stone through the new hole in the wall and Azula is grinning and bolting through the doors without a second glance for her fallen minion. Toph and Aang take off in immediate pursuit, Sokka only steps behind as he does a quick scan to make sure no one is behind them before following into the tunnels.

They sprint as fast as they can, and Sokka is achingly aware that Aang and Toph are limited by Sokka’s pace, that they could use their bending to close the distance if it didn’t mean leaving Sokka behind. And no matter how hard he tries, he can’t seem to gain any ground. Azula is always just in front of them, smirking and calling out mocking comments and weaving around and under Toph and Aang’s attacks with such an air of casual unconcern that for a moment he wonders if he isn’t dreaming.

“It’s refreshing to find someone who practices nonviolence so *aggressively*,” Azula laughs as she dodges and dances around Aang’s staff before twisting out of his range again.

She’s frustratingly unbothered even as Toph manages to trap her last Dai Li agent with a sudden, wrenching rush of metalbending—“Oh, aren’t you *such* a treasure. How the Beifongs ever let you slip out of their hands…”—like they might as well be playing tiger seal, tiger seal, tiger shark.

Most of the time, at least.

Azula flips off a wall and Sokka *knows* this move, even without the fire attached to it. He reacts without thinking, chest clenched around a sudden surge of nervous hope, his sword jabbing toward the spot where Azula should be landing, except—except she’s dangling one-handed from a metal strut instead, one foot braced against the wall, gaze venomous.

“Do *better*, Water Tribe,” she hisses, real anger crawling beneath the words, and Sokka is so taken aback that he recovers backward without thinking to put his back to the wall, meeting her hostile stare in tense stillness. Naked animosity slides over her face before Aang rounds the corner and she’s off again.

Sokka gapes after her, mind scrambling in the moment of rest. He doesn’t really know anything about Azula, but her slides between a resentful kind of antagonism and amused, almost playful taunting if you didn’t mind the risk of cutting yourself as you played—

Sokka’s hand darts out almost without his permission, snagging Aang’s arm as he runs by. “Wait! Aang, Toph, stop! She’s stalling, she doesn’t even want to fight!”

“Not true,” Azula calls, poised for movement and eyes narrowing as they slide to Sokka. “I would *love* to fight.”

“You’re just trying to waste our time,” Toph shouts, fists clenching hard enough to turn her knuckles white.

“Dear, that *is* what the peasant just said,” Azula drawls, making a little tsking noise. “Since you’re blind, I’ll tell you that I’m rolling my eyes right now. Really, I’m starting to see why the Beifongs didn’t let you out.”

Toph snarls, rocking forward only to be stopped as Sokka throws his arm out, holding her back. “She’s just baiting you,” he cautions without taking his eyes off Azula. “She’s baiting all of us.”

“So, what?” Aang asks, his staff slowly lowering into a defensive position. “We just ignore her?”

Sokka holds Azula’s gaze, feeling his battle-calm solidifying around him again as he starts to back away. “We still have plenty of time left to find the Fire Lord.” Maybe not plenty, but enough. “She’s powerless. We can forget about her.”

Azula’s face goes still in a way that Sokka recognizes with a little jolt as something presaging an emotional blowup. But this into Zuko—where *is* he, Azula’s talking enough about him that his absence feels like a nearly a physical between her and Sokka—so Azula just stays still, watching them go, calculating.

“Go if you want,” she says after a few heartbeats, relaxing her stance and still not breaking eye contact like Sokka is the only one she’s talking to. “You’re good at walking away, after all.”

Sokka grits his teeth against the jab, against the instinctive protest that *he* isn’t the one who’s done the walking, and turns around. The back of his neck crawls, being exposed like this, but he trusts Aang and Toph to follow and their combined awareness to notice an attack before it lands.

“You’re so *good* at walking into traps, too,” Azula adds, almost as an afterthought.

Aang and Toph hesitate, but Sokka waves them on.

“And leading others into them, of course.”

A pause for reaction, and Sokka just sets his shoulders and tries to block out her words while still being aware of the potential danger she represents, trying to think about where to search next. They only have time for one last spot.

“My favorite prisoner talks about that all the time, you know.”

Sokka’s step stutters.

“You must have made quite the impression.”

Sokka’s feet stop without his permission, Toph and Aang pulling a few steps ahead before they realize.

“She was stoic at first, you know,” Azula says, sounding just like the rich Ba Sing Se ladies sharing gossip over tea. “All she would do for so long was insist that you would come for her.

*She*—who—what—Sokka didn’t—wait—

“But everyone breaks eventually. And it turns out Kyoshi Warriors break in such *interesting* ways.”

Sokka whirls around, fists clenched, to find Azula grinning from across the hallway.

“*Suki*. That was her name.” Her smile turns sharp at whatever must be showing on Sokka’s face. “Oh, *that* hit a nerve. Does Zuzu know how much you care?” She asks, shaking her head in mock regret. “Maybe he would have gone easier on her if he knew.” She lets the implication stand until Aang sucks in a hard breath of realization. “Or maybe not. You know how *angry* he gets.”

“Sokka,” Aang says, low and urgent. “It’s like you said—”

Azula projects her voice a little louder, somehow drowning out Aang’s words because suddenly she’s all Sokka can hear over the buzzing in his ears. “She’s lovely, isn’t she? Such striking features, even without the face paint.” She jumps down from her perch and begins strolling over, unhurried. “And my brother, well—*striking* is one word for it, but it’s not quite the same, is it?”

Her tone invites him to share in the joke, and she makes a little, exaggerated moue of disappointment when he doesn’t reply. Sokka can barely breathe.

“I did warn Zuzu that he has to work just a *little* harder to make up for it,” she says, shaking her head and scaping Sokka with a once-over just this side of scathing. “But he was so *sure* that he’d done enough with you.”

Sokka inflates his lungs with a gasp, jerking back around toward the others and forcing himself to walk again on legs that he can barely feel. He needs to get out—*they* need to get out—he can’t—

He can’t escape her voice, suddenly flat, the mockery sliding away to reveal venomous anger. “You know, I did try to tell Zuko that no one who actually thought they cared would try quite so much to get him killed. But you know how he is.”

“Wha—” Sokka bites the word off before he can finish it, but it’s already too late.

“Oh, do you not *know?”* A peal of delighted laughter rings out, her boots striking like a metronome as she paces closer. “Poor Zuzu, always trying to hide things, even from the people he claims to care about.” Her tone shifts back toward malice. “What else did he hide from you? I’m guessing more than you know.”

Sokka takes a deep breath, shoving away the queasy knot at the base of his throat to hear his own thoughts coming out of her mouth. “I know what you’re doing and I’m not going to fall for it.”

“Once fooled, twice shy? At least *you* recognize it.” He can imagine her eye roll with disturbing ease. “Zuzu will be crushed that you didn’t care enough to try to find out, though. He so hates failing. And he does have that whole *thing* for making you come to him, doesn’t he? He’ll be so sad you gave up right at the end.”

She laughs at whatever she reads in his body language as Sokka tries to concentrate through the way she’s trying to recast weeks and months with just a few deliberately casual words. “We’re going,” Sokka forces out, his voice wavering more than he would like but his feet finally managing to move again.

“Hm, into the trap, yes, you said. Maybe we should ask your two little friends what they think of that,” she suggests, saccharine sweet and acknowledging Toph and Aang’s existence for the first time since Sokka started trying to leave. “Especially after you chased Zuzu across an entire ocean. The eclipse *is* a wonderful excuse, but, well…”

Sokka can practically *hear* the little you-can-fill-in-the-blanks shrug she must be giving.

“It would be one thing if it was just you,” she continues, sounding slightly scandalized in a breathless, excited way. “But to lead all your friends into it too? And so *many*? I suppose you left your sister behind, though. So at least you cared about *that* one.”

Sokka tries to make his feet go faster, but he’s feeling disconcertingly disassociated from his extremities right now. It’s like every single word has been designed specifically to tear him down, with the kind of precision that could only come from knowledge. But how would she *know*. Fuck, he doesn’t remember this hallway being so long when they were first running down it. How much time do they have left? It’s like her words and the steady cadence of her boots are worming their way into his head, disrupting his internal clock, his internal everything. And even though he knows she’s doing it on purpose it’s still *working*.

“Of course, it’s all too late now. For Zuko, I mean.” A weighty pause, her next words tinged with regret. “He only had so much time to prove his value to Father, after all.”

Sokka stops dead, every muscle locking against what she’s suggesting. He tries to will his body to keep moving, but he can barely hear himself over the cacophony of his emotions and the sound of Azula’s voice slicing through everything else.

“You know how it is, coming back from exile and everything. And, well, you just took so *long* to get here. He insisted right to the end that you would come, but, well—” Sokka whirls around, chest heaving, to find Azula barely out of reach, smirking, looking like she’s savoring the taste of the words on her tongue as she says them. “—you were just too *late*.”

He stares at her, feeling his face twisting into some terrible shape as he swallows back the scream clawing at his chest, his heart slamming so hard against his ribs he has to brace against it. That’s not—that isn’t—*no.*

Sokka forces himself to take one step back, then another, feeling like his legs are barely holding his weight, like any faster and he’ll just start falling. Azula mirrors him with a look of faint amusement, not trying to catch him, just keeping pace, and somehow he can’t bring himself to just turn around and run when everything in him is trying to fall to pieces.

“You’re lying,” Sokka finally rasps out, with none of the surety he needs.

“Am I?” Azula raises one perfectly arched eyebrow. “How would you know?”

“You’re *lying,”* he repeats, the words guttural, barely above a snarl.

“Then where is he?” She tilts her head, quizzical, like she’s genuinely looking forward to what he comes up with. “You must know at least something about him after all that—” she wrinkles her nose “—*time* together. Do you really think Zuko would stay away? That he would just sit quietly in a safe little room somewhere?”

No, Sokka doesn’t, and hasn’t he been wondering where Zuko is this whole time? Hasn’t he been wondering it for weeks, quietly tense over the idea of Zuko being back in this place that’s never been kind to him, equally tense over the idea that Zuko never made it out of Ba Sing Se. “He’s a Prince,” Sokka tries. “No one would—”

“Really?” Azula laughs, incredulous. “No one? Didn’t he tell you about how he got such a pretty face?”

Sokka’s breath freezes, and something flickers through Azula’s eyes too quickly for him to read.

“Maybe he did,” she murmurs, voice suddenly pitched like they’re confidants. “His voice didn’t use to sound like that, you know. Before.”

“Shut up,” Sokka says, swallowing back sudden nausea, dread hooking into his spine.

“But the way he *screamed*.”

Sokka is distantly aware of Toph’s voice, her urgent words barely penetrating the rush of Sokka’s rising desperation. He needs Azula to stop. Talking. “*Shut up!”*

“I only watched the first time of course. It’s a different thing,” she muses, holding up her right hand, “When you’re up close and—”

Sokka is moving before he’s even conscious of the impulse, lunging forward as Azula finally manages to light the powder keg of his emotions. She doesn’t try to fight as he slams her by the shoulder back into the wall, her face twisting into a smirk that doesn’t even try to cover hatred as he looms over her. “*Where is he.”*

“Why would you care, *Sokka*.” She spits his name like a curse, voice suddenly low so her words sit just between them. “You’re the reason he's not here." She leans forward, hissing, "You're the reason he died.”

“No.” Sokka feels wild, blind, his head buzzing with something frantic. He slams her back against the wall like that can shake the truth out of her. “*No*.”

Azula seems utterly unconcerned by the treatment, or maybe more focused on the blood she can scent in the water than her own physical comfort. “He was so *sure* you would come for him. He kept saying it, over and over. Right up until that last day.”

Sokka can’t hold back the raw, wordless noise that slips out of him, something that’s a mixture of rage and denial and fear. He stares down at her almost-familiar features, fingers digging into the soft gaps where her armor breaks to allow movement, feeling more than hearing the way the stiff leather creaks.

Azula purses her lips, a mockery of thoughtfulness. “Want to know his last words?” A quick smirk. “Well, not his *last* last ones, obviously. But the last ones he had for you.”

Sokka is frozen, everything in him wanting to shove her away, to reject anything that falls from her lips even as his mind screams for him to hold onto any piece of Zuko he can get, to not turn away from this opportunity in case it’s the only one he has.

“Ready?” She leans up, coiled strength pressing against his hold, tawny eyes locked on his, almost a parody of a kiss if it weren’t so blatantly aggressive. Her words are a bare whisper he has to strain to hear, her breath ghosting over his skin firebender-hot in a way that makes his stomach twist. “He wanted you to know that I only tell lies when the truth isn’t good enough.”

Sokka stutters, stumbles, throwing himself back as her words penetrate the clamoring panic of his thoughts. He staggers for balance, and he can feel that he’s looking at her with wild eyes, can feel that he must be visibly ragged around the edges as he tries to understand what —does that mean—but then—

She doesn’t chase, finally, just stays leaning back against the wall where he pinned her. A vicious little smile settles on her face, like an octocat that’s done playing and is ready to eat, as a sudden rumble of—of *thunder?—*echoes through the tunnel.

“Sounds like the firebending’s back on,” she says brightly, and if Sokka's thrown off balance by her suddenly upbeat demeanor he’s thrown even more when she kicks her leg up into a high, *burning* heel sweep. Sokka barely hurls himself back in time, tripping again and falling to his knee as Toph pulls up a barrier between him and Azula’s next blast of flames. Sokka rolls out of the line of fire, scrambling to pay attention, to get back into things, to remember that this is a battle, *his* battle, orienting himself just in time to catch the tail end of some whirling flip that Aang barely manages to dodge.

Azula lands neatly on her feet, not even breathing hard, and flicks a piece of her bangs back into place. “Father is at the end of the hall, down a secret stairway on the left. Pull the rusty sconce.” She smirks, lightning or blue fire or something briefly dancing over her fingertips. “I, unfortunately, can't keep entertaining you. Duty calls, you know. But I’m sure Father would be delighted to see you now.”

Azula darts off, fast enough to drive home the point that she’d been toying with them all along. Sokka finally stumbles back to his feet, hauling Aang up too and staring after her in horror as he feels every single one of his carefully plotted plans go up in a careless puff of smoke.

“Sokka…” Toph sounds gentle, almost, and that’s enough to snap him out of his own head for the first time in…he doesn’t know. Too long, considering they only had eight minutes to start with. The longest eight minutes of Sokka’s life.

“Let’s go,” he says, a harsh edge to his voice that he can’t put any energy toward softening with about right now, just like he can’t devote any part of himself toward dissecting every single way he fucked this up from the very start. Not yet. “We need to get back to the others.”

“I’m ready,” Aang offers tentatively. Both he and Toph are acting like Sokka is a rabid polar leopard and they aren’t sure if he’s going to keel over or go on one last rampage through the village. “I can still face the Fire Lord.”

“It was a trap, Aang,” Sokka grinds out, the words bitter in his mouth. “I led you all into a trap.” Not just Aang and Toph, but the entire invasion force. Spirits, it was like the whole thing was designed just for him and his way of thinking. “The best thing we can do now is get out of it.”

Toph and Aang nod after a moment’s hesitation, accepting his decision in tense silence as if Sokka hasn’t just proven, in truly spectacular fashion, that his judgment can't be trusted. All that planning and he couldn’t see…anything.

Fuck, it’s just like Azula said. Which makes for one truth, at least, amidst who knows how many others, as Zuko's absence throbs like an open wound in the center of his chest.

&#45;-

“Azula really did have it all planned out,” Sokka says grimly as Appa climbs higher into the air than they were expecting to need to. The sky is full of airships and war balloons—fucking of course, how *else* can Sokka contribute to the Fire Nation’s victory today—and from this high it’s easy to see the way the invasion force is being neatly surrounded.

“We’ll have another chance, Sokka,” Toph says quietly, firmly, her grip on his arm as tight as ever as Appa banks around enemy fire.

“Let’s get out of this one first,” Sokka mutters as they tilt into a steep, sharp dive.

Appa lands into chaos, Sokka spinning to take it all in his he vaults down to the cobblestones. Fire is coming at them from above and at least two sides, their earthbenders wholly on the defensive now, trying to shield their own forces from the bombardment. And without benders focusing on pushing the enemy back the Fire Nation is advancing slowly, steadily, efficiently closing down the lines of retreat.

“Sokka!” Katara calls, dashing over to the cover of Appa’s armor-clad bulk. “What happened?” She looks at them with a mixture of anxiety and excitement and tentative hopefulness that cuts right to his raw, unprotected heart.

Aang and Toph glance away, so Sokka takes a deep breath and grinds out, “It was a trap.” The words hurt on their way out and Sokka feels like Azula’s voice is still in his ear even when she’s nowhere to be seen.

“What?” Katara gasps, her eyes sweeping them for injury.

“Azula knew we were coming,” he says, turning to eye the lines, which *do* need his attention, but mostly so he doesn’t have to see the accusation or suspicion or whatever cross her face.

“She was ready for us,” Toph puts in, subdued in a way she rarely is, expression shadowed by her helmet.

“She had everything plotted out,” Aang agrees with an uneasy glance toward Sokka, who sets his jaw and pretends he doesn’t see it or feel it like ant flies crawling over every inch of his skin.

“But I thought we—”

“She had a trap for me,” Sokka cuts in, words tight, because with even just a tiny bit of distance now he can see that all that was for him. That she set out to stop an entire invasion and messing with Sokka was the means to that end. “And I fell for it. I used up all our time.” Spirits, that Azula could *do* that to him...it makes his stomach heave. Fuck, what did she know? *How?*

Aang sidles up to his shoulder. “Sokka, it’s not your faul—”

Sokka jerks away from his extended hand, feeling like he’s about to shatter if anyone disrupts his barely-there equilibrium. “We don’t have time for this,” he says, harsh and ignoring the way Aang flinches back. “We need to get back to the beach and the ships as fast as we can.”

“Right,” Aang says quietly before straightening, new purpose in his stance. “I can provide air cover. I’ll do what I can to slow them down.”

“Appa and I will help,” Katara says, giving Sokka an uneasy glance but thankfully tucking away whatever she has to say for later.

Sokka watches them take off, vaguely wondering how long that kind of willingness to do what he says is going to last when they realize just how badly he fucked this whole thing up. Then he shoves that aside, because they’re still in this and the eclipse might be gone but they still don’t have time. He forces himself to concentrate, doing some quick mental math on the aerial forces arrayed against them and quickly realizing that the two of them won’t be enough to turn any tides, not unless Momo displays a heretofore undiscovered talent for combat.

Sokka takes a deep breath and turns back to his troops, trying to see the shape of the battlefield and the path to get them out of this foolish thing he’s led them to. Everything is falling apart around him and none of his plans accounted for anything remotely like this. Stupid, stupid, stupid. Now all he can do is try to keep it from getting worse.

&#45;-

Zuko feels all his brittle steadiness disappear from his legs again when he bursts into the prison tower to see the first guard on the ground, unconscious. For a moment he can only stare, motionless. Then he lunges for the stairs, taking them two at a time, going so fast he’s nearly dizzy from the spiral by the time he reaches the top.

They wouldn’t attack civilians or prisoners. They wouldn’t. There’d be no strategic value in it, even if the Fire Nation did it first. Sokka wouldn’t—but what if Sokka isn’t in charge? Fuck, Zuko didn’t even—And even if he is, Zuko isn’t an idiot. He *knows* what can happen to soldiers in wartime when they’re finally cut loose on those they think of as the enemy.

Agni, to think that after all this Zuko could have been wasting his time talking to the Fire Lord while Uncle*…*

It takes Zuko too many heartbeats to comprehend that Warden Poon is on the ground but alive, and that the gaping hole in Uncle’s cell looks rather like one of those blooming teas Uncle likes so much. The ones that furl outward when they hit hot water, the iron bars twisted and bent. Outward. Not—

Zuko lunges for the Warden. “*Where's my Uncle*?”

“I don’t—I—”

The man looks dazed, and he probably has a head injury, and Zuko could not give fewer fucks about that right now. He snarls, hauling Poon up and watching the man’s eyes widen in fear. “Where is Prince Iroh?”

“He’s gone!” Poon babbles. “He—he busted himself out! I don’t—he was like a one-man army!”

Zuko growls in the back of his throat, unceremoniously dropping the Warden back to the ground as fury surges through him. “He’s the Dragon of the West you fucking *fool,* and*—”* And something that sounds suspiciously like an airship crashing into another airship sounds outside the tower. Zuko doesn’t have time for this.

He doesn’t have time to explain, in exact detail, precisely how badly the Warden miscalculated. And he doesn’t have time to think about what it means that Iroh escaped on his own. Not now, when Zuko still needs to escape the city himself. But he can’t help noting, distantly, distractingly, dangerously as he dashes back down the stairs so fast he’s nearly falling, that this changes things. Changes some, and confirms others.

Zuko grimly adjusts his plans—fuck, fuck, *fuck* he’s already trying to thread the smallest of needles to begin with—and sets his feet toward the caldera’s ridge, gritting his teeth against the slow burn of sprinting uphill. This part of things, at least, doesn’t change, and Zuko can only rely on the chaos of the counterstrike for so long. He flicks a quick glance skyward, counting airships and war balloons and two swooping figures. There will still be enough time, for all of them. There has to be.

&#45;-

Sokka can’t tear his eyes away from the ground, even when they’re so far away that he can no longer pick out the specific figures as his dad and the other adults are surrounded. Appa is moving slower than usual, exhausted from battle and weighed down by armor and burdened down by fucking *children*—Spirits, how many ways could Sokka have fucked this up—so Sokka has plenty of time to watch his invasion force surrender.

He knows, in that bone-deep wrenching kind of way, that this is going to haunt his dreams once he regains the capacity to feel anything other than emotionally deadened and numb. It’s like his mind has retreated from the painful things until the hits stop coming, and because everything is a blow right now in some way, he just…can’t engage.

*This is going to hurt*, he distantly notes. *A lot*. When he stops feeling so utterly hollowed out inside, whatever rushes back into that space is going to be terrible, because *this* is struggle and anguish, self-inflicted in the worst of ways. The Southern Water Tribe has been a persistent thorn in the Fire Nation’s side, an uncatchable menace that’s come out of battle after battle miraculously unharmed. And now, because of Sokka, every single other man in the tribe will be sitting in a Fire Nation prison. And that’s the best-case outcome.

Sokka is aware, in a way that almost feels separate from his reality, that he just rather thoroughly ensured the genocide of his people. Apparently, he has a real talent for playing into enemy hands. The Fire Nation should give him a fucking medal.

He glances up when Katara finally breaks away from tending to the scrapes and cuts among their new additions, crouching in front of him with a silent offer of water and a few dried berries. He stares at the food a moment, blank, before giving a single sharp shake of his head. He can’t eat right now, not when just the sight of food and water is enough to make his churning gut give a dangerous heave.

“Sokka?” Katara pitches her voice low, worrying at her lip as she tries to examine his face. “Are you okay?”

“No.”

“…Okay.” She sits back on her heels, thankfully not pressing. “We’re going to the Western Air Temple to…figure it out.”

“Great.” More planning. Perfect.

“We should be there in a few hours,” she says gently. A few hours before he needs to be functional, she means. A few hours where Sokka doesn’t need to do anything except sit here.

Sokka almost cracks, then, under the weight of his gratitude and relief. But instead he just nods, throat clogged, and leans back as she moves on down the line to the next battle-shocked child needing a kind word and bite to eat. He closes his eyes, trying to block out the high, anxious, too-fast chattering of kids way too young for what they’ve seen trying to convince themselves that they don’t need to be afraid.

Dad was right when he said that they tasted victory today, despite how everything ended. And in exchange, they came out shredded and tattered. *Sokka* came out shredded and tattered. Spirits, he wishes they never tasted it at all if the price was going to be watching everything go up in flames around him.

&#45;-

Zuko is almost at the abandoned monsoon shelter, the one they don’t use anymore because it floods in the rain which makes it positively useless for anything except playing on clear days and getting outside of Caldera without needing to climb the ridge, when a quiet voice locks his feet in place.

“Going somewhere?”

Zuko finds Azula immediately as he glances back, the shape of her armor unmistakable as she leans in the deep doorway of a shopfront, tucked against the side so he could only see her if he looked back. Zuko gives her a quick, automatic scan for injuries but doesn’t reply yet, wary of her presence where he never expected her to be, hyperconscious of the position of his hands relative to the sword hilts over his shoulders.

“You’re always running away.” Her words are observational, unsurprised, even if her face is set with the kind of blankness that Zuko knows she rarely needs to use. Shit.

“I’m not,” he says, words quiet but firm, level. He doesn’t want this to be…whatever it could be, if he rises to her mood.

“I’ve wondered why,” she continues as if he hasn’t spoken. “Where did we go wrong, to make you never willing to stick out the hard stuff?” Her tawny eyes are flat in a way that makes Zuko nervous, in a way that belies her disinterested tone. “My theory is that it’s because you have no regard for anyone but yourself.”

“That’s not true,” Zuko protests. And why is he even bothering to engage with her when she’s like this? He knows better, even if he can’t seem to stop.

“No, I suppose you are right.” She shoves off the doorway, stepping down into the street but not closing the few strides between them. That feels…like it’s not a good sign. “You have plenty of *regard* for your peasant.”

“Azula…” He doesn’t know what to say. He never does, when it comes to Sokka.

“I was *not* impressed, Brother. He is going to get you killed.”

Zuko sags a little at her words, at the confirmation in that ‘is,’ even as his inner fire gives a tight twist of concern. Agni, if Azula thinks Sokka is a threat… “He won’t.”

“Don’t be a fool,” she snaps, a rare spark riding her words. “The degree even the *idea* of it gets out—”

“I know,” Zuko interrupts, chest clenching with reflexive anxiety over the thought. “I know.”

“And you think it won’t? After what I just saw?” She stares, incredulous, before disgusted realization flits over her face. “You just don’t care.”

“I care, Azula,” he insists, feeling the futility of the words when he can’t quite bring himself to meet her eyes while saying them.

“Just not enough,” Azula spits, expression twisting with anger as she steps closer. “I *knew* you couldn’t do it when it mattered,” she hisses, open fury boiling in her words. “I knew you wouldn’t be able to handle it. I knew it.”

“Azula, this doesn’t—it’s not—I haven’t forgotten. I haven’t—”

“Haven’t what? Haven’t *walked away*?” She snorts, derisive, throwing a hand out to encompass exactly what Zuko is doing now. “Sure. Whatever lets you sleep at night, *Brother*.”

Zuko knows that it’s pointless to protest when Azula’s mind is made up like this, but he can’t stop, can’t let it pass without trying. “Azula, it’s not—”

“Actions speak.” That shuts him up, and he can’t move as she reaches up and grabs the hairpiece out of his topknot, using her left hand so he can see the whole thing, eyes daring him to resist. “Go,” she snarls. “Play your games.”

Zuko takes a deep breath, refusing to let the sudden fall of hair into his eyes throw him. He… deserved that. “It isn’t a game.”

“*Everything* is a game, Zuko,” she spits with all the venom of someone who’s never lost in her life, who’s never allowed losing to be a viable option. “And if you don’t know that yet then you really are stupid.”

“Azula…”

“Go.” She jabs him in the chest with the sharp end of the hairpiece. “Before I change my mind. Go run off to your *peasant*. Make your choices. We’ll see who wins in the end.”
