## Chapter 10: Only Ashes

### Notes

#### Chapter Notes

No particular warnings for this one!

### Text

Walking the rest of the way on foot to the Western Air Temple feels like some kind of metaphor for their collective failure. Or it would if Sokka were feeling any less worn down around the edges to figure it out. And really, it’s not their collective failure, is it? It’s Sokka’s failure, because what exactly is The Duke responsible for here?

Appa was too tired between the armor and the extra bodies and the strain of battle to make it all the way to the Temple, and it’s a probably sign of how low the bar has become that Appa landing with a rather alarming thump rather than just falling out of the air feels like a win.

At least Aang knows the rest of the way by foot—something about foraging expeditions and learning to be at one with nature—which is one small thing to be grateful for, especially with all the kids in tow. And Sokka should really stop calling them that before he slips and says it out loud…They just all seem so *young*.

Spirits, Sokka should really find it in himself to feel some gratitude that all these kids are with him at all. That he and Toph and Aang and Katara made it to the heart of the Fire Nation and back out again with minimal physical injury. He should be relieved by that, and by how few casualties there seemed to be in general, and even by the lack of property damage they inflicted outside of military installations. Fuck, by the fact that they have the Temple to retreat to in the first place.

Sokka should be relieved by a lot of things.

But how can he feel relief, or gratitude, or anything at all, when it doesn’t feel like the invasion is actually over? When Sokka keeps rehashing it, again and again and again in his own head. Stepping minute-by-minute through the day, trying to find every place he stepped wrong—holding back Katara from the strike team—and every clue he missed—actually believing the defenses would be *that* incompetent in such a militarized nation—and all the things he failed to account for. Like an actual evacuation plan instead of an ad hoc, scrambling retreat, because Sokka knows his dad, he *knows*, so why didn’t he *realize* that for Hakoda, separating at the signs of real trouble was always going to be the first option?

Defeat is fresh and bitter in his mouth with every breath, his skin still tacky with dried sweat and dust, aches and pains flaring across his body with every step he takes and branch he shoves aside and jumble of rocks he helps Teo navigate. That should be more than enough to deal with, to have to be aware of, to occupy his focus, but still every single thing he could have done differently throbs inside his skull like the sun over the Si Wong Desert.

Sokka can hear, when he cares to pay attention to it—or when he forgets to hang toward the back because he can’t stand another iteration of The Duke’s nervous-excited recapping of the battle to Haru—that Katara and Aang are talking about what to expect when they finally reach the Western Air Temple. Regrouping, reassessing. Beginning to figure out what comes next. And Sokka knows he should be doing that too, or at least thinking about it. Every plodding step through the forest is one step closer to the moment when they’re going to need to decide what to do now that nothing has turned out how it was supposed to. He should be involving himself in the conversation. He should be up in the front with Aang, leading the way and charting the path for the others. That’s what Sokka *does*. It’s what he would have done this morning without a second thought—Spirits, he would have been the one pestering the others to think ahead.

But Sokka can’t quite bear to think of much of anything at all right now, and especially not the future. Not so soon after so spectacularly displaying, in so many ways, just how much his planning and judgment are worth.

The fact that he’s sticking near the back, that he isn’t taking charge…Sokka feels like everyone's looking at him every time he glances away. Judging him. And the intellectual part of himself might be able to repeat that it’s all in his head, that the only looks coming his way are worried, filled with concern. But the emotional part of Sokka is wrung dry in too many ways to count right now, far too much of a mess to be contained by anything so flimsy as reassurance. Sokka can’t stop thinking that they *should* be looking at him with a lot more animosity than that. That if they knew, they would be.

Because even now, trudging through the forest with only seven people, an air bison, and a lemur left of the entire assembled invasion force. Even now, with Sokka agonizing over with every step over where he went wrong and all the things he could have done differently and better to turn the tide. Even now, with the best chance they’ve ever had in one hundred years to defeat the Fire Nation thoroughly wasted. Even now, Sokka can’t stop churning over *Zuko*.

Zuko. Who didn’t help them—probably—and might not even be on their side—maybe—and either way wasn’t *there*—right?—and is a *distraction*—without question—that Sokka is realizing far too late he can’t afford. Because maybe if he wasn’t so fucking distracted by Zuko’s presence and then his absence, Sokka would have come up with a better plan in the first place. Maybe if he wasn’t so distracted by Zuko when he should have been thinking about everything else, Sokka wouldn’t have fallen for Azula’s plot and ruined the one chance they still had.

Sokka thought he had it under control. He thought he knew how to handle it, how to box away the parts of himself that he couldn't afford to indulge, to set them aside for later, but clearly he didn't have anything figured out at all. And that Sokka can’t stop agonizing over *this*, when he has so much else to agonize over—that he *should* be agonizing over—isn't that just more evidence of how badly he was fooling himself in thinking he had this handled? And if he fooled himself about this, about so much of the invasion, what else does he have wrong?

Spirits, he *hates* that he's thinking things like this. He feels like there's a pit inside of himself that's clawing to be filled with confidence, with surety, with purpose, and instead all that's there when he tries to ground himself is Azula’s voice, poisonous and sharp, offering a steady litany of things that could be truths or could be lies and either way are equally effective at eroding any surety Sokka might have tried to latch onto.

Was Zuko using him in Ba Sing Se? Sokka doesn’t think so, even if Azula implied it heavily. But what if Sokka just doesn’t *want* to think so? He can tell himself that Zuko never learned the kinds of things Azula clearly knew about the battle plan from Sokka, and he can be confident saying it, but Sokka can’t deny that Azula clearly knew things. Things about him, too*.* About *them*. But all the things she seemed to know—the caring and the softness and the reality of Sokka’s own knowing of Zuko—aren’t those the very things that Sokka looks to in order to remember that it was real? Aren’t those the very foundations of the walls he built around that fragile flame of his conviction? So for Azula to know those things—that Sokka cared and Zuko cared back—doesn’t that mean they were there for her to know in the first place? That they were true?

Or maybe Sokka is just eight steps behind, outthought at every turn once again. Because Sokka knows that believing in something doesn’t make it true. He'd like to think that Azula implying that Zuko both used Sokka for his own ends and cared about Sokka are two separate things, one clearly a lie. But he is painfully aware that they don't have to be. Fuck, he’s painfully aware that Zuko didn’t even need to *intend* them to be, for it to have turned out that way. What he and Zuko had being real doesn’t mean it still couldn’t have become something to offer up to get back into the Fire Lord’s good graces, a way to be welcomed home. Because Zuko might not have ever brought up returning home in all their time in Ba Sing Se, but Sokka remembers how desperately Zuko wanted to in the North. How desperately he felt he *needed* to. Sokka can’t quite manage to wholly believe that Zuko truly stopped caring so quickly.

But if Zuko didn’t intend to do the things Azula implied—does that mean that he’s on Sokka’s side? The Avatar’s side? Azula’s? No one’s but his own? Sokka still has no idea because Zuko wasn’t *there* and Sokka...Sokka had apparently been relying more than he ever realized on that not being true. On Zuko being there, in some capacity, in some way, to settle all the questions Sokka suddenly desperately needs answered.

Which just goes to further demonstrate how *stupid* Sokka is to have relied on something like that, even unconsciously. Because now, when he can barely trust himself to pick the right way to climb up this hill let alone successfully parse through months of interactions to the correct conclusions, all he has is Zuko’s conspicuous absence and Azula’s insidious words and Katara’s suspicions and Aang’s worry and Toph’s silence to fill that void where his confidence used to be.

That, and the thing he can’t think about. The scenario that Sokka would rather stew in the possibility of betrayal than even look at. The idea that Zuko could be—that he might be— Spirits, Sokka doesn't even want to *think* it, like somehow that might make it more true. He feels like Azula reached into his very psyche and found the thread of his sanity and is slowly, inexorably unraveling it with every step Sokka takes away from Caldera. And how long before his edges become so frayed that he can’t keep up even the semblance of being moderately functional anymore? How long before it becomes easier to feel the fury of betrayal and the ache of his own failed judgment than to consider that she might have been telling the truth about this?

Sokka can’t believe it. Doesn’t *want* to believe it. But Sokka also knows that Zuko nearly got assassinated less than a year ago in a very public, very explosive manner. And he knows that Zuko himself is aware—if you can pin him down and strip away his defenses when he’s raw and hurting enough to admit it—that he’s a problem for his father that needs solving.

And Zuko, who was—is, *is—*a ball of seething rage on a good day would have gone home at Azula’s side, without the Avatar that was the one condition of his return, and encountered… what?

Sokka can’t quite muster up the nerve—or the stomach—to try to get into the head of the man who already burned off half his son’s face, who’s still in control of Zuko’s life in so many ways, to try to truly answer that question.

And Sokka might not want to believe it but he can’t stop thinking about it, much as he would prefer to go back to ruminating on all the ways he might have been betrayed instead. It's nauseatingly within the realm of possibility, is the thing. And Azula was so hostile toward Sokka in a way that didn’t make sense. Sokka's just a supporting player in Aang’s journey, but she was so specifically angry, like he’d *done* something to her when Sokka’s barely interacted with her before. Would she really take them invading Caldera personally? And if so, why only take it out on him and not the Avatar, too? It’s almost as if—

“Sokka?”

“Huh?” He feels like he’s clawing his way out of a fog to pull his attention back to Katara. Spirits, he needs this day to end.

“We’re here,” she says, gentle in a way that makes his skin itch even though Sokka knows he can’t really handle anything else right now.

“Okay,” he says after a beat, trying to marshal his sluggish thoughts toward anything remotely productive. “Great.”

—it’s almost as if Azula were resentful of Sokka. Which doesn’t make a lick of sense, because the only thing Azula might have to be resentful of is something related to Zuko. And Sokka's far too familiar with the number of scars Zuko wears that prominently feature Azula in their acquisition to be able to make sense of that. Especially not when Sokka doesn’t have any faith left inside himself for his own ability to reason his way to the right answers. Not anymore. And especially not when he’s talking about a person and not a battle plan.

&#45;-

Exploring the Western Air Temple is something that Sokka recognizes he would normally be into. There’s the history, the remnants of a past battle—though less than Sokka would have expected—the engineering it took to ensure that the base of this vertigo-inducing inverted pyramid is strong enough to support everything beneath it.

Sokka *should* be into it all. He just…isn’t. He can’t seem to register more than a remote interest in the architecture and a faint annoyance at how windy everything is. Which makes sense, because Air Temple, he just—wishes a lot of things right now.

At least it seems like a well-fortified position for them to camp out in, for once, instead of a random cave or hilltop or lakeside. Not that the Fire Nation hasn’t successfully attack it before, of course...Fuck.

Sokka wanders from room to room, vaguely noting which areas seem suitable for sleeping or training, which parts seem like maybe they should keep the younger kids elsewhere if they don’t want anyone plunging through the floor. He’s restless now that they’re here and he doesn’t have putting one step in front of the other to focus on. Some of his numb shell is starting to slide away without that single, manageable physical activity to focus on, and Sokka isn’t ready to deal with the weight of everything pressing against it.

“Sokka.”

He stops, turning to find the source of his name and realizing that he’s come to a wide, open plaza without being entirely sure of how he got here, which…is really not good, when every left turn here plunges you off a cliff.

“Help me cook dinner if you’re going to just wander,” Katara says, eyes flashing up and then back down too quick for him to read.

He hesitates, recognizing that the request is out of character for her. She’ll let Sokka help if he asks, but she almost never seeks assistance over the small set of tasks she considers hers. But his feet take him slowly over to her fire anyway, unable to resist the lure of something mindless to get lost in.

“Here,” she says, pushing a paring knife into his hands and jerking her head toward one of their supply bags. “Prep those.”

Sokka obeys without speaking, because if he speaks then he might need to engage with the layers and layers of emotion he can hear simmering underneath her terse words. Things that sound like worry and upset and ‘I told you so’ and recrimination and disappointment. Though maybe Sokka’s projecting, with some of those.

Feeding basically double the people is going to be tough, he realizes, as he looks at what has to be nearly a quarter of their supplies going into one. They should have had food stashed away somewhere for a quick resupply, but, well—Sokka didn’t really plan for an after that involved more than just themselves but not everyone else. Another oversight.

He glances up when Katara mutters something beneath her breath, taking in the tight press of her lips as she handles her half of the prep, the furrow between her brows, the constant darting of her eyes around the space as the sounds of the others exploring drifts in and out on the wind.

She’s clearly focused on getting their suddenly much bigger band through the night, and maybe Sokka would have thought to have supplies cached somewhere if he’d focused more, too. If he hadn’t let himself get distracted by things that aren’t supposed to matter, not in the grand scheme of things. Maybe Katara wouldn’t look so worn right now if he’d just…done better.

They’re both bent over their respective tasks when she finally speaks, low enough that Sokka can only hear because the wind has momentarily died down. “What happened?”

He takes a deep breath, eyes tracking the path of his little knife over the melon squash. He should sharpen it soon. He can feel that it’s just starting to catch, to require a little extra effort to get the job done. It wouldn’t do for someone to push too hard one do and slip.

“Sokka.”

“I already said, Azula was ready for us,” Sokka says without looking up. “She knew we were coming. That *I* was coming.” He can feel the way that admission hangs in the air. “What more do you want?”

“I want to know what happened.”

Sokka feels a sharp, wild, pained flare of anger and at least has the sense left to still his knife. “What do you want, a play-by-play of my failure?”

“No,” Katara says, audibly annoyed. “I want to know why you’re acting like this.”

“Well, how about the invasion I’ve been planning for months, the one that was supposed to win us the war, not only didn’t work but got basically our entire resistance captured! Including all the men in our tribe and our *Dad*, and—”

“So it’s because of Dad?”

Sokka stutters to a halt. “What?”

“Why you’re so upset,” Katara says, like Sokka is a particularly obtuse polar bear dog. “Is it because of Dad?”

He just stares, feeling struck dumb and more than a little overwhelmed by the idea of all that he’s feeling could be boiled down to one single reason. To a single *word*, something as—as *measly* as *upset.*

“Sokka,” Katara sighs. “I’m not—I wouldn’t be surprised if you were angry, okay? I—I know you worked hard on the plan, and it didn’t—I wouldn’t be surprised if you were beating yourself up for that. But you’re…” She searches for words before visibly bracing herself and plunging forward. “You’re acting like you did after the Fire Festival,” she says heavily, fingers twisting in the fabric of her dress as she waits for him to deny it. “So please, just. What happened?”

Spirits, is it going to get easier or harder to talk about with distance? His chest shudders under the idea that it could feel harder than this. “Azula…said stuff. To mess with me. To waste time.”

“And it worked.”

The quiet words aren’t a question, but Sokka answers anyway, as if they aren’t all aware. “It worked," he says, staring grimly down at the melon squash still in his hands.

“…What things?”

Sokka blows out a hard breath, fingers turning white around the melon squash. “Just—*stuff*, okay, just—what does it even matter, it’s not like—”

“Hey,” Katara cuts in, startling him into looking up at her with the hardness of her words. “This isn’t done, okay? We’re still here, Aang's still here, Sozin’s comet *isn’t* here. This isn’t the end. And you’re acting like—like everything is gone and done already,” she snaps, gesturing with her knife in a way that has Sokka sitting up straight in alarm. “You didn’t let me sit and wallow after Jet, or Hama, or ever once in my entire life, while you always go off and brood in the corner like you’re in some two-copper romance sheet. So if you think I’m going to sit back and let you drown in whatever’s going on in your head right now? Then you’ve got another thing coming.” She brandishes her bitter potato for emphasis, and Sokka isn’t entirely sure that she isn’t going to throw it at him. “What. Is. Wrong.”

Sokka stares at her glare, at the white-knuckled grip she has around her paring knife, and swallows hard, finally marshaling himself to actually engage with what’s in front of him for the first time since Appa left Caldera behind. “She—” He clears his throat and tries again. “She said things like—that Suki was captured. And tortured. And…implied that Zuko tortured her.” He takes a steadying breath that doesn’t do much of anything, licking dry lips and cutting his eyes away from her. “And that he was—that’s how she knew about the plan, and—everything. That Zuko—that he was using me.” He can hear the way his voice is wavering, feel it, but can’t make it stop. “Or that I was using him. That…” He reaches for words, fiddling with the wraps back on his wrist because it’s not like they need to be in disguise anymore, and Sokka couldn’t get the armor off himself fast enough.

“That?” Katara carefully prompts, reining back his wandering thoughts.

Sokka is choking on the words, has been ever since they formed. “That Zuko might be— might be dead.” It’s like a knife, sliding neatly between his rubs and then digging in, twisting, tearing. “And that I—that they killed him because of—” *Get it out*. He just needs to get it out once and then he never has to say it again. He can do it. Once. Just once. “—me,” he gasps, fingers clenched so hard around his own wrists that he distantly registers that he’s going to have bruises. “Because of me.”

“Oh, Sokka,” Katara says softly, shoulders slumping, sounding sad in the way you’re sad when a kid breaks something you told them not to be too rough with and now they’re crying because it’s gone.

Sokka just bends his head, hiding his face as much as he can sitting in front of a fire with his hair pulled back. He’s desperately glad that no one else is around for this. That if it had to happen it could be just her. The collective pity is already more than he can deal with, any more of it...

Katara eventually picks her knife back up, pulling her pile of bitter potatoes back toward her, finally asking without looking up, “Do you believe her?”

They both know he wouldn’t be so thrown if the answer was ‘no.’ “The stuff she said,” he finally whispers, “It wasn’t all lies.”

Katara hesitates, then nods, and after a moment presses another melon squash into his hands before retreating to her side of the fire. Sokka gratefully accepts the out, the excuse to hide himself even a little bit after peeling himself so wide open. He feels hollow now that he isn’t keeping what happened locked inside, empty-handed almost, like the weight of keeping it contained was all he had to keep himself upright and now he’s…bereft.

Which doesn’t make sense, because the plan was never meant to end with them carrying away anything more than they came with. They just weren’t supposed to leave with nothing.

&#45;-

After dinner Haru, Teo, and The Duke head off to do more exploring at Haru’s suggestion, Hari casting the four of them left around the fire a quick, understanding look as he rallies the others. Maybe he isn’t as much of a kid as Sokka thinks of him as, even if his weird thin mustache makes him look like a child playing dress-up. Shit, he’s probably older than Sokka is, now that Sokka’s stopping to think about it.

Sokka contemplates that strange reality until their new additions disappear out of earshot, leaving the four of them to discuss…everything. What comes next. Except no one seems to want to break the silence, which stretches tense and tight and full of awkward looks and uncomfortable glances and prickly discomfort and so much blame that Sokka thinks he might drown in it.

Finally, Aang can’t take it anymore.

“Let’s just acknowledge,” Aang says, arms wrapped around his knees and voice firm. “That today *sucked*. It didn’t go how we wanted.” He waits for anyone to comment, but no one's going to challenge him on that. “And now we need to just move forward. There’s no use in wallowing in things we can’t change,” he finishes, not looking at Sokka who still takes the comment like a personally addressed letter.

Sokka opens his mouth, reconsiders, shuts it, grits his teeth, gives himself a quick ‘man up and fix it' pep talk, and finally manages to grind out, “Fine.”

No one else says anything—apparently, no one else feels the need to also agree, which is *just* *fine*—until Katara steps into the noticeable gap of Sokka’s silence to get things started. “So what are our options?”

“Assassins,” Toph says promptly.

“We’re already dealing with one of those,” Katara says tartly. “I don’t think we want another.”

Toph isn’t one to let an idea go easy. “Maybe they could fight each other.”

“The original plan,” Sokka says before things devolve before they even get going, feeling like he needs to drag the words out of himself. “It was always for Aang to master all the elements and face the Fire Lord that way.”

“But Sozin’s Comet is coming in the summer! It’s spring!”

And already partway through, Sokka thinks. But what he says is, “Well, you got water and earth in a few months each.”

“Don’t we need a Master for that, though?” Toph asks. “Do we even know a firebender?”

The silence is deafening, everyone not-looking at Sokka with a kind of fixed determination that might as well be outright staring.

“One that Snoozles isn’t pining over,” Toph clarifies just before Sokka gets up and throws himself off the edge of this temple.

At least she said what everyone else was thinking. Sokka doesn’t engage with it, doesn’t know how he would at this point, and Toph shoots a quick, tense look in his direction, her bare feet shifting over the cobblestones.

“Jeong Jeong?” Katara suggests.

“That guy was awful,” Sokka mutters.

Toph shrugs. “If he was a Master and isn’t on the Fire Nation side…”

“He taught Aang to be afraid of fire already,” Sokka bites out. “So he did a real bang-up job to start.”

“Maybe it’s worth trying again,” Katara says gamely, as if she didn’t get burned last time bad enough to put Aang off firebending permanently. As if that whole experience wasn’t a disaster for all three of them, in so many ways.

“We can find someone else,” Sokka insists, restlessly picking at the end of his wrist wraps.

“How are you going to do that?” Toph asks, and it isn’t even particularly challenging, seems genuine, but Sokka can feel himself floundering anyway.

“The Colonies, or—I don’t know, just—” Fuck, he’s feeling so exposed and picked apart just with that innocuous question. There’s no way he can deal with having his plans interrogated right now. And Spirits, this isn’t even a plan, just an idea.

Katara sighs and shoves her hair back from her face, looking like she’s marshaling herself before saying with surprising gentleness, “Just because you want it to be Zuko doesn’t mean we can turn away the only option we have.”

Sokka flinches. She’s right, like always. He *does* want that, even though he’s never bothered to put the want into words before. But still, even if he sets that aside—laughable, to think he could—his instincts are screaming that Jeong Jeong isn’t the right choice. Not that Sokka can’t trust those anymore, either. But he still says, “We don’t even know where Jeong Jeong is, so I wouldn’t exactly call him an option yet.”

“You can’t hold out for—”

“I’m *not* holding out, I *told* you what—what Azula said. I’m not—I’m not *waiting*.”

There’s a moment where everyone clearly tries to figure out how to respond, and Sokka wishes he could just hide his face behind his hands and never have to meet anyone’s eyes ever again. Never have them look at him. This conversation is supposed to be practical and action-oriented and about saving the world and instead Sokka can’t stop spewing his messy emotions all over the place.

“Sokka—”

“It’s fine,” he cuts in, pressing the heels of his hands against his eyes. “Just—drop it.” He doesn’t want to become the topic of conversations, *can’t* become the topic of conversation. Not when he isn’t ready or willing to admit that he’s clinging with everyone he has to the thin grace in Azula’s jumbled use of ‘is’ and ‘was’ and ‘will.’

“…Iroh,” Toph suggest into the silence, and Sokka's too worn thin holding back everything else to keep in the angry hiss that slides past his teeth. The anger papers over some of his fragile edges, and it feels good and comfortable and safe to let himself be mad instead of everything else.

Toph lets out a huff of annoyance. “I don’t get why you don’t like him.”

“Take a *guess*,” he snaps.

Aang shoots to his feet before Toph can snipe back, getting up so abruptly that Momo nearly slides off his shoulder. “I’m going to clear my head.”

Katara is on her feet now too. “Aang—”

“It’s fine, Katara. It’s—I just want some space,” Aang says, already striding away a touch too fast to really sell being ‘fine.’ But then, Sokka isn’t going to judge. Aang snaps his glider open and dives off the edge of the plaza into the open air—which will never not be unsettling —to leave Sokka and Katara and Toph behind in sudden silence except for the whistling wind swirling over the Temple’s open edges.

Katara slowly finds her seat again, foot tapping as she stares after Aang. “So…what are we going to do?”

Sokka sighs, his combativeness deflating with Aang’s departure, and starts wracking his brain for everything he knows about the Fire Nation and firebending. Which really isn’t a lot, even if it’s more than the rest of them. Sokka knows Zuko’s meditative breathing decently well… maybe Aang could figure out how to convert that into something having to do with fire? And Sokka can add a lot of inappropriate-sounding things about control and release, which he would prefer not to…Could they find some scarf dancers like the ones from the Fire Festival? And hope that Aang can somehow translate the movements into live bending?

None of these things really feel like the foundation of a solid plan. But then, Sokka isn’t trying to put a plan together. Just ideas. Someone else can stitch them into a path forward.

“This would be easier,” Toph finally grumbles. “If we knew where anyone *was*. Iroh, Jeong Jeong, Sparrowkeet—” She ticks the names off on her fingers, and Sokka’s heart turns over. “—It doesn’t matter if they’d help or not if we have no clue where any of them are.” Sokka appreciates the built-in assumption, there, that Azula was just lying.

“We don’t have time to look for long, either” Katara says, trying not to sound grim and mostly failing.

“Maybe Piandao…” Sokka says before he can catch himself.

Katara frowns. “The sword maker?”

“He…might know someone.” Sokka almost immediately wants to pull the words back, but he knows that between Katara and Toph he won’t be able to just drop it now. But going to Piandao would mean relying on Sokka’s ability to judge the Master’s personality, to read between the lines of things said and implied and inferred, with no real ability to sit someone down and explain it all so they can tell him if he’s being crazy or not. “He knew I was Water Tribe, and he knew about the Avatar, and he still helped me.”

Toph chews that over. “Is he an ally, then? Or just neutral?”

Sokka shrugs, feeling helpless. “He seemed friendly enough.”

“'Friendly enough’ is our standard now?” Katara mutters, sour but not necessarily disagreeing with the idea.

“Friendly enough and we know where he is? Sounds like the best we can get right now,” Toph says decisively, and thank the Spirits one of them is, or else they might be here all night. “Let’s go find Aang.”

&#45;-

They coax a reluctant Appa into helping them find Aang because Air Nomad architect is a nightmare for actually trying to get from one point to another with any efficiency. Sokka shudders to think what Water Tribe society would be like if they were all waterbenders too— probably doing dumb shit like living in bubbles beneath the sea, or only traveling by wave. Earthbenders would be exactly like they are now, or else they would go full underground-dwelling badger mole people. And firebenders…well, the Fire Nation already has islands that seem to be primarily full of flammable things.

They finally find Aang topside, riding thermals near the overhanging cliff edge that forms the base of the inverted temple. He matches the orange-streaked evening summer sky rather well and they settle in to watch him by silent agreement. It’s a graceful sight, really, the banks and turns and lazy dives. Sokka thinks they could all probably use a moment to appreciate something simple and beautiful after this never-ending day they’ve had. Aang will come to them when he’s ready.

Sokka is letting himself think about nothing but how Aang on his glider puts him in mind of Hawky at his finest, when Aang suddenly falls out of a wide turn, arrowing down toward them and shouting something that’s immediately carried away by the wind. His urgency is unmistakable, though, and there’s no way he was struck by a sudden desperate need to chat about their plans.

Sokka and Katara scramble to their feet, scanning for threats in the sky, Toph dropping the ball of clay she’d been snapping into different shapes just as Aang hits the ground. He’s glaring past them, his glider swinging forward in blatant threat just as a throat clears behind them.

“Uh—hello. Um.”

Sokka freezes still facing the canyon. His entire body locks down at that familiar rasping voice that can’t actually be what he heard. It can’t be. Because he cannot be *here* of all places, not when he wasn’t *there*, he can’t—

Is it possible to brood so much that you start hallucinating the object of your unwilling obsession?

“Zuko, here.”

Or maybe Sokka just dropped dead from the stress of it all, and this is what’s greeting him in the afterlife.

&#45;-

Zuko eyes the Avatar’s tense, openly hostile posture and wonders if getting blown into a canyon to his death at this stage of things would be an ironic way to go or cathartic or just a fitting one. Maybe all three, depending on who was asked.

*Don’t get ahead of yourself*.

“I, uh—you’re probably wondering why I’m here,” Zuko starts, reaching for his prepared words and already acutely aware that he’s flubbing it. Sokka still hasn’t turned around, but his shoulders look painfully tight, his stance unnaturally still, and Zuko’s heartbeat wasn’t exactly slow before but now…Agni’s balls, he isn’t here for Sokka, he needs to focus, he just…needs to know that he’s okay. It takes every bit of control Zuko has not to let his heat sense sweep outward now that he can feel the press of Sokka’s almost-fire against it.

“We might be,” Katara says, cuttingly sarcastic like it was a dumb thing to say in the first place, which…okay, yeah, it probably was, but Zuko had needed a general opener since he couldn’t keep all his situation-specific introductions straight.

“Okay, well, um, I…” Zuko trails off as the sky bison suddenly lumbers over. He’s just as big as Zuko remembers, his fur looking healthier than last time Zuko saw the thing though it’s still matted and dirty. From battle, Zuko supposes.

Zuko eyes the creature, nearly vibrating with the need to get himself out of crushing range but refusing to let himself be scared away so easily, if that’s what this is. Or is it some kind of test? Or fuck, does he need to respect the sky bison’s personal space? The animal is eyeing him back—should Zuko step away? Or forward, to show confidence? Is Zuko blocking his way somehow? Fuck, is he being rude to the Avatar’s spirit companion?

Appa suddenly huffs, hard enough that Zuko needs to squint against the force of it as the hair is blown back off his face. Then the creature leans forward and…licks him. Twice. Wetly. With a tongue as big as a medium sized child. From mid-thigh to the top of his head, so that Zuko’s hair slaps back down against his face after, which just—

Zuko…didn’t bring enough clothes for this. Not if it’s a regular thing that Sokka just failed to ever mention.

Zuko squints his unscarred eye back open when nothing else gigantic and slimy touches him to see Appa lumbering away, somehow conveying satisfaction through all that fur. He blinks open his other eye, shifting his attention back to see the Avatar with his staff dropping slightly in surprise and Katara gaping and Sokka…Sokka turned partway around at some point and now he's giving Zuko a quick head-to-toe, his face weirdly still, and oh, Agni’s tits, Zuko is…he was already dirt-streaked and now he’s *covered* in sky bison spit, tacky and slimy and borderline snotty and—

“Keep talking,” Katara orders, openly suspicious like Zuko's somehow tricking the sky bison or something into licking him, which—ugh.

“Right, okay, um.” Can he wipe the spit off his face at least? Would that draw too much attention to what just happened? Is it worse to act like it didn’t happen at all and just…drip? “I…” Fuck, what was he supposed to say at this part again? “I want to join you guys.” Zuko tries not to stare at Sokka when he says it. He's aware that he fails.

For an agonizingly long stretch no one reacts, and Zuko can’t even keep time by counting his heartbeats because they’re coming so fast. Did he—did he not actually say it out loud? Should he—

“You want to *what* now?” The smaller girl—*Toph, he knows that, use it. Show that he* *listened*—finally demands, digging into her ear with a finger.

“Join you,” Zuko repeats, shifting uncomfortably. He didn’t practice needing to do that. “To be, um, on your side. In the, uh. You know. The war.”

Sokka suddenly makes a sound in the back of his throat like he’s dying, jerking himself half away so that Zuko can barely see a third of his bowed face, shoulders hunched like he wants to hide even that. Zuko steps forward on instinct, inner fire snapping to anxious, protective attention over anything that would make Sokka sound like that, only to stumble back as Katara rounds on him with a glare of warning.

“You can’t possibly think that we could trust you,” Katara growls, laying a hand on Sokka’s arm, and Sokka doesn’t shrug it off, doesn’t protest, and for a moment Zuko can only stare at that, can only hear Sokka’s telling silence. “After everything you’ve done?”

Zuko flounders for his script again, trying to *focus* when it suddenly feels like all he can pay attention to are Sokka’s arms folded tightly over his chest, the bow of his head, the thin sliver of a clenched jaw. Agni, Zuko’s here to prove himself to them, not for—he needs to get it together. “I—I know that I’ve made mistakes. In the past. And—”

“Oh, *mistakes*?” Katara’s glare burns, and fuck, the decision to leave his armor behind is suddenly feeling less like symbolism and more like stupidity. “Like attacking our village? And burning down Kyoshi Island? And stealing my mother’s necklace? And—”

“That didn’t—the whole island—I didn’t *steal* it,” Zuko says, inner fire trying to rise in response to her tone and shit, shit, he can hear himself failing at keeping his own tone conciliatory, deferential. “I *found* it, and I didn’t know—”

“—trying to kidnap Aang, and nearly getting him *killed* in the snow, and *fighting me on your* *sister’s side in Ba Sing Se*? And now you want to join us? Do you think we’re stupid?”

“I’m different now!” Zuko swallows back the urge to plead, because Katara—he doesn’t think that will work with Katara. But he doesn’t know what will, because Zuko thought—he wasn’t prepared for her to be the only one—he thought the others would—

He doesn’t know. Zuko doesn’t know what he expected.

“I’ve changed,” he says, trying to find some of his composure again. “That isn’t who I am anymore.”

“That’s who you were two months ago!”

“I wasn’t—”

“What?” She snarls. “*What?* You think you can just run around hurting people and using them when it’s convenient, and then expect them to turn around and welcome you with open arms?”

Zuko can’t take his eyes off her hand still on Sokka’s arm. “That’s not—I don’t—” Is that what Sokak thinks? Is that what he’s told them? Zuko is suddenly dizzy, spiraling at the edges, chest tight as he scrambles to find all the careful words he practiced over and over and over. “I’ve shown—”

“How? How have you shown *anything*?”

“I—I helped an Earth Kingdom family whose son was being conscripted, and—”

“Which, conveniently, no one can prove,” she says, words acid.

“I freed your sky bison! In Ba Sing Se! From the Dai Li, beneath the lake.” Zuko sees that ripple through them and tries not to let himself hope. “I—I didn’t only do bad things. I didn’t," Zuko says, his eyes sliding toward Sokka without his permission. Sokka, who still isn’t looking at him, and Zuko knows it’s a mistake to look like this. He isn’t here for Sokka, he’s here to help the Avatar and he needs them to believe that. He can’t have them think—not if they already think he *uses—*

Oh, but seeing Sokka again? Finally being able to look instead of just remember? To feel that core of heat within him, maybe too-fast and maybe too-thready but undeniably *there*? Everything in Zuko is ready to kindle to life the moment he lets it have even a spark to catch against.

“Why?” Katara challenges, and he forces his attention back to where it’s supposed to be. “To get in our good graces? Planning a few months ahead again?” Her hand tightens protectively on Sokka’s arm and Sokka still doesn’t shake it off, doesn’t move, and does he think—Agni’s *cock*, what if Katara didn’t tell him after Ba Sing Se? Or far more likely, what if Zuko miscalculated in thinking that Sokka would understand, in believing that Sokka was one of those few people who still heard the things Zuko couldn’t say directly?

The other girl—Toph, *Toph*—suddenly shifts her weight, a look of intense concentration on her face. “*Was* there a plan? With Appa?”

“I—” Agni, Zuko has no idea what to say, can feel the panic trying to worm its way down his spine, the anxiousness trying to fog thoughts that need to be sharp. “I wasn’t—no it was just —it was the right thing to do.” Zuko’s inner fire drops, his words wavering just a little. And maybe the others will hear it as anxiety or nerves, but all Zuko can see is the way Sokka’s hair swings as his head twitches further away. Sokka knows the sound of Zuko telling a half-truth, and Zuko still isn’t wholly sure he can explain to himself, let alone anyone else, why he did what he did underneath that lake.

“What’s different?”

Zuko startles, eloquently offering a “Huh?” as he jerks his attention back to the entire group and Katar's cold, cold stare. He thinks Katara might be trying to have a very different conversation than the one they seem to be having, and Zuko—he needs that to be wrong. Agni, he can barely handle the one he planned for, and he desperately hopes he isn't visibly reeling right now. He strongly suspects that he is.

“What’s different,” the Avatar repeats, tone cautious and every single bit of his body language wary. “You’re saying you’ve changed. Okay. Then what changed between today and yesterday?” His gray eyes flicker in the direction Appa wandered off in. “Between today and Ba Sing Se?”

“I…” Zuko briefly considers laying it all out, the whole plan in all its wild dreaming, all its desperate hoping. But he isn’t entirely sure he can articulate it in a way that would make sense, that wouldn’t make him seem insane, not without explaining years and years of history. Which…he doesn’t know if he can do under Katara’s hostile eyes. And they already don’t trust him, so what would even be the point? Especially when they aren't asking about what's next. They're asking about the past, and now. “I’m not who I was when I crashed into your village. Or when I chased you around. I’ve…I’ve changed since the North.” Since before the North, really, but it's already hard enough to reveal himself this much when every instinct he has is screaming at him to keep everything tight and close and guarded if he wants to stay safe. “I’ve traveled, and I’ve learned. And grown, and…And I want to help.”

“I’ve heard those things before,” Katara says, voice and face hard. “And you might be full of pretty words, but actions speak louder.”

Zuko wants to laugh, not in a good way, hearing the echo of Azula in her rejection. At the idea that he’s ever had *pretty words* anywhere in him. And Agni, at the fact that they’re all talking around the existence of Zuko-and-Sokka as if they aren’t fully aware of it thrumming beneath all of the cut-off words and quick glances and sharp gestures and the way Zuko can’t keep his eyes off him.

It all makes Zuko feel uncomfortably frantic as he turns to the Avatar, his inner fire twisted in his chest. “You said that you thought we could be friends, once. So that—you must have thought there was good in me.”

The Avatar’s face is serious, unreadable, as he agrees, “Once.” The airbender stares for an endless heartbeat before turning to the others. “We’ll vote, then. We’ve all heard what Zuko has to say. And we’ve all been there for most of it. More or less. So we all get a vote, and—”

“I can’t,” Sokka suddenly gasps, the first words Zuko’s heard from him in months and for a moment he can’t even register what they are. “I can’t,” Sokka repeats, shaking his head in sharp denial and stepping back so that Katara’s hand finally falls away, and Zuko *definitely* hears the words this time. “I can’t,” he says again, and Zuko’s heart finally stops pounding in favor of going utterly, wrenchingly still. “I can’t. Toph—” Sokka shoots her a wild-eyed look, words edged in desperation.

“Shit balls,” Toph mutters before stepping forward, shoulders going back. “Alright,” she says, manner brusque. “Sokka doesn’t get a vote and he doesn’t get to speak.”

…What? Zuko gapes, inner fire doing—he doesn’t even know what this is.

"Toph, what—"

“No questions, it's already done. Everyone else, go.”

Zuko…doesn’t understand. He doesn’t get what’s going on, why Sokka wouldn’t get to speak, why Sokka wouldn’t *want* to get to speak. He can only stare, because now that Sokka’s spoken Zuko can’t look away even as his ears ring with the sound of Katara’s condemnation and Toph’s neutral equivocation and Aang’s slow, regretful finality.

And through it all Sokka listens and breathes like it hurts and bows his head a little lower with each word and silently nods like it aches to move when the answer is no, and never speaks another word the entire time. Zuko feels it hitting him but abstractly, numbly, like from a distance. Like he’s watching one of the few things tethering him to the earth slowly burn away as is too far away to stop it. Like the tether’s *been* gone and Zuko's only just noticing now that he’s drifting away. Even though Zuko knows—he *knows*—that it was never supposed to be just one thing keeping the ground solid beneath his feet.

&#45;-

Sokka can’t look at Zuko, can’t listen to anything he has to say, can’t handle any of this fucking decision-making when all his thoughts, his entire *being*, are still reeling from the fact that Zuko is alive, alive, alive. Alive and unhurt, from the brief glance Sokka had of him. Alive and half-covered in Appa-spit. Alive and wanting to join them. Alive and saying he’s changed. Alive and here and fulfilling every one of Sokka’s useless daydreams he’ll barely even admit to himself that he has, even with the tiny fact that he’s alive and here but not for Sokka.

Even without looking, though, Sokka can still feel Zuko’s eyes like a touch on his skin, can feel the banked heat of him even across this distance, like Sokka is a magnet attuned to Zuko’s true north, and he just—can’t. Because Zuko is alive, but that still leaves...everything else. Zuko is alive, alive, alive and here and that doesn’t mean that Zuko can’t be playing them, that Zuko isn’t working with Azula, that Zuko isn’t showing up right when Sokka is at his lowest as stage three or four or who knows how many of the Use Sokka to Fuck Over the Avatar plan.

And Sokka *wants* it, wants it so much, wants what Zuko is offering like it is tailor-made for Sokka, and he can't help but be wary of that because Sokka's wanted things badly before. Things like a quick end to the war, and look where that got them.

And fuck, Sokka doesn’t—he doesn’t really think that. Not really, even if it would be easy to. Even if maybe he should, even if Katara clearly does, Sokka still can’t make something like that make sense, the idea that Zuko would use him that way. That Zuko would be someone who *could* use a person that way. But Spirits, Sokka can't deny that it feels safer right now to think those things than to try to contend with the sudden reality crashing down on him right now and everything that comes with it.

Zuko is here, alive and apparently well. And it's like that single moment of relief at seeing Zuko safe wholly fractured the fragile shell that was allowing Sokka to function, and now he’s drowning under just how real the possibility was that Zuko could have been dead. Zuko isn't dead but he *could have been.* In Ba Sing Se, on his way back to the Fire Nation, at his father’s hand or his sister’s, or at no one’s at all, maybe just an accident. Or a convenient ‘accident,’ or fuck, maybe just as regretable collateral damage in the battle that no one had time to notice and that Sokka wasn’t around to see.

Sokka can’t look at Zuko without seeing him dead in so many ways, can’t deal with him being here alive without feeling the sharp realization of just how truly unlikely that outcome actually was in the grand scheme of things, even if it was the only outcome Sokka could accept. And now that Sokka isn’t suspended in the agony of not knowing—because fuck, Sokka wouldn’t have *known*, he would have *never* known, who would have ever told him? *Azula?*—the true horror of what could have been is sweeping through him and taking what little sense of stability and judgment Sokka had left, and Sokka just—can’t.

So he stays out of it.

Sokka stays out of it when Zuko’s shoulders cave in like their rejection has punched him in the chest, watching out of the corner of his eye because he can’t bear to not see—not again, not so soon—but he also can’t bear to look at Zuko headlong, not when he doesn’t know what his face will reveal. Not when Sokka doesn’t even know if he’d be able to hold himself back when it’s already taking everything he has not to cross the few paces between them, but he *has* to hold himself back right now. Doesn't he? But his heart still flips when he sees Zuko’s shoulders suddenly stiffen, his back straightening and face going tense with the kind of reckless resolve you get when you have nothing left to lose, the kind that Zuko used to wear all the time when Sokka first knew him. The newly long hair falling into Zuko's face might soften his scar, but it does nothing to soften the determination that settles over his expression.

“If you won’t have me as your ally,” Zuko rasps out, suddenly kneeling down out of nowhere in that graceful way of his, *bowing*, raising his hands in surrender. “Then please take me as your prisoner. I’ll accept—whatever you deem necessary.”

Sokka’s going to be ill. He’s going to be sick seeing Zuko abase himself like that, hearing Zuko so easily offer himself into the hands of people who just fucking *said* they view him as an enemy. The gesture came so easily, so *naturally*, like it's nothing for Zuko to make himself small and vulnerable for those who have no reason to treat him kindly. Like it's nothing to throw himself at the mercy of silence and regretful neutrality.

It’s a good thing that everyone's staring at Zuko right now and that Zuko's staring at the ground because Sokka doesn’t know what his face is doing right now but he’s pretty sure it’s nothing good. Sokka is used to seeing Zuko on his knees in a totally different context, lit from the inside out and magnetic with it, and this…this is wrong. Bad. Not how it's supposed to be. He wants to run forward and tug Zuko to his feet and—

“How stupid do you think we are,” Katara spits. “You actually think we’d bring a viper rat like you with us?”

Sokka cringes from her tone, half-turning in protest before he even realizes he’s moving, and then she's restlessly popping the cork off her water skin and Zuko is on his feet and scrambling backward, covering ground with the kind of jerky responsiveness that speaks of nearly-instinctive fear.

Definitely, Sokka is going to be sick after this.

Katara bends a threatening strip of water into her hands, the setting sun at her back casting her whole face into ominous shadows. “Go.”

Zuko recoils but doesn’t step away, visibly bracing himself. “I’m just—I’m trying to explain.”

“And I want to listen,” Aang says regretfully, shaking his head. “But I don’t know how we can trust you, not so soon after—everything.”

Zuko goes white, scar stark, eyes sliding to Sokka and they’re not even begging, just silently looking for confirmation. *Expecting* confirmation, and Sokka can’t move, can’t respond, because he needs to stay out of it, needs to go back to the Fire Nation and punch Ozai or Azula or whoever took his gorgeous amazing firebender and did *this* him right in the face, needs—

“Don’t look at him.” Both of them flinch from Katara’s caustic tone. “You don’t get to look. Not anymore. You need to leave.”

Sokka can feel a protest caught in his throat, the words choking him, but after what feels like an endless amount of time Zuko finally moves, giving an infinitesimal nod, his face devastated in a way that makes Sokka *ache*. Except Sokka might feel it, but he can't act on things like that. He needs to stay out of it because if there’s ever been a time Sokka's been compromised, it’s this. So he just watches, holding back the thing trying to claw its way out of his chest that feels too much like a scream as Zuko walks away, steps heavy and shoulders slumped and clothes still matted from Appa’s spit, and Spirits, even now Sokka can’t help drinking in the fact that he looks fine, looks healthy, that he doesn’t move like he’s physically hurt even if emotionally…well, Sokka wouldn’t trust either of their emotional stability right now.

Every part of Sokka in that moment wants to run forward and haul Zuko back, to make him stay. But Sokka stays out of it, because he doesn’t know how he can trust himself to be impartial anymore, to do the right things and make the right choices. Not after today showed just how incapable Sokka actually is when the things he truly wants are on the line.
