## Chapter 11: From The Ashes

### Notes

#### Chapter Notes

Warnings for a bit more than canon typical violence in this one

### Text

Sokka would really love it if everyone would just stop so pointedly not looking at him. Not that he wants them *to* look at him, just—they came back to the campsite on Appa in silence and now they’re sitting around the fire in the falling dark in silence and Sokka feels like everyone is waiting for him to have a meltdown. And he might be on the verge of having one, but that doesn’t mean they all have to *act* like it. It’s not like them knowing that he’s an emotional wreck who couldn’t even look at Zuko, let alone interact with him, is *helping*.

Spirits, why couldn’t he *do* anything?

“Guys, are we—are we sure we aren’t making a mistake?” Aang casts Sokka a not-so-subtle anxious look, and Sokka wishes it were still dinnertime so he could be stuffing his face right now and have that as an excuse to not look anyone in the eye.

Katara snorts, tossing her hair. “By *not* trusting someone who might have already betrayed us on multiple occasions? And that’s just that we know of?”

“I mean, we don’t *know*—”

“You’re right, we don’t know,” Katara cuts in, arms folded and face set. “And if after— after *everything*—” She flicks a tight glance toward Sokka, so fast he wonders if he imagined it. “—we *still* don’t know? What does that say?”

“That Sokka and Sparrowkeet have disastrous communication skills?” Toph mutters, and Sokka just sighs because the more time passes, the more he realizes how right she is. Fuck, Sokka has heart to hearts with Aang all the time, but he finally sees Zuko and suddenly can't even *try* to communicate? When he’s spent the past months bursting at the seams with questions he ached to ask?

Fuck. Fuck.

Aang doesn’t look convinced. “I mean, we didn’t really let him explain…”

Katara looks like she’s barely holding herself back from stomping her feet the way she used to do when she was little and got overwhelmed by how mad she was. “What did you want to hear, Aang? He hurt us! The first thing he did was hurt us, and he never stopped! We don’t owe him another chance to do it again.” *Us.* Sokka wonders how much it’s really about ‘us’ right now.

“But…” Aang’s eyes dart to Sokka again. “He’s done *some* good stuff. He never tried to kill me, only, you know, capture me.” Katara snorts at that, unimpressed, which…it’s an admittedly low bar. “And he freed me when Zhao captured me,” Aang soldiers on. “And if he did free Appa…” Aang glances at Toph.

“He was telling the truth,” Toph confirms, arms wrapped around her knees. “He was telling the truth the whole time.”

“You couldn’t tell if Azula was lying,” Katara points out, and Sokka flinches at the idea of putting Zuko and Azula on the same pedestal.

“Zuko isn’t a good liar,” Sokka offers without looking away from the fire, words quiet but landing about as well as a scream would have, with the way everyone shuts up. Except Katara.

“Oh,” she says sarcastically, apparently worked up enough to unleash her protectiveness on Sokka, too. “Isn’t he?”

Sokka doesn’t reply, and after an awkward moment, Toph shifts and says, “I’ve been able to tell before, with him. Just saying. If he knows how to lie like his sister, he can turn it on and off.”

“Like that makes it better? All we have is that sometimes he does self-serving things, and—”

“But we didn’t know about Appa,” Aang interrupts, glancing around. “Right? How can it be self-serving if he didn’t tell anyone?” His gaze finally settles on Sokka, for the first time not immediately skipping away. “Did you know?”

Sokka just wants to lay down and sleep so this day can *end*, and maybe never wake up so he doesn’t have to pick all this back up tomorrow. “…No.” And that makes one more thing Zuko kept quiet, even when Sokka talked about it so often around him in those days right after. And sure, they didn’t see as much of each other after Sokka started helping Kuei and the invasion plan started to pick up in earnest and then Zuko got sick, but…why wouldn’t Zuko *say* something? And Spirits, what did Sokka do to make Zuko think he wouldn’t be heard?

“So he didn’t do it to get anything,” Aang concludes, satisfied.

“*And* he wasn’t being honest,” Katara tacks on, and no one tries to argue that deliberate omissions shouldn’t count.

Toph isn’t willing to let it drop, though. “Considering where we’re at, it might be worth considering that maybe you’re starting off a bit hostile, Katara. If we all just step back—”

“Are you trying to tell me to get over it?” Katara demands, bristling, and Sokka winces. He knows better than to engage with Katara when she gets like this unless he’s willing to fight. Taking a reasonable tone like that’s never the way to go until she’s worked her emotions out. “Because you don’t know what it’s like to be attacked by Zuko, Toph. But the rest of us do, okay?” She swings toward Aang. “Can you honestly say you don’t still have nightmares about him? Because I do.”

Sokka ducks his head at her blunt words, chest aching, body tight, just...fuck. He knew that the other’s feelings toward Zuko weren’t exactly happy-go-lucky—except, Toph, maybe, who just seemed endlessly amused. And sure, it’s not like Zuko ever spent time with them in Ba Sing Se, or trained with them, or wrote to them, or spent hours and hours making sure they were okay, but…Sokka never realized.

Sokka’s had months of seeing Zuko in the most disarming context you could see him in— frustrated by customer service but all bark and no bite, affectionate in his own way toward his uncle, vulnerable and caring, haltingly apologizing for his past and totally unaware of the things he should deserve an apology for. But the others haven’t seen Zuko as anything but an antagonist, in the North or that town with Azula or beneath the palace. To Sokka, Zuko is… so many things. But to Aang and Katara, he’s the enemy. And Sokka thought them feeling better about him and Zuko in Ba Sing Se extended to them feeling better about *Zuko*. But now he’s suddenly seeing that Sokka sleeping with Zuko is an abstract fact, for them, not a character reference.

“The salient point we are all ignoring,” Toph is saying, “Is that we need a firebending teacher. And we have a firebender offering. An *Imperial* firebender, which is no joke. Are we really going to waste our time going to Piandao and hoping he can come up with someone?”

“Wait,” Aang blinks. “What? That’s the plan?”

Sokka sighs. “Piandao knows Zuko.”

“See? We would just be right back here!”

“I thought,” Katara bites out, “That you were staying out of it.”

Sokka…doesn’t have an answer for that. He did force himself out of it, forced them all to make the decision without him. Like his judgment couldn’t be trusted, which might be true, but—Zuko was here. After so many months, Zuko was here, unharmed when he might have been dead, safe, asking to join them, like some feverish reimagining of the ice outside Agna Qel’a. What was there to *judge*?

But then, apparently Sokka is the only one who’s ever looked at Zuko and felt safe. Sokka’s dreams are full of Zuko too, but they could never be nightmares. Not before today, at least.

“Say something if you want, Sokka,” Katara presses, visibly annoyed by his withdrawal. “You’ve been saying you thought he had a plan this whole time, so why are you suddenly—”

“I thought *I* had a plan, too, Katara,” Sokka speaks over her, words rough. “It didn’t work out.” He musters a half-hearted glare for the fire. “I don’t—I don’t know, okay? I don’t know anything anymore.” And he *hates* it, hates that he doesn’t feel sure of anything except that he still wants so fucking much, which is just…absolutely useless.

“Do you think he was on Azula’s side?” Toph asks, direct and blunt.

“I can’t just—

“Yes or no. Stop squirming out of it.”

“…No.” With the way Zuko was so afraid that Azula was in Ba Sing Se, when none of them else were? When Zuko had so many opportunities that he didn’t take, and if he didn’t take them…isn’t that the same as a no?

“Do you think he was on our side?” Aang asks quietly.

Sokak sighs. “I don’t know,” he says, pressing the heels of his hands to his eyes. Sokka has no data points to answer that, not really, even if he trusted himself enough to interpret them. His internal compass—or maybe that shiver of heat in his chest that Sokka hasn’t felt in so long—points too firmly toward Zuko for any answer to that question is more than a want, a fear, a need, a speculation based only on his own longing and anxieties, belief based on things he can’t put into words. On the quiet, persistent voice that can only think to reply, ‘Don’t you want him to be, too?’

And knowing that Zuko’s so close—because Zuko definitely wouldn’t give up with just that, Sokka knows him well enough to be sure of that—and still not having answers to the questions that have been clamoring at the back of his mind for weeks and weeks and weeks? Fuck, Sokka should have made him stay. Should have gotten his shit together enough to engage when Zuko was there, to at least ask a question like a normal human being instead of being unable to function past the cacophony of delayed terror and weak-kneed relief and confusion and anxious uncertainty…

“If Zuko is on his own side, then I still don’t think we can trust that,” Katara finally says, tone daring anyone to challenge her. “If even Sokka doesn’t know what that means? Then we need to look at his actions. And he set Aang free, and he set Appa free—two things against how many fights? How many times he was on the other side?”

“He didn’t fight us in the invasion,” Toph points out.

Katara snorts. “Not getting in our way isn’t the same as helping.”

Sokka exhales slow and shaky, remembering the sight of Zuko walking away and painfully aware of just how right Katara is.

&#45;-

Sokka is sitting up in his bedroll, stiff and aching and trying to blink the grittiness that comes with no sleep from his eyes, trying to tell himself to get up and start the day—can it even count as starting, if you barely even slept? Is this just yesterday, still endless, still here, somehow even more awful?

The prospect of moving when his body feels like this after the battle is daunting, makes him preemptively brace himself against the idea of all his bruises and dull throbbing hurt flaring to life. But all of last night showed that laying in stillness with nothing to focus on but his own hazy thoughts and dragging tiredness and the sharp knot in his chest and trying to count breaths of everyone around him that were simultaneously too many and not enough—that wasn’t exactly better.

The only thing Sokka will get if he stays here is more images of Zuko’s face falling, of his shoulders slumping, of him walking away running through his mind over and over. All he’s going to think about are all the things he should have said, the things he couldn’t get out in the moment. Things like ‘wait’ and ‘stop’ and ‘I’m so happy you’re here.’ Things like ‘can we just think about this’ and ‘hold on’ and ‘I’m so stupidly grateful that you aren’t dead that I can’t even function and can I just have a moment, please.’

All Sokka’s going to do is remember over and over the way all he could do in the moment was nothing at all, for anyone. Fuck, what did they gain by sending Zuko away? Some perception of safety, at the expense of a firebending teacher for Aang? When no matter what way Sokka looks at it, even with Azula’s voice still whispering in his ear, he can’t see how sending Zuko away could have possibly made anything safer for anyone.

And why can Sokka only think of these things now? Where was all of this last night? Spirits, he spent the night aching with things to say to Zuko, but how would he even say them? It’s not like he knows where Zuko is, other than around. It’s not like he has Hawky like back at the beginning of it all.

So. He might as well get up. And in the end, it only takes four words from Katara to go from lethargic and barely functional to wide awake and deeply alarmed: “Has anyone seen Toph?”

Sokka jerks halfway to his knees before every single one of his bruises protests. “She  
isn’t *here*,” he asks, voice crossing at least four octaves from the sudden onset of pain, or maybe from the panic fluttering in his throat, or the nearly queasy rush of adrenaline on an empty stomach.

Because Toph on a good day? A force of nature with a level of general concern for the opinions of others that makes Sokka happy he's her friend. But Toph missing? Terrifying. The idea that she could have been taken against her will, quickly and quietly enough that no one realized, is nearly laughable even if it makes Sokka’s hands tremble with the need to clutch his people close. But her leaving on her own, of her own agency—that doesn’t make it *better*. Who knows what she could be doing, where she might be in this half-crumbling building. Sure it's made of stone, she's probably fine, but there's also the entire structural foundation of their inverted temple in the sky to consider.

Fuck. Sokka thought Toph was more sensible than this, that she understood what it would do to them—to *him*—to disappear on the heels of a day like yesterday, even if she always makes a show of not caring. Where *is* she?

&#45;-

Sokka gets to experience a whole different kind of alarm when Toph finally makes her reappearance in typically brisk fashion, knocking down an entire wall to tumble down from the surface in lieu of trying to find some stairs. For a too-long, exhausted second Sokka can barely comprehend that he’s seeing Toph *fall*, when she’s normally so sure on her feet, and then he takes another to shove away the sense of impending dread before rushing over with the others to check on her.

Sokka can think of a few ways Toph might have gotten hurt in the night, from crumbling architecture to her own tiredness dulling her reactions, and one very startle-able one in particular.

Please let her have stepped on a giant thorn bush, or fallen through a reasonably sized hole in the floor.

“What happened,” Katara exclaims, water at the ready as she skids to her knees next to Toph.

“I hurt my feet,” Toph mutters, shoving herself upright on her rock pile.

“How?”

*Thorn bush, thorn bush, please be a thorn bush…*

Toph shrugs, sullen, but not pulling away as Katara gently lifts up one calf to get a better look at the damage. “They got hurt.”

Katara freezes in a way that has Sokka’s gut tightening in reluctant anticipation. “…This is a burn.”

Toph grunts something that could be agreement and Sokka feels his heart drop. Fuck. It’s not like Toph walked into a campfire and no one noticed. It’s not like Toph’s walked into a campfire in her entire life. There’s only one possibility, and Sokka doesn’t know if anything worse could happen right now than Zuko hurting Toph. He can practically *see* Zuko losing any scrap of ground he might have gained with the others after last night’s discussion. And Spirits, Sokka of all people knows how Zuko is about his bending, about the idea of hurting someone with it. Fuck, about the idea of anyone getting hurt by fire in general.

Sokka can’t believe that it was intentional, not knowing Zuko, not with the way Toph won’t admit to anything despite Katara’s badger moleing. If she’d just what, stepped on some windblown coals last night? Toph would have made it *very* much known the minute it happened. And he can’t think why she’d keep quiet if she went out looking to tangle with Zuko. Which means it was unintentional. Which means it was an accident and Toph got hurt anyway and Sprits, Zuko’s probably having a breakdown by himself out in the woods somewhere.

Sokka’s chest aches. Fuck, he should have made Zuko stay. He should have found a way. That’s what Sokka does, right? He finds the ways to make things work the way they’re supposed to. The way they *need* to. Even if the others didn’t feel like they could trust Zuko, they could have at least kept an eye on him. Sokka could have at least known he was *safe*.

Though this past day—*days—*Spirits, how long has it even been since the invasion started?— is showing that maybe Sokka isn’t so good at making things work as he thought.

“Please just tell us how you got burned,” Katara presses, as if she doesn’t already know. They all know exactly what controlled burns look like, the ones that come from a firebender instead of just a natural fire. Except Aang, maybe. But if he doesn't, he’s about to learn.

Toph lets out a gusting sigh, making her displeasure known, but finally caves and answers. “So…I kind of went to see Zuko last night.”

“You *what*?” Aang exclaims, eyes bugging out of his head.

Sokka takes advantage of the fact that he’s standing behind Katara and Aang to briefly indulge himself and shove the heels of his hands against his eyes hard enough for the back of his eyelids to light up with flashes of bright. Fuck everything. His stomach lurches, sick with the confirmation, while some stupid part of him kicks out with dismay and  
fucking *jealousy* of all things and just—what, does *he* want to be the one who got burned?

He firmly ignores the flicker of heat in his gut that says *yes*, because *that* isn’t what happened to Toph.

“Zuko attacked you,” Katara says, sounding like she’s handing down a condemnation, like this is the final nail in the coffin of whatever thin leeway Katara had been willing to allow him.

“I mean, it was sort of an accident,” Toph mutters, shoulders hunched.

“How do you sort of accidentally firebend at someone’s feet?” Katara asks, relentless, before tilting to get better light. “Tui and Lai. When did this happen? I wish I could have gotten to these sooner, they're going to take a while to heal without taking your calluses too.”

Aang shifts from foot to foot, rubbing uncomfortably along the back of his head. “Do we need to be worried about Teo and Haru and The Duke wandering around if Zuko is burning people?” He cuts Sokka quick, nervous look. “Do we need a patrol or something?”

Sokka can’t swallow back a noise of protest at the idea that Zuko is some kind of predator stalking the Temple and looking for prey. That’s not—that’s not how it *is.*

“Do we need to stop him?” Katara asks, looking like she wouldn’t entirely mind putting Toph’s healing on hold to go run Zuko down.

“Zuko didn’t *chase* her,” Sokka blurts out, horrified.

“You don’t know that,” Katara snaps, slashing him a hard glare, and Sokka rocks back because…he doesn’t know. But he still *knows*, and—Spirits, why can’t he *do* anything? Sokka doesn’t know how to take a stand for Zuko that will do anything but make it worse when Toph still can’t put weight on her feet.

“Or—hear me out—we could just invite him back here,” Toph huffs, and Sokka is desperately trying to figure out if there’s any way to shout ‘*yes’* and not have Katara dig her heels in even more when he suddenly registers a new, horrifyingly familiar whistle of super-heated air.

“Sparky Sparky Boom Man!” Toph screams, throwing up her arms a bare second before the Temple explodes around them. The shot goes wide, but rains stone and chunks of earth down on top of them that Toph grunts to deflect without being able to ground in her stance. Fuck, fuck, fuck, this is what he gets for tempting the universe, *this* is the worst thing that could happen right now.

“Get toward the center of the Temple,” Sokka shouts, desperately glad he had the habit still this morning despite his tiredness of strapping his boomerang onto his hip. “We need to break his line of sight! Katara, return fire with Aang, Toph—” He draws up short, staring at Toph’s propped up, half-healed feet. *Fuck*. “Change of plans, Katara, cover our retreat. Aang, help Toph—”

“I can help myself,” she snaps, twisting her whole torso into the effort of sending a small boulder flying across the plaza and then bending herself a fucking *throne*, is the only way Sokka can think to describe it. A throne that can move, apparently, as she does just that.

“Okay, Aang—”

“Sokka,” Aang cuts in. “*You* get to the middle and *you* get down.”

“A boomerang is a perfectly fine distance weapon for—”

“He’s trying to hit *you*,” Aang shouts as they all dive to the side, another jet of fire slamming into the cobblestones. “So get in the middle so we can protect you!”

“We don’t know that,” Sokka argues, because he isn’t about to risk the *Avatar* on a weird feeling and a hunch. “And even if he is, I should stay on the perimeter to draw his attention, so you guys don’t have to worry about crossfire!”

“You should *all* run so I can *cover our retreat*!”

Right. Sokka breathlessly examines the increasingly-debris-strewn space, mapping out his path toward the interior Temple doors. “Alright, on three,” he says, gesturing with his hand toward the path they’ll take and trusting Toph to follow. “One, two—”

A hoarse shout stops Sokka dead, the sound more volume and projection and loosely directed, prickling anger than words. He freezes for a moment, wide-eyed, but then it comes again—suspiciously sounding like ‘*Run,’* that absolute *idiot*, as if Sokka would *leave him* *here*—and Sokka can’t tell himself he’s imagining it.

“Sokka? What happened to three?” Toph complains, but Sokka is jerking around, rising up onto his knees to scan the plaza, and then the arched ceiling because Zuko seems to have a thing for that, and then past the sweeping barely-there excuses for windows because Sokka knows he heard him so *where is he*.

Sokka’s breath catches when he finally finds Zuko, squared off in front of Sparky Sparky Boom Man on a far-too-narrow ledge. Zuko’s feet are rooted, arms wide, and *fuck* he’s never looked so small. He’s all lean muscle and coiled intensity and he barely even comes up to Sparky Sparky Book Man’s sternum. And it looks like he’s *talking* to the guy instead of fighting him, and where are his swords, what is he *doing*.

Sokka is halfway to his feet with no plan other than to get up there and help when Sparky Sparky Boom Man finally takes a step forward and Zuko lunges to meet him. There’s a tangle of limbs, angry snarling, and then Sparky Sparky Boom Man almost casually shoves Zuko aside toward the sheer drop off the mountain face. Sokka’s heart climbs into his throat in an instant as Zuko somehow stops his momentum, wobbles, and for half a second Sokka thinks it’s going to be fine, that he’s going to recover.

Then the blowback from Sparky Sparky Boom Man’s next attack sends Zuko teetering over the side, and Sokka barely has time to scream a protest, let alone move, before he’s getting hauled to the ground by Aang and shoved behind Katara’s covering wave, the steam of impact as fire and water collide filling the air and obscuring any chance Sokka has of seeing if that single reaching hand managed to find a hold.

*No*. Sokka refuses to believe that Zuko didn’t find a grip. He just went through the turmoil of thinking Zuko might be dead and the almost debilitating relief of it not being true. He refuses to go through that again, refuses to even consider it, not when Zuko is like cat, all ridiculous balance and more agility than should fit into a single body, with nine lives to get through and by Sokka’s count he’s still got four left.

“Sokka!” Katara cries, skidding back as she deflects another attack, arms trembling. “You need to run!”

“You go,” Sokka insists, ducking behind a column and forcing his rattling brain to *work*. Fuck, fuck, there’s a *reason* he always plans so much, because he can’t afford to get knocked on his ass at a time like this.

“Even *Zuko* told you to run,” Katara shouts, pausing to grab more water and give him a furious glare as Aang sweeps forward with an arc of air to whip at Sparky Sparky Boom Man’s feet.

“It’s fine! Go!” There are so many decorative stone details, if he can get from cover to cover then he should be able to avoid lingering too long for any one moment out in the open, and if he zigzags—

“I’m not leaving you!”

“Then get ready to fight,” Sokka says, scooting over to make room as Toph brings her throne-thing grinding over behind his pillar. If they won’t leave without him then they’re all staying for this battle, because Sokka can’t run away from Zuko. Not when Sokka can see him, not when Sokka just got him back, and especially not when Zuko is fighting for him, risking his fucking life, still, when Sokka couldn’t even ask Zuko to stay.

“Toph, status?”

“I can defend myself and keep this place from coming down on our heads,” she says grimly, reaching to slap a hand against the floor. “That’s about it.”

“Alright, we stay mobile,” Sokka says, waiting for the others to signal their agreement as he shuffles through months of drills and formations and two- and three-man attacks. “Keep his attention away from Toph, don’t stay in any one place too long, don’t let him focus on any one of us too long. It’s three against one—he’s going to wear down before we do.” Hopefully. Spirits, please let that be true, because Sokka is tightly aware that Sparky Sparky Boom Man didn’t fight an extended physical and emotional battle yesterday.

Nods all around, and Sokka takes one last deep breath. “Did anyone see if—”

“He was hanging on the cliff,” Aang interrupts, flexing his hands around his staff and giving Sokka a quick, assessing look. “You ready?”

“Let’s do this.”

Katara pulls up a cloud of mist, Aang setting it swirling, then they break from cover, shooting wide and relying on the dim light so early in the morning within the canyon and the shifting air currents to conceal at least the initial few steps of their passage. Sokka focuses on weaving and bobbing and wishes that using a boomerang didn’t rely quite so much on line of sight, too.

Aang is engaging Sparky Sparky Boom Man from a distance, using the unpredictable winds slicing in from the canyon to aid his attacks, doing his best to hold the man’s attention, which should theoretically let Katara and Sokka flank the guy. Except Sparky Sparky Boom Man keeps firing for Sokka and what the fuck, *why,* the Avatar is setting himself up on a platter, why would anyone come for *Sokka—*

“Down,” Katara says coolly, and Sokka throws himself to the ground with barely a second of clearance as Katara bends a rippling sheet of icicles across the plaza.

She yelps at the immediate return fire, and Sokka yanks her behind a rather conveniently toppled column as Aang hits back—Spirits, thank anything listening that Toph is keeping this place from falling because not all of these columns can be decorative—before joining them.

“So he’s *definitely* after Sokka, right?” Aang pants, taking a peek from behind cover and immediately ducking back when that high whine of coming fire sounds through the air.

“Definitely,” Katara grunts, her and Aang bracing to hold a shell of ice around them that steams away in seconds.

“Okay, okay. I’ll lead him and—” He ducks as another explosion bursts above them in a shower of stone shards, glancing up as another pillar topples.

“What the *shit*,” Toph exclaims from somewhere behind them, the Temple floor suddenly shuddering from what Sokka *really* hopes is the force of her bending.

“He’s going to blast the whole Temple off the cliff,” Aang says, voice going hard and gray eyes narrowing with determination.

“We don’t have time to waste, then,” Katara says, grim, and Sokka silently agrees, thinking of Zuko, dangling, imagining him trying to keep his hold with only one hand, fingers slipping a little more every time the Temple shudders…they don’t have any time at all.

“Okay, so if I—"

Sokka breaks off when he hears a shout, a *familiar* shout, ducking out from behind cover and ignoring the alarmed cries behind him because through the dust and still-present mist he can see *Zuko*. His firebender swings himself up onto the ledge using a—a *plant root*, what the— using the motion to kick out an arc of fire and flip onto the crumbling safety of the ledge.

Sokka misses what happens next as Katara grabs his shoulder and hauls him back behind the pillar with a horrified “Sokka, what the *fuck*,” but he shrugs her off and lunges forward again —lower this time—just in time to see Sparky Sparky Boom Man try to blast Zuko from close range. Sokka strangles a shout in his throat, but Zuko darts smoothly out of the way before rooting his feet and reaching with his hands and making some stiff, sharp gesture that Sokka hasn’t seen before, but whatever it is seems to make Sparky Sparky Boom Man stumble and snarl and turn on Zuko again and Zuko just slides out of the way, staying squared up like being targeted is what he *wanted*, that stupid *idiot*.

Aang launches forward, taking advantage of Sparky Sparky Boom Man’s distraction to throw out a wall of air that takes the man from the side, shoving him off balance. Zuko darts into the opening, dashing forward and throwing fire and skipping away, clearly trying to draw Sparky Sparky Boom Man away. Except the assassin keeps turning back toward the Temple, his eyes finding Sokka over and over, and only Katara’s quick bending saves Sokka from getting exploded when he mistimes his dodge toward new cover.

Fuck it, Sokka can’t let any of them—any of them—put themselves in danger any more than they already have because of him, especially not while he hides. He throws himself back to his feet, grabbing his boomerang and darting forward and relying on the sudden change in tactics to give him a moment of surprise to work with. Zuko is back on the same ledge as Sparky Sparky Boom Man, trying to engage him more fully now that it’s clear Sparky Sparky Boom Man won’t chase him, doing that weird stiff-hand-pull thing that seems to throw off Sparky Sparky Boom Man’s aim somehow, which is *great*, except Zuko can’t seem to find any kind of rhythm with it because he keeps needing to throw himself down or back when Katara attacks.

“Don’t—” Sokka immediately cuts himself off.

“*Later,* Sokka. *Move,*” Katara growls before whipping a coil of water toward Sparky Sparky Boom Man’s ankles, aiming to tug his feet out from under him.

Sokka obediently gets his fucking head in the game, focusing on darting around so that Sparky Sparky Boom Man at least needs to turn to hit him. Sokka can feel his legs beginning to ache, though, his sleepless night beginning to fuzz the edges of his reaction time. He grits his teeth and keeps moving but fuck, he isn’t going to be able to keep this up forever. The battle is raging in fits and bursts across the plaza, terraces crumbling and ledges collapsing and Spirits, how long is it going to be before it doesn’t matter how tired Sokka is because Toph can’t keep this place together anymore? Before Zuko missteps and goes off that fucking ledge again?

That fear, and his determination not to let any of it happen, is front of mind when Sokka finally catches Zuko’s eye for the first time since Ba Sing fucking Se. Zuko is skidding backward under the force of a fire blast and they both pause for less than a heartbeat, eyes locked.

Then Sokka is hurling his boomerang and Zuko is dropping into a crouch as the boomerang flies overhead, popping back up to throw a few quick punches of fire that keep Sparky Sparky Boom Man in place before ducking *again* because Zuko knows how this works and Sparky Sparky Boom Man doesn’t and the sound of the boomerang cracking against Sparky Sparky Boom Man’s skull is the fourth most glorious thing that Sokka’s ever heard.

Sparky Sparky Boom Man is staggering, dazed, but he isn’t down and shit, now he’s looking angry. And Sokka’s out in the open and exposed because he needed to be to throw. But that means he’s also too far from Katara for cover, and Aang’s all the way across the plaza, and Sokka’s going to have nothing but his reaction time to rely on as Sparky Sparky Boom Man inhales and leans back for another attack, eyes locked on Sokka’s face.

The explosion never comes, at least not toward Sokka. Because Zuko is here, too, and Zuko is moving, not even bothering with fire as he streaks across the ledge, and he can’t even be half Sparky Sparky Boom Man’s weight but his full body weight behind a lunging knee to the lower back—plus Zuko’s weirdly strong legs—would be enough to move anyone.

Sparky Sparky Boom Man stumbles forward, right to the crumble of the ledge, and he must not be able to pull his blast back once he’s committed because the fire jets out toward his feet and explodes outward. Sokka can just pick up the faint outline through the blaze of Zuko throwing up a shield, the power of the strike breaking against Zuko’s fire and ricocheting back again and then it’s all dust and rocks and flying shards, and when the air clears the ledge is sheared off and Zuko is standing there on what little remains, rooted and tense and ready, fixed on the space where Sparky Sparky Boom Man used to be.

Toph’s voice sounds from somewhere behind his shoulder. “…Things are still a bit fuzzy with the feet. Did Sparrowkeet just kill a guy to save you?”

“I mean.” Sokka doesn’t quite know what to do now, is pretty sure that his heart climbed so far up his throat that it exited his body at some point. “Technically the assassin took himself out.”

“Talk about a gesture,” Toph mutters, and Sokka has no reply to that. Besides, he’s too busy watching Zuko finally twitch back into motion, stepping back from the edge into what little solid ground he has and eyeing his route down the plaza. And then fucking *leaping* down, with the total lack of regard for gravity that you’d expect from an airbender,  
and *Spirits,* that’s nearly enough to do the job that Sparky Sparky Boom Man couldn’t manage.

Zuko lands in a light crouch, shoulders set with wariness as he glances around, picking out Aang and Katara and lingering for a moment on Toph before finally settling on Sokka with that familiar focus that makes Sokka’s heart make a sudden reappearance to turn flips in his chest.

Zuko’s eyes sweep Sokka head to toe, not hungry but still heated, intense, like any scratch might be enough to send him diving off the cliff after Sparky Sparky Boom Man to make him pay for it. Sokka’s giving Zuko his own once over, taking in the scrapes and scuffs and dirt, the longer hair he couldn’t fully take in yesterday, the breadth of his shoulders that Sokka would recognize anywhere.

Alive, Zuko is alive, and fine, and fighting for Sokka, putting his own life at risk for them even after they sent him away because he has *no sense* of self-preservation. And fuck Sokka still doesn’t know if he can trust himself and his own decisions, but he can’t help wildly wondering if this kind of action speaks loudly enough that maybe Zuko will be allowed to stick around. It *has* to. Sokka *needs* it to, he’ll fucking make it loud enough that no one can ignore it. Because then Zuko would be here, and so would Sokka, and maybe…maybe Zuko will still be here when Sokka figures out how to feel like he’s acting on something more trustworthy than his own judgment. On something stronger than the fear and guilt that seems to be all he can find inside himself ever since everything started to fall apart.

They end up just staring into each other’s eyes, still breathing heavily, and Sokka doesn’t know how much time passes before Aang finally clears his throat and speaks. “I guess we, uh —we owe you a thank you, Zuko.”

Sokka can see the way that concept jolts through Zuko, uncomfortably, his body language immediately shutting down. “Oh. Uh…”

“Hey, what about me,” Sokka calls without taking his eyes off Zuko, drawing attention to give Zuko a moment of space. “I did the boomerang thing.”

“Glad you could participate for once instead of being the damsel we all need to rescue, Snoozles,” Toph drawls.

“I think it’s a nice change of pace for someone to be after Sokka instead of me,” Aang says, with the kind of levity you use when you’ve made it through and the giddy surprise is just starting to kick in.

“Instead of—fuck,” Zuko mutters, twisting to eye the spot where Sparky Sparky Boom Man went over.

“Come again?” Toph says, eager.

“Is everyone okay?” Katara calls, picking her way over the wreckage and thankfully preventing Zuko from answering.

“All good,” Sokka replies, giving himself a little shake for any sore spots to make sure, trying to sort through what’s new and what was already there. Some scrapes, some bruises, but nothing that needs attention over Toph’s feet.

“He never touched me,” Aang offers, the little show-off.

“All good except for my woefully burned feet,” Toph says, all chipper exaggeration. “What about you, Zuko?”

Katara’s face tightens, all eyes swinging to Zuko again, and Sokka can see him somehow tensing up even more under the renewed attention. “Uh…fine?”

“That was a lie,” Toph says, sounding positively cheerful.

“I—what? How—”

“He’s standing,” Katara snaps, crossing her arms. “He looks fine to me.”

“Katara,” Aang chides—or as close to chiding as Aang ever gets. “He just fought on our side.”

“So?”

“*So*,” Toph says with more than a little bite. “I think we should hear him out.” She pauses, eyes narrowed and daring anyone to disagree before she waves in Zuko’s direction. “The floor is yours, Sparrowkeet.”

Sokka will laugh, later, when everything still doesn’t feel quite so fraught, about the fact that it takes everyone’s full attention and a long beat of blank starting for Zuko to register that Toph means him. He blinks in realization, for a moment looking adorably confused before taking a deep breath and putting his shoulders back and finally pulling his attention off Sokka.

“I know that apologies and excuses don’t make anything better,” Zuko starts, his eyes darting between Aang’s face and the relative vicinity of Katara’s feet. “But—I—I’m not trying to make an excuse, just—I was told the world was a certain way, and that there was only one way it could be. And it took me a long time to realize that things could be different. And I’m sorry that all of you had to be part of how I learned that. But I *have* learned. I—I know there’s no future for me at the Fire Lord’s side. The Fire Nation like it is now can’t—it can’t work.” Spirits, Sokka wonders what it took for Zuko to finally be able to admit that to himself, let alone out loud even if he sounds like he’s choking a bit getting the words out. “And I don’t want to be part of any world where my father has power.”

Zuko’s eyes flick up, wary like he’s expecting a protest, or a challenge, and seeing that they’re all listening, waiting, seems to put a little steadiness in his voice. “I…sometimes none of the choices look good. Sometimes you’ve been told for so long that doing the right thing is wrong. But all I want is the opportunity to help. I want to play my part in ending this war and trying to fix what my family’s done. And I…I’ll accept whatever way you allow that to happen. I know I can’t—I can’t force you to accept me. I just…ask that you give me a chance. To prove myself. However I can.”

It’s quiet then, Zuko completely still with determination and concentration until it becomes clear that he’s waiting now for them. All eyes cut to Toph, except for Sokka, because that was more words than Sokka thinks he’s ever heard Zuko use at any one time, and Sokka knows every one of them was true.

Aang is the first one to speak. “The masters always taught us that making a mistake and showing genuine remorse was more valuable than always being perfect, because everyone is flawed, and it is only through admitting your faults that you can embrace your humanity.”

Zuko blinks, opening his mouth and then slowly closing it. His eyes cut once, quickly, to Sokka, a hint of his uncertainty cracking through. Sokka can only shrug. Zuko’s the one with the cryptic uncle.

Katara steps into the unsure silence. “I heard a lot of words. But I didn’t hear many specifics.”

“Come on, Sugar Queen,” Toph huffs.

“I’m sorry for using your mother’s necklace to hunt you,” Zuko breaks in, voice firm and eyes direct on Katara’s face. “It was an awful thing to do, even if I didn’t know what I was doing at the time.” He shifts to Aang. “And I’m sorry for carrying you into the tundra just because I was desperate. I could have gotten you killed if the others hadn’t found you, and I —I shouldn’t have taken you from the Spirit Oasis.” His gold eyes land on Sokka, and he hesitates.

“I don’t need an apology,” Sokka says quietly. At least not in front of the others, not before they actually have a chance to figure out what they might need to apologize *for*. “But can we talk?”

Zuko searches his face, quick, before finally nodding and shifting to Toph. “And I’m sorry for burning you last night. It was an accident, but that doesn’t matter. A firebender knows more than anyone how dangerous fire is without control. I’ll work harder on being careful. It isn’t okay to hurt someone just because you didn’t mean to.”

Sokka holds his breath at the ensuing silence, watching the tension creep into Zuko’s clenched fists and up his arms and over his shoulders and across his face until Toph finally leans forward, catching Zuko’s attention. “I accept.”

“Me, too,” Aang says immediately.

All eyes swing to Katara, who just crosses her arms, jaw set, and for an incredulous, infuriating moment Sokka wonders if this whole thing is going to sink because Katara’s going to give them the silent treatment. Spirits, why did Sokka ever think he should try to be impartial and stay out of it when Katara gets to act like *this*?

“I think we should vote again,” Aang suddenly says, turning away from her.

“*What*? What’s the point if we just revote every time—”

“Let’s vote!” Toph agrees over Katara. “I think Zuko should be allowed to join us. We need a firebending teacher, he’s a firebender, him and Snoozles are going to be hilarious. I see no downsides.”

“I understand that there are concerns,” Aang says with significantly more gravity than Toph. “But Zuko has apologized, and he risked his life for us when he didn’t have to. I think he’s earned a chance, at least.”

“Fine,” Katara grits out. “But if he’s staying then we need some conditions, he can’t just be —”

“No,” Sokka interrupts.

Katara pulls up, head jerking toward him in surprise. “What?”

Apparently, Sokka isn’t staying out of this one anymore. “Zuko can either join us, or he can’t. No conditional acceptances.”

“*You* might be willing to overlook basically everything Zuko’s ever done to us, but he needs to earn trust if he wants to have it,” Katara says, glaring. “And one fight isn’t enough to earn it from me, not after all he’s done.”

“You’ve done things to him too.” Sokka snaps. “Does that mean Zuko gets some conditions too?” Oh, fuck, that was stupid. He can see the indignant fury in every line of her body. “You can’t just demand that he obey some vague rules to make you trust him and leave it at that,” he hurries to add on, trying to moderate his tone before her anger has time to root any deeper.

“If you think you can just tell me to get over—”

“I’m not telling you to get over it!” Sokka says. He's painfully aware that he can’t force something like forgiveness. “But if you’re going to say he needs to earn your trust then you need to be clear on how that happens. And it needs to be objective stuff.” He raises a hand to silence the protest he can see on her face. “I know it’s a subjective thing, but it needs to be clear, or else this is always going to be a fight.” And Sokka isn’t willing to be part of putting Zuko into a constant state of uncertainty—fuck, any more than he already has. And he absolutely refuses to let slide yet another thing that makes Zuko feel like he needs to be worthy enough to be safe.

Katara grits her teeth, looking out into the canyon as she chews it over before finally relenting. “Fine,” she grits out. “I’ll think about it. And if he doesn’t agree with the terms then he leaves. Happy?”

Not really. “Fine.”

Zuko clears his throat, immediately shifting his weight like he regrets drawing attention to himself. “So, uh. Does that mean..?”

Aang breaks into a wide grin. “Welcome to the gang, Zuko!”

Sokka’s heart is pounding in his ears, and if his own knees are weak with relief he can’t imagine what Zuko must be feeling. His firebender looks more than a little dazed, visibly realizing that he doesn’t need to plead his case anymore. “I—thank you. I’m—thank you. For accepting me into your group. I won’t let you down, I promise,” he says, earnest and painfully sincere, eyes sliding toward Sokka, who desperately wants to trust his own painful wishing for promises alone to be enough.

### End Notes

#### Chapter End Notes

## Chapter 12: Where We Left Off

### Notes

#### Chapter Notes

No particular warnings for this one!

### Text

“There’s plenty of room in the plaza with all the rest of us, I don’t see what the big deal is.”

“I, also, do not see the big deal.”

“Very funny, Toph,” Sokka says, pressing his fingers to his temples and sounding like he’s silently asking for patience from some higher power. “Can you just cool it with the blind jokes for a second?”

Zuko doesn’t entirely understand why the topic of where he’s going to sleep is becoming such a point of discussion. Between himself and Sokka, sure, there’s…a lot that’s happened the past few months. But he doesn’t get why it seems like it’s becoming a sticking point with everyone.

But then, Zuko doesn’t understand much about his life anymore. He still can’t quite believe the last two days aren’t just some particularly realistic fever dream—confronting the Fire Lord and redirecting lightning, Uncle being gone and Sokka being here and Azula letting him go, being rejected and then welcomed, and almost dying at least once somewhere in the middle of it all.

Things somehow actually going mostly to plan. Even if he’d hoped to be able to take a different path.

He sneaks a quick glance toward Katara, who’s currently saying some rather caustic things about privacy. Maybe just kind of welcomed. Not that it matters, not really. Zuko came determined to win the right to help, to see this through to the end. Everything else is just extra.

Even though that everything else might help Zuko figure out what, exactly, he’s supposed to do with himself now that he’s accomplished his initial goal so quickly. His inner fire is still high, pressing against the undersides of his skin, somewhere between thin wariness and sharp readiness.

“Don’t we all deserve some basic privacy?”

“Oh, I’m sure you and Sparrowkeet and some *basic privacy*—”

“Toph, just—shut it. Please.”

Should Zuko start trying to train the Avatar immediately? His scarred ear is ringing faintly from battle and his balance isn’t as back to normal as he would like it to be, but he doesn’t want to seem like he offered his help on false pretenses. Except it feels rude to start when they only just finished healing Toph’s feet—Zuko cringes, again—and still need to clean up the rubble. Zuko eyes the debris, remembering the sight of Sokka dodging fire and tugging back the furious surge of his inner flame. Agni’s tits, Zuko shouldn’t have given up the element of surprise by trying to talk to Maka of the Third Eye. What was he *thinking* back there? He *knows* the man’s reputation.

And he must be not thinking in general, or maybe hearing, because—there’s no way there can be three other people who weren’t here who need to be checked on. How—how could there be three more people to this crew that Zuko’s never *seen* before? Where have they been this whole time? He wracks his brain and fails to come up with anyone else he’s ever seen get off Appa’s back, which—fuck, is Zuko just that dangerously unobservant? Do they just *walk*?

Agni, Zuko can’t lose his head just because he left Caldera. Azula wasn’t right that everything is a game, but that doesn’t mean Zuko can sit back and just hope. Just because this step came easier than he expected doesn’t mean that Zuko can forget that he needs to keep walking.

“But what kind of message are you sending if we don’t even try to include him?” The Avatar protests, because Zuko is getting the sense that the Avatar is *very* invested in Zuko sleeping at least in sight of the others, which…is it a monitoring thing? Do they not trust him out of sight? Except Sokka’s been pushing for Zuko to sleep on his own, so it can’t be that. And Sokka doesn’t seem like he’s pushing in a *them* privacy way, either, so it’s some other reason Zuko doesn’t understand.

Not that he understands much of anything, yet.

“How about the message that you don’t get to be best friends forever just by showing up and deciding you want it.”

“It might be a bit early for a cuddle pile, Aang,” Toph says, ignoring Katara and turning her head toward Zuko, which…is also a thing he doesn’t understand. Isn’t she blind?

Agni, Zuko isn’t even sure that he *wants* to sleep around the others. Just the *idea* of sleeping near Katara and the Avatar is enough to chase away any sense of restfulness, let alone the reality of actually trying to do it. And these other people that apparently exist? Zuko might not really know Katara and Toph and the Avatar, but he knows *of* them through Sokka, enough to feel like he understands the way he needs to act and what they’ll expect of him. New people, though? Fuck, Zuko’s pretty sure he already messed it all up by not even knowing that they were here. What were the names again—Deo? Taru?

Zuko is increasingly sure that he doesn’t, in fact, want to camp out with the rest of them, that whatever privacy Sokka is pushing for is exactly what Zuko wants. But it still makes his inner fire flare and then pull tight to be told that he can’t.

“I’m just saying,” Katara is huffing. “Even if we all want privacy, why does it need to be those specific rooms?”

Sokka visibly struggles a moment, flicking a quick glance over that Zuko can’t read. “It… doesn’t,” he finally allows.

“Then how about the fourth-floor guest chambers?” The Avatar pipes up.

“No,” Sokka says immediately.

Fuck, Zuko…kind of desperately wants to know those conditions that Katara said she would have, even knowing that she wasn’t offering them from a place of kindness. Zuko doesn’t like not knowing what his guardrails are, the space he needs to work between. When he steps out of those bounds, he wants it to be on purpose, not because he didn’t know, and it makes him feel on edge, not knowing when he’ll be out of line, like he’s constantly bracing for an unexpected blow. And he can’t just guess at it, not with something as important as this.

And Sokka tried to take those clear rules off the table, too, which is just…yet another thing Zuko doesn’t understand.

“You’re being weird, Snoozles.”

Is she talking to him again? No, ‘Snoozles’ is Sokka, apparently, which…Yeah, okay. Zuko can see it.

“I am *not*.”

“Yeah,” the Avatar says with an apologetic little shrug. The Avatar is surprisingly conciliatory for someone who just tried to end a war via what Zuko can only assume was a strategic assassination. “You kind of are.”

“I’m not!”

“So then the fifth-floor guest chambers are fine,” Katara says, her exasperation clear even to Zuko who’s never really seen her anything other than spitting mad.

“…Fine,” Sokka grumbles, very obviously not fine with it, whatever ‘it’ is. Zuko still has absolutely no idea what’s going on.

But he knows better than to ask questions in front of a group like this, at least before he’s sure of who allies with whom yet. Just like he knows better than to heed the leap of his inner flame when a disgruntled-looking Sokka turns to him and jerks his head.

It takes Zuko a moment to register that this was a silent request to follow and that the conversation—discussion, fight, debate, whatever—is done. He belatedly jolts into motion, feeling suddenly awkward and uncoordinated with the way everyone is watching him. It makes him itch, makes his inner fire feel thready and spiky, makes him skirt wider than he necessarily needs to around the rubble to avoid getting too close to Katara, and then he has to hurry to catch up with Sokka as a result and just—Agni’s balls, Azula would kill him for that if she were here to see him revealing himself this way.

But she isn’t. Which Zuko never thought he would think was a bad thing, but as he trails an awkward pace or two behind Sokka—who did *not* reach back, and Zuko already doesn’t like this way of doing things, he much prefers the Ba Sing Se way of going to Zuko’s bedroom and—fuck, don’t think like that, don’t go there, too late, too late, too late.

From back here Zuko can only stare at the strip of tan skin along the back of Sokka’s neck, so familiar even though Zuko never spent much time looking at it from behind, and even though it’s now shadowed by more hair than Zuko’s used to seeing—is Sokka trying out a new style? Maybe Sokka lost his shaving knife? Zuko…will not offer to help. That would be weird, right? He's pretty sure that would be weird. But his fingers still itch, missing the feel of touching that short, bristly undercut, harder to ignore now than it was a week ago.

Zuko wants to kiss that skin, wants to hide his face against it, most of all wants to curve his hand protectively over that expanse that’s so strong and so achingly vulnerable, particularly when a fucking *Imperial assassin* is after you. What the *fuck,* Azula. Agni’s flaming dick, Zuko is aware that his sister isn’t a fan of using her words to communicate rather than cut, but shit. Have a fucking *conversation* before you set a paid killer on someone.

The distance between Zuko and Caldera has never seemed further, not even when he was first in exile and still trying to make sense of the world. *Fuck* does he need to have words with his little sister, and he uselessly wishes he hadn’t left Gao behind again. Zuko hadn’t wanted to risk him, but Agni, he’s suddenly not sure that being back in Caldera is any safer when it’s become this dangerous to be something she considers hers.

At least Sokka is unhurt, Zuko consoles himself, trying to soothe down his inner flame. Physically, at least. The rest…Zuko is less sure about that. They’re climbing a set of stairs— one of the few in this place— in silence, have been walking in silence, and Zuko wants to say something, do something, anything to shift out of this silent-trailing-behind thing that they’re doing. The urge to have Sokka’s attention and eyes on him has his inner fire shoving restlessly against the underside of his skin.

But the line of Sokka’s shoulders looks a bit…tense. Which makes sense, he did almost just die, which Zuko *cannot* think about right now. And Zuko doesn’t have it in him right now to reach across the gap between them without knowing whether or not he’s welcome, at least not when Sokka’s staying so perfectly outside the radius of Zuko’s body heat that Zuko doesn’t think it can be anything but deliberate. Not when always-talkative Sokka suddenly has nothing to say despite the privacy they finally have from the others. Zuko knows how achingly vulnerable it can feel to look your own mortality in the eye like that, the way it makes you want to retreat behind whatever you can find to hide behind.

He wonders if this is the first time, for Sokka, or just the most recent. He isn’t sure which would be better.

Zuko eyes the space between them, eyes Sokka head to toe, and resists the urge to let his inner flame spiral out. He isn’t entirely sure if his fire wants to get free to reach for Sokka’s brightness or to find something to immolate, but either way, Zuko can’t let it. But yanking his fire back toward his core just lets his hands fill with the need to follow the slope of Sokka’s back, to touch familiar cool skin, to find their place again along the curve of Sokka’s ribs, his waist.

Zuko curls his fingers into fists, trying to shove back that urge as well, and fuck, now he just feels like far too many words are pressing against his lips.

Agni’s balls. Zuko always knew that being accepted by the Avatar and his team and being accepted by Sokka were never the same thing. He *knew*, he accepted it. He did. He knows what he risked by going with Azula the way he did. But…fuck. The lump of metal in his pocket suddenly feels like it's digging into his thigh hard enough to bruise, like it's weighing him down heavy enough to slow his steps.

“This is it,” Sokka finally says, shouldering open the last door at the end of a long hall. Zuko wonders what he’s supposed to read into the fact that it’s the furthest room Sokka could have chosen while still being in the fifth-floor guest rooms.

There’s an awkward moment—made even more awkward by the fact that Zuko’s painfully aware that it *wouldn’t* have been awkward a few months ago—when they both realize that Sokka’s standing in the doorway and can either go into Zuko’s bedroom or step back into the hall toward him, or stay where he is and force Zuko to slide past him, body to body. Zuko can see the options flickering over Sokka’s face, is *fully* aware of which one Sokka would have chosen with a smirk and a spark in his eyes back in Be Sing Se.

But this isn't Ba Sing Se, even though his inner fire is thrumming in his veins at the proximity. And the fact that they’re here, not there, is sharply underscored when Sokka finally blows out a hard breath and slips through the doorway first. Zuko releases his own breath, trying to shake out the tension he doesn't want in his shoulders and to steady his inner flame and to remind himself what he is and isn’t here for before trailing Sokka into a surprisingly wide room, empty except for the lone stone sleeping platform.

“We’ll find some blankets,” Sokka mutters, frowning at the platform. “I think we’re out of pillows…”

Zuko clears his throat. “I have one.”

Sokka looks over and their gazes catch for an endless, tense moment. Then both of them awkwardly turn away, making a show of examining other parts of the room, and Zuko wonders if he’s imagining the nearly-soundless relieved or frustrated or who-knows-what exhale from behind him.

Zuko walks slowly into the center of the room, taking in the stone and the wood paneling. He’d been impressed years ago, in some distant corner of his mind that still noted those kinds of things, by how well the decorative detailing of the Temple had survived without care for nearly a century. Something about the dry air around here, maybe, so unlike the humid heat of the Fire Nation. It had scraped in Zuko’s throat, then, sat thin and strange in his chest, the absence of home a physical ache every time the wind pressed against the raw left side of his face.

Zuko turns a slow circle now, taking in the single entrance and the wide, low window and the lack of much else. It’s…a good space. The second biggest room Zuko’s ever had to call his own, with no sign that anyone used to live here. He wishes he knew if its remoteness and sparseness and privacy are supposed to be a gift.

His drawn-out examination ends with Zuko face to face again with Sokka again, who’s still leaning against the wall by the door, arms folded and fingers fidgeting, all bare skin and white wrist wraps and somehow both exactly like Zuko remembered and totally different. Zuko’s eyes flicker down before he can tell himself not to, running over the flex of Sokka’s biceps, taking in his restless fingers, lingering on the scrapes he can see on Sokka’s shoulder before finally rising to meet breathlessly familiar blue eyes.

Agni, there’s so much Zuko wants to say, and this…he didn’t have a script for this. Where does he even begin? And shit, when was the last time Zuko felt this wrong-footed around Sokka?

“Your hair is different,” Zuko blurts, immediately wincing as he hears himself and then compounding it all by awkwardly gesturing toward the side of his own head as if Sokka wouldn’t know what he was talking about. Zuko can feel the prickle of a blush over the unscarred side of his face and Sokka’s just blinking and Zuko should just…probably change the subject. But he can’t think of anything else, because now that Zuko’s had time to get used to the difference, he can’t help wondering what it would feel like to sink his fingers into the strands behind Sokka’s ears instead of scraping his fingernails across stubble. To twine his fingers in and cradle Sokka’s skull and tilt his head back and—

“You’ve got stuff?” It takes Zuko a frantic, wild moment to catch up and not embarrass himself. His own thoughts might be off and running but Sokka’s are clearly not moving in the same direction. Sokka's more closed off than Zuko can ever remember him being, not necessarily locked down and remote, because he isn’t—his shoulders are hunched and his eyes are skating away and he can’t seem to leave a loose thread on the edge of his tunic alone. There’s nothing locked down about him. But his face is somehow so far past neutral, so full of every possible thing, that it might as well be expressionless for Zuko’s ability to read it.

Fuck, this…doesn’t seem good. Did Zuko do this, on all his own? Or did something else happen to Sokka?

“Yeah,” Zuko belatedly says, clearing his throat and trying to read anything specific in Sokka’s face or body language. Is Zuko this out of practice? After being in *Caldera?* Or… shit, is Sokka actually trying to hide? Did he have the time to learn that in the Fire Nation, too? “Back where I was camping.”

Sokka pulls a quick face. “Toph can get it then,” he says, tone briefly dark in a way Zuko doesn’t know how to react to except to tense against, even though he doesn’t think it’s directed at him. Probably. And Sokka notices him tensing, because of course he does, he always does, and frowns in confusion—of *course* that’s the first thing Zuko can read—before checking himself and sighing and giving a little shake of his head like he’s telling Zuko not to worry or something, which—Zuko can’t do that.

Still, that little softening in the unreadable expression Sokka’s been wearing, the glances Sokka keeps taking…

Zuko takes a deep breath and lets the words out before he can talk himself out of it. “I—it’s good to see you,” he says tentatively, eyes careful on Sokka’s reaction. “I was worried I— I’m…I’m glad you’re okay.”

Sokka’s arms tighten over his chest, face shuttering in a way that has Zuko bracing himself, which he isn’t used to doing with Sokka, not anymore at least. He watches anxiously as Sokka seems to consider a series of responses, silently kicking himself for saying the wrong thing already but still unable to find it in himself to want to pull the words back.

“'Okay’ is a broad word,” Sokka finally says, low, eyes sliding away even as he seems to track Zuko’s every breath.

Zuko shifts his weight, fists opening and closing, inner fire turning back on itself as he searches for his own reply. Does that mean that Sokka *isn’t* okay?

“Are *you* okay?” Sokka abruptly asks, eyes slashing back up to Zuko’s face.

“I’m fine,” Zuko says, shrugging. He’s here, isn’t he? The Avatar didn’t throw him off a cliff. Zuko was through some miracle close enough to intervene this morning when he heard the first explosion go off. Things might actually be proceeding as he’d planned—hoped—they would. And Sokka…Sokka is talking to him. Which is more than Zuko allowed himself to expect when he walked away from Ba Sing Se.

“…Are you sure?” Sokka says, eyes narrowing slightly, and Zuko still isn’t sure how to read his expression, but he can’t help shifting uncomfortably under it.

“Um. Yes?”

“Because Toph said you were hurt,” Sokka says, voice going tight and fast. “We did roll call and asked if everyone was fine, and you said you weren't hurt, and Toph said you were, and if you’re—but now you’re saying you’re fine.”

“I mean.” Zuko scratches at the crown of his head where his top knot would usually sit, feeling the aches and bruises and light burns that come with fighting another firebender in close quarters and falling off cliffs and clawing your way back up. “It’s not a big deal.”

“It’s not—Zuko, we *asked* you. We wouldn't do that if we didn't want to know! Spirits, why don’t you—” Sokka shoves the heels of his hands to his eyes. “Why don’t you  
ever *say* anything?”

“It—it didn’t seem important,” Zuko says, his inner fire giving a confused twist in his chest.

“You being hurt is important!” Sokka says, frustration breaking into his voice that Zuko instinctively wants to flinch from. “You’re acting like it doesn’t matter but it *does*. We can’t do anything about it we don’t know! We can’t help, we can’t work with you, we can’t—if we don’t know in time then we can’t do *anything*.”

“It’s not a big deal,” Zuko repeats, scrambling to find his footing. “Other people were more hurt.” And Zuko just gave two—*two—*monologs to the others that Sokka was there for. *Two*. Does Sokka…want his own apology? Except Zuko just apologized to everyone else and Sokka said he didn’t want one and then they came here, so why would Sokka think he’d need to demand it now?

“Zuko, come *on,*” Sokka says, nearly pleading, and Zuko can feel anxiety tightening around his chest because he doesn’t understand what Sokka's pleading *for*. “You just—you *have* to tell people things. If you’re hurt, if you have plans. If you’re doing things and not telling anyone then—then it’s bad, okay? How are we supposed to—You just run off and do things and don’t let anyone know and how am I—” His voice cracks and he sucks in a sharp breath. “—how are we supposed to figure out how to *help*?”

Zuko…thinks this might not be about him being bruised up anymore.

“Are you asking if I have a plan?” Zuko asks, worry tightening around his chest. “Did she not —I tried to tell your sister…” Agni’s balls, what if Katara *didn’t* pass on the message? If this whole time…

“Some cryptic shit about long games and hope? And it’s not—it’s not what you said  
to *Katara*,” Sokka says, burying his hands in his hair. “It’s every other opportunity you had to tell *me.* You fucking freed Appa and I didn’t even know! Why—why *didn’t* you?” Sokka searches his face, looking half-desperate, and Zuko’s heart lurches at the idea of putting all that uncertainty and hurt in Sokka’s eyes, at the knowledge that Zuko doesn’t have anything to give him that will make it better.

“I just…didn’t,” Zuko says, wincing as he hears himself. It just hadn’t seemed important. Or not important enough, not balanced against Sokka’s shrinking time and Zuko’s exhaustion and the knowledge that the end was hurtling closer and that Zuko had, at least in part, been the one to shove those final gears into motion.

“Spirits, Zuko, I just—what did I *do*? Why did you think I wouldn’t—?  
Fuck, *everyone* thought that you’d—that you were working against us.” Zuko feels a stab of pain in the center of his chest. Was Sokka part of that ‘everyone?’ “And I’m there trying to say no, there’s a plan, no, it isn’t exactly what it looks like, with no idea what it *is*. Or what the goal is, or who’s involved, or if you need us to do something, if you need *me* to do something. What the *fuck*. Do you have any idea what it’s like to sit there day after day after day and have everyone telling you everything was just a lie?”

“Yes,” Zuko bites out before he can stop himself, stung. “I do. When my sister told me about your *invasion*.” Sokka flinches, and Zuko doesn’t know how to react to that—it doesn't feel *good—*but it doesn’t really matter because now that Zuko’s started he can’t seem to stop, smoke on the back of his tongue. “You’re mad that I didn’t tell you things? Do *you* know what it’s like not knowing something like that when Azula does?" Zuko's heart stutters in remembered fear. "Agni, I just—You didn’t—you didn't tell me things either," Zuko forces out, hugging his arms over his chest and struggling to pull his gaze any higher than Sokka's shoulder where his restless fingers have gone still.

“That’s not—when have I not answered a question you asked me?” Sokka protests, looking stuck somewhere between hurt and guilty, and Zuko has no trouble figuring  
out *that* expression when he’s feeling the exact same way. “When have I not told you something you said you wanted to know?”

“Sokka, I—how was I supposed to know to *ask*?”

Sokka pulls up short, staring, eyes wide as emotions chase across his face too fast to read, and Zuko clenches every muscle he has against the urge to immediately take it all back, to rush over and soothe and do anything he can to make this go away, to let it go. His inner flame is flickering too fast and too thin that he’s pushing back instead of smoothing things over, that he's maybe even *escalating,* but—

Yes, Zuko hid things, didn't share things he could have. But so did Sokka. Big things, world-changing things, life-risking foolish reckless things that Zuko could have told him not to do, or at least not to do that way, if only Zuko had known he was thinking about doing them. And it’s not Zuko’s fault that he didn’t know.

“…Fuck,” Sokka finally mutters, almost to himself, slumping back against the wall, everything seeming to rush out of him as he scrubs his hands over his face and lets out a humorless little laugh. “Fuck. Yeah, I guess that is our thing, isn’t it? That's exactly how we do things.”

“It’s not just—” Zuko immediately clamps his mouth shut because this would tip him from maybe escalating to definitely escalating, and what's the point when Sokka is agreeing and Zuko already barely has room in his chest for air around his instinctive need to diffuse everything about this situation. Except Sokka’s looking at him now, expectant, openly bracing himself but also...still here. Waiting, when he’s right by the door and it would be the easiest thing in the world to just leave. Waiting to hear what Zuko has to say, when this whole thing started over *not* saying things. “It’s not just stuff,” Zuko finally gets out, struggling to keep his voice even, to even find the words now that he's trying to say them. “It’s not just sharing. It’s—you didn’t say *words*.”

Sokka stills, even his fingers going quiet, everything about him frozen, and Zuko doesn’t know what to do with that and he’s already started so he just keeps going.

“You *always* have something to say, Sokka. You can’t be quiet, that’s—that’s what you *do*.” Though maybe that’s just how Sokka is with Zuko. Maybe Sokka saves up all those words for him.

Sokka’s looking rather stricken, though. So maybe not.

“You never don’t have something to say, but you—yesterday you didn’t *speak*.”

“Yesterday was—Zuko, yesterday was the *eclipse,"* Sokka says, shoving his hands through his hair. "You—we’d just—we’d just tried to end the *war* and it didn’t work, it didn’t—not at *all*. And then we had to leave people behind, and get here, and—and fucking figure out what to do *next.*" Sokka gives another of those tight, humorless laughs. “And then out of nowhere you just—and I didn’t...I didn’t *mean* to not give you that. To make it harder. I just…Zuko, after *everything*, I just didn’t—I didn’t know what to *do.*”

"I’m not—I’m not saying you didn’t have an awful day, and I—maybe I should have picked a better time. To try to come here," Zuko says, clenching his fists against the way his hands want to tremble. "I didn't want to make anything harder for you. But yesterday was—it was hard for me too, okay? I didn’t have to leave Caldera.” Not yet, at least. Not ever, if he went along with Azula’s way. “But I did anyway, I walked away from everything to help the Avatar, and that wasn't easy even if I—even if I chose it, okay? And then you didn't—I didn't know what to do either, but I still...”

Sokka makes a low noise in his throat and shoves a half-step off the wall before he seems to flounder for what to do next. "I—I’m sorry," he says, stumbling, and Zuko hates seeing him so uncertain, especially having been the one to do it to him. "I didn't...I didn't want to make anything harder for you either, I promise I didn't mean to." Zuko has to look away, itching at feeling so exposed, even being the one to do it to himself. "I should have figured it out, I should have—that’s what I’m supposed to do, I’m supposed to figure it out, and it was like I couldn’t—fuck, I just wasn't thinking." Another of those awful little laughs. "Spirits, fuck. I just...wasn't thinking."

Zuko...doesn't know how to respond any of that. "...It's fine," he finally says.

"It's really, really not," Sokka sighs, slowly slumping back against the wall again. “You showed up to do something and I just…did nothing.”

"It...happens," Zuko tries again, shrugging and trying to breathe through the tight band of discomfort around his chest.

"...Yeah," Sokka says after a beat, quiet and looking more worn down than Zuko can ever remember seeing him. "It does." He lets out another huge breath, then glances up to search Zuko's face, hesitating a few times before finally saying, "Zuko, you...you said everything?”

…Fuck. Zuko’s inner fire flinches back toward his spine as he forces himself to not hunch his shoulders against what he knows is coming.

“Where’s, ah—Does that mean...Where’s Iroh?”

“I don’t know,” Zuko bites out, the words clear and sharp as his inner flame gives an unhappy wrench.

Sokka's back to fidgeting, fingers picking at the end of his wrist wraps, face somewhere between uncertain and troubled as he carefully says, “Do you want to—Are you okay?”

“It’s *fine*.”

Zuko stares down at the ground as the silence stretches out after his clipped response, not feeling a single bit good about the way Sokka immediately backs off. Zuko flexes his hands open and closed, feeling…burned through. Like drawing that line after everything else that's already happened today used up the last of Zuko’s frustration and willpower, and now there’s nothing left strong enough to stop him sagging. Agni, this…isn’t how Zuko wanted things to go.

“I think,” Sokka eventually says, voice low, staring down at his own boots when Zuko risks a glance. “I think we maybe can’t be okay with things being fine anymore.” Sokka's eyes flash up when Zuko doesn't reply, the uncertainty on his face mirroring Zuko's own. “I’ve been okay to let things be fine. Or, with them being fine. And…I don’t know. I don’t know what I’m saying.” Sokka kicks at the ground, looking frustrated. “You should be more than fine, and I—whatever. Ignore me. Forget it. It’s—forget it.”

Like Zuko can ever ignore Sokka when he talks, can ever forget the things he says. But he doesn’t press anyway, and this silence as it settles is more drained than tense, more exhausted and spent than anything else. Agni, Zuko doesn’t remember things being this halting between them since…the Fire Festival? Maybe the early days of Ba Sing Se, when they were still figuring out what the boundaries were of the things that needed to be unsaid?

Maybe they figured that out a little too well.

Zuko comes out of his brooding when Sokka finally stirs, his own thoughts apparently having gone someplace very different as he asks, voice low and eyes still on the floor, “You were in Caldera?”

“Yeah,” Zuko says, his own words equally quiet.

“For the eclipse?”

“…Yeah.”

“I didn’t see you.”

“…No.”

“I saw your sister."

“…Yes.” And both of them seem equally unhappy for having met each other, judging by the way Sokka blows out a hard breath before nodding. Great. Just great.

“…I’m sorry?” Zuko tries, assuming he didn't get it right when Sokka looks up with some like surprise on his face.

“…Why?” Sokka finally asks, brow furrowed as he eyes Zuko.

Fuck, how can Zuko feel more picked apart under Sokka’s gaze right now than he ever did with Li and Lo? “…Leaving you with Azula?”

“Not leaving *with* Azula?”

Right. Right. That’s…harder to apologize for. “I’m sorry for the way it happened,” Zuko finally says. The suddenness of it, the inability to send any real kind of word, the way Sokka got sucked between him and Azula, right where Zuko never wanted him to be.

“But not *that* it happened,” Sokka says, glancing away, swallowing hard, and it doesn’t sound like an accusation but Zuko can’t stop himself from going against every instinct he has to haphazardly offer up the thin explanation he has anyway.

“I didn’t—I didn’t have one for long. A plan, I mean. You weren’t…really around by the time I…” He trails off with a shrug, looking at Sokka’s hands instead of his face because that feels like too much right now. “It was after I got sick.” Sokka flinches at that, almost imperceptible if Zuko weren’t already looking so closely. “And Azula—she was…I didn’t expect…that.”

“You don’t say,” Sokka mutters, scrubbing his hands over his face again and looking more than a little strung out. “It would have been real good to know,” he adds.

Zuko huffs. “It would have been real good to know that you were planning to invade Caldera on the Fire Nation’s single most-prepared day in centuries.” He winces as he hears himself, waving an apology toward Sokka's half-guilty, half-stung look. “But Sokka, I wasn’t—” He takes a deep breath. “I get that you’re upset. But...I thought that not sharing stuff was just… how we did things.” How they kept the weight of who they were separate from who they were to each other. How they were able to live their very separate lives in Ba Sing Se but still carve out a space that was theirs, protected from the things that might try to come between them.

Sokka stares for a moment, then grunts, fidgeting with that loose string on his tunic again. “…Do you think it worked?”

It’s Zuko’s turn for a sharp, humorless laugh. “In Ba Sing Se.” But they aren’t in Ba Sing Se anymore and haven’t been in months, and the limitations…well, they wouldn't be having this conversation if they both hadn't become aware of them.

“Yeah,” Sokka sighs, closing his eyes and dropping his head back. “Yeah. Maybe,” he adds after a moment, voice low, “We shouldn’t anymore.”

Zuko shifts, uncertain.

“Not share stuff,” Sokka clarifies, cracking an eye open. “Maybe we should stop not sharing things. Because this kind of sucks right now, right?”

Zuko snorts out a surprised laugh. “Yeah,” he says, his inner flame settling over that flash of levity and shared understanding. “It does.”

When Sokka finally opens both his eyes it’s to fix on Zuko’s face with an intensity that Zuko isn’t used to experiencing in this context, not when he doesn’t at least have some idea of what’s behind it. “Can I ask you something?”

Zuko blinks. “Yeah.” He doesn’t exactly know how he’d say no when Sokka's looking at him like that.

“You came back for Aang?”

“Of course,” Zuko says, even though he doesn’t think that was actually the question.

“Was—” Sokka takes a quick breath. “What that the only reason?”

Zuko stares at Sokka, heart trapped in his throat. Fuck, this—how can Zuko answer this when either answer he gives could be potentially disastrous? When he doesn’t know where Sokka’s head is at to know which is the right one to give when both could be true? Zuko is here for the Avatar, yes, but training the Avatar—that’s a means. That’s not one of his three most important things.

“Because…if you’re back for me,” Sokka continues, clearly picking his words carefully. “If you’re doing it like this because I’m involved—”

“That’s not fair,” Zuko cuts in, finally finding his words, “You *are* involved. I can’t just take you out of it.” Especially when Zuko’s pretty sure he *wouldn’t* be here if not for Sokka. He would be dead in the North, or killed by Zhao, or just another body somewhere in the Earth Kingdom. He would never have had the chance to make the decision to leave Caldera because he never would have seen it again. “It’s not like I can just—redo the past year,” Zuko says, restlessly crossing and uncrossing his arms.
