Agni, he can’t even begin to imagine what his life would be like without Sokka. “I—how could you even—” Zuko pulls up short, a stab of uncertainty taking him in the chest. “Can—can you take *me* out of it?” Zuko asks, wincing at the insecurity he can hear leaking into his voice.

“No,” Sokka says, immediate, unthinking and ringing so true that Zuko can’t help his sigh of relief, quickly followed by a kick of confusion that Sokka would ask Zuko to try to take him out of it. “If I could redo it, I’d… there are some things, maybe. That I’d do differently. But not—yeah. Not you.”

…Oh. Zuko swallows hard. Oh.

“That’s…actually not what I meant, though,” Sokka says, awkward and looking nearly apologetic. “I more meant that…Zuko, if you’re back for me, I’m not…in a good place right now. I’m glad you’re here, I am.” Sokka makes a little face like that’s an understatement, and Zuko…doesn't see why it doesn't *sound* like a good thing. “But…”

Sokka trails off, kicking at the floor again, and as the silence drags Zuko’s heart drops. Oh, Agni. Maybe there's nothing more. Maybe that’s all that needs to be said. ‘But’ everything. But Zuko’s past, and his present. But the choices he made and the ones he didn’t, the things he withheld and the things he still doesn’t know how to say. But Sokka finally realizing that Zuko’s more than just the pieces that Sokka always focused on, that Zuko is full of jagged, uncomfortable parts that don’t go away.

Zuko’s on his second pass through the stages of grief when Sokka suddenly picks back up. “But I don’t think…that would be good right now.” Everything Zuko trips to a halt because that’s—that not a *no*. Zuko’s so busy managing the flare his inner flame throws out that he almost misses Sokka’s next words. “I’m not sure if it would be good for either of us. I'm not —I mean, fuck, we can’t even—I hurt you and I didn’t even notice, that’s not—fuck,” Sokka says, closing his eyes, pulling himself tighter with each word until he’s smaller than Zuko’s ever seen him. "That's not *okay.*"

“I hurt you too,” Zuko says a beat, trying to breathe through the confused twist of his inner flame, because—what is Sokka saying? He’s not saying no, but he also doesn’t…?

“That still doesn’t make it okay, though,” Sokka says, words sad in a way that Zuko doesn't understand, but it still makes his chest hurt.

“So, what, so—what?” Zuko doesn’t—he doesn't get what Sokka's saying, but he feels a little bit frantic at the edges because a ‘but’ isn’t the same as a ‘no,’ and a ‘right now’ is something very different. Zuko can work with ‘right now,’ if he’s hearing it right, he just needs to be sure that he *is.* “What does—can I do anything?”

Sokka sighs, shoving a hand through his hair. “I don’t know. I—Zuko, it’s not you, it’s—”

“If you're about to say ‘it’s not you, it’s me’—”

“No! I’m not saying that, that’s not—Zuko, I need *time*,” Sokka says, practically hugging himself as he searches Zuko’s face. “After the past few days, I’m*…*not really okay. To be honest. If we’re doing the openness thing.” Sokka glances away, jaw tightening, visibly self-conscious. “And it’s a lot of stuff, not any one thing, okay? But it just happened and I just… need time. Spirits, I...I need to make sure I’m not going to fuck everything up again.”

“…Okay,” Zuko finally says, tight, grabbing onto the possibility there with everything he has before he lets himself start to spiral after his inner flame. “Okay, I—you didn’t fuck everything up. Just…so you know. But I can—I can do that. I can give you...that.”

It hurts to know that he helped break what was between them this way, and to realize that he’s finally allowed to be with Sokka but won’t be *with* Sokka. But he shoves that away, because it also means that there’s still a possibility for a *with* again, if Zuko can just…figure out how to fix things without tossing away what he still needs to do.

The always-fragile balance of his inner purpose wobbles, but it holds.

Sokka nods after a long moment, looking exhausted and finally pushing off the wall like his whole body hurts, and Zuko reigns back the anxious twist of his inner flame because he isn’t sure yet what he’s allowed to show without crossing this new line Sokka is drawing.

“For the record,” Sokka says, hesitating in the doorway and glancing back to catch Zuko’s eyes. “I am happy you’re back. Just in case I didn’t make that clear. I know I don’t seem it, but—I am. It’s good that you’re—that you're here.”

“...Yeah,” Zuko says inanely, clearing his throat, hoping this is safe to say at least if Sokka said it first. “Me, ah—me too.”

Sokka slips out of the room with that, the sound of his steps fading all too quickly into silence, finally leaving Zuko in privacy and quiet and with the uncomfortable awareness that, once Sokka leaves it, Zuko might be the only living thing on this floor.

Which is probably good, because with Sokka gone the delayed adrenaline rush Zuko’s been trying to stave off finally hits. Zuko locks his hands to try to stop their trembling, his inner fire flaring between tight and clinging to his spine and shoving against his skin as he takes deep, gulping breaths, his knees go shaky with…something. Relief, maybe? The aftereffects of battle? Or delayed fear, a kind that has no place here because Zuko knows that Sokka isn’t like that, he knows, he doesn’t know why he’s reacting like this, he just—fuck, Zuko  
nearly *shouted back*. Nearly let his anger cut free, *did* let his words get away from him, escalated when he could have diffused.

Zuko abruptly sinks down into a seiza, giving up on standing right now in favor of preventing himself from spiraling any more than he already has. The quiet is nice. And all the space to… decompress. And the wind, gusting in a rhythm that Zuko's slowly able to pace his breaths to, until he calms enough to remind his body that this isn’t the palace. He isn’t in Caldera, isn't back in a place where even *thinking* about doing what he just did is enough to make his pulse spike and his inner fire shudder with readiness.

He isn’t in front of the others, isn’t burning through his control for the Avatar or Katara to see. He’s alone in this little corner of the Temple that’s become his in some small way already, and before this he was with Sokka. Sokka, who was upset, too, but who…gave Zuko an apology, even though Zuko wasn’t looking for one and has absolutely no idea what to do with it now that he has. Sokka, who isn’t okay, a thought that makes Zuko’s heart lurch, but who’s still happy Zuko is here, which makes Zuko's inner flame flutter somewhere in his chest. Sokka who thinks it’s good that Zuko’s here and made a point of making sure Zuko heard him say it, even after they fought.

And if Sokka said they should stop not sharing, the both of them, that means they *should* share things, right? Maybe that means more than just things, more than just information and facts and history and secrets. Maybe it also means the sticky, messy emotions underneath.

In which case…maybe Zuko didn’t actually mess up all that bad after all.

&#45;-

“Toph,” Sokka says as he borderline-stalks back into the plaza, trying to distract himself with the in-progress repair work from the way his hands are still tingling with the urge to touch Zuko, from the way adrenaline is still fuzzing the edge of his nerves, from the rising sticky feeling that he finally got his chance to speak to Zuko and nothing came out the way he wanted. “Where was Zuko’s camp?”

“Getting his stuff?” Toph asks, not even breathing heavily as she bends a gigantic column back into place that Sokka wouldn’t be able to get his arms halfway around.

“Yeah.” Sokka glances around, but he doesn’t see Katara, and he hates the way a little knot of tension between his shoulder blades unwinds with the realization. He loves his sister but the wall of hostility she’s putting out right now is making it nearly impossible for Sokka to find his own equilibrium, and he just—he’d really like that back.

Fuck, part of him *aches* to shove aside everything else and close the distance between them and allow himself to be enfolded in Zuko’s arms again. Part of him is still loud with fear and terror and the delayed after-battle hit of all that could have gone wrong suddenly becoming apparent, all the things that nearly did go wrong because there was no plan for fighting alongside Zuko and fuck, why *isn’t* there? But Sokka can’t pretend that nothing happened between Ba Sing Se and today, not with his hands still trembling from battle, not with his shoulders still weighed down from the losses of the invasion.

Sokka isn’t sure that Zuko could pick things right back up where they left off, either, but Sokka…Sokka doesn’t trust his reactions after Azula, doesn’t trust his insight and judgment after the eclipse, doesn’t trust his choices in the moment after yesterday. If Zuko reaches out a hand, how could Sokka reach back when he doesn’t trust himself to hold it safe? Fuck, he needs to figure himself out. He just—he needs *time*. The one thing he’s never had enough of when it comes to Zuko.

“I can go get it,” Toph offers.

“It’s fine, you’re busy. Just tell me where.”

“If you give me like, twenty minutes, I’ll be done.”

Sokka glances around at the scale of the remaining wreckage, raising his eyebrows. That’s… impressive. “I can do it.”

She pauses, gaze swinging toward him, knowing in a way that returns that little knot of tension right back between his shoulders. “Wanting some alone time?” She guesses. “No, wait—wanting some alone time with Sparrowkeet’s things?”

“*Toph*,” Sokka sighs, scrubbing his hands over his face. Spirits, like Sokka needs to compound everything by pawing through Zuko’s things. *That* will show that he’s welcome here. “Just—the first one, okay? Just tell me where.”

“I can help you out, Loverboy,” she says, cheerfully ignoring his annoyance as much as she’s been ignoring every single bit of the tension that she must have been feeling between Sokka and Zuko over the past day. Fuck, not even a day… “This is just like when The Gecko and The Gopher were on the outs back at the Earth Rumble. Let me tell you what to do.”

“That’s not—who? You know what, no. I don’t even want to—”

“They’ve been together for like, as long as I’ve known them.”

Sokka...is aware that the sum total of the time he's spent physically *with* Zuko, if you take away everything in between, probably adds up to less than two months. And that the one thing he *has* managed to do since Ba Sing Se when it comes to Zuko is already feeling like yet another fuck up. "...Fine," he says, giving in. “Fine. What do I do?”

&#45;-

Zuko can feel that it's into the early afternoon by the time he has the wherewithal to truly examine the only-a-little-bit-crumbling room he’s been given. It’s a good-sized spaced, but also…not big enough to train in, to work out his restless energy in. And as Zuko shifts to eye the still-open door he abruptly realizes that he doesn’t know if he’s allowed to leave. It didn’t occur to him to ask when Sokka was here, and now that Zuko’s alone the possibility that this could be meant to be a rather nice prison on top of a serviceable place to sleep is suddenly springing persistently back to life.

It’s not that Zuko thinks Sokka wants to imprison him. It’s just… Zuko’s aware Sokka is just one voice of many, here. That imprisonment isn’t such an outlandish thing, for the two of them. And the possibility isn’t something Zuko *wanted*, but—he didn’t *not* expect it. And sure, Zuko could get out of any attempt to keep him if he had too, through fire or swords or climbing or his own knowledge of this place that he’s spent far more time in than they have.

But leaving…Zuko isn’t ready to leave yet. Not that way, at least, truly burning the ground behind him, and truly leaving him with only one option left.

Zuko slowly settles on the stone of the bedframe, looking blindly out the window instead of that dark doorway he’s suddenly unsure of. He tries to focus on the wind, on the sound of the breeze, on his own breathing, anything but looking too hard at all the twists of choice or outcome or whatever—*not* fate—that brought him back to this place, years later but still trying to grasp something intangible, still with only a goal and the shape of an idea of how to reach it.

&#45;-

“Katara,” Sokka says, hearing the tightness in his voice and just…unable to do anything about it, even as she pauses in her meal prep to shoot him a pointedly and specifically annoyed look. “Where did you move your paper?”

She blinks, frowning. “My what?”

“Your paper,” Sokka repeats, doing his own pointed and specific ignoring of the fact that Aang just dropped the sweet squash he’d been peeling. “It’s not where it usually is in your bag.”

“…I knew it,” Katara mutters, turning back to her cutting board. “I fucking knew that shit was disappearing too fast on the way North.”

“Yes, sorry, I’ll buy you more the next time we aren’t fleeing for our lives,” Sokka grinds out. “Where is it?”

“How do you know I have any?”

“*Katara.”*

She huffs, giving him a sideways look. “Why do you want it, anyway?”

“To draw another picture of Appa, why do you think?” He blows out a hard breath, trying to even out his tone, because it’s not her he’s frustrated with—actually, no. He is frustrated with her, but as a very distant second. “Please?”

“Fine,” she grumbles when Aang takes his turn to deploy a pointed and specific look. “I put it in Toph’s bag.”

“Why did you—you know what. I don’t even want to know.”

“I feel the same way,” she mutters, just a shade too loud to be inaudible as he sets off to find Toph’s things.

&#45;-

Zuko eventually ventures out of his room that may or may not be a very nice cell as darkness begins to fall, driven by hunger and the smell of things cooking. He knows the path back to the plaza, where…oh. Where the earthbenders have apparently cleaned up. Looking at the state of things now and remembering the scale of the damage, Zuko realizes that he’s…very lucky that Toph is twelve, and hasn’t learned yet to react to unexpected pain by hitting back.

Zuko hesitates as he considers that thought and how badly last night could have gone when he already thought it went about as badly as it possibly could. And then just hesitates, like all his determination and focus went into getting himself here and now that it’s happened, Zuko doesn’t know what to do with himself.

Which might be a larger statement about his situation that Zuko doesn’t have the energy to deal with right now. Now when he’s struggling already to fight back an instinctive suspicion over the genuineness of his welcome, because the Avatar said he was welcome, not Azula, and Zuko’s been reminding himself of that over and over without actually being sure if that means he should be more suspicious or less. And alongside that, equally as strong if not more so, is the awareness that regardless of his welcome, this is still Sokka’s space far more than it’s Zuko’s. And Zuko’s never been in Sokka’s space before, not unless you count their first meeting, which—well. It feels huge and momentous, like it deserves to be savored and gently held, to be treated with gravity and care the way Sokka treated that first—intentional— meeting with Uncle.

And like maybe it shouldn’t involve three to five other people and at least two animals that Zuko’s managed to get eyes on so far.

This is something new, in so many ways and for so many reasons, and Zuko wishes that he’d done this at least once before for…so many reasons. Right now, though, mostly so he could have even a shadow of an idea of what the rules are. Maybe he can just stay here at the edge of the plaza and try to observe for a while. Maybe he can figure a little bit of it out that way, start to get a sense of how this group works and how Zuko can fit himself into it, and indulge at the same time the not-so-small part of him that’s desperately curious to see how Sokka acts on his own turf around these people that Zuko’s heard so much about. Which—shit, what do they know about him in return? If Sokka’s talked about Katara and the Avatar and Toph and even Momo to Zuko, does that mean he’s talked about Zuko back? Zuko’s stomach gives an uneasy lurch as he realizes that he has no idea which of his secrets they all might already know, and which are still his.

“Sparrowkeet, stop lurking in what I can only assume are the shadows and come over here already. You’re creeping me out.”

Zuko startles, flushing and reluctantly making his way out of the doorway. He trains his eyes somewhere around the base of the cook fire like that means everyone won’t notice the way his face is turning hot, determinedly ignoring the way everyone is looking at him. Through force of will he manages to only look at Sokka in his periphery, watching the way Sokka’s eyeing him the same way back while making a show of being deeply engrossed in running a polishing cloth over his sword. It’s a nice sword, Zuko notes as he gets closer. Wonderful craftsmanship. Sokka’s hands over it look sure and strong in a way that’s new, and in the shifting firelight his fingers almost look like they could be spotted with ink, and—

And Zuko needs to stop thinking like that, because Sokka asked for *time*.

“Why do you keep calling me that,” Zuko asks, hesitating a moment before cautiously taking the seat the Avatar scoots over to offer him instead of the space Sokka flicks a quick glance to at his side. Zuko would far prefer to sit next to Sokka, but in front of Katara…maybe it’s not such a good idea. And the Avatar is giving such a bright smile, like he *wants* Zuko next to him, which…puts the Avatar solidly in Zuko’s blind spot, and…Zuko can handle it. Zuko can absolutely handle this.

“Cause your heart goes a mile a shitting minute.”

Zuko blinks, confused—is that—that’s not an Earth Kingdom colloquialism. Zuko would have noticed. Is that a regional usage? Except Sokka sighs and mutters, “Not quite,” while frowning slightly at Zuko in…worry? And Zuko doesn’t know how to respond to them except Toph pout dramatically before turning her uncomfortably focused blind gaze back on Zuko, so maybe it wasn’t addressed to Zuko in the first place. And wait, how does she…is this related to the lying thing? The heart thing? Agni’s dick, Zuko doesn’t need someone around keeping track of his blood pressure or whatever she’s doing. He doesn’t think he can sustain the constant anger he would need to deal with that.

“Besides,” Toph grins, as if she never stopped addressing him. Or maybe like she can tell his pulse just jumped? “Everyone deserves a good stage name.” A pause. “Know mine?”

“…No.”

“The Blind Bandit.”

…So not a stage name for her career in theater. “Did you rob people?”

“Of their dignity.”

“That’s…nice.” Zuko glances around the fire, but no one else seems to find this alarming or notable.

“I think so,” Toph agrees, cocking her head like she’s listening, grin turning wolfish.  
“Did *you* ever—”

“Dinner ready soon?” Sokka asks, casually cutting over her without looking up from his sword.

“As soon as the last time you asked,” Katara mutters, and Zuko gingerly tries to settle his legs cross-legged like the others instead of kneeling as the conversation shifts. Zuko’s aware that Sokka just gave him an out. And maybe implied that this secret is still his, in the process, and Zuko’s unabashedly grateful for it. Zuko doesn’t want to know how they would react to all his exploits as the Blue Spirit, if Aang ever told them, or knew more than just Pohuai.

Zuko can’t help stealing a quick glance toward Katara at the thought. Maybe they can bond over antique bending scrolls acquired through dubiously legal means. Not that Zuko has any of those anymore, but, well—that’s where the dubious legality comes in, doesn’t it.

Sokka and Katara quickly fizzle out on their discussion of dinner with only a few comments from Aang on good herbs in the area to keep it going, and as silence falls Zuko wonders if it’s always like this or if things are just so stiff because he’s here. He isn’t sure what he expected of the Avatar’s team, of Sokka’s crew. But they seem remarkably…subdued. Maybe they’re all just tired? The Day of the Black Sun was only a few days ago, even if it feels like a lifetime to Zuko’s wired, too-little-sleep-and-too-much-anxiety brain.

“So when do you think training can start?”

Would it be weird to scoot out of the circle a bit so Zuko can get them all into his field of vision at once? And maybe get something at his back other than the wide openness of the plaza with all its entrances and dark corners.

“I can’t wait to get started!”

Fuck, feeling so exposed, needing to constantly turn to take everyone in is making him feel extra fidgety right now, overfull of restless energy in a way he can feel leaking into his inner fire, into the twitching of his hands. Zuko’s adrenaline is singing, and he knows enough about this thin, tight kind of uncertainty to know that no amount of telling himself that this is not, in fact, a combat situation is going to make a difference. Fuck, he should have sat in the space that Sokka was offering, and burn everyone else’s opinions, because now all Zuko can do is make sure his ready inner fire stays confined to his skin.

“Maybe we can even start right now. We’ve got a fire all ready, right?”

What if Zuko just sat on his hands so no one could tell that he can’t sit still? He winces to think what Azula would have to say about that, and then again at the fact that if his hands are under his thighs, then Zuko would need an extra half-second if he had to firebend. Which shouldn’t be a factor in the decision, he shouldn’t be considering reaction times, he knows that.

They welcomed him and that has to mean something. Sokka said he is happy Zuko is here, and that *does* mean something. Even if in this specific moment it’s feeling a bit like being welcomed into the Council Room, down to trying to pace his breaths to the rhythm of Sokka’s inner flame which…would work better if Sokka’s inner flame were at all steady.

Agni, Zuko needs to try to make this work before he burns this bridge behind him, too. Or burns it again, rather, and much more thoroughly.

“Zuko?”

Zuko freezes, belatedly realizing that the Avatar’s been addressing him this whole time. He shoves down a wash of horror at his inattention, glancing up to see Toph frowning faintly at him, more curious and confused than disapproving, and Sokka giving him a questioning look that Zuko doesn’t know how to respond to here, and the Avatar looking excited, and Katara not looking at all. Zuko’s heart pounds once, twice with relief, sharp and breath-stealing before settling into a moderately more even rhythm.

“What, ah—”

“Firebending training,” the Avatar repeats easily, without an ounce of judgment. “When can we get started?”

“Tomorrow,” Zuko blurts, immediately regretting it. Shit, he doesn’t have a curriculum worked out, no training plan. But then Zuko’s been stuck on the basics long enough that he should be able to get through the first day or two with just that, right? How fast could a twelve-year-old who’s already mastered the three other elements and has lifetimes of subconscious memory to call on pick it up?

…Fuck.

The Avatar is nodding, at least, and looking pleased by the answer. “I have afternoons with earthbending tomorrow, and maybe some waterbending before dinner, but I’m sure we can —”

“No,” Zuko shakes his head. “In the morning. Firebending is best learned in the morning.” Zuko’s inner fire twists with the realization that he just tried to dictate proper bending practices to the Avatar and he tries to breathe it back to something more level. “I mean, of course, if—”

“That works too,” The Avatar says brightly, leaning back on his hands.

“Where?” Katara asks without looking up from her cooking, face half-curtained by the fall of her hair.

“Uh…the Eastern Plaza?” If it’s anything like Zuko remembers, it’s wide open, has a minimal amount of wood paneling, and enough walls that the wind shouldn’t interfere too much with any young flames.

She grunts. “Fine.”

“What she means,” Toph drawls, “Is see you there.”

“You…want to learn too?” He supposes breath control is helpful for everyone, and it will be mostly physical fitness and endurance work at the start, but—it’s Katara.

“Nah,” Toph answers for her. For all of them? “Training is a bit of a spectator sport around here.”

…Great. Fucking great. He glances over to catch Sokka’s eyes on him again, searching, questioning, asking things Zuko doesn’t entirely understand, let alone know how to answer here in front of everyone.

“Let’s not get ahead of ourselves,” Katara suddenly says, tapping her spoon sharply against the cook pot. Zuko makes quick note, as everyone looks at her in surprise, of the exits and just how much liquid is in that pot. “He isn’t training anyone in anything until he agrees to the rules.”

“Pretty sure he’s sitting right there and you can address him directly,” Sokka bites out, head still bent but his polishing cloth stilled. His body is suddenly radiating a kind of focused intensity that Zuko isn’t used to seeing from him. Is it over Katara’s rules? Their conversation earlier today? Or is it because of the looks he keeps shooting Zuko’s ways, seeking and concerned. Or maybe Zuko’s become an object of disagreement within their group. Again.

“What did you have in mind,” the Avatar asks, conciliatory, and Zuko shoves those thoughts aside and tenses in readiness.

“First off,” Katara says, giving the pot a vigorous stir—it’s reassuringly rice-like. “No bending unsupervised.”

Zuko inhales a shocked breath, his inner flame flaring in protest, nearly spilling past his skin. This…isn’t starting well. And this might be more of an imprisonment than the Avatar’s welcome suggested. He’s suddenly achingly conscious of his instinctive awareness of the cookfire, of the heat of everyone around him. Does she mean this, too, and not just generating fire? Fuck, Zuko doesn’t even know how to turn this off, it’d be like trying to eat without tasting.

“Katara,” Sokka says, voice sharp, nothing more than her name but packed with reprimand and exasperation and you-promised and barely-hanging-on-to-my-patience.

“Really?” Toph huffs. “Are you even trying?”

“That’s not fair,” the Avatar agrees, sitting back upright in afront, which unfortunately shifts him closer to Zuko.

“He burned Toph!” Katara protests, familiar blue eyes spitting unfamiliar daggers as she glares at him. “He *just* did that!”

“I surprised him when he was sleeping,” Toph says, waving the whole thing away. Zuko… hadn’t, actually, been sleeping. Just trying to. But now maybe isn’t the time to point that out. “Just announce yourself going into his room at night and you’ll be fine.” A pause. “Right, Snoozles?”

Zuko barely manages to keep himself from staring at Toph in open horror, but he can feel heat crawling up his face again, the squirming feeling of being overly seen twisting in his throat. Agni’s *balls.* It’s not that Zuko expected it to be exactly a secret, Sokka spent the night enough that people can obviously *infer*. But—isn’t Toph like twelve years old? Do they just all *talk* about it? That casually? Fuck, how much do they *know*?

Self-immolation, he reminds himself, accomplishes nothing. Even if it seems incredibly appealing right about now.

“These need to be real, Katara,” Sokka is saying, fixing her with an annoyed scowl. “Come on. Would you stay somewhere where you weren’t allowed to bend?”

Katara’s face makes the ‘no’ very clear, in a belligerent kind of way. “Fine,” she relents. “But no wandering off on his own. If he’s going somewhere, he tells someone.” Sokka shifts like he doesn’t much like the sound of that either—Zuko adds another tally to the ‘actually imprisoned’ column and starts mentally stepping through all the Temple’s side passages to the surface—but Katara glares Sokka down before he can voice another protest. “After a week, he can be in the temple on his own. After another week, the grounds. You see how it goes?”

Zuko…is pretty sure that was one of those rhetorical questions.

“He isn’t a prisoner,” Sokka says, voice low.

“Consider it probation,” Katara bites out.

“What, forever? Or maybe you just restart it whenever you feel like it? Or how about until your—”

“We shouldn’t treat him different,” the Avatar cuts in with a frown, heading off what Zuko could tell was about to be a burst of angry words. “He’s part of the team now.”

“Then he shouldn’t mind letting us know where he is,” Katara shoots back. “Because none of you wouldn’t answer if I asked.”

“Yeah, *asked*,” Sokka snaps. “Not—”

“It’s fine,” Zuko breaks in, his inner fire spiking and sharp when all eyes swing onto him, and Agni, he can’t even look at the mix of confusion and outrage and anger on Sokka’s face right now, even knowing it’s not directed at him. “It’s…fine. I can do that.” It’s not the worst thing, really. It’s not like there’s anything he needs to do other than train the Avatar for now. It’s not worth them fighting over. And, well—if he really needs to, Zuko knows he can get out.

But Toph is making a weird face that he doesn’t understand, so maybe he should have just stayed quiet, not assumed that his input mattered. After all, even if it’s a better imprisonment than he expected, it’s still looking like an imprisonment. Prisoners don’t generally get a say in things. Even if Sokka is staring at him like he’s waiting for some cue Zuko doesn’t know how to give him, and even if he did…He shouldn’t push it, not when some part of him is still surprised they aren’t talking about chains.

“Alright,” Katara finally says when no one suggests that it is, in fact, not fine. “Next—”

“That’s not enough?” Toph mutters, apparently unconcerned that it might rile Katara up, which Zuko…doesn’t understand even if Sokka’s nodding along, glaring. Zuko wonders if something about him burning her feet made her decide to needle Katara for the day. Katara ignores it, though, so maybe Toph’s just always like this.

“—If someone tells you to leave them alone, you do it. That one is non-negotiable.” Her voice turns hard, dark with something that feels uncomfortably close to anger. “That one never goes away.”

“But…that’s just common decency,” the Avatar says.

“Yeah, well, some people apparently need it spelled out.”

“*Katara,”* Sokka hisses, low enough that Zuko can’t tell if it was meant to be private, and Toph shifts, looking briefly uncomfortable as the siblings glare at each other.

Zuko clears his throat into the tense silence—he thinks it's tense, at least. Maybe it’s just tense for him. “I don’t—yes. That’s—fine.”

Katara doesn’t entirely look like she believes him, but she doesn’t make it a fight. “Next—”

“How big is this list, Sweetness?”

“*Next—*you pull your weight with the chores. You might be a Prince and used to having servants running after you everywhere, but no one gets special treatment here. Someone tells you to do something, you do it.”

Sokka sits upright, entire body stiff as he stares at Katara, mouth working silently. Zuko flexes hands callused from fire and swords and weeks of laboring through the Earth Kingdom and years of climbing surfaces that weren’t designed to be climbed, and speaks before Sokka can voice whatever’s about to burst past his lips. “Fine.”

“Last—” Katara scowls at Toph before narrowing her eyes back on him. “If we’re in trouble, you fight on our side. *Actively* on our side. Not sitting out, no standing aside.” Her face is set with challenge, and Zuko feels a cold trickle of dread slither down his spine. “You don’t get to sit out of the fight just because you don’t like it. You’re with us or you aren’t. And if you aren’t, you leave.”

Zuko’s breath freezes in his throat. This…he doesn’t know if he can do this. It would be easier to hold his bending in, at least he has something like practice at that for all that he sucked at it. This…He draws in an audibly ragged breath, hating how much it reveals that it takes him a few tries to manage to find words. “…I won’t become a weapon against my own people.”

“You can’t just expect him to take on every one of our fights,” Sokka protests. “You’re out here blowing up factories and you think he should just go along because you say so? Are you going to make that a *chore*?”

“In case you weren’t aware, we’re fighting the Fire Nation here,” Katara snaps, glaring Sokka into silence. “You can’t just show up and sit on the side and then decide to be part of things again when the danger’s done. You don’t get to only be here when it’s convenient.”

“That’s not—I know we’re trying to overthrow my—the Fire Lord,” Zuko says. “But he isn’t the Fire Nation. They’re not the same.” Please, let them not be the same. Zuko’s risking a lot —everything, really—on the belief that his people are more than what their rulers this past century have tried to make them.

“No one is trying to have any unnecessary fights,” the Avatar says, back in soothing mode, apparently, not that Zuko thinks it’s doing much good

“We don’t go out of our way to get involved in battles we don’t have to,” Sokka echoes, eyeing Katara as he says it like he shouldn’t need to remind her. Zuko wonders if he’s needed to before.

“I can fight on your side,” Zuko says, marshaling his composure. “I *will* fight on your side. But I won’t just—kill Fire Nation civilians for no reason. Or harm towns that don’t deserve it. Or try to hurt foot soldiers who aren’t doing anything but the job they were told to do.” No one should have to be punished for the decisions of others, and Zuko…he doesn’t want to walk over this, but training the Avatar is *a* means to an end. It’s not the only one.

Katara’s face tightens, but Toph leans forward before she can speak. “That sounds reasonable to me,” she says, overly loud.

“Agreed,” Sokka says, scowling at Katara and nearly tripping over the end of Toph’s words.

The Avatar turns to Katara, big-eyed and serious. “I don’t think anyone wants to attack anyone else unless there are no other choices.”

“…Fine,” Katara mutters. “But I wouldn’t assume the Fire Nation thinks the same thing, Aang.”

Zuko waits for more, Katara just grabs up bowls and starts dishing out some kind of stewed rice and vegetables thing and—is that really it? Just as suddenly as it started? Zuko’s still so tense with uncertainty that he nearly fumbles the bowl that Toph casually shoves in his direction with unexpected accuracy, but Sokka is giving him a look that is…reassuring? Questioning? Soothing?

It’s a look that’s something, at least, enough that Zuko is able to take a deep breath and settle the food awkwardly into his lap, frowning as the bowl keeps tipping. Zuko knows how to keep it steady when he’s kneeling, but this cross-legged seat is all uneven and tied up. And he can’t think about how Sokka always managed to do it—bowl balance on one knee, gestures loose as he talked around a mouthful, usually shirtless—without his mind tripping toward places it really shouldn’t go right now, for a number of reasons.

Before he can catch the impulse Zuko flicks a quick look at Sokka, who has his own bowl settled just like Zuko remembers. Sokka’s gaze catches his for a single heartbeat, full of worry and concern and lingering frustration, and Zuko slides his eyes back to his own food and abruptly realizes that his earlier appetite is gone.

Toph heaves a giant sigh and rolls her eyes—isn’t she blind? How did she learn that?—and starts shoveling food into her mouth with…actually very neat manners.

Zuko knows he should eat too. He barely had any breakfast the Day of the Black Sun and it’s been a while since then and there wasn’t much to scrounge in the dark last night. But his stomach is tight and roiling again from all the tension and spikes and crashes of adrenaline over the past few days. Or maybe more from the fact that Zuko has people sitting on both sides of him and no idea what’s at his back, and Sokka is across from him which is great, but the Avatar on his left which…is not the least bit calming. Though he supposes it’s still better than Katara if it were Katara.

The fireside slowly fills with the sounds of spoons knocking against bowls and quiet chatter and the unmistakable feeling of people looking at him. Zuko feels overly exposed with nothing but his new rules to fall back on, none of which exactly apply to mealtimes. Unless someone tells him to leave them alone. In which case, Zuko supposes he would just…go to his room.

Zuko risks another peek up, eyes automatically dragging toward Sokka, who’s still staring at his bowl, brow furrowed and not really participating in the conversation, not even eating he’s so lost in thought. Is he…is Sokka always like this? It’s so different thank Zuko is used to, but then, this whole situation is different than Zuko is used to. Or maybe he’s just this quiet and withdrawn because Zuko's here and Sokka—Sokka doesn’t want him to be? Except Sokka said he *was* glad that Zuko is here, just this morning, and has been stealing looks and being *concerned,* and Zuko isn’t sure how concern works with needing space but he doesn’t get the impression Sokka is worried for Katara, here.

Maybe *about* Katara, which…Zuko understands. Little sisters aren’t something it's typically safe to ignore.

The urge to just get out of here and away from the eyes and reactions he doesn’t fully understand and the expectations he doesn’t fully grasp is suddenly clawing through Zuko’s chest, and he blurts out the first thing that comes to mind that might let him get out of here without questions. “Can I go, and uh—can I go take a bath?”

Agni’s tits. He shouldn’t have said that. Did he just make it weird? Weirder? Fuck, he definitely just took an uncomfortable thing and made it worse, because now everyone is openly staring at him with various levels of surprise and startlement.

“You’re hauling the water,” Katara finally says, stabbing her spoon into her dinner like that will physically keep her from needing to help.

“Oh.” Zuko glances around. Where do they even haul the water from? “Is the cistern system broken?”

The Avatar slowly turns to him. “…The what?”

This…really didn’t get Zuko away from eyes and reactions and expectations the way he’d wanted. “The bath system?” Zuko offers tentatively, glancing around and avoiding any single person’s eyes. “On the highest level? With piping all down through…”

Sokka is openly staring. “…The what?”

“It uses pipes and these—channels to gather rainwater from the surface…” Zuko should have listened to Engineer Heng more when she explained, but he—well, he wasn’t exactly retaining much back then. But it would be great to be able to lose himself in a technical explanation right now, because Zuko does *not* like the way they’re all looking at him. Except Toph.

And Sokka, whose expression is finally losing some of that tension and worry it’s had over the entire meal in favor of a rising let’s-knock-the-walls-down-and-see kind of curiosity, so… maybe this isn’t actually so bad?

“How—how do you know that?” The Avatar asks, sounding…choked? Tight? Angry? Is he angry? Zuko shifts, trying to scoot back without being obvious about it so he can get more of the Avatar into his field of vision without losing Katara.

“I…” Zuko flicks his eyes toward Sokka, who’s looking increasingly excited and animated, full attention on Zuko like he can’t wait to hear what Zuko says next. Sokka who…wants them to share important things. And this doesn’t feel important, just like a normal piece of Zuko’s history that didn’t come up before, but maybe to Sokka it would be. “I came here after —when I left the Fire Nation. The first time. I spent some time…” Clearing out remains and relearning how to stand when the world still felt like it was spinning under his feet, metaphorically and physically. “…exploring, I guess.”

Sokka looks like he’s aware of something unsaid in that pause, and also like he isn’t going to raise it. Then Zuko is flinching back as Katara intercepts Zuko’s look with a glare, and Zuko clamps his mouth shut and drops his eyes down to his lap, fiddling with his spoon. They still didn’t say yes or no to him leaving…

The others are debating whether Toph can open up some walls or not—the Avatar is firmly on the side of not, Sokka is making a strong pitch for the benefits of indoor plumbing even as he keeps half an eye on Zuko, that frown slowly returning, and Toph is insisting she can put it back the way she found it—and Zuko…still wants to leave. If he needs to tell someone where he’s going before he goes there, does that mean he can’t go if they don’t say it’s okay?

“Hey, is it story night?” A piping voice suddenly calls from somewhere behind Zuko’s shoulder, a deeper voice following with, “Is that jook?”

Zuko is on his feet in an instant, pivoting to put his back closer to a wall, adrenaline surging as he tries to choose between keeping the Avatar, Katara, and this new threat in his field of vision. Fuck, he’s not—he not supposed to *attack*—he needs—with a gasp Zuko yanks his heat sense back in, the bright flare of Sokka against it making Zuko realize he’s let it spill outward, let it *seek*.

But Zuko can’t make himself let go of the campfire, the flames firmly in his grasp and pacing to his breathing—too fast, too thin, flickering—as he tries to calm himself because it’s just— it’s just the other three, the three Zuko doesn’t know. The three strangers who are all staring at him with open curiosity, at his scar, at his red, red, red clothes, and their faces are going still and scared and angry and full of questions and so are everyone else’s and—

“Zuko,” Sokka says, halfway to his feet, nearly dumping his mostly-full bowl onto the ground in the process.

“I’m going to go to bed,” Zuko bursts out, waving Sokka to stay because he just—*he* needs space. His voice is too tight, too high, and he hates himself for being so weak that all this is spilling out so clearly. He doesn’t wait for permission, just gives them all a sharp, quick nod and then does *not* run off, aiming for the deep shadows and the south entrance. It’s not the direct route back to his room but Zuko can’t—those three kids were in his way. And Zuko needs to settle himself, needs to quiet his inner flame, needs to just…settle.

He forces himself to take deep, grounding breaths when he finally manages to escape to shadows and darkness and privacy, belatedly yanking his fire sense in and wincing when he tugs so hard his inner flame stings in protest. Some teacher he’s going to be.

Agni’s tits, this might somehow be harder than Zuko thought. Harder even than being back home was, because at least there he could ground himself in the memory of Sokka’s wanting and Uncle’s happiness and the possibility of more. At least there he knew what was expected of him, even if he also knew he would never be able to truly meet those expectations.

But even with Katara’s conditions openly stated, Zuko is realizing he still doesn’t know enough about how he’s supposed to act here. He isn’t surrounded by enemies or subordinates, he isn’t serving tea, he isn’t an anonymous refugee or a Crown Prince. Agni, it feels more like Azula’s risky brand of allyship than anything else, which…should make it familiar, actually, but it still isn’t because Zuko understands this even less than he does hers. Especially when he doesn’t know if falling back on the reassurance and support Sokka seems to be offering crosses some boundary Zuko’s still trying to understand. Is it just habit on Sokka’s part? He understands that Sokka wants some kind of openness between them, for them to volunteer and share and speak up, but—in front of the others, too? Or just when it’s them?

Agni, Zuko doesn’t like feeling this close to being adrift again, Uncle gone and Sokka needing *time*, whatever that means, and Azula openly set against him. He slumps back against the wall, reaching desperately for that sense he had in Ba Sing Se, looking out over that first snow, that his path was clear before him, that certainty that he could walk it on his own and chart the destiny he wanted for himself, for the world. A feeling that wasn’t predicated on anyone’s validation and approval but his own.

That feeling is still there, once Zuko manages to soothe his inner flame enough to be able to feel anything beyond its sharp-edged near-panic. Nothing is done yet. Nothing is ruined yet. It might look a bit different than it did at the start, but the path is still there, still clear. And Zuko might prefer to walk it with others, but that doesn’t mean he can’t stand on his own feet if he has to. Even here.

He might want to see approval in Uncle’s eyes or pride in Sokka’s, but at the end of the day, Zuko isn’t here for validation. It’s always been about seeing his three most important things through all this and nothing else. He might hope otherwise, might dream of more, but Zuko knows better than to expect to have anything left but ashes for himself at the end of it. The consequences of burning bridges.

Zuko slips through half-remembered corridors, trailing his fingers over scrollwork and intricate carvings, finding the chips and mars that he remembers from swords and spears and who knows what else that left its mark in fire-scarred stone and wood. This isn’t a place for the Fire Nation, he reminds himself. It never was.

And Zuko needs to get himself under control because they aren’t here for him to be a mess, they’re here for him to teach the Avatar. Zuko left Caldera with his eyes open. The Avatar, Katara—this was the plan all along, after all. Zuko isn’t here to be welcomed, or to make friends, or to be with Sokka. He’s here with a purpose. And Agni, Zuko wants so badly the right to call Sokka his again, to think of himself as Sokka’s in return, but at the end of the day, Zuko is aware that he started walking this path because he wants—*needs*—more for himself than only that.

&#45;-

Zuko wakes from a new nightmare—the Western Air Temple falling from its perch, blasted by the Avatar in a white-eyed rage, all of them falling into an ocean below that is cold, cold, cold crawling down his throat—with his body aching in that full-body clench way that he knows he’s going to feel in the morning.

He sits upright, ignoring the raw feeling in his throat in favor of reassuring himself he can gulp in as much air as he wants, trying to shake off the images just like he tries to shake off the wild idea that Sokka could have just slipped out of the room right before Zuko opened his eyes, with the way his brain is conjuring that leather-sunshine-metal scent of him. Which is how Zuko’s nightmares usually go, these days, like his subconscious has decided that waking needs to be a form of punishment too.

&#45;-

Sokka pads on near-silent feet back toward his bedroll, pointedly ignoring the looks he can feel Katara and Aang giving him in the lingering silence after Zuko’s nightmare. He can feel the curious uncertainty from Haru and Teo as well, where they’re whispering to The Duke, but that’s easier to ignore, especially with the way his hand is still trying to close over the shape of a scroll that isn’t his anymore, not now that he’s given it.

Sokka knows intellectually that those strangled, hoarse screams aren’t still echoing off the stone, that they cut off as abruptly as they started. But he can still hear the choked cries ringing in his ears like he had hoped he wouldn’t, can still feel the urgency that turned his careful tiptoeing into an all-out sprint vibrating in his legs. Spirits, Sokka isn’t so egotistical to think that he’s the reason for Zuko’s dreaming, but hopefully, the words Sokka found in himself to give can still help in some way.

Sokka still brushes his thumb over that linen-wrapped bundle at the bottom of his bag most days, can still bring to mind every word they exchanged, can calm his heartbeat calming if he immerses himself in the shape and memory of Zuko’s characters on the page. Maybe Zuko was—is—the same.

“…So,” Toph says in the darkness. “The third-floor ceremonial rooms, huh? The ones with no windows and big thick doors.”

“Drop it,” Sokka mutters as he nudges Momo aside to slides back under his blankets for what’s probably going to be another sleepless night. “It’s done.” They sure as fuck aren’t going to move Zuko now that they’ve settled him, not unless Zuko asks for it. Sokka won’t have him thinking that he’s a problem that they’re trying to hide away.
