## Chapter 13: Performance Anxiety

### Notes

#### Chapter Notes

Warning in this one for internal thoughts that might read in a 'victim of abuse' way

(Please feel free to drop a comment if you would prefer not to read and I can provide a high-level summary, or answer any questions)

### Text

Zuko rises with the sun the next morning, Agni’s touch fizzling through his blood, pulling him from the light doze he finally managed to find as dawn was just beginning to shade the sky. He feels sandy-eyed and sore and what on anyone under the age of ten would get called cranky, but on an adult, he’s pretty sure gets categorized as irritable instead.

He briefly thinks about spending some time trying to sort himself into something marginally more composed—he hasn’t truly meditated in…a long time—but quickly discards the thought. He can already tell that nothing like composure is going to happen this morning, not with his inner fire so sharp and restless. Nice as this plain box of a room is in its utter lack of personality, Zuko’s mind is far too occupied with all the things lying outside its door.

Speaking of the door…Zuko eyes the solid, only-a-little-rotted-at-the-edges wood like it might spring off its hinges and attack him. Is he even allowed to go through that door on his own? Or does leaving his room to find the others qualify as going somewhere without telling anyone where he’s going? He definitely doesn’t have explicit permission if he needs it. But is he really supposed to just sit here and wait for someone to come get him? What if they’re waiting for him to show up?

Zuko blows out an annoyed breath, yanking back his inner flame when sparks come out. He did not, he thinks, give Katara enough credit for the neat little coals she was handing him to burn himself with.

Zuko can feel Agni crawling higher in the sky as he strains for the sounds of anyone approaching and weighs the benefits of calling for someone to come get him against the feeling of needing to be fetched like a toddler.

They can’t possibly want to waste time sending someone to get Zuko every morning or before every meal. And if they do…then it’s just the one time he’d be making the mistake. Surely he wouldn’t get sent away after less than a day because he misunderstood. Right?

Zuko snorts. Surely Katara is full of understanding and forgiveness when it comes to Zuko.

“Agni’s steaming shit,” Zuko mutters. This is ridiculous. But he sets his shoulders and shoves a hand through his shaggy hair and pulls on a marginally less glare-y version of his usual scowl and leaves his room for the Eastern Plaza, head swiveling the whole time so he can fully take in his surroundings and anyone who might be approaching or following or… whatever.

Which turns out to be a waste of energy, because the Eastern Plaza is empty except for the first rays of early Spring sun trying to reach through the mist into the canyon. The Avatar is nowhere to be found, and after another extended bout of debating—Zuko’s Masters never came to fetch him, not even Uncle, but then Zuko isn’t exactly a Master, is he?—Zuko makes his way to the Western Plaza where everyone else seemed to be bunking down. Maybe they’re just wrapping up breakfast?

When he finally pads as quietly as he can to the entryway, though, Zuko can only stare, his chest full of some mixture of stunned and annoyed and flustered and frustrated. Everyone is still asleep. Everyone. Including the Avatar.

He…Zuko *told* them training would be in the morning. The Avatar asked, and Zuko answered, and the Avatar said that worked for him. Does that—does that mean something different outside of the Fire Nation? Did Zuko mess up converting the times, somehow? But he didn’t say a specific hour, and no one in the Earth Kingdom ever seemed confused by exchanges like that…

Is Zuko supposed to wake the Avatar up? His adrenaline spikes at the mere idea, his inner flame biting in warning. He…really doesn’t want to do that. And fuck, is he supposed to wake them *all* up? The earthbender said they liked to watch training. A wild-feeling sensation that might be a laugh bubbles up in his chest. Fuck, is he even allowed to do that? If someone sleepily tells him to go away, does he have to leave?

This is…somewhere beyond ridiculous. Fuck.

Zuko stares for longer than he would care to admit—Sokka’s hair is all loose and disheveled and half over his face, and seeing it grown out *and* down makes Zuko wants to get his hands into it even more, and it’s just…unhelpfully distracting. But finally, even that isn’t enough, and Zuko tears himself away from his brooding contemplation of everyone’s nice fucking peaceful sleep, turning on his heel and stalking—*not* stomping—back to his room.

Zuko will just…wait until he hears someone awake to come back out. Or wait for someone to come for him after all, though starting off the day with a bout of malicious compliance might not be the foot he wants to start on once he manages to burn through his annoyance. He isn’t here to demand anything of anyone, he reminds himself, let alone of the Avatar. Not time, or attention, or even wakefulness. He’s here to be of use, and if this is how they feel their time is best used then it’s not Zuko’s place to comment.

And maybe he’ll spend *his* morning reevaluating where *his* time and attention and wakefulness can be best used.

&#45;-

Zuko cautiously emerges again when he finally smells smoke on the breeze. Which turns out to be probably another mistake, and one Zuko wonders if he should have picked up from Sokka’s stories, because it turns out that Katara is the one who wakes up first to make breakfast.

Zuko teeters on the edge of entering the plaza, leaning toward escaping back to his room again when Toph suddenly mutters from a pile of haphazard blankets, “Balls, you’re  
so *loud*.” And that sends Katara glancing sharply up and Sokka jerking into wakefulness, only a quarter alert and looking blearily around for whatever set Toph off.

Zuko stills, drinking in the sight of a sleep-soft Sokka slowly turning himself back into a functional waking person. It’s achingly familiar and quietly breathtaking and distracting enough that Zuko utterly loses his opportunity to escape, and then to act like he wasn’t staring, and just…fuck it. Fuck this whole burning day already. Zuko isn’t entirely sure what he expected of his first morning, but it definitely didn’t include needing to walk a gauntlet of stares toward the campfire after being caught ogling his…whatever Sokka is.

No one points out that Zuko showing up as everyone woke up means he traveled without permission, and he files that away to mean that it’s okay that he did, the boundaries of the space he has to work in starting to take shape.

The Avatar drags himself out of his bedroll just before the food is served, which…Zuko isn’t quite sure what to do with. Zuko never thought he would meet anyone less of a morning person than Sokka, but apparently, that was a lack of imagination on his part. It doesn’t seem like a great sign, for someone trying to become a firebender on a deadline.

Zuko picks at his breakfast, unsure what to make of the hopeful, searching little looks Sokka keeps flashing in his direction and the rising tension in Sokka’s shoulders, but too focused on tracking the Avatar’s progress through his own bowl to be able to give it much thought right now. He’s starting to shift from annoyed to antsy to find an opening to ask when, exactly, they might be ready to start training when Katara suddenly drops the heavy cookpot in front of him in a clatter of metal-on-stone, and bowls and spoons and chopsticks crashing together.

Zuko flinches back, falling from his kneeling position into a ready crouch, scarred ear ringing and inner fire flaring in preparation for a fight as Sokka exclaims, “Katara, what the fu*—* unn.”

But Katara has her arms crossed, ignoring Sokka, staring at Zuko but hands away from her waterskin, which—what—

“That needs to be cleaned,” she says, words annunciated with biting clarity and eyebrows raised in challenge.

“Uh—” Everyone is looking at them curiously, but without much alarm. Except for Sokka, who’s left sleepiness thoroughly behind and is eyeing her with open suspicion. Is this… normal?

“And since I cooked…” She prompts.

…Right. Right.

Zuko eyes the pile of cookware and dishes and does a quick count of how many people are still working through their food. Dishes for eight people isn’t an insignificant amount, but Zuko’s been more in the weeds than this back in the teashop and made it through.

Of course, he had a sink there.

Zuko glances around for a basin or body of water or anything, really. “Where..?”

“I can show you,” Sokka cuts in before Katara can offer whatever she’s opened her mouth to say.

“Otherwise, Sugar Queen here might send you topside to find a river,” Toph adds, tart. And Zuko’s inner fire gives an uncomfortable kick in his gut when Katara’s glower and Sokka suddenly whipping around to glare at his sister suggests that Toph might not be entirely off the mark.

Agni’s balls, Zuko wants to try to make this work. But he’s tightly aware that they’re working on a clock that doesn’t leave much time for figuring it out.

&#45;-

Everyone, the whole crew, *including* the three new ones Zuko still can’t stop twitching around—the Avatar had asked if there were bugs that only bit firebenders, which…great, just great—are finally making their way in the direction of the Eastern Plaza once Zuko comes back with freshly scrubbed cookware and bowls. It was a quick, efficient task once he figured out the water situation. Washing dishes in the teashop was Zuko’s favorite job, if he were forced to pick one, a familiar kind of semi-mindless activity that could occupy his hands and a portion of his thoughts and let the rest of him just rest.

Zuko is picking his way at the back of the straggling group, counting heads and making sure everyone is in front of him and running through his first-day-of-training speech again when Sokka suddenly glances back from near the front. Sokka's eyes search a moment before finding Zuko, and Zuko doesn't know if he expects them to jump away or to linger, but he definitely doesn't expect Sokka to suddenly square his shoulders, visibly take a bracing breath, and then peel away from Katara. Sokka steps to the side and slows, letting the others pass, doing something that's...definitely hovering, and in a very purposeful manner. Waiting for Zuko to catch up.

Zuko eyes the set of Sokka’s shoulders, the way Sokka’s fingers are restlessly undoing and retying the end of his wrist wraps, how Sokka’s gaze is tracking Zuko's progress and ignoring the other's curious looks, and braces himself. Zuko would like to follow along with the hopeful little leap of his inner fire, but a single night doesn’t exactly seem like ‘time’ the way Sokka was asking for it.

Finally, Zuko reaches him and Sokka searches his face, hesitating before falling into step beside him, opening and closing his mouth a few times before finally offering, “…Hey.”

“…Hi,” Zuko says, trying not to get immediately tripped up by Sokka’s atypical awkwardness. This is Sokka in his own space, Zuko reminds himself. This is something new. Zuko doesn’t really know anything about what Sokka’s like here.

“So…” Sokka tugs on his wolf tail, clearly searching for words, and that isn’t exactly normal for him either. Though after yesterday, maybe it’s expected. “Did you…”

Zuko gives him a sideways look when nothing more comes. “Did I…?”

“…Right,” Sokka says, looking down and taking a quick, fast breath, “Okay. Um. You…So we’ve trained together before.”

“…Yes?” Zuko didn’t mean for his confirmation to come out as quite so much of a question, but…why is Sokka bringing up something that Zuko can’t remember as anything other than an intimacy?

“And you’ve taught me some of your sword moves and stuff.”

“Yeah,” Zuko agrees, feeling a spark of wariness as Sokka’s fidgeting increases.

“Training Aang is going to be different,” Sokka says, glancing down and seeming surprised to find he has half a wrist wrap undone.

Zuko stares. “…Obviously.” For too many reasons for Zuko to even begin trying to list.

“Sorry, obviously that’s—sorry.” Sokka winces. “I meant, Aang...probably needs a lighter touch? Than maybe how things were in Caldera?"

Zuko nearly freezes as he finally gets it, some miracle keeping his feet still moving as something like shame trying to wash over him, prickling at the surface of his skin as his inner fire shoves back in protest. He wants to refuse to let it, but—Zuko had no idea that Sokka knew. He never outright told Sokka that he was too hopeless to learn the way Azula did, the way all the Masters and Uncle wanted to teach him. But apparently, Sokka figured it out anyway. Even being a non-bender and having no idea whether Zuko’s technique was sloppy or perfect, Sokka figured it out.

Agni’s balls, it’s a fucking miracle they let Zuko stay to teach the Avatar at all instead of laughing him right back into the forest.

"You're the expert, obviously," Sokka is continuing, frowning at the ground as he steps between some rubble. "So definitely ignore me if this sounds wrong. But a few months ago, he—" “

"I’m not—I wasn’t—I wouldn’t fucking *do* that,” Zuko cuts in, feeling like he can barely expand his chest all the way. It’s the *Avatar*. He isn’t going to be miserable at firebending like Zuko is, not once he gets started.

“What?” Sokka says, head shooting up, eyes going wide at whatever he sees on Zuko’s face. “No, no, no,” he rushes to say, expression transforming into a look of horror. "That's not what I meant." Zuko’s fire still twists, hard, because great, Sokka just confirmed that he *knows*. “Fuck, I’m sorry, Zuko, I should have—I was trying to give you a heads up." A warning, Zuko hears. "You're going into this lesson and I don't know if I've ever talked about the time Aang tried firebending before?"

Zuko can only stare. "I've been there for it," he finally gets out. Hard to forget an entire island melting.

"No, not in the Avatar state," Sokka says, flicking a quick look toward the others and then lowering his voice. "When we were on our way to the North he was looking for a firebending teacher—"

"Out of cycle?" Zuko breaks in, frowning.

Sokka blinks. "Out of what?"

Agni's flaming dick. How are they still alive? "Nevermind," Zuko sighs, pinching the bridge of his nose. "Just—okay, he was looking for a firebending teacher?"

"And he found someone, and...it wasn't exactly a great experience." Yeah, no shit, it was *out* *of cycle.* "And things got a bit out of control—" Zuko bites his tongue against asking what exactly they expected, trying to start an airbender with fire before water and earth. "—and he hurt someone." ...Fuck. "Not badly, but..."

Zuko starts furiously revising every planned lesson he has in that silence.

"I think he might still be kind of afraid of it, sometimes? And I don’t know, maybe that’s normal for beginner firebenders? But I just—in case it wasn't I thought you should know," he finishes, uncertain and sounding more than a little self-conscious. "You might need to explain things a lot more and really talk theory and...yeah."

Great. Just great. Zuko's favorite. “The Avatar doesn’t seem afraid during fights.”

Sokka shrugs, smoothing flat the newly-tucked ends of his wrist wraps. “He didn’t hurt someone in a fight.”

Zuko grunts, nodding and reassessing the energy in the Avatar's step. He thought it was all eagerness, but maybe he can see the nerves that could be there under the bright grin and loud laughter.

“So just…I don’t know. Yeah. I wanted to let you know, in case no one else has.” Sokka joins Zuko in gazing at the Avatar's back, sighing. “I don’t know if Aang will bring it up himself and it seems important, and…Yeah. Not like training with me. And...I’m going to stop now.”

Zuko can’t stop the way his breath catches as his mind skips away from thoughts of fearing fire to remember what training with Sokka *is* like, and he can hear Sokka sucking in his own breath when he realizes what he said, can see out of the corner of his eye the slow creep of a dark flush under Sokka's skin. Agni’s tits, Zuko has no idea how he’s supposed to react. Pretend he doesn’t see it? Act like he didn’t hear? Acknowledge it so Sokka can try to laugh it off? Stay stoic no matter what? Zuko doesn’t know how he’s supposed to *be*, how to be with Sokka like this, in the open and not stolen away but also not whatever they were before.

And now isn't exactly the time to figure it out.

“Thanks,” Zuko finally says, clearing his throat and trying to diffuse the moment despite his own sharp embarrassment. He ignores the part of himself that wants to lean into the tension and coax more of it out. To feel the way that flush must be heating Sokka’s cool skin. “For, ah—” He shrugs.

“Yeah,” Sokka says, tugging on his wolf tail and coughing a little. “Anyway, I’ll just—”

"Yeah, I need to—"

"Right," Sokka says, already giving a little wave that stops halfway through and turns into a vague, tight gesture to go along with his sudden brisk head nod that ends with a pause and a frown and then a forced smile that immediately freezes halfway through and—

Zuko blinks at Sokka's fast-retreating back. That...that was a goodbye worthy of Zuko himself. And since he's alone at the back of the crew again and Sokka definitely won't be looking back any time soon, judging by the blush Zuko can see over the back of his neck from here, Zuko allows himself, just for a moment, to let his shoulders slump. Of course the Avatar would be afraid of fire on top of needing to learn on a short clock. Of course this wouldn't have come up yesterday when they were talking about training. Agni’s dick, why does it always have to be so hard to do the things that Zuko knows he’s supposed to do?

Uncle would have some neat, barely comprehensible phrase at the ready for this. Something like, ‘when you’re thirsty, the grown-over path you carve through the wilderness is more rewarding than the paved road to water.’ Which, just like one of Uncle’s real aphorisms, doesn’t actually make any sense. So Zuko shoves it away just like he would if Uncle were actually here—it feels just the same—and sets himself to dredging up memories he suddenly suspects he's going to need to get the job done.

&#45;-

It’s late morning when they finally get started with the Avatar’s firebending training. So still, technically, morning, but Zuko is quickly realizing he’s going to need to be a lot more precise with his language going forward. Like how he talks to Azula, maybe.

Zuko is also quickly realizing that things are in much worse shape than he thought.

Thanks to Sokka's warning he isn't caught wholly by surprise. But Sokka maybe underplayed just how badly things went, or else hasn't noticed that 'still kind of afraid of it' is worlds short from what Zuko is starting to suspect he's working with.

Maybe Zuko should have pressed for more information when they were walking over here. Does it count as sharing, if you’re asking about someone else’s business?

“You shouldn’t fear firebending,” Zuko repeats, managing to keep the frustration out of his voice because he spent half the night preparing his opening speech and now it’s all off course already.

The Avatar nods agreeably, back perfectly straight in his neat lotus position across from Zuko even as his fingers tap and his knee jiggles and his foot twitches with nervous energy.

“But you *do* need to appreciate its dangers.”

The Avatar chews on his lip, considering. “Can’t we just, you know.” He mimes throwing a punch and makes a little whoosh sound which…isn’t what fire sounds like.

“No.” He ignores the Avatar’s dramatic drooping. “Firebending starts with the breath, and with awareness of the flame. Not with—” He can feel himself making a face. “—that.”

“But I can already make a flame,” the Avatar points out, like he isn’t strung so tight that he might climb right up one of those columns if Zuko begins even a basic kata.

“Great,” Zuko says, scooting back slightly, trying to give him space. Already being able to make a flame is the problem. And maybe Zuko…underestimated how hard it would be for the Avatar to learn from someone who used to be his enemy. Or from someone who wears such visible evidence of the ways fire can go wrong. “So then you should be able to make your own to meditate over.”

The Avatar nods slowly, eyes big on Zuko with some mix of uncertainty and expectation. Right. Explanation.

Zuko frowns as he tries to break down something he can’t ever remember having to consciously think about. Even when he was reacclimating after the Agni Kai, he knew what to do. He just couldn’t do it. “You want to cup your hands in front of the seat of your flame. That’s usually the stomach, or the diaphragm, where the spark of your inner fire lives.” Zuko’s own is rather…atypically uncontained, from what he's picked up with his heat sense from the other firebenders back in Caldera. “Using your breath and your intention, you want to draw a thread of that inner flame up and out, toward your palms, and—”

Zuko lets a little fire kindle in his hands and barely suppresses his own flinch when the Avatar startles, jerking back. He freezes, watching the Avatar carefully for a moment, taking in the too-wide eyes and half-raised hands. Shit. Zuko takes a purposefully steady breath and carefully snuffs out his flame, moving with slow deliberation to broadcast his intentions and gather his thoughts.

Fuck, Zuko wishes there wasn’t an audience for this. He can feel the neat line of eyes on the unscarred side of his face, is aware that he instinctively shifted toward the defensive when Katara straightened and the Avatar flinched, and now both of them are sitting here, on edge and nervous. This…is not good.

Zuko keeps his words observational. “You’re afraid of firebending.”

“I’m not afraid of fire,” the Avatar immediately bristles. “I sit by the campfire all the time!”

“I didn’t say fire. I said firebending.” The Avatar squirms a little, suddenly looking every bit twelve years old, and Zuko wonders how badly he would have fucked up before noticing if Sokka hadn't said anything. Zuko takes a deep breath and forces himself to ask: “Just mine?” Agni, his stint as a teacher is about to be very short if the answer is ‘yes.’

“No,” the Avatar says reluctantly, and it’s inappropriate for Zuko to feel the amount of relief that he does at the answer. “It’s—I hurt someone, before. Someone important. Because it got out of control.”

“Control is one of the most important parts of firebending,” Zuko says quietly, glad he has the words at the ready. “It’s the first thing any firebender learns.” And from the flicker of guilt he sees, Zuko can guess that it was an early lesson for the Avatar, too, and one that didn’t stick. “But you can’t master control if you don’t try.”

The Avatar bites his lip, nodding along but still looking shaky and jittery, which is just about the worst place to start with fire.

Zuko sighs to himself and quietly torches his whole carefully structured lesson plan and progression. “Let’s switch things up, a bit. Let’s just—get you used to firebending, first. Being around it.” Zuko glances around for ideas, and kindling. “Fire behaves differently when it's being firebended than when it's free. Your subconscious has probably noticed that.”

The only way Zuko can describe the next hour is grueling. For both of them, Zuko thinks, as he does everything and anything he can think of to try to acclimate the Avatar to firebending as fast as possible. Zuko doesn’t have time for Uncle’s quiet, easy methods, can only silently apologize as he pulls out the bare bones of the concepts and burns away the gentleness. Zuko is painfully aware of how many days are left until Sozin’s Comet, just like he’s painfully aware that pushing this just an inch too far could make the Avatar even more skittish than he already is. But fuck, they don’t have time for him to spend months getting comfortable. It feels like they barely even have days.

It doesn’t help—for either of them—that everyone is watching. It’s all Zuko can do to keep pressing forward with the knowledge of the borderline-predatory blue eyes on his back ready to pounce with every flinch the Avatar makes. Though the Avatar, at least, seems to take some kind of reassurance in the you-can-do-it looks Katara gives him whenever she isn’t glaring at Zuko behind the airbender’s back.

Slowly, though, the Avatar flinches less and less, his hands no longer fluttering nervously around his knees, his shoulders turned full-on toward Zuko instead of angled half-away. And finally, Zuko pulls his fire sense back from the little fire he had the Avatar light with a spark rock, nearly sagging in relief to see the airbender looking calm, steady, centered despite all the contortions Zuko had been putting the flames through.

“Good,” Zuko says, clearing away the awkward tightness as he tries to get the praise out. Sokka said *not* how he learned, though, and he might not have meant the way Zuko took it, but Zuko figures it doesn't hurt to cover his bases just to be safe. “That’s good.”

The Avatar flops back in relief, letting out a dramatic gust of air, arms thrown out wide. “I can’t believe it!” He cranes his head up to look at the fire again, a delighted little grin on his face. “This is amazing! How do you *know* all this stuff?”

Zuko can’t quite stop the cutting edge to his words. “How do you think?”

The Avatar immediately sits upright, face set in an apology that Zuko hurries to wave away before it can be voiced. Someone forgetting about his scar is enough of a novelty that he doesn’t need anyone saying sorry for it. He wouldn’t know what to do with the words, anyway.

The Avatar doesn’t stop looking, though, curiosity—which Zuko hates in general,  
but *especially* about his scar—seeping into his expression. “…Is that what your nightmare was about?”

That…isn't the question Zuko expected. “…Huh?” He catches a sudden flurry of motion on his right, looking over just in time to see Sokka shoving his hand under his thigh from where he was…making a throat-slashing gesture at the Avatar? Whose face is pure oh-fuck when Zuko looks back to him. “…My what?”

“I’m sorry,” the Avatar rushes to say. Agni, Zuko doesn’t know if he’s ever received so many apologies in his life, and they’re all coming in the past few hours. He still has no idea what to do with them. “I didn’t realize I wasn’t supposed to bring them up.”

Bring…them up. Bring…his *nightmares* up. Which means his nightmares are a—  
a *conversation* topic. Zuko slowly turns to Sokka, whose face also has a bit of oh-shit about it even as he sets his shoulders and meets Zuko’s eyes. Zuko stares, that expression driving home the truth. “…You know?”

Sokka blinks, gapes. “…*You* know?”

“I—what?”

“I didn’t—you never—” Sokka shakes his head, taking a breath and determinedly meeting Zuko’s eyes. “Yes. I knew.”

Zuko doesn’t want to be doing this in front of the others but Agni, his inner fire is trying to crawl up his throat and he can’t seem to stop himself. “…How long?”

Sokka’s eyes dip away, his fingers tugging at his wrist wraps. “You don’t really sleep without them.”

Zuko just…freezes, retreating instinctively behind a glower even though he’s feeling something much more hollow than anger right now. Something more like overly seen, in so many ways, to find out now of all times that Sokka knew this about him and Zuko didn’t realize. That the rest of them know, however they know it, and Zuko didn’t realize that either. That this whole conversation is happening with a full audience to see them both being surprised by the other’s knowledge of what goes on in Zuko’s head at night.

“…Right,” Zuko says, pointedly turning back to the Avatar and just…setting this all aside for later, jerking his inner flame back down. “Right. Let’s talk about your breathing.” He refuses to feel anything at all, not even a little bit of relief, when the Avatar hesitates but goes along with the clear end Zuko wants to draw to this wonderful little moment.

&#45;-

It’s like Zuko acknowledging the others are actually there opens some kind of floodgate, because everyone might be firmly not bringing up that little interlude with Sokka, but now that the Avatar has moved on to actual foundational training—

“What is that?”

&#45;-Katara won’t stay the fuck out of it.

Zuko grits his teeth. “It’s a meditation exercise.”

“Why?”

“Because breath controls the fire,” Zuko says again, trying to convince himself that the Avatar can benefit from hearing the explanation repeated, too, and that maybe if Zuko says it enough his own inner flame will stop trying to snap out. “And you need to be conscious of your breath in order to control it.”

&#45;-

“Why are you doing that?”

Zuko pauses mid-gesture, glancing down at himself. “…So the Avatar can see what he’s supposed to do?”

“Why are you doing it so *fast*, though,” she scowls.

“…Because that’s how you are supposed to do it?”

&#45;-

“What’s this?”

Zuko determinedly doesn’t take his eyes off the Avatar. He needs to check his form, Zuko tells himself. “Hot squats.”

“How does this have *anything* to do with firebending?”

He forgets that he’s supposed to be looking at the Avatar’s form. “How does anyone’s body have anything to do with any bending?”

”*Katara*,” Sokka hisses, so low it's almost more a collection of syllabus than a name if Zuko wasn’t already familiar with the sound of him saying it like that by this point in the day. “*What?”*

“Stay out of it,” Sokka whisper-shouts. “You don’t know shit about firebending.”

“Yeah, well, it’s not like he’s a Master. So we don’t know that he does either.”

“Like *you* were a Master?”

“I am now!”

Zuko takes a sharp breath and turns away at that, pretending that he didn’t hear and that his inner flame isn’t shoving against his skin in protest. He focuses on counting out the Avatar’s reps instead of on the sting that grows larger and larger in his chest the longer the hissed fight draws out behind him, because Zuko is aware that there’s no ‘I am now’ to end the argument for him.

&#45;-

“Alright,” Zuko says, taking in the sweat clinging to the Avatar’s robes and reminding himself that the kid mentioned he has two other elements that he still needs to practice today. “I think we can call it for the first—”

“Really?” Katara cuts in, sounding so outraged that even the Avatar startles, shooting Zuko a guilty, half-apologetic look that…Zuko doesn’t really understand.

Zuko risks closing his eyes for a breath, reaching for patience because he’s almost done. With day one. Fuck. “What.”

“You’re really going to end it there? Aang’s first firebending lesson and no actual fire?” “We did fire at the beginning, to—”

“You could at least show him what he’s supposed to be trying to learn,” Katara…accuses, is the only word Zuko can come up with.

“…I wouldn’t mind seeing a demonstration,” the Avatar admits. At least he sounds sorry about it.

“See?” Katara raises her eyebrows in challenge. “What’s he working toward here?”

“Sweetness—”

“I don’t see why it’s a big deal,” Katara snaps, turning to Toph. “Would *you* hesitate to show off your skills?”

Toph doesn’t reply. Even Zuko knows the answer to that.

“It’s not a parlor trick,” Sokka says, frowning down at whatever he’s sketching out in his lap and Zuko jolts a little. Was that wording deliberate? Should he read into that?

“No, it’s *firebending*. The thing he’s supposed to be teaching Aang.” She turns her glare back to Zuko. “So let’s see what it all builds up to. Let’s see what all the fuss is about.”

“Fine,” Zuko says, jumping in as Sokka opens his mouth again. He doesn’t want to be any more of a division between Sokka and Katara, that’s not what he’s here for, in so many ways. “Fine. Just…” He glances around the cobblestones. “I’ll show one of the intermediate katas.” He takes a deep breath and tries to remind himself that he’s the teacher, here, as he addresses the Avatar. “See if you can see how the basic forms that we worked on will evolve to this.”

Zuko backs into open space, making sure everyone is far enough away to clear his flames. He takes a moment to center himself, because he knows how to do exactly this, this isn’t any different than training on the deck of the *Wani*, it isn’t, and who cares if Zuko always hated that a little, too. Then he launches into the kata he always uses to transition from warmup into real training, the one—the only one—he knows he does perfectly every single time.

Except that this time, he isn’t. Zuko can tell within the first few breaths. His inner fire is *there*, it’s moving, but it feels…off. Sluggish whenever Zuko tries to call it, reluctant where it’s normally eager to fly free, almost slippery in his grasp like he’s fighting another bender for control of the flame which doesn’t make any sense because when it comes from inside himself, it’s supposed to be *his*.

Zuko can feel down to his bones that he’s nailing the physical forms and the timing of his breaths, but all the actual firebending is coming out…kind of sideways, and flickering, and thready, and just…wrong. And nothing Zuko can think of is making it better, not changing the cadence or deepening his breaths or even trying to draw on his heat sense and his fire sense at the same time, even though he knows how useless that’s probably going to be when he’s this close to Sokka and trying to let his heat free without letting it reach for Sokka’s brightness, like having a cut in your mouth that you can’t stop poking and prodding once you’re aware of it, and fuck—is this why his fire is like this? Because somehow he’s tangled it so much up in the pathways of Sokka’s chi that now it doesn’t want to move along his own? Because somehow now that they’re close again his fire doesn’t want to concentrate on anything else? Except it doesn’t have that drunk, lazy quality he associates with moments like that. It feels exactly like it should, it just isn’t *working.*

Zuko stops halfway through the kata, closing his eyes and trying to calm himself because his heart is pounding so loud he can barely hear himself think. It feels like he’s about to overflow with frustration and anxiety and fear, so much fear, because for the first time in his life, if Zuko actually has truly somehow fucked up his fire? There isn’t a single other firebender around to help him fix it.

Agni, has there ever been a firebender as inept as he is? How do you go to bed perfectly fine and manage to mess yourself up in your *sleep.*

“I don’t—I don’t know what’s wrong,” he finally says, aiming for a level voice and thinking he probably achieved it for everyone except Sokka, who’s looking at him with an open concern that Zuko can’t deal with right now, not when his inner fire is suddenly unresponsive to his call but still *hungry* for any inch Sokka will give him.

“…What just happened?” Toph asks, wiggling her toes against the cobblestones.

“Zuko, ah—” the Avatar clears his throat. “Didn’t really firebend.”

“Isn’t *that* convenient timing,” Katara snaps, raking Zuko with a glare. “You what, forgot how to firebend just in time to ‘defect’ from the Fire Nation?”

“There’s been a lot of change over the past few days,” the Avatar frowns at her. “A lot of stress. It’s totally normal for that to impact your bending. At least—” He shifts toward Zuko. “It is for the other elements?”

Zuko shrugs, helpless, at least able to answer the Avatar where he can’t seem to find the energy to engage with Katara. “I don’t—this has never happened before.”

“Could it be because of the eclipse?” Sokka asks, voice odd, almost…hopeful? Zuko must be misunderstanding his tone, and the look on his face, and the stillness of his body.

“It was fine before,” Zuko reminds him, his inner fire shrinking back against his spine— where it shouldn’t get to hide, it hasn't earned the right to hide—at the idea of his tether to Agni snapping during the eclipse and not coming all the way back again.

The Avatar rubs the back of his head. “You could just be like…blocked up?”

Toph pipes up. “Performance anxiety?”

And now on top of everything Zuko’s going to *die*. Katara’s face freezes and Sokka turns absolutely scarlet, but manages to say with admirable evenness—Agni, like Sokka has to do this a lot, fuck, fuck—“Toph. Do you know what that means?”

“Yeah,” Toph rolls her eyes. “Like in the Earth Rumble, when someone shows up for the main event and gets nervous in front of the crowd and instead of having a good firm base, they go all limp and useless.”

Katara chokes, and Zuko vaguely wonders what it would take for his inner fire to get on board with the idea of setting a nice distracting blaze on the other side of the room so Zuko can flee.

“Sure,” Sokka says faintly, sounding strangled. “That’s…about the gist of it.”

“Have you ever—”

“What good is a firebending teacher who can’t even firebend,” Katara cuts in, and Zuko doesn’t know whether to be thankful or not that now they’re all back to focusing  
on *this* aspect of his inadequacy. Agni. What the fuck has he gotten himself into. “We might as well have just gone with Sokka’s idea and found a scarf dancer or whatever.”

*That* was who Zuko beat for the spot? A *festival* dancer? Who can’t even *bend*?

“Maybe you just need to get back in touch with the roots of firebending,” Toph shrugs. “Go back to the source. Sometimes your head gets too full of other stuff and it can distract you from your roots. But once you understand the source? You can always get back to it.”

“What,” Sokka says sarcastically, cheeks still tinged dark. “Did you spend a lot of time in the gardens?”

Toph flicks a stone with unerring accuracy, pinging it off his shoulder hard enough to leave a mark. “I ran away from home and learned earthbending from the badgermoles.”

Sokka slowly closes his mouth. “…Right.”

“The air bison were the original airbenders,” the Avatar says, bouncing a little on his toes. “Katara, who did the first waterbenders learn from?

Katara looks reluctant to offer non-combative participation in a conversation that includes Zuko, but finally says, “In the North, they said we learned from the moon and the tides.”

“So was Agni the first firebender?” Sokka asks, not-quite looking at Zuko like he isn’t sure where to put his eyes still after Toph’s little interjection.

Zuko blinks, wondering if he lost the thread of what they were talking about. “The sun doesn’t firebend,” he finally says. “The sun is fire.” Water can’t waterbend itself. Right?

…Right?

“So who was the first?” The Avatar asks.

“The dragons,” Zuko says, rubbing at the back of his neck and hiding an instinctive wince. It’s hard to break a lifetime of habit on the subject. Everyone can acknowledge that it’s an awkward topic these days at best, even the ones who supported the hunting.

“Well, let’s go find some then!”

Zuko stares. ‘Everyone,’ apparently, doesn’t include the Avatar. One hundred years in the ice, he reminds himself, and not even a year yet out of it. “…They’ve been extinct for a long time.”

“What?” The airbender rocks back onto his heels, looking horrified. “But—there were so many when I visited the Fire Nation before.”

Zuko shrugs, feeling a stab of bleakness as the Avatar’s expression turns pleading. “A lot can change in a century, I guess. They used to live all over.”

“What *happened?*”

Zuko fidgets, uncomfortable, but when he glances up for help he can see that none of the others know it either. Agni’s balls, why does he have to be the one to explain this to a pacificist vegetarian? “It became a sign of great firebending mastery, to kill a dragon,” he finally says, looking down at his feet. “You got a title and everything, if you did. There’s only one person left alive now who’s done it. They…went quick.”

“The Dragon of the West,” Toph says slowly.

Zuko doesn’t reply, and Sokka slowly sits back in the silence, brow twisted with something Zuko can’t entirely read, something that looks close to upset, which…why would Sokka care about dragons?

“Shit balls,” Toph finally says succinctly, shaking her head. “Well. What’s the next best thing if your idiot culture killed its own source?”

“The Sun Warriors, I suppose,” Zuko sighs after a moment. “They’re the earliest human benders I’ve ever heard of.” Azula had had an intense, one-week fascination with them when she was six or seven that ended as abruptly as it started when she realized that they were conquered during the Warlord Era just like everyone else.

“Wait a second,” Katara says, looking around, incredulous. “Are we seriously talking about sending Zuko off on his own to get in touch with himself or whatever so he can ‘relearn’ firebending?”

“Wait,” Zuko says, blinking. “What?”

“Good point,” the Avatar says, offering her a happy smile. “I’ll go with him!"

"Uh, Aang—"

The Avatar keeps speaking right over top of Sokka. "That way we can learn together!”

Zuko…doesn’t think he succeeds in masking his genuine, quiet horror. Hopefully Sokka’s the only one who can read it.

"Just the two of you?" Sokka asks, and Zuko winces at the way Sokka's voice comes out a shade too high. "We can all—"

"Just us!" The Avatar says, turning the full force of his enthusiasm on Zuko. "Just two firebenders learning from the world and the wisdom of those who've come before us. We can share the process of discovery and awakening knowledge, it's going to be so great!"

"Um." That sounds...awful. Zuko's had enough wisdom from his ancestors to last a lifetime.

"Yeah, sure, sounds great," Sokka says with a frown, eyes flashing between Zuko and Aang. "But you need someone to read the map to get there, right?"

"I bet Zuko can do maps, he lived on a ship!" Zuko...didn't think he would ever regret Sokka teaching him that.

"Alright, well you still need someone to watch your back while you do your learning thing," Sokka tries.

"I'd be happy to watch your backs," Katara cuts in, and Zuko's inner fire flares in alarm, which—where the fuck was all this flaring a few minutes ago?

"No, you need to—train," Sokka says, clearly glancing around for inspiration, his gaze hitching on Zuko, open with uncertainty. "And...heal people? Zuko's good with his swords, so —"

"I thought they needed someone to watch their backs?" Katara asks, eyes narrowed, and while Zuko appreciates that look no longer being directed at him, he doesn't exactly feel any better seeing it directed at Sokka. Especially when the topic is still him. "Why are you trying to go along with them so bad?"

"I..." Sokka freezes, visibly grasping for words. "Don't you want someone to go, too?"

"Yeah. But I want to know why you're acting like it needs to be *you*."

Sokka's eyes flit to Zuko, unsure, and the idea of Sokka laying out all of Zuko's fears and anxieties to see if the other's judge them worthy enough, or fuck, of Sokka lying to his friends to keep them hidden—no. Zuko just...needs this conversation to end.

"It's fine," Zuko hears himself saying, voice shockingly steady as all eyes swing to him. "If this seems like the best course of action, I'll go with the Avatar. We can...process our discoveries. Together." Whatever the fuck that means. But Zuko can't stop himself from reaching again and again to assure himself that his inner flame is still *there*, even if it isn't responsive, and...Zuko just needs *this* to end, too.

If Zuko’s firebending is well and truly fucked…that suddenly doesn’t leave him many paths left at all, and none of them ones he cares to take.

"No, it's *sharing* the process of discovery," the Avatar is saying, nearly vibrating with excitement. "I'll tell you all about it!"

Great. Great. Whatever it takes.

&#45;-

The morning feels like it’s lasted years when they finally break for lunch. Zuko trails the others back to the plaza, eyeing the mess that’s been made of his nice clean cookpot. Haru and Teo and The Duke—is that really the kid’s name? It can’t be. Zuko’s just going to avoid ever addressing him until it's safe—handled the cooking, and Zuko…doesn’t actually have the energy to care about this right now.

Zuko’s last in line, happy for the moment to have everyone in front of him and turned away and no one staring or sneaking glances or peeks or tossing concerned looks his way. He takes advantage of the thin privacy to do his own peeking, watching Sokka pass out bowls as Teo fills them, his face shadowed by a worry that hasn’t left it since Zuko’s bending failed.

Zuko supposes, theoretically, that Sokka worrying for him is nice. But Zuko himself is so far past that point that he can’t quite comprehend what it would be like to be *just* worried right now. He feels like he’s moving on nothing but pure instinct and reaction, his mind fuzzed with a numb kind of *oh-shit-oh-shit-oh-shit* dread over the idea of going on some kind of two-man adventure into firebending’s past with the Avatar. Fuck, what if it doesn’t work and the Avatar gets mad that Zuko’s a bare step above a festival dancer himself right now? What if he thinks Zuko deceived him? What if he melts another island? What if Zuko’s still on it again?

Zuko grabs both bowls from Sokka’s hands when it's finally his turn—fingers *not* touching, he at least has that much control left—turning toward the array of toppings as Sokka twists away to say something to the three chefs about salt and flavoring.

It’s a familiar rhythm between them as Zuko adds quick-pickled vegetables and herbs and a portion of meat to each, slightly more to one than the other. Then he trades the meat-filled bowl to Sokka with an absent “here” in exchange for a jar of chili paste that Zuko’s careful not to use too much of—he hasn’t seen another jar around, so this one has to last just in case —finally trading the chili paste back for a set of chopsticks.

Both of them tap their chopsticks against their bowls, sliding them into a more comfortable grip, turning together so their arms nearly touch to look for a seat and suddenly freezing.

…Fuck.

Zuko can see the realization coming over Sokka’s face the same way he can feel it creeping up inside his own chest, the sudden awareness that they just fell back into a habit that they built in a privacy they don’t have anymore. That they just acted as if they were the only two people in the room when they definitely are not, and now all those other people are staring with various shades of surprise and amusement.

“…Don't stop there," Toph says agreeably, patting the stone pavers next to her in offer of a seat and grinning over at Sokka as if she can tell that he's faintly blushing again. "So," she says as the two of them make their slow way over, taking a bite of her lunch and smacking her lips. “Have a favorite congee shop in Ba Sing Se?”

&#45;-

Katara wordlessly shoves the cookpot in Zuko’s direction after lunch with the same silent, eyebrow-raised challenge before she gathers up a surprised-looking Avatar for his waterbending lesson. The airbender opens his mouth, glancing between Katara and Zuko before snapping it shut and trailing after her.

Zuko…doesn’t understand the interplay. And honestly, he doesn’t want to know, much as Azula might berate him for turning away information. He just can’t deal with it right now, even knowing he needs to figure it out if he’s going to try to be part of this crew, and a pile of dishes is exactly the excuse he’s been itching for to get away from the curious-concerned-probing *looks* everyone has been giving him.

Zuko is arranging the cooking implements for easy carrying when he suddenly registers Sokka lingering again, grabbing up the bowls and neatly arranging the chopsticks, his hands stuttering when he glances up and catches Zuko looking.

“Need, ah—need help?” Sokka asks, glancing down at his neat stack of dishes like he’s suddenly questioning whether he’s supposed to be holding them.

Zuko…doesn’t know if Sokka is. “I can do it,” he says cautiously, wondering if it counts as shirking chores to not be the only one doing them.

“I know,” Sokka says, tugging on his wolf tail. “Do you want help? Or—I can go, too. If you want some space..?”

Zuko considers the lack of looks coming his way, other than Sokka’s, and how nice it would be to lose himself in a mindless task against his ability to actually do that now that he’s noticed that Sokka looks like he has something he wants to say. “…You can stay.”

They finish gathering up the cookware and dishes in a silence that doesn’t feel entirely companionable, not when Zuko’s trying so hard not to feel anything at all right now but the still-present heat of his inner flame, but it at least doesn’t feel like yet another thing Zuko needs to ward himself against. They finally set off for the fountain the crew uses for their cleaning—Zuko took one look at how Sokka was trying to balance the bowls and made him take the cookpot instead—and it’s not until they’re moving that Sokka finally speaks. “Can I ask you something?”

“Yeah,” Zuko says slowly, trying to read the tenor of the words. Worry, yes, but maybe some reluctance? And an edge of guilt?

“Are you okay?”

Zuko gives him a flat look, nearly coming to a stop.

“Okay, that—” Sokka winces. “Yeah. Sorry. I guess I meant can I—can we help?”

“I think it was made pretty clear what the solution is tomorrow,” Zuko says, anxiety tightening in his chest, making him sharp.

"That's just one option though, right?" Sokka says, giving him a quick look. "I bet we could figure this out another way. You know so much theory, and there's so much bending knowledge here. You can get in touch with the roots of firebending, sure, but what if it's something physical, or psychosomatic, or—"

"It's decided, Sokka," Zuko says, striving for levelness and refusing to even think about opening his head up to the others right now. Sokka? Fine. The kid whose name Zuko can't even remember? Katara? "We don't have time to figure out something else."

“Yeah, but—" Sokka cuts him a quick, anxious look. "Are you okay with going off with Aang tomorrow? Do you want to?”

Zuko’s skin itches, inner fire twisting. He doesn’t want to be *handled* right now. “I want my bending back.”

“Right,” Sokka says, glancing down at the cookpot in his arms, uncertainty chasing across his face. “This...does seem like a good way to at least get some clues. Do you…I mean, I know Aang isn’t the easiest, for you.” Zuko sets his jaw against the reminder. “If you wanted, I could try to come with you guys again? Or not me, maybe Toph, or—”

“No,” Zuko says, giving a sharp shake of his head. That would open the door again to *why*. And besides, Zuko doesn’t want to have to worry about loyalties and distractions and keeping track of anyone except the Avatar tomorrow. Even Sokka—Zuko doesn't know if he can stay alert like he needs to be tomorrow if Sokka is there.

“Okay,” Sokka nods, brow still furrowed. “I could also talk to Aang?”

“Please don’t.” Fuck, Zuko wants that even less. The idea of the Avatar being aware of just how on edge Zuko always is around him…Zuko’s running as far as he can with the fact that the Avatar apparently has no idea just how unsettled he makes Zuko. Zuko knows all about faking a thing until it becomes enough of a habit to maybe be true, about clinging so hard to perception that it starts to become reality.

“Alright,” Sokka says quietly as they finally reach the fountain, setting down the cookpot and then looking like he has no idea what to do with his hands except frown at them. “If you change your mind, I’m…here, I guess. I’ll be around.”

“Yeah,” Zuko sighs, dropping down his own armful. “Okay.” Agni, the day is barely even half done and Zuko already feels exhausted and he just…needs a break from the implication that Sokka thinks he can’t handle tomorrow. Or that Zuko could handle it if they do it a different way. Or...whatever is being implied, here. “I think I have it from here,” he adds.

“Oh. Yeah, of course,” Sokka says, blinking, hesitating before stepping back. “Sure, I’ll…see you at dinner, then?" Another awkward step toward leaving, clearly without knowing how. "Shout out if you need anything.”

“…Sure,” Zuko says, mustering up this at least. “See you at dinner.” Then he turns himself toward the task at hand, trying to block out everything else beyond building up the foundation he’s going to need for tomorrow. As Uncle would say, hands that are busy with warp and weft belong to a mind that is…also busy with warp and weft? That can’t be right. Was it, hands empty of work are like a mind empty of thoughts? Zuko glances down at his hands before giving a little shrug and reaching for the first bowl, ready to keep his hands busy and prepare his mind for what’s to come.

&#45;-

Zuko’s grateful that the Avatar has other bending lessons in the afternoon that apparently are equally worthy of spectating, because he's craving the time to himself. He’s sitting in his room where he can hear anyone approaching, back to the wall beneath the window so he can keep his right eye on the door as he tries—in vain—to get his bending to work. Sokka is right, Zuko *does* know theory. Caldera Standard theory, Uncle's theory, the theory found in old scrolls long out of date.

It's just that like always, knowing doesn't actually seem to matter.

He can grab and manipulate external fires just fine, can heat things up and bleed heat from one thing to another, but nothing he can think of will make his inner fire manifest. Which he’s trying not to panic about, which he *won’t* panic about, because panicking has never helped anything. It’s just that that’s the fucking core *fundamental* part of firebending. Carrying their element inside themselves is what sets firebenders apart from the other elements. It’s what makes them the touched of Agni. You can’t *be* a firebender and not be able to access your inner flame. And you certainly can’t be a Child of Agni.

Zuko’s down to seeing if he can snap himself back into place—not really anyone's theory but his own, by this point—shoving his fire and heat sense out and then yanking them back in sharp enough to sting—like popping a dislocated shoulder back into place, or…something like that—when he feels a body-sized concentration of heat at the far end of the hallway.

He tenses, instinctively reaching for his fire and then silently cursing as he remembers that no amount of reaching is going to help. But as the only thing up here other than empty rooms, Zuko assumes whoever it is must be coming for him, especially with how quickly they’re moving. Zuko can at least reach out with his heat this way still, getting a feel for whoever’s approaching before their footsteps become audible. It’s not Sokka, he can tell that immediately, but he can’t keep thinking of him. Maybe because there’s a similar kind of ebb-and-flow in what he’s feeling, but more, and—

And Zuko is an idiot.

He’s on his feet, not even bothering to pretend to be doing anything but eyeing the door when Katara steps into the open doorway, filling the space with a white-knuckled, wide-set stance that says she’s braced for a brawl. Zuko takes in the bag in her hand. There’s no way it could hold water, and it doesn’t look heavy enough to be full of rocks but that doesn’t mean it still wouldn’t hurt if she comes at his head with it. He considers and immediately discards the idea of squaring up in his own ready stance. He can just imagine what provoking her that way would result in. And Zuko remembers Ba Sing Se. If Katara’s here without water, if she tries to start something purely physical…well, Zuko spent weeks dancing around the Dai Li without his fire. And if she does have water? Zuko remembers Sokka’s tight fury back in the Jasmine Dragon well enough, too.

Fuck, though, part of Zuko wishes they could just punch it out and have it all done with, the way he sometimes saw his crew doing when Uncle and Lieutenant Jee weren’t around.

“You might be getting what you want,” Katara finally says—accuses, more like—blue eyes flat in a way that has Zuko’s shoulders pulling in tight. “But you better know that *I’m* not fooled.”

Zuko bites back a stab of humorless laughter. “What about this do you think I *want?”* Agni’s balls, how many private threats is she going to deliver before she finally decides the message has been received?

Maybe as many as it takes to get Zuko to leave.

“Going off on your own with just Aang. At his suggestion?” She rakes him with hard eyes. “Quite the *long game*.”

“That’s not—I’m trying to help,” Zuko protests, wondering why he’s bothering to waste breath on words. “I *want* to help.”

“Sure, suddenly you want to *help*. Suddenly you don’t care about your *honor* anymore, just about being helpful. How convenient.”

“Nothing about this is convenient,” Zuko grinds out, looking away as much as he dares because those words were more bare than he ever intended to be in front of her.

“Don’t try to play me, Zuko,” Katara says, eyes narrowing. “That shit might work on Sokka, and it might be working on Toph, but I’ve been on the receiving end of *this* before,” she growls, leveling a finger at him. “And I know where it ends up.”

“I’m not—I’m not trying to play anyone,” Zuko says, wanting the words to come out decisive, confident, and instead hearing them low and tired. It’s hard to bear up with the weight of her distrust so heavy on his shoulders, even with his inner flame high with readiness. But it’s not like he didn’t earn it. It’s not like he didn’t know he was earning it.

“No, it just all seems to work out so nicely for you, doesn’t it? What luck.” Her words are saccharine sweet and utterly laughable. “Always finding your way from one side to another and then right back again. And now you’re here,” she says, fists clenching so tight Zuko can see the hard lines of her tendons, “And tell me Zuko, what comes next? How long this time before it’s back again?”

Zuko folders his arms over his chest to keep from flinching, forcing himself to feel the way her words hit far too close because he’s earned it, he’s earned this bit at least. “That’s not—I can’t go back. Not after—not with the Fire Lord—”

“And that works out nicely too, huh?” Her face twists, and her features aren’t really like Sokka’s but—just enough that seeing them this way makes Zuko’s fire twist with unhappiness. “Attach yourself to the people trying to dethrone daddy dearest and step right into the power vacuum.”

“…I’m not trying to be the Fire Lord.” Zuko can think of a number of things he would prefer to do instead, starting with lighting himself on fire.

She gives that a derisive snort. “Remind me, are you still Crown Prince? Or did they finally strip you of your titles?”

Zuko can only stare in response, keenly aware of the Crown Prince’s headpiece tucked in the bottom of his bag. Even if he doesn’t technically have the right to wear it anymore, Zuko knows how important symbols are, how strong the laws of possession are. There’s a reason Azula was so angry it went missing in the first place.

“Whatever,” Katara finally mutters, tossing her hair. “Just know—you might have tricked the others, but you haven’t tricked me. I know *exactly* how fast Appa flies. Sokka’s going to show me *exactly* how far away this island is. And if you aren’t back exactly when you’re supposed to be? There’s nothing in the world that’s going to stop me from finding you. And Zuko?” She waits for him to flick his eyes to her face, to take in the deadly seriousness of her expression. “If Aang gets hurt in any way, I will freeze your fucking *blood*.”

Zuko wonders at the luck that brought two murderous fourteen-year-old bending prodigies into his life. “Katara…”

That’s apparently the wrong move—it usually doesn’t work on Azula either, come to think of it—her face going bloodless with anger. “Don’t try to—you—don’t try to fucking *calm* me. We lost a *lot* of people in *your* capital city, and you want to just waltz in here and act like you weren’t part of that?”

“I didn’t—”

“You might not have fought but don’t act like you don’t know that you were involved,” she hisses.

Zuko stares for a long moment, yanking back his inner flame and trying to find his footing in the conversation again because…he doesn’t actually know what she’s talking about. Zuko has a sense—foreboding. The sense is foreboding—that she’s referencing specific events, and a suspicion that her particular rage means it has to involve Sokka, and, well—Zuko knows how Azula has a way of burrowing into the back of someone’s mind to live long after she’s left the room.

He picks his words carefully, trying to be conscious of all the pieces he still doesn’t have. “I haven’t been working against you since—”

“Save your words,” Katara cuts in, waving them away. “Or use them on Appa.”

“…What?” On…the sky bison?

Katara throws the bag at his feet, the gesture sharp and tight and angry and Zuko is halfway toward defending his head and bringing up his fists before he realizes she isn’t aiming for it. “You want to ride Appa tomorrow on your little field trip? Then you can groom him and get him ready today.” She whirls, apparently fulling willing to leave Zuko to figure out the rest, but pauses in the hall to grudgingly add, “Sokka says dinner will be ready when you’re done. So hurry the fuck up.”

Zuko waits until he can’t feel the heat of her on his level of the Temple before finally exhaling. Agni, he…really hopes that the last part was a Katara addition.

He crouches down to grab the bag where it’s skidded along the floor, sifting quickly through its contents to see brushes and combs and scissors and what strikes him as a very large nail file and some kind of inexplicable pick thing that Zuko might know what to do with if he were about to groom Jasmine, but with a sky bison…maybe he can just set that one aside for now. What he doesn’t see is any kind of oil for Appa’s fur, even after he dumps the bag out onto the floor, which…maybe that’s just an ostrich horse thing?

Or maybe the Avatar and his companions have no money, no allies, and no supply lines. Maybe they barely have soap for themselves, from what Zuko’s seen of it. He can’t exactly expect bottles of scented grooming oils.

It would be nice, though, considering Zuko’s about to spend the better part of a day on Appa’s back tomorrow.

Zuko sighs at the reminder and begins repacking the bag, huffing in annoyance when he realizes he tossed the pick thing just out of reach—this fucking *day—*and pausing halfway through leaning for it. The afternoon sunlight is starting to stretch long fingers across the floor, and—is there something under his bed? Zuko would have noticed yesterday during his restless examination of the room. Did it come out of the bag somehow?

Zuko scoots forward on his knees to reach under the raised platform, just brushing the edge of whatever it is with the tips of his fingers. But that glancing touch is enough to have his breath stuttering, his heart pounding once, hard, in his chest, his inner flame going utterly still and tight and ready like the littlest spark might send it burning outward.

Zuko squeezes his eyes closed, sucking in a slow, deliberate breath as something like dread or anticipation or disbelief or longing or maybe all of them together starts climbing up his throat. That was paper. A roll of it, like a scroll, since it moved when he touched it. Something that could so easily get knocked to the ground and lost. In the midst of a nightmare, for example, so that you might not even realize it was ever there when you woke up.

Zuko slowly presses himself flat against the sun-warm stone, concentrating on the ambient heat and reining back the desperate surge of his inner flame, pacing his breaths slow and steady against the wind and ensuring his hands are completely dry before reaching under the bed and snagging the scroll.

He wonders if he’s imagining the throb of recognition at the weight and feel of the paper, at the sight of its uneven edges and spotted imperfections. Is he kidding himself that he can make out the shadow of characters through the page enough to know exactly what he’s going to see before he even unrolls it? Or is it just that there’s nothing else in this moment that Zuko can accept finding except the familiar strokes of Sokka’s handwriting.

*Dear Zuko Zuko Dear Zuko*

*I don’t know how to start I’m not really sure what to say I have so much in my head I* *keep remembering you walking away*

*You asked me for words, earlier today. And I’ve been so full of things I wanted to say to* *you and ask you since you left in Ba Sing Se and seeing you before, after everything, and* *suddenly not being able to say anything, it just gave me even more that I wanted to say.* *But then when we finally did speak, I don’t think I gave you the ones I meant.*

*So I’m trying again, and maybe I’ll do it better this time, and maybe you’ll be willing to* *read it, because I’ve been thinking since you left since we made you leave that I messed* *up, and after talking to you today, I’m pretty sure I messed that up, too. At least it* *doesn’t feel like I got it right because things aren’t supposed to feel this bad when* *they’re right, are they? because I’m so full of things I feel like I need to say still if only I* *could be in front of you to say them, except that didn’t go so well is sharing even* *possible after that and it felt like the early days, so…this.*

*First off—I am so happy you are here. It’s such an unexpected gift for more reasons than* *And I’m more sorry than I know how to say that I didn’t make that clear yesterday when* *you first showed up. It’s like my head is full of so much that I can barely think. Like I try* *to make the thoughts come and they just don’t, or like nothing makes sense until hours* *and hours later when it’s far too late. I used to be able to figure out all the things that* *could come next but now I’m thinking I never saw much of anything at all. But that’s* *what I’m supposed to do, you know? That’s what I do, and it’s feels like all I can do to* *put on a good face and I don’t even think it’s that good because I’m not I don’t know how* *to fake my way through this one. Except it feels like everyone needs me to be able to do* *that even more than before, now, and there’s so much in my head that it’s like I can’t* *hear and I can’t think and—*

*I started this before dinner, but now I’m realizing that I definitely really did mess up,* *didn’t I? Spirits, I didn’t know how to make you comfortable without airing out all your* *business for everyone, and I know you hate that, and it seemed like you wanted space* *and I didn’t want to push but now I’m wondering if that was a mistake, too? If I should* *have followed you or pulled you aside or maybe just brought you food in your room in* *the first place except I don’t want you to be alone there even if I think you were still*

*I don’t like that I did nothing when you came here to do something. I don’t like that my* *head was so full and everything was hurting so much that I couldn’t see anything else,* *not even when you were standing right in front of me twice*

*But I do think I still need time. Because what if I keep not seeing you? What if I can’t* *ever figure out what comes next? It’s not that I want to walk away like that’s some kind* *of gift to you. And I hope this isn’t walking away unless you want. But I’m so afraid that* *I’m going to keep doing nothing if I don’t figure this out and I’m so afraid of I don’t* *know if you see it like this always but sometimes it seems like the people in your life who* *are supposed to be there for you and care for you and help you end up hurting you* *instead. And I’m realizing that maybe I’m one of them, too. And it feels so scary, and I’m* *so afraid of how much that makes me feel because isn’t not being able to look past my* *feelings what caused the problem in the first place? But its about you, not me, and I* *don’t want to not be there for you. But I don’t know what to do when it feels like* *everything I do is wrong, even doing nothing. And I’m so afraid of messing it up another* *time. How many chances does a person get?*

*I don’t even know what I’m hoping to get out of writing this. For you to know that even* *though I don’t think I can be your boyfriend lover romantic special person right now,* *that doesn’t mean I don’t want to try to be there for you? That I just need to figure out* *how? That there has to be something between nothing and everything? That I’m sorry?* *Probably for more than I even know what to apologize for. We were friends first, right?* *Or did we go too fast? (I don’t think you have my letters anymore. I still have yours)*

*Your Friend Pen Pal,*

Zuko reads the letter twice before he finally sits up, then three more teams leaning against the bed, then another two by the window where he can angle the paper against the light and try to see the pieces that have been inked out, wondering if Sokka meant for him to still be able to guess at what’s underneath.

Finally he smooths the paper flat against his thigh, tipping his head back with a sigh, his inner flame a complete tangle, twisting and turning back on itself. This…would probably be why Sokka was giving him so many searching, lingering, hesitant looks this morning. But Agni, what is Zuko supposed to do with this, when he barely understands—still—half of what Sokka is trying to say? When he’s seeing it now instead of whenever the fuck Sokka left it? When his bending is broken and he has chores to do and plans he needs to figure out how to make work if his bending never comes *back*, and Katara to deal with, and on top of it all Zuko didn’t exactly leave Caldera with any fucking *paper*.

Zuko takes a moment to leash back his inner flame, because who knows what it will do when it’s feeling like this and apparently doesn’t move to his will anymore. Then he forces himself to get to his feet, wavering a moment before tucking the letter beneath his pillow and grabbing up Appa’s bag. He makes himself leave his room at a steady pace, walking himself through breathing exercises and active meditation routines, trying to blow out his frustration and the sharp worry that lives alongside his still-active, still-unresponsive inner flame and leaves little space for anything else. Certainly not for things like figuring out whether he’s supposed to reach across the gap Sokka’s made between them in response to this, even though he has no idea what that would even look like or what it would mean right now. And fuck, when Zuko doesn’t even know how wide that gap actually is, between this letter and Sokka’s words and Sokka’s silence, between today and yesterday and the Day of the Black Sun and everything that came before and between.

&#45;-

Zuko shows up to dinner desperately in need of another bath, every part of him covered in fur and sky bison spit drying on at least a quarter of his body. Agni’s balls, it feels like Appa’s musk-and-grass smell is in his *clothes*. Zuko just *cleaned* them.

He’s physically exhausted and so far past done with this day and the only thing keeping him from just going straight to bed where he can attempt to mentally prepare himself to not completely lose his shit tomorrow is the fact that Sokka apparently specifically wanted him to know about dinner, and after reading that letter, Zuko thinks he needs to know why more than he needs the extra space.

So he’s running on the dregs of his energy and control when he walks, with all the grace of a drunken sailor tripping off the end of the docks, into the fact that Sokka somehow managed, with whatever they had on hand, to make rice in the style of cold spiced sesame noodles. Zuko’s favorite whenever Sokka brought dinner for them in Ba Sing Se.

Zuko stares at his helping, overwhelmed and utterly still so as to not upset his suddenly teetering equilibrium. He vaguely registers the sounds of Katara and the less-good-earthbender gasping and coughing through their first bites.

“Tui and *La*, Sokka, did you mix up the sweet peppers and the chiles?”

“…Something like that,” Sokka mutters, flashing Zuko a look almost too fast to see before staring fixedly down at his own bowl, something that might be a flush or might just be firelight and shadow moving over his cheeks.

Zuko finally unlocks himself enough to take a second bite, briefly closing his eyes to savor the taste. It’s heat and spice and thick sauce and it’s not the same but it’s *trying,* it’s an *effort*, and Zuko has absolutely no idea what he’s supposed to read into the gesture, or into the worry still on Sokka’s face. Is this what an apology looks like? Is that trying to be there while not being able to actually do anything? Agni, all it does is fill Zuko with more questions he doesn’t have the mental space to deal with right not, until all Zuko knows for sure is that things like this make it hard to remember that he resolved to do this all on his own.

And annoyed that he still doesn’t have any fucking paper.

&#45;-

Momo lets out a chitter of protest when Sokka slips into his bedroll that night and almost immediately crushes the lemur in his haste to fish the edge of the scroll he can feel brushing against his bare arm out from the mess of blankets. Fuck, it better be a scroll. Is this—who else would—

“Everything okay over there, Snoozles?” Toph calls, low enough to get lost under the sound of the others getting ready for the night, propped up halfway toward sitting like she’s about to come over.

“Fine,” Sokka gasps, finally closing his fingers around his target and then immediately loosening them when he feels the paper crush in his grip. “Fine,” he says, clearing his throat and hitting something a bit more even.

“…Alright. If you say so.”

“Just moon peachy,” Sokka whispers, sliding back down into the covers and murmuring a quick apology to Momo. Worry and uncertainty and excitement and nervousness are a churning mess in his stomach, a feeling so familiar and so like those days before the North— before the Fire Festival—that for a moment he could laugh from it that after all this time he’d be holding a letter again and feeling like this. The past few days aren’t for laughing though, and Sokka doesn’t think he can wait a moment longer after spending the whole day in agony over what Zuko must have been thinking and feeling and wanting to do but holding himself back from and—

Sokka blinks when he shifts around to get his hands into the light and his blanket still protectively up over his head and feels something hard digging into his side. He whispers another apology to Momo as he squirms to reach under himself again, pulling out…what is unmistakably Katara’s ink and brush.

…Right. Sokka will just…hold onto these. Maybe put them in an obvious place near his bag. Along with a stack of paper, when he realizes after a single moment of heart-pounding fear—

“*Sokka*?”

“I’m fine, Toph.”

“You really don’t—”

“I promise it’s fine.”

&#45;-that he’s staring at his own words not because Zuko is throwing them back at him, unread or rejected, but because he’s added his own to the back, their dark shadow half-imposed over Sokka’s own messy, scratched out characters.

Sokka flips the page, anxiety in his throat when he notes the brevity, taking a moment to pull Momo reassuringly tight and warm against his chest before opening his eyes and reading.

*Sokka – I don’t really know what to say, but I suppose that isn’t new. You gave me a lot of* *words, and I appreciate that, I do. But I still don’t know what you mean. I don’t* *understand what you want from me here. You say you need space and then that you’re* *going to try and then you’re making me food and sending me letters (in the night? Were* *you there, right before I woke?). Is that what friendship is to you? Things unsaid in a* *new way? Are you trying to go back to pretenses and being one thing to each other on* *paper and another thing in public? Because you asked to end that in Ba Sing Se. And* *you might have the scar but that doesn’t mean I don’t remember, too.*

*Maybe if I’d actually seen this last night, things would be different. Maybe today would* *have gone different. But I didn’t, and today happened, and Sokka I just don’t know what* *to give you right now, not when my bending is gone (does that make us even?). I need all* *my attention on fixing that. So maybe that means I need time, too. Or at least that I need* *all my time for this. Right now, at least.*

*Your*

*(PS I just want maybe I shouldn’t (But Sokka, either way I get to decide what’s for my* *own good or not. You can’t tell that you’ve hurt me too much for you to stay without* *even asking if I’m hurting first.)*

*-Zuko*

“Sokka, really, are you *sure?”*

“Toph,” Sokka manages to get out, tucking his face into Momo’s fur and not caring that his voice has to be audibly unclear, that he has to be so clearly hiding. “I *really* don’t want to talk about it.” Not when he’s holding the evidence that he still can’t seem to find the right words to say.
