## Chapter 14: Tangled Up

### Notes

#### Chapter Notes

No particular warnings for this one!

(Except that the posting schedule might be permanently bumped, I know I said I was aiming for Tuesday still for Chapter 15 but we might be looking at Wednesday, TBD)

### Text

Sokka watches Appa yip-yip away from the Temple and can’t help the way his dread crawls higher and higher the smaller Appa gets. He’s been feeling it ever since Aang first suggested joining Zuko in this little adventure and it only got stronger over the course of the afternoon, settling hard and tight in his gut until he could barely get halfway through his breakfast this morning. It’s been constant and impossible to ignore, and the fact that Sokka can’t actually pick out the tense lines of Zuko’s body anymore does nothing but make it rise to wrap like a band around his chest.

Sokka might be newly aware, in a number of ways, of all the things about Zuko he doesn’t know, but he still knows Zuko well enough to recognize that his every-muscle-so-tight-it-might-snap tension had very little to do with climbing onto an air bison for the first time and a lot to do with his traveling companion. Zuko hasn’t said anything—never has, about this, not explicitly—but Sokka can read well enough into Zuko’s persistent visible discomfort with having Aang on his left side to see between the lines there. And now Sokka’s feeling particularly shitty watching Zuko fly away with the literal object of his nightmares.

Fuck, it’s not that Sokka doesn’t think Zuko won’t be okay, not that he doesn’t think Zuko can’t handle himself. He just doesn’t want Zuko to *have* to, not on his own. And Sokka doesn’t know if he can trust his guilt over the fact that Zuko *is* on his own after that letter back, not after he spent most of the night staring out into darkness and wondering just how often he’s projected his own wants and desires onto Zuko and never thought to check if Zuko wanted those things, too.

Iroh was the one to point out that Zuko might break himself trying to meet Sokka’s expectations, and Sokka quietly, desperately hopes it hasn’t gotten to that point, yet. Because Sokka can fix broken things, but only if he can figure out how. And all he can think of now is that Zuko asked for words and Sokka gave them to him, but clearly didn’t do it right. Or maybe didn’t give Zuko the right ones. Or too many of them? Or just different ones, or… something.

Fuck. Sokka…will figure it out.

“This is fucked up,” Katara mutters as Appa finally disappears into a cloudbank, and Sokka’s first impulse is to agree before he realizes that she’s talking about something very different. Sokka holds back a sigh. Good to know that her bad mood isn’t just a product of Zuko’s physical presence. Apparently, the mere concept of him will do, too.

Still, it *is* fucked up. Less than two days of having Zuko around, *always* around, not bookended by missions and shifts and returning relatives and the steady clock always ticking down their time together. Less than two days, and Zuko is gone again. And on top of everyone else Sokka is missing so soon after getting them back? On top of so recently needing to leave nearly all of them behind? There’s something about watching Zuko fly away, even knowing he’ll come back, that sits heavy and hard and uncomfortably in Sokka’s throat. With the fallout of the eclipse—Dad injured, Bato becoming smaller and smaller on the ground behind them, Azula’s smirk— still something Sokka actively remembers moment to moment instead of something his mind has accepted as fact, Sokka just…needs what few of his people he still has in his sights to be okay.

Though there might be a kernel of a blessing in Appa finally disappearing into the skyline, because with Zuko gone for the day—

“There better not be a scratch on him when he comes back,” Katara grumbles, popping the cork of her waterskin like she’s already getting ready. For healing or for revenge, Sokka isn’t sure.

—Sokka doesn’t have to worry about piling more stress and anxiety on Zuko’s shoulders by finally having it out with Katara.

“Katara,” Sokka says, dragging his eyes off the sky to give her a flat look. “It really feels like you want to start something right now.”

“I didn’t say that,” she mutters, tossing her hair in a dismissive gesture that Sokka hasn’t fallen for since he was thirteen.

“No, let’s do it,” Sokka says, crossing his arms and hearing the way his voice goes hard. “Let’s start something. You clearly want to. Let’s get it out.”

She eyes him, body wary and jaw set with stubbornness, and Sokka is just…so done with trying to step gently around her anger, especially now that he has at least half a day’s reprieve from worrying over who’s going to take the heat of it.

“Know what I did last night?” He ignores the face she pulls, refusing to let himself get derailed by her discomfort when she hasn’t cared a single bit for anyone else’s over the past day. “I tried to figure out when I became someone who would let his sister be a bully.”

“What?” Katara yelps, indigent and stung out of her silent treatment.

“What do you mean, ‘what,’” Sokka says, incredulous. “Did you hear yourself yesterday? Because I did. And shit, how much were you holding back because I was sitting next to you?” She rocks back on her heels, guilt flickering over her face, and Sokka feels his anger truly spark. “What the *fuck*, Katara? What were you thinking? You *know* what it feels like for your bending to not work. Did you forget the North already? Did you forget *Hama*?”

“That’s not the same,” Katara says immediately, face darkening. “The moon died—” Like Sokka needs the fucking reminder. “—the bending was *gone*. That’s nothing like—”

“It’s exactly like!” Sokka says, hand slashing through the air. “Zuko’s going through the exact same thing, and for *hours* when it was just—just what, minutes for you? And you decide that the best thing to do is try to make him do the fucking dishes again? *Why?* Why would you *do* that?” He truly, genuinely, doesn’t under*stand.*

“His bending was working just fine before,” she snaps, squaring up and clearly finding her footing on her own anger.

“So that’s it? That’s *it?*” Of all the fucking stupid— “You think he’s lying? That it’s some trick to get Aang alone?” Sokka could laugh at the thought, if every part of him didn’t feel so tight right now. Spirits, the convoluted—they don’t exactly post a watch at night. It’s all Sokka can do to hold back that Zuko would only need to wait for Aang to fucking fall *asleep*.

“We still don’t know if he’s on our side!”

“He fought for us, in case you forgot two whole days ago when he was saving our lives!”

“Once,” she says, sounding thoroughly unimpressed by it. “He fought on our side once.”

“Twice, if you count freeing Appa. Three times, if you count freeing Aang. Four times, if—”

“And how many times against?” She cuts in, glaring as Sokka fumbles, because he doesn’t exactly have those numbers readily available. And also doesn’t think she genuinely wants a count. “He might say he’s changed, and *you* might be comfortable just taking his word on it —” Her tone makes it *very* clear what she thinks about that, which does nothing for the wavering confidence in his own judgment that Sokka wonders if he should just give up on rebuilding. “—but I haven’t seen real evidence yet. I’ve only seen the enemy.”

“Come on, Katara, what evidence—”

“All he’s done is had some bad dreams—”

“He’s done a bit more than that.”

“—if they’re even real—”

“They are.”

“—and everyone acts like he’s a whole new person. But know what? I have bad dreams too, and *his* face is front and center in them.”

Spirits, Sokka really hopes she never tells him that. “And that makes it okay? To treat Zuko like this?”

“I’m not treating him like anything,” she huffs, glowering somewhere between offended and annoyed.

“Stop playing stupid, yes you *are,*” Sokka bursts out, frustration spiking so hard his voice cracks. “Zuko’s trying to do something he thinks is right, something that *helps us*, and you’re going out of your way to make it harder for him. Spirits,” he shoves his hands through his hair. “What else have you been doing?”

“Nothing!”

“Really?” Sokka scrapes her with a look, putting every inch of skepticism he feels into it. “Nothing? Like how threatening him in Ba Sing Se was nothing?”

“Not everything is about you, Sokka,” Katara snaps, dripping acid.

“Well it sure as fuck feels like it is when you’re coming at my—” Sokka chokes off, his anger suddenly wobbling against uncertainty over what he could possibly finish that sentence with, considering the letter that’s newly imprinted on his brain.

Katara’s eyes narrow. “Your what,” she prods, voice sharp, and Sokka takes a deep breath and forces himself to reach for the only thing he feels absolutely sure of.

“Someone who deserves a lot more than he’s gotten here so far,” Sokka says, the words coming out low and ragged. “From either of us.”

Katara physically recoils from the idea. “You don’t—we—I don’t owe him anything!”

“Yes, we do!” Spirits, how did Sokka miss how deeply her hostility is rooted, that they’d even be arguing about this in the first place? “We owe him a basic fucking level of decency, and I didn’t think I would need to say that to you!” And for himself, too, much as it’s like a knife to the chest to realize it. Because how else could Sokka have lost sight of the fact that just like Sokka sleeping with Zuko isn’t a character reference for Katara, Sokka feeling safe around his friends doesn’t mean a single for Zuko.

“Don’t talk to me about basic decency,” Katara growls, hands tight fists. “We’re feeding him, aren’t we? And giving him a place to sleep, and—”

“Fuck, Katara, is that really what you think?” Sokka feels nearly lightheaded with horrified disbelief. “Have him do all your chores and don’t make him sleep on the ground in the woods and expect him to be thankful for it? I thought after traveling through the Fire Nation and seeing he wasn’t working against us, that you’d—”

“What,” Katara cuts in, her fists clenched in open frustration. “What? What did you expect, Sokka? That I’d just get over it? That I’d just forgive him because suddenly it’s inconvenient for you?”

“I *thought*,” Sokka says, feeling fury and worry and desperation tangling in his chest, “That you’d stop acting like every Fire Nation person you see is the embodiment of evil. Fuck, Katara, I just—I don’t understand where this is coming from! I feel like I need to watch you during the full moon with the way you’re acting.” He refuses to let himself feel his instinctive stab of guilt and regret as she flinches, her face going bloodless.

“The Fire Nation hurt us,” Katara finally manages to say, voice shaky and low and tight. “They’re who you’re fighting against, in case you’ve fucking *forgotten*. They hurt you—*he* hurt you—and he—they—hurt me too! And Dad, and *Mom*, and the whole—”

“Zuko isn’t the Fire Nation,” Sokka protests. “You can’t hold Zuko responsible for every single thing—”

“He’s their Crown Prince!”

“He walked away from that to be here!”

“Well then maybe he knows a little bit about what’s it’s like to lose—”

“*Don’t*,” Sokka spits, pivoting away and then whirling, sharp, back toward her. “Don’t. He already knows, you *know* he already knows in case *you* forgot that you told me what you talked to him about in Ba Sing Se!” Unless she lied, which…Sokka can’t even contemplate. “And fuck, Katara, even if he didn’t, he shouldn’t have to—to what, suffer enough to earn the right to *eat*? He shouldn’t—” Sokka’s voice breaks. “He shouldn’t have to suffer at all*,”* he finishes, feeling his eyes stinging and hot, swallowing hard against the sharp awareness of all the pain that Zuko’s felt at the hands of those who should have cared for him.

Katara stares, eyes wide, hesitating for the first time since this all began. “Sokka, you—"

“No,” Sokka cuts in, shaking his head and stepping back, feeling the way his hands are trembling as he shoves the heels of his palms against his eyes. “I’m done with this conversation right now. It’s done. Stop glaring, stop commenting, stop *cork popping*, before you do something you aren’t going to be able to heal away with some magic water.” He levels her with a hard stare, refusing to crack at her uncertain, half-stricken expression, refusing to bend. “Words don’t go away just because now you want them to,” Sokka adds, voice low with warning and throat tight with self-recrimination. “Stop before you do something you’re going to regret.”

&#45;-

“Need a training partner?”

Sokka pauses partway through the kata as Toph calls out, letting his space sword come to a halt. He’s already been at it for…a while. He isn’t actually sure how long. His muscles have that achy-hot feeling that borders on overuse, but his mind is still churning with far too much for him to rest. Did he say the right things to Katara? Should he have tried to reason with her, instead of letting his anger take over? Sokka’s always stepped back from riling her up when she’s already that upset, given her the space to calm down, but how could he keep stepping back from this?

“What did you have in mind,” he asks cautiously, because he’s seen the way she trains with Aang. Toph doesn’t exactly know the meaning of holding back, and Sokka doesn’t think he has the focus for that today.

Toph shrugs, tossing a rock from hand to hand. “I can throw some rocks at you, and you can cut them out of the air or something. I don’t know. You’re the sword Master.”

“Sure,” Sokka rolls his eyes. “Why not.” Is this some rich person thing, offering up something to hit when someone is upset and frustrated?

That’s…actually rather awful to contemplate, given what else Sokka knows—suspects— about Zuko’s childhood.

“You know,” Toph comments after a few minutes of throwing and kicking rocks over. “You’d probably do better if you weren’t so stiff.”

“Thanks for the advice,” Sokka grits out, returning his sword to the ready position and ignoring the way his arms are beginning to tremble.

“You got something to be tense about?”

As if they all don’t. Sozin’s Comet is still coming, isn’t it?

“Cause Katara’s pretty tense, too.”

Sokka snorts, darkly amused despite himself. “I’m sure.”

“So.” Toph sends three rocks flying at him in quick succession, legs, torso, head. “You tense for the same reason?”

“…Probably,” Sokka admits, somewhat breathlessly as he sets his feet for her next volley. The person you like as more than a friend going off with someone who they’re more than a little bit afraid of, while you stay behind wrangling a small existential crisis over your prior actions and what they say about who you are as a person? Yeah, he and Katara are tense for the same reason.

“Some say that a burden shared is a burden sold. Or something like that.”

Sokka sighs, closing his eyes. Subtlety is not her strong suit. “If you have a question just ask it, Toph.”

Toph suddenly shoots into a lunging kick that has Sokka scrambling to avoid cutting himself on his sword as he dives out of the way of a jutting spike of rock. She waits for him to roll back to his feet, sputtering and furious, before saying, “Stop acting like you don’t know exactly what’s been going on since yesterday. I can hear your heartbeats, remember? You’ve been freaking out since lunch yesterday.”

Sokka watches her, tense, cautiously lowering his sword when she just folds her arms and makes no move to send another rock at him. “…Do you have a baseline for all of us? For our heartbeats?”

“Of course,” Toph snorts, like any other idea is laughable.

Sokka opens and closes his mouth a few times. “…Do you have one for Zuko?”

Toph pauses. “…He isn’t exactly a calm person to begin with.”

Sokka winces at the confirmation, not that he exactly needed it. But that Toph might have noticed before Sokka did? Spirits, Sokka needs to fix this. Fix himself, and without getting bogged down in his own misery over hurting Zuko, this time.

“Do you know what he’s so worked up about?” Toph asks, shifting on her feet with uncharacteristic uncertainty. “Like why eating food seems like such a thing for him?”

“Yes,” Sokka reluctantly admits.

“And are you going to tell us?” Toph says, flicking a frustrated pebble his way.

“It’s not—”

“Or are you just going to let it bite us in the balls when we could’ve been prepared?”

…Fuck. How does he keep missing, until it's far too late, all the ways he set Zuko up to fall, here? “I’m sorry,” Sokka sighs, rubbing a hand over his face. “I just…they’re not my things to share, you know?”

“We can only work with what we have, Sokka,” she says, her tone going serious. “It’s hard to know when you’re about to make a misstep when you don’t know where the fault lines are.”

“I know,” he says. But Sokka can’t guess at this, not when Zuko’s already stretching himself so thin and sharp. Sokka can’t inadvertently tear away some shield Zuko is leaning on. But Spirits, he can’t let his fear of stepping wrong push him into inaction with this. Not again.

Toph kicks another rock up, turning it over in her hands. “You hear things when you’re a Beifong, you know,” she says slowly, cautiously. “Even the kind of Beifong that everyone wants to pretend isn’t there. Especially then, maybe.”

Sokka takes a moment to swallow back his sudden queasiness at the idea of Zuko’s past being nothing but gossip for Gaoling’s version of an Upper Ring tea lady. Fuck, no wonder Zuko hated that job so much. “What kind of things?”

“Let’s just say *I* wouldn’t want to be Crown Prince of the Fire Nation. For anything.” She shoots a significant look in his direction. “And I don’t know if I’d be brave enough to seek the origins of an element that hurt me like that.” Which says plenty about what that gossip would have been like. Toph didn’t exactly see the scar and put two and two together

“Yeah,” Sokka says after a moment, clearing his throat and desperately wishing that it could be just that. “Me either.”

Toph pauses in tossing the rock back and forth. “…Why did that feel like a half-truth.”

“Let it go, Toph,” Sokka says quietly.

“Sokka.”

“I need to talk to Zuko first, okay?”

“…Fine,” she says, flicking her rock away. “But do it fast.”

“Yeah,” Sokka snorts, shoving a hand through his sweat-damp hair. “That’s the plan.” If only wanting it to happen faster would do anything to bring Zuko and Aang back sooner.

&#45;-

Sokka is topside, theoretically watching the birds riding thermals over the gorge in between sharpening their cooking knives. Not that he would be able to sell either excuse right now, since he’s spending more time staring blankly at the sky than anything else. His muscles have a might-have-worked-too-hard achiness on top of his just-did-a-battle soreness, and combined with a quick rinse and a snack, it’s would normally be enough to make a nap look especially attractive right now.

If only he weren’t so fucking jittery with every inch the sun travels across the sky. If only Sokka thought he’d be able to get anywhere close to sleep, with everything clamoring in his head right now, half-formed thoughts and ideas he can’t seem to wrap the right words bouncing around his skull no matter how many times Sokka tries to write them out on another stolen piece of paper.

He’d tried doing this below, but everyone watching him fidget himself to a state of exhaustion between periodically lunging his way toward the brush and ink hadn’t exactly felt conducive for thinking. Grabbing their cooking knives and making his excuses to hide away topside had seemed like a good idea, a way to grab some privacy and space to think.

But it turns out the wide-open sky isn’t particularly conducive, either, when you’re desperately hoping to see something in it. And what Sokka actually has is a smattering of barely legible, half-formed sentences and a set of cooking knives that are collectively sharper than they’ve ever been before. And still, his thoughts feel stuck in a fruitless circle that runs from Zuko to Azula to Dad to the Tribe to the war and all the ways that Sokka’s never been good enough when he truly needed to be, all the ways he’s been *harmful* when he needed to be good.

Even doing nothing—or maybe because he’s doing nothing—he still freezes when he suddenly hears footsteps behind him. For a wild second, he wonders if there’s any way he could possibly escape notice, sitting exposed by the edge of the cliff like this. But the footsteps, tellingly, freeze too, before picking back up, definitely coming toward him now. Sokka suppresses a sigh.

Katara settles beside him without a word, busying herself with settling her skirts neatly around herself, neatly smoothing them before tucking them under her legs. Then she’s still, head bent, and Sokka fiddles with a blade of grass, subtly scooting paper and ink further into the shadow of the far side of his body. The constant breeze rustles leaves along the tree line at their backs.

It’s not exactly a restful kind of quiet.

Katara finally sighs, reaching into her pocket to pull out a small packet of…candied cinnamon ginger? It’s half-crushed and worn at the edges, the kind of thing she must have bought for herself at a market one day and been carefully hoarding ever since. Sokka knows her. She’s probably been having a piece each night, something quiet just for herself to savor. “Want to share?”

Sokka fucking loves candied cinnamon ginger.

Still, he hesitates a moment, trying to read her profile before he slowly accepts what’s clearly meant to be some sort of peace offering.

“It hasn’t even been half the day yet,” she mutters, eyeing the packet of candy before making her own selection.

Is that supposed to be a criticism? “You’re up here, too,” Sokka points out. Growing up with a dad who would leave and come with the tides attuned them both to the habit of finding good places to watch the horizon.

“I’m worried,” she sighs, offering him another piece as she scans the sky.

Sokka hums a noise that could be taken as agreement. She doesn’t seem as hostile and upset as a few hours ago, but it’s hard to stop himself from preemptively tensing. He doesn’t *like* fighting with Katara. But when it comes to Zuko he just…always seems to be on the verge of it.

“Aang hasn’t been off on his own since the guru,” she says. “Or—the invasion, I guess. But we were still there for that.”

“We haven’t split up in a long time,” Sokka agrees carefully. And thinking of kidnappings and near-drownings and spirits mumbo jumbo—it hasn’t generally turned out all that well when they do.

Katara’s following the same line of thought. “And last time we did…”

“He’ll be fine,” Sokka says, trying to let the confidence he feels in Aang surface above his nervousness for Zuko and his uncertainty toward himself. “It isn’t going to be like last time.” For one, Katara’s not going to get kidnapped from the Temple. So.

“How can you know that, though?” She says plaintively.

“…No one can know,” Sokka finally says, cutting her a quick glance, sighing at the worry tightening her face and trying to dredge up the words that used to come so easily whenever Katara sought him out for assurances back home. “Aang knows what he’ doing, Katara. This kind of quest to find your roots or whatever is solidly in his wheelhouse.”

“You really think that?” She asks quietly, voice suddenly fragile in a way that makes part of Sokka want to set aside everything else and pull her into a hug.

He just nods, though, not quite ready for that after this morning, still wary about where this might be going.

“Then…what are you worried about?”

Sokka pauses in the middle of picking out another piece of cinnamon ginger to give her a look.

“What? I—” Katara scowls, huffing as she turns back to the sky. “I’m *trying*.”

Alright, then. Sokka will run with that as long as it lasts. “This just…feels like it’s going to become a spirit thing, somehow.” He shoots her a sideways look. “You know how I hate all that stuff.”

“So…” He can practically hear her thinking. “It’s not about..?”

“Yes, of course it’s about Zuko,” Sokka says, exasperated. “I just got him *back*. After thinking that maybe he could be—you know.” He doesn’t even want to think about Zuko being dead if he can avoid it, let alone say it out loud. Which somehow just seems to make it that much harder to think about anything else, Azula’s voice still whispering in the back of his thoughts. “But…Zuko knows what he’s doing, too. He’s been on his own a lot longer than any of us have.” Sokka wishes the thought actually made him feel any better.

Katara eyes him, her face full of words but thankfully choosing not to push at his rather bleak tone. Sokka lets the silence stretch, both of them pretending they’re watching the hawks and not barely avoiding burning their eyes looking into the west. Katara can probably fix that kind of thing with her healing anyway, right?

“How is it so easy for you to forgive?” Katara finally asks, voice quiet enough that Sokka could almost lose it beneath the sound of the wind. “I’m just—I feel like I’m so *angry*, all the time. Even when I’m not, it’s always just…there. But you…it’s like it doesn’t even matter, to you.”

“It does matter,” Sokka says immediately, refusing to let her run with that thought even as he flinches from the reality of just how deep and wide her anger can run. He’s been on the receiving end of it enough times in his life to know how hard chipping through it can be, and he’s worried he’s already let this fester far too deep. “And it isn’t easy.” He glances over when she makes a disbelieving noise and tries to find some way of articulating the careful balance he’s walked with Zuko. “It’s more like realizing who I should blame,” he finally says. “What’s the point of holding Zuko accountable for things he didn’t do?”

“He’s done plenty,” Katara says, face dark.

Sokka slashes her a warning look. “I’m not trying to fight you about that, Katara.”

“And you’re fine with it?” She presses, brow furrowed with a more genuine kind of confusion. “You can just—let it go?”

“I don’t know—maybe? I guess.”

“…Sokka,” Katara says, staring at him in disbelief.

“What? It’s not—it isn’t ‘I don’t know,’ I don’t know, it’s just—I don’t *ignore* it. But it’s not, you know…a frequent topic?”

”*Sokka*,” Katara repeats, smacking her hands flat against the ground. “How could you get involved with him when you don’t know if you can be okay with that?”

“It wasn’t really a thing before,” Sokka defends himself, aware that he’s standing on thin ice. “Ba Sing Se was…weird. The city was weird.” Cut off from the world through a collective delusion that Sokka had, apparently, been entirely willing to engage in, too. Forgiveness just wasn’t something Sokka thought about in relation to Zuko that way, and especially not when it was just the two of them, because where would forgiveness come into it when it was just them?

“Tui and La, you can’t just run away from things you don’t want to think about,” Katara says, incredulous. “Who are you trying to be, Dad?”

Sokka hitches in surprise, staring. Why…why wouldn’t he?

Katara sighs, waving away the question Sokka can feel trying to form on his lips. “Do you actually not know? Sokka, have you really not thought about this?”

“I just…I don’t know how to explain it,” Sokka says, shifting uncomfortably. He never thought words were his issue, but suddenly it seems like he can never find any in the cacophony in his head. “I don’t think about it the way you do, and you…you get so mad.” He winces hearing himself, knowing that that can’t be a real excuse but unable to stop feeling the fourteen years of caring about it he’s trying to work against. “I know it doesn’t sound good when you say it like that—”

“You think?”

“—but even back in the city, Zuko was…” Sokka tries to find the right words. “He wasn’t lying about being different, Katara. He is. He—you’re talking about forgiveness, but it’s not like he ignores the things he’s done.” Even if Zuko didn’t necessarily see them without prompting, but Sokka of all people can’t exactly find fault in that, now, can he? “He wanted to do better. Wants. Even back then. And…that matters to me. That’s not easy, you know? To look at yourself like that and try to change.” Fuck, is Sokka newly aware of just how not easy it is.

“He has a funny way of showing it,” she bites out, words barbed.

“Yeah, well. I invaded his homeland. So.” They weren’t exactly exchanging hair beads and sonnets here.

Katara grunts, giving him a sideways look. “So what? You’re even now?”

“Now?” Sokka scans the horizon, not entirely keeping the little bit of sadness out of his tone. “I don’t know anything about now.” He doesn’t know anything about anything anymore.

Sokka can tell that she’s fighting back a lot of responses before she finally, carefully, asks, “…Are you still not sure if he’s on our side?”

Fuck sides, and the idea that there are only two of them, and that everyone has to choose just one. “Zuko doesn’t want to work against us, Katara,” Sokka says, sharply aware that the world has rarely been as black and white as she seems to want it to be. “*He’s* not going to set himself up as our enemy.” But if Katara keeps pushing, Sokka’s worried she won’t leave him any other choice.

“Zuko’s wanted to do the right thing before and failed,” she points out, managing to sound observational, for once, instead of accusatory.

“Haven’t we all,” Sokka sighs, scrubbing at his face and trying to exhale all his…everything.

“…You think he’s going to again?”

“I don’t—what am I supposed to say to that,” Sokka says, exasperated. “No, I don’t. But no one’s perfect, Katara. I’m not, you’re not, Zuko’s not—of course he’s going to mess up, we all mess up.” Right? Sokka suddenly, desperately, needs her to agree. “That’s not a reason to never give him a chance.”

“So you don’t.”

“Katara,” Sokka says, feeling exhausted, hating the way he wants to flinch from the fact that she didn’t, in fact, say he was right about messing up.

“I’m just trying to figure this out,” she huffs, scowling down at her lap.

“Yeah.” Sokka shoves his hand through his hair, hissing in annoyance when his fingers tangle and get caught. “Sure you are.”

“Don’t give me that,” Katara says, sharp. “He shows up and you go all quiet and weird? What am I supposed to think, Sokka.”

“That I’ve told you all of this before? That we’ve had some version of this conversation how many times? That—that I can make my own decisions.” He rips his hair tie out in annoyance, trying to straighten his wolf tail, frustration biting deep with the wind immediately starts picking at the loose strands. “That you could just ask me, and I’d tell you.”

“What? What would you tell me?” She shoots him an annoyed look. “That it’s fine? That you’ve got it all handled? Not to worry about it? We don’t stop worrying just because you say it’s fine.”

“…I’m sorry.” That’s… basically how Sokka feels every time Zuko says ‘fine’ to him. “I never meant to shut you out.”

“We can’t help you if we don’t know what’s going on,” Katara says, openly frustrated.

Sokka winces at the echo of his own words. “It’s just…a lot to figure out right now.”

Katara eyes him, unconvinced. “How so.”

Sokka gives her a flat look.

“No, really. How? What’s there to figure out?”

Sokka could laugh, he feels so incredulous. How can she genuinely ask that after the past two days? “Um. Everything?”

She frowns. “Is Zuko being weird to you?”

“No, he’s not—no,” Sokka says, scrubbing his hands over his face. If only. He might know what to do then. “It’s…I think I’m probably the one who needs to do the figuring.”

The line between her brows carves deeper. “And he isn’t sticking around to help? How can you—”

“No, no, it’s not—” Spirits, the last thing he needs is her getting another head of steam, or another thing she thinks she needs to defend him against. “I don’t want to make him have to deal with all of my stuff on top of everything else,” he tries to explain. Sokka desperately doesn’t want to drag Zuko down even further into this morass of uncertainty with him. “He’s got so much going on…”

“…Wow,” Katara says, sitting back. “You really *are* trying to be Dad.”

Sokka…doesn’t understand. “What—”

“Sokka, you’re the one who runs around talking to us about teamwork and doing stuff together all the time. You’re the one who says none of us are in anything alone.”

That’s…true. But it’s not the sa—

“It’s not any different just because you’re the leader,” she finishes, annoyed.

That…Spirits, Sokka is kind of horrified by the idea of trying to lead Zuko, of needing to schedule him and keep him on task. That’s…so deeply not what he wants.

“…Sorry,” he finally says, belated and more than a little hollow as he tries to shape himself around yet another thing he might have been fucking up without realizing it.

“I can’t believe you’re making me say this,” Katara mutters, dark, “But it’s not me who needs to hear that.”

“…Yeah,” Sokka says, eyes drifting back up to the clouds. “I’m seeing that.”

It’s not nearly enough time later—or maybe too much, depending on how desperately you’re wanting someone to come back before sunset and how much you still need to figure out how to tell them—when Sokka finally speaks, looking up at the clouds instead of Katara. “Are you going to freak out if I start something up with Zuko again?”

Katara sighs heavily but sets aside her sewing to lay back beside him where he’s sprawled in the grass, the fall of her hair tickling his arm. “I want you to be happy, Sokka,” she finally says. “But this…Tui and La, make sure it actually does.” She nudges him with an elbow to be sure she has his attention, her eyes serious. “Don’t just…fall back into something because it’s habit or an expectation or whatever.”

“It’s hard to feel happy about anything right now,” Sokka admits quietly. And it’s hard to imagine ever feeling that way again with the ache of the invasion so deep and sharp, even when he knows that being with Zuko used to make him feel that way. And he wants it to again, but Spirits, he needs to fix it first.

“I know,” Katara whispers, giving his hand a quick, strong squeeze.

“I…Spirits, Katara, I messed up *so bad*.” Sokka closes his eyes against the sting of tears. “Dad got captured and Bato and *everyone*. There’s no one left but me, and the technology got captured too, and you *saw* what they did with the balloons. The whole thing fell apart before it even started and we didn’t gain *anything*.”

“We all could have done things differently,” she finally says, which sure, matters, but Sokka was the one with the *plan*. “And it's back on track now.”

He sucks in a shaky breath, something painful and clumsy in his chest lurching at the idea, some desperate clawing need for reassurance that he hasn’t felt this deeply in a long time. “You really think that?”

“I might not trust him, but Zuko is a good firebender when he isn’t all—backed up or whatever’s going on,” she says, sounding like it pains her to admit it. “It’s probably better that it’s him teaching Aang than Jeong Jeong.”

“He’s more flexible than Jeong Jeong,” Sokka agrees, thinking of the rigid Caldera style Zuko had demonstrated, and Zuko with his swords blazing around him. Aang was too much an airbender for the former.

“…Ew.”

“Wh—*Katar—”* Sokka shoots upright, cutting himself off as he catches the expression on her face.

She—she did that on *purpose*. She *intentionally* tried to get a rise out of him the way she knows always works, and now she’s looking up at him with wide-eyed mock innocence, and Sokka might be flustered and more than a little outraged, but…he’s also firmly out of his own thoughts, for once.

…Huh.

“Brat,” he finally mutters, grabbing a chunk of her hair and tossing it over her face, pointedly turning back to watching the sky as she sputters and spits to get it out of her mouth. Spirits, what a little sister.

But maybe he needed something to jolt him out of his thoughts. Because with them both retreating back into their respective silences, Sokka’s fingers are slowly itching more and more for paper and brush as he turns over the idea of forgiveness, and forgiving, and being forgiven. Of what a person earns or deserves or is subjected to. Of chances, and atonement, and moving on and moving forward and all the thin shades of difference between them. And of running away, and sacrifice, and leading, and whether it might be less about intention and more about perspective that decides which a person is doing.

&#45;-

Sokka’s heart nearly jolts out of his chest hours later when Katara punches him in the shoulder with an urgent “*Look.”* He jerks upright from his contemplation of the messy, mostly legible words he’s trying to organize, eyes darting to the horizon and immediately picking out a familiar six-legged, multi-ton shape growing steadily closer and closer.

“Thank fuck,” Sokka breathes.

“They’re early,” Katara says with open relief.

They both slump, letting the tension wash out of them. Then they look at each other, and around the clifftop. This is…very clearly a waiting-for-the-travelers-to-return kind of setup, all facades of productivity long since abandoned and two distinct body-shaped imprints in the grass. And Katara has grass all down the back of her dress, twigs in her hair, clothes wrinkled from being sprawled for so long and shit, Sokka can only imagine what he looks like with his hair this long untied in the wind.

There’s a moment of locked-eye understanding. Then they’re lurching to their feet, scrambling to gather up whetstone and kitchen knives and sewing and ink and paper, to brush off grass and shake twigs out of hair, mutually making a mad run for the Temple entrance.

They have just enough time to get rid of the evidence and find something to pretend they were occupied with. There’s no need, after all, for one half of the returning party to start wondering just how long Katara was waiting for them. And Sokka…will interrogate later, when it doesn’t feel quite so urgent, why specifically he doesn’t want to look like this much of a mess for talking to Zuko.

&#45;-

Aang is the physical embodiment of excitement as he tumbles off Aapa’s back, gestures huge with enthusiasm and Momo scrambling across his shoulders, his words tripping over themselves as he says something about fire and energy and life and…dancing?

Katara rushes over to Aang, grinning with relief, questions already spilling from her lips, the others fast on her heels. Sokka follows after too, but slower, sparing a quick glance to confirm Aang looks physically unharmed before setting his gaze on Zuko, his pulse already pounding in his throat.

Zuko’s standing at the edge of Appa’s saddle, apparently contemplating how to get down without emulating Aang’s artless tumble. His gold eyes are considering, assessing, but not tense, not upset, at least from what Sokka can see down here, even as they widen in surprise to find Sokka suddenly looking up at him. For a moment it looks like a hesitant, shy smile wants to flicker over Zuko’s face, Sokka’s breath catching at the sight and then leaving him in a single, sharp rush when Zuko’s eyes suddenly cut away instead, uncertainty replacing the expression.

“Hey,” Sokka says, tugging on his wolf tail and reminding himself that he doesn’t get to be upset if Zuko retreats when Sokka was the one to shove him away first.

“…Hi.”

“It’s good to see you,” Sokka says, glancing back up to find Zuko searching his face, brow tense like he’s trying to find clues. “How—how was it? How are you?”

“…Good,” Zuko says after a moment, the word quiet, something a little bit surprised and maybe even somewhere close to contented. Sokka isn’t sure which one of the questions Zuko’s answering—both, maybe—but the lack of tight stress, of barely-restrained anxiety, is enough on its own to let one of the hard knots of worry in Sokka’s gut slowly begin to unwind.

And fuck, he’s just standing here staring. “You, ah—” Sokka clears his throat and reaches for a neutral topic. “If you hold the edge of the saddle, you can kind of climb down his middle leg.”

Zuko eyes that path with open skepticism.

“Or, you know. Use his tail like a slide.”

“Middle leg it is,” Zuko murmurs, and Sokka…thinks that might have been a flash of humor? Oh, Sokka hopes so. He missed this. Not just Zuko here with him, but that hint of ease in Zuko’s eyes, the readiness of his lips to quirk upward, the open set of his shoulders. The picture of Zuko *comfortable*, which Sokka hasn’t seen in…so long. Sokka’s pulse flutters in his throat and he glances down as he steps back, trying to give Zuko space, trying to grab space for himself. Spirits, this…this is why he needs to figure himself out.

“Can I—” Sokka stops himself, forcing his words to come out something closer to steady than breathy. “Can we talk? I wanted to—there are some things you should—that you deserve to hear from me. And I… wanted to try to say them.”

Zuko hesitates, searching his face again and Spirits, it never used to feel this hard to meet Zuko’s eyes. “Now?”

“Or whenever is good for you,” Sokka says quickly, hands gesturing uselessly in front of him. “I know you just had a long day and it was probably super stressful, and I don’t know, you probably want some food or a bath or—"

“Zuko!” Aang suddenly calls, bouncing on his toes in the milling, chattering little crowd around him. “Come on, let’s show them!”

“It can’t wait until we eat?” Zuko pushes back, his eyes still on Sokka and his words too relaxed to carry any real rancor, which is…a bit of a novel thing to hear directed at someone else, actually.

Aang turns to Katara, eyes big and imploring. “Is dinner even started?”

“Nope,” Katara says, smiling in the face of Aang’s happiness. And maybe because she’s relieved. Or maybe just because Zuko’s about to do something he doesn’t want to do. Who knows, with her.

Zuko rolls his eyes but obligingly starts to make his way down from Appa’s saddle—using the middle leg, though with significantly less concern than Sokka would show for his distance from the ground---and Sokka backs up to give him room and then to just join the group around Aang entirely. The urge to reach for Zuko’s hand and tug him forward is itching in Sokka’s fingers, and that…would not be helpful right now.

“It’s so cool, guys,” Aang is enthusing. “Come on, Zuko, you stand here.” Sokka nearly chokes on his own spit when Aang tugs Zuko where he wants him and Zuko doesn’t flinch halfway across the room. “Ready?”

Zuko waits for Aang to get into position, voice soft as he counts them down, “On three—one, two—”

*Oh*, Sokka thinks as he watches them. *Dancing. That…makes sense*.

Zuko and Aang move in sync, opposite but mirroring each other in perfect time, their steps powerful and smooth, their arms somehow sharp and fluid at the same time. Zuko’s body moves with the kind of grace and confidence that Sokka generally associates with his firebender having a pair of swords in his hands, or with the hard beat of an Earth Kingdom drum on a fall night. His feet are sure, hands precise, and seeing that melded with his fire…

Something knotted in Sokka’s chest loosens seeing Zuko—seeing both of them—safe and looking confident in their bending, more relaxed and sure than they left. The course of a day changing something for the better, for once.

Both their fires look strong and bright and Sokka blinks, startled, when he realizes he can see the difference there, too. He didn’t realize he was such a connoisseur, but, well. Maybe he is. His eyes follow the smooth arcs and steady flow of both their flames, tracking the tight, crisp control around the edges, lingering on the interplay of colors around the heart of Zuko’s fire

Would that kind of bright, sparkling fire feel different than another firebender’s flame? And that thought starts Sokka down a path he really shouldn’t follow, especially here, and now, because he can feel the heat of Zuko’s bending from where he’s standing, can feel the thrum in his chest that he thinks might be moving in time with Zuko’s breaths, and…Fuck. Having Toph around has been hard enough *without* Zuko here. And now with these kinds of thoughts —this kind of *getting ahead of himself—*just waiting to spark and with Zuko so easy for them to spark against? Spirits, if it’s been dicey, it’s definitely going to get worse.

Sokka can’t imagine wanting anything otherwise, though.

“That’s it,” Aang grins when they finish with a showy, joint flourish that has their flames melding together. “That’s the Dragon Dance!”

“It’s amazing,” Katara grins, eyes only for Aang, and Sokka clears his throat, giving her a significant look that has her adding, grudgingly, “Both of you. I guess.”

…Sokka will take it, for now. Especially when that little bit alone has Zuko blinking in open surprise.

“So how’d you learn it?” Toph asks. “Were there people there or something?”

“Well,” Aang says. “We went to the island. The…” He turns to Zuko.

“The Sun Warriors’ Island,”

“Yeah, the Sun Warriors’ Island. And there were all these ruins, and…” He glances to Zuko again.

“Carvings.”

“And carvings! And we did the dance and…”

“It’s an ancient technique.”

“Yeah! And it was like—bam! Understanding!”

Sokka glances between Aang and Zuko, trying to adjust to their sudden rapport. He’s more than happy to see Zuko without that about-to-snap tension from the morning—at least where Aang is concerned, Zuko’s still keeping Katara firmly and warily on his right side. But for Zuko to be able to be even marginally relaxed in Aang’s presence, let alone allowing Aang to touch him, and so quickly…it must have been quite the life-changing set of carvings. Or else they left a lot out of the story.

The group starts drifting back toward the interior of the Temple, chattering, spirits feeling high for the first time in…too long, if Sokka actually has to stop to think about it like this. Toph is saying something about a nap and Aang about wanting to find Teo and Haru to show them the dance, but Zuko is shaking his head, stepping back, murmuring about having something to do first, and turning…to Sokka.

“Hey,” Zuko breathes when he’s close enough for his words to be private. Sokka’s stomach kicks at the familiar husky tone, which is stupid, and he needs to get himself under control, it’s not—it’s just Zuko’s *voice*. “I, ah—I have something to say too. Can we—” Zuko licks his lips, and through some heroic effort Sokka manages not to stare. “Can we talk somewhere? In private?”

“Oh, uh, yeah,” Sokka fumbles, trying to string a coherent thought together. “Sure, let me just —”

“Unsaddle Appa and do the laundry?”

Sokka and Zuko both startle as Katara pops up out of fucking *nowhere*—wasn’t she leaving with Aang?—eyebrows raised and face set with that challenge she seems to reserve for throwing a chore down in front of Zuko, even if her tone is…somewhat less combative than it was yesterday. Maybe.

“Laundry?” Sokka echoes, eyes narrowing. He specifically asked her to stop using chores as some kind of punishment, and Zuko *just* got back, why would she—

“Yup,” Katara says, blithely ignoring both Sokka’s scowling and the fact that neither Zuko nor Sokka is a *waterbender*. “You both missed the morning chores. So. Good thing there’s plenty of time to get them done together before dinner.”

…Did she hear Zuko asking for somewhere private to talk? Is this some kind of what, offer of privacy? An excuse to disappear together?

“Uh, sure,” Zuko says, glancing at Sokka. “I just—now?”

“Yup. Now.” Katara says, her eyes flicking between them. “Sokka can show you where it is. Topside. Since the rest of us will be down here.”

Well. Looks like she did hear. Or else she doesn’t trust them to think to seek out a moment to talk on their own, which…after everything that got them here, Sokka can’t exactly say is unfair.

&#45;-

They head topside after gathering up the laundry—Sokka pulled faces as everyone tossed over their sweaty, battle-dirty clothes, but Zuko was remarkably sanguine about the whole thing—Zuko leading the way. Sokka doesn’t know what it is, but something about Zuko coming back seems to be sending his emotions ricocheting through his chest even more than watching him leave. Or maybe it’s the hint of that less-tense Zuko make a reappearance, or just the familiar feeling of Zuko being gone and then back again on a schedule, because nothing about the Western Air Temple is like Ba Sing Se, but trailing behind Zuko toward some private place that Zuko says he knows how to get to—

“What about the laundry?”

Zuko cast the pile on the ground a dry look. “It’ll keep.”

&#45;-Sokka can’t seem to keep his mind in the present. Or his eyes off Zuko’s ass, which…might be related. In his defense, Sokka needs to hold his stack of laundry down with his chin, which naturally tips the eyes downward. Which…stopped being an excuse when Sokka stopped having the laundry in his arms.

Spirits, he’s a mess. This? This right here? This shit is not helping him get his thoughts straight, no matter how tempting it is to indulge. And if he can’t get them straight in his own head, how is he ever going to explain them to Zuko? His veins feel like they’re bubbling, full of nerves to be walking into this with a page of half-sketched notes and nothing even approaching a plan beyond the desperate need to *try*, to do his best to make this feel at least a little bit right again.

“So how was the day?” Sokka asks, trying to get himself refocused on what he’s supposed to be thinking about, which is Zuko’s feelings and thoughts and wants, *not* his ass, Sokka doesn’t get to think about that, not yet at least. “Was it okay? Were you alright? How did it go? You seemed like you were better with Aang, but it was just a day and I know there was a lot—”

Zuko cuts him a look, and Sokka bites his tongue, swallowing back the rush of questions trying to burst out of him. Great. Great start.

“It was a full day,” Zuko says after a beat, and Sokka lets out a brief of relief that his tone is quiet, contemplative, maybe a little wondering, even, but nothing anxious or tense.

“Will you tell me about it?” Sokka asks, taking another peek at the expression on Zuko’s face and feeling warmth bloom in his chest. “If you want to.”

Zuko is quiet a moment, clearly turning that over, and Sokka’s trying to stay calm about the idea that Zuko might *not* want to tell him about it when Zuko finally says, apologetically, “I can’t really share the details. I’m…not really supposed to talk about it.”

It’s Sokka’s turn to walk in silence for a bit. “…Is it a firebender thing?” Aang and Katara and Toph have always been so open about practicing their bending regardless of whether Sokka’s there, but maybe that’s not normal?

“Something like that, I guess.”

“Okay,” Sokka says, nodding slowly. It’s… not a bender thing, it’s a *fire*bender, thing, and that…that’s okay. That’s like Suki not sharing her knowledge until Sokka put on the Kyoshi uniform, right? Sokka just…can’t ever put on this outfit, but that’s…still fine. Most people can’t. “Did—can you still—can you not talk about it at all? Can I ask how you think it went? Was it helpful?”

“I got my bending back,” Zuko says, a small smile curling his lips that cuts right through Sokka’s lingering uncertainty.

“I saw,” Sokka grins, relieved and chest light with happiness that it’s back, that Zuko seems so pleased with it. “So was it like Aang said? Did you know and learn the process together, or whatever?”

Zuko huffs, reluctant amusement on his face when he glances at Sokka. “Something like that,” he says, a little bit rueful.

“And you and Aang…I mean, you seemed okay, just now?”

Zuko hums, nodding and clearly searching for words, eventually shrugging. “It was a good trip.”

Sokka nods, filing this away as something to maybe ask about later, if—*when—*they’re standing together on something more solid than whatever this is now. He doesn’t think he can demand any kind of openness that Zuko doesn’t want to give right now, no matter how curious he is. “I’m glad,” he says, skipping forward a half step so he can duck a little to catch Zuko’s eye. “Really, I’m—I’m happy for you.”

Zuko holds his gaze for a moment, the gold of his eyes tentative and just a little bit soft. “Thanks,” he says, quiet, and Sokka struggles to keep his pace even at the unexpected flutter between them of a not-entirely-bad kind of tension, like an awareness of intimacy, or a hand outstretched. Maybe not extended all the way, but not held back, either.

“So,” Sokka says, dropping back a little again and clearing his throat. It’s not that he doesn’t want to sink into the feeling, to let it grow and spin out and root deep. He just—Spirits, they really need to talk, and that overfull feeling, like he has too many things inside all trying to come out at the same time, it hasn’t *helped*, before. “How, uh—” Sokka glances around what seems to be a completely identical stretch of forest to every other bit of forest around here, desperately looking for something else to focus on. “—how do you know this place?”

Zuko glances back over his shoulder, holding a branch out of the way until Sokka clears it. “I used to come here. Before.”

Sokka measures Zuko’s tone against the tension on his body and decides there aren’t any tripping hazards here, yet. “Before, when..?”

A little bit of tightness winds back into Zuko’s shoulders, but then he shakes himself like it’s a physical thing he can brush off. “Yeah I, ah—after I…couldn’t be on a ship full time? For a bit? Because—healing stuff. And also, well—the Avatar. Air Nomads. Clues.” Zuko makes a little what-are-you-going-to-do shrug. “And it’s—it was close to Caldera, but no one would…it made sense.”

“It seems like a decent place to recover,” Sokka offers, trying to slot away every bit and piece Zuko just told him. It’s private, he supposes, and peaceful if you can get over the constant wind. Zuko could keep himself warm in the North, though, so—but no, Sokka’s pretty sure that Zuko didn’t learn that until he was already on his ship? So maybe not the most pleasant, then.

“It…kind of,” Zuko says, brow furrowed when he half-turns to slip around a rocky outcropping.

Sokka makes a questioning noise as he picks his way over the mess of protruding roots and rocks, grabbing onto the thin tree trunks around him as the ground suddenly pitches downward.

“…Have you ever been to any of the other Air Temples?”

“Yeah, one of the first things we did with Aang was head to the Southern one.” Sokka remembers his awe at seeing the kind of architecture he’d only heard stories of until then. And his quiet, mounting horror when he realized what all those drifts of snow were actually concealing. “…Oh.” He glances at Zuko’s back, trying to piece it together. “You..?”

Zuko’s eyes flash over his shoulder again, peeking from the left side this time. At least a little bit anxious, then, about the topic, and not wanting to be. “I didn’t really—I couldn’t do much. I mostly…sat. But Uncle…” He shrugs, shoulders going tight and words apparently drying up.

“Well,” Sokka says after a beat to make sure nothing more is coming, struggling to consider one man—fuck, one *crew*—trying to manage all that on top of having a too-burned-to-travel Zuko on his hands. “That was…kind. Of both of you. You didn’t have to do it but I’m glad you did. And I’m sure Aang appreciates it, too.”

Zuko gives another little half-shrug, like appreciation is immaterial to him, which…really isn’t the conversation Sokka is trying to have today. But Zuko’s back at least seems to loosen again with the gesture. Or maybe with Sokka’s words. “Yeah. Me, too.” Then, tone abruptly changing, “This is the spot.”

Sokka ducks under another branch to step into…a shockingly cozy clearing. The ground is smooth grass, uncluttered by roots or stones or branches. There’s a little grouping of rocks in the center, a few different boulders and weather-dulled peaks coming together at just the right kind of width for sitting. And to catch rainwater at their center, he sees as he gets closer and takes in the crystalline little pool shivering in the gentle breeze. *Water, earth, and air*, he thinks as he takes in the quiet and the birdsong and the wind muffled to a whisper by the trees. *All it needs is fire*.

Sokka glances back to see that Zuko is watching his reaction, still on the edge of the tree line like Sokka might take in this little piece of probably-holy forest and decide that no, he prefers something less relaxing and calm, please.

“It’s nice,” Sokka says quietly, fingers trailing absently over warm stone. He bets the sun hits that pool at the right time of day and lights this whole place up. And he isn’t sure that they should be here—he’s getting distinctly Spirit-adjacent vibes—but it *is* so nice, and Zuko’s breathing out a little puff of something that might be relief? Does that mean he values Sokka’s opinion on this place? Or that he thought Sokka would put up a fight about it?

“Yeah,” Zuko agrees, finally moving to circle the outcropping to take a seat on the far side. “It is.” Sokka watches the unthinking way Zuko vaults up the rocks and gives himself a little mental shrug. If Zuko’s been here before and not been smited—smote?—for it then Sokka isn’t going to ruin the moment by suggesting the possibility.

Sokka climbs up opposite Zuko so they can face each other across the little pool, glancing down to see that the water is clear enough that Sokka doesn’t see his reflection looking back, just the dark stone beneath. He stills when raises his eyes again to see Zuko watching him, studying again, an edge of reserve and caution back in his face that makes Sokka’s pulse flutter with unease.

“You had something you wanted to say,” Zuko says, voice so perfectly neutral Sokka can feel himself on the edge of floundering. Fuck, he can do this. He can.

“Yeah, but—you did too?”

Zuko assesses him a moment, fiddling with the fabric of his pants. “You first.”

“Right,” Sokka nods, taking a deep breath and straightening and trying to marshal all his thoughts into the order they’re supposed to be in. This is going to be his third try to get this right, and fuck, he can’t keep messing this up. “I wanted to apologize.”

Zuko is quiet a moment before sneaking a glance through the fall of his hair. “…What for?”

Sokka opens his mouth and freezes as every single one of his thoughts and worries and desperate fears light up all at once, all crowding to the front of his brain, tangling and tripping over themselves and—

He fumbles in his pocket, tugging out a creased, grass-stained sheet of paper, fingers miraculous steady as he unfolds it and to reveal his…honestly barely legible thoughts, between the haste he wrote them in and the smudging of the ink and everything that he tried to cross out and correct and get just perfect. But the piece at the top, the part clearest in both his own head and on the page, is at least enough to get him started again.

“I think I messed up before,” Sokka says, trying to focus on what he wants to say and not get distracted reacting to Zuko’s head-down, face-hidden listening. “Probably a few times.” Sokka forces his free hand to stop tugging on the end of his wrist wraps. “You came here to help us, and we haven’t—I haven’t—made that easy for you.”

Zuko ducks his head a little more. “You can’t make yourself feel something you don’t feel.” “It’s not about feeling, though,” Sokka says, trying not to let his voice shake with urgency. “I —I do feel, it’s like I feel *everything*, feeling isn’t—Fuck,” he breaks off, frustration spiking. “I didn’t want to focus on that, this is supposed to be about you, not me. Or about us, or— shit.” He checks his notes again. “It’s like I have so much in my head that I don’t know which way is up anymore, and just…it hurt so much after the eclipse. And it…kind of still does, but right after it felt like that’s all that was there.”

“It was a bad day,” Zuko says quietly, and Sokka holds back a sad noise because he *still* doesn’t know why it was bad for Zuko, beyond the obvious, and it’s his own fault for not knowing.

“Yeah, but—*you* were there. And I didn’t…all I could think about was how much I’d already messed it all up, and how upset I was, and that…that wasn’t fair.” And Spirits, beyond the fairness, beyond the way it’s hurt Zuko, it was *dangerous*. Being that unaware—would Sparky Sparky Boom Man have managed to get so close in the first place if Sokka had been paying attention like he should have been? “You came here, and you didn’t have to, but you did it anyway. And we just—I just…haven’t made it good for you.”

“It’s fi—”

“I don’t want you to feel like you’re on your own here,” Sokka says all in a rush, barreling forward because he needs to get this out and he can’t get stuck again on what is and isn’t ‘fine.’ “And I mean, maybe I’m just making this up? Maybe I’m just reading into things. But I don’t—I don’t think I’m doing a good job at making it so you don’t feel like that.”

Sokka tries not to wince when Zuko is tellingly silent, because it’s not like Sokka hasn’t had the entire day to walk back through every single moment of the past three days and come to his own conclusions. Not that Sokka is sure he trusts himself all that much when it comes to conclusions, anymore.

“I just…you got hurt before? I think?” Because Sokka doesn’t want to make *that* mistake again, not when Zuko’s sharp, tight characters are still burned into his mind. “And when I realized it was like all I could think about was how much it hurt to know that I’d done that, and I tried to make it better but I think I maybe just…hurt you again. Trying to explain, or— whatever.” Spirits, that letter feels like a worse and worse idea the further Sokka gets from it, except for the fact that maybe it got them here. “And you deserve more than that, and I didn’t give it to you and even when I knew I wasn’t, I couldn’t figure out *how*, and I’m…I’m still afraid that I’m not sure and that I’m just still going to…yeah.”

Sokka forces himself to finally stop talking, fizzling awkwardly into silence but Spirits, he can hear himself verging on increasingly incoherent. But now that he’s not talking the urge to squirm and fidget, like his skin is suddenly too tight, is growing and growing and Zuko is just sitting and sitting and…thinking about whatever he’s thinking about.

“We all have stuff going on,” Zuko finally says, and Sokka doesn’t know if that’s supposed to be an acknowledgment or an excuse or a brush-off, but either way he just—he just needs to make sure Zuko understands this time.

“Yeah, but Zuko, you’re…you’re getting your stuff done, and I can’t even—Fuck, I mean, you just did this amazing thing in a *day*. With Aang who…you seem easier with now, yeah, but it can’t have been easy.”

Zuko hesitates, then glances away with another shrug and Sokka just— he hates that Zuko acts like none of it should *matter*. Spirits, that Sokka could have done something to make him think it didn’t.

“You’re here doing things,” Sokka continues, blinking the stinging heat from his eyes. “And I didn’t even think about Katara. And she’s my sister, and I know—I just should have. I should’ve just…thought about what could happen, if you ever…if something like this ever happened. And not just today, or yesterday, or the day before, I should have *been* doing more. And instead, I…Spirits, Zuko, you’re not some shameful secret,” Sokka says, clearing his throat as his voice wavers. “I think you’re so amazing and wonderful and I don’t—I don’t ever want you to feel like you’re less than that. But I didn’t want to expect that it would ever happen and put that on you, you know? I just…messed it up. Really bad. And maybe made you feel that way anyway? And I just…I’m so sorry. And I hope you can forgive me, and I —” Sokka takes a deep breath and forces himself to look up, to meet Zuko’s wide-eyed, startled stare. “I’d understand if you can’t, and…and either way I want to do better. I do.”

“What…” Zuko clears his throat, eyes skipping away to the base of Sokka’s throat. “What does that mean?”

Sokka flails a little, trying to sort through what other words he could give after all that, chest tight with a stab of anxiety that he just said so much and again none of it was *right*.

“What does doing better look like,” Zuko adds, shifting to catch Sokka’s attention. “That’s what I—what does that part mean?”

Oh. Right. “I don’t have it entirely worked out,” Sokka says, worrying at the paper still in his hands. “I don’t really have a plan yet.”

“I’m not asking for a plan,” Zuko says, words quiet and steady and enough to let Sokka set aside at least a chunk of his worry.

“Okay, I think…Listening? More? I…need to get out of my own head and pay attention, and not…assume. Or, maybe it’s not assuming, but…not acting like something will work for you because it worked for me.”

Zuko nods, silent, *expectant*, so Sokka…keeps going.

“And…following your lead? When you’re involved? And…being better about being a—a friend.” That one Sokka knows is right. “I want to be, I just…don’t think I’ve been a good friend, or teammate or anything, right now?”

That…Sokka didn’t mean for his voice to tick up at the end like that, for his uncertainty to turn the whole thing into a question, and Zuko raises his eyebrow, eyeing Sokka for a long moment. “Are you asking me?”

Sokka hesitates, trying to think through his stab of fear that he might cross some line by pulling Zuko into the mess of his head. Shouldn’t Sokka be able to figure this stuff out? Shouldn’t he not need someone to tell him in the first place? “I don’t want to make you feel like you need to fix my problem,” Sokka finally says, staring down at his hands. “Not when you’ve got so much already to deal with.”

“…Do you remember two days ago when you were mad at me for doing things alone and not telling people?”

“…Fuck.”

“You’re a person too, Sokka,” Zuko says, frowning down at the pool. “You don’t have separate rules or standards or whatever you seem to think you need to do that everyone else doesn’t.”

Sokka…wasn’t expecting Zuko to sound so much like Katara, today. “…I think I might not be good at that,” he finally says, tugging uncertainly on his wolf tail, feeling uncomfortably squirmy to admit it so plainly.

“Who is,” Zuko sighs, expression flashing toward something wry so quick Sokka isn’t entirely sure if he saw it. “You can ask me, you know,” Zuko adds, eyes darting up to Sokka’s face and then away. “If I need something. Or I can just…tell you?” Another flitting glance, and the uncertainty that chases across Zuko’s face is much easier to read. “Then you wouldn’t have to guess.”

And then Sokka will have no excuses he if fucks it up again, but…he doesn’t think Zuko means it that way, thinks Zuko means it in a way that’s leaving him feeling more than a little stunned. “I…think that would help me,” he admits, folding and refolding the paper that’s unreadable now anyway between the dimming light and his own sweat-damp hands smudging the ink. “I’m—I still feel like I’m a mess. I don’t…really trust myself to read things right. Or to…do anything. If we’re being honest.”

Gold eyes flash up, examining his face. “Sometimes you just need to do something anyway,” Zuko points out.

Sokka nods, trying to take that in. Maybe once the idea settles it will ease some of the tight, tangled fear Sokka can’t stop feeling over getting it wrong. “You don’t, ah—You don’t have to stick around while I figure it out,” Sokka says, trying not to let his voice show the reluctance curling in his chest. “If you want to, of course, but…I’d understand if you didn’t. I don’t want to just…practice on you, or, I don’t know. You don’t have to wait for me.” “…Do you think there’s someone else?”

“I mean—” Sokka has no idea what to say. “Not necessarily, just—you’re *you*, so—who wouldn’t, and you, you know…deserve that, if you want it, and I don’t…know how long it’s going to be.”

“I think,” Zuko says, with a sudden look of…fond exasperation? It’s not an expression that Sokka associates with Zuko, at least not in this context instead of those moments when they’re tangled together and Sokka can’t stop talking, either because he actually can’t or because he can’t wait to see what Zuko comes up with to shut him up. Sokka…doesn’t know how to react to seeing it here. “That I’d prefer that you practice doing better with me *with* me, than on someone else.”

“Right, I—right.” Sokka…has been shut up. At least until a stab of uncertainty cuts through his chest again, a frayed-edged anxiety over having intentions and ideas but no plan, so specific series of steps yet to get there. “You—you’ll tell me if I mess up? I—you can pull me aside if you don’t want to say something in front of anyone else? Or we can come up with a signal, or—”

“I’ll tell you,” Zuko cuts in, voice nearly gentle, and Sokka…Spirits, he wants to just fold himself into it, wants to wrap himself in that tone and everything he hopes it means.

“Thank you,” Sokka says, clearing his throat when his voice comes out surprisingly hoarse “I…thank you. For the chance.”

“We all deserve chances,” Zuko says, glancing away, as if chances are something that get offered over and over instead of running out far too quick.

But maybe they don’t, even though it’s never felt that way. Maybe that’s another thing Sokka has wrong, one that wouldn’t be so bad to realize has been different this whole time. Sokka lets that idea sit a while as a silence falls between them that isn’t necessarily easy, but also isn’t strung so tight with uncertainty it might snap. He doesn’t know if he can trust his judgment one way or another right now to know, but…Zuko seems to have an opinion.

“You…you had something to say, too?” Sokka finally says, reluctant to break the silence but also not wanting to hit the limit of his ability to take in new information, to think through however he’s going to respond, before Zuko gets a chance to speak. “Unless—did you want to talk more? About what I said? We can still—or not talk at all, if…”

“No, I can go,” Zuko says, lapsing right back into contemplating the pool between them. Sokka tries to force himself to a similar kind of calm, trying to pace his breathing and clear his mind and still his body, everything he can think of to ready himself for what Zuko might have to say, to ready himself to *listen*, and then…to figure out what it might mean. For Sokka, and for Zuko, and for…them.

“I learned something else. On the island,” Zuko finally says into the quiet, fingers fidgeting where they’re clasped together. “Something Aang didn’t.”

Sokka’s having trouble pinning down the particular flavor of Zuko’s sudden nervousness. “Like…a cool firebending trick?”

“It’s about the…” Zuko takes a deep breath, eyes fixed on the vee of bare skin at Sokka’s throat, which is…familiar, and not necessarily a good start. But not necessarily a bad one, either. “You know that thing I can do?”

Sokka’s mind goes in too many different directions at once, somehow managing to come up perfectly empty. “…Firebending?”

Zuko huffs, amused. “The other one.”

Not sex, not sex, he’s *not* talking about se—oh. “…Heat bending?”

“Yeah.”

“Okay…”

Zuko hears the unspoken request for more. “Specifically, the way I can do it to, um. You.”

Sokka’s mind dives straight to waiting-to-be-kindled handprints on his skin and strong-hot-good fingers wrapped around his wrists and kisses that are knee-meltingly hot, and his words just evaporate right out of his throat. Zuko peeks up at his silence, gold eyes going wide when he sees it on Sokka’s face because fuck, of course all of Sokka’s thoughts would be visible there.

“No,” Zuko hurries to say, pink creeping over his unscarred cheek. “Not—not that. Not—I meant the other. The other thing. The…” His eyes drop to Sokka’s chest, and after a blank moment Sokka finally gets it.

“The chi bending?”

“It’s actually not called that, it’s—” Zuko glances up again and redirects. “Yeah. That.”

“Okay,” Sokka says, trying to get into the right frame of mind for whatever this is going to be. He’s glad that Zuko wanted to have this conversation in private. This particular topic— the way Zuko has a grip on his fucking *lifeforce*—has always felt too intensely personal for Sokka to share.

Which…might not actually be a high bar to clear, Sokka is starting to realize.

“We practiced, before, how to…resist it.” Sokka nods. He remembers. Vividly. “They—”

“They?”

Zuko winces. “I can’t talk about it,” he says, flashing Sokka a look that’s half-apologetic and half-regretful.

“Right, sorry,” Sokka says, even though he’s bursting with curiosity now, even more than before, so much that it would absolutely derail whatever conversation Zuko is trying to have. “Okay. So…they?”

Zuko lets out a breath, flashing Sokka a grateful look before he picks up the thread again. “They said that it’s not entirely unheard of. What I can do. But it’s usually…not an accident. And that it’s not…” Zuko’s expression twists as he looks for words, expression forming something too complicated for Sokka to read. “That always having someone in your fire sense isn’t really…done.”

“…Zuko,” Sokka finally says, “I still don’t know enough about bending to know what that means.”

Zuko sighs, deliberately flattening out his fingers against his thighs before saying quietly, “They showed me how to let you go. From my heat sense. So that I don’t…hold onto you. Like that. Anymore.”

“…Oh,” Sokka says dumbly, blinking as he tries to process the words, replaying them over and over and lingering over every hitch and nuance of Zuko’s tone. Sokka…should be happy. About this. Sokka’s never been entirely easy with the fact that they didn’t know what it could mean for him if Zuko died, or if his bending got fucked up, or something equally horrible. It’s never been wholly comfortable, the knowledge that Zuko could literally be holding Sokka’s life in his hands but that they just didn’t know enough one way or another to be sure.

Though Zuko always seemed sure, with a kind of brittleness about that surety that Sokka had never wanted to probe.

Sokka should be relieved to hear this, then. Objectively, Sokka knows he should be leaping at this opportunity. He just…isn’t. Spirits, the idea of actively severing something between them? Sokka thinks of that pull he always feels toward Zuko somewhere in his chest, that localized gravity. Would that go away, if Zuko cuts this tie? Sokka isn’t entirely sure it would, it’s not like he’s drawn to Zuko *because* of this weird bending, not like he didn’t feel the pull before he got sick. But Sokka still isn’t entirely sure that he wants it to be gone.

Not that that matters all that much, if Zuko does.

“Apparently, I’m too—tangled.” Zuko scowls at that. “And I’m getting close to my inner fire being too tightly woven into—” He shakes his head, blowing out his annoyance. “Anyway. They showed me how else it could be.” His fingers are tapping on his knees now, and Sokka isn’t quite sure how to read that. Anticipation? Readiness? Anxiety? “And you wanted space —” Sokka can’t quite hold in his flinch. “—And regardless, even if you didn’t, I should still learn. So.” Zuko shrugs. “Yeah.”

“Right,” Sokka manages to get out, voice shockingly level. “That…seems sensible.” Sokka dreams of being bathed in fire, some nights. He sits as close as he can stand to the campfire when he’s feeling lonely and missing home. There’s nothing about him that wants to be sensible right now.

“So…” Zuko shoots him a quick uncertain look. “I’d like to practice?”

“Yeah, of course,” Sokka hurries to say. “Of course. Just…let me know when. I’m around.” Obviously. “I don’t have anything else going on. I’m totally free.” And Sokka should probably shut up now before he manages to somehow veer back to the topic of his tattered self-confidence.

He doesn’t know that he entirely manages to stop himself soon enough, though, with the way Zuko is looking at him, face carefully neutral but gold eyes intent.

“Will it—will it be like how we practiced before?” Sokka asks, trying to push this back toward what Zuko wanted to talk about, much as thinking about losing that tie between them makes him want to find a nice quiet place to have a nice small breakdown.

“…Probably less active for you,” Zuko says after a moment, brow slightly furrowed as he continues to study Sokka’s face, and wow, Sokka didn’t think he could like this idea any less, but needing to just sit there and let it happen…ugh.

“Okay,” Sokka says, trying to shove the feeling away because Zuko needs this, and Sokka can admit in a corner of his brain that he probably needs it himself, too. “I—yeah. Just let me know. I’m happy to help how I can…” Sokka trails off, clearing his throat when Zuko gives him an openly skeptical look.

“Are you…is this okay?” Zuko asks, shifting uncertainly. “If you don’t want to practice, we don’t—”

“No, it’s not—just—” Sokka takes a deep breath, shoving his hand through his hair. “I’m wondering if—if you know how to let someone go. That doesn’t mean you can’t ever hold on again. Right?”

“Oh,” Zuko says, toneless, then, “*Oh*.” Sokka can feel himself flushing and doesn’t even know why, it’s not like Zuko doesn’t know Sokka likes him. “The elders—shit,” Zuko mutters, shaking his head before picking back up, “They said that letting go of someone from your fire sense and letting go of someone aren’t the same thing.”

But it could be, if there’s no reason to hold on, Sokka thinks, even as his shoulders slump in relief. He can take in the reassurance anyway, because Sokka can listen and share and figure himself out and make sure there’s a reason to hold on, a reason to stay.

“No, uh, no pressure, though?” Zuko adds after a beat, looking suddenly self-conscious and rubbing at the back of his neck, his own cheek pink.

…Right. Right. No pressure at all.
