## Chapter 15: The Space Between Us

### Notes

#### Chapter Notes

No particular warnings for this one!

### Text

The first time Zuko lets go of Sokka’s chi, Sokka bursts into tears. He doesn’t mean to and is acutely horrified to be doing so out of nowhere. But the swelling in his chest, pressing against his ribcage from the inside, and then the sudden void where Sokka didn’t even know he’d been full until it’s gone—it’s like his body reacts before his mind even registers the loss, and now he can’t make it *stop*.

“It’s fine, it’s fine,” Sokka says wetly as he scrambles backward and swipes furiously at his face, not at all selling it as he gasps in a breath.

“Fuck, fuck, *fuck*,” Zuko chants, eyes wide with alarm. He rocks forward on his knees, reaching, and Sokka chokes as he feels his inner flame, chi, *whatever* suddenly flares down into his stomach and up into his throat, nearly bursting into another round of tears over being able to feel it again even as feeling it like *this* just makes him want to squirm down and then up after it.

“*Shit.”* Zuko yanks his hand away so hard he falls back onto his ass, scrambling and sitting on his hands, eyes wide. Sokka makes a sound halfway between a sob and a protest as his chi plummets back toward its baseline, whole body clenching against the feeling of loss as a fresh wave of tears presses against his eyes. “I’m sorry, Sokka, I’m so sorry,” Zuko says, hurtling far too fast toward panicking. “What can I do, what’s wrong, I’ll fix it, I promise I’ll fix it, I didn’t mean to, please be okay please, please—”

Sokka tries to make a reassuring gesture and is pretty sure he fails, since Zuko’s half-terrified words just come out faster. “Zuko, it’s fine,” Sokka sniffs, pressing the heels of his hands to his eyes like he can physically force the tears back in. “I’m okay, I’m not hurt. I’m fine.”

“You’re *not*.” Zuko sounds close to tears himself now. “I *did* something. They told me it wouldn’t hurt you, they *told me,* and they *lied*.”

“They didn’t,” Sokka says shakily, trying to force himself upright, trying to get himself under control because Zuko clearly isn’t going to calm down until he does. “They didn’t. I’m not hurt. Zuko. *Zuko*.” Sokka waits for Zuko’s frantic stare to bounce to him, his scarred eye peeled as wide open as Sokka’s ever seen it. “I’m not hurt. I promise.”

Sokka can practically see the words land, Zuko’s hysterical body language slowly falling into stillness except for his too-fast breaths as he searches Sokka’s face, his body, looking for confirmation. “You…you aren’t?”

“No,” Sokka says, unwinding his wrist wrap because he needs to blow his nose now and fuck if he’s going to use his shirt like a toddler, this is already embarrassing enough. The feeling in his chest is gradually starting to feel less like a yawning void and more like a waiting space.

“But then—what—” Zuko’s expression is somewhere between confused and hectic, but he seems to be calming a beat behind Sokka. “—*Why*,” he settles on.

“I don’t know,” Sokka says, finally feeling steady enough to creep back forward to where he‘d been sitting when this all started. Zuko hesitantly mirrors him, settling back onto his knees. “It just…feels weird.”

“You—because it felt *weird*?”

“I don’t know, I’m not a bender,” Sokka mutters, tossing aside his dirty wrist wrap and then pulling the other one off because one is more noticeable than none. “It’s like…I don’t even know what. I didn’t even realize anything was there and now it’s not. And…I know what it feels like for it to not be there—” even if it’s been most of a year since he’s been without it. “—I just…need to remember.”

Zuko’s gaze flicks from Sokka’s restless fingers as he finishes pulling off his wrist wrap to his face to the base of this throat and back again, visibly digesting the words. “I…I didn’t mean to upset you. I—”

“Zuko,” Sokka breaks, taking another breath and forcing some steadiness into his voice. “I’m not upset.” Not enough to cry about it, at least. “My body just…didn’t seem to know that.”

Zuko makes a skeptical noise in the back of his throat even as he nods, and Sokka sighs because it’s not like he doesn’t get it. It took him a long time to be okay with Zuko on his knees in front of him again after that one time in Ba Sing Se, and that was when Sokka understood why Zuko was freaking out. Spirits, Zuko had had to pin Sokka to a wall to finally—

Okay. Time to think about something else.

It takes more than a bit to fully reassure Zuko that he’s okay, and then a bit more to talk him into trying again. Which is particularly difficult when Sokka isn’t exactly eager to get punched in the solar plexus by that re-awakened sense of absence, but Zuko needs to practice. And Sokka might need to get used to it.

When they finally give it another shot Zuko is tentative, the not-there-but-totally-there touch of his bending hesitant and creeping and slow and Spirits, it’s so weird that Sokka can feel the difference in something he can’t even see. But he supposes he’s always had a thing for Zuko’s bending, back before he even had the words for it. And being able to tell that this is cautious rather than assured doesn’t seem so far from being able to tell, without fully understanding how, whether the heat washing against his skin is playful or absent or intent before he ever sees Zuko’s face to confirm.

Zuko’s entire body is set with concentration, his hands slowly becoming steadier as he practices just reaching out and brushing against the thing in Sokka’s chest. It feels like a warm hand on Sokka’s lower back, except…inside his ribs somehow. Then Zuko works on just holding on with his bending, not trying to stoke it higher or bank it back, which feels like being tucked into the warmth of a body. And then releasing Sokka, smooth and easier and easier each time, which feels…not great, but nowhere near as alarming as the first time.

When that progresses without tears—

Zuko checks again, half-anxious and half-suspicious, and Sokka narrows his eyes and pretends they aren’t still a little bit gritty from the aftermath of crying. “Zuko, it’s okay.”

“Okay, but, you just made a noise, so I wanted to—” Zuko’s words cut off as he ducks the balled-up wad of clean wrist wrap flying toward his face.

“I’m *fine*.”

&#45;-they both brace themselves and cycle through it again and again and again. At different speeds, then with Zuko at different distances, and then using different methods that Sokka entirely fails to understand from the technical explanation—

“Instead of holding the inner flame directly it's more the space around the flame, and moving the flame by moving that.”

“…Like a pressure vacuum?”

A blank stare. “…Like a what?”

&#45;-but Zuko does different hand stuff each time, so it must be different, at least if every bit of bending Sokka’s ever seen is anything to go by.

When Zuko finally calls it quits after an hour—only an *hour*, Sokka would be sure they’ve been at it half the afternoon if Zuko’s sense of time weren’t so consistently precise—Zuko looks strung out and exhausted beyond what that amount of bending should have done to him. Not that Sokka feels much better. Physically he’s fine, acclimated enough now that the absence inside him no longer feels so much like a loss even if it’s still noticeably *there*.

But starting with tears and needing to talk Zuko down? And then needing to stay calm while it felt like Zuko was stroking pure fire through his very core? While a heat that could be Zuko but could be all Sokka’s own slid through his veins? Sokka’s more than a little worn at the edges by this point, far too much to risk relaxing his tight control like he knows he should to really sell his okay-ness. But with Zuko right there and looking all approachable and unguarded and surrounded by ambient heat…

Maybe physically ‘fine’ isn’t quite right, considering Sokka is distinctly physically unsettled, and with the potential to get very *visibly* unsettled if he doesn’t get his thoughts under control. But with nothing to focus on beyond himself and Zuko except for retreading the same well-worn trails of self-recrimination through his mind, it's all too easy to drift toward the types of thoughts and questions that Sokka can’t voice while still claiming to be wanting space.

Zuko’s quiet rasp breaks through his thoughts. “Are you okay?”

Sokka looks up from his contemplation of the floor—he could *not* keep staring at Zuko when he looks like that—to eye the tentative, cautious expression on Zuko’s face.

“You look like you have something on your mind?” Zuko continues, fingers fidgeting with the fabric over his knees before he presses them flat. “If you want to…I can listen. I’m happy to listen,” he corrects himself, gaze skating away.

“I…” Sokka spends half a second thinking about how Zuko’s expression would change if Sokka found a way to explain that he’s feeling turned on and tempted to reach across the space between them, to chase the distraction it would offer and the temporary reprieve from his own thoughts without being able to give Zuko anything else in return, which would be… so deeply unfair. Then he shoves that firmly aside. “Was this helpful for you? Even with all the—” he gestures toward his own face, aiming for a wry smile. “—dramatics?”

“Yeah,” Zuko says after a moment, shoulders relaxing. “It was…good.”

“Good,” Sokka says, mustering a more genuine smile. “That’s—I’m glad.”

“What about you?” Zuko asks, peeking between his lashes. “Was it…good?”

Oh, Spirits, *that* question, with Zuko unintentionally looking at him like that, and when a corner of Sokka’s mind is already desperately searching his schedule today for some alone time.

“It was definitely…educational,” Sokka manages to say, voice only a little faint. He decides to call it a win when the look Zuko gives him is only partially bemused.

Sokka was wrong to think of himself as a body in orbit around Zuko, that his firebender has his own gravity. Because as the days pass at the Air Temple, it becomes increasingly clear that they’re both circling around each other, or maybe circling around some central point between them. Some concept of ‘us’ that they both feel the pull of, that they both keep forgetting isn’t a space they occupy anymore—yet, at least—as they try to figure out the shape of the space they’re in instead.

The possibility of it looms large between them, at least for Sokka. It’s constantly there, constantly tugging at his awareness much as he tries to carve out space, stretched taut in even the most mundane of moments in a way that makes it feel like it would be dangerously easy to fall back into the way things were before without actually making sure that this time they’re better.

“Really, Loverboy?” Sokka jolts to attention as Toph leans into him, jerking back to get her smirking face into view without crossing his eyes. “What’s he doing—hauling the cookpot to clean?”

That is, in fact, exactly what Zuko is currently doing. Hefting their main cookpot in one hand, forearm flexing, deftly balancing their breakfast bowls in the other with a deftness that says he maybe wasn’t as terrible a server as he made himself out to be. He glances up at Toph’s sudden movement, gold eyes bright and curious behind the fall of his bangs, gaze immediately catching on Sokka’s. Then there’s one of those—very, very frequent—drawn-out moments of vibrating tension that always takes up far more of Sokka’s thoughts than they should, until pink starts to dust high over Zuko’s unscarred cheek and Sokka really needs to yank his attention away.

“I mean, I get that you think he’s cute,” Toph says, grin sharp. “But he looks *that* good doing the dishes?”

“Shut up,” Sokka mutters, trying to shrug the tension off and ignore the fact that Zuko does, indeed, look that good.

“And he doesn’t even have an apron on.”

Sokka drops his head back with a sigh. “Spirits.” He’d hoped she forgot about that.

“Maybe you should tell him.”

Sokka grunts, risking a glance back down to see that Toph’s uncharacteristically serious tone is matched by her suddenly challenging expression.

She raises her eyebrows at his silence. “Maybe *I* should tell him.”

“*No*,” Sokka blurts out, panicked, *loud*. He jerks his eyes up to see that everyone is staring at them. Including Zuko. Who immediately flushes again when Sokka makes eye contact, questioning and shy but his eyes so direct…Fuck.

“You are the *worst*,” Sokka hisses as everyone slowly gets back to whatever is left of their various post-breakfast morning rituals.

“Just looking out for you,” Toph grins, popping to her feet and grabbing Sokka’s almost-empty breakfast bowl.

“Hey!”

“Want to get it back?” Toph calls over her shoulder, taking a big bite of the last of Sokka’s rice and heading straight for Zuko.

Sokka glares at her back and doesn’t follow, just like she knew he wouldn’t, because Toph might act like it’s a joke, and things might feel marginally less frantic than they did before, but Sokka still desperately needs time and space and distance. Putting himself any deeper into that orbit than he already is…There are too many little things, almost unnoticeable things, things that should be just in the background of his day except that Sokka keeps actively needing to not react to them because he’s not *trying* to send mixed signals here. Things like Zuko’s arms, bare and flexing with every little thing he does. Like the quiet rasp of Zuko’s voice that somehow seems to cut through every other sound whenever someone can coax Zuko into the conversation.

Things like the fact that apparently, when Zuko isn’t pretending that he isn’t a firebender, the heat just spills out of him all the time, not just when he’s alone with Sokka.

Fuck, Sokka can feel it like the ghost of a touch from across the room even when they’re sitting around the fire at mealtimes and the heat of the flames should rightfully be more intense than Zuko’s ambient warmth. He’s noticed everyone else twitching and reacting to it, as Zuko incrementally becomes more comfortable and relaxed his tight control, has watched the others second-guessing themselves over whether they were actually feeling anything at all or if it’s just a sudden warm breeze. But Sokka knows. And he *thought* he was used to it. But not all the time, apparently. And not like this, when there are other people around and someone is always watching. Not when Zuko doesn’t have to pretend to be something he isn’t.

It took Sokka days of glances and questioning looks and tangled confusion to realize that the constant, outstretched heat wasn’t on purpose, that it’s just this latent *thing* that Zuko doesn’t even seem to know he’s doing, and the only thing that makes him feel better about how long it took him to figure it out is that yesterday Sokka got to watch Aang finally realize that Zuko’s fucking *body heat* is how Aang could always tell when Zuko was coming up being him. It would have been amusing, all the staring and back-and-forth looking and eyeing the air like it couldn’t be trusted, but Spirits, Sokka couldn’t spare a single breath for laughter when he was working double-time to keep his blood pressure steady as that first wave of heat slide over his skin.

And when Zuko and Aang are training, and Zuko’s actually *using* his bending? Fuck, Sokka needs to sit as far away as he can without being out of the room entirely. Because Sokka knows how he is with Zuko’s bending—if he had any doubts they would have been *thoroughly* answered by now. And he doesn’t know how to let himself feel those things, to trust the impulse to reach for the things he wants when Sokka has messed it up so many times before.

Spirits, Sokka is aware that compartmentalizing the different parts of his life might be what got him at least partially into this mess in the first place, but it was undeniable easier when he could carve out a little mental box for Zuko and soft feelings and the kind of daydreaming that’s dangerous in wartime, and only open it up at scheduled intervals.

Now that mental box barely even exists anymore, even if Sokka were willing to try to shove Zuko into it. All of it is lurking in the background of his mind, just waiting for a glance or stray thought or anything at all, really, to rush to the forefront of Sokka’s thoughts and consume his attention. And that’s *without* Toph trying to draw attention to it at every opportunity, and Aang sending him those big-eyed, speaking stares whenever Zuko’s back is turned that Sokka doesn’t know how to interpret.

And Sokka doesn’t even pretend that there’s a way he could try to keep Zuko separate from his life—that trying in the first place, was…naïve, at best—but Spirits, he hates how much of a struggle it is to figure out how he’s supposed to act when Zuko is undeniable in it now but not in the way that Sokka always imagined.

Zuko takes a careful breath and pretends he doesn’t see Sokka edging toward Katara at the end of the line of spectators that still show up for firebending training. Zuko has resigned himself to the spectators, by this point, to the fact that the audience will not, apparently, peter out once the novelty of firebending wears off. But Sokka inching away? Zuko is not at all resigned to that, even if—maybe because—he has no idea what to make of it.

Is Sokka trying to put distance between them? Trying to quiet Katara, who might be less hostile but can still put quite the bite behind her comment, especially when it seems like Sokka isn’t there to remind her otherwise. Trying to just get better light for whatever it is he’s sketching at today?

Zuko might normally try to get clues off of Sokka, but trying right now to parse every shift of his expression and hitch of his breath and wonder what it all means? Letting the fear take root that Sokka wasn’t entirely truthful when he insisted through tears that he was fine and okay when Zuko carefully untwined his fire sense from Sokka’s inner flame, and that’s why sometimes it feels like he’s sidling away like Zuko is pressing against his boundaries even though Zuko isn’t trying to push?

Fuck, it almost feels like those early days of letter writing, before either of them were sure of the other or the thing trying to grow between them. Which is probably a more accurate comparison than Zuko would prefer. And Zuko is aware he could spiral here forever, trying to figure out how things are supposed to be now when he has no idea what he wants them to look like except not the same as it was before. Or at least, not entirely.

And Zuko is also aware, as he signals Aang to launch into another kata, that all of that is a constant, nagging distraction from the limited time Zuko has to whip Aang into shape.

It might be different if Zuko actually had other things to do, other ways to occupy his thoughts and busy his hands and tire his body in a way that feels productive, in a way that Zuko didn’t even realize he needed. In the palace there was always something to be doing or learning or getting better at, and a ship always has work for idle hands, and even in Ba Sing Se Zuko had things to do, regardless of how purposeless he felt doing them. But with training only lasting a few hours, and Zuko’s ability to meditate very much at capacity, he’s realizing that he doesn’t quite know what to do with the reverse, with feeling so grounded in his intentions but so aimless in his days.

He still can’t go anywhere outside the Temple without permission, according to Katara’s timeline which he is feeling utterly uninclined to try pushing. Which leaves what—chores? Practicing his own bending, when there’s only so much time Zuko can spend feeling out the new shape of his post-Ran and Shaw fire before meditation slides toward brooding, which verges too close to anchoring on Sokka, which just leads to staring down how much of the communication that seemed to work so well in Ba Sing Se apparently happened through the medium of intimacy and physicality, and how unsure Zuko feels trying to navigate with only words.

It’s a neat trap, really, formed of Katara’s rules and Zuko’s agreement and the thin shreds of his honor that are still strong enough to prevent Zuko from ever going back on his word. He wonders if he should try talking to Sokka about it, but what would he say—that he doesn’t like the situation he accepted with eyes wide open? That Katara is behaving entirely within the bounds of the conditions she laid out but Zuko still doesn’t like it?

No, Zuko doesn’t want to step between Sokka and Katara again, not when Sokka already seems so uncharacteristically uncertain of himself in a way that Zuko doesn’t like. Not for something as small as Zuko being *bored*.

Zuko considers, as he finally lets a sweaty and somehow-still-bouncy Aang free from training, whether he could force himself to become comfortable watching some of the other bending lessons instead of seeing potential threats in every drop of water. It’s certainly what the rest of the crew seems to do with their time. He sat next to Sokka the one day, and it was fine, but…isn’t Sokka the one who said maybe ‘fine’ shouldn’t be enough?

Which Zuko is still trying to figure out…

Maybe Zuko could bring himself to ask to join Teo’s exploration of the Temple, even though Zuko shut the offer down so thoroughly on his fourth day here that he doesn’t it will ever come again. Zuko truly loathes the idea of being confined in half-crumbling hallways with three near-strangers. And also the idea of exploring in general, with the way it brings him too close to memories of his first time here. But still. He could ask. He’s sure they’d say yes, no matter how reluctantly.

It’s just hard for Zuko to figure out what he should do when he isn’t really sure how he fits into this crew. It’s not like that first day or two, but it still doesn’t make *sense*. Aang’s moved from slightly afraid to slightly in awe of him, and Toph seems inexplicably happy just to spend time with him, which Zuko is almost *sure* is a way to lull him into a ‘friendly’ duel, and having watched her throw Haru across a room with a pebble yesterday, Zuko’s going to put that one off as long as possible. And then there’s Sokka so uncharacteristically skittish, and the other three making Zuko…rather characteristically skittish. And in the midst of it all is Katara’s suspicious hostility, banked but still present and Zuko almost appreciates it for its predictable, understandable consistency.

Zuko sometimes daydreams about the expression that would probably cross her face if he told her she reminded him of Azula, that way.

“Zuko,” Aang says brightly, tugging him out of just one of those daydreams as they finish up a quick meal that’s lighter than Zuko would have preferred after a morning of training. “What are you doing after lunch?”

“Well,” he starts slowly, eyeing the way Toph is carefully scraping clean her bowl. And is Sokka trying to decide if the burned bits from the pot are not-burned enough to eat? After days of cleaning up after Teo and Haru’s particular style of cooking, Zuko can tell from all the way over here that they aren’t. Maybe he *can* find something to do. “I didn’t have specific —”

“Great!” Aang interrupts, and Zuko snaps his mouth shut at the Avatar’s burst of enthusiasm. “You can watch the waterbending then.”

Voluntarily spending time around Katara when she’s practicing her tentacle arms is about the last thing Zuko wants to do, given the holes she was trying to burn in him with her eyes all morning. “Um. I was actually thinking that I could maybe…forage? For—”

“But you can’t miss it!” Aang pouts, turning what Zuko thinks are supposed to be polar bear puppy eyes on him. It’s…much less effective than when Sokka does it. “This tandem move has been really tricky, and I think that breathing exercise you showed me is going to make a difference!”

“Um.” That wasn’t permission, exactly. But it also wasn’t a direct ‘no.’ Maybe if Zuko tries another way? “While you guys do that I could actually—”

“Come on, it’s going to be so cool,” Aang presses. “You have to stay and see it!”

“Oh.” Right. Zuko takes a slow, careful breath and tries to shake off the unsettling sensation of being trapped. He isn’t, he’s choosing this and he knew well enough what it could be, he just…can’t quite seem to make himself accept it like he used to be able to. “I…sure.”

“Flameo,” Aang crows, and Zuko stares. Is that…a directive? But the airbender is bouncing off, so maybe not.

Zuko can feel himself getting more and more worn at the edges with each passing degree, stretching thinner and thinner with every crackle of ice and strangely solid snap of water. Zuko can only distract himself from it for so long, even with Sokka offering him cooking knives to sharpen, which—Zuko’s never seen a sharper paring knife in his life. It definitely doesn’t need the additional edge Zuko put on it.

Zuko tries centering his mind on the new feel of his inner flame, tries finding some place between meditative and ready that can let him sit through the rest of Aang’s lesson with Katara. And at least at first, Zuko’s able to distract himself well enough prodding at the bright feeling in his inner flame. He feels dumb thinking of it that way, it's fire, of course it’s bright. But where before it burned and shone and flared, now it does all those things with a halo of warmth. Which, again, fire. But, well—Azula’s inner flame felt cold against his heat sense, and their father’s jagged, so Zuko thinks that the physical properties of fire need not entirely apply, at least when it’s within the bounds of a firebender’s skin.

A person gets acclimated fast to something that’s always inside them, though, and it’s not long before Zuko can’t stop his instinct to fight or flee or *something* from sparking to life with every unnatural swirl of water through the air. Halfway through and he’s already a mess, twitching and hitching and jumping every time Katara or Aang do something particularly fast or flashy or big with their waterbending.

“Zuko,” Sokka says quietly, brow furrowed as he leans over after a particularly violent flinch that has Toph glancing over from across the room. “Why are you—Do you want to be here? I didn’t think this was your…thing.”

“Aang wants me to be here,” Zuko says tightly, forcing his breathing back into control through sheer willpower, trying to coax his inner flame away from the edges of his skin.

“Okay,” Sokka says slowly, face still hesitant. “It’s not because you’re trying to…get used to it, or something?”

“He wanted to show me some breathing thing,” Zuko gets out. “From our lessons.”

“That makes sense, I guess,” Sokka says after a moment, eyeing where Aang and Katara are walking through the motions of a paired bending set. “Do you…need anything? I don’t know, there’s a good spot on the other side of the room. Or I can go get some more cooking knives or something.”

“Can you just…talk?” Zuko says, wincing at how thin his voice sounds, but fuck, there’s a reason Zuko’s tried to avoid waterbending practice in particular. More than just Katara, that is. Agni’s tits, he’s going to have trouble sleeping tonight.

Does telling Sokka when Zuko needs something cover situations where Sokka isn’t the one doing anything?

“Sure,” Sokka says, blinking a moment before straightening with something like determination. “Ah, anything in particular?”

“…Nothing about boats,” Zuko says after a moment, his inner flame turning over itself at how revealing the request is, but…it’s not like Sokka doesn’t *know*, not like Sokka didn’t already make a point of bringing activities and sitting himself next to Zuko for this.

“…Want to hear a moment-by-moment account of the time I was high on cactus juice in the desert?”

“Sounds great,” Zuko says, giving in and letting his heat sense spill outward as he tries to lose himself in the sound and flow of Sokka’s words, the rhythm and cadence of it that’s still rolling and fluid but different enough from the movement and sound of the waterbending in front of him to be enough.

Still, Zuko is feeling undeniably ragged by the time the training session ends. Which might not be why the situation happens in the first place, but maybe it’s why it feels like Zuko fumbles it so hard. Or maybe he shouldn’t try to blame anything but his own special awkwardness for reacting without thinking when Sokka falls into step on his left side.

Zuko shortens his stride without pausing to consult his active mind about it, reaching out with his heat and his hand. For a few brief heartbeats Zuko’s fire curls around Sokka in greeting and their fingers slot together with easy familiarity.

Then Zuko’s breath stops and his steps stutter as he registers what’s happening, just as Sokka’s hand goes rigid against his own. Sokka pulls away like he’s been burned, eyes wide and whole body jerking sideways so hard that he nearly stumbles, and Zuko whips his hand behind his back like it might take on a life of its own if given unimpeded access.

“I’m sorry,” Zuko rushes to say, reaching out his *other* hand to steady Sokka and then yanking that one back too because he can feel his fire reaching ahead of it, and Agni’s dick, they’re practicing so that this shit *doesn’t* happen without Zuko telling it to. “I’m sorry, I didn’t—”

“It’s fine,” Sokka says quickly, flexing his hand open and closed. “I just—I was surprised. I overreacted.”

“I didn’t mean to—push, or anything,” Zuko says, the words nearly tripping out of his mouth.

“No, I—it’s—Zuko, it’s fine,” Sokka repeats, giving himself a shake and shoving a hand through his hair. “What—are *you* okay? I—I startled you?”

“I’m fine,” Zuko says, his heartrate nowhere near normal after this and an entire waterbending’s lesson worth of anxiety as its baseline, his adrenaline trying to spike even though there’s nothing to get worked up about.

“Okay,” Sokka says after a beat, looking half-guilty as he searches Zuko’s face, which— what? “I didn’t mean to…yeah. I…guess it’s not a big deal? Right?”

“…Right,” Zuko says, like his skin isn’t still tingling from the cool press of Sokka’s hand, like his inner fire isn’t straining against his hold. Right. “I—sure. Okay.” He can feel more words pressing against his lip, fighting to burst free, and barely manages to lock them back because he isn’t—he doesn’t *want* to reach for something that isn’t there right now. Fuck, he used to be better at this, but something about Sokka just seems to wash right through his usual control. “Um. Did you…”

“I’m…just going to ask Teo something,” Sokka says before Zuko can find the rest of his question, “His dad used to do some stuff and I don’t want to forget to ask about it.”

“Oh,” Zuko says, blinking. “Sure…” That…was that supposed to make sense? He doesn’t know why the idea of anyone meeting Teo’s dad is so surprising.

Sokka flashes him a quick, tight-eyed smile, his shoulders visibility loosening with the distance as he drops back. All the way back, to the end of the line of people straggling their way topside where Toph prefers to do her training.

Fuck. Just…fuck. Even with Sokka saying it's fine, it’s hard not to feel like Zuko tripped over his own feet with all of that. Which…maybe is why Sokka so often side-eyes all of Zuko’s ‘fines.’

Shit.

“You know,” Aang pipes up from behind Zuko’s shoulder, startling him so bad that he almost makes tripping over his own feet literal. “The monks always said that the lemur that hides too well from its predators also hides itself too well from its prey.”

“I—what?”

“It’s about intentions,” Aang says sagely, clarifying absolutely nothing. “Monk Gyatso always said that a person’s life is the embodiment of their thoughts, and that your thoughts are really just your beliefs. So the course of your life is a record of your values.”

Zuko blinks. “Okay?” Agni’s balls, this is even worse than talking to Uncle. Aang’s actually trying to explain and Zuko still has no idea what he’s talking about.

Aang peeks over his shoulder before sidling closer to Zuko. “What you think,” Aang says confidentially, giving him a knowing look, “Attracts similar thoughts.”

“Thank you?” Zuko has no idea what’s going on. And that was apparently the wrong thing to say, because Aang is eyeing him with a look that’s half-confused and half-put out. “Or…your welcome?” Zuko tries. Fuck, this better not be about destiny.

“I’m talking,” Aang finally whispers, glancing back again, “About your *inner world*.”

Oh.

Wait, no. That still doesn’t make sense.

“Um,” Zuko says dumbly, craning to see what Aang keeps looking at and swallowing back a yelp of surprise when the airbender immediately yanks him forward again.

“Don’t *look*,” Aang hisses, grip surprisingly tight over Zuko’s bicep as he glances around like they’re trying to spot a tail without being obvious. “It’s like you’ve never done this before.”

Zuko hustles a step or two to catch up to Aang’s surprisingly quick pace. “What, ah—what are we doing?”

Aang sighs, a personal breeze gusting around him with the force of his exasperation. “Look —do you like Sokka?”

Does he—does he *like* Sokka? Zuko’s skin prickles with warning. “What does that have to do with anything?”

Aang gives him an incredulous look. “That has *everything* to do with everything! That’s what we’re talking about!”

“…It is?”

“Yes,” Aang says, rolling his eyes as Zuko starts frantically trying to figure out how lemurs and Sokka are connected. Is this about Momo? “So do you?”

Zuko has no idea what’s happening anymore. “Do I what?”

“Like him.”

“Oh. Um.” It really shouldn’t be hard to say when everyone has to know. Even The Duke seems to have figured it out. “Yes?”

Aang makes a face. “Are you sure?”

“Yes,” Zuko coughs, clearing his throat and fighting back a flush as he makes his voice firm. “Yes. I do. Like him. A lot.” And time to stop saying it before he starts providing reasons. Somehow he doesn’t think Aang will take ‘I like the way he says my name’ the way Zuko means it.

“Okay,” Aang nods with all the seriousness of a general preparing for battle. “Good. He likes you too.”

“Um.” Zuko rubs at the back of his neck, wondering if it’s invading someone’s space if Zuko didn’t initiate this. Or is this open communication? It probably doesn’t count if Sokka isn’t actually involved in the conversation... “I’m not sure if he—”

“I’m sure,” Aang cuts in with the immense confidence of someone who’s never themselves been in a relationship.

—w*ould want us to be talking about this*, Zuko silently finishes.

“You don’t run away from holding hands with someone because you don’t like them,” Aang continues, blithely ignoring Zuko’s wince at the confirmation that everyone probably saw that little disaster go down.

“I don’t know,” Zuko says, risking a quick glance back to ensure that no one else is close enough to hear before Aang tugs him to face forward again. “Sokka asked for some space, so…that seems like wanting space, to me.”

“Huh,” Aang digests that for about half a breath. “Okay. Well. He asked for space, but make sure you still show your interest.”

Zuko stares, blank. “He asked for space,” he finally repeats, slower this time.

“And you can give him that,” Aang assures him, again with a complete assurance that… seems to be based in nothing but his own confidence. Must be nice. “But the monks always said that the key to harmony and balance in yourself and in others is a true understanding of not just the limits and bounds of your physical form, but also of achieving alignment with the spiritual form, and nurturing both. So, see? You can do both.”

“I guess…” Zuko says slowly, trying to picture himself doing…that. Whatever that is. He isn’t entirely sure. He could just…ask after Sokka’s spiritual alignment? And somehow that will help? “I’m not really…Are you sure about this?” Sokka just spent a good portion of his cactus juice story complaining about spirit foxes.

Aang shrugs. “That’s what the monks always said. They seemed to know what they were talking about that.”

Zuko pauses to consider that, giving the Avatar a careful look. A twelve-year-old monk might not seem like the most obvious authority on the subject. But the Air Nomads *were* pretty famous for their orgies, from what Zuko gleaned from the scrolls that always Uncle hustled him away from reading, the ones that Zuko didn’t know how to say he already owned.

Zuko takes another glance over his shoulder, breath leaving him in a surprised little noise to see Sokka already looking back. Zuko hastily turns forward again, then eyes Aang thoughtfully. There are worse people to take advice from than the Avatar and Sokka’s best friend.

&#45;-

It takes Zuko a few days to remember the semi-secluded room he found years ago on the fourth floor, and then another day to remember exactly how to get there. It’s more terrace than room, just like he remembered, the canyon-facing wall almost wholly open, the mist and wind curling in almost as easily as it does on the open plazas.

It’s a relief to finally find it again, to have a place that he can go to outside his room that doesn’t require permission to go to. For days he’s felt his inner flame getting tighter and tighter, sharper and sharper, tenser and tenser, and he can recognize this feeling enough to know that he just…needs a break. From still being overly conscious of how he’s training Aang, from Katara, from constantly checking himself when he’s around Sokka when Katara is there, and being around Sokka in general, and just…people, really.

He’s needed this for days, he reminds himself as he settles on the edge of the low window, foot dangling down into the open air. It isn’t because he can’t stop tracking Aang’s progress against the steadily ticking clock. And it’s definitely not because Sokka ran away from Zuko this afternoon like he has fucking pentapox, no matter what Aang seems to think that says about Sokka’s interest, which just—makes no *sense*, you don’t show interest by running away, that’d be like shoving someone into a fountain because you have a crush on them.

So no, Zuko’s needing to calm down and ground himself isn’t because of this afternoon, or the waterbending, or the sense of not knowing what to do with himself despite knowing that he’s doing exactly what he’s supposed to do right now.

That’s just what tipped him over the edge into needing it *now.*

So here he is. Working through it. Too restless to just meditate, and the idea of running through katas—*practicing—*making smoke curl on the back of his tongue. So instead, he’s fiddling with that lump of metal again like he hasn’t needed to do since leaving Caldera. His new post-Ren and Shaw fire seems even more equipped for this than before, which…is interesting. Like somehow his fire sense, or maybe his ability to insulate himself from the heat in his hands, has become even more finely tuned.

If only Zuko’s sense of what he wants the piece of metal to become wasn’t completed washed away by the past stretch of days. Every shape he tries to pull from the metal feels too jagged, or too soft, or too asymmetrical, all of it too wrong to be anything worth keeping. He thinks he can work it out, but frustration sparks hot and tight in his chest that he can’t seem to figure it out *now*.

Zuko’s pressing everything back into a misshapen sphere in a fit of annoyance when he feels another body pressing against his outstretched heat sense. He tenses, wary, then relaxes as he recognizes that whoever it is, they aren’t all that big, which narrows it down to The Duke or Aang or Toph. Zuko…can deal with any of them right now, if he has to, even if he’s more than a little unnerved by the unerring movement toward where he that he was…well, not hiding, exactly, but—he thought no one knew where he was.

He has his right eye on the door, something about the feel of whoever it is—direct, focused, contained without being tight. Did he always used to be able to pick out details like this?— leaving him wholly unsurprised when Toph strolls into the room as if she’d invited him to meet her here.

“Exactly how much of your body,” she says as she pauses to scowl at the entire open wall in front of her, “Is just dangling in the air right now?”

“Um.” He blinks, glancing down at himself. “By weight or by height?”

“Too much, if that’s your answer,” Toph mutters, striding over while adding something under her breath about airbenders. Zuko eyes the closing distance and the tripping-height window ledge the blind girl is rapidly making her way toward. “Relax, Sparrowkeet,” she huffs, grabbing a pebble out of her pocket and pinging it against the low ledge for emphasis. “You’re already loud enough when you aren’t getting yourself bent out of shape.”

“I—okay.” Zuko still doesn’t know how to respond to the casual way she references the fact that she can hear *heartbeats*. Or to the fact that she keeps calling him that and everyone always knows exactly who she means. Does that mean *Sokka* calls him that?

Zuko…doesn’t know how he feels about that. It seems…affectionate?

Toph snorts, dropping down on the floor just before Zuko would have made a move to stop her to set her back to the window ledge. There’s a moment of nothing but silence and Zuko’s confused stare and the swirling breeze, then she rolls her eyes and scootches ever closer so her shoulder is just against his hip. Which…okay. She does seem to inexplicably seek out his presence, and like to sit next to him, and…this is fine. This isn’t weird. It’s…fine.

Zuko forces himself to relax as his inner fire curls out, wary. She isn’t even *looking* at him, and it’s just her shoulder and it’s barely even touching him, it’s not—it shouldn’t—who *cares*. He exhales hard, consciously loosening his body, and to—

Actually, no. This *isn’t* fine. Toph’s already confusing enough to deal with, with her uncontained brashness and total disregard for rules and convention, to also not being able to see when she’s smirking. Zuko twists, carefully so as not to startle or bump her, pulling up one leg to sit half-cross-legged instead, his left leg kicking at nothing outside the window and Toph comfortably within view. There. Better.

“So,” Toph asks once he’s settled himself, seeming unconcerned by his shuffling around. “What are we doing here? Hiding?”

“Um.” Yes, but wait, is he supposed to be doing chores right now?

She cocks her head. “Arts and crafts?”

“…What?”

“Brooding?” She reaches back and pokes his knee when Zuko just stares. “Just need some alone time?”

“Something like that,” Zuko says after a beat, eyeing her as she very much doesn’t offer to leave.

“I get that,” Toph nods sagely. “Sometimes the whole lot of them can be a bit much.”

Zuko isn’t sure if he wants to laugh or sigh at how neatly she excluded herself from that statement. “So, uh—why are you here?”

Toph shrugs. “I’m bored. It seemed like you were up to something.” Zuko glances around himself. He was just sitting still, how…? “And your heartbeat isn’t right for meditating, so. Figured I’d come check it out.” She jabs him in the leg again when he doesn’t say anything. “So what are we doing?”

“We,” Zuko repeats before he can catch himself.

“Fine,” she huffs. “You.”

Zuko’s fingers curl even tighter around the pendant. “Nothing.”

“Nothing,” Toph asks like a trap.

“…Nothing,” Zuko says, aware that it sounds significantly less than certain with repetition.

Toph reaches out with unerring accuracy and flicks his fist. “Then what’s this?”

Zuko freezes, his inner fire sparking with alarm, something shocked and too vulnerable bubbling up in his chest and sliding instinctively toward defensiveness. “Nothing!”

Toph scrunches her face, eyes narrowing in suspicion. “This isn’t a sex thing, is it?”

Zuko chokes. “No!”

“Good,” Toph says, totally unconcerned by his floundering. “Because we aren’t there yet, Sparrowkeet.”

Zuko nearly swallows his tongue. *Yet?*

“So, what is it?” Toph…well, demands. Zuko doesn’t know what else to call that complete expectation that her question will be answered.

“It’s…nothing,” Zuko flails, confusion and rising alarm loud over his thoughts. No one knows, he *knows* no one knows. They can’t, not when he only takes it out when he’s alone. Not even *Azula* knew for sure, and Toph can’t even *see*.

“Well, now I definitely don’t believe that,” Toph says, pausing as her bare foot shifting over the floor. “Why are you freaking out?”

“I’m not—” He absolutely is.

“Am I not supposed to ask about it? You wouldn’t always have it with you if it was nothing.”

“I—what? How—?”

“Oh, I can metalbend,” Toph says casually, lips curling at the corners, like it's nothing, like that falsely humble statement doesn’t have the potential to change entire societies.

Zuko…doesn’t understand. “…You can what?”

“Metalbend.”

It doesn’t make any more sense with repetition. Zuko wonders if he’s having some kind of mental break. Hallucinations. Maybe a stroke. “That’s not…”

“Possible?” Toph’s tone is edged with glee. “It is, I’ll show you.” She reaches out, pausing with her fingers just above his white-knuckled fist. “Is this something special?”

Zuko’s brain is broken. Metal edges are digging into his palm. “Um.”

“I’ll leave it alone then,” Toph decides, reaching into her tunic to pull out a little lump of iron-ore studded stone, the kind that’s all over the earth topside. She holds it up for a moment in the general direction of Zuko’s face so that he can see, after a moment of cross-eyed leaning, that it is, in fact, more metal than rock.

Then she flexes her fingers and it *moves*—not just the parts that are stone but the whole thing. She spins the ore out into a ribbon, then snaps it into a jagged-edged ball, then something vaguely rectangular, and finally just lets it drop back into her palm as a neat little sphere.

“Agni’s flaming dick,” Zuko says, numb. Fuck. He knew Toph was good, but…*fuck*. No one has invented a new bending style since…Kyoshi’s time? That’s when the texts on lightning bending start to talk specifics, at least. “What the fuck.”

Agni’s balls, they could have restrained him real well with that, if they’d accepted his offer to be their prisoner. Zuko had been…somewhat banking on his ability to escape if he had to, when he made it.

Fuck, this…is going to do awful things to all the current protocols for detaining earthbenders.

“Can anyone else do it,” Zuko asks, his voice sounding like it’s coming from a distance as he tries to wrap his mind around the new world he’s apparently been living in.

“Not yet,” Toph says, smug.

“That’s…” Good. That’s good. Great, even.

“I know,” Toph grins, picking dirt from between her toes. “I’m just the greatest earthbender in the world.”

“I…sure.” She is. Maybe ever. And she’s only *twelve*. “Fuck.”

“So,” Toph eventually says into Zuko’s stunned silence. “What’ve you got? The metal feels weird. All…loopy.”

“Oh, um.” Zuko slowly uncurls his fingers, revealing the silver to the light. “It’s…that’s probably because it’s hot.” He reaches out, gently bleeding off the lingering heat. “Is this more normal?”

“Huh,” Toph says, fingers twitching. “Yeah. Heat it back up again?”

Zuko obliges, unconsciously moving his fingers as he does, testing and feeling for the moment when the rigidness starts to give way beneath his touch. He doesn’t need the motion, but something about the whole ritual of it helps to center him, pulling gently on his focus and attention in a way that he needs right now more than when he started. Fuck.

“Oh,” Toph says, sitting up a little straighter. “You’re making something.”

“I…maybe?” He is, he just…has no idea what anymore. “I don’t know, I just…it helps.”

“…Is this actually a sex thing after all?”

“*No*,” Zuko huffs, torn between exasperation and amusement. He can tell that she’s teasing, at least, with the way she’s broadcasting it enough that even he can pick it up.

Toph purses her lips. “Is it a Sokka thing?”

“Ah…”

Toph nods. “Can I see it? I won’t change it,” she tacks on when Zuko hesitates.

He bites his lip, turning the metal in his hands, fighting back his instinctive urge to hide it away. But she already knows it’s here, and it’s not like it’s much more than a lump of misshapen metal at this point. “Okay,” he finally mutters, spinning off the heat until it should be bearable for anyone else before wordlessly passing it over.

His inner fire spikes along with his anxiety anyway, to see the would-be pendant in someone else’s hands. But Toph is treating it gently, with a delicate touch that he shouldn’t find surprising. For all her brashness, she bends with a brutal precision.

“I shitting *knew* it,” she mutters to herself before finally handing it back, which—whatever. Regional Earth Kingdom colloquialisms are the least of his worries right now.

“Knew what,” Zuko asks, half distracted as he folds the pendant back into the warmth and security of his palms, metal digging into the heels of his hands before he makes himself let go and tuck it securely back into his pocket again.

Toph just shakes her head, waving off the question and getting unerringly back onto the track she wants to be on. “So. It’s a Sokka thing.” She flaps a hand toward the otherwise empty room. “Why are you hiding out then? Did you want it to be a secret?”

“Uh—yes?” Zuko seizes at the excuse, but Toph scrunches her face and punches him solidly in the arm, hard enough that he needs to brace to keep from swaying.

“No half-truths,” she warns, and Zuko sighs, shoulders hunching as he relents.

“I just…needed a break.”

“From Snoozles?”

Zuko shrugs, picking at a loose thread at the hem of his shirt.

“I mean…I get that sometimes *I* need a break from Snoozles,” Toph says after a beat. “But I’m not the one making a *necklace* for him.”

Zuko casts her an anxious look at the emphasis she put on that word. “It’s *not* a—”

“I’m going to stop you right there, Sparrowkeet,” Toph says, throwing up a hand, “Before you dig yourself any deeper trying to tell me that it isn’t exactly what it is. I learned courting customs just like you did.”

“…Fine,” Zuko grumbles, cutting his eyes away.

“So.” Toph picks back up the thread of her interrogation. “You’re taking a break from Loverboy?” Zuko winces at the nickname, fiddling with that loose thread again and keeping his mouth shut. “Does that have anything to do with why Sokka was all worked up over talking with Teo?”

Zuko grunts, trying not to react to the idea of Sokka being worked up over anything. Toph scowls at his nonresponse, bending her metal orb into a sudden handful of little marbles and flicking them out, one by one, catching them with her bending and pulling them back without ever letting them touch the ground. It’s…honestly a terrifying display of skill. Even if it were normal stone marbles, Zuko can’t think of many earthbenders who could manage what she’s doing, at least not so casually.

“I guess I get it,” Toph finally says with a kind of barbed sweetness that immediately has him tensing. “I’m sure he’s different than he was in Ba Sing Se. Not the charmer he was before? He *has* been a bit all over the place since the whole complete and utter collapse of his plan to end the war. In a real mood, you know?” All the marbles snap back into her hand with a crack that has Zuko flinching. “And the Lightning Princess giving him a real solid working over in the middle of it, of course. Can’t forget that. Or the fact that his entire tribe except for him and Katara got captured and are imprisoned somewhere. Or—”

“Okay, okay, I get it,” Zuko cuts in, his inner fire twisting from her words. “I already know— I don’t need you to tell me that he has a life here.” Separate from Zuko still, and Sokka might say that he’s happy Zuko is here but that doesn’t mean either of them seems to know how Zuko is supposed to fit. “I’m not—I get it, okay?” He isn’t trying to guilt Sokka into anything or demand that Sokka get over things he isn’t ready to deal with. Zuko…can give him more space. After all, finding their way back to each other might be more than welcome, but it’s not why Zuko's here.

“…That’s not what I meant, Sparrowkeet,” Toph says quietly, jerking his spiraling thoughts to a sudden halt. “So I’m not sure that you do.”

Zuko eyes her, wary, inner fire swirling around the uncomfortable lump of his emotions in his gut. “Then what did you mean?”

“Look, you had a whole plan or whatever to end up here, right?” Zuko shrugs. Not quite this exactly, but close enough. “So you were ready for it. Even just a little bit. But Sokka never thought he would be here. And you know how our Snoozles has plans for everything.”

Plans A through Z, usually, and multiple contingencies for every step of the way. Yes, Zuko is familiar with the way that Sokka shores up his confidence by accounting for every possibility. And he’s become more familiar than he wants to be with the unexpected uncertainty that seems to cling to Sokka these days, following him moment to moment and creeping into the edges of any quiet.

Zuko contemplates the mist swirling around the bottom of the canyon where Agni’s touch rarely reaches to burn it off, turning over Toph’s words. He knew, factually, at a high level what happened in Caldera that day. He knew what Azula planned for, saw pieces of it in distance glimpses, distantly registered in the midst of everything else Sokka’s succinct summary—*‘tried to end the war and it didn’t work, not at all, and then we had to leave* *people behind.’*

Expected, for Zuko, but…not for Sokka.

And for *Sokka* to be here, the way he’s here, and not have thought it out in advance…It’s hard, when the ground gets yanked out from beneath you. Especially when you never saw it coming. When you never even thought a potential outcome was a concept let alone a viable possibility. Zuko…is very aware of that, and the way that it leaves you…a mess, to use Sokka’s word.

Zuko didn’t like the idea that Sokka’s hesitance and doubt were because of him. He thinks he might like this even less, though.

“You were there,” Zuko finally asks. “With Azula?”

“Yeah.” The word is quiet and serious and incredulously frustrated the way only Azula can make a person.

“…What did she say?”

“You don’t know?”

“Neither of them said.”

“Neither, huh?” Toph flexes her hands, the marbles flowing back into a single ball. “Well then you should ask Sokka about it.” She somehow manages to cast him a disappointed look while staring a few feet to his right. “You guys need to get into the habit.”

“We’re already trying to share and ask questions and whatever,” Zuko mutters, aware of exactly how much he sounds like a petulant child as he says it.

“Maybe you aren’t asking the right ones.”

Zuko scowls at the side of her head. “Maybe that’s some cryptic ostrich horse shit that you’re a few decades too young to pull off.”

Toph smacks his arm again, looking torn between glee and affront. “Aang does it all the time.”

“Aang is one hundred and twelve years old,” Zuko says. “Or close to ten thousand. Depending on how you’re counting.”

“Maybe physically or spiritually or whatever,” Toph says. “But mentally?”

“…Point.”

“It took us a bit of time,” Haru explains as they navigate their way through an interior corridor made partially accessible by plunging roots from the forest above.

“When the Prince mentioned them, we decided to go looking,” Teo cuts in. He still struggles to use Zuko’s name.

“But we did it,” The Duke finishes proudly, beckoning Sokka forward.

“That you did,” Sokka says slowly, slipping under a particular aggressive root to enter a wide, high-ceilinged chamber. It’s one of the few he’s seen that doesn’t have a window or opening or entire wall missing to let the air flow through. What it does have are three deep, inset squares in the floor. As Sokka picks his way closer he can see that they’re tiled differently, with small mosaics and designs. Mostly animals, he thinks, trying to picture the way they must have seemed to move and dance as the water shifted over them.

“We think this is where the water came in,” Teo says, wheeling over to the far side of the room where an elaborate, ornate sculpture takes up the entire wall. It’s very…abstract. Arches and swirls and if you look sideways maybe there are figures and creatures peeking out, flowing from the wall out onto the smooth floor.

“And see these channels?” Teo reaches down to brush debris clear from a hand-span wide indent in the floor. “There are a ton of them meandering all over the floor.”

“They all end in the pools,” The Duke supplies, arms out as he walks one curving path for demonstration.

“What we think are the pools,” Teo corrects, ever the scientist.

“Seems like a reasonable theory,” Sokka says, crouching down to examine the sculpture wall more closely. “Is this all one piece,” he marvels, fingers trailing over the stone. “I can’t see any seams.”

“It’s not made with earthbending either,” Haru offers. “I don’t think, at least.”

“It must have been so cool when it was working,” The Duke says, hopping between channels like he’s skipping across a river.

“Yeah,” Sokka agrees absently, trying to figure out if the water would have come out of just one point in the carving, or through the entire thing. From the top is obviously the most logical choice, if the water was coming from topside like Zuko suggested.

“Sokka, are you coming?”

“In a bit, Haru,” Sokka says, half-laying on the ground to get a better look. There are so many holes and dark places and curves toward the bottom of the sculpture that could be decorative but could also be ornately decorated spouts of their own.

“Alright, we’ll see you there.”

“Sounds good,” he mutters. Multiple points, maybe? So that the system wouldn’t get overwhelmed if there were heavy rains? Or maybe just for aesthetics.

It must have been working, when Zuko was here, for him to know about it. That was only what, four years ago, give or take? Sokka shifts to eye the bone-dry pools. So some kind of recent obstruction, or a break in the intake system. If they cleared out the debris and dust and followed the pipes back up toward the surface…It’s all in the walls, though, and Aang wouldn’t want to open anything up. But Toph is so good at sensing things beneath the surface. Maybe she can teach Aang and Haru to do the same? And if the pipes are made of stone or clay too…

But no. This whole place is inverted, hanging off a cliff. The risk to start opening walls—and besides, Sokka doesn’t really know much about piping. He only encountered indoor plumbing for the first time a few months ago, and now what, he thinks he can fix a whole complicated foreign system?

Sokka follows the channel The Duke was walking, brushing it free of dust and twigs as he goes. It seems otherwise intact, all the way to the edge of the pool. Sokka stares down at the sunken, debris-littered floor for a moment, trying to imagine what the room must have been like when it worked. The movement of water, the interplay of light off the surface, pools so big you could practically swim in them.

Spirits, but a bath would be amazing. Not just a quick rinse in a bucket, or standing shin-deep in the shallow, wide rivers that seem to be the only thing available around here. But to be fully in the water, sinking down to his chin, weightless and boneless and drifting…Sokka practically shivers with longing, trying to remember the last time he had that.

Hama’s inn had more of a standing dump-a-bucket-on-yourself situation, and that stolen Fire Nation ship where Aang recovered had showers, which means…

*The taste of spice-and-smoke on his tongue and lips trailing down his throat. A wet hand* *buried in his loose hair, another pressing Sokka close with growing urgency as Sokka’s* *fingers trail over endless firebender warm skin, Zuko between his thighs, pure coiled tension* *in the best kind of way.*

…which means Ba Sing Se, at the Jasmine Dragon.

Sokka shoots to his feet, taking a step back from the empty pool like it’s going to suddenly suck him in, wobbling when he nearly steps into one of the water channels. He expects to hear a snicker from The Duke, or a concerned comment from Teo, and it takes him a moment to register that the sound doesn’t come because Sokka’s alone. When..?

*Dinner*, he realizes, finally out of his own thoughts enough to register the quiet grumbling of his stomach. *They must have gone to dinner*.

Which is a good thing, Sokka decides as he hurries out of the room and retraces his path back toward their usual plaza with as much speed as he can in a place where a quarter of the floor tiles might at any moment just crumble out from underneath you. He didn’t need an audience for that little stumble. Or to comment on how long he might have spent staring at nothing while getting way more flushed and flustered than any thoughts about pipes and water intake systems have any right to make him.

It’s good to have the walk back to get his breathing back toward normal and his heart rate toward something that Toph won’t immediately comment on, to shake the lingering memory out of his limbs of what it feels like to have Zuko beneath him.

The downside, of course, is that it means Sokka is late. And if Teo was exploring, and so was Sokka…that means Katara was cooking.

“So nice of you to finally join us,” Katara mutters, jerking her chin toward the last bowl. “We appreciate you fitting us into your busy schedule.”

“I didn’t mean to,” Sokka says immediately, wincing at how guilty that sounds. “I got distracted and lost track of time.”

“Sure,” she snipes. “You and Zuko, both distracted.”

Sokka glances over to Zuko in surprise, noting the mostly-full bowl in his hands. Zuko just shrugs, shoving a spoonful of jook into his mouth in answer to Sokka’s silent question.

“Well, some of us didn’t get distracted.” Katara is still grumbling. “So some of us got hot food, and the rest of us will just have to deal with what they have since they had other *priorities*.”

There’s nothing worse than cold, congealing jook. Except for maybe self-righteous little sisters who are annoyed their cooking isn’t being represented at its best, and possibly also over the fact that their big brothers might be sleeping with people they don’t like. Which isn’t even happening, and is none of their business anyway, and wouldn’t annoy them if they just stayed out of it in the first place.

“Enjoy,” Katara finishes with false sweetness, and all Sokka’s big brother instincts flare to life.

“I will,” he agrees. “Hey, Zuko—” He holds the bowl out toward the firebender. “—help a guy out?”

“Sure,” Zuko says with the blithe ease of a person who’s missed all of someone else’s sibling dynamics, setting down his own gently steaming bowl and grabbing Sokka’s.

Sokka holds Katara’s increasingly outraged stare as Zuko does his thing, passing back a bowl of perfectly warm jook after a few heartbeats with a relaxed, “Here.” Then Zuko considers for a moment before reaching out and nudging Toph’s half-eaten bowl back up to freshly-cooked temperatures. “There,” he says, quietly satisfied and giving Sokka a quick flash of an almost-smile before tucking back into his own food.

“There,” Sokka agrees with a grin, dropping down in the space next to Aang and shoveling a full bite into his mouth. “Hm. So good,” he says around his food. That always annoys Katara, too. “I love jook when it’s nice and hot.”

There’s a moment of silence, and then Zuko goes, uncertain, “Sure?” and Toph breaks, letting out a cackle and rocking backward under the force of her laughter.

“You—he—how!”

“What kind of bending was that?” Aang cuts in over Katara’s sputtering outrage, ever the peacemaker. “I’ve never seen firebending like that.”

“Oh, it’s just a trick,” Zuko shrugs, darting a glance toward Sokka. “Not many people bother with it.”

Sokka pauses, another mouthful of hot jook halfway out of his bowl, giving Zuko a quick, assessing look. Does Zuko still think that? Or is he just being shy in front of the others? “It’s a really rare skill,” Sokka says, just to be sure. “Barely anyone knows how to do it, and Zuko’s a real master.”

“I’m not a Master,” Zuko mumbles, flushing and ducking his head. “And plenty of people know it, Uncle uses it all the time for tea.”

“Wait, ditch your Caldera Standard ostrich horse shit for a moment,” Toph suddenly says, sitting up and suppressing the last of her giggles enough to talk. “You can heat stuff up without lighting it on fire. Is it just stuff?”

“I mean…” Zuko frowns, glancing at Sokka, who shrugs. He doesn’t know either. What’s the opposite of stuff, abstract concepts? “Do people count as stuff?”

“Table that for later,” Toph says after a pause. “Can you do it with spaces too?”

“…Spaces?”

“Like, for example, this incredibly drafty and cold and completely exposed-to-th- elements plaza we eat and sleep and hang out in. Just, you know. For example.”

“Oh.” Zuko glances around. “Well, not the whole thing—”

“Good enough,” Toph says, rising to her feet and marching across the circle to shove herself down between Zuko and Aang, grabbing Zuko’s arm and yanking him over to her. “Heat pack me.”

“I—what—” Zuko is rigid with surprise, arm caught in Toph’s deceptively strong grip as he looks toward Sokka with wide eyes, seeking explanation or help or maybe something else, Sokka isn’t entirely sure. He’s too busy being shocked that Zuko’s allowing anyone that close into his space, let alone letting Toph sit there touching him like that.

“Toph,” Sokka starts, trying to figure out a way to get her to back off without drawing attention Zuko won’t want. “How about—”

“Shut up, Snoozles,” Toph says, snuggling even closer. “I can hear his heartbeat. He’s fine. You’re just jealous.” She nudges Zuko with her elbow. “Heat pack me.”

“I’m not—!” Oh, fuck. He totally is, not that he has any right to be. He blows out an annoyed breath transferring his attention to Zuko. “Are you—?”

“It’s fine,” Zuko says quickly, cheeks dusted pink but the word ringing true for all his awkwardness and confusion.

“Like I said,” Toph huffs. “So come on. Let’s experience the magic.”

“No fair,” Aang mutters from her other side. “*I* was next to Zuko first, *I* should get heat packed too.”

“You don’t need it, Twinkletoes, you’ve got your never-gets-hot-or-cold airbender thing going on.”

“That doesn’t mean it wouldn’t be *nice—”*

“Nice? *Nice*? I’ve been shivering my tits off here for days, and you care about nice?”

Sokka gapes at the quickly-descending-into-squabbling happening across the circle from him. Squabbling over who gets to sit next to *Zuko*. And Zuko is just…staring at it, mouth silently working, *not* shouting or snapping or snarling or glaring otherwise bristling his way out of the situation, or doing any of the silent, tense, rigid things that Zuko does when he doesn’t want to make a scene.

“You know,” The Duke finally says, looking perfectly comfortable with his cape pulled around his shoulders. “He has two sides.”

Toph and Aang freeze, Zuko blinking at The Duke in surprise. Then there’s a mad scramble that Sokka can barely keep track of, Aang diving over Toph and Zuko trying to fall back off his heels with his arm still caught in Toph’s grip, Zuko’s knees jerking up protectively and catching Aang partway through his dive and Toph screeching in outrage over the whole process.

“Good idea,” Aang says, a little bit breathless as he finally snuggles onto Zuko’s right side like he didn’t almost just knee him in the balls, giving The Duke a smile and sticking out his tongue at Toph.

“Do your thing, Zuko,” Toph orders, pointedly ignoring Aang as she does her own snuggling. “Heat us up.”

“Um. Okay?” Zuko looks to Sokka again, eyes wide with confusion, the skin over his cheek pink from more than just firelight. He’s stiff between Toph and Aang’s bodies in the wake of their frenzied motion, visibly trying to relax inch by inch when nothing more happens, and Zuko doesn’t exactly seem at *ease* but…Sokka doesn’t think he’s asking for help.

Still, Sokka gives a little nod for lack of anything else to do, letting out a little breath of relief as Zuko’s shoulders drop another inch and then catching his breath again when Toph suddenly blinks, letting out a long, “Ohhh,” and Aang sighs, saying “That’s nice,” both of them melting even more against Zuko’s side, and Zuko suddenly seems to just…melt along with them? Like a switch in his brain flipped at those dual affirmations from uncertain-confused-ready to bemused-baffled-just-go-with-it.

And seeing that sudden release of tension, Sokka…doesn’t know if he’s ever been more jealous in his life. Over a pair of *twelve-year-olds.* But watching them both press up against Zuko, seeing the way Zuko *relaxes* with them, knowing that they’re right now probably being wrapped in wave after wave of Zuko’s fire—Sokka knows it isn’t the same as what Zuko does with him, not at all, but he still wants to yank them away. Or maybe join in, hide his face against the sweat and smoke and spice smell of Zuko’s skin and press against him and feel that moment when Zuko just slides into bonelessness. That moment is supposed to be *his*.

Except—it’s not anymore, is it? Sokka gave that up, at least for now, and he knows that there’s no guarantee that ‘for now’ can’t become ‘forever.’ And Sokka isn’t sure how much of that is his new well of uncertainty speaking or something more genuine, but either way it fills him with a nagging urgency that he worries is going to make him rush something he needs to treat with care.

“Hey, Zuko,” Sokka says, poking at his jook. It really is the perfect temperature. “Do you want to train tomorrow?” Shit, they’re supposed to practice chi bending tomorrow, aren’t they. “Or—the day after? It’s—it would be nice to practice sword work with someone else. With you.” Fuck, was that too raw? Was that too much to say in front of the group, when he knows how reserved Zuko is? Fuck, when Sokka knows how reserved *he* is when it comes to the two of them.

“Oh,” Zuko says, eyes wide before he ducks his head, the fall of his hair long enough now to shadow his expression, but not before Sokka catches the flicker of surprise and the softening of the usual tension in his face. “That—yes. We should. That would be…good. Tomorrow or after. I—I’d like that.”

And now it’s Sokka’s turn to duck his head. Zuko’s unexpectedly open shy pleasure at the question, the undertone of warmth in his reply—Sokka feels all flustered and warm, and then a spike of sticky worry that he only asked out of jealousy, except…Sokka *does* want to train with Zuko again. He wants the easiness that had grown between them in Ba Sing Se to finds some space to take root again. He misses that sense of assurance he used to when it came to Zuko. Or maybe that assurance in himself, that confidence that he more often than not knew what to do.

It’s just that none of the ways Sokka knows for how to act toward Zuko seem to work when he’s supposed to treat Zuko like just one of the others. Not when Sokka’s really only ever been alone with him before, outside of Iroh. Not when Sokka can’t seem to look at Zuko without some corner of his mind helpfully remembering what Zuko looks like without his shirt, when just thinking about Zuko sends him down well-worn memories of the weight of Zuko’s cock in his hand, when hearing him talk is enough for the echo of his voice cracking around a laugh to ring in Sokka’s ears. None of which was a problem before and none of which feel remotely appropriate now. Not when the things that used to be just theirs—sharing meals and glances and history and *heat*—are suddenly group activities that require figuring out a whole new way to be.

Spirits, this needing-space thing is just…the worst. And he needs to figure it out, needs to at least find a way toward what Toph and Aang seem to be building with Zuko, that burgeoning ease in each other’s presence, and teasing, and…friendship. Something that could maybe be the foundation for more, if they build it right. Something that never used to feel like such a difficult thing to figure out.
