Zuko doesn’t quite know what to do with himself. Meals are usually the tensest of all the moments in the day. Everyone is present, no one can leave, they all need to interact, and even implying that the food isn’t good enough...

The first time Zuko tried to just grab food and disappear, Aang protested so immediately and loudly that Zuko barely made it a step, and then had to deal with everyone staring at him in blank-faced confusion. The first time he tried to just skip a meal altogether, Katara came storming to find him with an entire grumbled tirade about ungrateful, disrespectful royalty that Zuko was for a moment sure was going to result in him getting kicked out of the group even though he didn’t know eating was the same as a chore.

Zuko still doesn’t love them, even if he can allow that they aren’t as stressful as they were those first few days. There’s more than one person he can tolerate in his left side, and the side conversations and cross-talking no longer make his scarred ear ring trying to keep track of it all, and most of the fumbling, obvious missteps are them—the first time Aang prompted Zuko to participate in story night was…not good. Apparently, the Water Tribes have traditional storytelling structures. Apparently, Katara likes them very much. And *scary* story night—if Zuko hadn’t known Katara had a mean streak in her he would have known it then, particularly after he asked whether her habit of breaking the fourth wall was a technical element or just her own personal style.

So Zuko doesn’t typically look forward to meals at the Temple. They’re when he feels most scrutinized, and most like every action he takes risks a misstep, and when it most feels like Zuko and Katara are somehow dancing around each other with Sokka in the middle, in a way that reminds Zuko uncomfortably of Sokka and Uncle, and…Zuko’s just going to think about that later. Agni, were Sokka and Uncle ever as hostile toward each other when Zuko wasn’t there as Katara is with him when Sokka isn’t around?

But maybe meals aren’t so bad if they lead to things like this. To Zuko with two solid, surprisingly cuddly weights on either side of him who interact as if physical affection were the expectation, not the exception. And to Sokka seeking out time with him. Asking for… support, maybe, in front of the others. Zuko thinks he can get behind mealtimes, for things like that.

&#45;-

Sokka is staring up into the darkness above him, trying to will himself to sink into that blackness as he listens to the sounds of the others’ breathing. There’s Aang’s deep, strong breaths, always even. Toph’s occasional snuffling, a counterpoint to The Duke’s thin, sighing rhythm. Teo, short-short-long in a way that took Sokka a while to get used to, and Katara, so familiar he barely even registers it except for the way her rhythm hitches just a little whenever Haru lets out an intermittent snore.

Sokka should be sleeping too, but he can’t seem to stop counting breaths, counting bodies. He wonders if he’ll ever stop feeling like there’s something hollow in his chest that the number is never what it should be. If he’ll grow used to it enough not to notice, with time, or if it will be just a bit of dissonance he eventually learns to breathe around.

Spirits, he misses just…being able to turn his brain off. Boxing away his worries and finding his way to sleep and waking in the morning maybe not entirely refreshed, maybe not entirely energized, but at least with a new day to work with. He’s never had trouble sleeping before, not for this long at least that the days start to blur together in his mind, and it feels deeply unfair that it would be happening now, on top of everything else.

Though if it weren’t happening, then Sokka wouldn’t be awake to hear the quiet, barely-there rustle of clothing from across the plaza, coming from the direction that no one has bunked down in.

Sokka stills, straining to listen, readying his body to move, to shift Momo and toss back the covers and surge to his feet, and—

Another rustle, an almost-silent step and a huff and a warm awareness in Sokka’s chest and— Oh. Oh.

“Zuko?” Sokka whispers, easing Momo aside and himself upright, scraping his hair back from his face. The campfire is down to bare embers, not enough to see more than the idea of a body in the shadows if Sokka didn't already know it's there, but after a moment the fire catches again, flaring just an inch or two higher, enough to reveal the shape of Zuko against the darkness.

“Sorry,” Zuko says after a moment, shifting further into the light. “I didn’t mean to wake you.”

“No, I was already awake,” Sokka says, getting to his feet because it feels weird to be sitting in bed while Zuko is standing, straightening his sleep clothes and then…running out of things to do. The paving stones are cold against his feet, and it’s that out of every else, the way his toes instinctively curl after the warmth of his bedroll, that makes him suddenly acutely aware that with everyone else asleep, it might as well be just the two of them alone in the darkness.

“Are you okay?” Zuko asks, his face too shadowed for Sokka to really read his expression even with firelight briefly lighting across his scar.

How to even begin answering that. “Just couldn’t sleep,” Sokka finally says, resisting the urge to stack one stone-chilled foot on top of another. “What about you? Why are you awake?”

“…Just couldn’t sleep,” Zuko says after a long moment, and Sokka supposes he didn’t really need to ask.

He shifts in the silence that falls, barely able to make out the way Zuko’s fingers are tangled together, the uncertain set of his body like Zuko rarely allows himself to be in the light. Or maybe like Zuko rarely allows himself to be when he feels like he can be seen, and between Zuko’s intense dislike of being on display and the memory of his intent need to always have Sokka’s eyes, Sokka doesn’t quite know what to make of the fact that he might now qualify as someone Zuko doesn’t think about being seen by.

“There’s no moon out tonight,” Sokka finally offers, not wanting to follow wherever those thoughts might take him this late in the night.

“…There isn’t,” Zuko agrees. Like he wouldn’t be aware.

Sokka takes a deep breath. “Want to go topside?” A silence. “We can look at the stars.”

“Sure,” Zuko says after a moment, and the firelight shifts just enough for Sokka to see the way his eyes drop to Sokka’s bare feet. “That would be—sure.”

&#45;-

Zuko knows a spot, which doesn’t surprise Sokka in the least. By the time they settle back to stare up at the night sky, scattered with familiar stars and deep and endless without Yue’s light, Sokka’s fingers are itching from the urge to reach forward and grab Zuko’s hand, to be tugged along again instead of just invited to follow.

The grass is soft and cool beneath his body, tickling at his exposed skin and poking through his thin sleep clothes, making him hyperconscious of just how underdressed he is compared to Zuko. Bare arms, bare legs, hair down, feet shoved hastily into unlaced boots, and Zuko lying next to him looking like he could be ready to start his day in an instant.

It shouldn’t matter, shouldn’t be anything at all, Zuko probably isn’t thinking a single thing about it. But Sokka can feel a slow flush working down his chest and can’t entirely suppress the shiver that slides through him, his skin prickling with awareness when he sees Zuko glance over out of the corner of his eye.

“We could have waited for you to get dressed,” Zuko reminds him, the darkness making his voice seem even hoarser, even closer than the soft words and stretch of space between them warrants.

“It’s fine,” Sokka says, clearing his throat. He absolutely will not admit that he hadn’t wanted to risk the noise of it waking anyone else or that the delay might give Zuko time to change his mind.

“You’re cold,” Zuko points out, and that…wasn’t what the shiver was about, but it’s also not untrue. The Spring nights are still cool, especially with the wind around here.

Still. “I’m Water Tribe,” Sokka says, flashing Zuko a purposefully cocky smile. “This is nothing.”

Zuko hums, lips quirking before he finally turns back up to the sky, and Sokka releases a slow, careful breath, quiet enough that he’s reasonably sure Zuko can’t hear the edge of shakiness to it. Though Sokka is absolutely sure his hitched breath is audible a few seconds later when he hears the rustle of grass against skin and clothes, out of sync with the rhythm of the breeze—Zuko’s hand sliding slowly over the grass between them.

Sokka holds his breath, clenching every muscle in his body as his heart leaps into his throat, barely biting back a noise he’s sure would be entirely too revealing, entirely too embarrassing, when Zuko’s finger whispers against his wrist, barely even a touch that sends warmth sweeping through him, haloing his body, cocooning him from the chill.

Through some heroic effort Sokka manages to avoid openly gasping for his next breath, or fuck, *moaning*, as Zuko’s hand retreats back across the space between them and Sokka settles into the just-right warmth he’s left behind. Spirits. Fuck. Tui and fucking La. Agni’s flaming whatever. Sokka is aware that Zuko didn’t need to touch him to do that, and Sokka knows that Zuko knows that he knows that Zuko didn’t need to touch him, and fuck, Sokka could get stuck in that loop forever, wondering if he should reach back, if he should have tried to hold on, wondering what else Zuko might have been offering other than literal warmth.

Sokka feels like he might burst from the force of everything inside him trying to get out. Instead, he licks his lips and murmurs, shockingly even, “Thanks.”

“Any time,” Zuko says back, and Sokka wonders if that was supposed to sound like a promise or if it just did by accident.

Sokka forces his hands flat against the grass, forces himself to look up instead of over, clearing his throat and trying to remind himself of all the reasons he needed—needs—space. “The mink snake is bright tonight,” he finally says. They came up to look at the stars. Constellations have to be safe to talk about, right?

“Which one?” Zuko asks, and Sokka doesn’t need to look to picture the motion that would accompany the sounds of rustling and shifting, Zuko tilting his head back, searching the night sky.

“There,” Sokka says, tracing out the familiar pattern of stars hanging in the west.

“We call that the mongoose lizard.”

Sokka stares, then tilts his head to the side. “A mongoose lizard?”

“Yeah, see—” Zuko stretches his hand out, sketching the lines from star to star, and Sokka tries to pay attention to what Zuko is showing him and not Zuko’s hand. Spirits, he’s…a mess.

Sokka wrinkles his nose. “That doesn’t look like a mongoose lizard.”

Zuko snorts. “It doesn’t look like a mink snake either.”

Sokka grins, shrugging and scanning the sky, holding close the sound of Zuko’s amusement as he looks for… “What do you call that one?”

“The archer.”

“We call it the boomerang.”

“…The archer is better.”

“Yeah, kind of,” Sokka laughs, glancing over in time to catch a flash of Zuko’s smile in the starlight. Oh, that…all the struggle of holding himself back is worth it, for that. “Did you learn this stuff on your ship? For navigation?”

“Before that,” Zuko says, and Sokka closes his eyes to soak in the sound of Zuko’s voice like this, calm and easy and raspy, quiet even though they’re the only ones up here. Or maybe because they are. “The stars live in Agni’s sky. She calls them to wake with the dusk and sends them to their rest with the dawn.”

That’s nice. Poetic. “My Dad taught me,” Sokka says, opening his eyes again to find those familiar patterns, remembering nights spent pressed against Dad’s side, their hoods pushed back and breath misting in front of them, glowing white in the moonlight. “We used to go out onto the ice at night. The sky gets so clear in the cold, remember?”

“Yeah,” Zuko says, hushed and like the memory is a good one, which sparks its own kind of warmth in Sokka’s chest.

“He’d tell me the stories of how the Moon set the constellations in the sky, and show me how the skies moved with the seasons so that no matter where I was on the ice or the sea, I’d always be able to find my way home as long as I could see the sky.”

Sokka can see Zuko glance over out of the corner of his eye. “That sounds nice.”

“Yeah,” Sokka agrees after a moment, picking out all those guiding markers—the tiger seal, the crone, the snow rat, the wolf. “It was a nice thought.” Even though he doesn’t think finding home is anything as easy as that anymore, and he knows you can’t always rely on being able to look up and find the sky.

Still, it had kept Sokka warm to know that he could find his way if he was lost, and eventually to remember that Hakoda could do it too. To sit with Katara on the ice and tell her the stories exactly like he remembered Dad doing to him and talk through how to navigate by the night sky, like as long as Sokka remembered and made sure Katara did too, and the little kids when they got old enough, then he could make sure Dad would never forget, either.

Sokka had always thought it was reassuring for Katara, too, but…What did she mean, that Sokka was trying to be like Dad, with a tone like that wasn’t a good thing? Sokka can’ remember a time when he *didn’t* want to be like Dad, and sure, he knows that Katara felt Hakoda’s absence differently than Sokka—Katara feels lots of things differently than Sokka —but Sokka *understands*. He gets why Hakoda had to go no matter how much he wanted to stay. Going is what kept them all safe, what kept the war from coming back to the South’s shores. How could you stay, with that in the balance? No matter how much your children might want you to.

“Do you want to talk about it?” Zuko voice is low as it breaks the silence, somehow both warm and so neutral that Sokka couldn’t find the question an imposition even if he wanted to. “I can feel you thinking.”

“I don’t really know what to say,” Sokka admits. Like that’s something that requires admission at this point instead of just the new status quo of Sokka’s life, apparently.

A moment of quiet, then, “How’s working it out on your own going?”

“…Not great.”

Zuko hums in acknowledgment, not pressing, but how could Sokka not share in the darkness and the quiet, surrounded by Zuko’s warmth and with the hint of his amusement still fluttering in Sokka’s throat.

“Katara said something a few days ago and I just…I don’t really know what she meant.”

“…She’s usually pretty clear,” Zuko says, suddenly dry, and Sokka huffs out a surprised little laugh.

“Is she?” Spirits, Sokka wishes he still felt that way about her.

Zuko’s shrug is more audible than visible. “What did she say?”

“Stuff about my Dad,” Sokka says, an unwelcome, newly familiar uncertainty coiling in his chest. “But like she expected me to know what she meant? And I just…don’t.” And the sense that he’s *supposed* to sits nagging and hard between his shoulder blades, impossible to shake off and impossible to ignore.

Zuko makes a quiet, encouraging noise, and Sokka realizes he’s fallen back into his thoughts again.

“She made it sound like he just…runs away from hard things. But he doesn’t. He’s leading the tribe and the fleet, he left home to keep us safe.” He sent them all away and stayed behind, as Sokka’s plan fell apart around them. “He’s *doing* the hard things. I don’t get what more she wants from him.”

“Maybe,” Zuko finally says, “She thinks there’s something else he should be doing?”

Sokka sighs, shoving a hand through his loose hair. “But what else could he *do*?”

“I don’t know,” Zuko says after a moment, glancing over. “Do you want him to do anything else? Or different?”

Sokka’s breath hitches as he freezes, eyes fixed on the sky. Spirits, how could he even begin to formulate an answer to that? How could Sokka want more of his Dad when what Hakoda is already giving is so hard? How could he think about things being different without thinking about things never happening in the first place? And if Sokka knows that things can’t be changed, that some things can never be changed and that for the rest there was no other option otherwise they would have done it—What does it say about him if still wishes it could have happened another way?

What does it say that it was done anyway, regardless of wishing?

“You might need to ask her,” Zuko eventually says into the silence. “I’m not really an expert on dads.”

Sokka glances over, quick, his paralysis breaking under a stab of alarm. He slumps against the ground, relieved, when he sees that Zuko seems okay. And if he is okay…maybe that was an opening, or an offer, for Zuko to bring that up? “You were just home with yours,” Sokka says cautiously, holding his breath and straining to see Zuko’s reaction in the darkness without openly staring.

Zuko flicks over a quick glance, his face unreadable but his body still mostly relaxed. “I was in Caldera, yeah.”

Sokka waits for more, and Zuko just…waits with him, eyes back on the sky, seemingly content with saying only that, until the questions build and build in his throat and finally Sokka can’t take it anymore. “And how—how was that?” He asks, the words nearly bursting out of him.

“Fine,” Zuko says after a moment, almost contemplative, and in the pause that follows Sokka wonders if it’s possible to die from frustrated curiosity before Zuko adds, “I didn’t really see him all that much. It was probably for the best.”

“Yeah?” Sokka asks, trying to make it sound like the need to know more, to know what happened and if Zuko is truly, actually okay, isn’t clamoring across his thoughts.

“Yeah,” Zuko echoes, considering. “He tried to kill me.”

“That—I know,” Sokka says, trying to keep the fury trying to kindle in his chest from finding its way into his voice. “I remember.” Though he doesn’t know if he’s ever heard Zuko state it so plainly beyond that one time on the ice. “I’m so sorry you had to go back to someone like that. That you had to be around him in the first place.”

“…It turned out okay,” Zuko says, and somehow Sokka isn’t the least bit surprised by how fucking blasé he seems by it. “I meant recently, though,” Zuko adds, glancing over.

Sokka blinks. “What?”

“Recently,” Zuko repeats, clarifying nothing.

“Like—how recently.” Four years ago, recent? Months ago, recent?

“During the eclipse.”

“During the—*what?”* Sokka nearly shouts, shooting upright and staring at Zuko in horror. “The one—the just now eclipse?”

“Technically right after it, I guess,” Zuko says, like that distinction fucking matters.

“You—you almost got—during—” Sokka chokes off, folding over to press his forehead against his knees. Is Azula a fucking prophet, or did she *know*? Fuck, right after—could Sokka have been there? Azula told them how to find the Fire Lord and Sokka chose to retreat instead, and—and then Spirits, Zuko came *here*, and asked to join them, and…

And Sokka feels his heart break all over again.

“I guess I kind of goaded him into it,” Zuko says, considering, like Sokka isn’t struggling to breathe right next to him, like it’s some—some *play* he’s remembering.

“*How*?” Sokka explodes, jerking up in outrage. “What—what even—? *Nothing* you could have done—”

“I kind of told him I was going to go empower his greatest enemy to take him off the throne, and also that his reign is a sham and an embarrassment on the country.”

Sokka stares.

“It might have been a bit provocative.”

“That’s—not—” Sokka sucks in a deep breath, clutching at the grass as his entire body thrums with a surge of adrenaline that’s far too many days too late. “*Nothing* you could have done would warrant that. From *anyone*. Let alone your *father*. Spirits, *Zuko*.” Sokka just doesn’t understand how Zuko can seem so calm about the whole thing, like none of it *matters*.

“I’m not really sure,” Zuko says, sounding nearly introspective as he looks up at the sky, “That he is my father.”

Sokka startles, eyes wide. Oh, fuck. Sokka doesn’t really know what that would mean in the Fire Nation, but he knows enough about the Child of Agni thing to know that *that* piece, at least, would be a big deal.

Zuko glances over at his silence, pulling a face when he sees Sokka’s expression. “Not like that,” he says, waving a hand like he can chase the idea of illegitimacy away. “I mean, the blood part, sure, that was pretty thoroughly answered when I was a kid.”

Sokka…doesn’t know how to respond to the fact that it was even a question in the first place.

“But…being a father. It’s about more than just that, right? Than just the blood?”

Oh. *Oh*. This…Sokka slowly leans back down, mirroring Zuko’s position. This…will probably be easier if they’re both speaking into the darkness, if Zuko doesn’t feel like he has to avoid Sokka’s eyes and Sokka doesn’t feel like he needs to watch his face. “Yeah,” Sokka finally says. “I think so.”

“…What do you think it’s about?” Zuko asks, genuine, quiet.

Sokka takes his time answering, picking his way carefully for things that feel like they have to be true for more than just him. “Caring, I think. Knowing someone, what they want and what they’re afraid of. Wanting them to be happy. Trying to make their life better. Trying to keep them safe.”

“I think,” Zuko finally says, “That Uncle has been more of a father to me than the Fire Lord.”

Sokka…certainly can’t argue with that. “You sound sad about it,” he says carefully, trying his best to pull back his gut reaction to Iroh and what kind of parent the man was or wasn’t to Zuko.

“He kept a secret from me,” Zuko says, a thread of uncertainty winding into his voice, and Sokka barely holds back a noise. Just one? “And I just…feel weird about it.”

Sokka considers a range of responses, settling on, “Oh?”

“I’m keeping it, too, so I get it. Sometimes it’s too dangerous for people to know something.”

Sokka makes a listening noise, because he’s trying to hold back too many words and questions to be able to say something else.

“But…you can withhold something with actively lying about it,” Zuko frowns, which Sokka…is very aware of when it comes to Zuko. “But he did lie. To lots of people, I guess, not just me. And it’s not like I don’t know how these things work. Sometimes someone’s reaction is what really makes everyone else believe it, you know?”

…Sokka was less aware of that. But now he knows, and…it’s something to think about if Zuko talks like it’s a fundamental part of how people interact.

“But I still…” Zuko trails off, sighing. “I just keep wondering if I did something,” he finishes, frustration and something tight that might be hurt breaking into his voice. “Why did he think he needed to lie to me, too? He could have…not said anything. Everyone else already believed it, he didn’t have to repeat it.” Zuko glances over, searching for...something. Maybe an answer, and Sokka hates that he doesn’t have one to give. “I just…don’t know what I did to make him see me that way.”

Sokka swallows his own sadness back down, feeling like he’s never been more aware of the stretch of space between them, of how much he wants to breach it. “Sometimes it’s like people have already decided what they’re going to seen when they look at you,” he finally says, trying to offer understanding since he can’t offer anything else. “And it’s like they stop looking, you know?”

“…Yeah,” Zuko says, sounding exhausted. “I…yeah. I know.”

“And maybe you’ve figured it out,” Sokka adds, looking up at the sky because if he doesn’t, he’s going to break and reach and Spirits, he doesn’t want to misstep now of all times. “But I don’t really know how to change it. Even though there has to be something you can do to make someone see you, right?”

A long stretch of silence, so long Sokka would wonder if he misspoke if it didn’t feel so contemplative. Then Zuko shifts, rustling in the darkness to tilt his head away from the sky and fix his eyes on Sokka’s profile instead, and Sokka lets out a startled laugh when he realizes what Zuko’s doing.

“I didn’t mean it literally,” Sokka says, glancing over to share in the joke and flushing, surprised, to find Zuko’s face totally serious instead.

“That’s fine,” Zuko says, quiet. And he makes no move to turn his gaze, eyes steady and calm and gleaming gold in the thin starlight, and Sokka can’t bring himself to look away either, to end this moment of being seen.

&#45;-

Zuko is just starting to think that it might be time for them to head back inside when Sokka suddenly stirs, something Zuko both hears and sees and feels against his heat sense in a barrage of sensation that leaves his inner fire somehow caught between straining tension and melted uselessness.

“Do you ever think sometimes there’s just something you need to do?” Sokka asks, his voice so low it almost blends in with the wind.

“Yeah,” Zuko says after a moment. That could be a joke if Sokka didn’t seem so serious.

“What do you do?”

Zuko glances out of the corner of his eye, unsure how it’s even a question. “I just…do it.”

“…Huh,” Sokka says, quiet, and Zuko isn’t sure what to make of the fact that that sounded like a revelation.

## Chapter 16: Stirring the Pot

### Text

“Just keep your mind on the flame,” Zuko instructs, managing to keep his voice low, free of the tension settling in his hands as he watches the two candles flicker back and forth and back again, one at a time, never together.

For a few heartbeats, the leftmost candle matches Aang’s breath, then abruptly returns to its own dance as the wind lifts.

“Remember to count your breaths,” Zuko supplies, one corner of his mind frantically trying to figure out how Aang went from being able to do three candles yesterday to barely one today. “Firebending comes from the breath.”

Meditation has so far been a sure-fire way to get Aang into a groove and over a hurdle with his firebending. Zuko isn’t sure what to do with the fact that this time it seems to be making it worse.

“The count is one, and, two, and…” Zuko says evenly, his fingers tapping out a much more rapid rhythm when the flame starts finally flickering in Aang’s control but with the speed and threadiness of agitation. Occasionally it gains a few breaths of steadiness before losing it again, like a deer dog puppy chasing after a treat and only occasionally remembering that it’s supposed to sit and stay to get its reward.

“Alright,” Zuko says, his normal speaking volume causing the Avatar to snap his eyes open with a start and an unmistakably guilty look as Zuko snuffs the two candles. “You’re distracted. It’s too dangerous to firebend when you can’t concentrate.”

“I know,” Aang droops, sheepish. “I’m sorry.”

“Fine.” Zuko waves that away. “Just—what is it?”

“It’s nothing.”

Zuko fixes him with the mild stare he’s learned makes Aang squirm far more than any scowl. “If it was nothing then you would be able to pay attention.”

Aang bites his lip, poking at the ground and darting quick glances toward Zuko’s face. “Can I ask you something?”

Zuko tries to parse whatever that expression is. “…Is it about firebending?”

“Yes.”

“Then yes,” Zuko says, relieved, because for a degree he thought Aang was trying to work up the nerve to ask something personal.

“That heat thing you do…”

Agni burn it.

“With the food,” Zuko tries, pressing his hands flat against his thighs and using everything he has not to glance over to where he knows Sokka is sprawled across the ground, working on some kind of sketch or something.

“With the body heat.”

Zuko takes another desperate stab at directing the conversation to safe ground. “With you and Toph?”

“No, the thing you do all the time.”

Okay, that…seems safe enough, but now Zuko has no idea what he means. “What?”

Aang blinks, head cocking. “You know. The heat thing.”

They stare at each other in confusion.

“…There are different parts of firebending,” Zuko finally says. Hopefully he’s reaching for the right answer. “Not everyone can do all of them, or even more than one. There’s the inner and outer flame, obviously. That’s the most common. But there’s also lighting, which is often called cold fire, and heat, which is sometimes called—”

“Hot fire?”

“…No.”

“If you can do things with heat does that make you a hotman?”

“…Which is sometimes called the unseen fire,” Zuko picks back up, deciding to just completely ignore that question. “At least, that’s what my Uncle says.”

Aang thankfully goes along with it. “So as I get better at firebending, will I be like you?”

“What do you mean,” Zuko asks, already bracing himself for another conversation on the limits of what he can teach Aang. If Aang masters firebending then by virtue of that very act he won’t be like Zuko.

But Aang just says, “Running hot,” and it takes Zuko a few blank heartbeats to realize what he must be talking about.

“Oh,” Zuko says, glancing down at himself like there’d be anything to see. “That’s a Caldera thing, I guess. To kind of…press outward.” There are other ways to show dominance than controlling the fire in the room, after all. Particularly when the Fire Lord or Azula are present. “And no, not necessarily. A lot of firebenders run hot, but it might be different since you’re the Avatar. And most people don’t have the touch for lighting or heat, anyway. Just like not everyone can metalbend.”

“Huh,” Aang says, pressing his fingers on his arm like he might feel his body temperature changing just from that. “So does that mean you invented it like Toph did?”

“What?” Zuko almost laughs. “No.”

“That would make you the best firebender in the world,” Aang muses, testing the skin on his chest now.

“…I’m not.”

“Are you sure?” Aang frowns, glancing up and then over to Katara and Toph. Zuko’s shoulders tighten without his permission. He doesn’t need the reminder that he falls short compared to the Avatar’s other instructors.

“I’m just going to pull it back, for now,” Zuko finally says. “Since it seems to be distracting you.” He consciously coaxes his heat back underneath his skin, wrapping it into his fire sense, aware now like he never normally would be of the way it was pulsing gently in time with his breaths.

“Okay, Sifu Hotman,” Aang sighs, turning back to the candles arrayed between them.

Zuko stares. “…No.” That will not be his new name. No.

“What was that?” Sokka calls with uncanny timing, glancing up from his work. “Did Toph come up with a new nickname that I missed?”

“No,” Zuko repeats, as Toph cheerfully shouts out, “That one was all Aang!”

“I already have enough names,” he insists, a little desperate. But Aang is giggling, and when Zuko glares at him Aang just makes some hand-sweeping gesture Zuko doesn’t understand. Zuko frowns, confused, and after another giggle Aang rolls his eyes and tips his head toward Sokka, Zuko following his gaze and realizing with a jolt that his heat curled back out without him noticing, reaching toward Sokka the moment Sokka started speaking.

Zuko flushes, yanking it back and pretending he doesn’t see the way Sokka sways a little where he’s propped on his elbows, frowning down at himself before glancing around and shooting Zuko a questioning look.

“I think I get it, Sifu Hotman,” Aang says, sounding distinctly satisfied, and as Sokka makes a choked little noise that sounds suspiciously like a laugh, Zuko realizes that he’s never going to get rid of this one.

&#45;-

Zuko is feeling…good. About Aang’s progress today after his rocky start. About Sokka asking to train again. About all of the other night, which might not have felt relaxed or at ease like he and Sokka used to be, but also not like the tension was *bad*—it was like the whole conversation was wrapped in possibilities and maybes, filling Zuko's chest with the about-to-leap anticipation that comes just before jumping a gap between the rooftops.

There’s no way Zuko could be the only one who felt that way, right? There’s no way something like that could have stretched into every heartbeat, occupied every silence, if it were totally one-sided. His inner fire is flipping and looping and twirling, crackling with an excitement that Zuko can’t quite bring himself to embrace but also can’t bring himself to bank back.

It’s a dangerous kind of lightness, burning at the edges of Zuko’s usual caution, but as Zuko makes his way over to Sokka, absently skirting a few overgrown fallen columns, Zuko can admit that he doesn’t have eyes for much else but him. How could he, with the way Sokka’s almost-topknot is brushing the back of his neck in the breeze, and the familiar white of his wrist wraps setting out the darkness of his skin, and the way he just seems to *occupy* any space he’s in. And then the deep blue of his eyes as he glances up, rimmed with tiredness but crinkling in the corners as he catches sight of Zuko—

“Hi,” Zuko says, the word only a little-bit breathy.

“Hey,” Sokka says, smile flashing before he ducks his head back down. Zuko thinks he can see a blush dusting his cheeks, but Sokka’s shoulders stay relaxed, and when he clears his throat and glances up again his face is only a little bit uncertain, which is…good, actually, compared to what Zuko is used to seeing of him recently.

“What’s up?” Sokka prompts, jolting Zuko back to his purpose.

“Can I, uh—can I sit?”

“Oh, yeah, of course,” Sokka says with a jolt, blinking around himself before grabbing up the pieces of disparate leather he’s been working with—some kind of wrist guard? A bag? Zuko can’t tell if he’s taking something apart or putting it together—and hauling it into a half-haphazard pile.

Zuko settles into the space Sokka clears, trying not to be self-conscious as he rests on his heels and immediately fails to remember what was supposed to come next. Which is always Zuko’s issue. Once he gets going, he’s fine, but the getting going…Azula used to despair that it took Zuko at least three tries to hit his first cue every time.

“So,” Sokka finally says, smoothing a piece of leather against his knee and glancing over. “What'd you think of Aang's lesson today?”

“It was fine.” Zuko takes a deep breath, soothing down his inner flame and finding his way back toward his opener. “I wanted to ask you…”

“Yeah?”

Sokka takes another peek at him when Zuko doesn’t reply, his face open, curious, and it’s such a familiar expression, such a *Sokka* expression, that Zuko just goes for it. “I wanted to ask you about your spiritual…alignment?”

“…What?”

“Um.” Zuko scrambles to remember Aang’s phrasing. “Your, uh. Your inner world?”

“My—*what?”* The leather slips off Sokka’s knee as he stares at Zuko, brow furrowed. “Zuko, what are you trying to ask?”

“Um.” Zuko’s script feels like it's going up in flame. “Aang said something about…lemurs hiding too well?”

“Aang? Is this about Momo?” Alarm flashes over Sokka’s face. “Did Aang lose him?*”*

“No, no,” Zuko flushes, floundering, wincing as he hears the desperate undertone in his words and trying to calm himself and find his mark again. “I wanted to ask about your… spiritual self.” Fuck, that wasn’t it. He can hear how clunky his words sound, can already anticipate how awkwardly they’ll land without needing Sokka’s incredulous look to confirm it.

“Zuko,” Sokka says finally says, slowly, “You know I think all that spirit stuff is a load of shit.”

Zuko…is aware of Sokka’s general lack of patience for the supernatural. But… “All of it?”

“*Yes*,” Sokka says, rearing back like he needs distance to understand, which…wasn’t exactly the outcome Zuko was going for. Fuck. “Don’t tell me you’re about to start talking about fortune-telling or horoscopes or fate or some shit.”

“*No*,” Zuko says, surprising himself with his own vehemence, inner fire spiking and every muscle in his back tensing at the mention of fate. “No. Just…”

“Just what,” Sokka presses after a beat, fingers picking at his wrist wraps in little jerks, searching Zuko’s face like *Sokka* is the one losing the thread of the conversation here instead of Zuko being the one to…he doesn’t even know what. Fucking *metaphors*.

Zuko ducks his head, eyeing the doorway before forcing himself to look back to Sokka. Agni, why was this so much easier in the darkness? Maybe because Zuko wasn’t trying to do anything then, wasn’t scripting and planning and trying to follow advice he barely understands like being off the *Wani* will suddenly make that possible.

Agni’s balls, he should have never started this in the first place. Or started with something else, it’s not like Sokka was demanding to know why Zuko was here. Zuko could have just stuck to talking about his day, or fuck, just *shrugged* and enjoyed Sokka’s company and seen what Sokka might have filled the silence with.

Fuck Aang’s advice. Aang is twelve. And Zuko is an idiot, but he’s in it now, and maybe he can still find a way out.

“Just that, sometimes…I know you don’t like it, but…I mean, you were in that swamp once. Right? Before Ba Sing Se?” He winces when Sokka’s fingers spasm against his wrist wraps but presses forward anyway because *not* pushing is what they did before, and…Zuko doesn’t think that worked. “And maybe…near the Si Wong Desert, something happened too?” Zuko is less sure of that one, but—Zuko knows what Sokka’s inner flame feels like. And after hearing about that cactus juice incident... “It seems like—”

“Hold on a shit.” Zuko and Sokka both flinch as Toph’s sudden exclamation cuts over Zuko’s words, Zuko nearly falling off his heels as he belatedly registers that she’s just off his left shoulder, just into the edge of his blind spot. Fuck, how long has she *been* there? “Sokka’s cactus juice hallucinations were *real?”*

Zuko glances toward Sokka, inner flame still flickering with surprise in his chest. Openness in front of each other and in front of the rest of the crew is…not the same. “Uh…”

“That’s amazing,” Aang breathes, suddenly materializing over Zuko’s other shoulder and Zuko can’t stop himself from sharply scooting back to get both of them into view, his heart pounding in his throat as he looks wildly around. Sloppy, dangerous, *fuck*, how did his heat get so wrapped up in Sokka that he didn’t notice anyone else around?

“It’s like you both have some kind of spiritual connection,” Aang is saying when Zuko drags his attention back. “The monks spoke sometimes of people sharing an intertwined—”

“I’m pretty sure that’s not it,” Sokka cuts in before Aang can say anything about destiny or fate, thank Agni, but his tone sharp and repressive enough that Zuko still can’t hold back a wince. Except then their eyes catch, and Sokka rubs at his chest with something like idleness except for the directness of his gaze, and—

Oh. That. Zuko’s bending interwoven with Sokka’s inner flame is certainly *a* connection, its absence still nearly as clear against Zuko’s heat sense as its presence was.

“This could be really important, guys,” Aang protests. “We should work this out. How far back—”

“Aang,” Zuko says, unable to even think about cutting the Avatar off as he eyes the way Sokka’s fingers are tightening around his own wrist. “I don’t think it’s actually a big deal.”

“Not a big deal! You already said there were two instances. And the Swamp is a spiritual connection point—” A what? “—but the Si Wong Desert isn’t!” Aang is practically jumping in place with excitement. “Has this happened any other times?”

“What does it matter?” Sokka asks, and Zuko can’t tear his eyes off the way Sokka’s fingers are nearly white-knuckled now. Zuko isn’t exactly excited about the idea of the others knowing the details of what he can do with Sokka’s inner flame, but this feels like more than just that for Sokka.

“Do you know how rare this is?” Aang exclaims, throwing out his arms. “It could be the first case in centuries! How far back can you remember? Does Sokka always initiate it? What happens? Do you know if—"

“I don’t know anything,” Sokka bites out, tight and defensive like Zuko has rarely seen him. Fuck, fuck, Zuko needs to find a way to end this.

“Come on, *try*,” Aang pleads, nearly whining. “Sokka, even if it’s nothing with Zuko, to be untrained and have *two* spiritual encounters? In a few months? And I know there’s Yue, and the Spirit Library, and Hei Bei, and—”

“*I don’t want to talk about Hei Bei.”*

Aang snaps his mouth shut, eyes wide, even Toph flinching in surprise. Zuko sucks in a breath, his inner fire shoving urgently against the underside of his skin as he tries to catch Sokka’s eye, but Sokka’s too busy glaring at Aang to let him. And Toph just looks blank when Zuko glances at her, and Zuko has no idea why but Sokka is so clearly upset, and Zuko can’t just let that *go*. “What’s going on?”

Toph stirs but doesn’t say anything, and Aang just stares down at his hands. Sokka finally puffs out a breath and cuts Zuko a look that almost seems expectant, questioning, but why would Zuko know—

“Oh.” Memorized words from a letter that’s long since disappeared into the ocean bubble up, words about worlds turned upside down with nothing left to stand on. About the Spirit World, and insecurities made real, and desperately needing a touchstone to reality. That…really isn’t where Zuko expected this to go when he started. To the extent that he expected anything. “Before the island…?”

“*Yes*,” Sokka says, voice strained as he starts furiously piling up the pieces of leather he was working with, hands messy and fumbling. Getting ready to leave, Zuko realizes. Agni’s flaming dick, after being asked to train and looking up at the stars and that sense of possibility thrumming between them, Zuko turned around and is making Sokka *run away*.

The too-fast edge to his inner fire is trying to feed Zuko’s clamoring thoughts, his hands fluttering uselessly in the air as he searches for some way to fix this. “Okay, well—” He surges to his feet in a stumbling rush, unable to look at Sokka, unable to look at anyone, except now everyone is staring at *him*, and Zuko’s mind just…goes blank. And then throws itself desperately back to the script. “Here.”

“I—what?” Sokka barely gets his hand up in time to catch the packet of jerky Zuko fumbles out of his pockets and tosses toward him, which would just be the sweet glaze on this bao bun, if Zuko *hit Sokka in the face* while trying to nurture his physical form or whatever the fuck Aang was talking about.

But Sokka isn’t making like he’s going to immediately walk away anymore, even if he’s just sitting there looking baffled, and Zuko knows this part is right, at least. He might have completely fucked up the lead-in, might have no idea what to do with the spiritual, but Zuko knows what to do for the physical.

And maybe Zuko can still end this on a moderately successful note, now that Sokka looks knocked off the tight edge of his tension.

“I’ll, ah,” Zuko begins, just as Haru and Teo and The Duke burst into the plaza in a clamor of overlapping voices, The Duke somehow hitting a pitch that has Zuko’s scarred ear ringing, and Agni’s balls the only one missing is Katara, and with that thought, Zuko is just done.

“I’llseeyoulater,” he says in a rush, already making for the closest open doorway at a pace that could generously be called a brisk walk if the person naming it had never heard of running before. Which just makes Zuko’s inner flame twist even harder. Fuck. *Fuck.* Way to seem like a steady, competent, attractive human being. Agni’s dripping tits, sometimes he wishes he could just turn off his brain.

And his ears, because Zuko might be nearly running away, but his hearing is still far better than it should be once The Duke stops yelling.

“*What* just happened,” Toph demands

“I have no idea,” Sokka says, tone utterly confused, which is just—great. Great.

“…Are you at least hungry?” Aang asks as Zuko finally makes it to the relative safe-from-eyes privacy of the hallway.

“I—yes?”

Well. That’s something, at least.

&#45;-

“What,” Sokka asks, still staring after Zuko like maybe if Sokka looks intently enough Zuko will come back and help him understand what just happened. “Was that.” Spirits, he doesn’t know if he’s ever been as uniquely confused as Zuko is able to make him. Did he always use to feel this way? Did he just forget? Spirits, it’s like being back on Zuko’s ship again, trying to figure him out through prison bars.

“Wow. Okay,” Aang mutters, rubbing at the back of his head before turning to Sokka with something that looks like resolve. Sokka’s chewing slows so he can give Aang an appropriately suspicious look. *Why* would Aang be looking so determined after that? “Zuko was asking about you, right?”

“I—yes?” With a kind of focused, stilted purpose that had Sokka assuming they were about to talk about Zuko needing more from Sokka, or maybe some questions he needed answered, or…literally anything other than Sokka’s spiritual beliefs. Spiritual encounters? Sokka still isn’t entirely sure.

“Maybe he was trying to show that he’s interested in you?”

Sokka gives that a moment’s consideration as he polishes off his jerky. “No,” he finally decides. “I don’t think that’s it.” Zuko’s always been so forthright about it in the past, demanding Sokka write his name, slamming them into their first kiss, suggesting the training that slowly expanded the bounds of the time they spent together. Why would that change? Especially when, unlike all those other times, Zuko is aware of Sokka’s interest? Sokka explained back in that clearing after all, that he just needed time, not that he wanted an end.

…Right?

Aang briefly closes his eyes. “But wasn’t he asking about you? Something new?”

“Yeah, about spiritual…stuff,” Sokka says, feeling his face twist with automatic distaste. “Which doesn’t make sense, why would he—” Sokka straightens around a bolt of alarm. “Shit, do you think he was asking because it’s important to him?” Zuko’s mentioned the Fire Sages before, but Sokka always thought it was from a procedural perspective in terms of their relationship with the throne. Has Zuko been quietly devout this whole time and Sokka’s just been running roughshod over his faith without realizing it? Except Zuko curses like he curses, and wrote that he wasn’t sure he believed all that stuff about Agni’s blessing—

No. Zuko wrote that he wasn’t *always* sure that he believed it. Fuck. *Fuck*.

“Aang,” Sokka says, feeling a knot of desperate urgency take root along his spine. “Has Zuko ever talked to you about spirit stuff? Did any spirit stuff happen on the Sun People’s Island, or whatever it was? What kind of stuff did he say? Is he—are there rites he needs to do, or something? Does he worship anyone other than Agni? Do I—is it stuff with fire? I can—”

“Maybe,” Toph cuts in, overly loud and shutting Sokka right up, “Zuko was just trying to learn about you.”

Sokka stares. “But…he already knows about me.” At least in this regard. Right? No, it feels more like Zuko must have been trying to tell Sokka something, a thing that was hard for him to say. That would explain his determination and uncertainty, and Zuko always circles around a problem before finding a way to dive in. Spirits, Sokka fucked it up. He thought it was about him when really it was about Zuko, and isn’t that just how Sokka seems to work these days? Shit, he’s been trying to be *better*.

Sokka needs to find Zuko, needs to fix this. He’ll sit and listen and he won’t judge and he’ll just…take it in, and figure out what Zuko needs from him here. How Sokka can support or help or…Spirits, he has no idea what that would even mean. He should have been listening more to Aang whenever he went off about spirit stuff, then Sokka might know what to say or do instead of needing to rely solely on instincts he still doesn’t know how to trust, particularly with this.

“There’s always more to know about a person,” Aang is saying. “No one can ever be fully known. Not even by themselves.”

“…Huh,” Sokka says, half-distracted, trying to figure out what to do. “Sure, I guess.” Fuck, even trying to plan his way through something as small as this is making his lungs feel tight, is making his heart crawl up into his throat, and Sokka doesn’t have time for whatever his body is trying to do. He needs to get his shit together and figure this out and fix it. “So I shouldn’t expect Zuko to be fully aware of what he was trying to tell me?” That’s…going to make it harder. But Sokka knows how that feels, and he and Zuko have had those kinds of conversations before, right? Slowly drawing out the words they don’t quite know how to say to each other, giving each other space, being present.

“…I think you shouldn’t ask Zuko what he was trying to do,” Toph says after a moment, scowling at Aang which—did Sokka miss something?

“But—”

“Did Sparrowkeet seem like he wanted to talk about it?”

“Well—no.” He can’t really describe what Zuko did as anything other than bolting. “But Teo and the others came in, and he isn’t the most—”

“Let’s just look forward,” Toph suggests with the kind of firmness that suggests she’ll allow nothing else to happen. “Let’s put this one behind us.”

Sokka eyes the doorway Zuko disappeared through again and wonders how much he can trust his urge to reject her suggestion and how much of it is his automatic, outsized dislike of those specific words. “I’m not sure—”

“Well, I’m sure of something,” Toph cuts in again. “You’re training with Zuko soon. Just the two of you. Sweating it out, swords clashing, muscles working…”

Sokka jerks his head toward her in shock, choking as he tries to haul himself into a suddenly wildly different conversation, trying to keep his blood pressure from spiking. “…Do you even know what you’re trying to imply?”

“Nope,” she says cheerfully. “But I know it makes everyone’s hearts do interesting things.” Her grin turns wolfish. “Want to explain it to me?”

“I think training sounds like a great opportunity,” Aang gamely redirects, not looking in Toph’s direction as if he needs to hide the redness of his cheeks from her.

Sokka eyes her another moment, then transfers his skeptical look to Aang. “…A great opportunity to what?”

“To make your intentions known!”

Sokka nearly chokes on his own air again. His *intentions?* “I’m not courting him,” he gasps out, darting an alarmed look around the plaza to see if anyone else is close enough to be listening in. Courting is—courting is formal declarations between families on your behalf, and chaperoned walks, and households hosting each other, and pointed interrogations, and— and *Katara* is his only family around, since Dad is—Sokka and Zuko can’t *court*.

“Maybe you should be,” Aang says with a pointed glance toward the space Zuko was just occupying.

“I don’t even know if—I’m not—”

“You know,” Toph says, pinging an annoyed rock off his shoulder. Spirits, this conversation has been spiraling out of control from the moment Zuko walked over.

“Courting is an opportunity to learn more about each other,” Aang says earnestly, ignoring Sokka’s incoherent noises. “It’s when you figure out whether or not you and the other person fit.”

“I…” Actually. That *would* be nice. Sokka knows that he and Zuko fit together, but…it would be good to know how they can fit together *here*. “How would I even—” It’s not like he’s ever seen any couples courting back home to use for inspiration. The closest example he has is Yue. Or *Jet*, ugh, and Sokka can’t do any of *that*.

“Ask him for help with something, or to teach you something,” Aang encourages, “Like caring for your weapons.”

“…But I already know how to care for my weapons,” Sokka frowns. “Zuko knows that I know how to care for my weapons.”

Toph rolls her eyes. “That’s the point.”

Sokka…doesn’t understand. He’s supposed to pretend to be incompetent, and somehow that makes his intentions clear? Why does he have to pretend, he’s already feeling incompetent enough as it is. “I don’t know, guys…”

“It’s a thing to do together, Sokka,” Aang says, exasperated. “Don’t overthink it.”

At this point in the conversation, Sokka is so confused that he doesn’t know if he’s physically capable of overthinking anything. He can’t exactly seem to wrap his mind around it in the first place. “But we’re already going to train. That’s a thing to do together.”

“Sweet Oma,” Toph mutters before straightening. “Alright. Then how did you flirt with him before?”

“How did I—what?” When Sokka thinks of flirting he thinks of giggling and winking around double entendres and…Jet. Sokka thinks of Jet. And Sokka and Zuko didn’t exactly do…that. They just kind of…went for it.

“How did you signal that you were interested before?” Aang asks, ignoring the way Toph drops her face into her hands. “How did you know that he was?”

“Um.” Zuko was prickly and focused and defensive and like walking face-first into blizzard, all breath-stealing power and overwhelming intensity, and Sokka was…into it. “Well, we wrote these letters…”

“I’m aware of that,” Aang says, with a patience that borders on sarcasm, gesturing for Sokka to go on.

Except there is no ‘go on.’ “That’s…what we did.” And even that—Sokka didn’t know it was Zuko for so long, does the letter-writing even counts for this?

Toph scrunches her face in confusion. “Like…sexy letters?”

“*No!”*

“…That’s half lying.”

“We didn’t—not—not like *that*!”

“…Truth,” Toph says after a moment, sounding dissatisfied. “Fine.”

Sokka groans, hiding his face in his hands. He needs this conversation to end, please, and now if possible. Spirits, how *did* he and Zuko do it? Lots of things half-said and crossed-out that they both knew the other could read if they tried hard enough, and seeing between the lines and taking it on faith and eventually… “Zuko kind of just asked.”

“Well,” Aang says after a beat. “Maybe it’s your turn this time.”

“But he already knows I’m interested,” Sokka points out, but even though his voice comes out strong he feels a waver of uncertainty in his chest. Zuko…*does* know that, right? Sokka can’t imagine *not* being interested in Zuko, though he made it clear that he thinks Zuko is… pretty wonderful.

“Still sounds like it’s your turn,” Toph shrugs. “It’s not like hearing it again is a bad thing.”

…Fair. And after fumbling whatever conversation Zuko just tried to have so badly, maybe it wouldn’t hurt to be extra clear.

Zuko looks up the second he feels Sokka finally turn the corner, no longer even pretending to pay attention to whatever Toph’s been trying to show him about metalbending. Zuko hasn’t been holding Sokka’s inner flame these days, not without permission, but he’s still been… aware of it, like he would be of any spot of fire in his vicinity and especially after a practice session. And he’s been increasingly unable to focus on anything but the fact that Sokka has been lingering just out of sight far too long for it to be anything but deliberate, the intensity of that not-flame inside him steadily rising.

But now Sokka is finally moving, and it’s toward Zuko, and every line of his body as he comes into view says determination. Zuko’s inner fire jumps in anticipation even as his heart pounds hard, once, with something more like nerves as he tries to understand the expression of pure resolve and intent on Sokka’s face. There’s a bundle in his arms—a sword? Is there danger? Toph is still relaxed, but they aren’t *that* far from the Fire Nation, it’s not that difficult to guess where the Avatar might flee to from Caldera. Do they need to—

“Wannahelpmepolishmysword.”

Zuko blinks, trying to parse the rush of words. “…What?”

Sokka takes a deep breath, eyes doggedly fixed on Zuko’s face as he sets his shoulders before annunciating, “Do you want to help me polish my sword?”

Zuko…still doesn’t understand. Is this…this can’t be a euphemism. Can it? In front of the others? Zuko glances toward Toph and Aang, but Toph just looks vaguely like she’s despairing, and Aang is giving him a big-eyed, eager stare which is…basically how Aang’s been looking at him for days now, so that’s not really that helpful. “I…you want me to… polish your sword?”

Sokka shifts on his feet. “…Yes?”

“Like…a chore?”

“No! No, no,” Sokka hastily says, nearly fumbling the weapon as he waves his hands through the air. “Not—we could…do it together? You don’t have to though, it’s just an idea, you can say no.”

Zuko…*can* say no. Is he supposed to, then? Is this some kind of test? Sokka loves caring for his weapons, Zuko knows that. Zuko knows that Sokka knows that he knows that. Agni, Sokka gives such careful attention to his boomerang that his skin was—is—always smelling faintly of metal and polishing oil, to the point that Zuko can’t smell either without feeling a bolt of heat in his gut. Why would Sokka need *help*?

“Do you want me to,” Zuko finally asks, frowning up at Sokka.

“I—wait, what?” Sokka’s tense expression starts to edge with confusion, and they stare at each other for a long moment, Sokka finally breaking eye contact to cast a slightly pleading expression toward Aang that Zuko…also doesn’t understand.

“Do you not remember how?” Zuko asks carefully, eyeing the tired circles under Sokka’s eyes. Zuko knows the way exhaustion can drag at your thoughts. Sokka’s been asleep every day when Zuko comes down after dawn, but he was awake that night…Maybe he’s not sleeping well? “It’s not that different, between boomerangs and swords. And my dao and your blade should be basically the same…”

“Yeah,” Sokka mutters, scowling down at his bundle. “Sure. Right.” He glowers at Aang, fast enough that Zuko isn’t certain he didn’t imagine it. “I remember now.”

Zuko hesitates, barely tugging back the urge to reach out with his heat sense to test Sokka’s inner flame more closely. “Are you okay? Did you—did you get hit in the head?” Fuck, Zuko’s had enough concussions to know they’re nothing to mess around with, especially if Sokka’s already displaying signs of memory loss. “Did you fall? Where’s Katara? Do you know…” Shit, what can he even ask? Zuko himself barely even knows what day it is, and they eat basically the same thing every night so asking about dinner is out…

“Forget it,” Sokka sighs, pressing a hand to his temples. “I’m fine, Zuko, just…never mind. Forget I asked.”

Zuko scowls, not entirely willing to brush this off and entirely unsure of what just happened. He glances toward Toph and Aang, but Aang has his head in his hands, not looking, and Toph is shaking her head and leaning over to mutter something to Aang that sounds like…’hopeless’?

Zuko turns back to Sokka, who’s still standing, sword in his arms with what Zuko can now pick out as a polishing cloth and oil. Fuck, should Zuko have…invited him to join them on the ground? Because now Sokka’s eyeing the nearest hallway like he’s going to make a run for it, and Zuko barely even thinks before blurting out the first thing that comes to mind that might make him stay. “What’s it made of?”

“Huh?” Blue eyes swing back to him, Sokka’s face going momentarily open in question.

“Your sword,” Zuko clarifies, his eyes catching on the peek of dark metal through the cloth wrapping. “It looks—it didn’t look like a typical alloy? I was wondering if you know what it’s made of?”

“Oh,” Sokka says, breaking so suddenly into a wide grin that Zuko’s inner flame unwinds in surprise, then flips over in pleasure. “Yeah, I—yeah.” He unwraps the blade with quick movements and only hesitates a moment before settling down next to Zuko. Not *right* next to him, of course—but there’s no one between them, and Zuko could reach over and touch without even leaning, and if Sokka turns toward Zuko and Zuko turns toward Sokka then it could be almost like it’s just the two of them. “It's metal from space.”

Zuko takes a moment to get himself back on track. “Really?” That…must have cost a pretty penny, because Zuko’s nearly positive Sokka didn’t steal it. Did the Avatar find himself a wealthy benefactor at some point? In Ba Sing Se? Zuko has a hard time imagining Sokka taking it off some fallen soldier, but then, the dead have no use for the trappings of the living.

“Yeah,” Sokka says excitedly, grinning down at the blade and Zuko will just...keep these thoughts to himself. “Want to—“ He offers it out, both hands extended, and Zuko’s reaching before his mind even has time to consult with his body. For a brief moment, they’re both touching the blade, hands barely separated, Zuko’s fingers sliding over the faint warmth lingering from Sokka’s skin, both of them pausing to take in the sight of their fingers against the dark metal, Zuko staring at his pale his hand looks next to the dark tan of Sokka’s skin.

Then Sokka slowly pulls his hands back and Zuko clears his throat, ducking his head and pulling the sword into his lap and ignoring the loops curls of his inner flame. He can still see, out of the corner of his eye, that Sokka is watching his reaction closely, fingers fidgeting against his wrist wraps. It…matters to Sokka, then, what Zuko thinks. A realization that makes warmth bloom all through Zuko’s chest before he sets that aside to put all his focus toward the sword in his hands.

The metal is dark, as well-cared-for as Zuko would expect of any weapon of Sokka’s. He first takes it in as a weapon, testing the edge against his thumb, cataloging the leather-wrapped grip sized for two-handed use. The pommel is simple but weighty to balance the blade, with enough body around the guard to catch a sliding blade but not so much to protrude more than an inch on either side beyond the wielder’s grip.

It’s a good weapon. Not to Zuko’s particular style but not one he would be unhappy to use. And as he takes it in as a piece of craftsmanship next, Zuko realizes he would have fewer and fewer protests about using it. There’s a fine fit between the hilt and blade, clean lines, a simple artistry to it all. The folds in the metal are barely visible against the dark ore, and the metal itself…

“Do you mind?” Zuko asks, barely glancing up as he angles the blade toward the light and lets fire flicker briefly over his fingertips.

“Please,” Sokka murmurs, voice just on the edge of something Zuko would struggle not to react to if they were actually in private. Zuko exhales a careful breath, running a single fire-wrapped finger along the blade, watching the way the flame moves against the metal, reaching to feel the way the heat melts off the blade. But what heat does catch against the metal holds, low but steady. Interesting.

Zuko plays some heat into the blade, seeing how long it takes to sink heat to the core of the weapon at different points in the blade, how much effort it takes to push the metal to too-hot-for-a-nonbender-to-touch temperatures. The blade stays dark throughout, stays strong as the heat draws toward its center even once Zuko stops pushing it, like it’s kindled now at the heart of the metal. Interesting. Zuko tries to tug the heat away, a little sound of surprise escaping him when it’s harder to bleed off than it was to push in.

“What are you doing?” Aang asks, breaking Zuko out of his focus. “It feels like you’re firebending, kind of, but…”

“You’re doing that thing where you make the metal feel less…metal-y,” Toph adds.

“Oh, I’m just…testing it out.” He checks in with Sokka, but Sokka doesn’t seem to mind that Zuko’s messing with his sword, watching with open curiosity and interest, hand-half extended like he wants to test the intensity of the heat, too, but knows better. Zuko…knows that look. “It’s a good blade,” Zuko offers, quickly bleeding off the last of the intense heat and glancing up between his lashes to add, “It suits your style better than the boomer-dao.”

“Hey now,” Sokka smiles, and Zuko bites back a grin at the sight of it. “The boomer-dao is the weapon of the future. Blades coming at you from the front and the back.”

Zuko lets his grin break free at the memory—Sokka had truly committed himself to unpredictability that day—before looking back to the weapon in his hands. “It’s a good blade,” he murmurs again, tracing the pommel and then flipping the sword to look for the maker’s mark. “Do you know who made it?”

“Yeah,” Sokka says, and Zuko glances up when nothing follows to see Sokka looking strangely uncertain. “Do…do you know Piandao?”

Zuko blinks. “You could afford a Piandao blade?” A *custom* Piandao blade, like the kind that his students have to earn? Agni’s tits, what did they do to get the money for that, scam an entire town out of its treasury?

Sokka tugs on his wolf tail, looking suddenly shy, the weapon still in Zuko’s lap apparently becoming abruptly fascinating. At least Zuko assumes it’s the weapon. “I, uh, trained with him. For a bit.”

Zuko’s inner fire stills, words drying up. “*When*,” he finally gets out, mentally scrambling.

“On our way to Caldera?”

“…You—you just *stopped*? To do some training?” Agni’s balls, it took Zuko *months* to get accepted. After *years* of petitioning, and he’s still pretty sure it only happened because his mother somehow got involved on his behalf.

“We stopped for a lot of things, actually,” Sokka says, looking vaguely sheepish.

“What—how—?”

“When you’re already blowing up some factories and freeing villagers trapped in prison mines,” Toph philosophizes, which—what? “What’s a little stop to become a sword Master while you’re at it?”

Zuko freezes. He feels it happen, knows Sokka is going to notice. Fuck, he can see Sokka *already* noticing and going tenser and tenser in growing confusion, but Zuko still can’t seem to relax. “You’re a Master,” he finally manages to get out, voice shockingly even.

“I mean, that feels premature,” Sokka says, words coming out slow like he knows he’s stepping on delicate ground but isn’t sure just how hazardous it is. “I only—”

“If the man called you a Master then he called you a Master, Sokka,” Toph jumps in.

“Don’t see yourself short,” Aang tacks on. “You earned that!”

Zuko suddenly feels like he can’t breathe against the band wrapped around his ribs. “How long did you train with him?”

“…A few days,” Sokka admits, tone suddenly cautious in a way that would make Zuko scream if he wasn’t already choking back the desire to set something on fire from the realization that, other than *Teo* and fucking *Haru*, Zuko is the only one here over the age of *ten* who isn’t a Master.

“You became a Master Swordsman in a few days?” Zuko rasps out, hating the sudden waver in his voice.

“I mean—it was kind of ceremonial—?”

“No,” Zuko says, sharp and abrupt, feeling like his limbs are half-numb as he shoves to his feet, the sword sliding from his lap to the cobblestones with a bell-clear ring that sets Zuko’s scarred ear buzzing. “Piandao doesn’t—he doesn’t do ceremony unless he wants to. He doesn’t *train* anyone unless he wants to. He called you a Master?”

“Yeah,” Sokka confirms, reluctant.

“Then—congratulations,” Zuko says, gasping around the word. “That’s…great. That’s really great.” His words are rushed, jagged, making a lie of his good wishes and fuck, Zuko needs to get out of here. “I—I need to—check on Appa,” he mutters, already striding as fast as he can without openly running, both ears buzzing now and shoulders tight.

Agni’s tits, is *everyone* around Zuko a prodigy? And if everyone is, at what point is it maybe less about everyone else being spectacular and more about Zuko being so far below standard that even average looks amazing in comparison? Agni, it hurts to consider. And that it took him this long to actually think about…maybe Azula was right. Maybe at the end of the day, Zuko really is just too inept for his own good, for all he wants to do.

“…Your advice sucks,” Sokka mutters into the sudden silence ringing in the wake of Zuko’s departure, his entire body still paralyzed with the sensation of watching a cabbage cart go off the track and being unable to do anything about it.

“I don’t think it was the advice, Snoozles,” Toph murmurs, her tone full of rare regret.

Aang bites his lip, not taking his eyes away from the spot they last saw Zuko. “Are you going to—”

“*Yes*, I’m going to,” Sokka snaps, bundling up his sword with jerky, clumsy hands, for once not bothering to wipe off the dust. “I’m not a complete fucking idiot.” Not that his behavior recently really supports that.

&#45;-

Zuko isn’t in the first two places Sokka looks, and after taking a moment to consider, he eventually finds Zuko sitting on the edge of an open ledge, legs dangling out into space. Appa was recently in the room, judging by the disturbed hay and the way Zuko’s hair is still matted and damp on one side.

“You’re making me nervous, sitting like that,” Sokka says, pausing in the doorway to give Zuko a chance to ask him to leave.

Zuko just grunts, shoulders hunching slightly and eyes staying fixed on whatever is below his feet. Sokka gives it another breath before slowly walking over, carefully settling down on the floor a healthy distance from the edge. He tentatively scoots over, peeking into the swirling mist and nope, Sokka will absolutely not be joining Zuko in sitting with a third of his body over that side, thank you very much.

Instead, Sokka tucks himself against the pillar that forms more the idea than the reality of a wall, legs pulled up and forearms resting on his knees, looking at Zuko’s profile. He’s on Zuko’s scarred side, so he can’t see much of his expression beyond the tension around his mouth, but it only takes moments for Zuko to sigh and shift to face Sokka, wrapping his arms around one bent leg, the other still swinging.

Sokka takes a moment to study the protective hug Zuko has around himself, not sure how to meld this more open vulnerability than Zuko generally shows with the fact that all that openness is clearly saying ‘upset.’ “Do you want to talk about it?”

“I’m fine,” Zuko mutters into his knee, eyes downturned, jaw tight, head tilted to give Sokka his scar instead of his expression.

“Because you left pretty suddenly back there,” Sokka says, aiming for neutral, picking his words carefully.

“It’s fine.”

“See, you’re saying that,” Sokka says, stepping carefully around Zuko’s quelling tone. “But you aren’t acting like it's fine.” Zuko looks fully away at that, fixing his eyes out into the open space beside them, and Sokka takes a deep breath. “Did I…did I do something?”

“No,” Zuko sighs, gold flashing back to Sokka before darting away again. “I—it’s not you.”

“…Is it about Piandao?” Sokka thought he understood at least the broad shape of Zuko’s usual sore spots, and he didn’t think sword training was one of them, not like this at least. But then, maybe Piandao decided Zuko's unique needs’ deserved a very different kind of training than Sokka received.

Zuko pulls his knee in tighter. “Sokka, I—I don’t want to talk about this right now. Maybe later. Just. Not now.”

“Okay,” Sokka says after a brief struggle with his worry. “If you change your mind, I’m here. Just let me know.”

Zuko grunts, shoulders fractionally relaxing when Sokka doesn’t push, and Sokka lets out a breath of relief to see it.

“I do want to know,” Sokka adds after a moment, “I’m not just saying that. If you want to tell me, I want to hear it.”

A few heartbeats, but then Zuko nods. His eyes are still fixed down into the mist, but some of Sokka’s tension still unwinds at the acknowledgment, enough for him to start wondering if he should just drop the subject entirely. But he isn’t sure if that might be worse, to let it go when Zuko doesn’t even know there’s another piece to it. That feels too much like withholding.

“Piandao had a message for you,” Sokka finally says, making his own study of the floor in case Zuko wants to just pretend not to have heard him.

Zuko goes still. “…You told him about me?”

“No,” Sokka admits, looking up to see Zuko peeking at him out of the corner of his eye. “He kind of figured it out on his own, I guess.”

Zuko stares a moment, then shakes his head, huffing out a breath and muttering, “He would,” with something that sounds like…nostalgia? Fondness?

Sokka hesitates over that fondness, stuck somewhere between relieved and curious, but forces himself to stay on task. “He gave me a pai sho tile, too,” he says, wincing when Zuko goes abruptly motionless again. “A white lotus.”

“…Of course he did,” Zuko says, closing his eyes and sounding significantly less fine as his knuckles turn white against his knee. “Of course. That’s—that would—Right. Right.” He takes a deep breath, fists uncurling finger by finger. “I…should have expected that.”

Sokka anchors his hands in the fabric of his pants against the urge to reach for Zuko, hating the way he’s stacking up thing after thing for Zuko to be upset about. “Is this..?”

“Sokka, I *really* don’t want to talk about this.”

“Okay,” Sokka says quickly, because he truly doesn’t want to push against the wrong boundary. And maybe because there’s enough in Zuko’s reaction anyway for Sokka to slot at least the bigger pieces together, given what he already knows.

Spirits, fucking Iroh and whatever game he’s playing at.

“…What did he have to say,” Zuko finally asks, audibly reluctant, shoulders stiff and eyes tight when he glances over when Sokka is silent. “Piandao,” Zuko clarifies. “What was his message?”

“He said that the dual dao aren’t meant to be separated,” Sokka says, watching Zuko’s reaction closely and suddenly second-guessing the wisdom of providing what sounds so much to Sokka like second-hand relationship advice. Fuck, what if it seems like Sokka is trying to pressure Zuko into something? Or what if he’s misinterpreting the message and it just makes whatever Zuko’s going through worse.

Except all he gets is a “…Huh,” and a frown, more of a thinking one than the tight twist Zuko breaks out when he’s upset. So…maybe it’s fine?

But Spirits, Sokka’s been carrying these words for weeks and weeks and weeks, turning them over and speculating and wondering and maybe even hoping when he knew he had no reason to. He…really, really would love more than a ‘huh’. “Does that mean something to you?”

“Yeah,” Zuko says, absent.

“…Will you tell me?” Is it about him? Them? But Sokka still doesn’t understand how Piandao would know about that ‘them’ in the first place. Unless Iroh was sending letters from Ba Sing Se, which might be taking all of this speculation too far…Is Iroh still sending them, from wherever he is that isn’t here with Zuko?

Zuko’s eyes flick up, Sokka not entirely sure why he goes still as Zuko studies his face. “Later,” Zuko finally decides, shoulders loosening, and Sokka can live with that. With the idea of a potential later, and the reminder that it isn’t just now or never for uncovering these things about each other.

Sokka settles back against his column as he lets that idea sink in, fingers idly playing with his wrist wraps as he lets the silence settle over them. He should go, maybe, try to end this on a relatively high note, with things feeling a bit more settled and even-keeled between them. But he also hasn’t been truly alone with Zuko since the other night, not outside of chi bending time, and it’s nice to just *be*, with Zuko. Sharing space and skin prickling under Zuko’s eyes and both of them relaxing bit by bit into something close to what they used to have.

Sokka can almost pretend he’s the way he used to be too, like this. Someone who could just enjoy Zuko’s company without feeling the need to silence the quiet, intrusive awareness of all the ways he’s messed up and could mess up again. Someone who could just close his eyes and see the plan unfurling before him, the sequence of choices and actions that would get him where he wants to be. Someone who Zuko could rely on, if that was ever as true as Sokka wants it to have been.

Spirits, he can feel the heat of Zuko so close and warm and gentle, right next to him and somehow feeling impossibly far away.

“Can I ask you something?”

“Always,” Sokka says, blinking his eyes open at the question and straightening slightly as he takes in the way Zuko’s shifted to kind of…hide behind his drawn-up knee?

“Why…” Zuko immediately loses steam like he always seems to do, like he instantly reconsiders the whole thing and needs to work himself back up to it. “The other day. Why did you think I wouldn’t know about my own nightmares?”

Sokka suppresses a wince, trying to gather his thoughts around the memory of Zuko’s face going determinedly blank in a way that said Zuko was *reacting* to the fact that his nightmares were public knowledge. “You just…never act like they bother you.” He frowns down at his hands when Zuko just gives him a confused look, trying to articulate what Sokka can see now has always just been an unshakeable assumption at the back of his mind, one he never actually thought to verify. “You were barely even asleep at all, most of the time, and—they always seemed bad enough that I guess I just…couldn’t see how you could remember them and not show it.”

“I’m just used to them, I guess,” Zuko says, like that’s a simple thing and not quietly heartbreaking.

“Do…” Sokka glances up, waiting to continue until Zuko gives a little nod that questions are okay. “Do you always have them?”

“…Not always,” Zuko says, low, gold eyes flicking up to Sokka’s face before dropping down to the base of his neck, and it takes Sokka a moment to put it together.

…Oh. Not when Sokka is there, he hears, not always at least, and warmth unfurls in Sokka’s chest even as his heart clenches at the idea of Zuko dealing with those nightmares night after night after night. Fuck, Sokka hasn’t been at Zuko’s side far more often than he’s ever been beside him.

“I’m sorry,” Sokka finally says, clearing his throat. He doesn’t know what he could do when they don’t exactly sleep next to each other anymore—when they never actually got to do that all that often in the first place—but…maybe Zuko has ideas.

“There’s nothing to apologize for,” Zuko says after a moment, frowning over the top of his knee.

“There is,” Sokka says, fighting to keep his voice even, torn between letting this squirmy kind of guilt nest in his chest or trying to shove it away. “You don’t—You’re—and I’m not —"

“Sokka,” Zuko cuts in, straightening slightly. “You don’t…You said you needed time, I’m…I heard that.”
