Zuko is partway through organizing his mental to-do list—he has the itching suspicion that there’s something he keeps forgetting and he doesn’t have a lot of time today, not with the extra work added in—when Sokka’s voice sends his half-ordered thoughts right back into a jumble.

“What are you doing?”

Zuko looks up, his arms full of Appa’s brushes and the long banana fern fronds he managed to grab on their way back from their last foraging trip and fashion into a somewhat haphazard but definitely functional broom. “Just some chores.”

Sokka glances around and Zuko automatically follows his gaze, taking in wide-open terrace with Appa out for a flight, empty except for Momo sunning himself in a patch of sunlight. “What chores.”

“Cleaning.” And if Zuko can just figure out what he needs to do in which order, then maybe he can give a more specific answer.

“Cleaning,” Sokka echoes, the word strangely tight in a way that has Zuko’s inner fire snapping to attention.

“…Yes?”

Sokka stares at Zuko, long and assessing, before glancing around again, his eyes narrowing in a way that’s a bit too recently familiar. Agni, Sokka and Katara don’t look that much alike, not really, right up until suddenly they do. “You wouldn’t happen,” Sokka says with what feels like a deceptive calm, “To be cleaning out Appa’s space and getting ready to groom him when he’s back. Would you?”

“Uh—yes?” Zuko supposes it makes sense to start with that part of the list, as much as anything.

Sokka’s mouth flattens. “Right.”

Zuko resists the urge to drum his fingers against the brush clutched to his chest, inner flame burning sullen and low as he weighs Sokka’s tone and expression and words and the fact that Zuko’s barely said anything, and all he’s doing are the chores Katara told him needed doing, so why is Sokka acting so *upset*. “You’re mad.”

Sokka’s eyes snap back, widening as they search Zuko’s face. “Not at you.”

Great. But Sokka still walked in fine and got upset when he found out what Zuko was doing, so obviously it has *something* to do with him. “Why are you mad?”

“It’s nothing you’re doing,” Sokka repeats, turning in another slow circle, his face darkening even further, which just—

“Yeah, you said that,” Zuko says, hearing the sharp edge of his inner flame bleeding into his voice. “That’s not why I’m asking.” He blows out a short breath when Sokka snaps back around in surprise. “Something's going on and I don't know what. You’re mad and I don’t know why.” And Zuko is as equally unwilling to be the unwitting cause of Sokka’s frustration as the object of it.

Sokka blinks, mouth working a moment before he sags a bit, nodding. “Sorry, I—Is Katara asking you to do this?”

Zuko frowns, unsure how that’s relevant. “Yes.”

Sokka's lips press into a flat line before he finally bites out, “She shouldn’t be.”

Zuko hesitates, trying to parse that frustration. Zuko…really doesn’t want to be in the middle of something between Sokka and Katara, not more than he already is. “It’s fine,” Zuko finally says, shrugging. Zuko knows how to work. He doesn’t need to be coddled. He agreed to Katara’s rules.

Except Sokka immediately pushes back, hair swinging as he shakes his head once, vehement. "It isn't."

Zuko tries another way. “It’s part of the rules, Sokka. It’s fine.”

“…The rules.”

“Yeah,” Zuko says, and now it's his turn to stare. Did Sokka fucking forget? “I need to do chores if someone tells me to do something.”

Sokka’s expression moves almost too fast for Zuko to track, comprehension to anger to dawning realization. “You clean after meals and cook, though,” Sokka says, and Zuko… doesn’t understand. Obviously yes. Those are chores that Katara told him to do, that’s how rules *work*. “What else?” Sokka asks, voice tight, clearly struggling for some kind of calm.

Zuko shifts his weight, wondering if he's about to help that calm along or shatter it. “There’s the laundry—”

“I was there for that one,” Sokka interrupts.

“There’s the *laundry*,” Zuko repeats. Does Sokka think laundry just needs to be done once? “Grooming Appa, drying wood for the fire, hauling water for the fountain when it gets low, clearing debris in the training plazas—” Zuko cuts himself off, inner flame flaring sharp in his chest because Sokka’s face is just getting more and more upset. Fuck. Shattering that calm, then. “Sokka, why is this making you mad?”

“Katara’s taking advantage of you,” Sokka says, shoving his hands through his hair, something that looks like *distress* breaking over his face. “You aren’t here to atone or work or your debts or whatever she’s—” He blows out a hard breath, squeezing his eyes shut before snapping them up to catch Zuko’s gaze. “We split chores equally here. “...I’m pretty sure keeping me busy is the point,” Zuko says slowly. Restricting Zuko's free movement, his free time, trying to restrict his freedom to bend and curtail is choices—that seems clear enough for Zuko.

Sokka is staring like he’s been struck, though, and Zuko wavers, concern threading through his inner flame. Fuck, did...did Sokka not realize? He doesn't act naive like that, but then Zuko of all people is aware that the way you see your family isn’t always the way anyone else does.

“I’m pretty sure,” Sokka finally says, words shaky around the edges, “That you have better things to do with your time than everyone else’s chores. Even if all you wanted to do was sit, that would be your right. It’s your time, not hers.”

And it’s not like Zuko hasn’t had time to spend with Sokka, or to be by himself, not like Toph doesn’t seek him out at least once a day. “I want to contribute,” he finally says.

“You already are, though,” Sokka says. “Zuko, if you can waterbend you can do this job in five minutes, that’s why Aang and Katara are the ones who are supposed to do it.”

Zuko sighs, because again, isn't that the point? “But Katara still told me to do it. You want me to just say no? I’m not trying to fight with anyone, Sokka.”

“How about this," Sokka says, jaw tight. "How about I’m telling you to stop doing all this, and anything else. And I’ll take it up with Katara.”

“I’m not sure that’s a good idea,” Zuko says carefully. Agni, he hates to be the one to dump water on Sokka's candle here. “If you get mad at her because of me and she gets mad back, it might not be you she decides to be angry with.” Zuko's actually pretty sure it wouldn’t be Sokka she decides to be angry with. Or not only Sokka, and Zuko doesn’t really want to encourage Katara to start getting creative. Chores aren’t that bad.

“But a person can’t just do whatever they want because they get angry if you tell them no,” Sokka says, sounding sad, and Zuko can’t exactly argue with that. “I don’t want you to be alone in this,” Sokka adds, searchiing Zuko's face. “Can I help you with this? Can I talk to her?”

Zuko glances away, torn between accepting what Sokka so clearly wants to give and all the potential Zuko can see for this to escalate. “Do you really think talking is going to help?”

“…I don’t know,” Sokka admits after a moment, reluctant, “But I don’t think it will just get better by itself.” Sadness flits over his face again, and maybe something close to guilt. “If she’s taking stuff out on you and it's because of me? Zuko, I don’t know how we can just let that go.”

“Fine,” Zuko sighs, trying to ignore the nevous twist of his inner flame. He can’t exactly argue that letting it go until now has seemed to appease her. “Just…let me know how it goes after?” Zuko wants as much advanced warning of whatever he might be dealing with on the other side.

“Of course,” Sokka says, shoulders dropping with relief even as his back straightens with purpose. “You don’t want to be there?”

Zuko snorts. “Absolutely not.” He isn’t interested in any more fighting with little sisters than he already needs to do.

Sokka doesn’t know if acting when upset and frustration and outrage and something far too close to hurt are all tangled up in his stomach like this, but he doesn’t know how he could wait. Fuck, he thought he and Katara talked about this. He thought she *agreed*, and he can’t stop running furiously back through that entire day they spent waiting for Zuko and Aang to come back. Spirits, no matter how distracted Sokka’s been, no matter how little sleep he’s been getting and how impossible it feels some days to shape his thoughts toward anything useful, how could he have missed this?

Stop glaring, stop commenting, stop cork popping—Sokka didn’t think he needed to actually provide her an exhaustive list of all the things he was asking her not to do.

Sokka wants to kick himself almost as much as he wants to yell at Katara, and he grits his teeth because he knows he can’t do either of them right now. He can’t get stuck in self-recrimination and guilt, can't give voice to the instinctive protest that jumps into his throat at the idea of Katara turning her anger at Sokka onto Zuko because fuck, isn’t that exactly what she’s been doing this whole time? Without him even noticing?

How did he not think to press on what Katara was doing when Sokka wasn’t around? How did he take her 'nothing' at face value when he asked what else she was doing? No matter how tangled and sluggish his thoughts lately, he should have remembered how she is when she has her sights set on some percevied injustice. He shuld have remembered that 'nothing' in the moment isn't a promise of 'nothing' in the future. She said herself that she doesn’t trust Zuko, doesn’t believe him, thinks he’s lying, and Sokka what—took her grudging request that he not fall back into old habits as some kind of concession?

Spirits, Sokka was supposed to be trying to make things better for Zuko here. And he is painfully aware that he can't go back and fix what's already happened, but Sokka can sure as shit fix at least this one thing right fucking now.

“Katara,” Sokka calls the minute he spots her, clenching and then forcefully relaxing his fists as his voice bounces back to him off the walls, just as sharp and loud as he feels. Calm. He needs to be calm.

She immediately looks up from where she’s rubbing waterproofing wax into her boots, startlement transitioning to a worried frown as she takes in the expression on his face. “What’s going on? Are you okay?”

“We need to talk,” he says, taking purposefully deep breaths. Spirits, his anger feels bright and clean, the surest kind of purpose he’s felt since the invasion first started to fall apart around him. He wants to hold onto this surety as long as it lasts but fuck, he doesn’t think he can afford to let this out.

“What about?” Katara asks, worry twisting in confusion as she gives him that healer’s once-over of hers and apparently comes up with nothing wrong.

“Take a guess,” Sokka says, trying to force the bite out of his words. Katara will rise to his anger and he desperately needs that to not happen right now. He needs her to actually *listen.*

“I don’t know, the food stores?”

“Try again,” he says, wondering if this can actually be so insignificant to her that she doesn’t know exactly why he’s here. Or Spirits, maybe she just assumed he would never find out, which makes his stomach give a sickening lurch, because *would* he have? Would Zuko have ever said anything?

“Sokka, just tell me what's going on,” Katara says, exasperated. “And will you sit? Is this really all necessary?”

“Great question, Katara,” Sokka says, beginning to pace because the restless tangle in his chest won't let him be still right now. And maybe because he’s feeling contrary. “*Is* this all necessary?”

Katara’s frowns, her body language shifting toward wariness. “I have no idea what you’re talking about.”

“Don’t you?” Does she genuinely not know? Sokka doesn’t know if that makes it better or worse. Fuck, there better not be more going onthan this. “Why are you punishing Zuko?” “I’m not,” Katara immediately huffs, grabbing her boots back up again like that’s going to be the end of it.

“Aren’t you?” Sokka presses, shifting to stare at her face. Is there any world where she could truly not realize what she’s doing?

She rolls her eyes, scowling up at him. “Just because *you* want to coddle him, or treat him like a little prince in his tower—”

“You have him doing your chores,” Sokka cuts in, incredulous. “And Aang's chores, and Toph's chores. Is he doing Haru and Teo’s too? The Duke’s? Do they even know?” He shoves his hands through his hair. “Did you think I wouldn’t find out if you didn't give him any of mine? Or that I wouldn’t care?”

“I don’t know what he told you is going on, but—”

“Zuko didn’t tell me anything, Katara,” Sokka says, frustration biting at his chest. “I had to practically drag it out of him.” Because Zuko thought Sokka wouldn’t help? Because Zuko didn’t think it was worth mentioning? Both possibilities set nausea churning in Sokka’s stomach. “So why don’t you just lay out what your problem actually is here and cut the ostrich horse shit.”

She stiffens. “*I’m* the one who needs to cut the ostrich horse shit?”

“Who else?” Sokka asks, throwing out his hands. “You can’t have it both ways, Katara. You can’t say you accept Zuko into the group and then act like he’s some servant, or some—some *enemy* you’re trying to drive away with all your conditions and *rules.* Trying to tell him he can’t bend? That he has to do what everyone says and can’t go anywhere on his own? Are you *trying* to make him walk away?”

“No!”

“Then what, it’s just a happy accident if it turns out that way?” He asks, staring at her in disbelief when she just sets her jaw, his anger sparking. “Now you have another thing to blame Zuko for, Aang doesn’t have a firebending teacher and it’s Zuko’s fault? You don’t get to play both sides of this, Katara,” Sokka snaps, shoving the heels of his hands against his eyes and trying to modulate his tone because anger isn't going to help, it isn't, even if it would feel really good right now. "I’m not saying you have to like him—” Spirits, the idea that Katara might never soften toward Zuko is like a kick to the chest. “—but you can’t say you’ll try and then not make the effort. You can’t. And if you can’t live with your own rules then maybe you should have fucking thought of that before you laid them down in the first place.”

“You can’t expect me to be all friendly, Sokka,” Katara flings out, tossing her hair. “All—*best* *buds* like Aang and Toph.” The words are more than a little bitter, and Sokka thinks they’re both remembering how long it took Toph to warm up to Katara, how much time Katara and Aang used to spend together, side-by-side on Appa’s back.

“You don’t have to be friends, but you need to stop treating Zuko differently.” Sokka throws up a hand against the protest he can see on her face. “You told him that he needs to do what people say in order to stay, Katara. He thinks that if he says no, you’re going to make him leave.” Which just…Spirits, Sokka doesn’t know if it’s a good thing or a bad thing that everyone else is apparently too young to have thought *that* through. “Was that on purpose?” The idea of it makes him feel oddly desperate and thin around the edges. “Did you set it up like that from the start?”

“No! I—no! I didn’t,” she insists, shock bleeding into her wounded expression, the words sound truthful enough but it’s hard for him to believe that she didn’t see the advantages real fast of that particular rule in combination with Zuko’s ability to fit himself into whatever a situation requires of him.

“Katara, just—what’s the issue,” Sokka finally asks, feeling exhausted. “Can we just…get the real thing out in the open? I’m not saying we’re going to fix it or get over it or whatever, but can you just tell me what’s going on? So I can stop guessing what’s in your head?”

For a second he doesn't think she's going to respond, then the words suddenly burst out of her all in a rush. “Everyone’s just acting like the past doesn’t matter! Aang is friends with him like Zuko never tried to hunt him down, and Toph can’t spend enough time with him, and you —and he hurt us! All of us! And the mission, and our chances at ending the war, and that doesn’t just go away because now he wants it to!”

“Katara, that's not about you, though,” Sokka says. Aang and Toph and Sokka and ‘us.’ “If other people forgive him for things, why do you still get to hold it against him?”

“It’s not okay to hurt people just because someone says they’re fine being hurt,” Katara snaps, arms crossed tight.

“And it’s not okay to decide you get to replace someone else’s decision with your own,” Sokka shoves back. “Spirits, Katara, what did he even do to you? Pick up Mom’s necklace when you lost it and then give it back to you when he realized what it was?”

“He betrayed us! Me! You!”

“Except he didn’t,” Sokka says, trying to swallow back his frustration. “He’s never betrayed me—” Spirits, there’d need to be heaps more explicit promises than Sokka and Zuko ever exchanged for anything approaching a betrayal. “—and I don’t see how he’s betrayed you.” He searches her face, wondering if he’s misunderstanding. “Is this about Ba Sing Se again?”

“What do you mean ‘*again,'*" she glowers, clearly ready for a fight, and Sokka can only sigh, scrubbing his hands over his face.

“Katara, if this is about Zuko going back to the Fire Nation then I don’t know what to tell you,” Sokka finally says. “You’re upset about something that didn’t happen.”

“You don’t know what happened, Sokka,” she spits, fists tightening against her arms.

“And you don’t know what happened with Zuko either,” he reminds her. And unlike apparently her, Sokka doesn’t need a minute-by-minute accounting of Zuko’s every waking moment to know that regardless of the choices Zuko made in that cavern, he was never out to hurt them. “Have you ever even tried to see it from his side?”

Her expression is all the answer he needs. “He doesn’t see mine,” she muttres, belligerent.

Sokka isn’t so sure that’s true in the way Katara means it. He doesn’t think Zuko fully sees Katara’s perspective, but he thinks she would be at least a little horrified by the image Zuko's formed of her. “Have you ever even tried to talk to him? Actually talk to him? He can’t get to know you if you never give him a chance.”

Katara snorts. “He doesn’t want to talk to me.”

“Gee,” Sokka says, giving her a flat look. “I wonder why that is.” She flushes, glancing away with a scowl. “Are you going to hold that against him, too? That he doesn’t react exactly how you wanted him to?”

“I don’t *want* him to react any way at all!”

That is so blatantly not true that Sokka doesn’t even know how to begin tackling that. “Look,” he finally says, forcing his voice to be level. “Do you believe that people can change? Not just Zuko,” he adds. “Just…people.”

“…Yes,” Katara finally acknowledges, grudging.

“And that they can earn forgiveness?”

“Yes.” Her glare is sharp. “But they need to stop doing the thing they’re asking forgiveness for in order to get it.”

“Katara,” Sokka sighs, “I still don’t understand what you think Zuko is doing. You think what —that he’s betrayed us before and is going to again? That he used to want to capture Aang for the Fire Nation and that making him a better firebender is just some really long way to lure him into a trap? That he’s going to hurt someone?”

“Think?” Katara stares, incredulous. “I don’t *think*. If it were so easy then none of them would be here in the first place because the invasion would never have failed.

“Katara, blame Zuko for what he needs to be blamed for,” Sokka finally says, making his words firm. “For the stuff he’s done. But don’t do it for me. If I forgive Zuko then I don’t want you holding onto something just because you think I shouldn’t have let it go.”

She eyes him, scowling. “*Have* you forgiven him?”

“That’s between me and him,” Sokka says quietly, unwilling to let Katara across that boundary into the fragile thing growing again between him and Zuko if she's going to treat it like this. He doesn’t need her any more tangled in what Sokka is and isn’t thinking or feeling when it comes to Zuko, not when she seems to only take the parts she wants to focus on to shield her own upset.

“Maybe I’m a little more objective than you are,” Katara says, words short and tight with frustration.

…Yeah. Maybe not. “You don’t have all the details,” Sokka reminds her. “And you never will. Some things are always going to be just between me and him, just like some things between you and anyone you date aren’t going to involve me.”

Katara slowly closes her mouth, hesitation entering her expression for the first time.

Zuko skids down a short, grassy incline, half his attention split between trying to remember whether the plant life around them is edible or likely to kill them, the other half on listening to Sokka rambling about piping systems and plumbing and the probability and difficulties of clay versus stone construction. Which doesn’t leave Zuko any attention left for keeping track of their surroundings, or watching for sudden pitfalls and hazards, but hopefully Sokka has at least a quarter of his focus on that.

“—if Toph can bend for the *absence* of earth, instead of the earth itself. Does that make sense?”

Zuko hums, nodding. It does, actually, on some intuitive, instinctive level. Zuko doesn’t know what it says that apparently, he can pick up earthbending theory faster than firebending.

“So if we can follow the negative space in the earth…” Sokka trails off, brow furrowing as he considers the specifics of bending with the intent of *not* finding an element, and Zuko jumps into the brief silence.

“That shouldn’t kill us,” he says, squatting down to take a closer look at the low, lush-looking cluster of leaves. “Well, the roots at least. I have no idea about the greenery.”

Sokka steps closer to give the plant in question a closer look, his feet coming into Zuko’s periphery. “That’s real reassuring, buddy.”

Zuko shrugs, unbothered. “I’m not an herbalist.”

Zuko can hear Sokka’s raised eyebrows in the quality of his silence without even needing to look, but Zuko glances up anyway to take advantage of the sight of Sokka like this, amused and sarcastic and surrounded by nature. “You sure you know enough for this foraging expedition?”

Zuko raises his own eyebrow back. “How about, I’ve eaten this—” he gives the leaves a flick. “—and I’m still fine.”

“Yeah you are,” Sokka says, salacious and automatic and freezing halfway through a once-over, eyes popping wide as he suddenly seems to register his own words.

Zuko just rolls his eyes, though, feeling a smile tug at his scar as he watches Sokka beat back an embarrassed, flustered blush, his inner fire flipping at such open evidence of his ability to effect Sokka, at the physical proof to go along with Sokka’s words from the other day about wanting.

Sokka has been a mix of earnestness and clumsy uncertainty ever since they spoke by that pool in the forest, a combination of apparently simultaneous nervousness over being close and longing to be near that…hasn’t been the clearest for Zuko to try to parse through, or the easiest to figure out against the other things Sokka had written and said. But now that Zuko that the wanting underneath it all has never been in doubt, or what Sokka ultimately hopes to do with it—well, it would have been good to know earlier, but Zuko can appreciate now the way he can slot Sokka’s behavior against those words and feel the way his own footing becomes more sure as they fit together.

And Zuko can feel the shift in Sokka, too, the way his brow is creased over the past few days with thought just as much as uncertainty in the wave of their conversation. The difference between fumbling efforts to hold back abdhalting attempts to feel a way forward.

Maybe this whole open sharing thing is starting to work a little better, too.

Zuko certainly doesn’t have much to complain about when it comes to its results, at the moment. Sokka had pulled him aside before morning firebending even started, intent on asking what Zuko wanted to do with his day and so clearly determined to make it happen that Zuko momentarily hadn’t known what to say. His inner fire is still turning little flips over the fact that when Zuko had gathered himself enough to suggest foraging—and not just Zuko looking for plants and herbs to supplement their supplies, but that Sokka should come, too— Sokka had so immediately leaped at the idea that Zuko barely even finished Aang’s lesson before Sokka was there with snacks, carrying bags, a full inventory of their supplies, notes on everyone’s favorite flavors, and a rudimentary map of the grounds above the Temples so they could mark where to find things next time.

It was a level of determined thoughtfulness that Zuko had found nearly overwhelming until his inner fire had spun out, curling and twining around itself and sending Zuko jolting back into motion again.

“Anyway,” Sokka clears his throat, pulling Zuko’s attention away from his inner flame as he makes a production of crouching down next to Zuko, looking suddenly deeply fascinated by the plants. Zuko resists the urge to fluster him more. “Is there any particular way to harvest these?”

“Nah, just—yank them out.” Zuko hopes, at least. He only ever ate them, or hazily watched Ensign Teruko prepare them from a half-feverish nest of blankets. But no one seemed to be doing anything fancy, and the roots never looked any particular way coming out of the gather bags.

Sokka takes him at his word, yanking one of the clusters of leaves right out of the ground and brandishing the resulting dangling-root-and-leaf-top for Zuko’s inspection. It looks…close enough to what Zuko remembers. And Zuko could see on Sokka’s inventory that their dried supplies are running low enough—and he knows that Katara is enough of a healer—that close enough doesn’t seem too risky.

They work side by side, their bags slowly filling with knotted, thick roots. The dirt on Zuko’s hands reminds him of laboring through the Earth Kingdom, or the charcoal that used to stain his fingers in the teashop until Zuko ran out of charcoal sticks for the week and got demoted to register duty. A short-lived effort on the part of the owner, before he realized that Zuko could do a lot more damage making change with an attitude than taking orders with one.

Zuko is vaguely surprised that for once, thoughts of the teashop feel more nostalgic than frustrating or bitter. Maybe because Sokka is a warm presence at his side, occasionally pausing in his work to muse about angles and flow rates, his familiar chatter and quiet thoughtfulness tempering Zuko’s memories with a constant reminder of the good parts of Ba Sing Se. Or maybe just because Zuko can believe that he’s doing what he’s supposed to be doing now, standing on his own path when before he had nothing but Sokka to cling to.

“Alright,” Zuko finally says, sitting back before they pick this patch over too much to recover. “Let’s check out a spot along the northern ridge. Engineer Pima always said that was the best spot for cooking stuff.”

“So,” Sokka says in his thinking voice as he picks his way across the ground beside Zuko, both of them half-on a game trail that winds through the trees. “Did you always travel with a full engineering team?”

“It’s a standard part of any naval crew.” Zuko cuts him a wry look. “Fire Nation ships can’t exactly catch the wind.”

Sokka snorts, ducking under a branch. “No, definitely not. Did you ever learn?”

…To catch the wind? “Learn what?”

“Engineering.”

Zuko makes a face before he can stop himself, startling a burst of laughter out of Sokka. “No,” he grumbles. “Only the standard training.”

“Oh?” Sokka’s tone is excited, curious, and Zuko pauses, giving him a surprised look. Fire Nation ships *are* full of pipes, which seems to be the current subject of Sokka’s interest. He supposes there aren’t exactly the libraries around for Sokka’s dive into Earth Kingdom poetry to still be sustaining itself.

“It’s basically how to not blow up the ship,” Zuko finally offers with a shrug, “Nothing fancy. Any firebender enlisted in any branch of the military gets it, even the ones who can barely light a candle.” Zuko glances back as he hauls himself up a particularly steep spot to see Sokka looking blank. Or maybe staring at his ass. Zuko…is fine with that. “Can’t have someone getting upset and blowing out the engine with a flare-up.”

“Does that happen?” Sokka asks once he’s scrambled up after Zuko and Zuko’s done his own round of staring at the flex and shift of muscles across Sokka’s arms and shoulders.

“Never,” Zuko says, dry. “All military firebenders adhere perfectly to their training. That’s what makes them a valuable and treasured asset to the nation.”

“Look at you, telling a joke. Good job, buddy,” Sokka grins, laughing when Zuko gives him a playful shove just hard enough to rock Sokka’s balance, just long enough for Zuko’s hand to tingle from the fire curling beneath his skin. “So things blow up all the time, then?” Sokka asks, coming up alongside him again.

Zuko shakes his head at Sokka’s open excitement at the thought, biting back his own smile. “Let’s just say there’s a reason there’s a full engineering crew on every ship. Certain commanders are notorious for it.” It used to infuriate Zuko that Zhao always got upgraded to the latest models after wrecking the engines beyond repair on each and every ship he was given.

“That could be useful,” Sokka muses half to himself, and Zuko just shrugs. Unless the Northern Water Tribe gets involved, he doesn’t know how much naval secrets are going to matter in the next few months. Less than three to go…Zuko can’t not be aware of the time they have left, of just how much and how little it is.

“Here,” Zuko says as they finally crest the ridge, immediately spotting the delicate leaves he was looking for. “This is fire basil. We can eat this. The leaves and stems add a mild spice.”

Sokka pauses. “Mild?”

“Mild,” Zuko confirms. “Just be careful with touching your face, the fresh juices burn for a few hours if they get in your eyes.”

“…Are we sure we have the same definition of mild?”

Zuko gives him a quick grin. “Not at all.” Sokka and Toph are comfortable enough with spice when Zuko’s found ways to add it into his turns to cook, but Zuko’s still the one eating most of what’s available. It almost makes it so he doesn’t mind Katara’s tendency to eye any food Zuko’s handled with open suspicion. More spice for Zuko, to go along with the constant heat of her glaring.

…Zuko might be feeling an Azula-worthy edge of anticipation at the idea of adding these to the flavoring rotation. The leaves *will* get milder as they air out and cook down. They will.

They’re just very good raw, too.

They settle in to harvest, Zuko aware of and oddly content with how carefully Sokka is watching the way Zuko tackles stripping the leaves and cutting the stems at the base, keeping his fingers far from where his knife is working.

“I wouldn’t mind having an engineer around now,” Sokka says absently after a while, slightly wistful. His tone is mostly distracted, that rambling into the silence that Sokka does when he’s truly relaxed, when anything that drifts to the front of his mind comes right out.

“For the pipes?” Zuko asks, glancing up and quickly moving to gently redirect Sokka’s hand before he can itch at his eyes.

Sokka pulls a face at his just-slightly-sticky hands before saying with pure longing, “For the *baths*.”

Zuko breaths out a surprised laugh. “You can figure that out yourself,” Zuko says, giving Sokka a quick, maybe-not-exactly-platonic once over. Sokka had never been particularly fastidious in Ba Sing Se, but he also didn’t have a problem with the fact that certain activities made a person sweat. But once Sokka encountered hot baths? In tubs big enough to immerse his whole body in?

Zuko is absolutely sure that Sokka has the motivation to crack this problem on his own.

But Sokka is shaking his head, frowning, that atypical uncertainty that’s been clinging at his edges bubbling into his voice. “I’ve never done plumbing before,” Sokka hedges, fiddling with his knife. “And I have no idea how the Air Nomads would’ve done it.”

“Similar enough to the Fire Nation,” Zuko says after a beat, setting aside that tone, that hesitancy, until Zuko is entirely sure what exactly it is he wants to ask about it. “It’s where we got it from.” Zuko glances up into Sokka’s surprised silence. Oh. This…wouldn’t be common knowledge. “The Air Nomads figured it out a few centuries ago, but they weren’t exactly builders. The Fire Nation made it more scalable.” At least according to Zuko’s engineering corps, if they could be believed. But Zuko tended to trust the things they said when they didn’t realize he was listening more than he trusted the things they said when they could see him. And they were all on the *Wani* for a reason, after all, none of which had to do with the quality of their work.

“…Huh,” Sokka finally says, sitting back on his heels and wiping his hands absently against his pants. “So the same basic designs?”

Zuko tucks his knife away and carefully wipes his hands in the grass, considering. “Pretty much.” Engineer Arai in particular had complained frequently and at volume the minute she got a bit of paint stripper in her about the lack of meaningful innovation the Fire Nation had produced in the realm of basic infrastructure when so many resources were given to weapons development.

“Come on,” Zuko says, rising to his feet and then giving Sokka a gentle nudge with his boot when Sokka just keeps staring absently into space. “Let’s check out the slope.”

They set out back through the forest, Zuko’s inner fire lazy and looping to have Sokka just behind his shoulder again, or at his side where the space allows. The sunlight is warm, the thin air quieter off the face of the gorge, and Zuko’s ears are filled with the pleasant sound of the forest and Sokka muttering to himself about strategic localized tremors and precision earthbending. Even with part of Zuko’s mind constantly counting down the days left to Sozin’s Comet, Zuko knows he wouldn’t trade this time for anything, this opportunity with Sokka to just be, to act for a moment like they’re two normal people enjoying each other’s company with nothing else to worry about but that.

“So when are you doing it?” Zuko finally asks when Sokka’s rambling trail of thought starts to circle back on itself again.

“…What?”

“The whole plan you’ve been talking about.” Zuko glances up from where he’s kneeling to examine whether the underside of a particular plant has white-ribbed leaves or not. If the ribs are white…then it’s probably alright? Or maybe the other way around… “When are you doing it?”

“Oh.” Sokka freezes a little, rubbing at the back of his neck, glancing away with… discomfort? It’s hard to see his face from this angle when he twists like that, but Zuko is pretty sure it’s discomfort. “No, I—I’m good. I wouldn’t want to waste everyone’s time for that.”

Zuko pauses, trying to sort through Sokka’s sudden unease. “I’m pretty sure everyone would appreciate the baths being up and running again,” he finally points out. Bucket baths only get a person so clean, and not everyone wants to make a trek to the topside rivers to rinse off, particularly when the winds are high.

“People are training,” Sokka demurs. “That’s important.”

“People aren’t training all the time,” Zuko says carefully, sitting back on his heels and setting aside his knife to give Sokka his full attention. It feels dumb to say when clearly that’s the case. He and Sokka are here after all. And even if it wasn’t the case, Sokka is important too. His time is important, just like he told Zuko the other day.

Zuko…doesn’t like that Sokka might not think that.

“It’s fine,” Sokka says, waving away Zuko’s concern. “It’s just an idea.”

“It’s a good one,” Zuko frowns. There it is again, that uncertainty in Sokka’s voice. Zuko *really* doesn’t like it, not when Sokka’s always been so happy to offer up even his most half-baked thoughts. “I mean, I’m not as smart as you are, not with this kind of stuff,” Zuko says, trying to understand the hesitance in Sokka’s posture. “But it seemed like it would work.”

“I don’t know…” Sokka’s fingers worry at the edge of his wrist wrap, which Zuko hates to see when Sokka’s talking about plans and ideas and taking something apart to put it back together again. Those are Sokka’s *things*.

“Why not try?” Zuko asks, eyes fixed on Sokka’s restless fingers. “What’s the worst that happens? The pipes work less? They already don’t do anything.”

“We could misjudge the earthbending and destroy a key aspect of the stabilizing or supporting infrastructure and drop the entire Temple off the mountain.”

“…We could,” Zuko allows, blinking. That’s the kind of disaster-oriented thinking that Zuko’s usually the one to engage in. “But if fighting an imperial assassin didn’t do that, I think we’re probably in the clear.” Sokka still looks unconvinced, though. “Bring Toph,” Zuko adds. “She can fix anything Haru messes up.”

“There’s just no need to take the risk,” Sokka says, even as his face seems caught on the edge of wistfulness.

“It’s your choice,” Zuko finally says, bending back toward the plant that he’s almost entirely sure they can safely eat. Maybe they can test a little first. “But I think a hot bath would be pretty great.”

Only silence greets his words, but after a moment Sokka drops down next to him to fill his own gather bag. And it’s not a bad silence, more a hard-thinking one that Zuko is happy to be part of even if he feels like he doesn’t wholly understand what exactly about this is tripping Sokka up so much. But regardless, Zuko’s quietly pleased that every time he peeks over, he sees the bit of tentative consideration on Sokka’s face growing larger and larger.
