It’s one of those chilly, foggy, wet, awful mornings that seems all too common in the Western Air Temple until the sun rises high enough to burn the moisture in the thin air away, which takes far too long when you’re living inside a canyon.

“It’s spring!” Aang had exclaimed when Sokka complained about it. “What do you expect?”

“…Walls?” Sokka had said, incredulous.

All Sokka wants in life right now is a cup of hot anything to drink and some warm breakfast in his belly. Instead, he’s huddling across from Katara, look at the soggy, very much not-burning kindling they have to deal with. There must have been rain last night that blew through the nonexistent walls and found their woodpile, which is the kind of thing you need to worry about when there are *no* *walls*.

“Do you need help,” Sokka mutters, pausing in his food prep to take another peek at her nonexistent progress.

“I’ve got it,” Katara grumbles back.

“Because I can help,” he points out as another flash comes off her spark rock with no curl of smoke to herald a flame.

“I’ve got it,” Katara snaps, stopping to give him a glare.

“Because once in a blizzard I—”

“*I’ve got it!”* Aang snuffles in his sleep and Sokka and Katara promptly shut up, both sending the bundle of blankets a guilty look. They both like to let everyone sleep as long as they can before the food is ready to eat. Cuts down on the complaining.

“Fine,” Sokka sighs, going back to his side of the nonexistent fire. He gets his pot of tea ready to brew, the food they have ready to cook, and then all there’s left to do is watch Katara not make progress and flex his fingers to try to work out the chill.

It will be better once the day gets going, and Sokka knows that he’s certainly experienced worse cold than this, but fuck, the Southern Water Tribe at least has the sense to keep the wind out. And Spirits, to not hide away from the sun. That’s the worst part of it, without a fire—the lack of sunlight to add a single scrap of heat to the air.

Katara’s muttering curses under her breath, spark rocks distinctly not sparking, when Sokka catches movement over his shoulder. He glances back to see Zuko soundlessly picking his way through the sleeping bodies, looking around himself in confusion.

“Why is no one else awake,” Zuko asks, voice raspy and quiet as he gets close enough.

“Cause it's early,” Sokka grumbles, eyeing the way Zuko somehow manages to move without making any noise. Sokka can’t seem to figure out the trick of it…is it more to do with the way he places his feet and less to do with how his weight shifts? Maybe. Spirits, it’s too early by far.

Zuko flicks a glance up toward where the sun is presumably hidden by clouds and stone. “Everyone’s usually up by now.”

“Yeah, well, there’s usually breakfast by now,” Sokka says, then immediately winces because he didn’t mean that to be a jab at Katara, but—

“You know what, Sokka? Fine. I’ll ask for help.” Sokka has his hands halfway extended to take the spark rocks when she suddenly turns to Zuko with a tight scowl instead. “Zuko.” Zuko flinches in surprise, and Sokka is trying to marshal his wits to intercede when she continues, “Will you light this fire for me?”

Zuko blinks, staring long enough that Sokka thinks maybe his sleep-slow mind conjured this whole interaction up until his firebender finally goes, “…Sure?” And with a glance and a flick of his hand, the campfire roars cheerily to life, sudden enough that Sokka jerks before he can help himself, nearly falling.

Katara smiles at Sokka with saccharine sweetness as Sokka regains his seat, and it’s too early to resist the urge to stick his tongue out at her in return. Rude.

“…Are you guys okay?”

“Moon peachy,” Katara says in a distinctly not moon peachy way.

“Just great,” Sokka agrees before offering his teapot for Zuko’s startled hands. “This is supposed to be tea.”

Zuko takes the pot after a beat, bemused. “What kind?”

“Green.”

Zuko gives him a patient look. “What kind?”

“…I don’t know.”

“Didn’t you spend like, half of each week in a teashop for months,” Katara mutters, eyeing Sokka like he’s a special kind of idiot, which Sokka doesn’t appreciate because it’s *early*, he’s *allowed* to be an idiot before breakfast.

“We weren’t *in* the teashop, Katara,” Sokka grumbles back, making sure his tone conveys that it should be obvious, because it’s wet and cold and early and windy and fuck, Sokka is feeling cranky. Dammit.

“The tea leaves are already in the water,” Zuko observes, at random as far as Sokka can tell even though his face is expectant when Sokka looks over.

Sokka wracks his brain, but can’t come up with any idea of what Zuko expects. “…Yes?”

Zuko sighs, muttering something under his breath that Sokka misses as the wind kicks up, which is awful and terrible, but Sokka shoves that aside because Zuko is cupping the teapot in his hands, eyes falling half-closed, and it’s only a few breaths before the pot is giving off gentle steam.

“Here.” Zuko carefully passes the teapot back over, Sokka staring a second at Zuko’s hand casually on the metal base of the pot before he grabs the lacquered wooden handle.

“It’s not boiling?” Sokka half-asks, half-observes as he peeks beneath the lid. He might not know tea, but…the water is supposed to be boiling, right?

“You don’t even know what kind of tea it is, Sokka,” Katara huffs. “Don’t act like you know how to make it.”

“You don’t know either,” Sokka grumbles, resisting the urge to clutch the pot to his chest because he’s at least awake enough to know that would hurt.

“I mean…” Zuko flicks his eyes between the siblings. “It *is* green.”

Sokka eyes Zuko over the rim of his mug. “You’re taking a side in this?” He asks, taking a sip and immediately burning his tongue.

“Ah,” Zuko says, glancing from Sokka to where Katara is…giving Zuko a meaningful look as she tends the nice fire Zuko started for her, where she’s about to cook his breakfast. “Yes.”

“...Fair enough,” Sokka sighs, hunching over his cup and trying to focus on being at least a little bit warm, unable to stop eyeing the way Zuko is fidgeting and scowling over his shoulder.

“What?” Sokka finally asks, because he can’t zone out and wait for breakfast with the way Zuko pulls his attention, and he can’t enjoy having his attention on Zuko when Zuko is so visibly out of sorts.

Zuko blinks. “What, what?”

“What’s got you all pissy?”

“…I’m not pissy.”

Katara chokes and Zuko whips his head toward her, eyeing her for a moment before fixing his narrow-eyed look on Sokka. Sokka just shrugs. “Prickly,” he suggests instead.

Zuko stares. “Sokka,” Zuko finally says, sweeping him with a look that has Sokka’s straightening. “You have not *seen* me be prickly.”

Sokka opens his mouth and then promptly closes it again while Katara makes another sound of amusement, wondering what exactly he *has* seen, then, and deciding to just set that aside for later when Zuko looks over his shoulder again.

“People are usually awake by this time,” Zuko finally offers as some kind of explanation when he twists back around to see Sokka looking.

“It’s a good day to sleep in,” Sokka shrugs.

“*You’re* awake.”

“Regrettably.”

“Katara is awake.”

“Someone has to feed this lot,” she says, as if she didn’t fight tooth and nail to keep her primacy over breakfast and they all don’t know it, the little deceiver.

“I’m awake,” Zuko grumbles.

“You don’t sleep,” Sokka points out.

“That’s not the point.”

Sokka raises an eyebrow at Zuko’s not-prickliness, taking a sip of his cool-enough-to-drink now tea and humming in contentment as warmth fills his chest. “Then what is?”

“We’re supposed to be training by now.” Zuko glowers over his shoulder again. At Aang’s sleeping, completely immobile form, Sokka realizes. “Firebenders wake with the sun.”

“So?”

“*So*,” Zuko huffs. “Do you think waterbending training is going to be cut short if we get a late start firebending?”

“Don’t bet on it,” Katara mutters, under her breath but loud enough to be heard.

“So,” Zuko says, back to scowling at Aang. “We don’t have time for extended lie-ins.”

“Well, why don’t you go wake him up then?” Katara says, giving them an exasperated look when they both startle at her sudden full-volume suggestion. “Unless you’re trying to do it by just talking about it.”

Zuko blinks. “What?”

“Give him a good kick,” Katara suggests, which seems perfectly reasonable to Sokka, but Zuko is gaping at her so Sokka adds, “Not too hard.” He shrugs when Zuko’s horrified look gets transferred to him. “Just enough to make your point known.”

“I can’t—I can’t *kick the Avatar.*”

“Pretty sure you’ve done that before,” Sokka points out. He’s pretty sure Zuko and Aang have thrown each other off buildings.

“Not when he was sleeping!”

Katara makes a thinking noise, remarkably devoid of hostility all things considered as she measures salt from their dwindling stash into the cookpot.

“Okay well—” Zuko is eyeing Katara like he’s never seen her before. “I’m not supposed to do that anymore!”

Sokka hums, because while that *is* true, “I’m pretty sure kicking Aang isn’t the same as kicking the Avatar.”

Zuko stares. “It’s *exactly* the same*.”*

“I don’t know, feels different to me.”

Zuko gapes. “Sokka. It’s *exactly the same.*”

“Well,” Sokka shrugs, because Zuko can think that if he wants. “Then I guess you better find it in your heart to interrupt the Avatar’s beauty sleep.”

Zuko snaps his mouth shut at that, swallowing back in his words in favor of casting increasingly suspicious glances between Katara and Sokka. “Why are you in a mood,” Zuko finally asks, giving Sokka a wary look.

“I’m not.”

Katara immediately breaks into a fit of coughing that sounds remarkably like laughter.

“It’s cold,” Sokka huffs, turning pointedly to Zuko and refusing to dignify her with a response.

Zuko stares, incredulous, eyes darting to Sokka’s wolf tail and Water Tribe blue tunic and wrist wraps and the boomerang on his hip and *okay,* Sokka *gets it*.

“It’s *windy*,” Sokka grouses, hunching his shoulders. “There aren’t any *walls*.”

Zuko opens and then closes his mouth, looking at Sokka like he just said something stupid, and it’s *early,* Sokka’s *allowed* to say stupid things this early. It takes a man time to wake up! “…Do you want to be warm?” Zuko finally asks.

Katara lets out another very eloquent snort as Sokka rolls his eyes. “*Yes*, I want to be—” Sokka nearly bites his tongue as he’s suddenly enveloped in a gentle heat, warmth washing and curling around his body and chasing the chill from his skin, his muscles, his bones. By the set of Katara’s shoulders, she’s feeling it too, but he can’t imagine she’s feeling it like this, the way it wraps around him like it wants to cling, like it’s missed him, like there isn’t anything it would do but settle against his skin.

“Oh,” Sokka says dumbly, breathier than he intends. Then, as his heart rate settles a bit and his brain starts screaming out that this is *Zuko* and *heat* and *good*, “That’s mean.”

Zuko hums, something that might be a smirk just curling the edge of his lips. “I asked.”

“That’s still…” What? Still too close to what Sokka wakes up in the middle of the night aching for? Still too close to exactly what Zuko knows he likes?

Zuko raises his eyebrow. “I can stop.”

“No!” Sokka yelps as the warmth suddenly disappears, lunging toward Zuko like he can physically catch that heat and ignoring Katara’s annoyed huff as he nearly sloshes the remains of his tea into the fire.

“Oh, it’s *warm* over here,” Toph suddenly says from behind them, sleepy and mussed and snuggling right up to Zuko’s side as she drops between them with a boneless, careless flop. Zuko jumps in surprise but doesn’t flinch away, and she somehow manages to shoot Sokka a self-satisfied smirk as he pulls up short, like she knows she just took Sokka’s favorite spot, the one he was going for, and that he’s mad about it.

Wait. No. What. He’s—fuck. It’s too early for this.

“Welcome to the land of the living,” Sokka finally mutters, sitting back in his original seat and flustered with himself, hearing the way it comes out more bratty than sarcastic. Dammit.

Toph ignores the comment with the contentment of someone who knows they’ve won, but Zuko gives Sokka a mild look. “I’m going to go kick the Avatar,” he finally says. “You should eat something.”

“Well I would if there were anything to—” Sokka clamps his mouth shut, nearly dropping his empty mug to catch the cloth-wrapped packet Zuko pulls out of fucking nowhere to suddenly throw at him. “What—?”

“Have a snack.”

Sokka gives him an incredulous look. “Is this half a flatbread from two nights ago?”

Zuko shrugs. “They keep well.”

“Am I not *right* here, making breakfast *right* now?” Katara mutters, glaring at the surprisingly not-as-stale-as-he-expected flatbread that Sokka’s already stuffing into his mouth.

“Sokka gets pissy when he’s hungry,” Zuko says serenely before wandering off to nudge Aang awake, very gently and from a very judicious distance. Sokka gapes after him, flushing as Katara makes a sound that’s suspiciously laughter-like.

*Sokka’s* not the pissy one. He’s just—aware that it's early! *Zuko* is the one…gently coaxing Aang out of his bedroll.

…Fuck.

Sokka shoves another bite into his mouth, keeping his chin imperiously in the air and admitting only to himself that he feels better minute by minute with a full stomach and Zuko’s warmth wrapping back around his shoulders.

&#45;-

“It just needs a delicate touch,” Sokka reminds them all, trying to shut off the spiral of disaster scenarios flickering through his mind at the idea of anyone getting a little too not-delicate. “We aren’t trying to take the place down—” A hard glance to Toph because he trusts she’ll feel the intent behind the look even if she can’t see it. “—just seeing if we can tell if there are any blockages.”

“I still think we should just take the wall down,” Toph says, proving his point.

“But you always think that,” Katara says.

“And we don’t need to because you showed Haru and Aang how to tell if there’s empty space in stone,” Sokka says with a whole lot of emphasis. “Right?” *Right*? That’s what she *said* she was going to do when he asked. Fuck, what if she didn’t, what if he misread her response and —

“Right!” Aang confirms, bouncing on his toes with excitement.

“Right,” Haru echoes, looking distinctly more nervous about it, but, well—Sokka supposes he understands that. Haru’s bending lessons with Toph seem to consist largely of her commenting on how terrible his prior teachers were as she lobs boulders at him from new and interesting directions.

“And we all have our charcoal, right?” Zuko had obligingly made some that morning with a shrug and no questions about why Sokka needed so much of it, and now Sokka’s gratified to see everyone digging out their piece. Okay, so far so good. “Great. So pair up, and we mark the walls where the pipes are, and—”

“And you’ve told us this five times already!” The Duke throws his arms up. “Let’s go already!”

“What The Duke means,” Teo says with a smile because now Sokka is going back over how many times he’s told them and wondering if it was five or six, and maybe he should say it again just to make sure. “Is that we’ve got this. Right?”

There are nods all around, and then all eyes are back on him. Sokka stares back, wondering what he’s missing, and after a long moment, Sokka realizes that they’re waiting for his signal. Oh, that’s—oh. “Alright, well—get started then?”

The others immediately begin to disperse around the meditation room that sits above the bathing chamber and Sokka lets out a puff of…he doesn’t really know if he wants to admit that it’s relief, but it definitely is. Spirits, he’s a mess. The earthbenders put their hands to the stone walls, Toph’s voice quiet as she directs them—

“No, like *this*, not *that*. *Feel* it, don’t try to *pull* it.”

—and before long they’re branching out, each following what Sokka hopes are the hollow spaces where water used to flow. Theoretically, those hollow spaces should lead from the baths back toward the surface, and somewhere on that path Sokka’s hoping there will be some kind of blockage that they can tackle, or at the very least that they’ll find the source of the Temple’s water to unclog or redirect. All assuming of course that the Temple wasn’t just built with random gaps in the walls. Or that nothing has fallen or crumbled within them. And that Sokka understands the form the pipes would even take as a single hollow space…

Conceptually it’s all as neat and tidy as Sokka can make it, and watching Katara and Aang branch off, then Teo and Toph, then Haru and The Duke, he can’t help but be chest-tight nervous over the whole thing. Intellectually he knows that none of this actually matters, it’s just an afternoon’s diversion, the kind of side-quest the others love as a break from the serious work of training. It’s just a stupid little thing and Sokka’s reacting like he’s giving another presentation to the assembled Water Tribe navy and all their allies before the invasion again, or—

Zuko’s quiet, husky voice cuts right through the noise in his brain. “You’re overthinking it.”

Sokka glances back to see Zuko leaning against the doorway of the meditation room. He hadn’t inserted himself into the plan the way that the others had once they realized there was a plan to insert themselves into, seeming entirely content to observe. Which Sokka knows hasn’t always been the case when it comes to Zuko, but his shoulders are loose when Sokka checks, his face relaxed, Momo exploring the collar of his tunic and Zuko letting him, so maybe Zuko actually is fine, for once. Assuming Sokka can trust himself to correctly interpret everything he’s seeing, which…Zuko said he would let Sokka know if he was wrong.

“You don’t know what I’m thinking,” Sokka belatedly challenges.

Zuko gives him a half-amused, half-exasperated look, one of the ones that softens the tight lines of his scar, one of the ones Zuko seems to save for when the others aren’t around. “You’re freaking out about how nervous you are.”

“…Shut up.”

Zuko’s grin is quick enough that Sokka would miss it if he weren’t already looking. “It’s a good plan.”

“I *know* that,” Sokka says, even though he doesn’t, actually, and it feels like seeing water in the desert to hear Zuko say it. Fuck, he’s a mess.

Zuko hums like he knows exactly what’s going on in Sokka’s head, his gold eyes steady as he studies Sokka’s face, absently redirecting Momo when the lemur starts getting a little too interested in his hair. “You want to join the search party?”

Sokka feels kind of ill at the thought of just waiting and desperately hoping that he’s right and not being able to do anything but watch, actually.

“Or we could do something to take your mind off it.”

Sokka yanks his mind out of the gutter so hard it hurts. “…Like what?”

“We could practice chi bending.”

Sokka immediately starts to reconsider whether he wants to follow after Aang and Katara around the Temple and listen to their stilted not-flirting. The idea of needing to keep his shit together right now with that emptiness opening up in his chest…Spirits, after last time all Sokka wanted was to plaster himself against every inch of Zuko and feel Zuko’s weight bearing him down and grounding him and…talk about a mixed message.

“Or sword training,” Zuko adds, sounding more than a little knowing. Sokka’s eyes fly up, feeling a stab of guilt and not even entirely sure why he’s feeling it, his face flushing as he sees Zuko looking…yup, that’s knowing.

“I…”

Zuko raises his eyebrow. “You?”

“…Would love to train with some sword,” Sokka says, clearing his throat and caught somewhere between delighted and thrown that Zuko is teasing like this, because this is definitely teasing, he’s been doing it too much for it to be an accident.

“I’m sure,” Zuko murmurs, voice pitched some on the edge of something inappropriate, eyes fucking *laughing*, and yup—definitely not an accident.

&#45;-

They’re pleasantly sweaty and tired and more than a little horny—Zuko is, at least, and his inner fire is curling in a distinctly self-satisfied way because he recognizes the particular half-lidded glint in Sokka’s eyes even if Sokka is pretending it isn’t there—when a shout from inside the Temple rings out. An excited shout.

Zuko and Sokka share a quick look, then Sokka is setting down his space sword with as much haste as he can bring himself to treat the weapon and running toward the noise. Zuko sets down his own blades, pulling up a quick mental map of where the excitement seems to be coming from and what side of the Temple they’re on and—

“Not that way,” Zuko says, tugging Sokka’s arm to redirect him down a side hallway instead.

“Why,” Sokka asks, following along as Zuko skips over the mostly-intact floor.

“Airbenders,” Zuko tosses over his shoulder. “Not a lot of stairs.” Which Zuko doesn’t even want to think about how Haru and the Duke and Teo have been dealing with in their exploring. They’ve been running around with a notable absence of rope.

They start to hear voices as they climb up to the second level and Zuko lets Sokka pull ahead again as they follow the sound of shouting and excited exclamations and voices talking on top of each other until they finally burst into what seems to be some kind of office. The furniture has been pushed neatly against the wall and Haru is grinning while The Duke jumps in place.

“Guys! Guys! We found it!”

“We found something,” Haru corrects.

“It!”

“What are you feeling?” Sokka asks, tone barely below The Duke’s in eagerness. “What do you feel? Or sense or whatever?”

Zuko steps back, finding a good spot out of the way against the wall that lets him drink in Sokka’s excitement and the animation in every line of his body. It’s like Sokka’s worries drop away as his plan snaps into place around like, almost like a daydream come to life to see. Zuko likes Sokka like this, engaged and with his mind working and hands flying through the air as he talks, nothing but pure enthusiasm. It’s how Zuko always imagined Sokka would be in those rare moments in Ba Sing Se when Zuko allowed himself to think beyond the moment he was in, or in those brief snatches in Caldera when Zuko let himself consider the other paths out there that he couldn’t take.

Experiencing it live is even better than he imagined it would be, sweeter than any daydream for the fact that Zuko is actually here, actually living it.

Zuko stays tucked to the side as the rest of the crew pours in, drawn by the noise and the loud urgency. Their collective excitement adds a nearly tangible buzz to the room and Zuko can feel his own pulse beginning to pick up through pure proximity, his inner fire humming behind his ribs.

“I can feel where the hollowness stops, and it gets kind of…fuzzy?” Haru is saying. “I tried a little vibration, but I didn’t feel anything moving.” He glances at Toph who immediately steps forward, her demeanor matter-of-fact and focused.

“Show me,” she frowns, placing a hand against the wall, and Haru does, eyes closed in concentration. She grunts after a moment of what looks like nothing to Zuko, nodding, and Zuko wonders not for the first time what she feels—what she senses—like that. “Decent.”

Haru grins, because that’s high praise for her. “Should I go harder?”

“No,” Aang says, anxious. His hand is also against the wall now. “The wall’s thinner here.”

“I wouldn’t shake harder if we don’t want to be putting things back together after,” Toph agrees.

Aang frowns at the stone. “It feels like…something’s pressing down?”

“Water,” Katara suddenly says. “It’s muffled, but—” she runs her fingers lightly over the stone toward the ceiling, rising up onto her toes. “It feels like water’s in there.” She looks toward Aang who reaches up to imitate her, his face tight with concentration before breaking into a sudden grin.

“Okay,” Sokka says, and something that might be pride pulses briefly through Zuko’s inner flame at the way everyone immediately gives him their attention. “So the pipe is probably blocked here, and the water is pressing down on whatever it is. What if the water wasn’t there? Would you be able to shake the block loose then?”

Toph makes a thinking noise in the back of her throat as Haru eyes the wall, both of them giving a shrug. “Probably?”

“No promises,” Toph says, the determined cracking of her knuckles belying her words.

“Katara, can you—”

“Not for long,” Katara says, expression distant as she presses harder against the wall. “It’s heavy.” Zuko shifts, once, locking down the uncomfortable fidgetiness he feels at her having access to water he can’t even see. He’s still wary of the way she seems to be suppressing her usual hostility over the past few days, doesn't entirely believe that it's gone and not just hidden, and it’s weird to see her interacting and being just…normal with the rest of the crew, not on edge or suspicious or finding excuses to glare. It’s like she doesn’t even realize Zuko is there.

He…isn’t quite sure if that’s a good development or not.

“So timing is going to be important, guys,” Sokka emphasizes, glancing at his benders. “Aang, can you help Katara—?”

“On it,” Aang says, shifting to her side and face settling with focus.

“Okay, so Katara and Aang, you lift. And when they give the signal, Toph and Haru, *gently*, do your thing.”

It’s going to work. Zuko knows it’s going to work in a way he can’t articulate, in a way that has something to do with the sheer amount of bending power in the room right now, but mostly has to do with the fact that its Sokka and Zuko can’t imagine how Sokka wouldn’t be able to figure out anything he sets himself to.

There’s a grunt as Katara and Aang do something none of them can see, then Katara gives a tight nod and the earthbenders are slapping their hands to the wall. For a breath there’s nothing, then a slight shiver of dust rains down. Sokka immediately steps back to eye the joist running across the ceiling, The Duke jumping up and down next to him—Zuko isn’t sure whether it’s to help or because he’s excited for a potential structural collapse—and Aang letting out a nervous *eep* before Katara yanks his attention back to their task.

“Alright,” Toph says after an interminable few heartbeats, stepping back. “Let the water—” A muffled, rumbling, rushing kind of noise cuts her off, a sound that has Zuko’s shoulders automatically loosening because it means that the engine is fixed, that the desalinator is running again, that the *Wani* won’t need money it doesn’t have, that the pipes—

“Yes!” Katara whoops.

“It worked?” Sokka asks, face caught between hope and uncertainty.

“It’s flowing!” Aang shouts.

“It worked?” Sokka repeats, then again, half-laughing with so much of what sounds like relief and disbelief that Zuko just wants to—well, he just wants to kiss him, but that’s something Zuko wants all the time.

“Let’s go see!” Teo calls, already wheeling himself toward the door.

There’s a mad tumble as the seven of them plus Momo all try to dash out the single doorway at the same time. Zuko is scrambling back from the mess—is Aang briefly *upside down* wedged between Haru and the wall? How even—when Sokka, bringing up the rear, reaches out without even looking to grab his hand and pull him along.

Zuko stumbles more than a few steps before his body catches up and falls into an almost-run just behind Sokka. His brain is no use in the effort, too busy tripping over and around the fact that Sokka’s fingers are twined with his, and Sokka initiated it, and Sokka’s skin is as cool as ever, and the calluses are still familiar, and—

Sokka shoots Zuko a wild kind of grin over his shoulder as they turn a corner, immediately tugging him down a set of railing-less stairs that feel dangerously narrow for how many people are currently trying to use them, and Zuko’s heart is pounding and his adrenaline is spiking and he can’t help but grin back. Everyone is so happy, all of them trembling on the edge of accomplishment and hauling Zuko along with them just as surely as Sokka’s grip around his hand, and his inner fire is bright and sparking and bursting to throw itself in loops around Sokka, to dance on top of Zuko’s skin and through the air, to shine out his sudden joy.

Zuko and Sokka trip into the bathing chambers a few steps behind everyone else, and they’re here and Sokka’s still holding his hand, still keeping Zuko close and pulling him along into the cluster of chattering voices when Zuko might normally hover with his back comfortably to a wall. But Zuko doesn’t want to let go of Sokka’s hand, and with Sokka on his left, he finds that he doesn’t really care what is or isn’t at his back, not if caring means needing to pull away.

“It’s working,” Aang breathes, awed, and Zuko manages to drag his eyes off Sokka enough to see that it is.

The water is a disgustingly brown trickle, seeping in barely visible fits and starts from openings across the elaborate sculpture. But it’s a trickle that’s rapidly becoming stronger, becoming clearer, water seeping and then dripping and then flowing down well-worn paths to fall into the grooves along the floor. Soon enough it's pooling, creeping faster and faster through the sinuous channels until with a gurgling, sputtering burst a cluster of twigs and pebbles and Zuko doesn’t want to think about what else spits from one of the faucets.

Clear water in a steadier stream follows, still just from the one spout but it’s only a few heartbeats later that another clears, and as the first fall of muddy water splatters down into the main bath it becomes clear that they did, in fact, do it. It works.

“Fuck me,” Sokka breathes, his fingers tightening around Zuko’s in what Zuko for a wild moment thinks is intent before realizing its excitement. “It actually worked.”

“I told you,” Zuko says, watching happiness slowly taking over the stunned look on Sokka’s face and grinning because he can’t do anything else seeing it up close like this. He gives Sokka’s hand a squeeze back and almost laughs at the delighted surprise that’s winning out over everything else in Sokka’s expression. Agni, Zuko can’t wait for Sokka to get a look at the room when all the water is running clear and strong again, and the whole back wall sparkles like a jewel in the firelight and refracted sunlight. He hopes he’s here to take in the first time Sokka sees it.

“Fuck,” Sokka laughs, running his free hand through his hair. “We just need to clean things up, and—”

There’s a little shiver, and then Toph is bending the dirt out of the water with tight, sharp gestures and Katara is using a tiny whirlpool to gather up the other debris and spit them onto the floor, and in the space of seconds, there are only a few twigs floating in the slowly rising water. With more quickly joining as the other spigots sputter back to life and years of dust and grit flow out, but still. Point made.

“—and wait,” Sokka finishes with another laugh.

“It won’t overflow?” Toph asks, bare foot sliding over the floor, head cocked.

“No, there’s these drains—” Sokka gestures with both hands in his enthusiasm, crouching down to guide Toph’s hand to the inset drains tucked within the ornate scrollwork along the edge of the pool. He has to drop Zuko’s hand to do it, but that’s okay. His touch still tingles across Zuko’s skin, and Sokka finally feels warm and vibrant against his fire sense again, how he should be, how Zuko hasn’t felt him for more than brief snatches of time since Ba Sing Se.

“So…what do we do now?” Aang finally asks.

Sokka pauses, looking around at the various bathing pools all slowly filling, centimeter by centimeter. The very big pools. “We wait?”

&#45;-

It was mutually and near-unanimously decided that no one should spoil the moment by trying out the newly running water from anything except one of the bathing pools to start. They don’t need to be here to watch it fill up—Sokka had reluctantly calculated, at Katara’s insistence, that it would probably take a few hours—but even with everything else there is to do, Sokka is quietly pleased that no one else has been able to bring themselves to leave, either.

Sokka isn’t quite sure why, exactly, it pleases him so much, but he isn’t exactly into interrogating positive feelings like this these days, not when they sometimes seem so hard to come by.

They’re all sitting around the sides of the main pool, barefoot and pants preemptively rolled up, The Duke sitting on his hands to resist touching the little waterfall just within reach if only he stretches out the whole length of his body. The main pool is thankfully filling the fastest despite its size—Sokka had tried to explain the fluid dynamics and flow rates and role of different pipe sizes in contributing velocity, not that anyone had cared to listen. Katara had just shrugged away the physics, and apparently water isn’t Teo’s thing.

Even Zuko had given Sokka that fond ‘I like to hear you talk and have no idea what you’re saying’ expression of his, all the way from his seat across the pool. Sokka is a bit torn about Zuko ending up there, instead of still at Sokka’s side. He likes being able to look at Zuko like this, watching the way he idly swings one bare foot above the water, looking maybe the most relaxed Sokka’s ever seen him around the others. Maybe that’s because of the general collective anticipation, or because Toph is entertaining them all with a play-by-play of her second championship run in the Earth Rumble. Or maybe because Katara hasn’t glared at Zuko once so far that Sokka has caught, lobbing nothing more than a few cautious looks his way.

Or maybe it’s because Sokka can still feel the lingering heat of Zuko along the right side of his body, still finds himself absently flexing his fingers over the sensation of holding Zuko’s hand even though it’s been hours. Maybe Zuko’s holding on to that the same way Sokka is, which…Spirits, at this rate with the way Sokka’s adrenaline is surging and dropping and spiking over every little thing, Sokka might be at risk of passing if Zuko decides to sit next to him at dinner tonight.

But it’s because Sokka is staring, tracking the progress of the water up toward that bare swinging foot while everyone else chatters and swaps stories, that Sokka catches the moment the first bit of water brushes over Zuko’s skin.

Zuko stills, toes flexing, then leans back with a deliberate casualness to rest his weight on both hands. The gesture sits him further back, pulling his foot above the waterline. And also makes a line of his body from thigh to hip to flexed abs underneath the loose drape of his shirt to—

Amused golden eyes catch his and Sokka flushes at being so blatantly caught looking, even though Zuko’s expression is borderline hot and that might be the hint of a smirk tucked around his lips, and shit, maybe Zuko did that on purpose. His eyes are half-lidded as he watches Sokka back, glinting with something like anticipation in the flashes of sun that reflect off the gently rippling water.

Sokka knows he’s the next tallest—barely, over Haru, but Sokka will take it—and excitement coils in his gut as the water creeps higher and higher. It would be cheating to reach down, to stretch out for it. It would ruin the moment of discovery. And there’s something about the waiting with Zuko’s eyes on him, the way he’s watching Sokka’s reaction, making Sokka the object of his complete focus. Sokka feels breathless and excited in the best kind of way, his skin prickling, his heart rate picking up, his—

Sokka shrieks, jerking his feet back up onto the lip of the pool and scrambling back like the water might chase him. “It’s *cold*,” he says, plaintive, borderline an accusation as the others all flinch in surprise. Sokka might come from the South but this is ice cold, bone-cold, better-have-a-fire-ready cold, and his toes are already stinging from it. “*Zuko*.”

Zuko is smirking openly now. “Breath of fire,” he says, reaching back toward the water like it's nothing and paddling his foot a little just to make his point, the asshole.

“Don’t be a baby, Sokka, how bad can it be?” Katara says, rolling her eyes as she braces herself on the edge of the pool, dipping her foot forward and then freezing, sucking in a hard breath before deliberately pulling back. “…That’s cold.”

“Why wouldn’t it be?” Aang frowns, confused. “It’s spring outside still, especially this high up.”

Sokka stares. “Because cold baths are exceedingly unpleasant and if I wanted that I could just go swimming back home?”

Aang doesn’t look any more enlightened. “But it’s supposed to be about being in touch with nature and the elements and the spirits, and how they all come together in the physical self.”

Sokka slowly transfers his horrified stare back down to the water. Does that mean there’s no heating mechanism? No fire they could light somewhere? Fuck, immersing himself in that when he doesn’t have to? To get in touch with the *spirits*? Sokka can feel his balls preemptively trying to climb up into his body in protest.

“So just to get this straight,” Toph says. “Did we just do all that for cold bathwater no one’s going to use except for Twinletoes when he wants to commune with the winter or whatever?”

“Spring,” Aang corrects.

“Here,” Zuko intercedes, eyes still half-lidded again but more shy than smirky now that the others are looking at him “Try now.”

Sokka proceeds with a healthy dose of suspicion, but he cautiously stretches a foot back down, bracing himself, and— “Oh. It’s warm.” And it feels amazing, sweeping the lingering cold from his toes, nearly the perfect temperature. Zuko hums his agreement, the familiar sound grabbing half of Sokka’s attention up from the water to see Zuko studying his reaction before the water kicks up another degree or two.

“Just come get me whenever you want to use it,” Zuko says, words clearly for Sokka. “I can heat it up.” Then he visibly remembers himself, straightening and glancing around at the others, his expression shuttering again. “And, um, anyone else,” he tacks on, rubbing the back of his neck. “And—I’ll teach Aang how to do it too? So…yeah.”

Mercifully the others reach down to touch the now-warm water rather than pursue that little public moment. Except for Toph of course, who leans over under the cover of The Duke shrieking over the difference between the pool water and the water coming in from the channel to say, quiet but blunt, “Snoozles. I don’t even know what Zuko looks like or why it matters to you sighted people, but I know you’re being an idiot for not locking that down.”

“Toph—”

“I’ll give you the advice The Boulder always used to help with people’s relationship problems,” Toph says, as if an absence of advice is Sokka’s issue. “Hop on that before someone else does.”

Sokka chokes. Does she—Spirits, he *really* hopes she doesn’t know what she’s saying.

“He’s not going to be waiting forever for you,” she adds.

Sokka glances away but he can’t deny her words, can’t pretend he doesn’t hear them, that they aren’t true. Sokka knows that Zuko might be loyal and determined to a fault, but he also knows Zuko isn’t someone who’s content to just sit and *wait.* Spirits, even over the past few days now that Zuko seems sure of Sokka’s interest—and fuck does it hurt, to realize that Sokka fumbled that too, that he couldn’t see that something so obvious to him might not be visible to Zuko—Zuko’s clearly starting to do more than just wait for Sokka to get his act together, is clearly trying to prod and pull Sokka along.

If only Sokka could figure out how to get over his nagging, biting fear of messing this up more than he can fix. His need to get this right is so big that sometimes he can barely think through it, and Spirits, he doesn’t *want* to be someone who lets fear hold them back but some days Sokka can’t seem to see anything but the trail strung out behind him of all the things he’s already fucked up.

He just wishes that his mistakes felt fixable, somehow. Approachable. He doesn’t want to spend so long trying to turn himself into someone Zuko can be proud of, someone who Zuko can rely on, that he never reaches across the space between them. But Spirits, no matter how he looks at it Sokka can’t seem to find a way to make this tangle feel anywhere as easy to fix as the Temple’s bath system was.

But maybe that’s where Sokka’s been going wrong from the start. Maybe fixing *himself* isn’t how Sokka fixes anything.

Sokka splashes his feet in warm water that’s up over his ankles now, listening to the others joyful exclamations and watching Zuko relax into the sound instead of tensing against it, thinking that maybe it’s actually about things like this—little broken things set to rights again, the hurts of the past made right in the present even if they aren’t made completely whole. That maybe it’s less about who Sokka is now and more about what he’s done, and what he hasn’t done, and what he could still do to chip away at the mistakes he’s made and pull himself bit by bit closer to being brave enough to take the leap that Sokka so desperately wants to make.

&#45;-

Zuko automatically goes to gather up the dishes and cookware after lunch and nearly drops one of the few non-Toph-created bowls they have left when Katara suddenly goes, “I can help with that.”

Zuko glances around, wary. There’s no one else she could be talking to but him. He thought she left with the others to watch Aang and Haru’s eartbending training, but she must have doubled back, which makes Zuko’s inner fire flare to attention. Heat prickles in his palms as he mentally maps routes out of the plaza, picking out the ones that won’t bring him too close to the walls where he now knows pipes run just behind the rock, carrying her element throughout the Temple. Fuck, can she call it through the stone? He needs to find out.

“…Did you hear me?” Katara frowns, something like frustration flashing across her face. Sometimes she looks so like Sokka and other times she just…doesn’t. “I offered to help with cleanup.”

“Yes…” Zuko slowly confirms. And he isn’t sure if the offer is meant to be friendly or something else. Katara might have stepped back from actively trying to unsettle him, but Zuko is aware she didn’t do that for *him*.

“Well?” Katara demands, crossing her arms, then abruptly uncrossing them, face all annoyance and aggravation, and Zuko eyes her warily and tries not to glower back.

“Sure,” Zuko finally agrees, his inner flame high and alert. He doesn’t see how he can say no, not when that would just leave him wondering what she’s up to. He’d rather have whatever this is out in front of him instead of waiting to be sprung.

“Great,” Katara mutters in a tone that says it clearly isn’t. But she grabs up the cookpot and utensils, leaving Zuko to balance the bowls on his arm as he trails her toward the fountain they use for water.

Katara sets herself to cleanup with brisk efficiency, absently waterbending through the process in a way that makes it clear that this is something that she could do—probably used to do—in about a quarter of the time it takes Zuko. If she were inclined to, of course. Which today, apparently, she is. For no reason that Zuko can understand, a fact that puts him on edge and makes his inner fire burn sharper and sharper until she finally breaks the silence.

“You were holding my brother’s hand.”

Zuko forms a fist without thinking, like he can hold the skin-memory safe. “Yes…”

“Is that a thing you do now?” Her eyes slash up, paler than Sokka’s, more like ice. “Hold hands?”

“Um. You’d have to ask Sokka.” Zuko’s willing to hold a lot more than his hand the second Sokka gives him the go-ahead, not that he’s going to tell Sokka’s little sister that.

Katara scoffs in the back of her throat. “So what, you’re just sitting around waiting for him?”

“I—” Zuko is very confused by this whole thing. “I mean—no? I’m training the Avatar.” As if she doesn’t know that, and Zuko bites off anything else that might come out because he’s not about to talk about all the ways he’s decided to do more than just wait. Sokka’s been careful of Zuko’s privacy when it comes to the rest of the crew and Zuko doesn’t want to give Katara anything Sokka doesn’t mean for her to have.

She huffs out a frustrated noise when he doesn’t say anything else, though. “How about this,” she says, setting down the ladle she’s been cleaning to fix him with an intense stare. “What are your intentions toward my brother?”

Agni’s balls. Just…Agni’s balls. Why does she suddenly care? Why does she suddenly care enough to *ask*, when to Zuko it feels like his intentions are pretty fucking obvious. Shit. Fuck. Zuko carefully sets down the bowl he’s been scouring, taking a deep breath and trying to sort his thoughts into something he’s willing to share with her.

He can tell when the words finally come that they’re too formal, but Zuko doesn’t know what else to fall back on except the mostly-remembered lines and forms and rituals he might have had a chance to use with Mai one day if things had been different for all of them. “I bring the strength of my body, mind, and fire, to—” Not court, they kind of stepped sideways around that. “—the service of one who I admire for his intelligence, devotion, and—” Not purity. Um. “—perseverance. I would share his burdens, so they are made less, and share his triumphs, so they are made greater. I bring—” Zuko stops himself there, because the next part is listing the lands and holdings he has to offer, and the honor of his household, which he can’t exactly do given…everything.

And also because Katara is staring blankly at him. “…What?”

“Uh.”

Her face wrinkles in…something. She isn’t like enough to Sokka for him to figure out what that expression is. “Come up with that yourself?”

Not at all. “It’s…traditional?”

She purses her lips, finger tapping against the ladle still in her hand. “How about you say it in your own thoughts.”

Well fuck. Zuko’s never been any good at any of that. Azula was always free in her opinion that he should keep them to himself. “Okay, um. I can…My intentions are…wholly honorable. I would never bring dishonor to Sokka’s being or name if it were in my power to prevent it.”

“Dishonor,” Katara echoes, and Zuko suppresses a wince because even he can hear how hollow and thin that sounds, against all that’s inside him. “That’s a rather vague concept, isn’t it? It seems like in the Fire Nation you can do a lot of awful things without ever losing your honor.”

Zuko fiddles with the bowl in his hands, hearing the accusation in her words and trying to swallow back his sharp frustration. Does she think she knows his own country better than he does? “I just want him to be happy,” Zuko finally says, reaching for something bare and honest to offer her when part of him just wants to snap that Zuko’s *here*, isn’t he? Not just here, in the Temple—literally right here, enduring this conversation. What else does she need to know about his *intent*?

“More than you can care about your honor?”

“Uh.” Zuko…hadn’t really been thinking of them as mutually exclusive things. And he feels like he just walked into some sort of trap.

“Or do you suddenly not care about that anymore?” Her eyes are bright with challenge. “That’s not—I do still care about my honor.” Zuko wouldn’t have any kind of standing in the Fire Nation if he didn’t, and he can’t give that up. Not yet, at least, not without trying. “It’s just…different. Than before.”

Her gaze is coolly assessing, giving nothing back. “How.”

Zuko tries to flex the prickling, ready heat from his fingers as he searches for the words for something he’s never had to voice before, because who would he voice it to? “There’s honor in behaving with integrity,” he finally says. “And acting for the betterment of yourself and your name and your people. But there’s no honor in this war,” he says over top of the reply he can see forming on her lips. “There never was. And there’s no honor in harming others just to keep power. That’s…that’s not how it’s supposed to be.”

Her words are quick, like a spider cat pouncing. “Is there honor in betraying your nation’s leader and overthrowing him at the side of his enemies?”

Zuko flinches from her stark words, from the naked truth of them, but takes a deep breath and forces himself to meet her eyes. “Sometimes you only have bad options,” he says quietly, feeling his inner flame twisting against that reality. “You still need to make a choice.”

She actually pauses at that, her gaze dropping briefly to her hands. “And where does my brother fall in all these bad choices you have to make?” She finally asks. “How are you going to keep him from getting caught up in all of that?”

Zuko nearly laughs. “I’m not sure that I can. Not if he doesn’t want to stay out of it.” He takes a quick glance up, sighing at her visibly dissatisfied reaction. “I would do everything I could to keep Sokka safe, Katara,” Zuko says quietly, putting every bit of conviction he has into his words. “But I can’t hold him back if he wants to do something.” He hesitates, then risks adding, “Neither of us can.”

Katara looks pained at that, but she thankfully doesn’t push back against the underlying suggestion that they share in common wanting to keep Sokka safe. Or against the harder reality they share of being unable to protect him from dangerous things. Zuko thinks they both know that there isn’t much room to be safe, in war.

Sokka is feeling like a nice awake, warm, well-fed, and functional human this morning when he sidles up to Katara after breakfast, grabbing a spot on the ledge with a nice view of the plaza. He glances at the sewing she has half an eye on, the other half on Aang’s firebending lesson. “Need a hand?”

Her fingers still as she flicks him a quick, suspicious look. After a moment’s consideration, she wordlessly passes over her little bobbin of thread for Sokka to unspool for her. It’s a basic task, one she doesn’t actually need help with. Their mom used to have him do it when Sokka was little and she needed him to sit still.

“You and Zuko looked pretty cozy the other morning,” Sokka says after a while, watching Zuko demonstrating some kind of exercise. “Very warm.”

“Shut up.

“I’m just saying.”

She casts him an annoyed look. “I liked you better when you were shoveling your face with snacks because you get *pissy*.”

Sokka grins. “A man’s gotta eat.”

Katara huffs, exasperated in that amused-despite-herself way before she glances back toward where Aang is moving through some kind of hybrid kata-conditioning workout that honestly looks torturous.

“I don’t think Aang could shout about what he had for breakfast so loudly when he started training,” Sokka muses as Zuko gives a few choice reminders about the importance of developing lung capacity.

She shakes her head in disbelief. “I can’t believe that is what he has Aang saying.”

“Could be worse. Zuko said he used to have to recite the royal lineage until he got it right.”

“Tui and La,” Katara mutters, giving Zuko a half-horrified, half-fascinated look.

“Building breath control?” Sokka hazards. That’s what Zuko had said at least, as opposed to Sokka’s first thought which was ‘imperial propaganda.’

“Aang definitely has more of that now,” Katara says, eyeing the training ground where Aang has run out of food to talk about and moved on to explaining a dream he had last night while a slightly-pained looking Zuko comes at him half-speed, forcing Aang to time his tuck jumps and—

”*No airbending!”*

—and work his muscles.

“He’d have airbending in a fight,” Katara says, a little bit tart but only loud enough for Sokka to hear.

“Sure,” Sokka says easily. “That’s why you let him airbend all the water around, right?” He raises his eyebrows when she glares. “So,” he changes the subject before she actually gets riled. “I see you’re getting some sewing done.”

“Very astute, Sokka.”

He hums in the back of his throat. “Does that mean you don’t think Zuko is waiting for an opportunity to kill Aang anymore?”

Katara glowers down at her mending. “…Probably.”

“You stopped glaring at him so much, so. Figured I’d check.”

Katara mutters something under her breath, then, louder, testy, “He didn’t seem to care.”

“Thank you. For trying.” Because Sokka doesn’t think she’s right. Zuko *does* care, he’s just got good at hiding it. Sokka can make a number of guesses as to why. So Sokka appreciates that Katara is making an actual effort this time to try.

She doesn’t reply for a while, hands steady and even, before finally sighing. “No promises, Sokka.”

Sokka gently bumps her shoulder in acknowledgment, unspooling more thread for her and keeping most of his attention on Zuko as he demonstrates some new kata for Aang. His lips quirk as Zuko tries to find a way of explaining that Aang is supposed to jump, but not *that* high, not without throwing off the timing, which the airbender seems to have a fundamental inability to understand.

It’s good to see that Zuko can criticize the Avatar now without looking like he’s half-bracing himself to do it, and it’s good to see Aang’s progress coming along, too. Sokka hopes Zuko feels good about that, because Sokka can guess at the drive to make things right that would have sent Zuko out of Caldera after them.

Or maybe Sokka is projecting, there. But he feels like he knows more than a bit about needing to make things right, by this point, and about the lengths a person can go to in order to set things back the way they should have been all along, if only they have the conviction— the bravery—to follow through.
