## Chapter 18: Gone Hunting

### Notes

#### Chapter Notes

No particular warnings for this one!

### Text

Sokka looks like shit today. Not that Zuko thinks Sokka could ever truly look bad—he’s still *Sokka*—but today is…maybe not his best day.

He was the last to breakfast, eyes red-rimmed and puffy as he stared at his bowl like the idea of moving his body to eat was something he hadn’t fully wrapped his mind around yet. He was a beat late responding to Toph’s teasing as he blearily wrapped and rewrapped his wrists over and over, somehow managing to end up with uneven, lumpy fabric every time even though Zuko’s seen Sokka wrap his wrists in a heartbeat while focusing on far more complex things than Toph’s good-natured ribbing about earning his nickname this morning. There are chunks straggling out of the underside of his wolf tail that Sokka doesn’t even seem to notice, let alone care to fix, and watching him jerk like a scalded octocat when Haru let out a sudden bark of laughter—like Sokka zoned out so much he forgot where he was—Zuko feels the tendril of worry burrowing in his chest bloom into something much larger.

Zuko knows what it’s like to be exhausted, to have sleeplessness dragging on your limbs and fogging your thoughts and making your eyes gritty. And he knows what it’s like for it the thoughts causing the sleeplessness to be what’s weighing you down, instead. Seeing Sokka barely even react to the day’s firebending lesson ending with a contest of who could do the most elaborate flipping, twisting, flaming kicks? Zuko is sure that Sokka isn’t dealing with just the former.

And watching the almost-so-good-you-can’t-tell-it’s-forced smile he offers Teo on the way to lunch, seeing the way Sokka musters alertness and attention like he can physically claw them into his grip, Zuko is pretty sure Sokka doesn’t want the rest of the crew asking him about it.

Zuko, though? Zuko’s going to fucking ask. Zuko isn’t just ‘the rest of the crew’ to Sokka, no matter what it is they are to each other these days. And if Sokka doesn’t let Zuko run off and brood in isolation? Then Zuko isn’t about to fucking let Sokka be alone with whatever is bothering him, either.

Zuko finally manages to orchestrate a moment after lunch in the little bit of time there's been more and more of, recently—ever since Zuko took ‘it’s okay to kick the Avatar awake’ truly to heart—when Katara and The Duke are still cleaning up and everyone else isn’t quite ready to begin their afternoon yet. Teo digs out the teapot, looking hopeful, and Zuko obligingly sorts through their remaining leaves for the best ones as he absently brings the water up to temperature, making a mental note for their next foraging expedition to find something that boils decently well fresh.

He’s quick to grab two mugs when the tea is done, slipping away as the rest of the crew crowds around for their share to make his way over to where Sokka is nominally looking over their cook knives to see if any need sharpening. Zuko's pretty sure that's just an excuse to maybe literally doze off sitting up, because Sokka’s hands haven’t exactly moved in a while.

“Here,” Zuko murmurs when he gets close enough to see that Sokka’s eyes are, in fact, open, pitching his voice low so that Sokka stirs rather than startles.

Sokka blinks, automatically straightening and then relaxing a bit when he registers who it is, shifting to make room for Zuko to settle down next to him and accepting the offered tea with a quiet thanks. He eyes the second mug Zuko is idly turning between his hands, forearms resting on his upraised knees, and then visibly summons a bit of teasing. “Drinking tea?”

“Absolutely not,” Zuko says easily, watching the quick smile that curves Sokka’s lips before it disappears behind his cup. “I figured you might want another.”

“Thanks,” Sokka says again, shooting Zuko a shyly pleased look that has his inner fire burning with a distinctly smug edge. “I think I might need that.”

“Yeah,” Zuko says, glancing significantly toward the half-up, half-down mess of Sokka’s wolf tail. “I could tell.”

“Am I that obvious?” Sokka laughs, pulling a face as he reaches up and realizes just how little of his hair is actually tied back.

Zuko shrugs, his inner fire giving a pleased curl despite his worry to see Sokka’s rueful amusement. He can feel his scar pulling into a little smile in response, a feeling that’s slowly becoming less and less notable, more and more normal. Which Zuko...hasn't really thought about. He thinks Uncle might have liked to see it.

Sokka’s humor fades far too quickly for Zuko’s liking, though, and Zuko can see that furrow coming right back between his brows, the fidgety tension creeping back into his hands. Zuko might normally be content to sit in the quiet, to let Sokka choose to fill the space between them with words. But watching Sokka open and close his mouth over and over, hearing him taking breaths like he’s about to start speaking and then nothing coming out, Zuko thinks Sokka might need more than just Zuko’s lingering presence to give him a push.

“Something’s bothering you,” Zuko finally observes as Sokka finishes his tea, offering the second mug along with the words.

“Yeah,” Sokka sighs, flashing Zuko a grateful, wan little smile. “I…yeah.”

“Want to talk about it?”

“Yeah,” Sokka says, frowning down at his new mug. “It feels dumb, though.”

Zuko just hums a quiet encouragement, watching Sokka search for words. He doesn’t know if anything that clearly bothers someone this much can qualify as dumb.

“I had a bad dream,” Sokka finally says, face twisting like that’s an understatement, “And I just…I can’t seem to shake it.” He flicks Zuko a quick look before his eyes drop away again. “It was about the invasion, and it’s not like it was something I didn’t remember, or think about already, so I don’t…I don’t get why suddenly dreaming about it has me all—” He blows out a frustrated breath, vaguely waving to indicate…presumably everything about himself today.

Feeling like you’re living it again isn’t exactly the same as just remembering. But then, maybe Sokka doesn’t dream the same way Zuko does. “What about the invasion,” Zuko finally asks, breathing steadiness into his flame and double-checking that his shoulders are loose and open. He doesn’t want Sokka to worry about dancing around Zuko’s emotional response right now.

Which might not be necessary, considering Sokka is scowling down at his own forearms as he finally seems to notice after the entire morning that his wrist wraps are askew. “Leaving,” Sokka says, and then nothing else as he begins to pick his wraps apart.

That’s…vague enough that Zuko isn’t entirely sure how to respond. “What about leaving?” Just that Sokka had to go at all? That it didn’t end in the triumph Sokka had pictured? And what does it mean that Zuko felt a stab of relief, that Sokka’s answer was that instead of ‘Azula.’

“We had to leave a lot of people behind,” Sokka finally says, just loud enough for Zuko’s unscarred ear. “Everyone wasn’t going to fit on Appa. And the boats…”

Right. Azula would have made it a priority to eliminate lines of retreat before she ever sprung the rest of her trap. Zuko eyes Teo, Haru, and The Duke as they troop off for their latest bought of exploring—likely the youngest and lightest of them. “Ah.”

“And everyone we had to leave…” Sokka’s voice ticks up at the end, almost turning it into a question.

“They would have been captured,” Zuko finishes after a long moment, belatedly realizing that it actually *is* a question. “If there was no resistance they would have been captured.” Azula had been very clear on that point, about the uselessness of wasting resources on a fight that risked potential information and leverage in the process.

Sokka sags a bit at that, exhaling hard, staring at his unwound wrist wraps as his face seems to battle between relief and distress. “Everyone was there,” Sokka finally says, voice low. “The whole Southern Water Tribe fleet, all the men from my village, my dad. They were all there at the end. It wasn’t like they were back on the beach and we just couldn’t make it to them. They were *there* and we had to choose who was staying and who was going and…”

And they were all there to watch Sokka leave them behind, Zuko silently fills in. Fuck. Zuko hadn’t realized just how literal Toph was being when she spoke of Sokka’s entire Tribe being captured, which is now feeling like a painful oversight. And Zuko’s aware that even without that, Sokka would care very differently than Zuko would about the idea of his father being imprisoned by the enemy.

“I’m sorry,” Zuko offers, aware that it’s a flimsy comfort. Is this, out of everything else, why Sokka still can’t seem to find a way back to his confidence? When in the past he’s always been able to reason his way back to solid footing? “Anyone would find that hard to remember.”

“I just keep—fucking *reliving* it over and over,” Sokka says, openly frustrated as he begins to rewind his wrist wraps again, his hands sharp and jerky. “*That’s* what I keep seeing. Not Dad getting injured, not the fighting, not—” Another hard breath. “It’s not like I don’t remember the rest of it, but I don’t know why I can’t seem to just…treat this like a memory. And whenever I’m trying to figure out if I should do this or if I should do that, and I’m trying to tell myself it’s not a big deal, it’s not as scary as it feels, what’s the worst that could happen— and I remember that the worst that can happen is your entire tribe gets captured and your dad is injured and all your allies are scattered and your friends barely survived and it’s all your fault.”

Zuko blinks, trying to find his footing in the flood of Sokka’s words, trying to slot this against everything else he’s seen from Sokka since the eclipse. “How is it your fault?” Zuko finally asks. Maybe that’s not the most important thing, but…Zuko knows there’s a world of difference between things going wrong and things going wrong because of *you*.

Though maybe that was the wrong thing to say, because Sokka is shooting him an incredulous look like he can’t believe that Zuko even needs to ask. “It was my plan, my idea to begin with, I’m the one who led everyone into a trap, I’m the one who didn’t do a good enough job of planning in the first place, I’m the one who didn’t—” Sokka squeezes his eyes shut, voice cracking. “—who didn’t even realize that the Fire Nation would *know*.”

Zuko winces at the reminder of just how little it would have taken for things to turn out differently, if only they hadn’t been so focused in Ba Sing Se on what was immediately in front of them at the expense of everything else. “You weren’t the only one there, though,” Zuko points out, unable to stop his shoulders hunching a little bit. Was there some way Zuko could have stopped this, without tossing away everything else? Would he have been able to risk it if there was? “You weren’t the only one planning.”

Sokka snorts, tying off his second wrist wrap. “I know, it just…feels like I got everyone into this mess, and I can’t figure out how to fix it so now I’m just walking away like…like it’s *fine*.”

Zuko nods, turning that over and over and eventually tossing the bit at the beginning that no one can do anything about but live with and focusing on the piece that can be changed. “What would fixing it mean?”

Sokka shoots him a confused look.

“We can’t invade again like that,” Zuko says carefully, hoping he isn’t writing off something Sokka thinks is important. “We can’t change the past. But fixing it means doing something now, right? So what does fixing it mean?” He hesitates, searching Sokka’s face. “Is it fighting Azula again? Ending the war? Because we’re working on the one and I’m pretty sure it’s going to come with the other.” Much as Zuko hates that fact.

“I don’t know, I…” Sokka tugs on his wolf tail, then pulls the hair tie out entirely, his face somewhere between contemplative and uncertain. “I mean, the Fire Lord, that was the goal and we didn’t do it, sure. But…that’s not the thing that keeps me up at night. Maybe it should be,” Sokka adds, scrubbing his hands over his face. “But we’re here, you know? Together and training and everything. But Dad, he…he could be anywhere. Facing anything, and I just…I hate not knowing. What if he’s being tortured for information, or getting beaten because he won’t bow down, or killed in some—some prison fight or just—whatever, I have no idea and that’s the *problem,* I can’t *do* anything when I don’t know,” Sokka finishes, sagging, and Agni, Zuko hates to see him looking so defeated. Sokka should never look like this.

If it’s knowledge Sokka needs…Zuko considers Sokka’s dad, something he doesn’t try to do all that often. A non-bender, a warrior. Captured during the invasion of the capital, a leader both militarily and politically, someone known by role and by title within the Fire Nation if not by name and sight. “…Would he tell them that he’s the Chief?”

Sokka blinks up at him, confused. “Probably. Why?”

Zuko briefly considers that this might be stupid. But Agni, he knows how it feels for someone to be in danger because of you. Because you put them there and then could only sit and leave them and hope that you wouldn’t be too late. And that feeling when you *are* too late…fuck, Zuko doesn’t want that for Sokka. “What if you knew where your dad was.” Zuko takes a deep breath, searching Sokka’s face and hoping he’s offering more than false hope with this. “Would that help?”

“…What?”

&#45;-

Sokka feels like his brain is going to explode. He’s gone from mired in his own thoughts to whipping through new information and new possibilities so fast that he almost feels dizzy from it, suddenly going from looking down his own failures to looking out at something that feels almost close to hope.

He can’t stop gaping at Zuko as his brain works, even as Zuko shifts, rubbing at the back of his neck as Sokka struggles to marshal a single coherent word through the cacophony in his head right now—still loud and overwhelming but so different from what there was before.

Zuko, Aang’s teacher. Zuko, Sokka’s firebender. Zuko, Crown Prince of the Fire Nation. Zuko, who doesn’t just know things about Caldera and the royal family, who knows things about the *nation*. Who’s *offering* things about the Fire Nation, things Sokka wouldn’t have even dreamed of putting him on the spot by asking.

“So,” Sokka finally manages to say, “There’s like an eighty percent chance that Dad is in this place—Burning Rock?”

“Boiling Rock,” Zuko corrects, gold eyes steady as he shrugs. “But yeah, if he announced himself he’d be important enough to end up there. Assuming there aren’t too many other political prisoners right now. There aren’t a lot of high-ranking prisoners of war to begin with, but…I guess it kind of depends on Caldera,” Zuko adds with a frown.

Sokka’s rapid-fire thoughts immediately want to latch onto that—what does it depend on? The war? Or Caldera’s politics?—except he’s already trying to simultaneously think about too many different things to make room for that, too. Things like locations and tangible knowledge, like risk and reward, like the weight of inaction in the face of something to actually *do*.

“Sokka,” Zuko prompts, and Sokka jolts, realizing he’s just been staring blankly at Zuko again, his mind racing. “You okay?”

“…I’m having a thought,” Sokka manages to say. As if there’s just one. But there *is* one that’s particularly loud, that’s rising above the others, a huge one, so big he barely has the words for it.

“I can see that,” Zuko says, his tone edged with what sounds like amusement.

“I’m not sure if it’s a good one,” Sokka hedges, because he doesn’t know much of anything these days about the ideas he comes up with. This…might be monumentally stupid.

“I can see that, too.” Zuko’s definitely amused.

“I don’t even know where to begin,” Sokka admits, hands uselessly shaping the air like that’s going to help him. Spirits, if he can figure out how to start, how to take that first step—it could be so *good*.

“Maybe tell me about it?”

“Yeah,” Sokka huffs, cutting Zuko a look. As if it’s that easy. “I’m trying to figure that out.”

Zuko gives him a long, considering look, his fingers tapping against his knees a few times before he finally says, carefully, “…Are you maybe thinking something about your Dad not being imprisoned anymore?”

“…Yes,” Sokka admits. That…sounds very straightforward when Zuko puts it that way.

Zuko nods like that makes sense, which…is reassuring. “Does that feel like it would fix things? If he wasn’t?”

“I think so,” Sokka says, forcing himself to actually work it through, trying not to let the hope climb too fast up through his chest. “We’re working on ending the war, but that’s a long-term thing, right?” And in the meantime, there’s just… stagnating failure. “This is sooner. Faster.” But the diverted resources, and the potential risks…Sokka knows basically nothing still, even if it’s already more than he knew before. Though *Zuko* knows stuff…but Spirits, what can Sokka actually expect him to divulge about his own country?

“That sounds reasonable,” Zuko says, and Sokka blinks, more than a little surprised.

“…It does?”

“Sure,” Zuko shrugs. “If it feels like it’s getting you closer to where you want to be, that makes sense.”

It definitely feels like that, but, “I’m just not sure if breaking into a Fire Nation prison is really the path of least resistance right now.”

Zuko hums, offering another shrug. “It’s not really that hard to do.”

Sokka stares, playing those words back over again just to make sure he heard them right. “Wait. What?”

&#45;-

“Fuck,” Sokka mutters, crouched over Zuko’s battered, folded, water-stained, amazing, wonderfully detailed map. Sokka could have run himself in circles trying to figure out how to balance gaining information with protecting Zuko’s split loyalties, but the ready willingness with which Zuko is offering more information than Sokka’s ever seen at one time on the Fire Nation prison system has put those concerns thoroughly to rest. Zuko can clearly make his own decisions, there, if Sokka had any doubts. “Even if we could cross the water, it would take too long to walk there. Appa…”

“We can’t just take him,” Zuko repeats, firm in his insistence.

“We can’t take him without the others knowing,” Sokka corrects, because he’s pretty sure Appa loves Zuko and will yip yip with him anywhere Zuko wants to go. You don’t lick a guy that much because you don’t like him. At least in Sokka’s experience. “We could leave a note.”

“Hm.” Sokka recognizes a noncommittal judging-you hum when he hears one. Spirits, sometimes it’s clear just how much time Zuko spent with Iroh. “Remind me again why they shouldn’t know?”

“Because they’ll either try to join us or stop us,” Sokka says again, half his focus back on the map.

“And why’s the first one bad?”

Sokka eyes Zuko. “I know you’re saying infiltrating prisons isn’t a big deal. But doing it with six extra people?”

Zuko makes a face, conceding that point. “It could just be three more, though. It doesn’t have to be everyone.”

Sokka snorts. “How long do you think it will take to convince anyone to stay behind? Besides,” he adds when Zuko hesitates, clearly only partially convinced. “Have you ever tried to do something secretive and quiet with Aang before?”

“…Right,” Zuko says, looking like he’s reliving a particularly upsetting memory. “No others.”

“It might not matter if we can’t get there, though,” Sokka sighs, turning back to the map and glowering at the reality of knowing exactly where he needs to go, finally, and having no idea how to get there, and doesn’t that just feel like his entire life recently. “Maybe we could send Appa back…”

“…What if I had a war balloon topside.”

Sokka blinks, his mind stuttering to a halt. “…What if you had a what?”

&#45;-

Zuko has part of his attention on watching Sokka take in the war balloon—Sokka taking in something new is always worth watching—and most of his focus on checking the canvas bubble for any weak points along the seams. He isn’t about to fall out of the fucking air because some rabaroo got hungry one night.

“Alright,” Zuko finally says, sitting back on his heels. For some reason he expected solo vigilante missions to be behind him once he joined up with the Avatar. But he supposes this one isn’t technically solo. “Got the supplies?”

Sokka’s hands do a quick touch over his pack, his knife—Zuko managed to convince him to leave the swords behind, in case they had to do any extended sneaking—and the snacks tucked into his pocket. “All good.”

“And you told someone where we’re going?”

“I left a note,” Sokka nods.

Zuko considers. Yeah. A note sounds perfect. “Alright,” he says, kindling a fire to start inflating the balloon. “Let’s do this then.”

&#45;-

“Huh.” The final war balloons have cleaner lines than Sokka’s original design, but he can see how the new basket shape would help with stability during maneuvering even if it means sacrificing comfort inside. “This turned out better than I thought it would.”

Sokka bites back a smile when Zuko doesn’t react for a long moment before suddenly going, “Huh?”

&#45;-

It’s not until they’re in the air that Sokka realizes that part of this whole thing he didn’t really think about—which begs the unsettling question what else he’s missed, and he can only hope nothing important—is the logistics of spending the entirety of their journey in a confined space with Zuko, who hasn’t exactly been shy recently about taking his shirt off during training.

They aren’t entirely on top of each other, but there isn’t exactly room to walk around. There’s just enough space to lay himself out end to end if he wanted, which…Sokka really wishes it not the unit of measure he decided to use to mentally size up the basket, as Zuko sends another blast of sparking flame to push them higher.

This…is going to be a long trip.

&#45;-

“Nice clouds,” Sokka comments, head tilted back against the side of the basket. He’s a connoisseur of clouds after so many months of traveling on Appa. And he’s also trying to distract himself from the reality of true alone time with Zuko for the first time since Ba Sing Se, from the way his skin prickles under the heat spilling out of Zuko because his firebender isn’t thinking about holding that part of himself back anymore.

Zuko glances up at the sky from where he’s tending to the balloon’s cheery little flame, then down to where Sokka is sitting. Sokka suspects that he doesn’t actually need to watch it that closely, but, well—both of them are probably feeling some kind of way about their proximity. “Fluffy,” Zuko finally offers, bemused.

Sokka hums his agreement, stretching his legs out and stacking one boot on top of the other. A nice light-hearted exchange, without any accidental innuendos. Doing good. Keep it going. “Can I ask you something?”

Zuko makes a little inquiring noise, eyes back on the clouds like he’s trying to figure out what sets them apart from the less nice kind.

“What does the Fire Nation do about all the rust on their ships? No, seriously,” Sokka says when Zuko lets out a startled laugh. “It’s metal in saltwater. *Steel*. Who was dumb enough to think that was a good idea?”

“Some admirals a half-generation before Sozin,” Zuko says, laughter still in his voice. “It was cutting-edge technology back then.”

“Well maybe it hadn’t been done before for a reason,” Sokka says, trying to wrap his mind around the fact that the supposedly most advanced navy in the world is still doing the exact same thing they were doing over a hundred years ago. “What, did they need something to keep military grunts occupied? Spend all day fighting rust spots instead of each other?”

“I think it had more to do with steam power and not lighting your entire ship on fire,” Zuko says, dry.

“So lazy firebenders,” Sokka translates, sticking out his tongue when Zuko gives him a mock-annoyed look. Oh, Sokka likes it when Zuko feels relaxed enough to get playful.

“It’s lasted for a reason,” Zuko says, “*With* firebenders.”

“It sure isn’t because of the easy upkeep,” Sokka grumbles, flexing out the remembered ache in his hands from weeks of scrubbing decks and hulls and stairs and railings and every inch of that stolen ship.

“No,” Zuko snorts. “That’s one thing I don’t miss, all the cleaning and painting schedules. And the dry docking. And the monthly maintenance. And the replacement work.”

“Spirits,” Sokka mutters, silently trying to figure out what Zuko’s list would translate to in terms of expenses and man-hours. No wonder Fire Nation crews were so big, they needed dedicated painting staff on hand.

Zuko huffs, shaking his head. “Agni’s balls, I haven’t had to think about that in a while.”

He sounds half-wondering about it, and Sokka cocks his head to the side, trying to get a better look at his expression and unable to resist a little prying. “*Do* you miss it?”

Zuko’s silence is long, but it’s a thinking one rather than a not-going-to-answer one. He eventually settles down across from Sokka, slowly mirroring his position. “Sometimes,” Zuko finally admits, half-frowning as he says it like he needs to probe his own emotions in real-time. “I…didn’t love it, or anything. But.”

“But it was four years of your life?”

“Give or take,” Zuko agrees, sounding quiet and rueful and helpless about it.

“The spirit you know over the spirit you don’t,” Sokka offers.

“Something like that, I guess.”

&#45;-

“Can *I* ask *you* something?”

Sokka glances over, craning his head a bit since he’s transitioned to lying on his back perpendicular to Zuko. “Always,” he says, easy, because Zuko’s been opening and closing his mouth for a few minutes now and Sokka’s been itching to find out what he wants to say.

Zuko still does the usual little hesitation, that search-for-words-fuck-it-just-go pause and then rush of his. “You don’t have to answer.”

“I appreciate that,” Sokka acknowledges, waiting, patient.

“What was the plan? On the Day of the Black Sun?”

Sokka blinks, surprised, because—well, because part of him is surprised Zuko hasn’t gotten an answer out of someone else by now. Toph, or Aang maybe. He doesn’t quite know how to about the fact that Zuko waited to hear it from him. Shit, should he have volunteered it? Did he slide back into that Ba Sing Se mode of thought, the one where Zuko and invasion plans don’t occupy the same mental landscape?

But this isn’t Ba Sing Se, and Sokka won’t let himself fall into that pattern again, doesn’t want to hold Zuko separate from the other important things in his life.

Sokka turns onto his side so he can see Zuko more fully, taking in the uncomfortable, determined set of his face, his white-knuckled hands where they’re clasped together in his lap. “I mean…to invade, obviously. To find the Fire Lord.” Sokka…doesn’t really know where to start, but he wants to make sure he gets this right since it so clearly matters to Zuko. Zuko frowns down at his lap. “I…you guys really didn’t think the Fire Nation would know about the eclipse?”

Sokka sighs and shoves himself upright, because of course Zuko would arrow right to the heart of Sokka’s biggest failure with painful accuracy and not even seem to realize he’s doing it. “It just…seemed like a big secret.”

“…I mean. We don’t advertise it for a reason.”

“The reason being me,” Sokka says, feeling a little twist of wryness.

“Pretty much, yeah.” Which is…unexpectedly gratifying to hear, in a weird way, rather than pressing against the familiar, bruising ache of his failure.

“I don’t know,” Sokka finally sighs, restlessly tugging the tie out of his hair and gathering it back up again, trying to smooth the wind-blown strands. “I guess I just…got too carried away seeing all the advantages.” He just didn’t *think*. Even though seeing the big picture was supposed to be Sokka’s thing. Even when, in retrospect, there was *such* clear evidence that the Fire Nation had been to Wan Shi Tong’s library. He’d just been so…*excited*, so eager to finally have a way to contribute that was all his own.

“It’s not really considered polite to talk about,” Zuko says after a moment, which isn’t at all what Sokka would have expected. *Polite?* “It’s a scary thing, you know? Feeling your tie to Agni suddenly gone. It’s not something people want to have a talk about, usually.” He glances over to Sokka, darkness lurking in his eyes. “It’s like your blood goes cold. Like… some vital part of you is gone. It feels like your spirit or soul or something is just…ripped away, but they forgot to take you too and now you’re just…a body that hasn’t realized its dead yet.”

Sokka stares. Fucking…fuck.

“And you know it’s going to come back,” Zuko continues, Sokka’s heart clenching over how haunted his expression is. “You *know* there’s an end, because all the records say it ends. You know exactly how long it’s going to be. And every time before it's ended. But…what if this time it doesn’t?” Zuko’s eyes slide up, holding onto Sokka’s. “You don’t *actually* know, you know? Not until it ends. It’s Agni’s gift.” Zuko snaps, a burst of flames over his hand like maybe he needs to remind himself it’s there. “Gifts can be taken away.”

Sokka flails for the first words that come. “…Does that happen?”

“Not in living memory. Longer than that, I guess?” Zuko’s hand flexes again, and there are no flames this time and the air is thin and cold, but Sokka thinks that was something with heat. “Not that I’ve heard of, at least,” Zuko adds, “But still, it’s not…good. To experience.” Zuko glances away, shoulders creeping up toward his ears, and Sokka doesn’t know what to do with the fact that all some part of him wants to right now is light Zuko on fire which… Spirits, is something he never thought he’d feel, something he doesn’t know what to do with. It’s definitely *supposed* to be comforting…

“That sounds scary,” Sokka finally says, rubbing at his chest and remembering what it felt like when the moon was gone. Like the whole world had tilted off its axis, greyscale and gut-lurching and barely able to stand, like the earth itself was betraying him on top of the loss of the moon. Katara frantically reaching for an element that wouldn’t come. Would it be better or worse, to know that was coming back but have to anticipate it happening in the first place? To be a bender and feel that extra sense suddenly being gone? “But you made it.”

Zuko considers that, then shrugs, offering a humorless little excuse for a smile. “Yeah. I did.” Zuko cuts him a glance beneath his lashes. “You made it, too.”

Sokka pulls a face because it doesn’t feel like he made it through much of anything, most of the time. Then he breathes a surprised laugh at the similarity of their reactions, looking to see if Zuko noticed too and raising his eyebrows in question when he sees that Zuko is still peeking at him, looking through his bangs now—which Spirits, Sokka *still* hasn’t gotten his hands into—face going a little bit hesitant.

“You—when you were in the palace. You saw Azula.”

Sokka pauses, veering away from any line of thought that involves his hands and Zuko’s hair and trying to understand what’s going on in Zuko’s voice. He’s heard tension and anxiousness and annoyance and a weird kind of pride when Zuko’s talked about his sister, before, but never anything quite like this. “We did,” Sokka finally acknowledges, aware that that’s one of the larger understatements Sokka’s ever made in his life.

Zuko’s fingers are tapping against his thighs, eyes fixed on the base of Sokka’s neck. “What did she say?”

Sokka blows out a hard breath, dropping his head back against the basket as he tries to gather his thoughts. “She said plenty.”

“To you?”

Sokka pauses. “…Did Aang snow rat me out?”

“Toph. But…she’s my sister.”

Sokka raises his eyebrows, silently asking for more.

“I know how she is.”

Sokka wonders about that, sometimes. He silently traces the pathway of scars over Zuko’s body. He can’t see them from this far away, not that he could see beneath Zuko’s clothes anyway, but he remembers the story of every single one of them. He remembers how Zuko seemed unable to even comprehend the idea that what happened to him shouldn’t have—that little sisters shouldn’t literally hunt their big brothers through the palace.

“She said that you were using me,” Sokka finally offers, turning back to the sky above, because something about looking at Zuko when he can hear Azula’s voice saying the words is more than he can handle. He can still see the way Zuko winces at the words, though. “That you hurt my friends,” Sokka continues, and Zuko waits, quiet. So he knows how his sister is enough to have expected that, then. “She said that I got you killed.”

Zuko is still a long moment before he lets out a slow breath. “Ah.” There’s a world of grim revelation in that sound and Sokka drops his head back again, seizing the moment to let Zuko process, to let his own adrenaline settle from the instinctive rush of tension and terror that still comes with the idea of Zuko being not just away but *gone*.

It takes Sokka longer than he would like to feel steady again, considering the evidence he has right in front of him of Azula’s lies. But once Sokka does he sneaks a glance toward Zuko, checking in and wondering if he can ask his own question. Sokka doesn’t exactly want to dwell on the topic longer than they need to, even if most days it feels like he can’t do anything else, but…if they’re talking about it already, they might as well get it out all in one go, right? “What did she say to you?”

“Huh?” Zuko jolts a little, blinking, seeming to come back to the present.

“You said you know how she is. And, before, right when you—you said that she told you about the invasion.” Sokka sees comprehension dawn, followed by an almost-immediate scowl. “What did she say?”

“…A lot of things,” Zuko huffs, flicking an annoyed finger against the basket. “She has a way with words.”

Sokka doesn’t quite know what to make of the bit of envy he thinks he hears in Zuko’s voice, but he *does* know a non-answer when he hears one and gently shoves Zuko’s boot in request.

Zuko sighs, relenting. “I think her most eloquent version was ‘tripping over my own dick to get played by the first piece of ass to shake in my direction.’ Or something like that.”

“…Oh,” Sokka finally manages to choke out. “Uh. Wow.” That’s…remarkably descriptive, actually. Nearly eloquent. And cutting, for someone he’s pretty sure is around Katara’s age. He…Spirits, Sokka has no idea what he would do if Katara said something like that to him. She’s certainly expressed a similar *sentiment*, but…he suddenly has a deep appreciation for the delivery.

“Yeah,” Zuko shrugs, seeming…honestly, seeming less bothered by it than Sokka would have expected, which…Sokka thinks is good? Maybe he’ll reconsider that later, just to be sure.

“…It’s a high compliment to my ass, I suppose.”

There’s absolutely no way Sokka could possibly miss the way Zuko glances down, lingering, before dragging half-lidded eyes back up to Sokka’s face. “A deserved one.”

Well then. So much from distracting himself from their confined quarters. But Sokka supposes he opened the door for that one.

&#45;-

The extended waiting time with nothing to do must be getting to Sokka, because he and Zuko have been in an increasingly playful and bizarre game of one-up-manship for…longer than Zuko necessarily wants to check against the position of the sun.

“The first girl I had a crush on had a husband and two children and once sent me to bed without dinner,” Sokka tosses out, reclining back, one leg bent. “She made the best fry cakes,” he adds, expression going a little bit dreamy.

“*Wow*, Sokka*,*” Zuko laughs. “Truly, you have not changed a bit.”

“I was like, six, so you better hope I have.”

“Sure you were,” Zuko grins before offering up, “The first girl I had a crush on literally never said a word to me.” Librarian Anami had nevertheless made quite the impression.

Sokka snorts. “The first girl who liked me back made me put on makeup and a dress.”

Zuko glances over, picturing it. “Hot,” he offers, aiming for sarcastic and…probably missing. He didn’t actually try that hard. Zuko wouldn’t mind seeing that.

“You almost burned her village down.” Sokka’s smile is sharp.

“…Hot?”

Sokka rolls his eyes. “Sure.”

“The first girl who liked me pushed me into a fountain somewhat regularly,” Zuko says, Sokka’s surprised bark of laughter is worth the prickle of embarrassment.

“Hot,” Sokka grins

“I was, like, ten.”

“Huh. Never mind, then.”

&#45;-

“The first boy I kissed ended up being a huge manipulative dickbag.”

“Hm.” Sokka can hear Zuko considering his counter. “The jury’s still out on that one for me.”

Sokka’s eyes snap open. “Hey!”

“He might be able to redeem himself,” Zuko teases, openly laughing at Sokka’s outrage. “We’ll have to see.”

“Hey!” Sokka repeats, leaning up to give Zuko a shove that Zuko doesn’t even try to fight, just sliding down with a laugh, shoving back and then switching to suddenly pull Sokka forward when Sokka tries to brace so that he just completely overbalances instead. Sokka lets out a yelp as he goes down and Zuko laughs again, the traitor, and then they’re tussling in the confined space, playful and good-natured, and it’s only some miracle that has them ending up lying on their sides instead of on top of each other.

They’re both breathless and smiling, face to face, and Sokka drinks in the happiness in Zuko’s gaze, the way Zuko’s eyes track down to Sokka’s lips, the visible catch in his breath. Sokka licks his lips, throat suddenly dry, and for a moment all he can think about is how easy it would be to push up on his elbow and lean forward and see if Zuko’s smile tastes as good as it looks.

Sokka sucks in a sharp breath, abruptly rolling onto his back and jerking his eyes upward. He can feel himself flushed and wanting and Spirits, even if he’s ready for this again—and he isn’t entirely convinced he is, he’s trying to be smart about this and actually think, because he can’t mess with Zuko like it doesn't matter, he can’t—mere hours out from a mission would *not* be the time.

There’s a long moment of stillness at his side, Zuko’s eyes still hot on his face, then Zuko rolls onto his back too, mirroring Sokka so they’re nearly shoulder to shoulder, still next to each other but with a perfectly reasonable distance between. Close enough to reach across, almost like that night under the stars, and Sokka exhales, relaxing, and…Spirits, even this is so nice, to just be with Zuko like this, quiet and comfortable and familiar and with nothing but the sound of their slowly synchronizing breathing between them.

&#45;-

“So something I’ve been wondering for a while.”

Zuko hums in acknowledgment but doesn’t bother to open his eyes. Agni’s warmth is different up in the air like this, and the rhythm of their breaths is near-meditative. But not entirely, his mind still aware enough that Sokka’s words easily draw his attention.

“So Agni.”

Zuko cracks open an eye, because Sokka…doesn’t like spirit stuff. And doesn’t generally bring it up on his own.

“You like—I mean, everyone you, not just you, you. I know that it’s a, you know…national thing, not just a *you* thing. And I’m not trying, to, I guess, be rude or anything.”

“Sokka,” Zuko interrupts gently, bemused. “What’s your question?”

“Right,” Sokka flushes. “Agni’s like—got a body, right?”

Zuko blinks. “Yeah.” Most things do…

“Like a…human body?”

Zuko shrugs. “Sure.” As close as one of the primal guiding forces of the universe can be to human.

“So, um. What’s—what’s Agni’s gender?”

Zuko can feel the confusion tugging at his scar as he turns his head to stare at Sokka because…Zuko absolutely does not understand the question.

“Cause when you curse you reference tits and balls and a cock and that one time I’m pretty sure you said—well. Yeah,” Sokka says, as if that’s in any way illustrative. Zuko wonders if he should point out that the polite upper crust of society will swear by Agni’s toes, or if that will just confuse Sokka more. “So I was just…wondering.”

“There…isn’t one?” Does…does the Water Tribe have a different conception of gender than the Fire Nation? Because now Sokka’s giving him a look that’s just as confused as Zuko feels.

“…What do you mean?”

Zuko literally doesn’t know how to explain. “Agni is the sun,” he says, feeling helpless. “So…she’s the sun. She…can be what she wants.” It’s the *sun*, it’s not a woman or a man, it just *is*. As all-powerful and ever-changing as fire itself, moving in a breath from death to rebirth to everything in between.

“I…okay,” Sokka says, though the deep frown he’s wearing suggests he still doesn’t get it.

“I mean,” Zuko tries again. “What gender is the ocean?”

“Male,” Sokka says promptly.

Zuko blinks. “The moon?”

“Female.”

“…Oh.” Zuko…didn’t expect that. He’s read plenty of Water Tribe texts on waterbending, which usually touches on the Ocean and Moon eventually, but…he thought that was just a stylistic thing on the part of the authors.

“Her name is Yue,” Sokka tacks on.

…Not Tui? Zuko was…honestly absolutely positive that it was Tui and La, not Yue and La.

“She was pretty great.” Sokka’s tone is…wistful?

Zuko tries to process the degree of fondness and *personalization* in Sokka’s reply, given his general dislike of all things spiritual. “Did you, ah. Meet her?”

“Yeah,” Sokka says after a moment, simple and low and with a whole world behind it, a pain that sounds both old and fresh, the kind that flares to life whenever you prod at it.

Yue…is a Northern Water Tribe kind of name. And Zhao had wanted to kill the moon during that debacle of an invasion. And someone Sokka knew had died, during all that, with Uncle somehow mixed up in it. And Sokka had been so *mad* at Uncle that one time. All the time, maybe. “Did you—?”

“We were friends,” Sokka says in a quiet rush, like the words were just waiting for the moment to spill free. “Before she…you know.”

“Ah.” Zuko…doesn’t know, actually. He doesn’t entirely understand what Sokka is saying came after that ‘before,’ for someone to be a spirit now but not from the start. To be a spirit now and not—well, not just dead. Though Zuko doesn’t think that knowledge of death avoided would make the loss any less painful, any less real.

“She was engaged, so…”

“Ah.” That hurts, a little, in a way that’s easy for Zuko to brush away. Zuko can’t resent Sokka any happiness, especially not when Zuko wasn’t in any kind of place back then to give Sokka any of what he needed or deserved.

“So we were just friends,” Sokka continues. “And…yeah.”

Zuko carefully picks over his words. “Just friends when one side is pining is never just friends,” he finally settles on.

Sokka is still a moment before glancing over, the stiffness fading from his face as curiosity takes over, his tone clearly setting the topic of the moon aside for now. “Speaking from experience?”

“Something like that,” Zuko says after a moment, letting it go, too.

&#45;-

“Calligraphy.”

“Just…all calligraphy,” Sokka repeats, trying to wrap his mind around it.

“I mean, obviously there was sword training, too,” Zuko shrugs, a smile hiding in the corner of his lips at whatever he’s seeing on Sokka’s face.

“What about painting,” Sokka prompts.

“Nope.”

“Meditation?”

“Not a bit of it.”

“What about judging the way you make your food?”

“…Did you actually do any sword training with Piandao?”

“Yes,” Sokka says, outrage sparking at the memory. “And he pretended to try to fucking kill me! I thought I was about to die!”

“Oh, yeah,” Zuko says easily. “That’s a thing he does.” And *why* doesn’t Zuko sound at all upset about it?

“…The Fire Nation is fucking weird, man.” Sometimes it’s just…blindingly apparent that Zuko did *not* grow up anything like the way Sokka did.

“And yet,” Zuko says, laughter in his voice that part of Sokka aches to hear let loose. “Did you not get better?”

“…Fuck you,” Sokka mutters. It was weird and made absolutely no sense and it fucking worked.

“Hm. If you want.”

Sokka chokes, heat rushing to his face. But at least that part of him can appreciate the sound of Zuko’s laughter ringing free.

&#45;-

“Know who invented war balloons?”

Zuko pauses, hand half-outstretched from stoking the flame and checking their progress. The winds have been remarkably in their favor so far. “Some engineer?”

“I did.”

“…What?”

“With Teo’s dad,” Sokka adds, a mix of pride and pure glee on his face. Presumably at getting to shock Zuko, because Zuko…is confused.

“…The—”

“Not the earthbender,” Sokka rolls his eyes. “Or the little one.”

“I knew that,” Zuko glowers. He might still be half-convinced that the little one being named ‘The Duke’ is a joke that everyone else is playing on him, but after this long he knows his *name*. There aren’t *that* many of them.

“Sure you did,” Sokka agrees, with a *very* indulgent-looking smile. And was that a giggle? Agni, the altitude must be getting to him. Maybe Zuko should bring them down a bit.

&#45;-

“Winging it feels weird,” Sokka says, tugging on his wolf tail as he peers over the edge of the basket.

“I do it all the time,” Zuko shrugs.

Sokka cuts him a sideways look. “…How’s that working out for you?”

Zuko hums, actually giving the comment consideration. “Pretty great, actually. At least recently.” Zuko is still faintly surprised by it whenever he realizes it. He wouldn’t generally recommend using his life as a source of inspiration for anyone, but things *have* been going troublingly well lately…

“…That’s good,” Sokka says, giving Zuko an interested look before turning back to the fast-approaching column of steam. “I guess we can’t do much else, we don’t really know enough for a good plan anyway.”

“We know what we need,” Zuko says, unconcerned. All the prisons have the same general training and administrative structures unless you’ve got an oddball commander. That means the same watch rotations and schedules, standards and regulations. “It’ll be fine.” He huffs when Sokka just shifts, fidgeting fingers saying he's not entirely convinced. “Want a plan? Bust in, bust out. That’s the plan, alright?”

Sokka glances back over his shoulder, face somewhere between skeptical and amused. “That’s the plan?”

“Yes,” Zuko says, then adding after a moment, “Metaphorically, though. We can’t actually go in fists blazing.” That’s for the way back out. “We need to infiltrate.” Anyone who grew up with the Dragon of the West learned early to appreciate the value in things other than a full-frontal assault. When an unstoppable force meets an immovable object, the side that can reinforce itself with earthbending usually wins.

“I do know *that* much about breaking into prisons,” Sokka says, rolling his eyes.

“You’d be surprised what people don’t seem to know about prison breaks,” Zuko mutters, remembering Pohuai Stronghold. Agni’s tits, there was so much *shouting*.

“Maybe most people don’t think about it all that much?”

“That’s just a lack of imagination on their part,” Zuko shrugs. It’s not like it’s that hard to figure out. Get in, get out, don’t get permanently caught in the middle. What’s so hard about that?

&#45;-

“Thank you. By the way.”

Zuko glances over at him from where he’s getting his game-face on or whatever he’s doing, eyebrow raised in question.

“For coming with me,” Sokka clarifies. “For not—trying to talk me out of it.” For not just letting him churn in his own thoughts by himself, for offering up knowledge Sokka couldn’t have held against Zuko for withholding in order to help try to make this better.

Zuko shrugs, looking like he doesn’t know what to do with the gratitude. “I couldn’t let you go alone,” he finally says.

No, but Sokka wouldn’t have even known this was an option in the first place without him. “I still appreciate it.” Everything, the war balloon, the secrets Zuko freely gave without questions, the whole-hearted commitment and quiet confidence because once Zuko decides he’s doing something, he doesn’t know how to give it anything less than his whole self.

“It’s the least I could do,” Zuko finally replies, hiding behind his almost-too-long hair.

Sokka weighs that, considers what Zuko would expect of himself, the kind of responsibility he would put on only his own shoulders. “It means a lot,” Sokka eventually says, firm and insistent, because the least Zuko could have done is so much less than this.

&#45;-

Sokka is Water Tribe. He’s a fan of water, is comfortable near it and in it and with it in general. But he isn’t used to the water being so thick in the *air*. The steam coming off the lake is heavy, sulfuric, clinging to his skin and settling like a solid thing in his throat. Zuko’s crouched on the thin stretch of gravel beach between the prison walls and the boiling lake— which, Spirits, this better not be another volcano incident—not even *sweating* as he flicks his gaze between the high wall of the prison and the spreading ripples where they just pushed the useless-when-it's-too-hot war balloon into the water.

It’s a rather severe design flaw for traveling in the Fire Nation that Sokka will worry about when they’re out of this, because they’re in it for real now, the both of them. No turning back and reconsidering, now.

“No vigilante shit,” Sokka presses, and Zuko snorts, giving their surroundings a meaningful glance. “I mean it. No suicidal sacrifices,” he emphasizes, relaxing fractionally when Zuko pulls a face but nods. “We go in together, we get out together.” He waits for Zuko to nod again. “We aren’t here to be heroes. We’re here to get something done. Yeah?”

“In, out, together,” Zuko echoes, voice a firm, low rasp. “Heard.”

“Alright.” Sokka inhales deep, forcing himself to breathe through the thick air, suppressing the urge to cough. He’ll adapt soon, he knows it. He always adapts. “Let’s do this thing.”

Zuko’s wrist turns, sharp, a dagger of fire flaring to life in his hands, and as he gets to work on the drainage grate that spills out into the lake, Sokka considers the degree of faith they’re both placing in their ability to wing this and come out safe and whole on the other side. But maybe that kind of pressure is exactly what Sokka needs to get this right, even if it’s more than a little terrifying to consider the full scale of.

Or rather, it would be if there were time to think about things like that. Because the grate is falling, Zuko lunging to catch it before the metal swings wide to hit the rock of the prison wall, and it turns out breaking into Fire Nation prisons is rather easy after all, there’s no more time for wondering or questions as Sokka leads them into the blinding darkness, hoping that getting out will be just as simple.

## Chapter 19: Out of the Frying Pan

### Notes

#### Chapter Notes

No particular warnings for this one!

### Text

If Sokka didn’t already know it from Zuko’s ‘it’s not that hard,’ then getting inside Boiling Rock would have more than made it clear that Zuko is unreasonably good at sneaking into Fire Nation prisons. The way he knows the piping system will have a wide enough access point for them to slip into a maintenance hallway if they turn right instead of left, his comfort with the patrol schedules, the fact that he’s entirely confident that this nondescript door that looks exactly like every other door will open into a supply closet and not a guard room— Sokka is more than a little curious what, exactly, a Fire Nation Prince gets taught as part of their standard education.

Another question for the list, and probably not anywhere near the top. Maybe he should have asked a few of the bigger ones back in the war balloon, now that he thinks about it, instead of the fun ones that made laughter sit in the back of Zuko’s voice. Except, well—en route to a mission maybe wasn’t the time anyway for big things.

“We can work with this,” Zuko is saying as he assesses the contents of the closet, managing to sound both brisk and pleased. Sokka follows his gaze over stacks of tunics and trousers, rows of boots and helmets, neat lines of studded leather breastplates that are clearly Fire Nation even if they’re shorter than Sokka’s used to seeing. He supposes prison guards get different equipment than soldiers do. He supposes that’s good.

It’s all very clearly a uniform closet, which is…honestly exactly what they need right now at this stage in the infiltration. Sokka eyes Zuko again and silently upgrades his evaluation to *really great* at sneaking.

“I do love a convenient face-obscuring helmet,” Sokka murmurs as Zuko begins sorting through the options.

Zuko hums. “So does the Fire Nation.”

“And why is that, again?”

“Depersonalization as a means of eroding individuality and reinforcing a sense of loyalty toward the larger whole,” Zuko says immediately, tone absent as he holds up a pair of paints for consideration.

“…Right.” Sokka blinks “That. That…makes sense.” In a horrifying, practical kind of way, and now Sokka is back to wondering about that royal education again.

Zuko makes a noise of agreement. “These should fit you.”

Sokka accepts the offered pants and shirt—which *do* look like a good fit when he holds them up—before moving to the other side of the room to begin sorting through the armor there. Which…is much harder to judge than the clothing. Or, Sokka considers as he pulls out his fourth clearly wrong-sized breastplate that looked great on the rack, maybe Sokka just has less of an eye for it than Zuko.

“Here,” Zuko says from behind him, amused as he slips over to Sokka’s side of the closet and sorts quickly through breastplates and wrist guards and belts until he has a neat little stack for Sokka.

“You have a lot of practice sizing people for clothes?” Sokka asks as he holds everything up and realizes that yes, once again, each item Zuko grabbed is perfect. “Are you a secret tailor?”

Zuko rolls his eyes, the shadow of a smile sitting around his lips as he sorts out his own sizes. “The *Wani* ran on hand me downs. That budget needed to stretch.”

Zuko is quick and efficient about it, and then he’s stepping back once he has his own pile completed, hands going to the belt of his overtunic. At which point Zuko’s utilitarian briskness stutters to a halt, his eyes snapping up to Sokka’s face, wide with realization because—well, because they’re in a supply closet about to strip down together.

Sokka stares back, then blurts out the first thing that comes to mind to disperse the sudden taut awareness stretching between them that *really* has no place on a mission. “It’s nothing I haven’t seen before?”

Zuko blinks, mouth slowly opening and then closing as his eyebrow ticks upward. “…Do you want to see it again?”

Sokka flushes so hard and fast that his face fucking tingles from it, managing to gurgle out an “Um” before spinning around give Zuko his back. Zuko lets out a huff of laughter behind him that has Sokka blushing even more, that makes his heart feel like it’s fluttering in his throat.

Spirits, just…Spirits.

Sokka changes, feeling rushed and clumsy as he peels off his Water Tribe blues and tries to hurry his way into his new uniform, so fumbling it’s almost slow. He isn’t *trying* to be, even if some small part of him—despite the utterly inappropriate setting—wants to draw this out. He doesn’t—he has *some* self-control—but Spirits, that voice telling him to take his time and make a little show of slipping his tunic off his shoulders, of loosening his waistband, of unwinding his wrist wraps.

Just the idea that Zuko could be watching behind his back—and Sokka knows that he isn’t, is fully aware that Zuko wouldn’t peek without express permission—is enough to send his pulse racing. And fuck does Sokka ever want to take a peek of his own. Zuko when he feels like putting on a show is…Sokka doesn’t even have words. But he can’t look, Sokka knows he can’t, not without saying something.

Fuck, his timing with all of this is…truly awful.

“Ready?”

“Yeah,” Sokka says, clearing his throat as he turns around, the word coming out remarkably steady as something flips in his stomach at the sight of Zuko in armor again. The breadth it gives his shoulders, the way that belt defines his waist, that deep red and matte black…It’s not the same as it used to be, but it's close enough that Sokka can briefly imagine he smells spice and frying things, that he can hear drums and the shout of a crowd, that he can feel the weight of a mask against his face.

Zuko cocks his head to the side. “You sure?”

“Uh—yes?” Sokka yanks himself back into the present and glances down at himself. Boots on, trousers tucked, belt centered—it all looks right to him.

Zuko purses his lips. “…Can I?”

“…Sure?” Can Zuko what?

Zuko steps forward, face set with concentration. “It’s more of a…”

Deft fingers find the straps underneath Sokka’s armor, undoing some and tugging on others, redoing them crossed and cinched and *wow*, does that do wonders to make the armor fit more snugly along the lines of Sokka’s torso, to make it move with his body instead of just sitting on top of his shoulders.

“And the belt is more…”

Sokka holds his breath as Zuko’s fingers glide along his waist, repositioning and flattening the belt in question, tucking the trailing ends back underneath, the backs of Zuko’s fingers briefly pressing against Sokka’s stomach. The only thing that saves Sokka from making a truly embarrassing noise is the fact that he isn’t breathing right now, and even then, he doesn’t think it’s entirely unnoticeable, the way his body sways toward Zuko’s touch.

“There,” Zuko murmurs, somehow managing to look at Sokka through his lashes, eyes intent and cheek maybe dusted with pink—it’s hard to tell in the dim light—his hands oh so careful as he finally steps back.

Sokka clears his throat again. “Thanks.”

“You’re welcome,” Zuko says, a few beats delayed. Not that Sokka particularly cares about the delay as they stare into each other’s eyes, tension rising again between them along with Sokka’s awareness of Zuko’s proximity and the walls around them and the heat in the air that’s far too easy to confuse for the kind of that comes off Zuko.

Fuck, fuck, fuck. Sokka finally jerks his eyes away, looking to the door and forcing himself to remember that regardless of the feeling of privacy, they’re in a fucking supply closet in a high-security prison. “Are you ready?” Sokka needs to get himself back on track. “What’s your backstory?”

Zuko glances down at himself, then shoots Sokka a small frown. “Backstory?”

“Yeah. Like, I’m Private Wang Fire—”

“Prisons don’t have privates,” Zuko interrupts. “The military police use different ranks.”

“Guard Wang Fire, whatever,” Sokka huffs. “And I have a nice girl back home I’m trying to impress, and a wayward nephew I’m trying to be a role model for. And when I make enough money, I’m going to marry her, and—”

“Wait. You can get married?”

Sokka blinks, losing the thread of his character entirely. “What?”

“In the Fire Nation you can’t get married until you’re at least twenty-five,” Zuko frowns, shifting his weight from foot to foot. “You…the Water Tribe does it earlier?”

“…Sometimes,” Sokka says, eyeing Zuko, his curiosity sparked. “It’s kind of just when you feel ready. And if you’re an adult. And if the community supports it. Let’s come back to this later,” Sokka adds when Zuko immediately opens his mouth for another question. Sokka… actually really does want to delve into this. But standing in a closet in a Fire Nation prison is neither the time nor the place for comparing cultural marriage practices.

“…Fine,” Zuko concedes, and Sokka can practically see him setting himself a mental reminder to bring the topic up again later. Sokka…is interested to see how Zuko manages to find a way back into this particular conversation.

“Anyway. Should we practice your cover story?” Because Zuko can’t lie for shit.

Zuko shrugs, clearly still thinking about marriage, which…Sokka is going to have feelings about later. “I’ll be fine.”

“…Run it by me?”

“I’m called Lee. I recently came to the Fire Nation from the Colonies. The draft age was lowered to sixteen—” Wait. What? “—and my family cares a lot about the military, and I feel the need to prove myself so here I am.”

Sokka blinks, and slowly closes his mouth. That was…concise and full of just the right amount of familial tension to send most conversational partners hastily running for more neutral ground. And none of it was a lie. Except for the name, and even that—Zuko *was* called Lee in Ba Sing Se. So even that is…actually a carefully selected, carefully framed truth.

That’s…impressive. And maybe a little bit scary—or is it sad?—to see just how easily Zuko can call something like that up.

“We’re going to have a little chat after this,” Sokka finally says, and Zuko shoots him a confused look but gives an easy shrug.

“I’m ready when you are," he says, and Sokka doesn’t quite know what to say to the bald truth of that, how it sounds like Zuko is responding to so much more than just this, and Zuko seems to realize it, letting the tension hang another moment before shifting to a new topic. “Do you need help with your hair?”

Sokka automatically raises a protective hand toward his sort-of wolf tail. “What?” He’s seen the kinds of hairstyles Zuko has worn.

Zuko gives him a sideways look. “…Are you going to wear it like that?”

Well then. “I guess not,” Sokka says, even as he wraps a protective fist around his tied-back hair.

Zuko hesitates a moment, then raises a hand partway up before pausing. “Do you mind?”

Does Sokka mind. Does Sokka *mind*. Zuko’s hands in his hair, shaping and carding and moving against his scalp. Does Sokka fucking *mind*. “No,” Sokka says, clearing his throat and entirely missing casual, landing on soft and more than a little breathy with even just that one syllable.

Sokka can see the way Zuko’s breath catches, and Sokka doesn’t know whether to close his eyes or keep staring at Zuko’s face as Zuko shifts closer to fully enter Sokka’s personal space. Zuko’s hands slowly reach up to tug the tie from Sokka's hair and Sokka can’t help a shiver as the strands cascade down, sweeping along his jaw and across the back of his neck.

Zuko stares for a moment, looking quietly fascinated. And then both his hands are suddenly carding through Sokka’s hair, gathering it up in caress after caress that might be gratuitous or might be wholly necessary for the style, Sokka has absolutely no idea and no inclination to try figuring it out and certainly isn’t going to call Zuko out for it.

Finally, Zuko starts to form a bun on the crown of Sokka’s head, eyes narrowing with concentration, and Sokka does have to close his own eyes then or else he doesn’t know what he might do. His entire scalp tingles as Zuko gently shapes Sokka’s hair, his fingers deft with the hair tie and gentle as Zuko lengthens the topknot until it falls down the back of Sokka’s head, somewhere between a bun and a ponytail.

“This way it won’t bother you under the helmet,” Zuko says quietly, and Sokka can feel the words over his face. He opens his eyes then, desperate to see the expression that goes with the soft words and holding himself still as Zuko carefully tests the tension around the hair tie to be sure no strands are pulling too tight. Sokka can’t help a little sway, though, when Zuko’s hands shift to slide over the curve of Sokka’s skull, the back of his neck, forward, ghosting over his chest before Zuko finally drops them to his sides. His gold eyes are intent on Sokka’s face, the space between them a near-physical thing against Sokka’s skin from the heat coming off Zuko’s body and Spirits, how did Sokka think the heat in the air before was anything close to what Zuko can do?

“Thank you,” Sokka finally whispers, giving his head a little shake to make sure the topknot thing is secure, his pulse tripping as Zuko’s eyes immediately follow the motion.

“Any time,” Zuko murmurs, two little words with all the weight of a promise. Just like ‘in together, out together’—it’s more promise, more a mantra than a plan. But Zuko clearly knows what he’s doing. And it’s not like Sokka’s plans have always worked before, when it matters, so maybe a promise is all you really need.

&#45;-

Going their separate ways—especially when it involves not fighting a direct order to go their separate ways in front of an entire prison yard of riled guards and prisoners—is something Zuko can recognize as tactically smart even as it makes his inner flash lash against the underside of his skin.

Zuko watches Sokka force-march away a firebending prisoner who’s nearly twice his height and definitely more than twice his weight, keeping his face impassive beneath his and trying not to feel the flutter of unease trying to settle in his chest. He desperately wishes there was a way he could take Sokka’s place without causing a scene. If that guy decides to make an issue of being put in the cooler—and Zuko can imagine what that involves and personally wouldn’t want to get anywhere near having his inner flame chilled as punishment—Sokka has no ability to deflect that fire, not without a sword at the ready, and there’s no way to do that with his hands occupied trying to restrain the guy.

Not that Zuko would have a way to deflect an attack, either, not when he’s trying to be as inconspicuous as possible, which means making his bending as inconspicuous as possible, too. Just—fuck.

Sokka is smart, Zuko reminds himself. Smart and resourceful and a capable fighter and also wearing plenty of armor, way more than he usually has on. He’ll be fine, and Zuko standing around worrying about it isn’t going to do anything except make the job they’re here to do take longer.

Zuko lets the frustrated bite of his inner flame add some stiffness to his spine and crispness to his step, not quite stomping through the prison yard and hallways but not trying to stick to the shadows either. He could slide from pocket of darkness to pocket of darkness, but here it’s far easier to move with purpose and rely on his uniform to blend him into the background. Zuko knows how to let his clothes and others’ expectations do most of the work for him.

And it’s good that Zuko does know how to get by other than sneaking, because the general heat in the air, the thick humidity and curling steam that comes off the lake and just *lingers,* is really fucking with his heat sense. It feels blurred when he shoves outward, stretched thin because there’s just too *much* to potentially grab onto, so much that nothing individually stands out. Zuko thinks he could do a lot with it, if he wanted to get chaotic and didn’t care about the consequences. But it’s not exactly as helpful as he’s grown used to for picking out approaching bodies.

Which makes Zuko’s convenient face obscuring helmet, as Sokka called it, even more convenient. If Zuko can’t look without being seen, he can at least look without being completely obvious and notable in his attention, can at least try to replicate the air of impassive observation that all the best guards back in the palace wore like impenetrable armor.

Zuko studies every prisoner he passes, glancing at hands and peering at faces in the yard and in cells and in hallways. Skin and eye color are really all he has to go on, because Zuko is realizing that he doesn’t actually know what Sokka’s father looks like. Which could be a problem if there are multiple Water Tribe prisoners floating around, but hopefully a group will stand out in the largely Fire Nation population.

Not that Zuko is seeing much of anything that doesn’t strike him as very much Fire Nation so far, which lights a spark of disquiet in his gut. Are things really so bad in Caldera? Or is the fighting in the Earth Kingdom becoming so brutal that no one leaves the lines, even with the fall of Omashu and Ba Sing Se? It doesn’t make sense, not unless the Fire Nation prisoners are just lasting longer than everyone else, which shouldn’t be the case if the prison is being appropriately run.

But by the time the shift change rings out, Zuko’s seen a bit of Colony and no one else notably from outside the boundaries of the Fire Nation, and his disquiet has grown into full-blown unease. This isn’t what Zuko's here for, isn’t the kind of information that’s going to help them, but Agni, this…he wonders if Azula knows about this.

Zuko itches to keep looking, to try to find proof that he’s wrong, but the guards around him are all reacting to the shift change, and Zuko spent enough time obsessively reading up on military codes of conduct and organizational practices back when he was finally able to see well enough on the *Wani* to read without vomiting to know he needs to turn his steps toward the mess hall along with everyone else. A morning shift duty that ends before Agni is at her peak but after she is more than fifty degrees risen means a Four Shift schedule, and the guards in Shift Two—

Well. Zuko supposes that he can do whatever he wants since he isn’t actually a guard. But Zuko *is* hungry, and he knows that Sokka will appreciate any snacks Zuko can scrouge for him, so the mess hall is as good a place to take himself right now as any. And maybe he can see what there is to hear when there are no prisoners around.

&#45;-

Zuko quietly blesses Fire Nation standardization—again, really that is what’s enabling this entire mission—as he makes his way through the mess toward the food line with only a quick glance to take in the layout. It’s a familiar setup, with a familiar flow of bodies that Zuko can easily slip himself into and a familiar array of batch-cooked rations—barely a step up from what the prisoners themselves get, if he had to guess—that Zuko’s heart still gives a little leap over, seeing Komodo sausage mixed into the rice and the distinctive red of the over-spiced, overboiled vegetables that come standard with any Fire Nation military endeavor.

Zuko takes back his blessings for Fire Nation standardization when he reaches the end of the line at the head of the room and comes face to face with the Fire Lord. Or rather, with the Fire Lord’s portrait. Zuko…didn’t exactly forget that these are a typical part of any official governmental gathering space, but he also didn’t think about it, and the reminder is somewhat less than pleasant.

It’s an older portrait, Zuko distantly notes, one where Ozai looks regal and younger than he’s looked ever since he took the throne, his expression a mixture of parental firmness and kind regard that Zuko’s never actually seen in real life.

There’s a portrait of Azula below and to the right of Ozai’s, too, one that makes her look every bit as sharp as she is. Older, though. Or maybe he’s still just used to thinking of her from before and not as she is now. And around her image are blank spaces, spots on the wall that are just a bit less smoke-grimed than the rest, a suggestion of the other portraits that used to hang here too, to go along with the holes in the otherwise neat wall that could have been from picture hooks.

Zuko contemplates that emptiness. General convention would be for the entire royal family to have their portraits on the wall in order of their position in the line of succession—something that’s become significantly more manageable given the size of royal families in recent generations. Still. Zuko wonders at what point his and Uncle’s portraits were taken down. The blank spots don’t look fresh.

“You don’t want to spend too long staring, kid.”

Zuko startled at the brusque mutter clearly directed at him, turning to see a guard at a nearby table looking at him with an expression of…Zuko doesn’t actually know what that expression is. “What?”

“At the royals,” she says with a jerk of her head toward the portraits. “It means you’re too interested in who’s still there. Or you’re too interested in who’s missing.”

“Who’s missing,” Zuko repeats, slowly approaching the seat the guard nudges out for him. Being too focused on the portraits that aren’t there makes sense. The entire palace knew not to ask questions when Zuko’s mother’s portraits suddenly started coming down. But being too interested in the Fire Lord?

“The portraits came down years ago,” the woman says, her pale brown eyes no-nonsense as she pointedly doesn’t look to the wall. “And you never know when another one will come down. Or go up.” Her eyes go hard. “It’s not smart to ask too many questions. Especially not with our current Warden.”

Ah. Not asking questions makes sense, Zuko understands that. Though he wishes he could find a way to ask some here because his inner fire is burning low and wary with alarm. If there’s a big enough group of guards to be worth warning against in *Boiling Rock*—or fuck, the Warden himself?—who express sentiments about the royal family as individuals rather than a unit…Fuck. That’s…dangerous.

Zuko wonders if Azula knows about this, too. She has to, but…fuck. How could she know this and still think the timeline doesn’t change?

“You gonna take your helmet off, kid?”

Zuko startles again, hastily imitating her and setting his helmet by his left elbow. “I’m not a kid,” he says, resisting the urge to squirm as she studies his face. If his formal portrait came down years ago it would have been the one he sat for when he was ten, and he knows he doesn’t look like that anymore. Zuko had enough unsettling moments of not recognizing himself in paintings in Caldera to be sure of that.

Still, Zuko’s aware that the guard is eyeing his scar, and his youth, and drawing certain conclusions. He tucks his head down to his food, hiding his eyes. Even if he knows his uncovered face won’t out him to a common guard, Zuko still doesn’t like seeing the assumptions people make, especially when he can’t control what they see.

“You’re new?” She finally asks.

Zuko shrugs. “Just got here.” He takes a big bite, and it’s definitely not the best food he’s ever had by any means, but there’s a lot of it, and the familiar heat of spice on his tongue makes his inner fire pulse in happy echo.

“Where’d they ship you in from, kid?”

Zuko’s eyes flick up, but he doesn’t push back against the name again. “The Colonies.”

“Ah,” she says, understanding dawning over her face and relaxing the set of her shoulders. “Hoping for a transfer into the infantry?”

“Or the navy.” Best to have a reason to explain his knowledge, if it pops out.

“Not much opportunity there for a while,” she observes with such neutrality that it can only be a deprecating statement.

“I can’t transfer for a while,” Zuko shrugs, matching her tone.

“Well, keep your head down and do good work,” she says briskly, tucking into her own food again. “The Warden is tough, but he appreciates a hard worker and someone with a head on their shoulders. He should have some pull when it’s time.”

Zuko pauses, surprised by the freely offered advice as much as by the assumptions in it. “Thanks,” he says, belated. He doesn’t have a head for seeing how political waters will shift down the line, not like Azula always can, but he supposes it’s a reasonably safe assumption that Warden will have *someone’s* ear by then. Omashu might not have been the boon the family was hoping for, but with the Comet coming… “So working here is okay?”

She snorts. “I’ve worked in worse.”

Zuko makes a noise of understanding and interest and settles himself to eat and to listen. He hears about the quality of the food—“better than field rations”—and the barracks—“better than a field tent”—and the timeliness of the pay—“better than chasing down the quartermaster every month.” He learns about schedule changes and drills—“more often than you want”—and which coworkers are decent—“Karuko is fine”—and which are a pain to be on shift with—“Zumai complains”—and which ones will fleece you of your pay in a game of dice—“Karuko also cheats.” She warns him of the duties only a sucker volunteers for —“swabbing the gondola platform. Prisoners do it everywhere else”—and the ones that are a nice gig—“exercise time gets you fresh air”—and the ones that might land you in the onsite infirmary—“exercise time can also get you injured.”

It’s a lot, delivered in sparse sentences and with an absence of personal opinion that reminds Zuko distinctly and with a surprising pang of Lieutenant Jee. He does his best to fix all of it in his mind, even the things he can’t see are relevant, like the frequency of expected vacation time as he moves up the ranks. Zuko knows that any piece of information can be useful to pull a plan together in the right hands, and just because Zuko doesn’t know what to do with any of it doesn’t mean that Sokka won’t.

It’s like Uncle always used to say—the fisherman that knows the tides and seas is the fisherman who always gets some fish. Or something like that.

&#45;-

"It's good information."

It *is* good information. Zuko knows it’s good. Details on guard schedules and recreation time could be key for whatever escape they end up devising. So it's good to hear Sokka agree that it's good.

But Zuko thinks Sokka’s words have a rather distinctive trying-to-cheer-himself-up edge rather than any genuine enthusiasm. It's hard to be fully sure, with Sokka's expressive face hidden behind his helmet, but Zuko's eyes keep drifting back to the dissatisfied tilt to Sokka's lips once his flash of a smile fades.

"But it’s not what you wanted," Zuko finally says, deciding to just give it voice.

Sokka leans back against the railing with a bit more slump than Fire Nation training would generally allow. "I mean—I knew it was a long shot," Sokka mutters, as if knowing something means anything when you want badly enough.

Still, they haven't even been here half a day. It's early yet to talk like they’re giving up. "Just because he isn't here now doesn't mean--"

"There aren't *any* Water Tribe prisoners here," Sokka cuts in, voice tight as he kicks at the metal grating, which is *definitely* against the training standards.

Zuko hesitates, staring at the way Sokka is digging a toe into the walkway, trying to make sense of the burst of anxiety in Sokka's reply. Oh. Zuko should have expected this. "They might not have been brought here,” Zuko points out.

Sokka glances away, like he can’t even bring himself to acknowledge the fear hanging between them beyond the tightening of his jaw. The fear that they're too late, or that they were always going to be too late because maybe Water Tribe prisoners are more trouble to keep than they are worth. The Southern Raiders certainly took that approach, and Zuko’s aware that while their methods might be extreme, they’re not, strictly speaking, unusual for the Fire Nation.

Still. "There are other prisons in the Fire Nation, Sokka. This is just the most secure." And Azula abhors seeing potential resources wasted.

Though maybe it wasn't Azula's decision, which puts an uncomfortable flicker into Zuko’s inner flame.

"Yeah," Sokka says after a beat, blowing out a hard breath and straightening against the railing. "Okay."

Zuko eyes him, holding back his own worried fidgeting. Sokka is visibly tense and frustrated in a way that will stand out like a signal beacon among this sea of Fire Nation neutral faces. This isn't going to do, not if they’re going to keep searching.

“It's like my Uncle always used to say," Zuko finally says, reaching for anything that might help right now. "Sometimes when a storm seems really bad and there's lots of damage, actually..." Zuko tilts his face up as he tries to drag up the rest of this half-remembered, mostly-ignored aphorism. Fuck. "Actually it clears the way for new growth!"
