Zuko grins in triumph at finding the end of the saying before abruptly remembering that now isn’t the time for triumphant things. He ducks his head, hastily pulling on a scowl and resisting the urge to check over his shoulder to see if anyone is looking at them. That would be beyond suspicious and just…Agni’s balls, Zuko usually isn’t this actively nervous for things like this, can usually just focus on the next thing that needs to be done and set aside everything else.

But then, Zuko’s usually alone.

He cuts his eyes to Sokka, blinking in surprise to see some of the tension actually loosening from Sokka’s arms, a wry tilt to his lips before he sighs and moves to rest his forearms on the railing next to Zuko, casting his gaze out over the yard. "Okay," Sokka finally says, giving Zuko's boot a nudge with his own, one that might linger just long enough to count as something more than a nudge, and Zuko barely manages to keep himself from leaning into Sokka’s side in response. None of this is regulation-approved behavior. Zuko will care about that again soon. "That’s…Thanks. Thanks.”

"We have lots to work with now," Zuko assures Sokka again, scanning the walkway around them to be sure they’re still tucked out of view. "And we can get more, and then we can work out an escape." Zuko has no idea how they’re actually going to do that—he’s currently fairly tapped out when it comes to plans—but Sokka’s come up with solutions before that Zuko never would have even thought of. Zuko knows they’re in good hands.

"We just need to find someone who needs to escape first," Sokka mutters.

Zuko snorts. "How about us?" The knowledge of ‘in together, out together’ is drumming a constant, quiet beat behind his heart.

Sokka sighs, looking rueful. "Yeah, I know we need to--" He suddenly jerks upright. "Fuck me sideways."

"...What?" They need to—what?

“*Zuko*,” Sokka says, audibly gleeful as he backhands Zuko across the shoulder before grabbing onto his bicep with palpable urgency, his cool fingers squeezing nearly hard enough to ache as he stares intently into the yard. "Fuck me,” Sokka says again, laughing, “We just might have found our someone."

"What," Zuko repeats, craning his neck to try to follow Sokka's gaze without dislodging his grip.

Sokka's voice is reverent as he breathes out, "That's Suki."

“Oh,” Zuko says, blinking.

…Who’s Suki?

&#45;-

It's not until they’re fully in the process of doing it, and Suki is bolting upright on her cot, her bodied coiled with a dangerous kind of tensions, that Sokka considers that maybe it was a bit ill-advised to ask Zuko to tail Suki to her cell and then show Sokka where it is and then both obviously sneak inside before dinner while wearing full, face-obscuring Fire Nation guard uniforms.

"What is it?" Suki borderline demands with about as much deference to Fire Nation authority as Sokka would expect from her. Her eyes flick between Sokka and Zuko behind him, who’s easing the door closed and peeking through the grate to confirm that no one saw them, which…Sokka can now see might come across as suspicious. "I didn't do anything wrong."

"We wanted to talk to you, Suki," Sokka says, feeling his words fumbling and crowding his throat as her hands form into fists and she stiffens even more at the sound of her name. Zuko sighs, giving Sokka a gentle nudge. "Introduce yourself."

“Why do you know my name,” Suki asks, low and dangerous.

“What—? No, we just—it isn’t—wait—”

“Sokka,” Zuko cuts in, with some weird blend of patience and exasperation that really shouldn't be possible and especially at a time like this. “What are you wearing? Introduce yourself.”

“What the fuck is going—did you say *Sokka?”*

“Shit, right,” Sokka says, glancing down through the narrow eyeholes of his helmet to take in the studded leather armor and black and red of his uniform and hastily taking off his helmet. “Sorry, I know it’s been a long time, I didn’t mean to—”

“Sokka!” Suki throws herself forward, wrapping Sokka up into a hug so sudden and solid that it has the air flying right out of him. Sokka wheezes, nearly bobbling his helmet onto the floor as he grabs her back, holding her close and letting himself feel a stab of relief that she’s okay. It might be more than a little terrifying to think of her in this place—Spirits, what else did Azula say that was true?—but if she’s willing to throw down with two guards then he knows she’s alright.

And now that things are proceeding more as expected, Sokka can’t quite stop grinning at her utter shock, or at the clear enthusiasm of her greeting even after so much time apart. Suki might not be who he came for, but the fact that she’s safe—that she’s going to keep being safe because they’re going to get her out—does more than a little to keep away the sticky, cloying feeling of stacking a new failure on top of all his others.

"I can't believe you're here," Sokka says into the crown of her head, vaguely surprised to realize that he’s noticeably taller than her now.

"I can't believe *you’re* here," she says, the words half-muffled.

"The other Warriors?"

"Just me," Suki says, shaking her head, and Sokka can feel the flash of tension that goes through her at the words. "Because I'm their leader, they said."

Sokka murmurs something sympathetic even as his mind starts spinning. If that’s a policy, if that's how the Fire Nation does things for all their captured military opponents... "Well, we’re here now," Sokka soothes absently. "And we’re--"

Suki stills against him, then pulls away, taking in…a figure that Sokka realizes is very distinctly not Katara or Aang or Toph. "We?"

"Yeah,” Sokka hurries to say, “This is…” He trails off. How exactly does one go about introducing an ex-lover—if that’s really the thing to call Zuko—and increasingly-probable future boyfriend to his first crush and one-time dream girlfriend? Whose village Zuko also burned down…

Zuko takes off his helmet, resting it at his waist with significantly more grace than Sokka. "I'm Zuko."

"Oh," Suki says, tension suddenly winding back through her frame as her face goes flat. "Oh, I know exactly who you are."

"Oh," Zuko says back, looking startled and glancing at Sokka. "Um."

"*Everyone* in my village knows who you are," Suki adds, eyes narrowing and words veering toward aggressive.

Zuko looks to Sokka again in question, and Sokka remembers not to tug on his topknot thing just in time, awkwardly rubbing the back of his neck instead as he mouths, *You burned it* *down*.

"Oh. *Oh*," Zuko flushes, jolting with realization. "You're—yes. Right. I'm...sorry about that."

"I'm sure you are," Suki bites out, scathing before she turns to Sokka with a distinctly cool expression. "You're with him?"

"He's here with me, yeah," Sokka says, suddenly aware that his position in front of Suki with Zuko at his back might read as rather protective. That it *is* rather protective.

Suki frowns at the distinction, eyes flicking between them and then lingering over their uniforms as she takes a careful step back that—fuck, that honestly really hurts.

"...Maybe you guys need some time to talk?"

No one responds, the sound of Zuko uncertainly shifting his weight loud in the silence.

"Okay, well, I'll just...wait in the hall," Zuko finally says, putting his helmet back on and giving Sokka a long look that Sokka can't read between the helmet and the dim lighting. Suki and Sokka both watch him slip back into the hallway, Sokka suppressing a flare of anxiety. He knows Zuko is just outside the door, but after spending the bulk of the day on his own he just...prefers to have Zuko in his sight, especially without any kind of plan in place for what to do if they get separated again.

"Sokka." Suki's hard voice pulls his focus back to what's in front of him. "What's going on?"

"We’re here to rescue you," Sokka says, rubbing at his sweat-dampened hairline. He’s distinctly aware that the words aren’t technically correct, if you’re splitting hairs, but he and Zuko *are* here for a rescue, and that’s the heart of the matter, right?

Her face is pure disbelief. "The Crown Prince of the Fire Nation is here to rescue one of his own prisoners? From his own prison?"

"Shhh," Sokka hisses, glancing around like someone other than Zuko might be listening in. "It's not his."

"Why all the—" A sharp hand takes in his stolen uniform and general subterfuge. “Why not just pardon me?”

Sokka barely even knows where to start. He can’t exactly blame her for being suspicious when the last she saw of Zuko, he was probably wreaking general destruction across her home, but there’s so much between then and now.

This…is probably going to be a conversation that Sokka has a lot. "He isn't—he doesn't do that. Anymore." And Spirits, Sokka better improve fast if he’s going to keep having it.

"Pardoning?"

"…Crown Prince-ing?"

Suki grunts, still mostly suspicious as she casts the door a cutting look, like she’s thinking about trying to pin Zuko down through the reinforced metal. "Why are you really here, Sokka? What’s going on?"

“We’re looking for my Dad,” Sokka says, ruthlessly beating back the spark of hope that maybe she’ll know something, maybe she’ll have heard something or seen someone or— anything. “But he’s not here, and you are, and we came to do a rescue, so—you’re good to rescue, too. Let’s rescue you.” And if the Water Tribe warriors don’t need help because they’re in a less secure facility like Zuko suggested, or because they broke free already, then that’s fine. That’s great. They won’t need Sokka or his ability to plan or his capacity to not fuck things up, which is good for them. Really good. Really.

But maybe Suki does.

“Thanks for thinking of me,” she says, walking the edge of sarcasm, and Sokka winces as he quickly repeats back his own words. “But why is he here?”

“He’s helping,” Sokka says, firming up his voice at her skeptical look. “He’s not how he was back then, Suki.” Yeah, Sokka really needs to find more convincing words to communicate this point. “He’s different now. He’s learned, and grown, and…he’s changed.”

“Yeah,” Suki says after a beat, looking at Sokka like he’s gone crazy. “I’m sure he would say that. And look where it got him, the Avatar’s right-hand man just walked himself into *prison*. Sokka, what the fuck?”

“*Shh,*” Sokka says, “It’s not like that, okay?”

“Oh, so this was your idea?”

“No,” Sokka says, frustrated, “And that’s not the point. He—” Spirits, why is it always so hard to step back from how Sokka sees Zuko to think about how someone else might see him? “He doesn’t burn down villages anymore,” Sokka says, borderline triumphant as he seizes onto something he absolutely knows Suki cares about. “He has so much more control with his bending now, and—"

“Sokka,” Suki cuts in, gaping in disbelief. “Is that really the standard here? He doesn’t burn down whole villages so let’s follow him into prison?”

“No, just—Will you let me finish?” Sokka waits for her grudging nod to continue. “He left the Fire Nation to help us. He had the chance to go back home and stay and he walked away from it so he could train Aang.”

“And you believe that?” Suki finally asks, skepticism clinging to her words. “You’re just taking him on his word?”

“He gave up a lot for us,” Sokka says, catching her eyes and making sure his gaze is steady. “He put his life at risk for us, more than once. Sometimes without even telling us.”

“And you trust that,” she says, the words flat, somewhere between a statement and a question, and she isn’t writing him off entirely yet but wow, does Sokka hate the way she’s looking at him like that, like maybe his judgment can’t be trusted like she thought.

“I do,” Sokka says, voice firm. “I know we don’t have time to get into it all, but he’s shown that he’s different. It’s not just words. He really has.”

“Has he,” she says, eyeing the door. “And what, you’ve seen it? How long have you known him for?”

“…A good amount of time.”

Her eyes snap back to him, narrowing. “A bit more precise, please.”

“I mean…he was hunting Aang for a while—”

“I am well aware.”

“—and you know, you see a guy a lot in that circumstance, as it turns out. In a lot of different ways, you know? And then circumstances change a bit, and you see even more sides of a person, and I guess you could say one thing leads to another as you start to get to know him, and—”

“Wait. Sokka. *Sokka.*” Suki’s eyes go wide with…yup, that…looks like horror. “Is *Zuko* your ‘someone else?’”

“I...” Shit. Sokka wanted to lead into this a little more.

She casts a wild-eyed glance toward the door. “You couldn’t start something with me at the Serpent’s Pass because you of how much you were hung up on the *Fire Prince*?”

“*Shhh*,” Sokka hisses again. “And no! Or—not entirely!” Yue was in that mix, too, back then. Not in the same way, but in *a* way. “Look, it's complicated, okay?”

“You’re fucking telling me,” Suki hisses back. “How did you even—” She snaps her mouth shut, pinching the bridge of her nose. “You know what? No. Not the time. Fine. He’s with you? You trust him? I’ll hold my judgment. But you better believe I’ll be watching him, and you better *believe* I’m getting it out of you later.”

That’s…fair. And good, he supposes, that she isn’t willing to reject a rescue operation over it. That…would have been tough. “Okay. You’ll see. And I’ll tell you. But first, we need to figure out—”

Sokka bites his tongue as the sudden sound of boots turning down the metal hallway rings out, the kind of sound he knows from his time on Zuko’s ship echoes ahead of a person, but not by all that much.

“Hide,” Suki orders, the words sharp as Zuko gives an urgent smack to the door.

“What?” Sokka says, whipping his head back and forth.

“Hide,” Suki repeats, already tugging the blankets on her cot to fall over the edge. Could Sokka even fit under there? “It’s the pre-dinner headcount.”

“There’s a pre-dinner headcount?” Fuck, Zuko hadn’t known anything about that. Zuko, who’s standing in the hallway right now, *fuck*.

“Sometimes.” Suki holds up the edge of the blankets to reveal the dark, narrow gap that Sokka can probably just squeeze himself into. “Hide.”

“But Zuko—”

“You can’t be in here, Sokka.”

“But Zuko is—”

“Out in the hallways dressed as a guard where guards are supposed to be. Unlike you, who’s —”

The sudden sound of muffled voices has them both shutting up, Suki snapping toward the door as Sokka presses himself back against the wall.

“They don’t normally come in,” Suki mutters, carefully sitting back onto her cot. “If they just glance in the bars—”

There’s a sudden barked, “I *said* get out of the way,” followed by Zuko’s particular brand of snippy, “Well *I* don’t know what authority you think you have to go into a prisoner’s cell.”

In the stunned silence that follows Sokka has less than a single wild second to wonder if that shit is actually going to *work*. Then there’s an unmistakable scuffle of boots on stone, and then the incredibly distinctive sound of Zuko’s fist meeting someone’s face.

“*Fuck,”* Sokka hisses, dashing for the door and barely registering Suki’s frantic, “*Wait!”*

Sokka checks himself before he hits the door, pressing back so Suki can sidle up to the grate and assess the situation—“Only one guard, but a lot bigger. Zuko isn’t winning.”—before Sokka barrels into it. He darts on her signal back into the hallway, relying on the chaos as cover, and—fuck. Sokka can’t help, he immediately realizes with a cold wash of dread. He can’t take Zuko’s side, not without outing himself along with Zuko. Not unless they’re going to kill this guy, which obviously they aren’t, but even if they subdue him then means someone would *know*, and—

“Junior! Stop gawping like a toddler getting his first sight of a sun cake and help!”

“Sir!” Sokka barks, leaping forward and making a show of joining the fray. Except even with just making a show of it and not actually trying, Sokka quickly sees that his proximity is limiting Zuko’s effectiveness, reining in his unpredictable whirl of strikes and kicks because Sokka might be trying not to hurt Zuko but Zuko can’t take Sokka out, either.

Fuck everything, Sokka should have just hidden like Suki wanted and stayed away. Except they had no way to let Zuko know, he probably would have tried to bar the door regardless. Fuck this no planning thing. Not planning absolutely sucks.

“I’ll figure it out,” Sokka whispers, low and frantic as he makes a half-hearted, sloppy attempt to get Zuko into a bind that’s really about getting his lips close to Zuko’s unscarred ear. “I promise I’ll figure it out.”

“Sokka,” Zuko pants, tight and anxious, so low it's barely a breath as he wiggles in Sokka’s hold.

“I won’t let anything happen to you,” Sokka promises wildly. “I’ll do everything I can. But you can’t keep fighting.” Not if they don’t want more guards and even more of a scene and fuck, what if someone actually shows up with weapons instead of just restraints?

Zuko breaks easily out of Sokka’s hold, Sokka and the other guard backing up, Sokka to give him space and the other guard to flank him. Zuko hesitates, glancing between them, and Sokka can practically see the hypothetical scenario running over his face. Enemies on either side, a narrow hallway. It’s wider than a Ba Sing Se alley, but Sokka fully expects that Zuko will do the exact same thing he would do there, the exact same thing they joked about and practiced and discussed so many times.

And he does, darting for Sokka, trying to get past him to get all his enemies on one side. But Sokka is expecting it, and Zuko is expecting him to expect it, so it’s far easier than it should be—but still sloppy and flailing, because they still need to sell it—to trip Zuko up and catch him around the waist, to bring him down to the ground in a dramatic mess of squirming limbs and clamoring armor that miraculously doesn’t actually hurt either of them beyond knocking the breath out of Zuko.

Which probably has more to do with Zuko, really, than Sokka.

“You’re under arrest,” Sokka shouts, then softly as he makes a show of pulling Zuko’s wrists behind his back and hauling him to his feet as gently as he can without breaking his cover. “I will make this work. I *promise*.”

Zuko jerks his head, once, in something that could be taken for a nod, his jaw clenched and gaze fierce through his hair.

“Bring him to a holding cell,” the other guard says, striding forward to grab Zuko’s bicep in what has to be a bruising grip. “The Warden will want to know about this.”

Sokka nods sharply and makes a show of hustling Zuko along while his mind races. Spirits, being the one gripping Zuko’s wrists and directing his movements is a bit of a role reversal that Sokka can’t say he loves. But he’ll roll with it. He’ll make it work. They need to keep what cover they have left. Zuko can pass himself off as just some soldier who snapped, or some disgruntled family member of a prisoner or something. And Sokka—Sokka can come up with a plan. Zuko’s the one who’s done this before, Zuko’s the one who can just go from moment to moment and come out on top. Sokka needs something very different.

This is undoubtedly bad, but Sokka injects some confidence into his spine as he remembers that push comes to shove, Zuko is still a Fire Nation Prince. That has to matter, right? It’s not like there can be anyone here with the authority to harm one of Agni’s blood or whatever— right?

&#45;-

Zuko knows the Warden. Which maybe isn’t as relevant as the fact that the *Warden* knows *Zuko*. And they’re on a fucking *first name basis* because Zuko dated the Warden’s niece? And broke her heart? Like a *month* ago?

Zuko might not be so fine after all. Fuck.

&#45;-

It takes a long moment for Zuko to finally sit down on his honestly quite familiar cot when the steel door slams in his face.

Part of him is still frantically looking for balance after having his cover so spectacularly blown. Agni’s tits, but Zuko fucks up everything, doesn’t he? Mostly, though, he’s still feeling numb with shock that Makin isn’t sending for the Fire Lord.

Makin knows exactly who Zuko is and knows more than enough of Zuko’s standing in Court and of Zuko’s own action to know that Zuko is a traitor. And he still isn’t telling the Fire Lord Zuko’s here. Which means…something. Azula would be able to figure it out in a breath. Fuck, Azula wouldn’t have been dumb enough to get captured in the first place.

Is Makin waiting for the right moment? Covering up his lack of true access to the Fire Nation’s leaders? Contacting political allies first? Or is he pausing to exact some kind of revenge first? For breaking Mai’s heart—and Zuko has absolutely no idea what to do with that statement—or for being a traitor or fuck, maybe just for being a suddenly-punchable member of the family Makin’s worked his entire career for while never advancing beyond Warden of Boiling Rock.

Not that that’s a bad position. Not by any means. Zuko is acutely, keenly aware that on Boiling Rock, there’s no higher authority than the Warden’s judgment. And that there’s no love for those who undermine the Fire Nation to be found within these walls.

## Chapter 20: Into The Fire

### Notes

#### Chapter Notes

Warnings for a bit more than canon typical violence in this one

### Text

Zuko would characterize the current silence as…tense. There’s the hum of hundreds of bodies existing somewhere around them and the sound of Fire Nation regulation boots against metal flooring, which could almost be familiar enough to be comforting if it weren’t also accompanied by the sounds of Suki mopping. Which itself isn’t something Zuko is unfamiliar with, but she somehow manages to make the whole thing seem threatening, which…is a skill, he supposes.

Zuko had tried to offer an apology when they finally found themselves alone enough to not be overheard, but Suki had just looked at him like she was barely convincing herself to shove the mop into his hands instead of down his throat, so Zuko had clamped his mouth shut and decided he would circle back to that point after the rescue. Maybe after talking to Sokka, so Zuko can make sure he knows all that he might need to apologize for.

Zuko keeps a wary eye on Suki and bends his head to pretending he knows what he’s doing with a mop. He never actually learned what to do with one in Ba Sing Se beyond what he needed to know to make a production out of It, and watching Suki’s quick, efficient movements, he doesn’t exactly think she’ll appreciate learning that.

If only Katara traveled with a mop. Zuko would be an expert by now.

Zuko’s body remembers the rhythm of belligerently slopping water around faster than he expects, though, and as putting on a good show requires less and less of his attention, his focus shifts more and more toward his heat sense. It’s still fuzzy in the muggy, clinging air that lays thick across the lake, so much denser than Zuko is used to even compared to the stickiness of monsoon season at home.

But that disorienting mugginess means humidity, which means water in the air, and that’s basically just steam. And Zuko spent months and months getting to know steam, slipping out of kettles, dissipating into the air, shivering under someone’s breath—Zuko knows the way steam moves, the way it holds heat, the way he can thread his control around it, and he knows he can figure this out. He just needs to get a handle on the right way to grab hold of it when it’s all around him instead of discrete and defined like a teacup’s contents or a good solid fire.

“Heads up,” Suki suddenly murmurs, maintaining the appearance of total diligence while somehow signaling where Zuko should look purely through the direction of her mopping. Definitely skill.

Zuko glances up, tensing as he sees a guard approaching their out-of-the-way corner. Then his heat sense finds a familiar, discrete, defined almost-flame to wrap around and everything in him relaxes into sweeping relief. Zuko isn’t entirely prepared for how hard the sight of Sokka hits him, but Agni, he needed to see Sokka like this, moving smooth and easy and still in his uniform, still undiscovered, which means Sokka must have done okay for himself on his own last night

“Good,” Sokka says as he gets close, “You guys found each other.”

Zuko scratches the back of his neck, eyeing Suki, who just gives him a flat look. She very much found him this morning. And hauled him out of the general population before he could spark a prison fight over breakfast.

“Can you guys talk?” Sokka asks.

Zuko considers the half-lit hallway and intersecting corridors and stairways and Sokka’s guard uniform. “Turn your back.”

“Don’t look like you’re talking to us,” Suki adds.

“Are you okay?” Sokka asks as he obediently turns around, straightening when Zuko pointedly nudges him with his broom handle until he’s standing somewhat closer to regulation. Suki…somehow manages to mop with amusement.

“I’m fine,” Zuko says, belatedly getting back to his own water-sloshing.

“I’ve been here for months,” Suki says. “So, I’m great.”

“Great,” Sokka says, starting to look over his shoulder until Suki takes her turn to poke him back into place. “But what about the Warden—”

“It’s fine,” Zuko cuts in, glancing around to make sure they’re alone and then blowing out an exasperated breath when he sees that Sokka’s somehow managing to face forward in a very skeptical way. “But we should probably move fast,” he acknowledges.

“Well,” Sokka allows after a moment. “I guess that was the plan anyway.”

“And what *is* the plan?” Suki asks, her hazel eyes flicking between Sokka and Zuko with a reserve that Zuko’s pretty sure would make Sokka sad to see.

“It’s flexible, you know,” Sokka hedges, reaching up toward his helmet and then yanking his hand back down again. Zuko isn’t sure if Suki knows Sokka well enough to tell that he’s nervous, but it screams at Zuko in the way Sokka’s fingers are playing along his vambraces. “We wanted it to be adaptable, not too rigid because we didn’t—”

“Sokka,” Zuko interrupts quietly before Sokka’s rambling can really get legs, “It’s fine. Just say what you’re thinking.”

Sokka huffs, but after another moment of non-regulation fidgeting finally says, “I’m thinking that everyone’s so sure that they don’t have to worry about anyone escaping on the lake that they don’t really bother to watch it. So it’s actually a pretty open escape route if you think about it.”

Zuko hates to be the one to knock down an idea Sokka’s excited about, especially when Sokka’s been feeling so unsure of himself—he’s more than a little surprised by just for far his inner flame drops in relief to hear Sokka suggesting ideas again—but… “They don’t watch it because it’s literally boiling.”

“So, yeah, big hurdle.”

“They do a demo, for new prisoners,” Suki says after a beat. “The water lights wood on fire.” That…sounds pretty awesome, actually, under different circumstances. “Any craft on that wouldn’t last more than a minute.”

“Okay,” Sokka says doggedly. “But what if the heat wasn’t an issue?”

Suki gives the back of Sokka’s head an incredulous look. “What if the Boiling Rock wasn’t boiling, you mean?”

Zuko turns his mop in his hands, hesitating. “I could bend, but…” But they’d still need a craft, and it would need to be big enough for three. And the lake is large, so Zuko would have to lower the temperature of the water in a localized, constantly shifting area, because they would be moving *and* the water would be moving. Which would require so much focus and precision control that trying to lower the temperate of the entire body of water suddenly seems much more appealing, even though it would probably burn out his fire sense before they’re even halfway across, and…

And Zuko would really prefer this to not be the main plan.

“And that’s a great backup plan to have,” Sokka says, which has Zuko nearly sagging with relief. Zuko bending as a desperate last resort? Much more comfortable.

“Which means the main one is..?” Suki prompts.

“Coolers.”

Zuko blinks at Sokka’s back, sharing a quick, confused glance with Suki. “…You know they won’t stay cold in the water.”

“But they *will* stay insulated,” Sokka says, his grin audible, and Zuko blinks again because… they would, actually. And Zuko feels a lot more confident in his ability to control the temperate of metal, if he has to, than most other things.

“That’s ridiculous,” Suki is saying, looking intrigued despite herself. “How would you even get one onto the water?”

“Or off the building,” Zuko adds, because let’s not get ahead of themselves here, which… Zuko is not usually the one thinking.

“Into the water is easy,” Sokka says blithely. “There’s a blind spot with how the guard towers were built. We can ease it to the lakefront, and as long as we’re quiet it should be easy enough, especially with all that steam as cover.”

Suki is looking significantly more interested in the plan than Zuko expected her to be at this stage. “And off the building?”

Sokka’s hands are fidgeting at his vambraces again. “I’m still working on that,” he finally admits.

“What about rust?” Suki says, excited.

“What?” Sokka half turns around before Zuko can shove him forward again.

“Humidity, metal, close to the sea, there’s all this—”

“Forget the rust,” a sudden rumbling voice cuts in. “There are bolts on the inside.”

They all flinch, Sokka whirling around and Suki spinning with her mop at the ready, Zuko falling back into a bending stance, fire pooling in his fingertips. Fuck, it’s that prisoner for their first day, the big guy. Big and quiet and a firebender and in Boiling Rock and eavesdropping, any one of which on its own would be enough to make him really fucking dangerous.

“Who are you,” Sokka demands, reaching for some kind of authoritative tone and almost managing to hit it.

“That’s not the question, man,” the prisoner says, looming. “The question is who are *you*. Cause it sounds like you’re here plotting an escape.”

“You heard wrong, then,” Zuko says, low and dangerous.

“You heard right,” Suki cuts in, waving Sokka and Zuko back without even looking at them when they jerk toward her in shock, eyes fixed on the man as she lowers her mop. “You in?”

“Don’t ask dumb questions, Kyoshi,” the man rumbles.

“*Suki*,” Sokka whispers, outraged.

“It’s fine,” Suki says calmly. “Chit Sang’s cool. And besides, it’s better to have him in on it than trying to join in when we haven’t planned for it.”

“I would do that,” Chit Sang confirms, cracking his knuckles, fists nearly as big as Suki’s head.

“We didn’t *plan* for this,” Sokka hisses, and Zuko gives a decisive nod of agreement and doesn’t point out that they didn’t plan for anything. They’re planning now.

“So we got one more,” Suki shrugs. “Big deal.”

“I’ve got some buds, too.”

“So we got a few more. Coolers are big.”

“Of course you’ve got *buds*,” Sokka grumbles. “What, you and your ten closest friends?”

“Is that a problem for you, *Guard?”* Chit Sang asks, turning on Sokka with a scowl that has Zuko’s inner fire leaping under his skin. *“*Cause it seems like *you’re* here for *your* buds.”

“Guys,” Suki sighs, pinching the bridge of her nose and letting her mop-end drop, and Zuko sucks in a breath at the reminder of where they are and what this must look like, forcing himself to calm, because if this guy is getting worked up and Sokka is getting worked up then Zuko can’t be there with them.

“You know about the coolers?” Zuko asks, pitching his tone somewhere closer to businesslike than pissed and deliberately shifting his weight, pulling Chit Sang’s attention off Sokka as the other firebender reacts to Zuko’s still half-raised hands.

Chit Sang slowly narrows his eyes, eventually grunting something close to an affirmation.

“What’s the interior like?”

“Cold.”

Zuko gives him a flat look. If the man is joining, then the man is fucking *joining*.

Chit Sang grunts again, relenting. “Confined. I can’t stand. There’s enough room to sit cross-legged on the ground. But it’s all metal, so it's fucking *cold*. Gets right into your bones, right into your inner flame.” Zuko’s own fire quails in sympathy. “It’s made of separate pieces, but it's airtight. Bolted to the building, separate from the door. Eight bolts along the frame. Big ones.”

“Big enough to undo with your hands?” Sokka asks, and Zuko’s relieved that he seems to be still in planning mode and willing to at least entertain working with Chit Sang despite the suddenness of the addition, since they didn’t exactly have a choice in

“Not with how cold it is. Need a wrench for sure. Motor control goes first.”

“So we need to get someone inside with a wrench,” Zuko says slowly, looking around the four of them and taking another bracing breath. He…can see where this is going to go.

“I can get us a wrench,” Sokka says, brow furrowed in thought. “I saw some maintenance closets yesterday.”

“Perfect,” Suki says. “And Chit Sang can get Zuko inside.”

“No,” Sokka says immediately, startling Zuko with his vehemence. “*Fuck* no,” he adds, taking a step back from Suki, looking at her like she’s just suggested shoving Zuko into the lake, which…Zuko doesn’t understand. Who else would it be?

“Sokka,” Suki says, tone chiding, clearly confused and striving for a reasonable tone. “Chit Sang is too big, there’s no way he can unbolt it from the inside and not have it fall.”

Sokka’s scowl is fierce. “Voluntarily going in there—"

“Someone’s going to need to, though,” Zuko points out before Sokka can get any more worked up, forcing himself to stay steady when Sokka jerks to look at him like he’s the one suddenly being unreasonable, forcing himself not to react to the tightness he can see creeping into Suki’s frame or the suspicion crawling over Chit Sang’s face. “And I can do it.”

“But your inner flame—”

“Will be fine,” Zuko says, putting every bit of confidence he feels into the assertion.

“But—”

“I’ve done worse, Sokka,” Zuko reminds him, hating the way that makes Sokka flinch but also unwilling to back off this point. “It’ll be fine.”

Sokka opens and closes his mouth a few times, throat silently working, dissatisfaction slowly settling into every line of his body, what he wants so clearly at odds with what he knows needs to be done. Zuko is familiar with that feeling.

“Kid,” Chit Sang suddenly says in a surprisingly understanding tone. “You want to keep your friend a bit safer for a degree or two? Or you want to get all your friends permanently out of danger?”

“We don’t even know if it will work,” Sokka grumbles. “I can do more research, at least. Let me double-check a few things, and—”

“We don’t need more research,” Zuko interrupts, firm but as gentle as he can make himself. “We can’t know everything and it’s a decent plan. We can make this work if everyone is part of it, but we can’t hold people back.” Sokka finally looks up at that, blue eyes openly distraught behind his helmet. “Sokka, we can work out the rest as we go,” Zuko adds, reaching for the one thing he knows Sokka can’t argue with, “But we don’t have time for anything else. And doing this together means together, right?”

Sokka’s fingers go white-knuckled around his forearm, but after a long moment he sighs, nodding, shoulders slumping.

Suki lets out a breath and Chit Sang makes some kind of rumbling noise of agreement. “Good,” he grunts, turning back to Zuko. “What’s your name again, kid?”

Zuko gives the man a once over, entirely cognizant of the fact that as a traitor to his blood, Zuko’s almost guaranteed to be hated by any given prisoner he encounters, either for betraying the Fire Nation, for betraying his family, or for being part of his family in the first place. “I’ll tell you on the other side.”

Chit Sang considers a moment, then nods once, firm. “Deal.”

&#45;-

Sokka’s nerves are humming. He’s somewhere between battle calm and jumpy as he forces himself to keep his pace casual, his hands loose, his glances around as he looks for Suki relaxed. The wrench is a hard line against his lower back, biting into his skin beneath his uniform and forcing him to a regulation-correct posture that Zuko would probably be proud of.

There’s absolutely no reason for Prison Guard Wang to have the wrench, and absolutely no reason for anyone to suspect he *does* have it. As long as Sokka stays relaxed.

“You have it?”

Sokka barely holds in a shriek, turning his full-body flinch into a dramatic coughing fit as he just manages to stop himself from whirling around. “Spirits, Suki,” he mutters, glancing around from the cover of his helmet before making a show of finding a nice lookout post for himself above the prison yard. “Give a guy some warning.”

“You’re fine,” she says, eye roll audible, coming up from behind with her bucket and mop in hand, taking up position on the stairs just below him. “Run into any trouble?”

“None,” Sokka says. At least if you don’t count this. “The target has been acquired.”

Suki gives an infinitesimal nod, angling herself toward it. “Drop it.”

“I’m not going to drop a wrench on the metal floor,” Sokka says, hoping his tone suitably conveys the incredulous glance he can’t shoot her. Why not just throw it across the prison yard while he’s at it?

“I’ve got it,” Suki says, suddenly mopping pointedly right behind him. and Sokka has no idea how she thinks she’s going to maintain the picture of diligent work while catching a falling wrench, but if she’s sure…

“Get ready,” Sokka warns, folding his hands behind his back as he scans for any watchers. He sucks in his gut and shimmies a little, pressing the wrench up out of his waistband and then down from under his belt, holding his breath as he wills himself to let go. He tenses in anticipation of Suki’s sudden lunge behind him or of a resounding crash, all the air leaving him in a rush when instead there’s just the muffled thunk of the wrench falling into the thick cloth end of Suki's mop.

“Perfect,” she murmurs, pulling the mop back and making a show of bending to wring it out and pick debris from the loose ends. Sokka tracks the wrench out of the corner of his eye as she tucks it away into her loose prison clothes, the dull metal barely visible behind the shield of her body and certainly not to anyone from the yard.

It’s a smooth transfer, nearly seamless, and with it, the hardest part of this plan to get Zuko in position is behind them. Sokka should be feeling nothing but relief, nothing but the beginning-to-run-downhill gathering of momentum that comes with the end in sight. But Spirits, he would almost prefer it to be more difficult, almost wishes for some legitimate reason to step back and reassess and try another way, because this part done means they’re one step closer to sending Zuko alone into the cold and hoping he comes out okay on the other side.

“Sokka,” Suki says, her mop briefly hitching. “You okay?”

“Yeah,” he says quickly, forcing himself to tear his eyes away from where the wrench disappeared under her clothes and look back to the yard. “Yeah.”

A long pause, then, “If you have concerns…”

“It’s fine,” Sokka says, aware he sounds distinctly less than fine about it. “It’s the plan and we all agreed to it,” he adds, trying to firm up his voice and hiding a wince when Suki’s silence turns distinctly skeptical.

“…You didn’t want Zuko to do this,” Suki finally says, shooting him a quick glance under the cover of repositioning her bucket.

Sokka can only grunt in response. He absolutely doesn’t want Zuko to do this.

“Do you not trust him to do it?”

“What?” Sokka says, his tight worry momentarily loosening under a bolt of surprise. “Of course I trust him.”

“I don’t mean whether you trust him as a person,” Suki says, shaking her head as she wrings out her mop. “I mean whether you trust him to do *this*. You’re nervous. Is it because you aren’t sure he can do it? If you have doubts, we need to know while we still have time to adjust.”

“It’s nothing like that,” Sokka protests, forcefully smoothing out his frown before realizing that actually, frowning is probably one of the less notable expressions a prison guard can make. “Zuko’s one of the most capable people I know. He can do this.” Spirits, Zuko can do just about anything he decides he wants to, as far as Sokka can tell.

“Then what’s the concern,” Suki probes, risking another assessing glance. “Why were you trying to hold him out of it?”

Sokka sighs. Didn’t they decide they were setting this aside for later? He knows that was last night, but Spirits, is now really the time? “I just don’t like him being at risk, okay? It’s not about what he can do.”

“We’re all at risk here,” she says quietly.

“I know,” Sokka says, wincing. He’s more than aware of that fact right now.

“If you know that then why are you only trying to hold him back?”

Sokka stares blankly out over the yard, unsure of where to even begin. It’s not like he *wants* to risk Suki instead. It’s not like Sokka doesn’t know that Zuko can handle himself. It’s just that Sokka can’t help the way his stomach is tying itself into knots over the idea of sending Zuko into danger and not being able to be by his side for it, and what words can he give to Suki of all people when all his mind seems able to offer up is ‘I just want him to be safe *more*.’

“Are you trying to prove yourself?” Suki finally asks, a frown in her voice, her eyes set with misgiving when Sokka risks a glance. “If he’s saying you need to do that—”

“He isn’t,” Sokka cuts in, shaking his head. “I’m trying to fix a mistake, alright? I just...need to set this right, and know that things can be okay even if—even if they don’t always seem that way. And Zuko doesn’t have to be here, and he is anyway because he’s *helping* me. Not because he’s pushing me into something.”

"...Really."

"Yes, *really*," Sokka says, annoyed.

“Want to know what I see?” She doesn’t wait for him to continue. “You here, by yourself without your team, trying to make what seems like a really big gesture that whoever it’s for better really fucking appreciate.”

Sokka sputters, trying to find his voice, finally managing to push out, "Zuko's here,' and distantly aware that that was probably the least relevant part of her sentence. He’s not—this isn’t a *gesture*. It’s not about doing this for appreciation or recognition or whatever she’s trying to say. It’s about taking action and righting wrongs that never should have happened in the first place.

…Right?

“One person, then, when I know you have a whole lot of others,” Suki says, her mopping going distinctly sharp. “There’s strength in numbers. You know that, I *know* you know that. But you came here with just him, and now you’re trying to not involve him. So I’m just trying to figure out what’s going on.” Another quick, slashing look. “We can’t afford surprises here, Sokka.”

“It’s not that I doubt him,” Sokka finally says, forcing himself to stop fiddling with his vambrace and press his fingers flat against the railing. “I just want him to be okay. And I know I can’t make it happen, and I’m not going to try to keep him out of things, but I still—I can’t just stop feeling that. It's still there."

Suki makes an *ah-ha* noise like Sokka just said something particularly profound, pausing in her mopping long enough to study his face before nodding, her shoulders slowly relaxing. “Alright. I get that. You could have just spelled it out, though,” she adds, a bit of exasperation back in her voice. "There's no need to be so dodgy about it."

Sokka blinks, suddenly feeling like she’s stepped into a whole new conversation and didn't bring him along with her. “Spelled what out?”

“That you have confidence in your boyfriend but still don’t want him taking risks, which doesn’t mean you won’t support him when he does.”

…Did Sokka just say that?

“...Sokka,” she says, the suspicion sliding back into her voice when he doesn’t reply, the mop end suddenly poking him solidly in the back again. “That's it, right?" Another poke. "Is that *not* it?”

“No that’s—he’s just—we haven’t—” Spirits, Sokka can hear himself fumbling this. “We *were* together, but then there was this break, and we didn't really talk about it and then we did, and…it’s complicated,” Sokka finishes lamely.

“It’s not that hard,” Suki says, voice edging toward incredulous. “He either is or he isn’t.”

“It’s not that simple,” Sokka pushes back, resisting the urge to squirm. Is ‘boyfriend’ really what Zuko is to him? What Sokka wants Zuko to be? Was a boyfriend what Hahn was to Yue? What Jet tried to be to Katara, and fuck, to Sokka too? And if so, how can that possibly be right for what Sokka wants to be for Zuko?

“Fin and tooth,” Suki mutters to herself, before louder, “What’s so complicated about it? You care about him? You look out for him? You want to spend time with him?”

“Yes,” Sokka says, shifting uncertainly. All of that and more, so much that he doesn’t understand how it isn’t obvious to anyone who looks at him.

“And he does the same for you? Feels the same way about you?”

“Yeah…”

“Well fuck, then, Sokka, what more do you need?” Suki huffs, slapping her mop against the floor “A signed letter?”

Sokka…might actually have one of those already.

“It sounds like you’re doing it all already,” Suki continues, shaking her head. “I don’t see what’s so complicated about it except for you refusing to call it what it is.”

“It’s--”

“Nope,” Suki cuts in, tone going suddenly brisk as she grabs up her bucket and somehow manages to brandish the mop at him without ever losing the deferential prisoner-tilt of her head. “Absolutely not. I am not getting dragged into whatever this is. He volunteered to break into his own maximum-security prison for you and you trusted him enough to think it was a good idea. That’s all I need to know, and if you need more you can figure that out yourself.”

She turns on her heel and strides away without waiting for a reply, and Sokka can only gape after her, his mind still uselessly trying to reach for some response he’s far too late to give, anyway.

Sokka finally drags his eyes forward again, staring blankly out over the prison yard like her words aren’t looping over and over again through his brain, strong and firm and somehow nothing that makes sense. She makes it sound so easy, so straightforward, just a set of actions and behaviors. But Spirits, it feels so intangible and undefined in Sokka’s head. He can barely wrap his mind around it, even with her exasperated, confused words to give it shape.

Sokka has seen fathers and mothers. He knows how they act, knows what that means. And he’s seen siblings and children, friends and comrades. But boyfriends…fuck, Sokka barely remembers husband and wife, beyond a fading set of didn’t-pay-enough-attention-when-he-had-the-chance memories: entire conversations in a glance, hands that always came to rest on a lower back, two bodies that always knew where they were in relation to the other. And whenever Sokka tries to stretch his mind back, tries to grasp for more, he remembers Hakoda’s grief far more than he’s ever been able to remember what Hakoda was grieving. And that loss, that space, that absence—it’s had six years now to grow and change, six years to become something different than it ever was before, something far different than what used to live and breathe there.

Sokka feels like he’s reaching without any idea what he’s reaching for, except that he wants *more—*more than he has with Zuko now, more than he had with Zuko before. More of Zuko’s quirked smiles and dry humor, more cups of tea and teasing glances, more of Zuko’s shoulders loose as he sits with Toph and more of Zuko focused and confident as he sets himself to a problem, more of Zuko comfortable in his own skin, just—everything that Zuko could ever want and everything he would never even think to ask for, Sokka wants him to have more.

Could it really be as simple as all that? Not the amorphous *thing* Sokka aches to remember, but as easy and right and natural as Suki made it out to be? Trust and care and the awareness that Sokka would spend every day staring at Zuko if he could and still end it marveling at every part of him. Nothing Sokka needs to claw for and leap at and strain to reach, but something already there, already all around him, waiting for Sokka to pick his head up and realize.

&#45;-

“Incoming,” Suki murmurs, barely audible and just enough warning for Zuko to shift, casually angling into a pool of shadow and dropping his hand down to palm the wrench she drops into it as she strides by. It’s easy enough from there to tuck the wrench into the hem of his loose shirt, safely hidden until Zuko can find a more private moment to secure it more effectively against whatever the guards might do when they haul him in.

Zuko expects Suki to keep going—her part of the plan is done, now—so his inner fire flares with alarm when she only takes a few steps before abruptly turning back, eyes fixed on him with clear intent.

“What’s wrong?” He demands, shoving his heat sense out when she doesn’t immediately reply, pushing through the fuzziness of the humid air and looking for bodies, for threats, for anything that feels out of the ordinary, trying to focus past the fact that everything here feels strange and too loud against his bending.

“Tell me something,” she finally says, lips pursed as she eyes him. “Do you care about Sokka?”

Zuko blinks, most of his focus tangled in trying to sort out the dizzying rush of sensation pressing against his heat sense. What..? “Of course.”

“Do you try to protect him? And help him when he needs it?”

Oh. This. Zuko’s inner flame eases back, his heat sense sliding back beneath his skin as he transfers as much of his attention to her as it’s safe to give. “I do my best,” Zuko says, aiming for as much honesty as he can give her, too. She’s important to Sokka, and Zuko doesn’t want another of Sokka’s people at odds with Sokka because of Zuko.

“And you like him? Spending time with him? Not just the exciting stuff but the quiet stuff, too?”

“I always want to spend time with him,” Zuko says, not sure what else he can say. Around the others, when it’s just the two, when they’re busy, when there’s nothing to do but be in each other’s space—Zuko can’t think of many things that aren’t made better by Sokka’s presence.

“…Good,” Suki says, giving him a crisp, decisive nod before turning on her heel and striding off as if she never paused in the first place.

Zuko blinks, staring after her, then shrugs. If that’s all Suki needs then Zuko certainly isn’t going to complain about it. That was definitely easier than Katara.

&#45;-

Sokka has faith in the plan. He does. It might be a bit of a jumble of knowledge and insight and burst-of-inspiration inference right now, but it’s coming together surprisingly well—no, not surprisingly well. *Expectedly* well. Because Sokka can do this. He’s the Plans Guy, this is what he does. And Sokka will *make* it come together, and make it even better by the time they’re ready to execute, because this just-winging-it thing? This Zuko-style jump-in and figure out how to get out after?

It was one thing when Zuko was at Sokka’s side, was Sokka’s partner in this, an equal actor, someone who’s done it before. But now that Zuko might need rescuing too? Now that they’re purposefully sending Zuko into the cooler, after Sokka *just* heard him talk about the unique horror of feeling like his inner flame was gone?

Sokka is absolutely, categorically unwilling to have ‘bust in, bust out’ be all he has to work off of anymore.

For all his faith in it though, this plan scares the shit out of Sokka. It needs to be done, Sokka wasn’t lying to Suki when he said he knows that. But Spirits, he hates every single bit of it, and all he can do in the face of his fear and anxiety and impotence is plan—what they’re going to do if Zuko gets the bolts free and what they’ll do if he doesn’t, how to account for the wild card that is the Warden, how to take advantage of the surprisingly-not-as-much-of-a-wild-card-as-Sokka-expected that is Chit Sang. And most importantly right now, how to be here for Zuko, as much as Sokka can be considering that this part of the plan is entirely Zuko’s.

Sokka has no idea how staffing works around here, not like Zuko does, but Zuko said no one would be eager to mind the coolers, and it turns out it’s easy enough for Sokka to finagle his way onto a post right around when Zuko is supposed to be brought in. Even expecting him, though, it takes a scary amount of work for Sokka to muster a convincing scowl when Zuko is badgerfrog marched past, seemingly unharmed but with a truly spectacular glare fixed on his face. Sokka can feel his own face trying to do something much more like looking distressed as he watches Zuko get tossed unceremoniously into one of the cells, the door slammed solidly behind him as the other guards march away with a bare disgruntled head-nod for Sokka.

Sokka waits for the sounds of their boots to disappear before letting out the breath he’s been holding, allowing himself to sag back against the wall. They’re really in it now, then, the next piece falling into place.

Sokka had already pitched immediately letting Zuko out once the coast was clear—

“I’ll be right there! I can just—Who’s going to check?”

“The random patrols,” Suki said, arms crossed.

“Well, who’s going to know he’s supposed to be there!”

“Anyone who reads the logbooks,” Chut Sang rumbled, mirroring her stance.

—and been resoundingly shut down. Which makes sense, Sokka gets it, the level of risk if anyone came by would be huge, and that risk is even more real considering who Zuko is. Sokka *does* get it. But it means that not it’s just a waiting game, which just—ugh.

Sokka scrubs his hands over his face, then shoves off the wall and puts his shoulders back and stiffens his spine into as regulation-correct a posture as he can make it, and fixes his eyes on the sundial. He tracks every inch the shadows move, his internal clock ticking down each minute he has to wait, his mind cycling through plans and counterplans for the escape and for after and after that too—anything to keep him where he’s supposed to be instead of breaking for Zuko’s cell like he knows he can’t, no matter how much he wants to.

&#45;-

The very second it's allowable, Sokka is rushing to the cooler door to get Zuko the fuck out. He’s alone, he’s memorized the patrols by now, and fuck waiting a moment longer. Even in his urgency, though, Sokka can’t stop himself from instinctively yanking his hand away when he touches the door handle, the sudden shock of dry cold biting through the metal, sticking to his damp skin. It’s jarring and sharp in the thick heat and Spirits, that’s just the ambient cold through the door…Fuck. *Fuck*

Sokka braces himself to find Zuko nearly insensate or huddled and cringing like the last guy Sokka saw hauled out of here an hour ago, and yanks open the door. He sucks in a breath as the light sweeps in to reveal Zuko curled over himself, legs crossed and knees tucked up, arms folded in the hollow between his chest and his knees, forehead pressed down. Trying to hold in heat. Sokka knows that pose, he taught it himself to all the little kids in the South as the kind of emergency measure to take if they ever got trapped out on the ice by themselves. It’s so your breath can heat the space and you aren’t sucking cold air into your lungs. It’s an emergency pose, an oh-shit pose, a no-more-hope-in-trying-to-get-out pose, and—

Zuko glances up, gold eyes gleaming between the fall of his hair. And then he smirks— *smirks—*and exhales a fucking curl of *fire*, the heat of it brushing against Sokka’s cold-prickled skin. It’s wholly unexpected and fucking *smug* and such a relief that Sokka could nearly laugh from it, if it wasn’t honestly also a little too sexy for the circumstances. Especially as Zuko uncurls, barely even stiff, to show off the collection of bolts wrapped up in the bottom of his shirt, the hem raised enough to reveal a swathe of skin and abs and hip bones, and Zuko looking up at him the whole time with the most self-satisfied expression Sokka’s ever seen on him that didn’t involve Zuko sinking to his knees first.

“Most firebenders don’t learn about heat,” Zuko says, sparks flickering over the words, rasping and low and sounding savagely pleased with himself.

Sokka lets out a choked noise, sagging back against the doorframe as he’s suddenly slammed square in the chest with relief and giddiness and Spirits, *Zuko.* Sokka’s been tying himself into knots worry and the suicidal idiot isn’t even *bothered*, and fuck, Sokka—Sokka doesn’t even know what he’s doing until he’s doing it, reaching down with nothing but urgency and the shaky aftereffects of unrealized fear to haul Zuko up and into a kiss that’s all clumsy surprise and gasping breaths and then melting heat and eagerness and smoke and spice.

“You did it,” Sokka mumbles against Zuko’s lips, “Fuck, you’re unbelievable.” The words spill out as he runs his hands through Zuko’s hair, *finally*. “I knew you could do it,” he says, pulling back just enough to search Zuko’s face, “But we’re *never* doing this again. Spirits, Zuko.” He tugs Zuko in again, chest to chest to feel the strong, steady beat of his heart. “I’m out there losing my mind and you’re fucking *meditating*.” Zuko just offers a breathless little laugh in response, more air than sound, and Sokka just pulls him even closer, ignoring the hard press of bolts still caught up in Zuko’s shirt between them. “Fuck, I can’t believe you. You’re amazing. Incredible. Do you know that? Spirits, I love you, I don’t know how you even *exist*, the *things* you do, I can barely—”

Sokka bites off the rest of the words crowding to come out as Zuko suddenly plants a hand against his chest and shoves back, so hard that he nearly presses the air out of Sokka’s lungs. Sokka freezes, startled and unsure how to respond to Zuko’s sudden stillness, to the hand so warm and solid against Sokka’s chest but so firm in keeping him away as Zuko searches his face, gold eyes suddenly intent and searching and urgent in a way Sokka doesn’t wholly understand. Sure, okay, the kiss...kind of came out of nowhere. But it’s not like they haven’t been dancing around it! It's not like Zuko hasn’t been openly teasing Sokka. And he kissed Sokka back! And was soft against him, and melty, and that eagerness wasn’t wholly one-sided, and Sokka *knows* what it means when Zuko’s mouth tastes like campfire smoke like that, so why did that suddenly change, what the fuck did Sokka do or say or—

Wait. Did Sokka just—did he just—out loud?

Sokka can feel his expression slowly forming into something that must be close to dawning horror, judging by the way the cold is suddenly stinging at his too-wide eyes. Anxiety twists hard and deep in his chest at the rush of icy air between them as Zuko still just stares. Sprits, fuck, *fuck,* Sokka can’t believe he just—what kind of person just blurts something like that out? At a time like this? Out of fucking nowhere? After saying he needed *space*?

“You have,” Zuko finally rasps, “Terrible timing.” Which are *not* the words Sokka would normally want to hear, except…Zuko’s looking breathless, and that intent urgency is giving way to something that looks—that looks *delighted*. And the hand on Sokka’s chest is no longer pressing away, it’s stroking and then twisting and grabbing and finding purchase to yank Sokka into another kiss.

Sokka swallows hard when they finally break for air, gasping and feeling himself flushed and weak-kneed and unable to be anything else when he’s taking in Zuko’s clear happiness from only inches away, when Zuko’s hands are finally on him again and Zuko’s taste is lingering on his lips. And Spirits*,* from this close Sokka can tell that Zuko’s fire is up, can see it in the almost-lightning-drunk look in his eyes, can feel it in the way Zuko’s heat is sliding across his skin, his own pulse leaping in answer.

Spirits, how could Sokka have ever thought that he didn’t need—that he needed *space* from —this?

Sokka abruptly shifts his grip, grabbing Zuko’s forearm and hauling him out of the cooler and down the hall, glancing around for any out-of-rotation guards and rapidly running through the layout of hallways and rooms and dark corners he’s scouted out for something that will work. And Spirits, Zuko’s fire is *really* up, because he’s fully crowding up behind Sokka, breathing heat down the back of his neck, making it nearly impossible for Sokka to find the voice to finally, belatedly say, “What do you want? Candles and rose petals?”

Zuko breathes out a laugh, letting himself get pulled into a supply closet—Sokka’s willing to thank any Spirit listening for one so close—one hand still holding the bolts and wrench gathered up in his shirt, which is good. At least they’re both paying half a bit of attention. Maybe between the two of them, that can count for one fully aware individual, because Sokka doesn’t feel like he can think of much beyond this right now.

“You’re okay,” Sokka says, not sure if he’s asking or stating and either way not waiting for Zuko to respond before he starts checking for injury.

“I’m fine,” Zuko murmurs as Sokka grabs Zuko’s fingers to examine his extremities like he would for someone stuck on the tundra, then presses the tip of his nose. That seems to greatly amuse Zuko, which…is good. Humor is good. Especially the way it lingers in the lines of Zuko’s body as Sokka runs his hands down Zuko’s neck and torso, crouching to press against Zuko’s toes in those thin prisoner’s slippers.

“I’m great,” Zuko says, wiggling his toes under Sokka’s hands. “The best. I promise.”

Sokka looks up at that, pausing as the clear truth in Zuko’s words settles like a gentle caress over the tangle of worry that’s been living in his chest for far too long. Sokka’s gaze lingers on the familiar stretch of skin between Zuko’s ill-fitting pants and upheld shirt, then on the playful quirk of Zuko’s lips, and then on molten gold eyes, fixed on his. Sokka holds that eye contact as he slowly straightens, rising off his knees, running his hands up Zuko’s calves and the backs of his legs as he goes, over his ass, and it’s definitely not a wellness check anymore and Zuko doesn’t seem to mind one bit, full out grinning as he presses forward into Sokka, hand heated as it traces the shape of Sokka around and beneath his armor.

Things are definitely moving in a direction *not* suited for a supply closet inside a maximum-security prison when the sound of heavy-booted footsteps suddenly registers, a crisp cadence moving down what must be an adjacent hallway but definitely in their direction. They both freeze, not even daring to breathe as they suddenly come back to where they are and who they’re supposed to be.

Guard Wang Fire is allowed to—supposed to—get Zuko out of his cell when Zuko’s punishment is complete. This particular method of prisoner retrieval would be…rather difficult to explain.

“We might need to start doubling up the nonbenders soon,” a voice says, becoming clearer as it approaches the intersection nearest them.

“We have space for a while yet,” a second voice replies, quelling. Okay, two of them. Hopefully just two. This is fine.

“Not if the political prisoners keep coming in like this.”

The other voice only offers a grunt as they—fuck, fuck, as they turn down the hallway that houses the coolers.

“War prisoners, sure, but adding another shipment of the political ones tomorrow afternoon too? That’s two weeks earlier than we expected.”

“We have space.”

“If Caldera is cleaning house…”

“We have space,” the second voice says, harsher, right outside the closet. Spirits. “That’s what matters. It’s not our place to judge guilt or innocence.”

“It’s our job to ensure they serve their sentence,” they finish with a chorus. “I know, I know,” the first adds on. “All that paperwork work for the transfers though? In a day? It’s going to be a madhouse.”

The footsteps begin to fade away as the pair must take another turn, and Sokka slowly, carefully, eases away from Zuko, trying to be as silent as possible when his pulse is suddenly racing for a whole different reason than a few seconds ago. Zuko is near vibrating enough for Sokka to feel even without touching him anymore, his eyes bright with excitement as he catches Sokka’s gaze, his face mirroring the intensity Sokka can feel settling over his own expression.

The plan to escape is in full swing, the bolts still gathered in Zuko’s shirt clear evidence of that. But a shipment of war *and* political prisoners being transferred in? And the Chief of the Southern Water Tribe surely qualifying as both? Sokka can see the clear question on Zuko’s face, can feel it resonating through his own chest, and he doesn’t have an answer, but… maybe they aren’t entirely done here just yet.

&#45;-

Sokka stands on the rocky shore, careful not to let the steaming water actually brush his boots, and tries to convince himself that he believes what he’s saying. “We should go.”

“You don’t sound sure,” Zuko observes, glancing up from where he’s crouched far too close to that water for Sokka’s comfort, hand hovering like he’s thinking about touching it.

“We don’t know that my Dad is going to be there,” Sokka says, distantly wondering who exactly he’s trying to convince. “And if I had just cut our losses in the invasion in the first place then maybe there wouldn’t be such a mess now to try to undo. If I hadn’t tried to do it all on such a big gamble…”

“Was that really the problem?” Suki frowns, stepping back from where the cooler is slowly beginning to move with the water as they ease it off the gravel beach. “Trying?”

“No one can succeed at everything, Sokka,” Zuko says, voice nearly pensive, and maybe a little bit sad. “Not forever. But if you’re too afraid of failing to even try in the first place…”

“I know,” Sokka sighs, shoving a hand through his hair and thoroughly destroying his topknot thing. “I know I can’t just do nothing because I’m afraid. But going would still be doing something, right?”

“Sure,” Zuko says easily, finally rising to his feet. “But are you going to constantly be thinking about what else you could've done instead?”

Sokka doesn’t know what to say to that, when the only answer resounding through his brain is yes. When he knows it’s the things that he chose not to do that still cut the deepest.

“Sokka, whatever we do, it’s together, okay?” Suki says, her words firm and hazel eyes direct. “We’re a team. We’ll help each other.”

“In together, out together,” Zuko echoes, like it’s all as simple as that and not the chaotic mess of nerves Sokka feels over needing to decide whether they stay in danger or not. But...maybe this is like all those other things Sokka thought were so complicated he could barely understand them, only to find out they really were just as simple as that in the end.

“Hey, how about you get *in* the boat together,” Chit Sang suddenly whisper-shouts, glaring from his spot in the cooler. “And then we can get *out* of the boat together on the other side. We don’t have all day here, kid.”

“You’re right,” Zuko says, eyes steady and even on Sokka’s face. “We don’t. You should go. We’re staying.”

“What?” Sokka says, shock giving him words again. “Zuko, I don’t want to drag you into something even more dangerous.” Zuko’s cover is already partway to being blown, and he has to know the risks, has to know them even more than Sokka does, but he’s just *shrugging* like it’s not a big deal that the cooler is shoving off the beach without them in it.

“I’ll drag you then,” Zuko says. “You were going to second guess this forever if we didn’t stay.”

That…is probably not entirely inaccurate. Still, “We’re going to have to come up with another plan to get out, now,” Sokka says faintly, watching the cooler already catching the current.

“We’re a resourceful bunch,” Suki says with surprising cheer considering her previous reserve around Zuko. Fuck, considering the fact that she probably knows the risks most of all of them. And...she still weighed them against the chance to leave this place and reunite with her Warriors and decided it was worth staying.

Spirits, Sokka…doesn’t know what he’s done in his life to deserve people like this in it. “This might be really dumb,” he finally says, wondering if he should be feeling guilt or concern or upset, because the thing bubbling up in his chest is definitely yet another hit of giddy relief.

Zuko hums, shrugging. “It’s only dumb if it doesn’t work.”

“If it does then you’re just daring and brilliant,” Suki tacks on with a sharp smile, and Sokka…supposes that daring and brilliant is what they’re aiming for, then. And Zuko is already daring, and Suki is already brilliant, and Sokka...is something in all that mix. Something they both feel comfortable relying on.

So maybe this isn’t actually quite so crazy after all.

&#45;-

Sokka’s father—it has to be him, Zuko doesn’t know if Sokka would light up like that for anyone else stepping off the gondola—is shorter than Zuko expected. Maybe of a height with Zuko himself, or a few inches taller. But he’s broader, clearly strong, straight-backed and hard-faced and sharp even as he blinks in the sudden sunlight in a way that makes Zuko think Sokka takes after his mother.

Sokka is so clearly delighted, grinning in a way a guard probably shouldn’t, and Zuko’s inner fire is looping and curling to see it. Sokka is standing with purpose in the line of his shoulders and self-assurance back in his step, and Zuko can’t get over just how much that was missing in the Temple now that he’s seeing it again.

Though some of that feeling might also be because of the overwhelming, hugely inappropriately timed delight trying to burst through Zuko’s chest. Sokka *kissed* him, and then said that he—Agni’s balls, Zuko can’t even think it without feeling light-headed, his inner fire fluttering uselessly through his veins.

And because looking love-struck in the middle of a prison yard is a bit of an attention grabber, Zuko just—can’t think about it. Even though he’s still staring at Sokka, at the way he’s animated and bright with his excitement even across the yard.

Agni, Zuko could stare at Sokka like this forever, if only sitting underneath Zuko’s sparking inner fire wasn’t an unmistakable thread of worry. Because things are working out between them getting back inside unnoticed and Sokka’s father actually being here, and Zuko can’t ignore the familiar hovering dread that his luck is about to run out. Or maybe it’s not his luck, maybe it’s just time that’s suddenly running away from them, because Chit Sang is almost certainly about to get interrogated, and Zuko doesn’t have any illusions about the method’s the Warden will use to get the information he’s after.

Zuko is uncomfortably aware that it wasn’t exactly *good* that Chit Sang got recaptured. Ethically, it’s great that the guards brought him in largely unharmed instead of just letting him die on the lake. It speaks to the Warden’s honor and integrity, which Zuko supposes he should feel good about given what Makin has hanging over Zuko’s head.

It’s just that now they have a ticking clock on a critical information leak. Suki might vouch for the guy, but Zuko’s painfully aware that no one knows how they’ll hold up under an interrogation until it's actually happening.

Zuko doesn’t quite think that Sokka realizes the circumstance they’re working in now, though he’s sure Sokka will figure it out once he steps back from his enthusiasm over his father to actually think about it. But Zuko can tell that Suki knows, and that she has her own internal countdown running as she glances up toward the sun and then around the yard and toward Sokka’s father, clearly wondering how this is going to go.

Zuko is sure that they’ll figure it out, but he can’t deny the tight, driving need beginning to settle along his bones to hurry. It feels like things are suddenly going right in his life, and Zuko knows that just means something even worse is waiting to crash down. Zuko doesn’t get good luck for long and he can’t have this run ending with them all still in Boiling Rock.

Though maybe Sokka has better luck, where Zuko doesn’t. Maybe Zuko can tag long on the back of his.

&#45;-

The grin Sokka is still biting back as he makes his way from Dad’s cell to Zuko’s dies a sudden, harsh death as he turns the corner to see Zuko already out of his cell. Which would normally be excellent, one thing they don’t have to figure out how to get done. Except Zuko is flanked by two stone-faced, hulking guards, each with a hand wrapped so hard around Zuko’s biceps that he’s rocking up onto his toes to try to relieve the pressure of it.

Sokka freezes, then forcefully shoves himself back into motion because a guard gawping at a prisoner being escorted somewhere, even roughly—especially roughly?—is a sure way to draw attention to himself. He tries to catch Zuko’s eyes as he walks by, but gold just flickers toward his face once, quick and shuttered, revealing absolutely nothing. Zuko’s face is set with pending anger and sullenness and a kind of unreadableness that Sokka didn’t realize that Zuko could even do. A kind of unreadableness that makes Sokka realize truly just how much of himself Zuko’s always shown to Sokka.

Okay. This is fine. Sokka will just…go to Suki. He’ll go to Suki, and he’ll tell her the plan, and also about Zuko, and it will be fine. It probably already is fine, it’s probably just…some routine prison thing that Suki can explain to him.

And maybe it’s something to do with the Warden, who may or may not personally hate Zuko, but…maybe not. And whatever it is, they’ll just adjust. The plan is flexible. Adaptable. They can make it work with whatever’s happening with Zuko. After all, the main plan hasn’t changed: in together, out together. There might be more people in that ‘together’ now, but that’s still exactly what they’re going to do.

&#45;-

Zuko doesn’t know what he expects to happen to him in this neat little room with its high barred windows that let in light and fresh air, and its thick wooden door instead of metal, and its two chairs and a table and a tray of food, and its nice rug that taken altogether say ‘honored guest’ far more than ‘prisoner.’

Actually, that’s a lie. Torture or poison. Zuko knows exactly what he’s expecting and its torture, distantly followed by some kind of poison that could be considered part of the torture. One of those that puts someone in a lot of pain without necessarily killing them, because Zuko might be thoroughly exiled now but he still knows the blood that runs in his veins. Makin would never have the right to be the one to kill him, not yet at least.

What Zuko absolutely isn’t expecting is Mai walking through the door. But she’s very clearly expecting him.

“…Fuck.”

“…Really, Zuko?” She stares at him, expression flat, before pointedly taking a seat and kicking out the remaining chair to clatter against Zuko’s legs. “Sit.”

Fuck, fuck, fuck. Zuko feels numb as he mechanically drops into the chair across from her, his mind unable to do anything but struggle with the fact that she’s *here*. Which means that Azula’s here, too. Which means…that Makin was, in fact, biding his time. *And* waiting to hear from his allies.

Zuko would wonder if the Fire Lord is aware of the Warden’s loyalties, or at least his willingness to share them, if he weren’t currently so occupied trying to fight down what feels uncomfortably close to panic. Agni’s flaming cock, is there ever a wild card in the mix now, one that shifts the balance of who has the right to do what entirely in the wrong direction.

Fuck. If the clock wasn’t ticking before, it definitely is now.

&#45;-

The plan might not be flexible enough. The plan might be a little less adaptable than Sokka and Dad thought it would need to be. Because Suki can’t see how they’re going to make it work for whatever is happening with Zuko, and neither can Sokka, and Spirits, if he could just get a little bit of *time* to figure this out.

“Hey, newbie! With us.”

“Uh, sure,” Sokka says, turning on his heel as if he were walking down the hallway the whole time and not coming out of Suki’s cell. “Why?”

“The Warden wants to see some people.”

…Fuck.

“Why’s that?” Sokka asks, feigning casualness.

The female guard shoots him an annoyed look. “I didn’t *ask*, newbie.”

“Right, right.” Sokka’s brain is racing. Maybe he can use this to his advantage—if they know where the Warden is, that will make him easier to capture. Except if they capture him then they need to escape, and Sokka still doesn’t know where Zuko is. But the Warden would know, right? “Does it have to be now? Like…right now?”

The male guard barks out a laugh. “It’s gotta be now, kid. Save your piss for later.”

“Right,” Sokka says faintly. “I’ll just…hold it.”

“Shouldn’t take long,” the guard says in consolation. “Something about a lineup and interrogating an attempted runner.” His eyes suddenly slash to Sokka’s face. “But you wouldn’t know anything about that, would you?”

Sokka gulps. “Nope. Nope. Definitely nothing about that. I mean. No more than what everyone knows of course. About. All of it.”

Fuck. Sokka snaps his mouth shut before he can manage to incriminate himself through sheer awkward rambling, and sets his mind to planning.

&#45;-

The almost-silence is such a physical thing that Zuko wonders, in a wild corner of his mind, if he should get up so it can have a seat at the table instead. Mai’s eyes are sharp and expressionless as she one by one, tiny dish by tiny dish, takes each plate off the heavy serving tray—Earth Kingdom make, his brain serves up, pre-Kyoshi. It must be the Warden’s—and sets it with a sharp, distinct *clack* onto the table.

One by one. Dish by dish.

Zuko tries to breathe calm into his inner flame as setting the table drag on, tries to contain his restlessness and the way he’s straining to hear anything out in the hallway, because she’ll see it and start wondering what it’s about when reasonably Zuko shouldn’t be focused on anything but her. And he *needs* to be wholly focused on her, on what’s in front of him, on whatever game she’s trying to play, not on desperately wondering where Azula could be and if she’s already tracked down Sokka.

*Clack. Clack. Clack.*

Zuko’s just on the verge of an offering to help bursting past his lips—he has lots of experience with serving trays after all—when finally Mai finishes. She sets the last small bowl down with a final little crack, adjusting its position after a moment so it’s perfectly in line with the others. Then she folds her hands—near her knives, of course—and pins him with her flattest stare. “A letter, Zuko.”

…Right. That. “…I didn’t want to just leave and not say anything.”

“So you decided to leave a *letter*?”

Zuko scowls down at the array of tiny little buns and cakes and rolls. “What else was I supposed to do?” What’s wrong with letters?

“How about tell me in person,” Mai says, incredulousness breaking through. “I thought we were—” She cuts herself off, turning her head sharply away.

*Broken heart*, Makin said, and Zuko wonders again what exactly Mai thought they were, wonders if she ever truly heard the ‘maybe never’ or just the ‘not now.’ “You would have tried to talk me out of it,” he finally says, instead of the ‘you would have told Azula’ that he’s thinking. Both are true.

“Damn right I would have tried to talk you out of it,” she snaps. “I don’t even need to know what ‘it’ is!”

Zuko feels like he’s hovering on a precipice, teetering on the edge between jumping out or stepping back onto sure ground. “Maybe you *should* know,” he finally says, low, inner fire coiling in his chest with readiness.
