Mai makes a noise of disgust. “I don’t want to be part of your *scheme*, Zuko. I’m not going to be some pawn between your family. I get more than enough of that from mine.”

Clearly, if the Warden reached out to her about capturing Zuko. Or to Azula? But that’s functionally the same thing, and that would be Mai’s primary value to the family, wouldn’t it? Unless Zuko manages to work his way back into the line of succession, of course.

He sighs, glancing away, inner fire turning over. Mai’s always hated the role she’s had to play. Fuck, she hates even being asked to play in the first place. But they both know she’s done it too well, has become too deeply entwined between the royal siblings, to have any hope of staying out of it. “I’m sorry.”

Her fingers rap the table, once, an outsized display of annoyance for her. “What are you even sorry for?”

“That things are going this way.” That Zuko did his best to leave her out of it and couldn’t even manage that.

“Not for what you’ve done?” Her tone makes it clear she already knows that answer, but Zuko still can’t quite meet her eyes.

“Not for that,” he admits. Even knowing it hurt her, he can’t regret it, not when it’s still in motion. Fuck, when it might have already been motion, far more than Zuko realized when he moved to force it along. And especially not when all his reasons for doing this are somehow inexplicably still hanging in balance, none of them shattered yet.

Mai sighs, slumping back in her chair, brooding at him from beneath her bangs. “You can’t come back from this, Zuko,” she finally says. “You aren’t leaving anything left.”

“I know,” Zuko says softly, folding his arms across his stomach because this…this is something he still can’t let himself think about too deeply without feeling it like a kick to the gut. He knew the consequences when he decided, but Agni, for so long ‘home’ was always something he knew he could find his way back to one way or another if he could just hang on long enough. But now…well, Zuko doesn’t think split loyalties are ever appreciated by a Fire Lord.

“Do you?” Mai’s eyes narrow in disbelief. “This isn’t going to be like last time.”

“I know,” Zuko repeats, harder now. He’s well aware of all the ways last time was different. He was fucking there for it, unlike Mai.

“You’re burning down your whole life with this,” she presses.

“Maybe,” Zuko snaps, “If it’s that easy to burn down, it isn’t worth letting stand in the first place.”

“Burning something down is easy when you can just walk away,” she says, eyes hard as obsidian. “The rest of us don’t have that luxury of getting to choose to be in or out.”

Zuko looks away, biting back all the words that want to rise up about the *luxury* of getting to betray his country. Because she isn’t wrong. Zuko isn’t the only one who’s going to feel this if it goes the way he hopes it will. The way he needs it to. Agni, Zuko *already* isn’t the only one.

“You won’t feel it,” Mai says as if reading his mind, voice getting tight. “But the rest of us will, and you don’t know what that’s—”

“You think I don’t *know*?” Zuko breaks in, feeling his scar pulling with the force of his scowl as he stares at her, stung. “You think I don’t know what it’s like to see your life turn to ash? You think I haven’t felt it before? That I won’t again?”

It’s Mai’s turn to avoid, her eyes lingering on the left side of his face before her gaze slashes away. She takes a deep breath after a moment, gathering herself. “Azula—”

“How many days until the comet?” Zuko cuts in again. Agni, he can’t just sit here and listen to what Azula thinks about the whole thing, to what she’s said about it. Not when in the end there’s really only one thing that matters to them both, and Azula’s always been the one to talk about doing what needs to be done. “How many,” he presses, when Mai just looks at him, silent.

She glances away, lips forming a tight line.

“You know what they’re going to do,” Zuko says, softer now in the face of her white-pressed lips. “She didn’t tell you, but you know, right?” Silence, again. “She isn’t telling you for a reason.”

“Don’t try to play mind games with me, Zuko,” Mai snaps, voice harsh. “It doesn’t suit you.”

“It’s not a game, Mai.” It’s never been a game. “I don’t want you to get hurt in this.”

She lets out a sharp, low bark of laughter. “Too late for that.”

Years too late, Zuko knows. Years and years since what could have been got wrecked against what needed to be done, what neither of them could avoid.

“Why did you come here, Zuko,” Mai finally asks, the words bitter and exhausted. “Why walk into Boiling Rock? What were you trying to do?”

Zuko keeps his mouth shut even as he knows his lack of answer will only make it worse, will only twist the knife of his distance deeper. But he can’t ignore the reality of Azula, of what his sister could do with even the smallest bits of information given what she already knows.

Mai finally snorts, glaring at the door before shifting in her chair to fully face the table. “I hope it’s going to be worth it,” she mutters, sounding disgusted as she straightens, suddenly looking nearly *prim* as she gives him her undivided attention.

Zuko blinks, inner fire flicking uncertainly at the underside of his skin, nearly sparking to life when a guard suddenly bursts through the door. The man half-leans into the room to try to catch Mai’s eye, not even looking at Zuko in his urgency—unbalanced. In the wide-open doorway. With no other guards in sight, and Zuko with a straight shot for the door, unchained despite the hardware bolted into the floor for that very purpose. And Mai…and Mai staring at him, ignoring the obvious disturbance, face expressionless but eyes expectant as she sits in the one chair that would force someone to step into the room to see both occupants.

Ah.

Zuko doesn’t pause to question or to reconsider if he’s actually seeing what he thinks he is. He just lunges, grabbing the antique tray Mai so helpfully cleared and swinging, pivoting from the hips to catch the flat-footed guard square in the chin with the heavy wood and sending the man’s head snapping backward. Zuko catches him as he falls, preventing a clatter of armor and weapons as he eases the man onto the floor, ensuring that he’s unconscious— Zuko’s vaguely surprised he didn’t need to even get his helmet off, but whiplash will do that to you—before glancing around to see if anyone else was drawn by the noise.

Mai is still sitting in her chair, one leg crossed, chin resting on her fist. She raises an eyebrow as they make eye contact, then neatly shoves a platter of steamed buns off the table to shatter against the floor, the sound echoing around the room and down the metal hallway in its startling delicacy.

Right. Time to go.

Zuko takes off down the hallway, focusing on speed and ignoring the sound of booted footsteps rushing toward the precise little crashes Mai is still making behind him. He’s fully aware that Mai could have stopped him—fuck, that she could have never allowed the opportunity in the first place—and shoves that knowledge away for later. He doesn’t have time to think about it or what it means and has no idea when he might. Fuck, it might not be until after the Comet, but it certainly isn’t going to be now when all Zuko can focus on is finding Sokka before Azula does.

&#45;-

Sokka doesn’t know why he bothers to be surprised that Chit Sang knows how to immediately and effectively start a riot. The man was able to leverage his own failed escape attempt to get back at his enemies within the ranks of the guards—clearly, this is someone who knows how to work a system. Which…is very useful to have on your side, as it turns out. Along with Suki’s sudden revelation that she can scale walls like a fucking tiger money. Spirits, she’s amazing. Sokka wonders how much of the Kyoshi Warrior outfit he’s going to have to put back on to get her to teach him that.

And Sokka is feeling good about that eventual possibility because they’re moving with a purpose now. All of them are grabbing weapons as they go, Chit Sang is picking up allies from the crowd, and Suki is casually and confidently directing the captive Warden with one hand on his bound wrists and the other using his gag like an ostrich horse bridle. Sokka briefly remembers exactly what he found so attractive about her in the first place, before the realities of sprinting through a prison toward their single means of escape rightfully dominate his thoughts again.

They run quick and surprisingly light-footed considering Chit Sang’s bulk and the Warden’s resistance, but between Sokka’s knowledge from walking the halls as a guard and Suki and Chit Sang’s experience mopping them as prisoners, they make good time across the complex. It’s honestly going better than Sokka expected, outside of one fairly major hitch that has him glancing down every crossroads and pausing at every cell door just in case.

Zuko isn’t here. Zuko isn’t *anywhere*, and Sokka is keenly aware that taking the Warden captive was seizing on a moment of opportunity that might not have presented itself again. They couldn’t pass it up, but Sokka was kind of hoping the riot would draw Zuko out or allow Zuko to escape, or fuck, that finding the Warden would mean finding Zuko. The fact that none of that happened…

Fuck. Sokka doesn’t have a plan for this, beyond the original one.

Suki gives him a quick glance as they hustle up a flight of stairs, Chit Sang cheerfully hauling the Warden by the belt. “Where’s—”

“I don’t know,” Sokka says, words tight.

Suki grunts. “Do we—”

“I’m not leaving him,” Sokka cuts in as they make the landing, feeling the stubborn set of his own jaw. It doesn’t matter what the question is, that’s the only answer Sokka can give. “In together, out together, right?”

“You better not be thinking you’ll stay behind to find him on your own,” Suki warns, which…might have been exactly what Sokka was thinking. But fine, he and Suki will stay. Sokka would *really* prefer not to need to, but he will put Dad—and Chit Sang, apparently— onto that gondola if he has to and trust that, worst comes to worst, the three of them can either fight their way out or go to ground and sneak until they can make their escape. It’s not like Sokka and Suki are important enough to the Fire Nation to really be worth expending a lot of effort to chase down, right? It’s not like anyone knows their connection to the Avatar.

And Zuko—Zuko is of Agni’s blood. And Sokka might think that’s more useless superstition than anything else, but he’s desperately telling himself right now that that kind of thing matters in the Fire Nation, and that it matters in a way that’s going to help.

Sokka is half-occupied trying to convince himself of that fact when an instantly familiar, jarringly unexpected voice suddenly chirping, “Oh, I’d *love* to see!” has him lunging forward to grab Dad before Hakoda can turn the next corner and throwing out his other arm to haul Suki back as she snarls in recognition.

“Save it for another time,” Sokka hisses, motioning for her to keep her hand pressed over the Warden’s mouth and ignoring his Dad’s and Chit Sang’s questioning looks as he frantically gestures for them all to tiptoe backward.

“Quietly,” he mouths, just to make sure they understand, before leading them back to a more circuitous but hopefully less enemy-filled route.

Fuck. If the pink girl is here, the rest of the trio must be around too, the knife one and Azula. Sokka has a terrible feeling that he knows exactly where Zuko got taken to.

&#45;-

Reaching the gondola platform happens suddenly and unexpectedly. They burst through what Sokka was sure was another interior door to fly out into bright light and open space and a platform full of startled guards. There’s a moment of stunned motionlessness all around, then the Warden is furiously yelling through his gag, trying to make clear what will happen if the guards don’t stop them right now, and Suki and Dad are shouting over top of the man, making it *much* clearer what will happen if the guards don’t put their hands in the air and back the fuck away *right* now.

One or two guards hesitantly raise their hands, more joining with increasing readiness when nothing immediately awful happens to the first few. Some part of Sokka is vaguely surprised that threatening the Warden is working so well against such a large group—maybe that says good things about the man’s leadership? Or yet another thing about Fire Nation power politics that Sokka doesn’t fully understand.

The larger part of Sokka is something closer to acutely anxious, though, because the closer and closer they get to their escape the closer they’re getting to the moment when Sokka’s going to need to dump his Dad and the others onto the gondola and break the lever so they can get away and stay behind and watch them go, because there’s still no sign of—

The entire platform flinches as two doors slam open, metal crashing against rock and steel-banded walls heralding Azula and Zuko’s arrival as they explode onto the platform from opposite directions. Sokka’s little party freezes at the sight—Sokka in relief, Dad probably in tense readiness, Suki and Chit Sang and Chit Sang’s friends in…Sokka doesn’t know what, actually. Shock, maybe, because that certainly seems to be the predominant reaction among the guards.

Azula raises an eyebrow as she rocks to a stop, her armor neat and red-painted lips pursed in annoyance. “Brother.”

Zuko narrows his eyes, scowling through his ragged hair as he skids in his thin slippers to stop his momentum. “Azula.”

“What a surprise to see you here,” she says, totally ignoring everyone else—including the Warden’s muffled screaming—in favor of returning her brother’s glare.

“I don’t want to fight you,” Zuko warns, and Sokka can see that he’s wound so tight he’s nearly vibrating with it, the wind whipping his prisoner’s clothes against his body.

Azula flicks her eyes around the platform, taking in the guards with their hands still in the air, the captive Warden, lingering on Suki. “You never do,” she finally says, her tawny eyes landing on Sokka.

A palpable ripple of ‘*oh shit’* flows through the guards, and Sokka barely has time to wonder what they’re all reacting to before both siblings erupt into identical lunging and blue and orange fire is blazing across the platform.

&#45;-

Zuko sends a wall of blue fire shooting upward off his tight, control block, narrowing his eyes against the heat and risking a glance to see that the guards have been motivated into action by the appearance of their Princess. Or maybe by the lack of throat-slitting of the Warden—Zuko could have told Sokka that that kind of thing only works if you sell the threat *and* if there isn’t someone with higher authority around to take the blame. Azula launching herself into the fight is as good as an order for the guards to join, too.

Zuko wishes Sokka had a bit more of a threat to balance that choice for the guards, though, because Zuko really doesn’t want to fight his sister and really does need to keep her away from the gondola that, given the way the others are fighting their way toward it, seems like their ride out of here. Sokka and Suki and Sokka’s father are holding off the guards while Chit Sang manhandles the Warden and seems generally threatening, some random prisoners Zuko can only assume are Chit Sang’s friends diverting the attacks of the firebenders arrayed against them.

And Zuko does his best to keep Azula contained and focused on him, diving and dodging and dancing to keep himself between her and the others without getting pinned or overly exposed. It’s basically a controlled retreat, which…well, there’s a reason firebending is primarily an offensive discipline. There’s a reason the Dragon of the West never retreated from Ba Sing Se while the enemy could still stand against him. A controlled retreat rarely stays controlled for long.

Azula’s face is tight, eyes blazing in a way Zuko’s rarely seen from her. Her ever-present smirk is closer to a snarl as they lunge and flip and kick and punch, bodies slicing through the air and twisting around flame and weaving between sheets of fire. They whip across the platform, darting from one side to the other and back again, and slowly, slowly, Zuko inches backward.

It’s like some awful game of Fire Nation army and Earth Kingdom rebels, except instead of slinging sand at each other and trying to gain ground before the tide comes in and it’s time for dinner, they’re jetting fire with such intensity across such close distances that the rest of the fighters have been steadily pushed more and more to the perimeter of the platform. No one with any sense would get between two firebenders in such close quarters, let alone two of Agni’s line set against each other.

The tight but open space is half-reminiscent of a formal duel, and Zuko knows he at least has far more experience there than Azula does. And more experience with battles in general, he suspects. He knows how to process the seething chaos around the perimeter without losing focus on the fire in his grip or the flames whipping across the ground toward him. And Zuko can use that experience, just like he can use the fact that he’s fighting with Sokka and Suki and the others while Azula is fighting on her own—the guards aren’t *with* her, even if Azula would ever let herself rely on them.

And where *is* Mai? Where’s Ty Lee? Zuko doesn’t have the focus to think about that either, but he knows those two have to be around somewhere. He can only assume that their glaring absence is in service of some purpose of Azula’s that Zuko can’t spend the mental energy figuring out and doesn’t want to stick around to experience, and Agni, they can’t have much time left before they make an appearance.

Which means that Zuko needs to capitalize on this brief, temporary window of having his people while Azula doesn’t have hers. So when Sokka slides into view on his blind side, which isn’t *entirely* blind, Zuko doesn’t hesitate. He breaks left on Azula’s next lunge instead of deflecting or ceding ground as he’s been doing, trusting Sokka to step forward in that space as Zuko throws out a block to cover where he *was* instead of where he is. Zuko covers enough ground to force Azula to turn to keep him in sight, Sokka’s sword swinging true enough to force her to briefly fight on two fronts, and together it’s just enough for Zuko to shift the plane of their duel, guards scattering back from suddenly newly-hazardous ground in a rush.

Sokka slips back before Azula can send more than an off-balance flick of fire his way, easily deflected off his blade, and then she’s whipping herself around to recover toward Zuko with barely a pause. But it’s enough of one for Zuko to dart to the side again, forcing her to pivot with him, both of them whirling and turning, fire breaking around and skimming past each other, all so instantly that it could be choreographed, an almost-dance ending with Azula flanked between Zuko and Sokka, hemmed in by threats instead of surrounded by support, the guards too wary to approach Zuko when flames are dancing around his feet.

Azula pauses, raising an eyebrow, eyes flicking around the platform to take in the new lay of the land. “Careful, Brother,” she says with a moue of annoyance as she brushes a strand of hair out of her face. “You might impress someone like that.”

Then she thrusts the heels of both hands out wide, blue flame exploding outward in all directions to send everyone except Zuko scrambling for the perimeter as a blur of pink bounds forward into the gap. The guards surge back a beat later and Zuko nearly skids kicking out a rippling lash of flame to capture Azula’s attention again as Ty Lee slams into the other escapees like a particularly bounce hurricane.

&#45;-

“Shit,” Sokka mutters as he pops back to his feet, the too-dry feeling of the skin closest to Azula’s flames almost immediately dissipating as clinging humidity and sweat beads the back of his neck again.

“What is it,” Hakoda asks, slightly breathless as he beats back a less-than-enthusiastic salvo from a lone guard. Sokka eyes the cluster of guards trying to marshal themselves a few paces away, setting his feet even as he keeps part of his attention on the firebenders. Sokka’s blood would be singing to be fighting the Fire Nation at his Dad’s side if he weren’t so fucking aware of the odds stacked against them, and the way they just shifted sharply in the wrong direction.

“Pink girl,” Sokka says grimly as he ducks beneath the guards’ opening attack and lunges up and in, planting his shoulder in a guard’s stomach—a move Zuko always gets a kick out of unleashing on Sokka—and dumping her on her ass back into her comrades. Huh. Surprisingly effective.

“Who’s the pink girl?” Hakoda sends another guard sailing through the air to bowl down a few more people into Sokka’s pile.

“A big fucking problem.”

“A big fucking rematch,” Suki corrects as she comes up beside them, voice dark and eager, her gaze trained on Ty Lee even as she incapacitates her current opponent. Her body is practically thrumming with intensity, and Sokka abruptly realizes that maybe Azula wasn’t lying about that favorite prisoner thing. Shit.

“A rematch?” Ty Lee calls from across the platform, popping onto her toes with an eager wave. “I love a rematch!”

“We need to get that gondola lever pulled,” Sokka reminds them. “And then—”

“And then break it so they can’t unpull it, I remember,” Suki finishes, with eyes only for Ty Lee as she launches herself forward through the crowd, and, well—that’s fine. That’s… happening. Ty Lee is enough of a threat on her own that Sokka doesn’t mind Suki taking her out of the field for the rest of them, even if losing Suki against the rest of the guards suddenly puts a strain on things.

Hakoda and Sokka wave each other back, the others pulling in tighter to try to close the gap of Suki’s absence. Sokka does his best to shift them carefully toward the center of the platform, relying more and more on the guards’ wariness of getting caught in the literal crossfire—or maybe of interrupting their Lightning Princess, especially in lightning-ing distance—to protect their flank.

Sokka knows they can’t rely on that wariness for long, though, especially with Zuko so clearly taking pains not to hurt any bystanders. But they don’t *need* long, because Chit Sang is shouting out as his buddies gain the narrow ramp to the gondola, which means a tighter space to defend, which means the guards’ advantage of numbers is suddenly neutralized.

Which means pulling that lever is the last thing they need.

Sokka and Hakoda exchange a quick glance-head-tilt-nod before breaking off from the others, relying on surprise to gain them ground before the guards realize their target. So far organized resistance has been surprisingly sparse, but Sokka knows they can’t rely on that to last. Still, it’s easier than he expected it would be to cut their way around the perimeter— maybe because these guards aren’t used to dealing with actual armed combatants? Or maybe because they aren’t used to facing different fighting styles like the soldiers on the front lines are.

Or maybe because they’re primarily focused on staying out of the way of any incidental flames while not losing sight of the—hopefully—rare spectacle of their Fire Prince and Lightning Princess actually fighting each other in earnest.

Sokka tries to take advantage of that distraction and split focus as much as he can, whirling and stabbing and spinning, punching people in the side of the knee and kicking them into their comrades just as often as he engages blade to blade, doing everything he can to play up the threat of maybe being tossed into the line of fire if any of the guards truly decide to engage. He darts toward and away from that no-man’s land of flame-licked air, pacing himself to the rhythm of Zuko’s bending and Azula’s attacks.

Zuko is blocking with a practically earthbender solid stance that sends blue flame sheeting wide around him, and fuck does Sokka wish they had practiced fighting together and not just fighting. They’re doing shockingly well, all things considered, but Sokka needs this danger zone Zuko and Azula are maintaining around them to shift along with Sokka toward the gondola lever, and he doesn’t know how to signal that to Zuko without distracting him in a critical moment or revealing to Azula what they’re after.

Katara would know how to set Sokka up, exactly how to give him an opening just by reading how he’s throwing himself into the fight. Sokka and Katara have *practiced*. Sokka and Zuko might have talked fighting and tactics and strategy, but they’ve never actually fought together instead of sparred against each other. And in the midst of a melee with the Zuko and Azula almost wholly absorbed in each other isn’t the best time to start experimenting.

A sudden shocked shout that sounds a little too like Chit Sang for comfort has Sokka almost looking behind himself in surprise, and he’s mid-riposte when the Warden’s voice—*how,* did the guy fucking chew through that gag?—suddenly rips across the platform, all the guards visibly snapping to attention. “*Protect the lever. Do not let them near it.”*

Sokka and Hakoda exchange a quick, resigned look. The octocat’s out of the bag on that, then. But at least it solves the issue of how to get Zuko in on the plan, because Zuko and Azula both pause, fire briefly evaporating as they turn almost as one to eye the lever with nearly identical looks of annoyance.

Then everything explodes into motion again. The guards boil forward now that they have a clear command and Azula and Zuko are suddenly jockeying for positioning again, Azula defending the platform now while Zuko tries to drive her back enough to give Sokka an opening to get through.

It’s not perfect, and they definitely didn’t practice it, but Sokka can work with what Zuko’s giving him. His skin is going too-tight from the dry heat as he skims the edges of Zuko and Azula’s fight, the ends of his swinging hair sizzling as he lunges to gain ground whenever the guards fall back from the red and blue flames, trusting Zuko to keep deflecting and redirecting without catching Sokka in the line of Azula’s fire.

It’s going well—they’re gaining ground, Hakoda moving in sync to hold what Sokka seizes —up until it isn’t. Up until Azula suddenly rips an attack wide of Zuko, instead of at him, forcing Zuko to scramble to divert the roaring blue flame raging toward Sokka and Hakoda, forcing Zuko to block wider and thinner as he overextends himself.

Sokka dives forward as orange- and blue-twined fire sheets over his head, distantly aware— fuck, *fuck*—that Hakoda threw himself back. Sokka scrambles back to his feet, barely getting his sword up before he’s needing to jump over a skipping lash of flame that slithers across the whole width of the platform. And that must be some kind of standard move, because Sokka is off balance as he trips away from a sudden back-stroke of angry fire biting at his ankles, but all the guards seem to understand exactly how the twisting, roiling snake of flame will move until Zuko finally slices out a kick that forces Azula to let the fire burn itself out in favor of defense.

It’s not a long attack, in the overall scheme of the struggle, but it’s enough for the guards to rush in while Sokka is still gaining his footing, advancing *between* Sokka and Hakoda—*fuck* *—* instead of circling up on either side of them again. Sokka might be better with his sword than the guards are, and might be able to leverage the space and his jumbled-together fighting style to his advantage, but that doesn’t matter if he needs to defend himself on literally all sides.

Sokka tries to fall back toward the thin safety of Azula and Zuko’s fighting ground, still slightly wrong-footed as he spins into a block. He catches his opponent’s blade, but it’s an awkward angle, just a bit too high, just a bit too weak with the footwork, and Sokka wavers back instead of holding strong, wrists bending instead of locked. Sokka tries to twist himself behind the protection of his blade even as his guard is collapsing inward, except he can’t move too much because he was already so close to all that fire, and Zuko’s too *far* and—

Sokka grunts as he’s knocked back a staggering step or two into the dangerous space around Zuko and Azula, stumbling under a punch to the meat of his side just above the belt of his tunic and below the protection of his breastplate. He quickly catches his balance and raises his blade, twisting to take advantage of the empty space in front of him as long as he’s in it and try to get himself—

Sokka hisses as his body flinches away from the pivot instead of doing what he tells it to do. He glances down in surprise—fuck, he needs to get out of the crisp zone, needs to get back toward Hakoda—then risks a second one as he belatedly notes an unexpectedly pale swathe —skin, his brain helpfully supplies—against the darkness of his tunic and registers the feeling of wetness down his side—blood, another helpful offering.

And like all Sokka’s brain needed was open acknowledgment, the pain sets in, deep and sharp and driving, enough to steal his breath and force a gasping inhale that fucking *hurts*.

A whistle-rush of air has Sokka jerking up his arms on instinct to deflect the coming blow, his body reacting like it’s been trained to block the tentative strike coming from a guard who’s visibly reluctant to breach so deep into the ring around the firebenders’ battle. But the glancing contact still ripples through his body, a strangled cry bursting past his lips as he tries to brace and his side *screams*.

A sudden rush of dry heat has Sokka stumbling on unsteady legs back from a lick of flame, that little shift enough to send him tripping to his knees. He clenches his teeth against another cry as his knee slams into the metal platform, the force of it like another hit to the side, clumsily transferring his grip to wield his sword one-handed. He sets his jaw, making his arm firm and steady and acutely aware that on one knee with his back to the firebenders is a bad place to be, that he’s utterly vulnerable as he clamps his free hand over his side, feeling the wet, wet, wetness of his own blood, hot and slick and fuck, this is a big one, *fuck*, Katara isn’t here. This is…this is bad.

“*Sokka!”*

Sokka can’t look toward Suki’s sudden scream, can’t turn toward the clamor that could be Hakoda trying to reach him. Only proximity to Zuko and Azula is keeping him safe now, and Sokka can see that the guards are working up the nerve to approach. Sokka doesn’t know if he has more than one or two parries in him. Fuck, Sokka doesn’t think it’s even going to get that far, because he’s familiar with the rhythm of Zuko and Azula by now and he’s bracing himself to feel fire, trying not to think too much about it as he fumbles to apply pressure and keep his breathing even. Panicking will just raise his heart rate, which will just make his blood pump faster, which will just accelerate—everything.

Except Sokka *doesn’t* hear fire, or the controlled breathing or grunts of effort that go with firebending. And the guards aren’t moving quite yet, and he’ll hear when they do, so Sokka risks a glance up and back to see Zuko frozen. *So close* to the lever but staring at Sokka, his face bloodless and horrified, so still he looks like he isn’t even breathing.

Azula is poised across from Zuko, hands raised and ready to bend even as her eyes flick between Zuko and the lever and the red seeping over Sokka’s fingers. Sokka can feel his breath coming too hard as he stares back at her, his own focus darting between her and Zuko, his body filling with an awful kind of anticipation because *fuck*, what is she waiting for?

“*Azula*,” Ty Lee shouts.

Her tawny eyes barely flicker, expression closed as she calls back, “I see it,” gaze finally settling on Zuko, who’s still frozen, still staring, chest moving way too shallow and way too fast. A distant corner of Sokka’s mind points out that that can’t be very good for firebending.

“Well, Zuzu?” Azula finally asks, voice low, soft enough that Sokka wouldn’t be able to hear it if he weren’t already too close. “Are you going to throw that away, too?”

Zuko makes a quiet sound, anguished, finally tearing his eyes from Sokka to turn toward Azula, and Sokka can’t see his face anymore, just the edge of his scar, body language all Sokka has to work with and Zuko isn’t giving him *anything* more than that horrible stillness.

“Zuko,” Sokka grits out, words tight with pain, trying to will Zuko toward action. “Do it.” He’s *right there*, right next to the lever. He can just pull it and *go*, because it’s in and out together but it’s also not just them anymore.

Azula looks toward Sokka and makes a noise of disgust. “You could at least *try,* Brother,” she tosses over her shoulder. Then she’s lunging, faster than Sokka’s ever seen her move, controlled and precise and Zuko is so not prepared, so wide open and distracted. Except instead of the frontal assault Sokka expects, or raising a shield against Zuko’s startled, erratic punch of flame, Azula takes a page out of Sokka’s book and throws herself low. She slides feet first over the metal grating in a screech of armor, forcing Zuko to jump to avoid getting his legs kicked out from under him, shooting smoothly back to her feet before he’s even landed to set herself in his blind spot.

She glares at her brother’s undefended back for a single beat of Sokka’s too-fast heart, hand raised, two fingers extended. Then she pivots, *away* from Zukoo, face flat and *angry* as she whips out her arm, a lance of blue-hot fire exploding off her fingers directly at Sokka.

Sokka distantly registers a sound that must be Dad screaming, another that has to be Suki yelling, but all he can do is flinch away to try to protect his face, hands coming up on instinct and *fuck*, Sokka thought the glancing edges of their fire were bad before? This is hotter than any campfire, forge-hot, drying the air in his lungs as it approaches hot, and Sokka briefly, wildly wonders if he’s somehow going to get burned from the inside out before the blue-white wash of it streaks past him to explode against the platform, and despite his best efforts Sokka can’t stop from *screaming* as his mind goes white with pain.

&#45;-

The wrenching, from-the-depths-of-his-guts cry that explodes from Sokka as he takes that glancing hit of Azula’s flame is the worst thing Zuko’s ever heard in his life. His inner fire writhes in sympathy, and the pure agony in it is enough to *finally* unlock his body from the immobilizing horror that’s gripped it ever since he caught sight of the blood seeping between Sokka’s fingers. Agni’s tits, he’s *useless*, he couldn’t even—

Zuko wants to scream too as he looks wildly between Sokka hunched over himself on the ground, and Suki trying to get past a suddenly uncertain Ty Lee, and Sokka’s father struggling to reach his son’s side. The guards aren’t even trying to fight back against Hakoda, their sheer mass enough to keep him away as more and more of them look toward the center of the platform like they’re aware that some sort of drama is unfolding before them in real time—a fucking tragedy, if Zuko doesn’t figure out what to *do.*

Because the lever is right there, so close that Zuko could just lunge for it, except—*Sokka*. And Azula, who’s standing, arm still extended, watching him with eyes that are cold, cold, cold, her expression making it clear that there’s only one choice Zuko can make that won’t result in a second attack.

But fuck, how can they get off the platform if Zuko cedes back all this ground? And with Sokka—they could get him somewhere safe inside, or into the gondola, but then they’d need to come back and reengage and fuck, *fuck*, that won’t work, not at all. Except if Zuko goes for the lever now, Sokka is *there* and *wounded* and Azula’s two fingers are smoking, ready, and—

“My uncle! Don’t let my uncle get hurt!”

Zuko jerks as a frantic shriek cuts through the thick air, high-pitched and desperate like Zuko’s never heard from Mai before.

“My uncle,” Mai cries again, black robes swinging around her as she runs out onto the platform. “You can’t let him get hurt! He’s my only uncle!”

Zuko’s brain trips, trying to understand. That isn’t true, she has two others just on her mother’s side alone. But Chit Sang doesn’t have a similar issue. He darts forward, quick for someone so large, threatening the Warden with renewed urgency and Mai screams again, hitting a pitch that makes the guards flinch and edge back, looking between their utterly still Princess—oh shit, oh *fuck—*and their Warden’s distraught niece, none of them sure enough of their purpose now to more than half-heartedly try to stop Suki from running to Sokka. Even Ty Lee lets her go, her normally bright face tense and wary as Mai lets out another pleading cry.

“Mai,” Azula snaps, voice slicing across the platform. “What is this *caterwauling.”*

“Oh, Azula,” Mai sobs, turning to her with *tears* on her face, what—Zuko’s *never* seen that before. She pushes her way through the mess of guards around the perimeter, stumbling and bumping in her distress. “You know how I love my uncle!”

“You don’t,” Azula says, voice dangerously clipped, her body slowly shifting to orient away from Sokka, away from Zuko, toward Mai. Oh, Agni.

“Oh,” Mai says, face going expressionless as she abruptly straightens, sunlight flashing off the knives that appear in her grip. Zuko feels like his heart is simultaneously lodged in his throat and plummeting through the bottom of his stomach, his inner fire trying to leap from his hands and crawl into his spine. “You’re right. I forgot.” Her eyes cut toward Zuko, flat and annoyed. “Go, Zuko.”

His body tenses to obey even as his conscious mind scrambles to understand *where,* exactly, he’s supposed to go to, and then her knives start flying across the platform, pinning down sleeves and knocking weapons out of hands, forcing guards to stumble back to protect their eyes. Space is opening on either side of her, a dual path toward the gondola for Sokka’s father, who’s hefting Sokka into his arms—blessed Agni *please* let that be good—and another rapidly clearing path toward the lever for her.

“*Go*,” she shouts, throwing a knife toward Zuko’s feet that finally jolts him out of his horrified disbelief, and finally he goes, running, ignoring Azula like he would otherwise never dare to do and full out sprinting to join Suki in the rearguard. Except *shit*, they still need to pull that lever. Fuck, what is Mai *doing*? What is she *going* to do?

“What is this, Mai,” Azula demands, more naked rage in those four words than Zuko’s ever heard from her, the sound of it making his inner fire flinch, making the guards start to press against the railings as they try to back away.

“What I should have done a long time ago,” Mai says, glowering through her bangs as she drops a fresh set of shuriken into her hands.

Azula lets out a savage scream, wild with anger, jagged knives of fire bursting to life in her balled hands. Sloppy. What the fuck, *sloppy*. “*Ty Lee.*”

“Right,” Ty Lee says, resolute, her characteristic cheerfulness nowhere to be seen as she leaps across the platform, the guards falling back before her, completely confused now as Ty Lee moves to flank Mai, positioning herself right next to the lever so that Mai *has* to split her attention. Ty Lee’s eyes are fierce with something Zuko’s never seen on her face before as she shifts her gaze to look past Azula’s shoulder and catch Zuko’s eyes and—

Metal fucking *sings* against metal as the lever snaps into position, and every Fire Nation citizen in earshot freezes as the sound tolls across the open water like the warning bells of Caldera. Everyone except Ty Lee, that is, who raises her foot and delivers another resounding kick, then a third that has the metal screeching as it bends and warps and crunches out of shape in a spray of rust and destroyed gears.

Zuko is distantly aware that he’s holding his breath along with everyone else as the shards finish falling, raining down in a deceptively cheery tinkle of metal on metal. The guards are completely frozen, no one daring to even try to get off the platform in case any movement draws Azula’s attention.

“…Why,” Azula finally says after a stretch of heartbeats that feels like *days*, her voice utterly devoid of emotion, her hands dry like the very breath has been knocked out of her, extinguishing her flames. “You know the consequences. You *know.”*

Ty Lee’s chin tilts up, her grey eyes hard and trained on Azula, and Mai steps carefully back, once, twice, to stand at Ty Lee’s side, both of them facing down Azula now. Together. Fuck.

“Kid,” Chit Sang calls, low, “Come on.”

“I guess you just don’t know people as well you think you do,” Ty Lee is saying.

Mai’s chin kicks up too. “You miscalculated.”

“*Zuko*.”

Zuko’s body reacts to Sokka’s urgent, clenched hiss before his mind even registers the sound. He snaps around, turning his back on his sister’s betrayal and setting himself toward the gondola that’s already starting to pull away. Sokka is leaning out, white-faced with pain and batting away his dad and Suki’s restraining hands, and Zuko stops trying to think entirely, just sprints, the guards falling back before him.

Zuko leaps across the gap, momentarily weightless. Then he’s grabbing onto the doorway of the gondola, letting Suki’s startled hands pull him all the way in, Sokka awkwardly grabbing at Zuko’s tunic as if he were in any position to do more than sag backward himself.

Chit Sang grunts, taking a deliberate step back to give more space to clear the doorway. “Some jump. *Zuko*.”

Zuko flicks him a quick look, taking in the wariness on his face and the cautious bunching of the other Fire Nation escapees. That…well. He’ll just…deal with that later. For now, there’s nothing he could possibly do except turn back toward Boiling Rock, where Mai and Ty Li are a blur of black and pink, defending the remains of the lever and the gondola cable as the guards press forward, Azula screaming them onward from her knees, her arms limp at her sides in a way Zuko recognizes all-to-well from one too many games of Earth Kingdom assassin with Ty Lee.

“What’s going on,” Sokka asks between clenched teeth, shrugging off the way his father is trying to urge him to take a seat.

“…I think we’re going to get away,” Zuko finally manages to say, feeling…numb. Worried for Sokka, anxious over Hakoda, distantly away that his heart is crashing against his ribs from adrenaline and fear, feeling it all like it’s happening to someone else.

“Oh,” Sokka says, panting now and finally sliding down the wall, the gesture sudden enough to seize Zuko’s focus. “Awesome.”

“We’ll be fine,” Zuko says inanely, not sure who he’s saying it for as he drops to his knees by Sokka, close enough to see his injured side but far enough to keep a healthy distance from Sokka’s father, who seems *much* bigger up close than he did across the prison yard earlier today. They’re going to be fine, he tells himself for a second time. Him and Sokka, and all the others.

*They’re* going to be fine, at least. But Zuko doesn’t think there’s any world where *that* was part of the plan, not at this stage of things, and his inner fire is shuddering against his spine from it. Agni, with all the players suddenly on different sides of the board…what’s the game going to be now?

#### Chapter End Notes
