## Chapter 21: Being Caught

### Notes

#### Chapter Notes

Warnings for sexual content in this one, and also for the author's lack of medical knowledge!

### Text

It’s organized chaos on the airship, a surprising amount of it considering how few people are actually in the sizeable cabin area. But maybe that’s part of the chaotic nature. Sokka doesn’t get the impression that the airships—which are so *cool*—are supposed to run on a crew of seven.

Or six—Sokka isn’t exactly contributing much.

“You’re sure you’re comfortable?” Zuko asks, hovering.

“It’s fine,” Sokka grits out, trying to focus on what’s around him instead of the persistent fucking *fire* of his side. It’s constant and biting and every time he moves it feels like he’s getting burned all over again, and it’s not like Sokka isn’t fully fucking aware that this is how burns work, but Spirits, Sokka does *not* appreciate this right now.

“I can find some cushions,” Zuko mutters, eyeing a door deeper into the airship. “The captain’s quarters will have cushions.”

“Maybe wait until we’re off the ground?” Sokka suggests.

Zuko looks dissatisfied with that idea, but nods and strides off…toward the captain’s quarters, somehow managing to grab Chit Sang’s attention along the way with just a jerk of his chin, too.

Well. Sokka wouldn’t *hate* something between himself and the unyielding metal of the floor and the wall at his back. He would just prefer that they get in the air and officially away from Boiling Rock and the threat of pursuit, first. They’ve made it this far dealing with Sokka’s injury, they can wait a few minutes longer.

At least he hopes it will only be a few minutes. One of Chit Sang’s prison mates managed to get them into the ship with an ease that suggests some kind of technical know-how, though her knowledge of all the parts that make an airship go *down* but only spotty awareness of the ones that make it go *up* suggests her familiarity doesn’t exactly come from serving as crew.

Zuko at least seems to know in theory where everything’s *supposed* to be, and it only took a few comments about naval layouts for everyone from the Fire Nation to apparently agree that his knowledge translates well enough. And Sokka might not feel great about ‘well enough’ when they’re talking about launching themselves into the sky and maybe not staying up, but he doesn’t exactly have the focus right now to help work through the technical details, so he should probably just tell his mental commentary to shut up.

“Water?”

Sokka eyes the offered cup and decides not to question where Suki got it from. “Thanks.”

“You should clean that,” Suki comments, tilting her head toward the mess of singed fabric and dried and burned blood and *hurt* that Sokka is curled protectively around, just in case he thought there was anything else particular in need of cleaning at the moment. “You shouldn’t wait,” she adds when Sokka just gives a tight nod.

“We aren’t too far from Katara,” he mutters, not wanting to think about exactly how far they are. It took most of a day to get here, riding the winds with Zuko. How fast can this thing move going the other way?

Suki grunts, not looking mollified in the least. “We have the time.”

Sokka’s well aware of all the time. But the idea of having this cleaned out twice… “If you help them with the map, it’ll go faster.”

“Infection isn’t something to mess around with, Sokka.”

He sighs, wondering if she and Zuko plotted this out together. “Fine. But can we get in the air first?”

“…Deal.”

Sokka lets his head fall back when she leaves, indulging in a moment of exhaustion before he slits his eyes back open, keeping track of the bustle as it flits around him. He scowls when one of Chit Sang’s friends approaches with a pillow in hand, transferring his glower to the back of Zuko’s head where he’s bent over the map with Suki and shaking his head at whatever Chit Sang’s other friend is saying, responding with a few frowning words that send her dashing off somewhere into the ship.

Sokka keeps glowering—he’ll be *fine,* they need to get away more than he needs *pillows*— right up until the airship suddenly comes to thrumming life, at which point Sokka realizes he is in fact stupidly grateful for Zuko’s stubbornness. The engine hums through the entire structure and Sokka can’t stop hissing through his teeth, gripping the pillow hard enough to make his knuckles ache as the vibrations rattle through every point his body touches the wall and floor.

Sokka is panting his nose, trying to figure out how to brace against the pain and breathe through it at the same time, when Zuko is suddenly crouching down in front of him and fuck, Sokka didn’t even notice him moving.

“This might help,” Zuko says, gently easing the pillow from Sokka’s grip and positioning it behind his back, getting the cushion into place just in time to throw out a hand to steady Sokka as the airship suddenly angles sharply upward.

“Thanks,” Sokka grits out, trying to will himself to relax as every nerve in his body screams at him to *do something* about the raw fire burning over his side.

Zuko bites his lip, anxious. “We’ll level out soon,” he says, casting a dark glare toward the navigation room. “It’ll be a bit better then.”

Then he’s giving Sokka’s arm a quick squeeze and he’s up again, across the room almost before Sokka can blink and snapping out a quiet set of instructions that may or may not have anything to do with the way the airship begins to climb a lot more gently a minute later.

Sokka watches Zuko, easing bit by bit into the pillow—which *is* nice—and slowly realizing that this might be the first time he’s seen Zuko act like a Prince. Not a Prince in Exile or a captain, not someone playing at a role, but just…command and direction and such an expectation of being heard that he makes it happen. And a glare that can put people in their place with just a slash of his eyes, when it’s called for.

Not that Zuko didn’t already have that piece before. And not that Sokka can really hear from across the room whether it’s called for or not. But he can tell from the tightness around Zuko’s scar and the way Zuko keeps shifting to set his back toward the nearest wall that Zuko’s too worn down for it to be worth mustering a scowl like that for nothing.

Even with Zuko so exhausted—or maybe because of it, because he’s too tired and worried about more important things to put energy into caring what other people are thinking right now—it’s something of a marvel to see Zuko taking command of the situation. To see him so publicly behaving like the version of himself that Sokka’s really only seen when they’re alone together, the version that Sokka desperately hopes is some true-to-himself expression of who Zuko is. Sokka didn’t think he would ever see Zuko quite like this again and it’s undeniably a good look on him, and one that seems to sit with the kind of ease Zuko never seemed to have on his ship.

It’s...also sparking all sorts of unhelpful, getting ahead of himself questions that Sokka doesn’t really have the focus to begin working through right now. But Spirits, Sokka has a sense that he’s going to feel all sorts of ways about Zuko’s air of authority when he’s in even a fraction less pain.

“How are you doing, Son?”

Sokka quickly tosses aside the thoughts tumbling through his head and musters a smile that probably looks more like a grimace, upon reflection, but he’s trying here. “I’ve been worse.” Dad makes a face at that but crouches down, balancing on the balls of his feet with the ease of someone who’s not currently nursing what’s probably a massive injury to his side. Sokka’s trying not to look, under the logic that if he can’t see it then there’s still the possibility that it’s not real. “It seems like we have a few hours yet,” Dad says.

Sokka holds back a sigh. “We’ve been at the Western Air Temple,” he offers, wishing for the first time that they’d found somewhere closer to the Fire Nation to go to ground. The time it’s going to take to get back makes sense, but Spirits, Sokka would like to be able to just fudge the distances on the map right now.

“Good spot,” Dad nods, eyes assessing and concerned on Sokka’s face, which kind of makes Sokka just want to let himself be pulled into a hug that would really fucking hurt right now.

“What about the others?” Sokka asks, reaching for a distraction against the pain and his desire to sag forward. “What happened after we left? Do you know where Bato and everyone ended up?”

“Planning another prison break?” Dad asks with a shake of his head and something in his voice that Sokka doesn’t have the wherewithal to figure out at the moment, whatever it is gone as he shares what little he knows about how the Earth Kingdom and Water Tribe soldiers were separated, how the leaders were weeded out, and what might have happened after.

If Sokka weren’t already sitting he’d probably be weak at the knees as he hears that most of the Tribe managed to stick together, at least the last time Hakoda saw them, and that they seemed to be sticking to the directive to keep their heads down and bide their time. He lets the relief slowly creep through them as he takes in Hakoda’s words, letting them chip away at the hard kernel of guilt that’s been sitting in his gut for…a long time.

The relief makes it easier to concentrate on what’s being said instead of the pain radiating through his side, makes it easier to breathe, to pace his breaths to Dad’s words like Zuko taught him until the pain gradually starts to feel like something Sokka can wrap his hands around, something marginally closer to manageable.

&#45;-

Sokka is starting to see the downsides of having a Crown Prince of the Fire Nation around when that also comes with citizens who apparently recognize Zuko as such. First, there was the pillow Sokka didn’t ask for, and then a snack Sokka didn’t quite have the stomach for even if he felt better after eating it, and now Chit Sang’s friends are helping Sokka into an interior room over his protests, purely on Zuko’s insistence that it happen. Zuko, who promptly darted off with averted eyes after doing all that insisting, to go do something suspiciously unclear with a map.

Sokka thinks about digging in his heels, but…honestly, the other things turned out pretty nice, so he just sighs and lets himself be ushered along, and in the end, it *is* quieter in the interior rooms, and steadier, the motion of the air currents and vibrations of the engine less apparent here.

The real problem though isn’t that everyone from the Fire Nation seems inclined to do what Zuko wants. The real issue is that Sokka can’t get rid of them even once he’s settled.

“So I think I’m good now…” Sokka trails off meaningfully, blinking when that… gets him nothing. “You probably don’t need to stay.”

The pair exchanges a glance, then shrugs, conspicuously not leaving.

&#45;-

“Some privacy would be good,” Sokka tries, attempting to level a meaningful stare and then immediately bailing out on that idea because he’s not trying to imply he needs *alone time* alone time, just…that he’d like some alone time.

Two sets of pale brown eyes stare impassively back.

“I’d like to be alone now,” Sokka says, feelings himself getting hot in the face, which, Spirits, how does his body even have the energy left for that at this point. “Not to—just—it’d be nice, okay?”

&#45;-

“Why are you still *here*,” Sokka huffs, aggrieved. It’s not like they’re *doing* anything, they’re just…*watching* him, and shifting whenever he winces, and what’s the point.

“The Fire Prince requested that we see you to this room,” the woman finally says, face flickering with…something, as she says it, exchanging a look with her company that feels a bit wild-eyed to Sokka and that he absolutely does not have the wherewithal to sort through right now.

“And here I am, mission accomplished.”

“Yes,” the man agrees. Not. Moving.

&#45;-

“You know,” Sokka suddenly says, struck by a fit of inspiration, “Zuko—” They both flinch slightly. “—Crown Prince Zuko might need some additional assistance now that you have accomplished this request.”

Sokka holds his breath. They glance to the door.

“Maybe you should check just to be sure,” he tacks on. “I’m sure the Prince would like that.”

Sokka is sure of nothing of the sort, but the two of them don’t know that, apparently, because the pair is out of the room in a heartbeat, leaving Sokka to stare after them and wonder what exactly Zuko’s been saying about him. Or maybe what they inferred all on their own.

Sokka sets that aside for later, though, because now that he’s finally safely alone, Sokka is going to take advantage of the opportunity to indulge in some grimacing and cheek biting and fist clenching and back-of-his-throat *fuck* noises. It’s a relief to just let it all out. Sokka hasn’t wanted to distract the others, especially when he’s pretty sure it’s fine—he finally took a tentative look and there isn’t any blood flowing anymore, and that’s good, right? So what’s the point in letting his pain show when it won’t do any good except to upset people about something they can’t do anything about until they get back to Katara.

Sokka quickly opens his eyes and smooths out his face when a tentative fist sounds against the door, though, because Sokka can count the number of people on this airship who would *tentatively* bang on the door with one finger. Zuko still seemed wound up and off-balance the last Sokka saw him, with none of the relief the others are starting to show now that they’re in the air, and Sokka doesn’t want to add more to his shoulders in particular. Though he has a feeling he got control of his expression a shade too late…

“That bad, huh?” Zuko asks after a pause, fingers tapping a rapid beat against his leg as he leans in the doorway.

“I didn’t say that,” Sokka tries.

“Sure.” Zuko pushes off the doorway and Sokka sees that he has some kind of kit in his hand. A healer’s bag, he realizes as Zuko kneels down next to him and starts sorting out gauze and bandages.

“What’s all that,” Sokka asks as Zuko begins laying out jars. clearing his throat to try to get the tightness out.

“Burn stuff.”

“And that?”

Zuko gives the bottle in question a little shake. “Paint stripper.” He peeks up through his bangs when Sokka doesn’t reply, lips quirking as he clarifies, “Really shitty alcohol.”

“Ah.” That…is going to hurt.

“Going to let me use it?”

“…Probably not,” Sokka admits. Not when they’re so close to Katara.

“Going to let me see it?” Sokka doesn’t know quite what to make of the neutral-but-not quality of Zuko’s question until gold eyes pin him with the beginnings of a glare. “Or are you going to tell me to go find a map like you did Suki?”

Sokka clings for one more heartbeat to the idea of holding out, then sighs, slowly forcing himself to straighten and drop his arms from their protective curl over his torso. Zuko slides forward, gaze intent as he fishes a pair of scissors out of the bag to cut away an uncomfortably large swathe of burned fabric from Sokka’s tunic. And Sokka might be feeling a little queasy seeing just how much burned cloth Zuko is peeling away, but watching Zuko work is somehow actually starting to let Sokka relax. The pain is still more than present, but the realization that he won’t need to contort out of armor and tunic, the care with which Zuko is treating even the skin away from the burn, Zuko’s utter concentration—well, it does a lot to ease the tight, nervous anticipation of pain that’s been feeding Sokka’s reluctance to do anything but wait for Katara.

Though all the care in the world isn’t enough right now for Sokka to actually want to see what’s going on between his ribs and his hip. He watches Zuko’s face instead, taking in the quiet, intense focus. Zuko’s hands are deft and sure over Sokka’s side, like Zuko somehow knows just when to gentle his touch and just where brace Sokka to lessen the strain, managing to apply an absolutely amazing cooling salve with only half the agony Sokka was readying himself for.

Sokka knows he should probably take a real look and assess the damage, especially as the salve sinks in and the pain begins to become less all-consuming. He just…really doesn’t want to. It’s been *feeling* bad enough, and something about adding in the sight of his own burned flesh when he already has the memory of it sliced wide and bleeding…Sokka much prefers to carefully turn his injured side further toward Zuko, inching forward as Zuko goes totally still, cautiously creeping until Sokka can finally drop his forehead against Zuko’s shoulder and just…stop holding himself up for a bit.

Zuko doesn’t move for a long moment, not even breathing, his hands held wide, and Sokka just concentrates on finding the smell of Zuko beneath the lingering scents of prison and sulfur from the lake. Sokka doesn’t know how long it is—as long as Zuko can hold his breath, he supposes—but finally Zuko shifts, slow and gentle as he eases Sokka more solidly against his chest, and Sokka’s more than happy to let himself be moved.

This…is better. Sokka lets out a tired, grateful hum as Zuko’s hand runs down his spine, a careful, soothing press before Zuko shifts his attention to sizing up a piece of gauze. Sokka closes his eyes, tilting his head until he can find the beat of Zuko’s heart, sighing as something like…not contentment, not happiness, but maybe actual okay-ness, after days and days of saying it without fully meaning it, finally settles over him.

It’s quiet for too many beats of Zuko’s always-fast heart for Sokka to count before Zuko eventually speaks, the words rumbling through his chest and rasping in Sokka’s ear. “Everyone in the Fire Nation learns the basics of burn care in school.”

Sokka makes a listening noise. He can fucking guess all on his own that Zuko knows way more than just the basics.

“This isn’t one of the best salves,” Zuko says as he carefully presses a pad of gauze against Sokka’s side. “But it’s good for military issue.”

“I’m surprised a royal airship doesn’t have the best there is,” Sokka mumbles into Zuko’s tunic.

“…It depends on how you think about burns, I guess,” Zuko says as he begins winding a bandage over the gauze to hold it in place, wrapping it over the remains of Sokka’s tunic in the process. “And whoever’s getting them.”

Sokka isn’t quite sure he wants to parse that just yet, and what it might mean about Zuko’s sister that she doesn’t have the fancy stuff.

“There,” Zuko says, carefully tucking the edges of the bandage under. “Anywhere else?”

“The side isn’t enough?” Sokka asks, aiming for a joke and immediately telling from the ripple of tension through Zuko’s chest that it doesn’t land.

“It’s better than it could be,” Zuko says, tight, and Sokka can feel the almost-pressure of his hand hovering over it.

“At least it isn’t bleeding anymore,” Sokka tries.

“…At least.”

Okay, well *that* Sokka needs to parse, that grim tone and the sudden unyielding stiffness he can feel in every point Zuko’s pressed against him. Sokka gingerly leans back, letting out a puff of relief when the feeling of fire trapped beneath his skin doesn’t flare up again—this salve really is amazing. Sokka tilts his head to try to see Zuko’s face without needing to move his own body too much, taking in the averted eyes and tight line of his mouth, the fidgeting fingers against Sokka’s lower back, the coiling and uncoiling tension like Zuko keeps having to fight the urge to pull away.

“…Why are you acting all guilty?”

Zuko flinches from Sokka’s question, then immediately sways back, so fast it’s like the support of his body never moved at all as the words trip out. “I should have been able to—I couldn’t—I’m sorry, Agni’s tits, Sokka, I’m *so* sorry,” he repeats, voice cracking. “You were —and I—”

“Zuko, you have nothing to apologize for,” Sokka says, giving up on trying to search Zuko’s face and carefully setting his hands on Zuko’s shoulders, moving them in slow, soothing circles when they aren’t immediately shrugged away.

“I couldn’t—Sokka, you were *bleeding.* There was so much—you would have—” Zuko bites off the words, squeezing his eyes shut. “I should have been able to *do* something.”

“It was a fight, Zuko,” Sokka says, striving for gentleness because he gets the sticky way guilt can cling, even when things were out of your control. Spirits, does he ever. “Fuck, it was basically a brawl. It happened, but it’s no one’s fault.” It was just shitty luck, and timing, and the kind of decisions you don’t realize are wrong until it’s too late.

“But I didn't do *anything,* and *Azula*—”

“There wasn’t anything you could have done, Zuko,” Sokka cuts in. He doesn’t want Zuko running around thinking he’s responsible for everything his sister does in his presence.

Zuko just looks away, though, tight-lipped and somehow looking even more upset than when he started, which Sokka doesn’t know what to do with, just doesn’t understand even as his pulse flutters in his throat with the need to soothe. Or maybe Sokka does understand. Having your own powerlessness pointed out is rarely a reassuring experience, especially not when you’re face to face with just how scary the things you can’t control can be.

Sokka reaches for the hand not resting on his back and gently tangles their fingers together, giving a careful squeeze. “Hey,” he says, waiting until Zuko finally makes reluctant eye contact. “It’s fine. Okay? I’m going to be fine. We all got out, things are going to be okay. In together, out together, right?”

It’s an achingly long moment before Zuko finally nods, squeezing Sokka’s hand back. “Right.”

And Sokka will just have to take that reassurance for now and be happy with it, even if he thinks it sounds a bit hollow. But he isn’t going to push, not yet at least. He certainly knows that coming to terms with the things you wish you could change doesn’t come easy.

&#45;-

Katara’s face as Sokka steps off a fucking Fire Nation *airship—*Suki wisely suggested they hang a bedsheet out the window as a white flag—is beautiful. A work of art. It makes his fingers long for a paintbrush. It makes him want to sculpt so he can preserve it forever in statues across the nations.

“…Must have been some hunting trip,” Aang says.

“Get any good meat,” Toph drawls, her tone bordering on salacious and Sokka firmly ignores that even as Zuko lets out a full-body twitch that really gives it away. Sokka’s going to have to talk to him again about not reacting to Toph’s continued attempts to figure out how to be a general menace to society.

“The best meat of all,” Sokka says, trying to soldier on like Toph never said anything, “The meat of friendship and fatherhood.”

“…Ew, Sokka,” Toph says, wrinkling her nose.

Zuko makes a low noise, shifting forward like he’s getting ready to catch Sokka if he keels over, which…might be warranted.

But then Dad and Suki appear at the top of the ramp and all the attention shifts thoroughly away from Sokka. Katara lets out a shout of surprise that turns into an excited shriek, running forward as Dad rushes down to meet her. Sokka grins, watching them crash into each other and letting Zuko gently ease him off to the side, out of the commotion as Suki gets her own greeting and then Chit Sang and friends make their appearance and need to be explained.

Katara finally breaks away, flushed and flustered but managing to muster something like a glare as she turns to Sokka where he’s letting—maybe needing—Zuko take some of his weight, because Sokka’s rediscovered that it’s quite nice to get to lean against Zuko and also that when he does he doesn’t need to use his abs. “A *hunting trip*, Sokka?”

“I mean.” Ah, shit. “We *were* hunting for something? Technically?” He resists the urge to swat at Zuko when he shifts at Sokka’s back.

“You pedantic little—you went to break Dad out of *prison* and you left a *letter?”*

“Hey,” Sokka protests, “What’s wrong with a letter? I was going to just—” Zuko suddenly coughs behind him, sudden enough to nearly jostle Sokka, making him bite his tongue in anticipation of pain that doesn’t quite come until he glances back to see Zuko staring rather intently at his own boots.

“I can’t believe you went without me,” Katara snaps. “Without all of us! No more vigilante stuff, Sokka, I thought that’s what we agreed to. Me and Aang weren’t even gone for a night and you lost your shit! You made me promise that we wouldn’t go off on our own anymore. That means you too! We—we had a *moment*.”

“…I wasn’t alone?” Sokka tries, wincing when Zuko makes a nearly soundless noise when Katara’s glare swings toward him. Sokka quickly adds on, “I didn’t want to involve too many people.”

He glances to where Aang is showing off one of his airbending tricks to Chit Shang’s friends. There’s a whole world of risks Sokka is willing to take on for himself that he doesn’t know how they could let Aang face. “It was better to keep it small.”

“*Small?”* Katara flings an arm toward the airship blocking most of the late afternoon sun. “You think that’s *small*? Did you hit your head while you were out there?”

“Not his head,” Zuko suddenly breaks in, voice tight and openly anxious enough that it briefly knocks Katara off the edge of her anger.

“You got hurt?” She blinks, refocusing on the hunch to Sokka’s posture, the protective band of his arm across his stomach. “Sokka, you got *hurt*.”

“Yes,” Zuko answers for him, and Sokka can feel him practically vibrating with urgency now that the topic is getting attention. “Bad. Please. I—do you need water? I can get you water. Or bandages or—whatever you need.”

“I don’t need water,” Katara says after giving herself a shake, falling into her brisk healer’s tone like she’s forcibly shoving away everything else. “Let’s get him away from this ship into better light.”

Sokka opens his mouth to point out that he can walk on his own, then considers Zuko’s already-barely restrained tension. He doesn’t want to dig his heels in so much that that tension snaps. Besides, there are still three Fire Nation citizens around keeping more than half an eye on their Prince. By this point, Sokka’s pretty sure Zuko is more than willing to summon then to the cause if he feels like he needs to.

&#45;-

Zuko is visibly disgruntled to get shoed away from the healing, but Sokka doesn’t entirely mind the opportunity it gives him to indulge in some dramatic grimacing and bellyaching. He’ll drum up whatever sympathy he can get to counter Katara’s lingering annoyance and quiet edge of concern. Besides, Sokka doesn’t know if he has it in him to be shy about his sighs of relief as Katara’s magic water sends wave after wave of coolness across his side and does its—well, its magic.

“You have the spirits’ own luck, Sokka,” Katara mutters as she finally pulls her hands back, eyeing his side.

“I’m sorry, who’s sitting in front of you injured right now?” Sokka huffs. “Wait ‘til a man’s healed before you start insulting him, at least.”

Katara gives him a solid poke in the ribs, which mercifully only feels weird and not bad. “Anyone else would have bled out from this before they could manage to get themselves injured again. And then you get yourself injured in a way that cauterizes it. Tui and La, Sokka, only you.”

Sokka has a retort half-formed on his lips when he pauses, something not entirely comfortable shifting in his brain. The map of scars and taunts over Zuko’s body, and Azula’s furiously precise disgust, and…Sokka isn’t sure if he knows how to follow where his mind might be going, isn't sure that he wants to go there on his own without Zuko beside him. “Zuko helped with it after,” Sokka finally says, trying to ground on things he can be sure of. “He knew what to do.”

“Did he now?”

“Yeah,” Sokka says, smiling despite himself as he remembers Zuko’s total focus and quiet competence and gentle hands. “He was good at it.”

“Hm.” Katara transfers her critical gaze to his face, rolling her sphere of water between her hands. “Just like that, then?”

Sokka blinks. “What?”

Katara sighs. “You really don’t know how to not just jump right into things, do you.”

“…Into what?”

Katara shakes her head, waving the question away as she refocuses on her water, blue light rising between her hands. “Just—be happy, Sokka. And don’t do anything stupid.”

Sokka…doesn’t think they are talking about the prison break anymore.

&#45;-

Sokka gingerly tests the range of motion of his freshly healed side as he takes in the way the airship gleams in the last light of the setting sun. It’s got amazing lines, really. It’s incredible to think of all that weight and bulk flying so smoothly. Sokka’s balloon might already be obsolete, he thinks ruefully. Though a balloon certainly requires fewer resources to produce…

His side is still a little tender if he twists too sharply or too far, and his body still keeps tensing in anticipation of pain. Katara’s probably right that he should have another healing session tomorrow, but considering where things started a few hours ago? Sokka’s feeling pretty great. And he makes a point of showing off his nice new range of motion as familiar steps crunch up behind him.

“You’re not helping get everyone settled in?” Zuko asks as he comes up alongside him.

Sokka shrugs, leaning into a demonstrative side bend. “Katara needed to work out some energy bossing people around.”

Zuko gives him a sidelong ‘brave of you when she isn’t around to hear’ kind of look. “So you’re contemplating your war prize instead?”

“Figuring out how to get rid of it, actually.” Sokka offers a lopsided smile at Zuko’s startled glance. “It’s kind of conspicuous to drag around with us if we’re in hiding. And I’m not sure we can keep it fueled.”

“No,” Zuko says after a considering moment. “I suppose not.”

“I’m not really sure how to hide it, though,” Sokka admits. “It’s pretty…large.” And shiny. And red. And the trees topside might be dense, but this isn’t exactly Hei Bai’s territory.

Zuko tilts his head, eyeing the ship from a new angle. “Sink it?”

“…It seems a shame to do that.”

Zuko shrugs, heartlessly practical in a way that makes Sokka want to cry because this machine is *beautiful*. “It definitely doesn’t float.”

Sokka sighs. “Maybe we should let the others figure out how to ditch it. They deserve some fun too.” And Sokka doesn’t know if he has it in him to destroy something so amazing, at least not tonight.

Zuko gives him a sideways look. “Want to see the inside first?”

“*Yes*,” Sokka says before the question’s all the way out, not even embarrassed by how breathlessly eager he sounds.

Zuko twitches, just a little. “And maybe we could also…talk?”

Some of Sokka’s breathless eagerness deflates as he takes in the sudden controlled tightness of Zuko’s shoulders. “Yeah,” he agrees. “That’s—yes. That’s a good idea.” A talk’s been necessary for a while, really. And now, before anything happens that tempts Sokka to put it off again, is as good a time as any to finally have it.

&#45;-

Exploring a military airship through Sokka’s eyes does a lot to settle the ragged edges of Zuko’s inner flame. Ever since leaving Boiling Rock he’s been feeling stretched thin, spinning loose, wanting something to grab onto but unsure where he’s allowed to grip yet. Everything feels like it’s been turned on its head, alliances made and broken, prisoners captured and rescued. One of Zuko’s most important things almost in his grasp even as something he’s long considered part of the bedrock of his world crumbles to pieces.

The last few hours—days? Months?—have been…a lot.

At least Sokka is moving easily again, that instinctive bracing and protectiveness slowly draining out of his movements. Zuko watches him closely as Sokka darts from wall to wall, his curious mind poking at and latching onto things that Zuko would never have even thought to give a second glance. It’s nice to bask in his enthusiasm by association, to track the easy rise and fall of Sokka’s chest now that it's unconstrained by pain, to time his own breaths to the rhythm of Sokka’s excited commentary as he tries to internalize that Sokka is actually *okay*.

Zuko’s inner flame can’t entirely settle, though. For too many reasons for him to even attempt to count, but among them the awareness, as they explore crew quarters and engine rooms and the main cabins, that ‘exploring’ can look quite a bit like ‘hiding.’ And Zuko, at least, is absolutely hiding right now. From Chit Sang and Yamai and Irumi, who are deferring to him in a way that none of them seem entirely comfortable with and that Zuko doesn’t quite know what to do with when his experience ordering people around is very much confined to the strict command structure of naval ships. From Katara, who is—understandably—pissed at Sokka, and with Zuko by association, and who’s also a walking, prickly reminder right now of the fact that Sokka was injured and in pain and *burned*, and he might be fine now, but he *wasn’t*, not before.

Zuko might also be more than a little eager to hide away from Toph right now, at least he can find his balance again. He knows that the minute she senses something going on in his or Sokka’s heartbeats she’s going to start trying to figure it and, and Zuko just isn’t ready for that yet. Not when he doesn’t even know himself what’s going on—he has ideas, and hopes, and things he thinks he can be reasonably safe inferring from Sokka’s behavior, and things he’s going to ask, but…Zuko doesn’t *know* yet.

Mostly, though, Zuko can admit that he’s hiding from Sokka’s father. The man is bigger and broader and more openly suspicious and wary than Zuko was prepared for. And he’s also *Sokka’s* father, Sokka who is…something, to Zuko. Someone Zuko was sleeping with and who he’s eventually—and hopefully soon—going to start sleeping with again, someone who *loves him*, apparently, what the *fuck*. And someone who Zuko was wiping burned blood off of just hours ago, the stench of it awful and still lingering in his nose even though he knows it’s gone, that it’s been gone, that it could have been worse and it’s healed now, and—

So. Zuko needs to just…hide, a bit. To let himself slowly unwind as he soaks in something that feels close to normalcy at Sokka’s side, or at least close enough to do the trick. To sink into exploring an interesting thing together, even if just for a moment, instead of worrying about leading prison breaks or trying to figure out how to fit all these new people into their existing crew. And to give themselves space to figure out, before the end of the night, just what Zuko has to hold onto when it comes to Sokka.

The awareness that that particular conversation is coming closer and closer, that what they’re doing now is just a precursor, somehow manages to simultaneously soothe and rile his inner flame as they work from room to room within the airship. Zuko is very much ready for this talk, but the more time he has to think about it, the more he realizes that *talking* is such a vague request, such a vague thing to agree to.

What if Sokka doesn’t want to talk about what Zuko wants to talk about? Zuko thinks Sokka does, he doesn’t think he’s reading Sokka *that* wrong, but…Zuko can’t *entirely* rule out the possibility that Sokka might still not be ready for where Zuko wants to go. Even though Sokka said *that*, and kissed him, and curled up against him as best he could while injured, and Zuko doesn’t know how else to take those things. But just assuming Sokka meant it the way Zuko took it feels riskier than Zuko is willing to be with whatever this thing is between them.

Though the way Sokka tosses Zuko a quick smile over his shoulder, somehow managing to look thrilled and happy and nervous all at the same time…Agni, Zuko needs to remember to pace his breathing to Sokka’s so this conversation doesn’t get sidetracked before it can even start because Zuko passed out.

&#45;-

They end up in the command center, because it has windows that Zuko can look down to the ground from, and lots of buttons and levers and controls that Sokka can fiddle with after he runs through every single guess Zuko can provide on what they all might do. Light filters in from the distant campfire and the rising moon, and for once Zuko doesn’t feel the need to shy away from it, not with Sokka here.

He nudges up the soft light of the lamps anyway, though. He wants to be able to see Sokka for this.

Zuko finds a nice spot against the railing to lean, surprising himself with the size of his own sigh as he finally stops moving for what feels like the first time in days. Agni’s balls, but Zuko’s tired. And this is a nice railing. Sturdy. A good height for slumping back against, but low enough that Zuko can still have a nice straight back while he does it so he can preserve the illusion that he isn’t actively contemplating finding a nice spot of floor to curl up on the minute he can get his mind to stop turning.

“So…” Sokka finally says, pulling Zuko out of his contemplation of the metal decking.

“So.”

Sokka glances down at the array of knobs before him, then up at what Zuko’s pretty sure is his reflection in the viewing window. “You wanted to talk.”

“Yeah,” Zuko says, trying to marshal his thoughts as he shifts so he can see a slice of Sokka’s reflection back.

“Anything…anything in particular?” Sokka asks, tugging at his hair and only meeting Zuko’s eyes even in the reflection for a flash and just—Agni’s tits, Zuko is going to explode out of his fucking *skin.*

“Sokka,” Zuko says, scrubbing roughly at his face. “You *kissed* me. You said—”

“I know, I know what I said,” Sokka says quickly, blushing enough that Zuko can see it over the back of his neck, and Zuko doesn’t know how to read Sokka’s tone without being able to see his face to understand if that embarrassment is good or not.

“Did—” Zuko licks his lips and forces himself to start again, voice level, because if Sokka *does* still need space then Zuko is going to fucking give it to him, even if his inner fire feels knotted in confusion at the idea that there could be any space after *that*. “Did you mean it?”

“Yes,” Sokka says, quick and firm, no doubt in his voice even if Zuko can see his fingers drifting toward his wrist wraps, and Zuko’s too tired to hold back his audibly relieved breath.

“Okay. Good.” The best, really, and Zuko’s inner fire is relaxing back on itself in something he can’t even name. “And…what does that mean?”

Sokka gives a quick glance back over his shoulder, frowning. “What do you mean, what does it mean?”

Zuko blinks back, wondering if he’s too tired for this. “I mean…what does it mean.”

Sokka turns fully around, which Zuko much prefers, his face still creased in confusion, which Zuko doesn’t. Fuck, maybe *Sokka’s* too tired for this.

“You’ve…” Agni’s tits, where to even start. “Sokka, I don’t—I’m not always good with people. I know what I *want* to happen now, but…I don’t want to guess at what you’re thinking.” He searches Sokka’s eyes, unwilling to give them up now that he has them even if it’s so much harder to force out the rest under Sokka’s stare. “Are you—do you still need time? Were you just…expressing a feeling, back there?” Expressing a feeling with his fucking *mouth* and his *hands* and— “I know we kissed, but that doesn’t mean we have to kiss again.” Even if Zuko can’t see how kissing and needing time can live together. “I just…I think I need some open sharing. With this.”

“Oh. *Oh*,” Sokka says, his eyes widening as he stands a little more upright. “I didn’t realize you—sorry, I—” Zuko can see Sokka cut himself off, clamping his mouth shut and taking a deep breath before starting again. “No, I don’t think I need more time.”

Everything in Zuko latches onto that. “You don’t *think*?”

“I mean.” Sokka’s starting to look flustered now, which…*could* be a good thing. “There’s a lot going on. Big stuff. And. It’s a big thing, too, this, and I don’t want to pretend it isn’t. You’re important, so this is important, and I really want to get it right, and—”

“Sokka,” Zuko cut in gently, relaxing even as Sokka’s words start tripping over themselves more and more. Thinking something but being too full of the noise of the world to be sure of your own thoughts—Zuko knows this ground when it comes to Sokka. “If you feel like you’re on the way but you just need a little more time, that’s fine. It *is,*” Zuko insists when Sokka eyes him askance. “I don’t want you to be rushed, or pressured, or—I want you to *know.”*

“I do though,” Sokka says quickly. “I said—I meant what I said. And yeah, it’s kind of scary, because I still feel like I don’t have all the pieces the way I used to. But you said it yourself, right? That I could get stuck trying to be perfect? And I don’t want to miss out on what we could have because I’m trying to figure something that maybe I’ll never know unless I just do it, you know? So…I want to try. I want to give this a shot.”

Zuko…maybe *doesn’t* know. Trying and giving it a shot and never being able to figure something out until he does it and being scared—what does all that *mean* to Sokka? Zuko just needs it plain and simple, even if he can barely find the words himself for that. “So, you’re… sure? That’s what you meant?”

“I…yes?” Sokka says, frowning as he searches Zuko’s face. “Do I—should—I can explain again? Or—”

“Because I need you to be sure,” Zuko cuts in, bracing himself. He doesn’t know if more words just from Sokka are going to help even if his whole body wants to instinctively tighten against voluntarily making himself so open. “That’s…I need that. I can be without you if I have to. I’m not trying to be mean,” he adds when Sokka flinches, just a little. “Just…like how we’ve been here. Friends, or whatever. I can do that. I’ve *been* doing that. So if you need more time, I want you to take it. Because I can’t…” He takes another breath, glancing away and shoving the words out. “Sokka, I can’t be all in when you’re still figuring out whether it’s worth trying for.”

“It’s never been about whether it was worth it,” Sokka says fiercely, urgently. “Being with you has *always* been worth it, and I don’t—Spirits, I *never* wanted you to doubt that.” He sags back, so suddenly that Zuko nearly darts forward to catch him before realizing Sokka’s not actually falling. “Fuck,” he sighs, sounding…about as exhausted as Zuko feels. “You mean so much to me, Zuko, and you’re so amazing and I just…want to be good enough for you. I want to be worth *you*.”

Sokka glances up, quick, his face writ with uncertainty before his eyes dart away again and Zuko…has absolutely no idea what his expression is doing right now, what his inner fire is doing right now, what *any* of him is doing right now. The idea that Sokka—*Sokka*—would be trying to be worthy of *him*…Sure, Zuko knows that Sokka is impressed when Zuko shows off with his swords or his bending. And sure, the words *amazing* and *wonderful* have been living in a careful, soft place in Zuko’s chest ever since Sokka said them. But this—Agni. This is…

“But I don’t want to get stuck thinking that’s some—some fixed point to get to,” Sokka finally continues, frowning at the floor, one wrist wrap half undone. “Or some moment in time or something that eventually I’ll reach and then it’s done. I mean, obviously if you tell me you need something I’ll work on it, I just—I don’t want to be the one who keeps putting *us* off trying to get to some…stationary place that might not exist anyway.”

“Oh,” Zuko finally manages, distantly surprised he can form words. “That’s…good.”

“…It is?”

“I…yes. That—yes. Me—me, too.” Words are…not coming any easier, Zuko’s brain stumbling over and over all the ones that Sokka just said, turning them this way and that and no matter what way he flips them coming up with the same sentences, the same meaning each time.

Sokka blinks, opening and closing his mouth a few times. “So that’s…you’re good?”

“…Yeah,” Zuko says after a long moment, inner fire turning so fast in his chest he almost feels numb from it, because the sum total of everything Sokka just said is that…Sokka wants this. Whatever they have together. Wants it *now*, not at some nebulous future point, not at some distant time. Wants it as he is and as Zuko is and figuring the rest out along the way, and…Zuko is good. He’s very good with that.

Sokka takes a slow, deep breath, shoulders relaxing even as his fingers tense against the control panel behind him, and Zuko isn’t sure which of those two things to focus on. “And, uh—you?”

Zuko…wonders if he blacked out for a bit there. ‘You’ what?

“You, um…just before, you said that you’re—that you could be all in?” Sokka licks his lips, searching Zuko’s face, clearly holding himself back from fidgeting. “What does—what does that mean to you?”

Zuko almost laughs, hearing his own question thrown back at him. At the idea of being able to put into words everything that Sokka is to him: unguarded smiles and puns and curiosity; being able to melt against the lines of a cool body and know that he can just stop thinking; his inner fire bright and spiraling and eager like it wants to crawl inside Sokka and live there forever; an anchor against his spinning thoughts, one that’s new but steady and constant; a challenge, both playful and serious, to do better than he did before. How can Zuko wrap words around the way he wants to wind himself around Sokka and be able to hold him in the circle of his arms and feel their breaths and hearts falling in sync and know that he never has to let go?

“It means that I want this,” Zuko finally says, aware of how insufficient his words sound in the quiet. “Not just wanting to—do stuff with you. Which I do,” he hastens to add, feeling himself blush as Sokka clears his throat. “But more—or just as much—or.” Another deep breath. “I want you with me. And I want to be with you. I want there to be a—a space, by your side, that’s mine. And I want you to feel the same way about me. I want us to be… partners.”

Zuko‘s talking to Sokka’s boots now, about as much of Sokka as he can take in and still be able to say this. “And I—I want you to feel…safe, with me. To tell me stuff. And to come to me with your problems, and the things that go well, too, and the things you want. And to ask me for help, and just…keep sharing the random things you wonder about, like whether Momo has nice dreams.” Sokka lets out a choked, wet-sounding laugh, and Zuko doesn’t know what to make of that.

“There’s no part of you that I don’t want,” Zuko says, shifting his weight and trying not to hunch, not to fold himself against all the ways he’s laying himself open right now. “And I don’t ever want to stop wanting that. In a year I still want to want that, and in five—and, yeah. I’m…yeah. That’s…that’s what I mean.”

A beat of silence is all Zuko can stand before he risks a glance up to find Sokka already staring back at him, eyes wide and lips half-parted. “Right,” Sokka finally whispers, licking his lips. “I…think I get the picture.”

He’s looking more than a little stunned, which…well, Zuko is a little surprised by himself, too, that he managed to get it all out. He just…needs to keep that going to get the last bit out, too, the thing he needs to make sure Sokka understands out of all the rest of it, so Zuko doesn’t wreck himself against the possibility of them.

“Sokka, I can wait for you to be sure, if you aren’t,” Zuko says, gripping the railing when Sokka glances up sharp and alarmed at whatever he’s hearing in Zuko’s tone. “But I need you to take the time, then. If you tell me it’s okay to want this? And we try and things don’t work out? Then—” Then Zuko doesn’t know what he would do. “—then that’s fine. But if you tell me it’s okay, and you aren’t sure yet if you *can* try?” Zuko forces himself to meet Sokka’s eyes, to shove away the out-of-rhythm twist of his inner flame over the fresh anxiety he sees there. “I need you to be sure.”

“Okay,” Sokka says, a bit shaky at first but slowly settling as he studies Zuko’s face. “That’s —that makes sense. I get that. I mean I—yes. I’m sure. I’m really sure, Zuko.”

Zuko hesitates, his inner fire wound so tight with the urge to tip over the edge that it’s a miracle he isn’t bolting out of this room right now, the only thing keeping him here the fact that it would mean leaving whatever this is conversation unfinished. “…Do you need to think about it?” Zuko…is not *unfamiliar* with the time it takes Sokka to work things over.

“I’ve thought about it,” Sokka says quickly, firmly, making a face at…himself, Zuko thinks. “I mean—” His eyes fly up, suddenly uncertain. “I can think about it more? If you want me to be extra sure? “…You already thought about it,” Zuko repeats, part of him distantly wondering why he feels the need to echo the sentiment when it’s not like anyone in the Temple could have been unaware of the depth and extent of Sokka’s *thinking about it* over the past weeks.

“I want this, Zuko,” Sokka says quietly, straightening and taking a deep breath. “Everything you said, and—and being able to help you, and knowing that you’re there to help me, too. Sokka shifts on his feet, face still set with conviction but fingers going white where they’re tangled in the loose end of his wrist wrap, and Zuko…doesn’t know how to reply, not when his inner fire is burning so high that Zuko isn’t sure where he starts and where his inner flame begins, not when warmth is rooting in his chest and sliding through his body and stealing every coherent thought Zuko has along with it. It would be really, really inconvenient to pass out right now. So Zuko better remember how to breathe.

“Oh,” he finally manages, finally managing to claw his way back to monosyllables, digging his fingers into the railing behind him and trying to shove the heat trying to build and build in him out into the metal, trying to find his breath control and his balance and his rhythm when it feels like all he can do is stare at Sokka and replay his words over and over again and think *yes, yes, yes.*

“Sorry if that was a lot,” Sokka adds after a long moment, tugging on his wolf tail, and Zuko is already shaking his head before the words are even all the way out.

“No, it was—it was great,” Zuko says, as if any words can ever be enough to describe it. “It…it was good.”

“Well good, then,” Sokka says, slowly leaning back against the control console.

Zuko lets the silence fall, stealing the space to let Sokka’s words settle over him, to let the implication of them land, to shrug them on and move with them now a part of him and with his inner flame burning alongside them, to get used to standing with the ground suddenly that much more solid beneath his feet. One of his three most important things not only in grasp, but reaching along with him, if Zuko could ever work up the nerve to ask.

Zuko drags himself out of his thoughts he Sokka finally stirs, glancing up to see the question settling over his face, Sokka seeming to take the eye contact as some kind of signal. “Can I ask you something, though?”

“How will it all work?”

“Okay,” Zuko finally manages to say, inner fire turning back on itself with pent-up frustration that suddenly has no place to land because Sokka seems…totally fine with Zuko not being able to do this. “We…can do that,” he adds, which just seems to relax Sokka even more, which…okay. Zuko…can work with that. With a promise to consider it, he supposes, and give it the time and attention it deserves. Zuko can do that.

“Good,” Sokka says softly, his fingers finally relaxing, expression turning a lot more sheepish when he looks down and notices the trailing edge of his wrist wrap. “That’s—I’m looking forward to it.”

Sokka focuses on redoing his wrist wrap in the silence that follows, movements careful and precise as he places layer after layer of linen around his forearm, strip after strip that hides the splash of his burn scar, pale even against this skin that sees so much less of the sun. Zuko paces his breathing to Sokka’s motions, trying to shove away the slow thread of tension that wants to settle into his hands and shoulders and chest and Agni, all through his body, until finally Zuko can’t take it anymore.

“Is that…” Sokka immediately glances up, face open with question, and after a brief struggle with himself Zuko decides they might as well get it all out in one go, if that’s what they’re doing. “Is that all?” Zuko shifts when Sokka’s fingers pause, his brow furrowing in confusion. “Is there…anything else you need from me? That you want to ask me?”

“…No?”

That…wasn’t what Zuko was bracing for.

It’s Sokka’s turn to shift, hands fluttering as he seems to consciously pull them away from his wrists. “Is there something you want me to ask?”

Not really, but, “You…didn’t ask me about the plan. When I left Ba Sing Se, or after, or…” Zuko trails off with a helpless little shrug, ignoring the way his inner fire is shoving in protest against him even giving this voice if Sokka didn’t raise it in the first place.

“Oh,” Sokka says, expression clearing, “That.” Zuko fixes his eyes on the way Sokka’s shoulders are relaxing back, trying to keep the nervous energy from finding its way back into his limbs as Sokka studies his face, looking like he’s cycling through multiple different responses before finally saying carefully, “Do you want to tell me?”

Not…really. Zuko *can* but…fuck, how far back would Zuko need to go for Sokka to hear it all and not think he’s crazy? For Sokka to not immediately try to talk Zuko out of it, or fuck, set himself against it? Zuko’s certain that Sokka would support the end goal, but Zuko’s chosen approach? That he’s a lot less sure of, and Agni, what if Sokka hears it and can’t look at Zuko the same after once he realizes the kinds of things Zuko is willing to do?

Shit, does that mean Sokka has the right to know, then? That Sokka needs to know, even though he’s standing here right now shaking his head.

“I trust you, Zuko,” Sokka says, eyes direct, like it’s that simple. “You’ll tell me when you’re ready, right?”

Well yeah, it will be kind of hard not to, but— “You don’t—you’re okay with that? You… were upset. Before. About not knowing.” Very, very upset…

“I…yeah,” Sokka acknowledges with a sigh, shoving a hand through his hair. “But…You know it. And you know what we’re doing, too, and you’ll be part of any planning.” Zuko blinks at the easiness with which Sokka says that, like Zuko’s inclusion is already a given. “So you’ll notice if there’s something we can help you with, or that you can help us with, right?”

“Yeah,” Zuko agrees cautiously after a moment. The Avatar’s crew isn’t exactly a secretive bunch, assuming none of the new additions change that dynamic.

“Then you have it covered,” Sokka shrugs. “And I mean, I want to help, obviously. I want to hear it. But I don’t *need* to know, not before you want to tell me.” Sokka’s expression goes wry, a spark of humor in his eyes. “I can’t exactly take a stand against someone needing time, here.”

Zuko wants to cling to that levity, to take what Sokka is offering, but he just—he needs to make sure this is okay first. “It’s…hard for me. To say certain things,” Zuko says, not quite an apology, but… “And this…it’s mine, but it’s about more than just me. It’s—I promised certain things, and not everything is mine to tell, and—”

“I get it, Zuko,” Sokka breaks in quietly, eyes serious again. “I do, it’s—look, do you think I’d support what you’re trying to do?

Zuko bites back his immediate response and forces himself to actively think about the question, weighing again everything he’s heard Sokka say about the Fire Nation and revenge and vengeance and walking away from wrongs and making things right. “Yes,” he finally says. “I think so.”

“And would I be okay with *how* the plan works?

“…You wouldn’t do it the same way,” Zuko says after a beat. “But it’s not…compromising your ethics, or anything.” Zuko’s honor, on the other hand…but then, that’s already in ashes.

“Then it’s good,” Sokka says, nodding like Zuko just said something particularly decisive. “As long as you feel good about it, Zuko.” A pause, when Zuko just stares, trying to breathe around the sudden lightness kindled in his chest, deep behind his rubs and burning nearly as hot as his inner flame. “Do, uh—” Sokka tugs on his wolf tail. “*Do* you feel good about it?”

“…Good isn’t really an emotion I associate with it.”

Sokka visibly flounders a moment. “Okay, but—you know what I mean?”

“Yeah,” Zuko relents, allowing himself to slump back against the railing a bit as that lightness eases into a more familiar warmth, into something that can wind through his limbs and exist in the hollow spaces within his body. “It’s…yeah.”

“Alright then,” Sokka says, relaxing back too. “Good. That’s good.”

It…is. It really is, and Zuko closes his eyes for a moment, grounding himself on it, letting himself silently repeat it and feel it echo in his inner flame and wrap into its rhythm until it finally starts to feel like a fact.

“So…” Zuko finally says into the silence, opening his eyes to see Sokka already quietly looking at him, which does something slow and warm in his gut. “Does that mean—Are we together? Dating, or…?” Have they agreed? Fuck, were they even trying to agree? Zuko’s lost the thread of this entirely.

“I mean—” Sokka looks suddenly nervous, something hopeful and eager and trying-not-to-get-too-excited which Zuko is more than familiar enough with to recognize. “Yes? And I know we just said a lot so only if you want to, obviously—"

“*Yes*, I want to.” Agni, Zuko could burn this airship to the ground with how much he ‘wants to’ right now.

“That’s…good,” Sokka says, laughing a little and tugging on his hair. “Because I do too, so…that means yeah, right?”

“Dating?” Zuko presses, because he needs to be absolutely sure but Agni’s *balls*, Zuko can feel his hands wrapped so tightly around the railing that his knuckles are starting to ache, his inner fire straining again, every part of him teetering on the edge of control to be cut loose.

“Dating,” Sokka echoes, a slow smile beginning to bloom over his face as he mouths the word again to himself, and Zuko’s inner fire is fucking *crawling* against the underside of his skin with how badly he wants to taste that smile. “Dating…sounds good. I’d like that.”

Dating. They’re dating. They’re *dating*, and Zuko nearly shudders because he feels like he’s going to break this railing in fucking half with how hard he’s squeezing it, trying to hold back from closing the distance between them and cutting his fire free, but they’re *dating,* and that means he doesn’t have to anymore.
