“…What?” Zuko pulls back to frown at Sokka’s face, absently adjusting to sit more comfortably across Sokka’s lap which…will never *not* be a sight, and Sokka will let himself get distracted by it right after this.

“I just noticed that we—that we didn’t…” Sokka takes a breath and forces himself to start again. “I know I don’t always know what I’m doing all the time. With this stuff. Sex stuff,” he clarifies, glancing away as Zuko’s frown edges toward a scowl, because Sokka’s aware that Zuko *does* know, more than Sokka at least, and that’s fine, it is, that’s not the point, but… “But we can do things other ways. Sometimes. Right?” He trails off, suddenly uncertain, because Zuko isn’t looking any less confused and…maybe Sokka *isn’t* right?

“…What?”

“We usually do things a certain way,” Sokka says carefully, part of his mind frantically reassessing every dirty joke and half-glimpsed erotic scroll and offhand comment Sokka’s ever heard, trying to figure out how he could have put them all together wrong. “And it’s not that things aren’t good that way,” Sokka says quickly, because being about to watch Zuko come apart is…fucking divine. “But it’s also okay if you want to…try something different? I guess is what I’m saying?” Like taking Sokka from behind, caging him in a different way, so that Sokka can’t see what’s going to come next, so that Zuko’s hands and voice and body are the only things holding him together. “That would be okay with me, and just…if you weren’t sure, I guess I just…wanted to say it, and…yeah.”

“I…Sokka, you say my name a lot,” Zuko finally says, cheek dusting with a blush because they both know that Zuko loves it. “Why…why wouldn’t I know that you know it’s me?”

“You just…” Fuck, Sokka can feel himself getting flustered, which is *not* helpful right now, and is really messing with his afterglow. “You know you have a thing for me watching you, right?” And Spirits, now that Sokka thinks about it maybe he has been a bit slow on the uptake for not seriously considering that Zuko’s discomfort with being stared at seems to check itself at the bedroom door. That exhibitionist streak might be deeper than Sokka realized.

“I…” Zuko stares at him, lips parted, nothing coming out, and Sokka can only stare back as surprise robs him of words. Looking at Zuko between cell bars, catching molten gold eyes from across battlefields, Zuko demanding to be seen—this is so fundamentally a part of what they do by this point, has so obviously been Zuko’s thing from the very beginning, that Sokka never even considered that Zuko might *not* know.

“Zuko,” Sokka says again, a nearly numb disbelief rising in his chest. “*Zuko*.”

“No, I *know*,” Zuko huffs, glowering at Sokka without any real heat behind when Sokka lets out an audible sigh of relief. “I know that. I just don’t get—Sokka, when we—You say my name a *lot*.”

“I guess I just noticed,” Sokka says carefully, “That you didn’t, um. Use your hands? In the way you usually do, not until we…more toward the end.” Not until Sokka was spun around and facing him again, when before Zuko was making him feel amazing but also not really touching Sokka’s dick. Which is *fine*, Sokka is more than on board for a good tease and riding out the anticipation. Just…as long as that’s what it was. Because Zuko might like it when Sokka watches him now, but Sokka is positive down to his bones that Zuko used to need it in a very different way. “And it’s not that it wasn’t good, it was great, I loved it, I just —also noticed that.”

A blank moment, then comprehension finally dawns over Zuko’s face, almost immediately followed by hesitation as Zuko visibly searches for words. “It’s not because I think you don’t know it’s me,” Zuko finally says, which it’s honestly a relief to hear because Sokka’s fairly sure it didn’t use to be that way back at the start of this thing between them.

“…But there is a reason?”

Zuko sighs, giving Sokka a sideways look. “I…need to be able to see your face. If I’m going to…” Zuko’s fingers wiggle against Sokka’s ribs. “You know.”

Sokka blinks, then again, trying to readjust his understanding who is needing what. “Oh.”

Zuko’s expression turns shy, even as his voice goes firm. “I need to see that it’s still okay.”

Sokka wouldn’t dream of pushing against that firmness, but he can’t fully shove aside the stab of worry in his chest. “You know I like it. Right?”

“I know. And I like giving it to you.” Well, that’s a fucking relief to have re-confirmed, given all that could have happened to either of them in the past few months. “But I need to know you’re struggling because you want to. Not because you want out. And the heat…I need to know before it ever gets close to being too much.”

Sokka nods, slow, rubbing circles over Zuko’s sides as he readjusts his understanding, feeling Zuko loosen into the motion and his own uncertainty fading away as he walks back through what just happened with this in mind. “Okay. I…That makes sense. I get that.”

Zuko hesitates, halfway to cuddling again before leaning back to fully look at Sokka’s face. “That’s fine? Good?”

Sokka checks the relaxed feel of Zuko under his hands, the question on his face, the lack of anxious tension. “Yeah,” he says, smiling and gently tugging Zuko back into his arms, pressing his lips to Zuko’s hair when Zuko easily folds back into him. “It’s good, Zuko. It’s great.” And in this little moment, with Zuko pressing a quick kiss to his neck before settling himself back against Sokka’s body, everything in Sokka’s world really is.

&#45;-

It takes long enough for them to finally stir themselves to get up and clean up and find their way off the ship—Sokka’s rumbling stomach is the true driver of that and he refuses to feel any shame about it—that Sokka’s starting to feel stiff and tight, bruises he didn’t have the time or mental capacity to pay attention to making themselves loudly known. And maybe some fresh ones, too, little speckles over his hip that would follow the spread of Zuko’s fingers, ones that are much more pleasant to focus on.

Sokka isn’t surprised by how much he likes that idea. Still, he tries to nudge it toward the back of his thoughts as he sets himself to tracking down his sister since some things should never occupy the same mental landscape. When he finally finds her, though, Katara seems to be having some kind of intense conversation with Dad, so Sokka pivots to finding the next best thing when it comes to getting stuff destroyed around here.

“Hey Toph,” Sokka says cheerfully, walking with…well, with an Aang-worthy bounce to his step over to where she and Aang seem to be hanging with bated breath onto Suki’s retelling of their escape. “I could use some help destroying some evidence.”

“I’m here for it,” Toph says immediately. “What are we destroying?”

Suki gives him an arch look. “And evidence of what?”

“A Fire Nation airship. And don’t worry about it.”

Suki snorts under Toph’s excitement exclamation. “And where’s Crown Prince Zuko?”

“*Zuko*,” Sokka emphasizes, “Is figuring out what we’re having for dinner.”

“Obviously stir fry,” Aang says, offering a shrug when they all look at him. “Zuko always makes stir fry. It’s good.”

“Useful,” Suki murmurs, glancing back at Sokka. “How long did it take you to domesticate him?”

“Oh,” Sokka says, still cheerful but showing a bit more teeth in his smile. “A person picks up all kinds of useful skills when they’re a fugitive in the Earth Kingdom wanted by all the nations.”

Suki purses her lips. “I suppose you would.”

Aang jumps in with his usual touch for redirection. “Your dad is talking with Katara.”

“I saw,” Sokka says.

“She got everyone settled, I think. We found rooms for all the adults. The Fire Nation ones wanted to stick together.”

Sokka glances at Suki, who tilts her head back and forth, considering. “They’re cool,” she says after a moment. “They’re used to being close together. Cell neighbors.”

“Did she put them near Zuko?” Sokka asks.

“Twinkletoes wanted everyone closer to the main plaza,” Toph says.

“Zuko’s too far away!” Aang protests, “He’s part of the group, he should be close, even with all the noise.”

Suki frowns. “Even with all the what now?”

“Don’t worry about it,” Sokka says.

“If all the adults have rooms,” Toph says mock-thoughtfully, with her usual instinct for potential chaos. “Does that make Zuko an adult?”

“…He fucking better be,” Sokka mutters, low enough for only Suki to hear, her choked-back laugh distracting Aang from his clear and open indecision over the question.

“Come on,” Suki says, voice still tinged with amusement as she rises to feet. “Let’s go find Chit Sang. He’ll probably love to smash some symbols of Fire Nation imperialism, too.”

“I’ll go check out how much metal there is in the meantime,” Toph grins, cracking her knuckles.

“…I’ll make sure the temple doesn’t come down,” Aang says, hurrying after her.

“So,” Sokka says as he walks with Suki toward, presumably, Chit Sang’s room. “Chit Sang’s one of those types, huh?”

“Don’t worry,” Suki says, giving him a quick, sideways look. “Your boy is safe.”

“Zuko can handle himself,” Sokka says immediately, as if he weren’t worrying for exactly the reason she thinks.

“Hm.”

Sokka takes a deep breath, his languor and general cheer beginning to fade away against the need to pick back up the practical realities. “I know that working together on a mission means we sometimes put aside things we care about,” Sokka starts carefully, “And I know the last time you saw Zuko it…”

“Wasn’t the best?”

“Sure,” Sokka says, shooting her a quick, nervous look, unsure of just how sarcastic that was meant to be. “So if you don’t want to—"

“You better not be about to suggest that I leave,” Suki says with deceptive mildness.

“…Okay.”

She eyes him a moment, then softens slightly. “I do want to find my girls,” she acknowledges, “But I know they can handle themselves. I can help more staying with you guys, for now at least.”

“We’d be happy to have you,” Sokka says, something loosening in his chest. Suki’s reserve seemed to fade over the course of the past few days, but Sokka can’t forget her initial wariness, or the knowledge that just because Zuko is dating—*dating*—him and Suki is friends with him, that doesn’t mean Zuko and Suki are anything to each other. “*I’d* be happy to have you.”

“Good,” Suki says, giving him a quick smile before her expression slides toward something much more devious. “So. How long has this whole thing been going on?”

Spirits, Sokka can already feel himself blushing. He needs to get better about sharing this, but where to even begin. “It’s complicated.”

“I’ve heard that before,” she says, rolling her eyes. “And I’ll repeat, it’s not that hard. Time isn’t really that complicated of a concept.” Said with all the ease of someone who’s never had to pinpoint the start of something they weren’t even sure existed until they were already in it.

“A few weeks after we were at Kyoshi Island, I guess. Kind of. Depending on how you’re counting. Or—I was a prisoner on his ship for a bit. So. Maybe then? Though there was this thing with this temple that kind of got wrecked and I guess there was a moment, and—”

“His propensity for property damage spoke to you?”

Sokka flushes. He does *not* want to get into what exactly spoke to him about the Fire Prince that early in things. “I didn’t—that’s not—that wasn’t his finest moment,” he finishes lamely.

“I’m sure,” she says, dry.

Sokka can feel his blush trying to creep down his neck, partially off-balance which is…a usual way for him to feel around Suki, actually. “He’s changed, since then.”

Suki hums, looking thoughtful. “I guess so.”

Sokka opens his mouth, ready to argue the point and then pausing as he registers her easy agreement. “…You believe me?” Sure, Sokka’s been saying that ever since that first conversation in Suki’s cell, but…he isn’t used to people actually agreeing so soon.

Maybe Suki finds working together to escape from a maximum-security prison by the skin of their teeth to be character-revealing, because Sokka isn’t sure he’s gotten all that much better at making his point.

“War makes you grow up fast,” Suki finally says, expression serious when she glances at him. “And war makes it easy to be someone you don’t want to be. To do things you don’t want to do. Not that I’m not still pissed about him burning my village, because trust me, I am, and we will have words. But he didn’t have to go into the coolers.”

“I mean…it made sense.” Even if Sokka absolutely hated it, still hates it, kind of wants to track Zuko down and wrap himself around him thinking about it just to reassure himself that he’s warm and safe.

“He didn’t have to stay, either. He could have gone with Chit Sang—and I don’t want to hear whatever you’re opening your mouth to say, what are you trying to do, argue against him?” Sokka clamps his mouth shut. “He fought his sister. That’s not a thing to do lightly in the Fire Nation.”

“No,” Sokka agrees after a moment. “I guess not.” And Sokka once again wonders about Zuko’s sister, but Sokka would feel miserable fighting Katara in earnest, and Zuko’s voice had rung with nothing but truth when he said that he didn’t want to fight Azula back on that platform.

“And besides,” Suki adds, pulling him back into the conversation. “He seems very into you. So I figure we’ve got something in common, at least.”

Sokka chokes on his surprise, wheezing as Suki lets out a peal of laughter.

“Calm down, I’m just teasing,” she says, before slanting a wicked grin in his direction. “Unless you guys ever want to mix it up. Then let me know. I can see what all the fuss is about.”

&#45;-

Sokka lets out a relieved breath as he manages to tiptoe out of the plaza without being seen. He timed it well, gathering up his bedding and slipping away in the quiet bustle of heading to bed, hitting the time after the adults already left but before everyone else finishes saying goodnight to Appa and—

“Going somewhere, Snoozles?” Sokka strangles back a shriek, fumbling his bedroll as he whirls to see Toph lounging in a doorway, tossing a shard of what has to be Fire Nation airship from hand to hand before suddenly aiming it in his direction. “Told you so.”

“Wha—you what?” Sokka asks, heart pounding as he finally gets his things firmly back into his arms.

“Shacking up. You didn’t even make it six months.”

“Toph!” Sokka hisses, glancing around in case anyone else is hiding in another doorway. “I’m not—we aren’t—stay out of it!”

Toph makes a show of rolling her eyes as she shoves off the lintel into the hallway. “How’s your carving coming along, Loverboy,” she asks, her unerring accuracy as she starts tossing that piece of metal again slightly unnerving. “Sparrowkeet seems like he likes himself some jewelry.”

Sokka sputters, floundering for a moment before he remembers that engaging with Toph has never left anyone’s dignity intact. He clutches his bedroll more firmly under his arm and mutters a borderline ill-natured goodnight, stalking away for the stairway to the third floor to the sound of her laughter.

It isn’t until Sokka actually *gets* to Zuko’s room that he realizes he wasn’t exactly invited. He’d just assumed that—well, he’d just assumed. Sokka freezes in the doorway, wondering how to avoid barging in with all his expectations on display given that he’s fucking clutching them in his arms.

But then Zuko glances up from where he’s toeing off his boots and smiles, pure welcome and not a hint of confusion on his face, as if of course Sokka would be here, as if it wasn’t even a question in his mind. Sokka grins back, feeling maybe more than a little stupid-happy over it, but it’s fucking late, and the days have been fucking long, and Sokka doesn’t care. They’re *dating*, officially, talked about and agreed upon. He shouldn’t *have* to play this cool anymore.

Sokka tosses his things down onto Zuko’s bed, spreading out his blanket and setting his pillow neatly next to Zuko’s and promptly freezing, staring. They’ve never actually had more than one pillow before, if they had one at all, and seeing the two next to each other is… weirdly domestic. But also unexpectedly uncomfortable, jarring in a way Sokka didn’t anticipate, like it’s defining two separate spaces on the low sleeping platform, one part Sokka’s and one part Zuko’s where before it’s just been theirs. Now it looks less shared and more like ‘stay on your side and ask permission before entering,’ and—

“Sokka. Just do whatever you need to do to the bed.”

“Huh?”

“Whatever you need to do so you stop glaring at it,” Zuko says, barefoot and with his overtunic off and looking so *approachable* even as he stays on the other side of the room. “And then we can sleep.”

Sokka stares at him for a moment, then glances back to the bed, belatedly finishing kicking off his own boots. “It’s not a big deal,” he hedges. This is just—weird, and not even a thing, and Sokka will get over it when he gets used to it.

Zuko gives him a careful look. “It’s making you uncomfortable.”

“It’s stupid.”

Zuko rubs the back of his head, giving the bed his own skeptical glance. “Sokka,” he finally says, face open with a kind of quiet, voluntary candor that Sokka’s rarely seen. Hopefully it’s not just a byproduct of tiredness. “We can sleep on the stone floor without blankets if that’s what you’re into. I’m sure we’ve both slept in worse places than that. Make yourself comfortable. Please.”

Sokka wavers a moment longer, then just—goes with what he wants, because he can always put it *back,* it’s not like it’s a permanent thing, it shouldn’t be a big deal let alone an active effort to grab his pillow and toss it onto the floor, but he’s already second-guessing himself as half-turning back to Zuko because Spirits, he’s being *dumb* it’s just a *pillow*.

“Huh,” Zuko yawns, finally moving toward the bed. “Good idea.”

Then Zuko’s slipping past Sokka, casually going body to body with a little absent hum of acknowledgment as he climbs into bed. He tugs a stunned Sokka down after him and Sokka lets himself be pulled, because he isn’t quite done being surprised by the lack of questions and he hasn’t entirely caught his breath at the reality of that casual contact.

The bed isn’t the most comfortable thing Sokka’s ever laid on, and there’s a brief awkward negotiation over blankets that they’ve never had to do before because there’s only ever been one of those, too. But then Zuko drapes himself in that boneless sprawl of his over Sokka, exactly where Sokka wants him and easily solving the problem, shamelessly using Sokka as a pillow and letting out a little sleepy noise of contentment that lands right in the center of Sokka’s chest.

Sokka almost wants to force himself to stay awake, to soak in every bit of this moment that he can. But then, he doesn’t have to do that anymore. This isn’t Ba Sing Se, there isn’t a fixed time limit on how long they have with each other. And as Sokka slowly drifts to sleep to the sound of Zuko’s even breathing he finally lets himself actually believe, for the first time since the eclipse, that maybe everything is going to turn out okay.

## Chapter 22: The Weight of Memory

### Notes

#### Chapter Notes

No particular warnings for this one!

### Text

Zuko is feeling a bone-deep kind of rightness with the world after waking up tangled with Sokka, something that he hasn’t felt since…well, he can’t remember the last time he felt like this. Rising gently from sleep as Agni’s touch prickles through his blood, the slow awareness of legs tangled with his own and the steady beat of a heart beneath his ear, sliding easily into meditating to the pulse of Sokka’s almost-flame again—it sets Zuko’s own inner fire sparkling with an uncharacteristic lightness.

The feeling lasts through Sokka slowly waking up, the shy exchange of smiles and close-mouthed kisses, hands interfering more than helping with getting dressed. It lasts right up until Zuko trails Sokka into the main plaza for breakfast, walking well within Sokka’s personal space and glorying more than a little in being there, and finds himself meeting a pair of icy, guarded eyes.

Katara, Zuko realizes, must get both her eyes and her tendency to wake up early from her father. Because Zuko’s finding that getting unexpectedly pinned by that assessing, flay-your-skin-off-to-see-what’s-beneath stare feels painfully familiar first thing in the morning.

Zuko’s steps stutter before he can check himself, instinctively putting distance between himself and Sokka even as Zuko reminds himself that he’s supposed to be here, that he isn’t intruding in the Air Temple. Sokka wants Zuko here, wants Zuko with *him,* said it in so many different ways yesterday that there’s no way Zuko can doubt it, and so do Aang and Toph, and Teo and Haru and even Suki seem at least neutral on the topic. And Katara might *not*, but she’s closer to neutral than she used to be, and besides, there’s only one of her, and Zuko’s vote definitely cancels hers out anyway. And fuck, Hakoda wouldn’t even *be* here without Zuko, so why should Zuko be the one feeling suddenly knocked off-balance?

Zuko forcefully snaps his eyes back up, his inner fire snapping in satisfaction when Hakoda leans back slightly in surprise at Zuko’s glare. Zuko can feel a flush trying to climb up his neck as he takes a few quick strides to catch up to Sokka and he will *not* let it, but Agni’s tits, he’s suddenly hyperconscious of the fact that he can still feel the echo of Sokka against his skin. He knots his fingers against the urge to touch all those lingering points of coolness and frantically sorts through years of etiquette for something that could apply here.

Courting rules? But no, they’ve already declared themselves to each other. Crown Prince of the Fire Nation greeting the Chief of the Southern Water Tribe? That feels…presumptuous, on a number of fronts.

Shit. Zuko knows how to be with Sokka, and he’s grown more comfortable with that around the rest of the crew, but he’s never been *together* with Sokka in front of anyone except Uncle. And definitely not in front of people that Sokka knew and cared about and valued the opinions of, the kind of people Zuko’s supposed to impress. And so far, all Zuko’s done in front of Hakoda is lose to his little sister and known where to get some bandages.

Fuck. Not that Zuko wants to *stop* being together, but courting rules might actually be kind of nice to be able to fall back on right now.

“Sokka,” Zuko says, low and urgent before they get close enough to be overheard.

“Hm?” Sokka glances back, then immediately slows, a little divot forming between his brows as he searches Zuko’s face. Zuko can only imagine what his expression looks like, if it’s showing even a fraction of his sudden off-footedness, his inner fire coiling with readiness.

“Does—does your father know? About…me? Us,” he clarifies, when Sokka just gives him a look of blank confusion.

“Oh.” Sokka’s face clears. “No.”

Zuko comes to a stop, Sokka swinging around to face him, and Agni, Zuko is *very* aware that this is happening in full view, if not earshot, of both Sokka’s father *and* Katara. Though it’s not like this is anything she doesn’t already know anyway….

“Is there a reason?” Zuko asks carefully, searching Sokka’s face and abruptly wondering if he needs to be prepared for a whole different kind of hostility than he’s been thinking of. Zuko knows how the North is, after all, but—Sokka’s never seemed concerned about it. And Katara’s issues have never seemed to be with the fact that Zuko is a *guy,* so Zuko just…kind of assumed the South was different?

“Well, I wanted to tell him back when I saw him a few months ago outside of Ba Sing Se,” Sokka shrugs, looking significantly less anxious than Zuko would expect him to be about it if the Tribes *were* united in this, which…feels like a good thing. “But I wanted to check with you first before I did anything, and you were pretty out of it when you were sick. And then, well…”

“…Oh,” Zuko says, belatedly placing the ‘when’ Sokka is referring to. Zuko would have been at the very best incoherent if Sokka had tried to ask him anything, and more likely unconscious.

“So not like a *reason* reason, other than timing, I guess,” Sokka says, eyes flicking down to Zuko’s shoulders before settling back on his face, hesitating a moment. “Do *you* want him to know?”

Zuko opens his mouth and then promptly closes it again. His instinctive reaction is a hard ‘no. Not because he necessarily wants to hide what he has with Sokka, but Zuko is wary of drawing any kind of attention from authority in general, most days, and this kind of authority in particular. And because every part of Zuko’s life has taught him that offering up this kind of ammunition to someone he isn’t entirely sure of is borderline suicidal. And regardless of what Sokka might say sometimes, Zuko isn’t *actually* trying to get himself killed.

Still, this is *Sokka’s* father—Sokka’s *dad*, which…feels different. And Zuko’s aware that Hakoda’s involvement in and approval of Sokka’s life is deeply important to Sokka in ways that Zuko certainly can’t judge. “It’s up to you,” he finally offers, wincing as he hears the reluctance underpinning the words.

Sokka makes an unconvinced noise he eyes Zuko, letting the silence drag out like maybe Zuko will change his mind. “Let's think about it,” Sokka finally decides, and if Zuko has the distinct sense that Sokka’s only saying that because Zuko’s the one who’s unsure, he still can’t help being grateful for it.

&#45;-

The day starts with an extra dose of chaos with five new people to fit into the usual routine. And food was already tight and is rapidly becoming a more immediate concern that will require foraging to remedy, even with the travel stores they pulled off the airship along with healing supplies, spare clothes, some much-needed salt, and enough pepper paste to make Sokka’s mouth tingle after kissing Zuko.

And before he deals with any of that Sokka needs another healing session just to make sure everything with his side stays not-bleeding, which means he needs to do laundry so he can wear the tunic that doesn't come wholly apart when it's undone since he doesn't want Katara looking too closely at his *other* side after Zuko dotted his fingerprints over it, and then Momo decides it’s time for reflexes training with the lunch prep, and then Teo has a question about war balloon design, so it isn’t until nearly dinner that Sokka finally has a moment to breathe.

Sokka finds himself a nice shady spot where he can lean back against a nice smooth section of wall, going through the motions caring for his space sword and mostly watching as Suki and Zuko tentatively exchange hand-to-hand combat moves. There’s so much to worry about and sort out and figure out, but Sokka can’t stop smiling as both of them gradually become less guarded and increasingly enthusiastic. Seeing them already on the way toward something like ease—maybe even friendship, if Sokka’s lucky—ignores something bright and happy in Sokka’s chest, and Spirits, it’s nice to sit with the feeling and the moment of quiet, all of it a welcome respite after the past weeks.

Sokka’s maybe more zoning out to the sight of Zuko trying to learn some twisty, sliding kick thing that Sokka is smugly aware *he* knows how to do when solid footsteps have him sitting up a bit straighter, picking his polishing cloth up again and yanking his eyes studiously back down to his lap.

“That’s quite the sword you have there,” Dad comments as he takes a seat next to Sokka, grunting as he settles back in a way that makes Sokka think his time as a prisoner might have been tougher than he’s letting on. “I didn’t have a chance to admire it before.”

“It is,” Sokka agrees, offering it up for Dad to see. “I haven’t had it for long.”

“Hm,” Dad hums as he examines it, hefting its weight and sizing up the grip. “Fire Nation make?”

“Yeah,” Sokka confirms, refusing to indulge the little flutter of nerves he feels over it. It’s a good sword. Sokka earned it.

“It’s a good blade,” Dad finally says, offering it back with an unreadable glance toward Zuko, who’s suddenly inverted into a handstand to demonstrate…something. Gravity is doing wonderful things to the hem of his tunic, so Sokka isn’t particularly concerned with what. “You’ve grown into quite the swordsman from what I saw yesterday.”

“Thanks,” Sokka grins. “I’ve been doing lots of training.”

“You had a lot of opportunities to learn new things, it seems, since you left the South.”

Sokka just shrugs in response, trailing his fingers over his sword’s pommel, unsure what to say. Dad isn’t wrong, but Sokka can’t tell from his tone if he thinks that’s a good thing or not, and Sokka isn’t used to being unable to read him.

“You’ve done a lot of growing,” Dad adds.

Sokka is starting to get the distinct sense that this is leading into something, his Dad’s usual way of making sure you know he isn’t *mad* right before he starts grilling you about what he’s mad about. Sokka barely resists the urge to sit on his hands to keep his fingers from picking at the edge of his wrist wraps.

“Something I’ve learned, though,” Hakoda continues, face going serious, “Is that no matter how much you’ve already done, a man should never stop trying to be better than he was the day before.”

“Okay,” Sokka says cautiously, because that sentiment sounds great, which means there’s a trap in this somewhere. Sokka hasn’t had one of these conversations in years, but he carries the memories of too many I-know-you-ate-the-last-sea-prune-and-I’m-not-mad-just-disappointed talks to forget what one feels like.

“Breaking into Boiling Rock?” Hakoda catches his eyes, his gaze steady, nearly grave. “I’m glad to not be in there, Sokka. I’m happy to be out of Fire Nation hands. But that was not a smart risk.”

Sokka scowls and looks away, fixing his eyes on where Suki and Zuko seem to be demonstrating ways to deliver a solid heel kick, the unquiet part of him that woke him up gasping in the night, desperate for the reassurance of Zuko’s relaxed weight on top of him, creeping back into his thoughts. Sokka is all-too-aware that it could have just as easily been Zuko on the receiving end of Azula’s fire back on that platform. But it worked out, didn’t it? Doesn’t that mean Sokka can focus on the ‘brilliant and daring’ part, instead of all the ways it could have gone wrong?

“I’m your dad, and you’re my son, and that will always be important,” Hakoda says quietly, and Sokka can feel his eyes on the side of his face. “But I’m also only one man. To risk the Avatar—”

“Aang wasn’t there,” Sokka interrupts, because they weren’t *totally* stupid about it. “He was fine.”

“Would he have been fine if you didn’t come back? If the Prince there didn’t either?”

Sokka bites his tongue, hands wrapped tight around his own wrists because—no, Aang wouldn’t have been okay. In either of those scenarios. But just because Aang would be upset about something doesn’t mean that it shouldn’t be done. If that’s how it worked then all of them would spend the rest of their lives sitting in the Western Air Temple, staying safe while the war raged on without them.

“You have bigger goals than just one person, Sokka,” Hakoda says gently. “Your goals have *always* been bigger than just one person.”

“People are important too,” Sokka says, tight. If Hakoda gave Sokka the responsibility of planning and executing the invasion then how can he turn around and expect Sokka to just walk away from the aftermath? Sokka doesn’t *want* to just walk away, not when it means leaving people behind again, and the idea that he has to, that that’s what he *needs* to do, sits scalding and tight in his throat.

“People are,” Hakoda agrees. “And part of being Chief is being able to keep the big things in mind without losing sight of the individuals. But it’s also not focusing so much on any individual person that you lose the big picture.”

Sokka scowls, glancing away again, eyes automatically coming to rest on Zuko. Who would probably say the same thing, wouldn’t he? Zuko’s all about sacrificing himself as an individual for the bigger picture, which Sokka simultaneously hates and loves about him.

“It’s the worst kind of lesson to learn the hard way,” Hakoda sighs. “But Sokka—don’t sell yourself short. Don’t underestimate what you bring to this group of yours. You’re not so easily replaced if something happens to you.”

“…Okay,” Sokka finally forces out, aware that Katara would probably be the first to tell Sokka—again, and at even greater length—just how bad a risk they took. And that Toph and Aang probably wouldn’t be that far behind.

Sokka didn’t think he was tied up in needing to prove himself and his worth the way he was a few months ago, but…maybe he still needs the reminder.

“I’d say don’t do it again,” Hakoda says after a moment. “But it’s not exactly for me to say anymore.” He offers a small smile when Sokka looks over, startled. “You’re a man of the Southern Water Tribe, Sokka. But you’re also your own man. I might be Chief, but I can’t make your choices for you. So I’ll just say, as a father—don’t do it alone next time. And,” he tacks on, voice suddenly dry, “Don’t hide it from your sister just because you know she’s going to shut you down.”

&#45;-

Sokka is making his way back to the plaza after wrapping up the last of the post-lunch cleanup to join Zuko for some caring-for-weapons-but-mostly-just-being-near-each-other time when he rounds the corner and nearly trips to see that Hakoda got there first.

It isn’t inherently *bad*, but Sokka feels like he’s looking at a cabbage cart flipping over in slow motion as Hakoda leans over to say something and Zuko’s hand jerks against Sokka’s boomerang-like he's about to go from just sitting with the weapon on his lap to wielding it.

“Hey,” Sokka calls, breaking into a quick jog. “What are you guys up to?”

“I noticed that the Prince here had your boomerang,” Hakoda says, giving Sokka a smile that seems genuine even if his eyes are edged with wariness and confusion. “I know it’s not the same as caring for a set of blades like these—” A head tilt for Zuko’s dao, which has Zuko’s hand nearly jerking toward those too. “—so I thought I’d offer a few tips.”

Decided to try to ease into a conversation, more like. Sokka knows exactly how that strategy works. “Zuko’s dealt with boomerangs before,” Sokka says, keeping his tone light and easy, trying to redirect away from whatever about this has Zuko so on edge. “He knows plenty of tips from me, right, buddy?”

Zuko’s answering silence could best be categorized as strangled, and Hakoda leans back slightly as the quiet stretches with no response in sight, shooting Sokka a more openly confused look. Right. Redirection not a success, then.

“Has he,” Hakoda finally says, eyeing Zuko like he isn’t entirely sure of that fact.

“Yup,” Sokka says, barely resisting the urge to tug on his wolf tail which he *knows* Dad will notice. “And Zuko’s taught me a lot about swords, too.”

“...Right,” Hakoda says, nodding, Zuko getting a look like maybe he’s one wrong move away from literally climbing a wall to get out of here.

Drastic measures, then.

“Speaking of learning things,” Sokka says, pasting a bright smile on his face, “Dad, ave you watched one of Katara’s waterbending lessons yet?”

Dad blinks. “No, I haven’t had the—”

“I think you’d really like it!” Sokka cuts in. “Katara’s come so far with her bending, more than just the healing stuff. It’s really impressive.” He goes for the kill. “I think it would make Katara really happy to have you there.”

“Oh,” Dad says slowly, shooting Zuko a quick glance before eyeing Sokka. “I didn’t want to intrude on her time.”

“She definitely won’t think it’s an intrusion!” She…might think it’s an intrusion, depending on what she and Dad have been talking about. But Aang will love it.

“Well, alright, then,” Dad says after a pause, shrugging. “I’ll just leave you two boys to it, then.” He rises to his feet, clapping Sokka on the shoulder and then turning halfway to Zuko like he’s thinking of doing the same before immediately reconsidering and offering some vague hand gesture instead.

Sokka waves after him, tracking his progress away across the plaza more by the steady loosening of Zuko’s shoulders than anything else.

“…You okay?” Sokka asks, settling carefully down across from Zuko and feeling a burst of relief when Zuko immediately shifts close, angling to be within casual touching distance.

Zuko eyes him from beneath his hair for a moment. “Yeah.”

“…Did he say something to you?”

“No,” Zuko says, flicking up a quick, questioning look.

“Because you seem a bit…tense.”

Zuko shrugs, offering Sokka one of his dao and finally picking up the whetstone. “It’s fine.”

Yeah. *Now*. Sokka digs his own whetstone out of his pocket, taking peeks at Zuko’s profile as he begins to work on the blade.

Sokka thought Zuko was starting to settle with the others—letting Toph use him as a heat source, engaging in civil exchanges with Katara, voluntarily going exploring with Teo that one time. And sure, there are more people in the mix now—five more, which is a lot, for a group their size. But Sokka doesn’t like seeing Zuko this jumpy again, and he especially doesn’t like not being entirely sure of *why*.

Is this just how Zuko is with strangers? Sokka…doesn’t exactly have a wealth of observed interaction between Zuko and adults who aren’t his soldiers or his teashop customer to know if this is normal for him, and Zuko at his most calm is usually still strung tighter than Sokka ever realized a person could sustain for the duration of an entire conversation, let alone an entire day.

Except Zuko seems particularly skittish around Hakoda, where the Fire Nation contingent seems to garner something more like clear bemusement and complete non-reaction to the wide-eyed deference Chit Sang’s friends seem to feel compelled to offer him.

Maybe it’s a perceived authority thing? Zuko being aware of the political standing he walked away from relative to a Southern Chief? Or maybe it's a parental figure thing, because Sokka can’t deny that Hakoda seems to be struggling to fit himself into the ‘benignly neglectful and lets us do what we want’ box that they’ve all come to expect from the adults around them by this point. Sokka had nearly choked on his breakfast when Hakoda attempted to take a paternal tone with Toph, who seized the opportunity to be crude and brash in front of a new person who couldn't stop being scandalized. And Suki and Aang both seem incapable of recognizing Hakoda’s bursts of attempted parenting, even if Sokka and Katara keep twitching from learned responses that apparently take more than three years to fade.

And Zuko…Zuko keeps wriggling away before Hakoda even gets the chance. Not that Sokka’s entirely sure his Dad would attempt it given the way he still can’t seem to address Zuko by name and not title...

Yeah, whatever this is? Sokka needs to figure it out.

“You know I’m here if you need anything,” Sokka says, nudging Zuko lightly to make sure he has his attention and feeling a familiar flutter in his throat when Zuko glances up absent and surprised and already half-smiling.

“I know,” Zuko says, nudging Sokka back before bending back to Sokka’s boomerang, and Sokka supposes that’s as good a place to start as any.

&#45;-

The afternoon’s training somehow turns into some hybrid version of tag and capture the flag, because Toph thinks her trainees need to learn the value of precise, minimal attacks even in chaotic circumstances, and because Aang loves a good game, and because everyone else thinks it sounds fun.

They find their way to a nice, open space topside where they can run and dive and bend to their heart’s content without getting close to touching the structural integrity of the Temple, split themselves into teams, and with an arms-flailing war cry, Sokka starts the game.

It’s messy and sloppy and silly and fun. Haru and Suki make a shockingly destructive team, The Duke reveals a real talent for sowing general mayhem, and Toph stomps through the whole thing yelling at her students until the playing area is strewn with new boulders and outcroppings and trenches. The boundary markers have gotten a bit less visible—or outright moved—in the process, but as Sokka huddles with Katara and Aang in a curve of boulders, he’s pretty sure that they’re at least halfway back to their home base with the other team’s flag.

Aang has the bright scrap of fabric clutched in his hands, an eager grin on his face as he gets ready to make a run for it.

“Only earthbending,” Katara reminds him as she takes up her own position on the opposite side of the outcropping.

“I remember!”

“Because you look like you’re about to do your air sprinting thing,” Sokka points out, Katara huffing in amusement.

“I won’t,” Aang assures them, just like he did the last three times.

Sokka rolls his eyes, slithering down to peek around the boulders, taking another look at the course before them. “Okay, so again, if Katara goes left and makes a big distraction, and Aang breaks right after she’s started, I can go at whoever jumps out of cover to try to go for Katara.”

“Heard,” Katara confirms, shifting into a sprinter’s crouch.

“This is great,” Aang enthuses as he slides to his side of the outcropping. “It’s just like old times, but with less danger and more friendship!”

A red-clothed shape suddenly plummets down from above, Zuko barely landing before he’s lunging to grab a startled Aang and lift him straight off his feet, breaking Aang’s root to the earth and neatly recapturing his team’s flag in the process. “Not quite like old times,” Zuko observes wryly.

Aang laughs and squirms to get free, snorting out giggles in a way that makes Sokka suspect that Zuko’s attempts to hold onto his wriggling prize are resulting in no small amount of inadvertent tickling. Sokka can’t hold back his own grin as he rushes forward to force Zuko to drop Aang—and that *flag*, Sokka’s here to win—and defend himself.

Except instead of dropping his prize Zuko straight up tosses Aang over his shoulder to free up a hand to bend, little licks of flame that force Sokka to skip back. Which is when Haru reveals himself, popping up with a set of careful, precise bending—Sokka’s distantly impressed, he’s clearly learning—that continually moves the ground beneath Sokka’s feet, raising and lowering the earth just until it feels like Sokka’s legs are made of noodles.

Sokka squawks as he continues to trip his way through the longest, most extended fall of his life, Haru cracking up now too, and it’s looking like Suki’s team is going to take the win when a sudden wall of water forces Zuko to use both his hands in defense. Aang tumbles to the ground off Zuko’s shoulder, laughing so hard he can’t even bend, which just makes Toph berate him from her sudden position on top of the boulders and only adds to the general chaos.

Zuko flicks out quick, darting attacks with one flame-wreathed hand while trying to work the flag out of Aang’s grip with the other, the only benefit Sokka can see of Aang laughing so hard he’s gone nearly soundless the fact that his hands are clenched into fists that he definitely doesn’t have the wherewithal to release.

Sokka’s trying to figure out how to redirect his ongoing stumble—fucking *Haru*—to at least let him be tripping toward his teammate instead of away when Aang lets out a shrieking laugh, Zuko’s searching fingers apparently finding another ticklish spot. Instead of diving toward his teammate, though, Sokka suddenly finds himself diving for the ground in what he belatedly recognizes as an instinctive response to a snarl from Katara, hitting the dirt a half-second before dual whips of water lash over his head, followed by a wall of ice shards that have Zuko yelping in surprise.

Zuko’s hands jerk up, way more fire spilling out than he should have had to use to defend himself, the flames just as abruptly pulling back as the fire licks far too close to Sokka in front of him and Teo and Suki coming up behind him.

“Katara,” Sokka snaps as he shoves himself upright, not even trying to hide his anger. “What the *fuck*?” They agreed to the rules, all of them. This is supposed to be practice for the earthbenders, not a training bout, and definitely not a real fucking fight!

“I—” Katara’s eyes are wide, her hands beginning to tremble slightly where they’re still frozen at the end of her attack, her face going bloodless. “You—”

“Come on, Sweetness,” Toph frowns. “You can’t do that just because you thought you were going to lose.”

Katara is shaking her head, hands coming up to clutch at the hollow of her throat, and Sokka frowns, Toph’s words not sitting right. He knows Katara when she’s feeling competitive, and that wasn’t competition, that was rage.

And…fear?

“Let’s just take a moment,” Aang says, shoving himself up onto his knees. “Maybe just… hang out for a bit.”

“Good idea,” Suki says, glancing around. “Is everyone okay?”

They do a roll call, The Duke piping up from behind the boulders, and everyone’s taking a breath and forcibly relaxing and nervously laughing when Sokka’s head jerks up as he registers a conspicuous silence. “Zuko,” he says, sharp. “You okay?”

“…Um.”

Sokka scrambles to his feet, eyes narrowing as Zuko’s expression turns vaguely guilty. “Zuko.”

“I’m fine,” Zuko insists, glancing uneasily at the eyes now on him from all sides, and Sokka knows better to trust *that* when it’s said in that particular tone.

“Would you think I was fine?”

Zuko clamps his mouth shut, which is about all the answer Sokka needs.

“Where,” he demands, scanning Zuko head to toe, looking for torn clothes or the red splash of blood because he knows that Zuko is far too good at pushing through pain to visibly favor any injury.

Zuko sighs but relents and extends his arm away from his side to reveal a ragged, sluggishly bleeding gash along the entire length of it, from his wrist nearly to his armpit. “It’s really not a bid deal,” he mutters, eyeing his arm with a vague kind of annoyance, like it’s just a minor fucking *inconvenience*. Fuck, he must have gotten caught by ice as he was pulling his block back in.

“Whoa!” The Duke exclaims as he catches sight of it.

“That definitely needs stitches,” Suki says.

“…That sounds not good,” Toph mutters.

“Katara can heal that,” Aang says, bouncing to his feet, face tight with concern, eyes so fixed on Zuko’s arm that he misses the way Zuko goes almost wholly immobile. *Sokka* doesn’t miss it, though. Zuko’s arm is still held out on display but his eyes dart with a quick kind of uncertainty toward Katara before flicking to Sokka with something like pleading.

Sokka immediately turns to Katara, who takes a step back, hands still clutched high at her throat. “Katara.”

“I—”

“You’ll heal him,” Aang says anxiously. “Right?”

Katara just takes another step back, face frozen, the whites of her eyes visible as she continues to stare at Zuko’s arm.

“…Alright, where’s the rotgut to disinfect it,” Suki asks, voice going brisk and efficient as she glances around like someone might offer up a flask. “And a needle and some thread.”

“Katara…” Aang says, slow and clouded with confusion.

“I—I didn’t —” She chokes herself off with a sound close to a sob, chest heaving before she suddenly whirls around, darting past the outcropping to disappear from view.

“Katara!” Aang makes to run after her, his momentum sending him spinning around as Toph snatches his arm and tugs him back.

“Let her be, Twinkletoes,” Toph advises, head turned in the direction Katara must have taken off in once she was out of sight.

Aang looks torn, reluctantly settling back, and Sokka goes to follow after her instead when a hand on his own arm stops him, too.

“I’ll go,” Zuko says quietly, his fingers warm against Sokka’s skin.

“Zuko—”

“It’s fine,” Zuko says, giving his bicep a little squeeze. “Promise.”

Sokka glances down at Zuko’s arm. It’s still bleeding, but not any faster, which…isn’t the absolute worst, he supposes. But Sokka doesn’t like seeing that trail of blood down Zuko’s skin, dropping slowly off his fingertips and darkening his clothes. “Maybe get that looked at first.”

“It can wait,” Zuko says, with so much quiet confidence that Sokka can’t find the words to protest until he’s already jogging away after her.

&#45;-

It’s not hard to track Katara’s path through their playing field. And once he gets going Zuko has a sense of where she might be heading anyway, so he makes sure to make plenty of noise as he approaches the wide, rocky pool that forms the rainwater catch that feeds the plumbing system. Katara is a blue-clad figure against the gray stone, more ball-shaped than person-shaped with how tightly she’s hunched over herself, arms wrapped around her drawn-up knees.

Katara glances back at his approach, straightening when she sees who it is, her hands balling into fists and jaw clenching as she jerks her face forward again. Zuko keeps his steps slow, giving her ample time to tell him to go away before taking a seat a few careful paces away. His inner fire shifts, restless and uncertain in the face of her clear anger and the flash of redness ringing her eyes.

“What do you want,” Katara snaps to the water, preemptively hostile. “An apology?”

Zuko blinks. “No.” It…never even occurred to him to ask, not for a training accident.

“Because I’m not going to give you one,” she continues, the words coming out in a tight, choppy rush. “I didn’t do it on purpose, okay? And you know what? Joking about that— about capturing Aang, that wasn’t—that isn’t funny!” She slashes him a sideways glare, eyes bright and furious. “The Fire Nation attacking isn’t a *joke*, it’s—it’s *not.”*

“It isn’t,” Zuko agrees after a moment, which only makes her shoot him another suspicious look, like his lack of fight doesn’t make sense to her.

“Why are you here if you don’t want an apology,” she asks, nearly spitting the words out, her red-rimmed eyes flicking down to his arm. “You want me to heal you?”

Zuko wonders if she meant to make the offer sounds like a threat. “Not if you don’t want to.” He understands Sokka fussing, but the cut isn’t even bleeding all that much to begin with. Dousing it with paint stripper is going to suck, but it’s not like it’s dire.

“Then what?” Her expression darkens, storm clouds sweeping over the ocean. “Are you going to tell me to let go of my anger? To find forgiveness in my heart for the Fire Nation?”

…Forgiveness for what, exactly? “No,” Zuko says after a beat. Just…blanket forgiveness? “That sounds very Air Nomad.” Far be it from Zuko to ever comment on anyone else’s anger.

Katara snorts, her words coming out like a challenge. “Or to stop blaming you for things that are out of your control?”

Zuko scratches at the back of his neck, not exactly feeling like a full participant in this conversation. Or rather, like there are other participants he isn’t aware of, even if he recognizes that one. “Sokka and I don’t always agree on what was in my control or not,” he finally says.

“Then what do you *want*,” Katara demands. “Why don’t you just leave me alone?”

Zuko takes a deep breath, forcing his inner flame to stay level in the face of her frustration. “I want to understand if there’s anything I can do so that you can start to trust me,” he says. Because Katara might be reacting like her bending suddenly went out of control, but Zuko thinks it’s harder than Sokka might want it to be to truly shift someone from the mental spot that says ‘enemy’ to ‘friend.’ Or vice versa.

“Nothing! I *did* trust you! Back in Ba Sing Se, and then you betrayed that trust!”

Zuko sighs, glancing away because…he can see how it would seem that way, from her shoes. Seeming to go right from Sokka’s side to Azula’s…

“You don’t just get it back because you’re fucking my brother again!”

Zuko can’t help wincing at that, even being familiar enough with sharp-edged little sisters to know that this hostility is probably covering just as much fear as it is anger. “You know it’s not just…physical,” Zuko says quietly, clearing his throat and refusing to let himself look away. Being with Sokka isn’t just some thing Zuko’s doing to pass the time, it’s…huge. Something that feels so much bigger than what they’ve named it.

“*Please* don’t talk to me about being *physical* with my brother,” she bites out, sounding disgusted, and Zuko…will refrain from pointing out that she brought it up first.

“I’m not asking to just have your trust, I know it doesn’t work like that,” Zuko says, focusing again on what he’s here for. “I’m asking if there’s a way to build it again.” If he can just get one thing to work toward, something concrete he can actually act on…Zuko’s pretty sure he only understands a fraction of how important Katara is to Sokka, and Agni, the idea of always being a point of contention between them…Zuko *really* wants to make this work.

“If there’s a way—can you reconquer Ba Sing Se for the Earth King? Can you make it so Aang never got hurt? Can you bring my mom back?” She glares at his silence, looking even more furious than when they started. Fuck. “Some things don’t get better just because you want them to.”

“…Most things don’t,” Zuko agrees, voice low, holding back a sigh when that just seems to make her angrier. He thinks of Azula at her most furious, at that point when lack of a fight only deepens her rage. Maybe Katara is the same, not that Zuko’s exactly inclined to test the theory without asking Sokka first.

“Just—don’t follow this time,” Katara growls, scrambling to her feet and pausing to give him one last glare. “And—*ugh.* Learn to throw a better block!”

Water is in her hands before Zuko can process, his own hands halfway into a *much* better block when he registers that the water’s glowing blue, staying close to Katara, rippling rather than whipping. And despite her furious expression, when Katara snaps her hand out the water rolls over itself toward him rather than lashing, wrapping around his wrist and twining up his arm, gentle and warm, with none of the biting cold or suffocating oppressiveness he’s come to expect.

Zuko holds his breath and holds his body and inner flame completely still as the water pulses, wrapping his arm like a sleeve and slowly fading back to the crystal clearness of the pool. Once the last of the brightness is gone it flows back into Katara’s hands and then back down the rocks toward its source.

“You weren’t even that hurt anyway,” Katara mutters as she stomps away, the wordslow and tight. A bit like someone trying to convince themselves as much as the people around them.

&#45;-

Zuko appreciates that it’s his turn to cook dinner tonight. It means he can light things on fire without alarming anyone, or close enough to get him to the same place—stoking and banking the flames across the cookfire, creating a hotspot to bring the pan up to heat and a low spot to keep the soup pot just on the edge of simmering, holding a nice flat piece of metal Toph made for him in one hand to get it ready for making quick griddle cakes. It all requires attention and control and the merging of his intentions with his inner flame in order to see his will made manifest, until finally the sharp sizzle of fat across the bottom of the pan is enough to let Zuko feel more centered, looser in all the places he was tight around the edges after talking with Katara.

A light brush of fingers over his shoulders as Sokka walks over does a lot, too, to center Zuko. The gesture is absent and more than welcome, and Zuko wonders if Sokka’s aware of just how much his touch resonates through Zuko, even the ones as thoughtless as this. Though maybe not entirely thoughtless, as Sokka proceeds to use Zuko for balance as he peeks into the cookpot, far more than Zuko suspects he actually needs. Not that Zuko minds.

“Not stir fry?”

Zuko eyes Sokka, trying to understand the teasing in his tone. “…I stir-fried the ingredients before adding them to the broth.”

Sokka flashes him a quick grin. “Smells good.”

Zuko smiles back, ducking his head so he doesn’t just melt all over Sokka right here and now and passing him a bowl. He watches Sokka settle out of the corner of his eye as the others make their way over, ignoring the slightly wild-eyed looks Yamai and Irumi are still giving food made by their Prince. It does a whole lot to ground the bits of Zuko that are still unsettled to see the relaxed set of Sokka’s face as he takes a bite, to feel more than hear his contented good-food hum across the scant inch of space between them, Sokka’s crossed leg almost touching Zuko’s thigh.

“This is good,” Katara says, sounding faintly surprised. Zuko isn’t particularly insulted by her tone, considering their very different perspective on ‘too much spice.’

“What’s that sour flavor?” Toph wonders, smacking her lips.

“Berries?” Aang suggests, poking at his bowl.

“Cherrybarb?” Chit Sang frowns.

“Cherrybarb,” Zuko confirms.

“…Interesting,” Suki murmurs, taking another half-hesitant bite.

“It tastes like…sea prune stew,” Hakoda says slowly. “Somehow?”

“Like how Gran Gran makes it,” Katara says, slowly turning toward Sokka.

“…Huh,” Sokka says, finally pausing to glance at his mostly-finished bowl. “Yeah.”

Toph slurps down another mouthful, all mock-innocence as she asks, “Is that how Sokka likes it best?”

Zuko ducks his head, making a show of examining his own bowl as he feels a blush trying to climb up his neck. Which doesn’t even make *sense*, there’s no reason to be embarrassed about knowing how Sokka likes his food and…fuck. Zuko eyes the fire, wondering if he can get away with dampening the flame enough to dim the light without Chit Sang or Aang calling him on it. Chit Sang probably wouldn’t. Aang definitely would, though, and probably without even realizing it.

Agni’s tits, Zuko barely bites back his annoyance at how in his own fucking head he is about fucking *soup*. Who cares if Zuko apparently inadvertently recreated Sokka’s grandmother’s recipe, based…solely on Zuko’s awareness of the kinds of foods and spices and flavors Sokka gravitates toward? That’s…not a big deal, right? Anyone could have done it if they paid enough attention.

…Fuck.

Zuko doesn’t *want* to feel self-conscious about things like this. He doesn’t want to be so aware of how revealing these mundane little intimacies are that he pulls away from them instead of enjoying them. Zuko *likes* those things, their comfortable banter and the indulgence of rambling musings and Sokka’s easy interpretation of Zuko’s silences and breaths and glances, like a whole conversation is happening with only one piece of it said out loud. And the seats taken next to each other without needing to ask, and coming to rest in each other’s space, and their bodies moving in familiar rhythm when they train. The fact that Zuko knows how Sokka likes his food, and Sokka knows how Zuko *doesn’t* like his tea, and they both can’t stop *smiling* whenever they realize they possess that knowledge about each other.

And Zuko was fucking *fine* showing himself in those ways before, to do that with Aang grinning and Toph teasing and even Suki rolling her eyes in a way that doesn’t actually feel harsh. So why is the fact that there are two sets of ice-hard pale eyes on him, one pair edged in defensive confusion and the other watching and giving nothing back, suddenly such a fucking *problem*?

Zuko takes in a slow, deep breath and exhales deliberate and firm, trying to push out the restless energy knotting his inner flame in his chest. Agni’s sweating balls, Zuko knew— knows—that Sokka comes with more than just himself, this time, just like Zuko knows that *he* doesn’t come as just himself anymore, if he ever did. And part of holding onto Sokka is figuring out how to hold all these things, too.

It would just be easier if Hakoda weren’t always fucking *watching.*

&#45;-

Sokka is acutely conscious of the way Zuko goes motionless when Dad glances at him, and of the fact that Zuko was already eyeing the almost-guilty scowl Katara kept shooting his way like he was trying to decide whether to scowl back. So Sokka isn’t exactly surprised when Zuko somehow manages to put an extra inch of space between them purely by straightening his back a little more precisely.

And Sokka’s pretty sure Zuko already used up the extent of his ability to be in the same room as the adults today when he finally came back from following after Katara, looking contemplative and distracted and a quarter crusted in blood. Hakoda had immediately stopped arguing about why Suki needed alcohol and started pressing Zuko about his injury, while the Fire Nation contingent made their concern equally known at varying volume, which ended with them all gaping at the empty air as Zuko darted back the way he came faster than Sokka could hustle across the room to intervene.

So Sokka isn’t exactly surprised when Zuko manages to slip away from dinner at the first available opportunity when his exit itself won’t be noticeable. But he still doesn’t like it.

Sokka worries at his wrist wraps, transferring his attention from the doorway Zuko slipped through to Hakoda across the fire. Hakoda is Sokka’s dad, and Zuko is now Sokka’s boyfriend—which still puts a thrill in Sokka’s chest—and it would be good if they could exist in the same room together. Though maybe that’s the issue—that Zuko is seeing his boyfriend’s dad, whatever that means to him, rather than the person in front of him.

Who is…definitely still holding onto a core of reserve toward the Fire Nation Prince, which Sokka is also going to need to figure out how to address without sharing more than Zuko is comfortable being shared just yet.

Sokka eyes the direction Zuko ran off to again. Sokka could follow him. He has a pretty good idea that even if he doesn’t find Zuko lingering a few corridors away—Zuko always knows when Sokka’s in his radius, and Sokka’s pretty sure he’d let himself be found if Sokka starts in his direction—Sokka would find him in that little glade of his. It would be nice to have some alone time with Zuko without needing to worry about someone wandering in. The day has been…long.

And Zuko said that he knows that Sokka is here for him, but maybe Sokka should take some steps to show it. Some things to make Zuko feel wanted and relaxed and maybe in more of a headspace by the end to find the words for what is bothering him, or to ask for whatever it is he needs when Sokka’s already showing his willingness to give it.

That feels better than just poking at his already-jumpy firebender. And besides, Sokka has just the idea he’s been turning over that he thinks Zuko will hear loud and clear.

&#45;-

Sokka has the candles set up and a sheet strategically hung to soften the stone walls and reflect back the yellow-orange candlelight in a way he thinks Zuko will like. Kind of like being inside a little campfire, in a very…abstract interpretation. Sokka found bunches of yellow and red and orange flowers to nestle around the room to complete the effect, and he’s just hopping down from hanging the last of them from the ceiling when he hears footsteps in the hall.

Sokka hastily tugs out his hair tie, tossing a few quick handfuls of petals in a path from the door to the bed before arranging himself on the blankets. Maybe he should lie like—but no, Zuko likes looking at his—but that feels a bit obscene, so if he just props himself up on his elbows and does some gratuitous arm flexing…

Satisfied, Sokka grabs up a loose flower to clutch between his teeth, just in time to look over his shoulder with a dramatic toss of his hair and meet Suki’s wide hazel eyes.

Sokka panics. He nearly chokes on the flower, shooting upright and then throwing himself back down on the bed because he’s not trying to give her a *better* look. Yeah, he isn’t naked, but he also isn’t wearing *pants.* He flails for the edge of a blanket and then realizes he’s fucking *sitting* on it which means he can’t pull it over himself. In a fit of desperation he just rolls over, holding onto the edge of the blanket and rolling himself right up in it because his dignity is already in tatters, why try for grace at this point.

Sokka finally runs out of room to roll and spits out the flower stem, coughing, as Suki explodes into laughter. “Wow,” she wheezes, glancing around the room. “*Wow*, Sokka.”

“I, uh. Didn’t expect—I didn’t think anyone—”

“Clearly not,” Suki giggles. “But what a show you put on anyway.”

“Let me just…find my pants.”

“Oh,” Suki says, straightening to lean back against the wall and making a show of studying the ceiling. “No need on my account.”

Sokka pauses in the middle of trying to extract himself from the tight bundle of blankets, eyeing Suki as he weighs staying prone on the bed with limited use of his arms against the fact that he isn’t wearing anything but the pair of too-small underwear that he chose *because* they fit far too tight these days. He untangles himself in a flurry and makes a run for his clothes.

“What’s the occasion,” Suki drawls, not even trying to hide her amusement.

“Does there have to be one,” Sokka asks, more than a little breathless as he fights to get into his shirt, which has never been this fucking complicated before.

“I guess not,” Suki says, muffling another laugh into her hand.

Sokka gives her a baleful look that he decides she'll still be able to sense even not looking as he fumbles fastening his tunic for the third time and gives up on having it closed, deciding it’s enough to just have it on even if it’s sagging distractingly open as he starts turning his pants right side out. Spirits, Katara can never know about any of this, the ‘I told you so’s over his messiness would never end. “Why are you here?”

Suki raises an eyebrow. “Does a lady need a reason to visit a warrior she admires?”

Sokka freezes, mentally tripping over the idea that Suki admires him as a warrior—or, no, wait, that she admires Zuko? It’s his room—when someone makes themselves known in the doorway: “Uh.”

Sokka lets out a fucking *squawk* of alarm, wide-eyed with a frantic kind of panic as he looks over Suki’s shoulder to see Zuko standing there, taking in the room and the mussed bed and Suki’s relaxed lean and Sokka standing in the middle of it all with his pants in his hands.

“And that’s my cue,” Suki says, giving Zuko a sweeping glance that ends in a smirk. “Enjoy yourselves!”

Zuko looks rather stunned as she leaves, slowly stepping into the room like he isn’t quite sure it’s actually his and then *firmly* shutting the door, leaning back against it as he takes another look at the candles and the hanging sheet and Sokka half-dressed. Fuck. All Sokka wanted to do was something to make Zuko feel treasured and cherished, to give him something tangible to help counter his anxieties, and instead…

“This was, um. Obviously for you. Not her.”

…Instead Sokka just stood here pantsless in his tightest underwear with his ex girl-he-used-to-kiss-and-fantasize-about.

“I figured,” Zuko finally says, sounding faintly bemused, and Sokka sags in relief as Zuko’s expression starts to slide from startled to something like a quiet kind of pleasure.

“Do you, um.” Sokka takes a deep breath, trying to get himself back on track. “Do you know what it means?”

Zuko’s eyes flick around the candles and flower petals, then back to Sokka’s, a hint of a lopsided smile sitting in the corner of his mouth. “Yeah.”

“I meant it,” Sokka says, finally finding his footing again. He still means it.

Zuko flushes, a smile breaking out even as he ducks his head, hiding behind the fall of his hair and Sokka cannot *wait* for it to get long enough to pull back so he stops losing the lines of Zuko’s face when he does that. “I don’t know what I did to deserve it.”

“We,” Sokka says, backing toward the bed and how he meant for this to go, “Are going to work on that self-confidence.” His pulse begins to flutter at the way Zuko watches him climb onto the bed, intent, lips parted. Except Zuko doesn’t come forward, and while Sokka isn’t exactly unused to Zuko going still when he’s really concentrating on something, this doesn’t quite have that same tenor. Sokka pauses, halfway into a sprawl that he thinks is rather artful, with the way his tunic is framing his chest and stomach. It should definitely have Zuko at least breathing a little ragged. “What’s up? Everything okay?”

“…I’m about to really ruin the mood,” Zuko says, eyes lingering on Sokka’s exposed skin and too-small underwear before dragging up to his face with open regret.

Sokka sits up straight, a bolt of alarm going through him as he automatically scans Zuko for injuries. “What? What is it?”

Zuko takes a deep breath, expression going series. “Will you tell me about your mother?”

That is definitely *not* what Sokka was expecting to hear. And Sokka…doesn’t think Zuko’s asking for good memories. He searches Zuko’s face, slowly drawing the edges of his open tunic over his chest. “You already know what happened to her.”

Zuko’s finger is tapping restlessly against the door, the only point of motion in his entire frame, eyes fixed somewhere around Sokka’s collarbones. “Will you tell me specifically? What happened?”

That’s not an easy memory, or one that Sokka often tries to call up, and he knows Zuko is aware of that. “Why do you want to know?”

“…The Fire Nation’s navy isn’t such a big world,” Zuko says, eyes flicking back up to Sokka’s face. “And I wasn’t fully in it, but…” A shrug.

‘But.’ But Sokka can fill in the rest—but Zuko knows people, met people, heard things. ‘But’ Zuko is here with a purpose that Sokka can see sitting behind his eyes. ‘But’ Sokka doesn’t really want to think about it, doesn’t want to weigh whether Zuko’s need is enough to counter everything that comes with dredging up these memories. ‘But’ Sokka doesn’t want to hold something back that Zuko wants to know, not when asking for things between them is so new, not when it’s *supposed* to let them learn the hard stuff.

With a sigh Sokka scoots back, silently gesturing for Zuko to join him on the bed. “What do you want to know?”

Zuko walks over, neatly toeing off his boots and giving the expanse of blankets an assessing stare before finally mirroring Sokka’s cross-legged seat. Zuko’s eyes are steady, hands open over his knees, just in reaching position in case Sokka decides to grab for them instead of his own wrists. “How did it start?”

Sokka takes a deep breath, the sequence of it coming all too readily to mind, and begins to tell Zuko everything he can. “It started with the black snow…”

Spirits, this certainly isn’t how Sokka envisioned the night going when he planned it. But if it helps Zuko in some way for Sokka to offer this raw openness? Then it’s more than worth it, no matter how hard it is to tell the full thing, something’s he’s never been able to do—never *had* to do—before.

At some point Sokka migrates across the bed into Zuko’s lap to hide his face against his neck, needing to get as close as possible to Zuko’s warmth but wholly incapable of talking about certain things while being seen. He’s still there at the end of it, so that Zuko’s quiet “Thank you for telling me” is felt as much as heard when it’s pressed against his loose hair.

“You’re welcome,” Sokka whispers, finally sagging now that it’s done. Fuck, is he drained, nearly light-headed with exhaustion. Or...maybe like something’s been drained *out* of him, or like the arms Zuko has wrapped around him and the heat of Zuko’s body and the steady beat of his too-fast heart are doing more to take the hold the weight of memory than just driving the cold chill of it away.

#### Chapter End Notes
