Zuko gives him a half-surprised, half-confused look. “Men with men,” he says after a beat. “Women with women.”

“It’s not…legal?” Sokka’s mind is suddenly bouncing through Azula’s very personal animosity and the jabs that never entirely made sense, leaping to Zuko’s tension around Iroh finding out about them that Sokka thought was just Zuko’s general reserve but…was maybe something very different.

“This kind of thing hasn’t been legal in the Fire Nation for a long time,” Zuko sighs, frowning down as he picks at the wooden railing. “Loss of status, transfer of assets. Imprisonment, depending on how egregious you were about it.”

“'This kind of thing,’” Sokka echoes. How—how could you *legislate* that?

“'Relations that will not bear fruit for the betterment of the nation,’” Zuko quotes before pulling a face and dropping the formality of his tone. “The Sages worked themselves into a state trying to determine whether that would apply to cross-national relationships, too. Thankfully they got themselves out of that corner a few decades back.”

Sokka doesn’t know if he’s more horrified by what he's hearing or by Zuko’s matter-of-factness about it. “How long has it been..?” He finally asks, feeling numb.

Zuko cuts him a look. “How long do you think?”

“…One hundred years?”

“I knew you were smart,” Zuko says, lips curling into a grim little smile.

“Zuko—that’s—*Zuko.* We—”

“We’re fine,” Zuko cuts in, firm.

They’re *fine?* “But—you’re—"

“Do you think I didn’t know when we started?” Zuko interrupts, eyes steady gold as they catch the firelight below. “I was raised to defend and enact the laws of the land. That’s what the royal family *does*. And this—” Zuko waves a hand between them. “—wasn’t a new idea for me, Sokka. *Doing* something about it was, but I’ve always known which ways I burn.”

Sokka really feels like this isn’t a conversation for a playhouse balcony, or one for Zuko to be taking so lightly. “Well, *I* didn’t know!”

Zuko leans back slightly, frowning at the vehemence of Sokka’s tone, searching his face in the darkness and Sokka can barely comprehend that Zuko is *surprised*.

“Zuko, I want to know if something we’re doing is dangerous for you,” Sokka says, shoving his hands into his hair. “Fuck, is this why Azula said I got you killed? *Is* it going to get you killed?”

“…I mean. Not directly.”

“Not *directly*.”

“It’s perceptions,” Zuko says quietly, glancing away. “If you lose your titles and your property, and you already have enemies, and all you have left is your bending…”

Spirits. *Spirits.* “Fuck, Zuko, is this—is this *Zhao* again? Someone finds out and suddenly anyone who wants can assassinate you? Why would you think that I wouldn’t want to know about that?”

“I…never really thought about it,” Zuko admits after a long moment, casting Sokka a quick, searching look. “It never really seemed important to bring up. It was different not being *in* the Fire Nation, you know? Especially with how the Earth Kingdom is—” Sokka blinks. Wait. How is the Earth Kingdom? “— and I didn’t know if I’d ever be back and we weren't talking about future stuff anyway, and then, you know. I came back, but I left again…”

“And now you’re back, but in secret,” Sokka finishes heavily, scrubbing his hands over his face. Fuck. He…can maybe see how it could have felt like it was never particularly relevant, or all that urgent to share.

“Would…would you have stayed away if you did know?” Zuko asks, not quite meeting Sokka's eyes, fingers tangled together. “I didn’t withhold it to deceive you, or so you wouldn’t know the risk you were taking on—"

“Fuck the risk to *me*,” Sokka says, incredulous. “*I* don’t have any property for them to strip away. And they’ll imprison me for a bunch of other stuff before this ever comes up.”

“Me, too,” Zuko points out, and Sokka pulls up short again.

“But you’re…”

“An exiled former Prince with a price on his head?”

“…I was going to say an offspring of the sun, or whatever you guys call it.” Which all the guards at Boiling Rock had certainly seemed to care about, and the prisoners too if Chit Sang is anything to go by...

“Child of Agni,” Zuko corrects with a half-smile. “And that only takes you so far when you’re actively betraying your nation.”

Sokka pauses, turning that over and studying Zuko’s face. That…hasn’t been his impression of what *Zuko* thinks he’s doing. “Is that what you’re doing, then? Betraying the Fire Nation?” Zuko gives a half-shrug. “Depends on your perspective, I guess. Azula might not be taking it seriously yet—” Wait. What? “—but when she does, I promise, who I’m sleeping with is going to be at the bottom of the list of reasons they try to imprison me. Besides,” Zuko adds, sliding off the railing as a chime signals the end of intermission and grabbing Sokka’s hand to give it a brief, tight squeeze. “Some things are worth it. Right?” Said with such simplicity and conviction that Sokka has no idea how he could possibly find the words to refute it even if he wanted to.

&#45;-

Zuko doesn’t quite know what to make of the fact that Sokka’s stunned silence—which… Zuko might need to find ways to be more verbally expressive, if Sokka is knocked back that easily by an admittedly roundabout compliment—lasts right up until stage-Sokka and stage-Suki disappear to make sweet, sweet love in the middle of the second act, all in the name of balance.

Sokka jerks up, gaping at the stage. “That never happened,” he gasps, turning wide eyes to Zuko. “It never did!”

“Yes!” Suki shouts, letting out a whoop along with the audience. “Get it, girl!”

“Sokka,” Katara exclaims, pinning him with a disapproving frown. “Really.”

“What—it didn’t happen,” Sokka protests. “You were *there*.”

“I would have remembered that,” she says, wrinkling her nose and pointedly turning back to the stage.

“I—*Katara!”*

Zuko coughs and shifts forward, giving Katara cover to lean back and hide the curve of her smile as Sokka continues to hiss, “Katara! Ka*tar*a!” until he finally chokes off when Toph pointedly states that some people have moved on from their unrequited love and would appreciate if others could as well, thank you very much.

&#45;-

Zuko decides that the appropriate reaction is amusement as Sokka falls into a significantly more strangled silence as his characters naps his way through the background of Ba Sing Se, waking up only to eat, crack jokes—

"What were you telling people every time you came to the teashop again?" Zuko can't hold himself back from asking, earning himself glower as stage-Sokka cracks a joke while sleepwalking to find food. And then sleepwalks his want into Jet again.

“That’s not what *happened,"* Sokka protests again, his new catchphrase of the second act, and Zuko surprises himself by being relieved to hear it, considering the timing that would have required. Zuko’s fairly confident that he was Sokka’s first. So if Sokka did anything like *that* with Jet—well, they didn’t exactly make promises to each other at the outset. But Zuko…would have questions.

Zuko doesn’t manage to formulate what those questions would be though, because his thoughts grind to a halt when stage-Jet dies a shockingly noble death.

“Jet’s…*dead?”* Zuko asks, stunned.

“...You know,” Sokka frowns, “It was very unclear at the time.”

Katara turns slowly in Zuko’s periphery, pinning with him a narrow-eyed stare. “…You know Jet?”

Zuko can feel himself freeze tellingly still. “Um.”

Zuko’s thankfully saved from further reply as stage-Zuko and stage-Katara reappear, captured by Azula—on Zuko’s part, because he couldn’t stop talking about his honor long enough to fight back, which…is really driving the fucking theme home. The characters quickly get over their hostility after discovering a mutual love of talking about themselves and their own personal interests—honor for stage Zuko, and being right all the time for stage-Katara, which has the real Katara sniffing in annoyance beside him.

And Zuko knows Uluzon style, and he’s already figured out the archetype everyone’s character is filling, but it belatedly occurs to him that no one else probably does right around the moment when Katara’s character makes a comment about where he can go looking for his honor, and the Zuko on stage obligingly goes searching under her skirts.

Zuko and Katara both join Sokka in his embarrassed slouch as Suki bursts into laughter and Aang lets out a sound that can best be described as a squeak as the scene fades to black with some…heavy implications. Ones that Azula’s character makes abundantly clear in the next scene for anyone in the audience who’s particularly slow about steam making, the crowd letting out shouts of laughter and a few comments of their own about drowning with a Water Tribe girl.

“Steam making,” Aang echoes, giving Zuko a confused glance when Toph just shrugs.

“Think about it,” Zuko mutters, refusing to get into the ins and outs of Fire Nation innuendo and insult and sexual politics and imperial politics in the middle of an Ember Island Player production. He *refuses* to credit them with that kind of intentional social commentary. The kind they've been doing the whole play. Ugh.

“Or don’t think about it,” Katara grumbles, wrinkling her face. “Gross.”

&#45;-

Everyone goes quiet—or rigid with outrage—as the second act closes again with Aang as a source of destruction, the only thing preventing him from leveling Ba Sing Se with nothing more than an “Oops’ turning out to be stage-Azula’s bravery and wit.

Zuko sinks further into his misery as he watches himself on stage throw over Uncle for Azula just because she says the words ‘honor’ and ‘Father’ in the same sentence, which…Agni, is horrifyingly close to how it actually went if all you knew to share were the words that were said.

Azula’s character gives her big brother an indulgent pat on the head, turning to the audience with a roll of her eyes, saying “Don’t worry, Brother. I’ll protect you *and* your honor.” It closes the second act with a laugh, but all Zuko can think is that whoever fed this playwright information knew a whole lot more than just the words.

&#45;-

Zuko hates the Uluzon style and he hates the Ember Island Players, and he particularly hates that as awful as they are on the whole, there always seems to be one part of their production each year they manage to pull off with impressive competence. Their brilliant costuming in the travesty they made of *The Chameleon in the Long Grass.* The heart-wrenching monologs in comically overweight *Tragedy of Qing.* The breathtaking set design in the otherwise wooden *Lady Yan Has Her Day*.

The fact that their awful script and ridiculous plotting and one-dimensional characterization are somehow still absolutely nailing the Uluzon style’s blurring of truth and exaggeration in *The Boy in the Iceberg*.

There are things that are so blatantly false, and yet the pieces that they get so pointedly right make it hard to fully trust his own recollection, to fully have faith in his own perspective on the things that seem outrageous. Particularly when Aang might be on his way toward a small breakdown over what Zuko thinks is an exaggerated but not entirely inaccurate portrayal. Zuko can’t exactly brush off the rest when he can’t tell Aang to do the same without the lie coming out.

“This is some ostrich horse shit,” Sokka mutters, arms crossed tightly as he stares moodily down the busy hallway during the second intermission. “I didn’t—I’m not—”

“You do like food a lot, Snoozles,” Toph points out, utterly serene in her representation of herself.

“Quite a lot,” Suki agrees cheerfully, patting him on the shoulder before heading off toward Aang, which has Sokka flushing and shooting Zuko a quick, anxious look, as if Zuko wasn’t already perfectly aware that in another life Sokka and Suki could have been more than happy together.

“Just because that part’s true doesn’t mean all of it is,” Sokka calls after her.

“Just the important stuff,” Zuko mutters, not entirely succeeding in holding back a stab of bitterness as he watches a group of children parade by with costumes and commemorative masks, each Zuko-character with the scar on the wrong side.

Sokka huffs, leaning back against the wall next to him and following Zuko’s gaze. “Don’t let it get to you,” he says, clearly not modeling the behavior himself, and Zuko wonders which are the parts that Sokka are feeling strike a little too close to home for comfort. It’s probably not the right time to share that the ambiguity is one of the fundamental trademarks of the style, the primary way it advanced political and cultural commentary under the restricted dynasty it originated in.

Someone in the Ember Island Players is being rather bold. Or banking on the Fire Lord not knowing his theatrical history.

&#45;-

Sokka finally reaches the limits of his ability to feel outraged when the Avatar’s invasion of the Fire Nation is derailed because stage-Sokka wanders off, distracted by some giggling Fire Nation girls who laugh at his increasingly bad jokes and wave around skewers of meat.

The moment doesn’t last long, though, only until stage-Aang crashes across the set, cheerfully blowing over houses and destroying property and chasing after fleeing Caldera citizens while shouting about balance. And it turns into a cold kind of horror as Azula kills Zuko on stage in a dramatic ball of fire as the audience *cheers*, wildly, and Zuko beside him is just—still. Far, far too still. Fire is always flickering and moving, and so is Zuko, unless something is wrong.

“I can only protect you if you don’t betray your family and your Nation,” stage-Azula explains to Zuko’s unmoving body before turning to proclaim to the audience, “And we all know the future crown is mine, unless I decide to give it to you!”

Sokka tries to catch Zuko’s attention, but Zuko’s eyes stay fixed firmly on the stage even though Sokka *knows* that Zuko can see more into his periphery than he’s pretending he can. But it’s the climax of the action, the noble and powerful Fire Lord Ozai killing the Avatar using the power of celestial fire, given to him by Agni to defend his people against the chaotic destruction of the Avatar. The audience cheers whole-heartedly as Ozai strikes the final blow, and then even more as a tapestry of the Imperial Flame falls dramatically across the background, Azula and Ozai standing proudly astride the fallen bodies of their opponents. Then the crowd holds their breath, rapt, as the characters trade off proclamations about Agni’s blessing and defeating would-be oppressors, about good Fire Nation values triumphing in the end, about how even a Child of Agni can fall from the light through failure to properly honor his family and his ancestors and put in the hard work demanded by his station, as both the Fire Lord and Lighting Princess have always done.

All the outraged muttering in their cheap balcony seats grinds to a halt, and Sokka feels Zuko stiffen even more beside him at the sudden silence, his face blank and pale and set even in the darkness.

Zuko was right, Sokka thinks as the lights rise to riotous applause. Coming to this play was really not a good idea.

&#45;-

Sokka tries to console himself that everyone leaves the playhouse disgruntled, even Toph, who is incensed by her lack of a role in the final showdown. Even Suki looks concerned, though that’s probably less about the play and more about the way she’s looking at them all like they’re barrels of blasting jelly about to go off and she’s waiting to see which way to dive for cover.

Which feels…unfortunately accurate. And Sokka doesn’t want any of the blowups to be from him, so he falls back with Zuko. If he stays up at the front with Aang, and by extension Katara, he knows that the Avatar-state stuff is going to bubble up again, or else the Jet stuff is going to come to a head, and Sokka just…would like to put that particular, embarrassing reckoning off a little while longer, and save the former for when he actually has something constructive to say.

Though Sokka doesn’t know that he’s going to do so well at staying quiet back here, either. Because Zuko’s silence is brooding and tight, and Zuko was annoyed the whole time they were at the play in a disgusted-with-this-production way, but he only got genuinely upset when Azula was on the stage. Which feels like something of a reflection of real life, in a way that makes Sokka uncomfortable to think about, even if he can't stop doing it.

Fuck, Sokka might be annoyed that the play basically depicted him alternating between following his dick and his stomach around the world, cracking jokes—and he would really like to believe that only one of those things is true. But with Zuko, they had *cheered.* Everyone in the audience, Zuko’s own citizens, who Sokka knows Zuko still cares about despite all his protestations of not being a Prince anymore—they applauded, loud and enthusiastic and whole-heartedly, to see him cut down.

“I knew this was going to be garbage,” Zuko mutters, shoulders tight. And Sokka didn’t expect Zuko to be the one to crack first—and clearly neither did Suki, with the way she hastens her steps to give them space—but then, maybe watching your own people heap praises on your death does something to your natural reserve.

“You did,” Sokka sighs, kicking at the sandy path. And here he thought that he was giving Zuko something he would like.

“The Ember Island Players always ruin everyone,” Zuko says, low and savage. “*Love Against* *the Dragons* was absolutely horrendous when they put it on.”

Sokka blinks, trying to follow along. Maybe Zuko...isn't cracking first? “Ah.”

“They cut the *entire* subplot that establishes the political tension that’s supposed to underpin the third act.”

“…Oh. Wow.”

“I know, right? It makes it seem like the whole play is just a romance when it’s really a commentary on the limits and interplay of imperial and personal power.”

“Is it, now?”

“Yes, that’s the whole—” Zuko glances up, openly irate and flushing clear even in the moonlight when he catches Sokka’s bemused expression. “Sorry,” he mutters.

“You can tell me about it,” Sokka says. He might have absolutely no idea what Zuko’s talking about, but Zuko clearly has a lot of opinions on it. This is why he thought Zuko would like this activity in the first place.

“It’s nothing,” Zuko sighs. “They just—they ruin everything.” He scowls at the others’ backs, hands restless and sharp with what Sokka is pretty sure is anxiety. “Things were—they were *fine*. And you were just—you thought I’d *like* it, and now everyone is—” He saves a hand, somehow managing to encompass the stiff shoulders and sullen cast to everyone’s mood.

“…We’ll get over it, Zuko,” Sokka says quietly, relieved that Zuko at least caught his intent with tonight even if the execution has…significant room for improvement. “It’s not like we all haven’t fought before about something or other, or had someone tell us something we didn’t want to hear.”

“I should have…”

“What?” Sokka asks, a flash of fondness breaking through his general frustration with the evening. “Told us that they sucked? You did. Multiple times. Creatively. It’s not your fault we thought you just had high standards.”

Zuko grunts, not entirely like he agrees but not pushing back either, and Sokka lets the silence settle as they make their way past the outskirts of town before he works himself up to what he really wants to know. “Are *you* okay?”

Zuko blows out a breath, steps slowing a bit more.

“Because…that was some heavy shit, Zuko,” Sokka says, keeping his voice low. “And I don’t know all the ins and outs of what just happened back there—”

“A reprehensible display of community theater and semi-professional playwriting?”

“—but I would be upset, if I saw stuff like that about me.”

“'Stuff like that,’” Zuko echoes, neutral in a way that feels dangerous.

Sokka wonders if he could possibly be misreading the situation so badly. “…They cheered.”

“I’m aware,” Zuko bites out, the prickly spike telling Sokka that no, he’s reading it exactly right. “I was there, too.”

“I get that it was a play,” Sokka soldiers on, “But seeing even a fake Azula do that? It—it’s fucked up.” It made Sokka’s heart stop, is what it did, made his stomach flip, made his entire body ache to cling to Zuko’s warm, live, safe form. “So…it’s okay to not be fine. If you aren’t.”

Zuko snorts. “Azula is one of the only things they got right. It would be a waste of time to be upset about that.”

“…We just watched her laugh while she killed you.”

Zuko shrugs. “They were foreshadowing that from the first act.”

“Zuko,” Sokka says slowly. “She *just* tried to hit you with lightning in real life a few days ago. She *did* hit you.”

“She didn’t kill me,” Zuko says, giving Sokka a sideways look like he isn’t quite sure why that needs to be said out loud. Except Sokka *also* isn’t sure why that needs to be said out loud, because not succeeding in killing Zuko shouldn’t be some kind of point in her favor.

“I—Zuko. If who she was on stage was accurate?” Zuko nods. “Then that’s messed up. Then she’s messed up.”

Zuko slashes him a look that Sokka can’t read in the darkness, but his words are audibly tight. “How so.”

Sokka can hear the warning in Zuko’s tone, but he can't just let this go if Zuko really doesn't see it. Spirits, is there some Fire Nation thing here around not acknowledging what everyone can see? Another pretense? “If that’s how she is, then she’s cruel, and mean, and she hates you, and she was back there glorying in your death, and you’re saying that’s *accurate*, and —”

“And I betrayed her,” Zuko cuts in, voice harsh. “So. Maybe she has the right to.”

That’s…fucked up, but Sokka isn’t going to state that, too. “In the play,” he finally says, words careful.

“What?” Zuko frowns.

“In the play,” Sokka repeats. “You betrayed her in the play.” Because for Zuko to betray her in real life, too, would mean…what?

Zuko holds his eyes for a moment, face opaque behind his scowl, then glances away, jaw set.

Right. Another piece for Sokka to tuck away to try to make sense of later along with all the others.

“Zuko…” Sokka says slowly. “Just because someone says they love you, that doesn’t make it okay for them to hurt you.”

Zuko snorts. “Azula would never say that to me.”

“That…makes it even less okay,” Sokka says, fighting to understand. “Someone who hurts you, over and over—they haven’t earned anything from you. Let alone your loyalty. Someone like that doesn’t deserve anything from you except to be told to fuck off.”

And Spirits, is—is Sokka contributing to this somehow? Is his love of Zuko restraining him, of skating toward the edge of pleasure and pain under Zuko’s touch, somehow typing Zuko up even more in seeing painful things as acts of love? In normalizing affection that hurts? But Zuko isn’t a *child*. Thinking like that, acting like Zuko must be twisted in some way, like he needs Sokka to show him how things are supposed to be when there’s clearly just far too much Sokka doesn’t understand about Zuko’s relationship with his sister—that won’t get Sokka anything but trouble.

“It’s not like that,” Zuko finally says, echoing Sokka’s thoughts, and Spirits, Sokka wants Zuko to be right about that for so many reasons.

“You’re saying it isn’t,” Sokka says, tugging on his wolf tail and wishing he felt like he were standing on more solid ground, with this, but he just doesn't *know*, “But how many of your scars are from her?”

“You don’t know what you’re talking about,” Zuko snaps, shoulders tight, and that's the fucking *problem*.

“Then *tell* me,” Sokka begs. “Zuko, help me *understand*. Because the way I see it? You’re willing to write off almost anything she does to you, no matter how awful, just because she’s the one doing it. At least help me see what she’s ever done to earn that!”

“…She’s my sister,” Zuko says, frowning down at his feet, tone somewhere between spiky and half-bewildered, like it shouldn’t even need saying.

“Family can still hurt you,” Sokka says, then winces, immediately feeling dumb. Zuko knows that more than anyone, he doesn’t need Sokka fucking informing him of that fact.

“She’s…protective,” Zuko finally says, words and body stiff, which Sokka wholly deserves. Spirits, he…could be handling this better, and maybe he shouldn’t have started it when he was already feeling so out of sorts after that play. At least Zuko didn’t just tell *him* to fuck off, for that.

“*Protective*,” Sokka repeats, trying to keep the incredulity out of his voice. Of what, her own personal ambitions?

Zuko gives him a sideways look. “You know what it’s like to have a protective little sister.”

Sokka is completely thrown. “Not like *that*.”

“No?” Zuko challenges. “Maybe because Katara hasn’t had to be yet, then.”

Sokka pulls up short, his immediate denial running up against the memory of Katara going after Zuko in Ba Sing Se expressly against Sokka’s wishes, of her suspicious hostility that took so long to thaw. Except…those things are different, right? And Katara was *afraid* of becoming like Hama, and that fear meant something. But...what if it only felt unfounded to Sokka because he wasn’t in Katara’s head?

“So what, it’s just the situation?” Sokka finally asks, trying to imagine the kind of circumstances that would make Azula’s behavior okay time after time after time and only managing to come up with the realization that he’s just fundamentally missing too much context to even begin. “You’re saying Azula really isn’t dangerous?”

Zuko shakes his head, a quick, sharp denial. “I would never say that.”

“Help me get it, then,” Sokka says, hoping he isn’t pushing against some hard boundary of Zuko’s. “I want to understand. I want to see it the way you do.” He *needs* to understand if he doesn’t want to keep running up against his inability to comprehend this fundamental part of Zuko’s life.

Zuko is quiet for so long that Sokka thinks he’s just going to ignore the question, that somehow he stumbled too hard against the vulnerable edges of Zuko’s past and forced a retreat. So when he finally speaks, it’s so sudden in the darkness that Sokka almost stumbles in surprise.

“When we were little,” Zuko says, voice low, “The other noble families in Caldera used to send their kids to the palace. Everyone wants their kid to grow up friends with the royal children, you know? And we were a whole second chance after Lu Ten for the generals and important families and wealthy merchants, even some Earth Kingdom nobles trying to hedge their bets. That kind of thing.”

Sokka nods as if he knows a single thing about generals trying to suck up to his family.

“But eventually the younger ones stopped coming. And then the older ones too. Because the visiting kids always seemed to somehow get more hurt than they should.” Zuko glances up at the moon cutting between the trees, Yue’s uneven light making dark valleys and sharp ridges of his scar. “Burns from fires that got a bit too out of control. Minor ones, but scary. And being burned in the Fire Nation, especially for a bender…” He shrugs. “Eating food they were allergic to, even though the kitchen staff would have never served it. Games of tag that always somehow ended with falls that were a bit too hard. A few broken bones.”

“…Getting pushed off roofs?”

“No.” Zuko’s tone is utterly serious. “That would have been too obvious.”

Sokka manages to control his reaction to a strangled, “Oh.”

“And I liked having people my age around,” Zuko says, picking back up the thread of his story. “So I was sad when the others stopped coming. The palace is big, too big for just me and her. And royal kids aren’t much use to anyone until we’re old enough to begin bending training for real, so we were at loose ends a lot. Having someone else to play with was…nice. So it sucked, all the other kids getting driven away until it was just me and her in and Mai and Ty Lee—and I wasn’t getting close to them, then, so they didn’t really count yet.” A shrug. “It didn’t seem worth it when Azula was still trying. It took her a while to realize their parents were willing to risk them.”

That’s…horrifying. And paints Azula in a truly terrible light, one that has Sokka genuinely worried like he hadn’t been before that she’s in the line of succession, a heartbeat away from even more power than she already has. Which…isn’t what he thinks Zuko set out to do. “I… feel like I’m missing something.”

Zuko struggles for a long time, opening and closing his mouth, Sokka forcing himself to stay quiet until Zuko finally finds his words. “It sucked. A lot. But…It sucked a lot less than when the kids got sent home with the kind of burns that happen when you’re too close to a fire when an adult firebender gets angry and doesn’t feel like keeping control.”

Sokka…really doesn’t understand. “Adults…went after kids? That was just a thing that happened?” Fuck, Sokka’s been operating under the assumption that what happened to Zuko *wasn’t* normal, he thought that’s what Zuko meant back in the North...

Zuko cuts Sokka a quick look. “It was never *allowed*,” he finally says, face tight. “But…I don’t know if the palace has ever been a safe place for children. Maybe when Lu Ten was little? Sometimes a display of anger was a useful thing, I guess."

Sokka feels numb as the implication sinks in, as if his body and mind don’t want it to be true, don’t want to let it stick, even though there is no other way to hear what Zuko is saying. Not allowed, then, but…condoned. Silently and maybe more and more easily as it went on, because Sokka can understand how even something as horrifying as that can become more and more normal the longer it goes on. Until maybe the idea of burning a child as public punishment doesn’t seem so out of the ordinary at all.

“I tried to take the blame for stuff, sometimes,” Zuko adds on, a frown settling over his features. “I didn’t like seeing them get hurt. But Azula didn’t like when I got hurt instead.” He catches Sokka’s eyes. “So she made sure it wouldn’t be an option anymore.”

By taking away the thing that was indirectly hurting Zuko, because she couldn’t touch the thing directly causing the harm. And if it hurt Zuko in the process to lose those friends… maybe Azula decided the emotional pain was tolerable, against the risk of physical injury. Sokka feels queasy. Fuck, how old were they? Because Zuko is talking about tag and being too young for real lessons, and Spirits, he’s older than Azula is.

Sokka abruptly remembers Zuko back in the North. Bruised and battered and running on nothing but willpower, explaining all the reasons why he couldn’t just give up. Explaining that he had to try to get back home, because his sister didn’t care about anything but what was hers, and if he didn’t make it then she could be in charge of…everything. Sokka wonders at the assumption there, the leap from Zuko's downfall to Azula's rise.

“…Does your sister think you’re hers?” Sokka finally asks, something like dread coalescing in his gut. *Still* think Zuko is hers, he maybe should have said, because there was a clear, bright streak of possessiveness in the story Zuko just told.

Zuko makes a sharp sound that might be a laugh under better circumstances. “I might be the only one left who can say that,” he sighs, tipping his head back. “And I’m not entirely sure anymore.”

Sokka supposes someone shooting lightning at you would make that fairly ambiguous, and Spirits, Sokka hates that this conversation is happening at nighttime when they can’t see each other as well, after that play when they’re both already off-balance, that they’re walking and can’t fully focus on each other. That they’re in the Fire Nation, where apparently *this kind of* *thing* is illegal, except Sokka also has the memory of Zuko’s *some things are worth it*, and after a moment of struggling with himself Sokka reaches out, knuckles grazing the back of Zuko’s hand, breath leaving him when a rush when Zuko immediately fumbles back in the darkness to tangle their fingers together and pull Sokka a little closer into his side.

"...Has she seen you redirect lightning before?" Sokka asks after a few steps, and Zuko’s low noise says he’s picking the thread of the conversation up right where it left off, too.

Zuko cuts him a sideways look through the fall of his hair. “Actually seen me do it?” Sokka nods. “Once.”

“Spirits,” Sokka mutters, trying to wrap his mind around the magnitude of the gamble Zuko seems to feel she’s comfortable taking, assuming all of this isn’t just…wishful thinking, on Zuko’s part. “And you think Katara’s like that?”

Zuko frowns, flicking his hair out of his eyes, openly confused. “You don’t?”

…Not really, but Sokka’s opinion is probably the less relevant one in this particular situation. “Does Katara know you think that about her?”

“I don’t know,” Zuko says after a moment, the motion of his shrug making it's way into their clasped hands. "I haven't told her."

“Maybe you should,” Sokka says quietly.

“…Why?”

“I think she’d want to know.” He thinks she’d be horrified.

“I don’t think it would make her happy,” Zuko says after a pause, echoing his thoughts.

“No,” Sokka agrees, sighing. “But she’d still want to know.” All that terror of becoming like Hama—that had all been real. Sokka doesn’t think he and his sister have changed so much, lost so much ability to read each other anymore, that he’s wrong about this.

Zuko nods after a moment, face still tight and frowning but with something more like thought, and Sokka lets the quiet draw out, thinking about protective little sisters full of power and determined to act and the kinds of things someone like that might do.

“Thank you,” Sokka eventually says, giving Zuko’s hand a quick squeeze. “For telling me. For helping me understand.” For going against what Sokka knows is Zuko’s instinct and sharing something that’s revealing of more than just his own past.

Zuko shrugs, head ducking with that mingled uncertainty and embarrassment he usually gets the minute anyone thanks him. “It’s what we’re supposed to do, right? Share stuff.”

“Well, yeah, but—not just because we’re supposed to do it.” It’s not an obligation, not some kind of tax they both owe the other for the right to say they’re together, it’s…feeling safe doing it with each other. It’s *wanting* to do it with each other. “It’s—" Shit, what were Zuko's words. "—sharing problems, right? And the things you want, not just the things that are good.”

Zuko is quiet a long moment, brow furrowed, his thumb absently stroking over the back of Sokka’s hand the only thing keeping Sokka from becoming a fidgety mess of anxious waiting. “Partners,” Zuko finally says, nodding a little and giving Sokka’s shoulder a light bump, and Sokka’s breath catches a little in his throat over everything in Zuko's voice in that one word. He supposes that works just as well.

And being a partner, being someone Zuko can lean on and rely on, and who Sokka can lean on in turn...that’s about more than just them, right? “Is…was all this a secret? Can I tell the others?”

Sokka can feel the way Zuko immediately tenses, his hand gripping Sokka’s a little tighter as he cuts him a quick, confused look.

“Sometimes,” Sokka says, “People have questions about you, and I don’t know how you want me to answer them.”

“Questions,” Zuko echoes, voice going tight.

“Like after you showed people your house the other day,” Sokka says, trying to catch a look at Zuko’s face under the shadow of his hair. “It seemed like you wanted them to see it.” Zuko offers a little shrug, glancing away, one of his little uncomfortable ‘yes’ gestures. “But then people wanted to know if you were okay after—” Zuko winces slightly. “—and I didn’t know how to give a real answer without saying something about your past, or something else you’ve told me. And I don’t want to share stuff you don’t want people to know, but I don’t want to act like *you’re* a secret. And if it’s hard for you to share, but I already know it, and then maybe you don’t have to be the one sharing it…” Sokka trails off, swallowing back the mess of words he could pile on and tracking the fractional lowering of Zuko’s shoulders as he thinks.

“It’s hard for me,” Zuko finally says, frowning down, “Not knowing what other people know or not. *Knowing* things is half of what Azula does. And knowing something that someone doesn’t realize you know…”

“You know no one’s trying to hurt you here,” Sokka says, a protective, sharp spark lighting in his chest. If Zuko says differently, if anyone is…

“It’s hard to just…stop that kind of thing,” Zuko sighs, leaning briefly into Sokka’s shoulder, rubbing a soothing circle over the back of his hand. “It’s habit.”

And Sokka supposes it would be especially hard to break the habits that kept you alive. “So do you want to be the one to talk to people?” Sokka finally asks. Because Sokka doesn't think they can continue not sharing at all. “I can tell people to ask you instead of me.”

“That’s not practical,” Zuko mutters, pulling a face.

“I’m not talking about practical, though, I’m talking about what you want,” Sokka says, tugging lightly on Zuko’s hand when Zuko just stares in response, nearly walking off the path as it turns. “What if I tell you after someone asks me something? Then you would know who knows what.”

“You can’t do that forever,” Zuko protests, as if the tension isn't slipping out of his shoulders at the idea.

“It’s just the six of us now,” Sokka points out. “And you only need to say things once with this group, anyway.”

“…It would be nice,” Zuko admits, ducking his head like it’s embarassing to say it.

“I can do that,” Sokka assures him, a relief unspooling through him at finally having a plan in place. “And you’ll let me know if I mess up and share too much?”

“I trust your judgment,” Zuko shrugs, nodding, which just sends another wave of something bright, something close to pride, flowing through Sokka and he half-leans into Zuko in silent thanks, feeling the solid strength of him and the vibration Zuko’s hum as Sokka trusts him with his weight.

They walk a few steps like that before Sokka straightens again, both of them letting the silence draw out beyond the sounds of the forest and the soft noise of their steps, the others barely audible on the path ahead of them. Sokka tries to sort through Zuko’s words in the quiet, does his best to hold Zuko’s image of Azula against the reality of her that Sokka has experienced without letting his own feelings and judgments get in the way. Which is harder than Sokka wants it to be—though maybe exactly as hard as he expected—and he’s deep in his thoughts when Zuko suddenly speaks, quiet and raspy and still making Sokka startle.

“I can hear you thinking, Sokka,” Zuko says, the question silent but still clear in the tap of Zuko's thumb on the back of Sokka's hand.

Sokka sighs. “I just…still don’t like the idea of someone hurting you,” he says, bracing himself for the possible return of Zuko’s defensiveness. *Protectiveness*, he corrects himself. “I’m not saying you’re wrong about Azula, but…it still feels really messed up. It doesn't feel like any of that makes it *okay*."

“The world is fucked up,” Zuko says quietly, with more than a little bleakness even as his hand stays loose and relaxed against Sokka’s. “We all do what we have to do to survive it.”

“You shouldn’t have to be fucked up to get through,” Sokka says, kicking at the sand as the forest path starts to give way to the beach. “Or let someone fuck you up, or whatever.” “No,” Zuko agrees after a beat. “You shouldn’t.” But his tone says how it should be doesn’t have much bearing on how it is, and Sokka hates that he doesn’t know how to argue with that.

He tugs Zuko to a stop instead, right on the tree line before they reach the beach where Sokka can see the shadow of the others moving against the cheerful little fire Aang’s brought back to life. Zuko turns easily into him, already reaching with his free arm to pull Sokka against him and keep him close as Sokka tucks his face into the curve of Zuko's neck, not quite sure if he's offering comfort or seeking it or something in between.

Sokka holds on tight to Zuko’s hand as his free hand finds it's way into Zuko’s hair, taking assurance in Zuko’s familiar warmth and the strength of his arm around Sokka’s lower back and the always-fast beat of his heart. He runs his nails over Zuko’s scalp like he knows his firebender secretly loves and turns over the possibility that there may be some things that no amount of sharing can ever replicate the experience of living, some things that Sokka may never be able to truly understand about how Zuko sees the world. And he rests his temple against Zuko’s, taking a moment to just *be* together, as he stares down the idea of hurting someone as an act of care and the fact that it might not be as unfamiliar as Sokka wants it to be.

&#45;-

Sokka is doing his part to prep the campsite for bed, inventorying their supplies and getting together a snack for Momo and Appa and maybe also himself. It’s what Sokka does every night, just like Katara always sorts out food for breakfast the next day, usually sitting across from him in quiet conversation or companionable silence.

The silence tonight is more strained awkwardness than companionable, and Sokka doesn’t kid himself that the conversation he can feel about to break is going to be anything approaching quiet.

Spirits, Sokka is just…really looking forward to crawling into his bedroll with Zuko on the far side of this and feeling the familiar, grounding way Zuko goes boneless and soft with sleep on top of him, safe and relaxed and unhurt at least in that moment. Sokka just has to get through this first, and he’s starting to wonder whether making himself available and letting Katara decide how to start is going to work here like it always used to for the aftermaths of their fights back home.

Jet wasn’t exactly a *fight* for either of them, after all.

“Can I have the knife when you’re done?” Sokka asks, frowning around the fire as he tries to locate their other paring knife. Shit, did he forget to put it back the last time he sharpened it?

“Maybe you want to have the knife first,” Katara mutters as she nods, low enough that Sokka isn’t entirely sure he’s meant to hear. “Or maybe we can use it at the same time, all nice and *balanced*.”

He was definitely meant to hear that. “Okay,” Sokka says, wincing, “One—ew. And two, no need to be so…”

“So what?” Katara huffs, voice low. “So *amazed* that I had to find out from a *play* that my own brother never told me that he—” She cuts herself off, cheeks flushed dark, looking like she can’t decide whether to retreat back behind her hair or keep glowering.

“That he *made out with* the guy you were infatuated with?” Sokka whispers back, putting some extra emphasis on what exactly he did do, because Spirits, the last thing he needs is her gutter mind running wild. “Probably within a day of you, right before the guy tried to trick you into helping him drown a whole fucking village?”

“I wasn’t infatuated!” Katara hisses, and Sokka is *more* than happy to focus on that piece instead.

“Jet literally kicked an old man on the ground, and you still wanted to give him a chance.”

“And how many times did *you* kiss him after that,” Katara asks, snide, smacking the knife down into the sand between them.

“Well I didn’t *want* to, after that,” Sokka snaps as he grabs the blade, annoyed that the answer can’t be ‘zero.’ Fucking Jet.

“Oh, but you just did it anyway? What, for the practice? What the *fuck*, Sokka. You *knew* I liked him! And you already had your—your letter thing going on.”

“*He* kissed *me*,” Sokka says, annoyed and not wanting to get into getting tied to a fucking tree and then—ugh. Especially when part of what makes Sokka so annoyed about it all is that he didn’t wholly hate it. “And not everything I do is about you, Katara.”

“You kissing the person who gave me my first kiss when you *saw* us talking like that feels like it is!”

“He was *talking* at me too,” Sokka snaps, stung. “And he was *also* my first kiss, so it kind of feels like maybe we should both be mad at him!” Sokka clamps his mouth shut, belatedly aware of his rising voice as all the heads that had been politely pretending not to notice the siblings squabbling suddenly turn toward them.

“How are we doing over here,” Suki asks after a beat, tone pitched to soothe which Sokka does *not* appreciate right now.

“Fine,” he grumbles, hearing himself sulky and clearly not fine which only makes him even more annoyed.

“Great,” Katara mutters, dripping with sarcasm as she glares down at the last of her meal prep.

“…Really convincing there, guys,” Suki says.

“Oh, do you want us to be more calm and *balanced*?” Katara snaps. “You don’t have to listen if it bothers you, you know. I was just having a nice little talk with my brother about his new habit of withholding important information.”

“Oh, *that’s* what we’re talking about now?” Sokka says, incredulous. “You want to act like I’m the only one who withholds here?”

She winces, jaw set even as she flashes a guilty look toward Zuko.

“*When* was I supposed to tell you, Katara?” Sokka demands, wondering if they could possibly be remembering the same events. “When you were dealing with the fact that the guy you thought was amazing and great turned out to be trying to use you to kill a bunch of innocent people? What good would it have done to add the fact that he was a total sleaze on to that? Or maybe I should have mentioned it when you and Aang were finally starting to trust me again,” Sokka continues, powering through the way his voice wants to waver. “Or during storytime one night? What fucking good would it have done!”

“It’s not about the *good*,” Katara says, lips pressed tight. “You shouldn’t have had to come up with a reason. I deserved to know, that should have been all you needed.”

“You don’t get to know everything,” Sokka says, shoving his hands through his hair and feeling suddenly overfull of so many things he didn’t even realize he was feeling. “And you didn’t *want* to know everything, in case you forgot that I had to get my fucking *heart* broken and pretend it wasn’t happening for you.” She flinches back, eyes going wide, and Zuko makes a low, tight sound behind Sokka. “Spirits, Katara, we couldn’t get any *space* from each other, and you want to know everything on top of that? I didn’t tell you because it wasn’t important!”

“It feels like it was pretty fucking important right now!”

“Well, it wasn’t important to *me*.” Not with everything that happened after, the storm and the ship and Zuko.

“Maybe you don’t get to decide what’s important,” Katara says, tight.

“And you do?” Sokka says, feeling his frustration truly spark. “And how are you going to do that? Do I just tell you everything and you get to let me know if you care about hearing it? Should I have been telling you about every time I jerked off, too, so you could decide if that was important? Or hey, how about the first time I gave a hand job? That was pretty important, want to know that, too?”

Katara flushes, glancing away, so determinedly not looking in Zuko's direction that it clearly takes physical effort. Aang clears his throat after a beat of taut silence. “You, ah. Actually told me about that.”

“And I overheard,” Katara mutters. Zuko makes another little sound, this one like he’s dying.

“Oh,” Sokka says, throwiing up his hands, his anger and irritation snapping for anything to hold on to, so much and so unexpected that he barely knows what to do with it. “Good to know I’m only supposed to tell you about *some* parts of my sex life.”

“You know that’s not the same,” Katara says, flicking him an annoyed, embarrassed look. “You didn’t even say anything about Jet in Ba Sing Se!"

"I don’t see how it was relevant in Ba Sing Se,” Sokka grumbles, and Spirits, he needs to send himself to bed, because he can feel himself devolving into pure contrarianism here.

“Don’t play dumb,” Katara huffs. “You’re the one who brought Jet to us.”

“Aang was there too!”

“Aang didn’t kiss Jet!”

“I didn’t,” Aang puts in, heartfelt. “I really, really promise I didn’t.”

“Look, clearly this is a touchy subject,” Toph says, breaking in as the voice of reason instead of the voice of further chaos, which is enough on its own to make Sokka hold his breath and force himself to pause. “And as much as I’d love to listen to you both detail your respective simultaneous crushes on this guy, he seemed like a total dickhead, and I’m *fucking* tired.”

She pauses, grinning, and Sokka feels his heart sink as he exchanged a quick, guilty look with Katara. Spirits take everything, they managed to make it all this time without slipping and they mess up over this?

Fucking Jet.

“So how about we just say whoever here hasn’t kissed Jet can cast the first stone on the subject,” Toph continues, “And everyone else can shut up about it and just accept that you both have awful taste in men.”

“I can live with that,” Aang mutters, rubbing tiredly at his eyes.

Sokka crosses his arms and so does Katara in a horrifyingly similar gesture under the circumstances, both of them looking sharply away as silence falls. Sokka…can also live with that.

“Well,” Toph finally says. “Since *no one else* is going to say anything about it then, I guess we can all—” She cuts herself off, and Sokka’s head is jerking up almost before he registers the implication, meeting Katara’s wide, startled eyes before they both turn to Suki and Zuko.

Suki scratches at her shoulder, looking entirely unconcerned. “Pretty tall and lean? Ridiculous hair, like he just fell out of bed? Always chewing on some straw? Did this—” She lets her face take on a half-lidded, seductive pout. “—lean-y thing?”

Katara chokes.

“Sounds right,” Suki says cheerfully, straightening. “I met him at the ferry terminal when me and the Warriors were working there. He had some time to kill before his ferry and my shift was ending.”

Sokka stares, not knowing if he should be horrified or…fist bump her, or…really what the reaction should be. The idea of Suki getting physical with someone doesn’t bother him, just…it’s *Jet*.

Sokka’s eyes swing to Zuko, who sighs, scratching the back of his head. “I was on the ferry,” he mutters, studying his feet very intently. “And. Um. He lived near the teashop. In Ba Sing Se. And came by. For a while.”

“…What the fuck,” Sokka finally says, pinching the bridge of his nose as Katara makes a noise of pure disbelief. How—what are the *odds—*

“...I take it back," Toph says, sounding stunned and absolutely delighted. “You *all* have terrible taste. Anyone who kissed this guy, shout it out, compare notes. Oma and Shu, the Earth Rumble didn’t have *anything* on this.”

&#45;-

Zuko…is mostly sure the silence between him and Sokka isn’t an awkward one in the wake of all the night’s revelations. But it’s definitely *there* as he slides into their shared bedroll, and knowing Sokka he doesn’t think it’s going to last.

Zuko trusts in the darkness to provide enough privacy from the others—Aang was relentless, once they left the Western Air Temple, in having everyone together—and holds himself up on one forearm until Sokka finishes wiggling down underneath him and getting comfortable. Then Zuko drapes himself in his usual spot over Sokka, letting out a little unbidden sigh of contentment as Sokka immediately begins scratching through Zuko’s hair.

“So,” Sokka finally says, voice pitched low, just for Zuko. “Jet, huh.”

Zuko takes half a peek at Sokka’s face, settling back to nod against Sokka’s chest when he sees it’s more relaxed and curious than anything else.

“You know, with me,” Sokka says, clearing his throat a little. “The play was uh, close enough to how it actually…you know. But, ah, how..?”

Zuko walks his fingers down the ladder of Sokka’s ribs, thinking. “Just…I was alone on the ferry except for Uncle. And there wasn’t really anything to do, except then he popped up and we kind of…”

“Did something only vaguely legal but very noble-sounding?”

“…Basically. And then Ba Sing Se is so…much. And he was the only person I knew other than Uncle, and he was making an effort to come around, and…well. You know how he is.” Or…was. Zuko still isn’t entirely clear, on that, and no one else seems to be either…

Sokka makes an understanding noise in the back of his throat, fingers rubbing thoughtful little circles on the back of Zuko’s neck that feel just…fucking divine right now. “Did you stop because of me?” Sokka finally asks, the words halting, like he isn’t entirely sure how he would feel about that.

Zuko snorts. If only. That would have made things easy, in comparison. Or—maybe complicated, but in a much more straightforward way. “We stopped because he came into the teashop with some swords trying to out us as firebenders.”

Sokka’s chest freezes for a moment beneath Zuko’s cheek. “That…does sound like Jet,” he finally says, fingers resuming their patterns along the base of Zuko’s skull.

Zuko hums in agreement, feeling his body loosen as Sokka’s hand migrates down to his shoulders. “I’m pretty sure he was only doing anything with me after the first few times to try to gather evidence.”

“That…also sounds like Jet,” Sokka sighs, voice sad.

“I mean. I was using him back, I guess,” Zuko shrugs, vaguely registering that the topic isn’t doing anything to prevent him from continuing to relax on Sokka. Zuko supposes that he spent enough time thinking about it that it doesn’t feel as raw as it used to, especially not when Sokka is against him and holding him and *loving* him, and just that word, that fact, feels magnitudes larger than every single thing that happened with Jet combined.

“…You seem remarkably chill about it all,” Sokka comments, working on a knot half-under Zuko's shoulder blade that has Zuko nearly groaning in pleasure-pain. “I still get annoyed when I think about him.”

Zuko can tell, with the way Sokka is more than a little tense beneath him. “I was, for a while,” Zuko says, refraining from pointing out that Sokka’s situation might be just a bit different. It’s not like Jet ever tried to make a move on Azula.

“But not anymore?”

Zuko makes the audible equivalent of a shrug, since Sokka has just finished massaging all the tension out of his shoulders. “I guess I never thought it was going to be some lasting thing.” He’d been shocked for days, really, when Jet showed back up at all. “I never really got why he was sticking around or what he was getting out of it. So it at least…made sense, after that.” Jet had been a conniving shithead and had known exactly how to capitalize on Zuko’s aimlessness, and Zuko could sit more easily with that than the idea that Jet was actually emotionally invested.

Sokka makes a quiet thinking noise, his hands still working down Zuko’s back, so Zuko shoves back the edges of sleep and waits for Sokka to gather his thoughts.

“It’s just feeling very weird,” Sokka finally says. “That he was my first kiss, and you also kissed him.” And so did everyone else in the crew, apparently, not that Zuko’s going to point that out again. “And then you were my first—everything else.”

“You were my first kiss,” Zuko offers after a beat, not entirely sure what to say.

“…And he was your first everything else?”

“Not everything,” Zuko says, trying to parse Sokka’s tone. “Are you…jealous?”

“No,” Sokka huffs, a quick little half-laugh. “Shit, can you imagine if neither one of us knew what we were doing? What a disaster that would have been. Thank the Spirits one of us hand a clue. I just…it sucks that he was such a shit, and that both of us had to deal with him. What are the odds that we both run into the same dickhead like that?”

“And Suki, too,” Zuko can’t resist murmuring—apparently, he *is* going to point that out again —peeking up with a smile when Sokka makes a noise of mock-outrage.

“Ugh,” Sokka groans. “Okay, fine. I’m done. No more fucking Jet talk tonight.”

“Oh,” Zuko can’t resist teasing, “I wasn’t aware you were wanting specifics.”

“You—!” Sokka bites off the word as Zuko muffles his laughter against Sokka’s chest. “Enough *Jet* talk,” Sokka repeats, quelling, giving Zuko’s ass a light warning smack. Then he pauses, considering. “We can talk about the other bit tomorrow.”

“It’s a deal,” Zuko grins, inner flame light as he finally lets himself slide toward sleep, able to let himself just sink down with something happy to look forward to against the steadily ticking clock.

### End Notes

#### Chapter End Notes

Did I write an entire three-part canon rewrite solely for the joy of Toph saying everyone who knows Jet has to shut up and the unexpected majority of the people present shutting their mouths? I'm not going to say no

## Chapter 27: The Bending Masters

### Notes

#### Chapter Notes

Warnings for sexual content in this one!

### Text

Sokka approaches the lunch fire—even when it's sweltering, they can’t seem to stop gathering around it, and Sokka can’t believe there’s anything worse than the Si Wong Desert, but at least the desert wasn’t *humid*—and sets himself down a judicious distance from Zuko. He watches as Zuko looks at the distance, then glances around the circle, finally giving a shrug and lifting up a spoonful of jook just as Toph casually lifts her face, face splitting into a wicked grin as she raises a hand.

Sokka tucks his bowl into his body and watches as a rain of sand showers down onto Zuko.

“Not even a warning,” Suki murmurs around her laughter, shaking her head at Sokka. “What a boyfriend you are.”

Sokka watches as Zuko slowly, carefully, brushes the sand out of his face. “I told him not to taunt her about the sandbending.”

“Who’s the greatest bender you’ve ever met *now*!” Toph crows, two orbs of sand forming over her hands.

“Probably still Aang,” Zuko says, eyeing them all before tilting his head forward and giving it a vigorous shake, sand spraying out of his hair around the circle. They yelp, jerking back— except for Toph—and Aang throws up his hands for protection, or maybe in preemptive surrender.

Toph tosses one ball of sand with more than a little menace. “I’ll undo it all if you admit I’m the best bender in the world.”

“…You’re the best earthbender I know?”

Toph considers that. “I’ll accept it if you make me some tea.”

“We don’t have any leaves left,” Zuko points out.

“Good thing you’re so good at getting supplies,” Toph says sweetly.

Zuko glances to Sokka, who hastily swallows his bite. “*I* think Toph is the best bender in the world.”

Toph flicks her fingers and a shower of sand drops from Sokka’s boots and pant legs back onto the beach. “As you should.”

&#45;-

Toph sniffs haughtily at the cup of tea Zuko offers her, pinky out as she takes a delicate sip. “A touch too warm,” she determines in a snotty, Upper Ring tone.

Zuko rolls his eyes. “My apologies, Lady Beifong,” Zuko says, and Sokka nearly laughs when Toph wrinkles her face at the respect before holding out her cup for Zuko to lay a finger against.

“Perfect,” Toph decrees. She makes a great show of savoring her next sip before finally waving her hand, the sand flying off Zuko. After another considering sip she twists her wrist and the sand comes out of Zuko’s bowl, too, which is a nice gesture considering Zuko already ate half of Sokka's.

Sokka scoots right over to Zuko when he sits back down, cheerfully accepting Zuko’s mild, “Traitor.”

“Only one of us knows how to make good tea.”

“*Wow*, Sokka,” Suki chokes, shaking her head.

Sokka’s too busy giving her a look to notice what Zuko’s doing until a hand is settling on his shoulder, abruptly pulling, unbalancing Sokka on his driftwood seat just enough that he needs to throw out his forearms to catch himself…in the sand.

Katara doesn’t even try to muffle her laugh, Aang giggling as Sokka pointedly rights himself and brushes himself off. He gives Zuko a sideways look, aiming for something dramatically wounded, but Zuko’s heating up his jook, and the answering glance he gives Sokka through his eyelashes is full of amusement so that…works, actually.

“Hey, Sand Shark,” Toph says, pausing in consideration before shaking her head and clearly discarding the nickname as a bad attempt. “You can heat this up—” She flicks a flick against her tea. “—and make it steam, right?”

“Yeah,” Zuko says, rolling his eyes and already reaching. Sokka thinks that a better new nickname would have been ‘Heat Pack.’

“Could you take the heat away and make it ice? Because Ember Island is really living up to its name right now.”

Zuko blinks, arm hanging half-extended as he glances toward Katara, who looks equally dumbstruck by the idea. “I…I can’t do ice,” Zuko finally says. “That’s…water.”

“But you can make things cold,” Sokka points out before he has time to consider the words and possibly needing to provide a moment to reference. He keeps his face carefully still and his breathing steady as he remembers that bathtub in Ba Sing Se, Zuko’s fingers stitching fire and ice down the ridges of his spine.

“I mean, I can dissipate the heat until it’s room temperate again,” Zuko says.

“No, you—that thread the needle thing. Remember?” Best not to think too much of that around Toph, if the sand can no longer save him.

Sokka watches realization hit Zuko, immediately followed by uncertainty as he glances down at his own hands. “I don’t…”

“You usually just make it match the ambient temperature?” Aang asks.

“Yeah. Heat wants to—” Zuko makes a rocking gesture with his hand. “—equalize.”

“And what are you doing when you make it hotter?”

Zuko scratches the back of his head, then grabs up his bowl, going still with concentration. “Inner flame,” he finally says.

Katara frowns, her own hands sketching half-completed waterbending gestures that Sokka is pretty sure usually result in ice. “Could you just…keep bleeding the heat away?”

“Sounds like experiment time,” Sokka says brightly into Zuko’s baffled silence, muffling a laugh when Zuko gathers himself enough to glare uselessly at Toph when she promptly offers up her tea, pinky finger extended.

Zuko carefully cups the mug, his stillness shifting toward a frown until he finally twitches, shaking himself, looking nearly physically uncomfortable. “It’s…I do heat,” Zuko says, flexing one hand, then the other. “And if it gets too cold it isn’t heat any longer. It’s like… trying to bend the absence of water. There isn’t anything there to grab.”

All the benders frown, considering that, and Sokka exchanges a glance with Suki. It sounds like philosophy, to him. He likes philosophy. The good stuff gets almost poetic, just how good poetry verges on the philosophical.

He has a feeling this is not going to sound like the good stuff.

“What if you do it really fast,” Katara finally suggests.

Zuko stares at the tea, brow furrowed, then reaches out and there’s never anything to see, generally, when Zuko plays with heat, but Sokka assumes he…does it really fast, just like Katara suggested, because he suddenly makes an odd gurgling noise and nearly drops the tea, coughing out a few sparks.

Sokka hastily transfers the cup to the ground, bracing Zuko up and giving him a few firm pats on the back until Zuko waves in away, sucking in a rough breath, then another. Sokka slowly sits back once Zuko’s breathing goes smooth again, finally glancing at the cup. The definitely cold cup.

“Maybe fast, but not in?” Sokka suggests after a moment, flicking a drop of cold tea at Zuko, earning himself a surprised flash of gold. “None of that—stoking yourself too high or whatever.” Sokka doesn’t particularly like to think of Zuko in relation to coal engines blowing up.

Zuko nods, carefully picking the cup back up, poking at the contents a moment with an expression somewhere between curiosity and uncertainty on his face before heating it back up until it's steaming. He stretches his other hand out toward the fire and frowning and—

The fire roars high, everyone flinching back in surprise except for Zuko, who goes, quietly, “…Huh.” And as Sokka leans back in, he sees that Zuko is now holding a little cup of ice.

&#45;-

Suki raises a knowing eyebrow at Sokka. “This wouldn’t have happened if you had just warned him about the sand.”

“Shut up.”

“I’m just saying.” She makes a valiant attempt at fighting a smirk. “You’re only in a trap of your own making here.”

Sokka snaps out his polishing cloth with more vigor than is strictly necessary and sets himself to ignoring her, because it is, in fact, entirely his fault. If Zuko had never had to make that tea then Toph would never have asked in the first place and Sokka wouldn’t be sitting further away than he wants from his firebender, crowded out by his very own sister of all people.

Katara is eager to see how fast Zuko can take something from boiling to ice, and then the reverse, and then how slowly he can go before he loses his hold on the water. She shows him how she does it with waterbending while Zuko holds the water in his heat sense, whatever that means, and then tries copying the move. Which involves Zuko looking bemused as he makes a wigglier gesture than he generally ever makes, to produce a rather limp-looking little column of smoke.

Sokka catches his eye and raises his eyebrows, which sets Zuko blushing, which is cute, and Sokka pauses in his polishing to peek at that, feeling his own cheeks going more than a little hot as Zuko peeks back until his attention finally gets pulled back to the others.

“What if *I* do it,” Aang enthuses, copying the gesture, tongue caught between his teeth in concentration. His rope of smoke is significantly more vigorous, and Sokka thinks the whole thing might be worth it just for the way Zuko's eyes shoot to him wide and laughing, a rusty *giggle* breaking free as Aang startles at the noise and turns between Zuko and Sokka, going, "What? What?"

&#45;-

Zuko has never really thought of his bending as something that could be particularly fun. Important, yes. Worthy of attention and dedicated focus and thought, absolutely. Something to turn to when he was frustrated, that could make things better or earn him affirmation, sure. But messing around with Aang and Toph and Katara, as trying to understand the limits of Zuko’s bending slides into just trying out each other’s bending forms, has been…one of the better afternoons Zuko can remember having on this beach. Particularly watching Toph try to execute airbending forms with so much extra prancing and flourishing that Aang can barely vocalize his outrage through his laughter.

Toph does eventually haul Aang off for earthbending practice, but Katara makes no move to go off to the usual chores she occupies herself with in the afternoons. She seems to be enjoying herself as much as Zuko, which is something Zuko’s becoming more and more comfortable with, the idea that he and Katara can share things other than wariness or a sense of dual purpose.

“I’ve seen you do a fire whip thing,” Katara is saying.

“Lash,” Zuko corrects.

“Whatever. But it’s kind of—” She roughly sketches the motion of something that’s close enough for Zuko to nod along. “And when I do a water whip, it’s more—” Her hands flow, tension rolling through her frame, and a little stream of water snaps out before she has it crawl back into her waterskin.

“Again?” Zuko mentally maps out the moves and the breaths as she demonstrates slower this time, and when he thinks he finally has it he pulls his inner flame and his chi into alignment like he would when preparing for a major bending form. He runs through the motion, the forms surprisingly comfortable, and he can *feel* it click, his bending grabbing and his chi moving unlike some of the moves he's tried where his bending just swirls at the ready.

Except…nothing actually happens.

Zuko glances at his hands, then at the fire, then at the little teacup still in the sand for good measure just in case.

“That *looked* right,” Katara says, chewing on her lip as she thinks.

“It felt right.” Certainly better than producing sad little puffs of ash when he'd tried airbending forms.

“Maybe do it again,” Katara suggests, setting herself up to look intently at the fire.

Zuko throws more power behind it this time, and then again exaggerating the motions, and then another for good measure. He’s moving slowly and deliberately as Katara analyzes each step of his form when Sokka’s strained voice breaks Zuko out of his concentration.

“What are you doing?”

“Practicing,” Zuko says, most his attention on trying to see if his bending can catch hold again mid-form the way he can sometimes muscle through a firebending form gone wrong, or if he needs to start at the beginning again.

“Great,” Sokka says, sounding not-great enough to grab Zuko’s full focus. “What are you practicing?”

“We’re still trying out each other’s bending forms,” Katara says, giving Sokka a quick, concerned sweep, also looking for the source of his tension.

“And…what did you just do?”

Zuko blinks. “This?” He does it again without thinking and almost fumbles right from the start when he *really* feels his bending grab hold this time. Or maybe because at the same time as Zuko feels his bending catch, Sokka makes a sound that’s relatively on par with the noises he makes when Zuko—well, it’s obscene. Zuko can’t bring himself to articulate exactly how, even to himself, when he’s sitting next to Sokka’s sister.

“Yup,” Sokka says, voice strangled and eyes shut tight and Agni, it’s taking everything Zuko has to fight back a blush. “That.”

“What—” Zuko loosens his hold, his bending releasing in a way that feels…familiar. Ish. Like it’s something he’s done before, but not this way that feels so natural and effortless, with none of the conscious effort it usually takes to maintain that initial separation between himself and the chi in his hands as he…releases Sokka’s inner flame back to him. “Oh.” How —Zuko didn’t even have to *reach* for it. It was just there, in his grasp, moving under his—oh.

“Yes,” Sokka clears his throat. “Oh. Let’s just…please never do that again when I’m in public.” Katara chokes a little, and Zuko is going to *die*. “Thanks.”

&#45;-

Zuko is embarrassingly grateful when Katara quickly suggests a new bending form to practice, both of them blushing and not quite looking each other in the eye after Sokka makes his way back to his training with Suki. Agni’s balls, Zuko doesn’t know what he would do if Katara asked what *that* was about. He doesn’t think she’d be upset over the fact of Zuko’s ability to touch Sokka’s inner almost-flame, but he’s almost positive she would demand Sokka come back for a demonstration and Zuko isn’t exactly unaware that Sokka usually leaves their chi bending practice half-hard and wanting.

“Do firebenders ever work together?” Katara asks, clearing her throat and keeping her tone brisk and professional.

“What do you mean?” Zuko asks, striving to match her. “Like against the same enemy?”

“There’s this push-pull move in waterbending that Aang and I do in tandem—”

“With the same water?” Zuko interrupts, frowning.

Zuko is so quiet, so still, that for one agonizing moment Sokka thinks he actually managed to fall asleep in the middle of that. “It’s not like other people haven’t experimented with bending styles before,” Zuko finally says, words more cautious than protesting. Testing, almost.

Sokka nearly rolls his eyes. “Who do you know who’s come up with a new bending style before without already knowing about it?”

“…Uncle.”

“And?”

“Toph.”

“And?”

“…Katara?”

…Katara did what?

“With the…body control, or whatever?”

“Oh,” Sokka says. Shit. “She showed you that, huh?” He didn’t think she was particularly eager for anyone to know about that. "Wait." He stiffens under a sudden bolt of horror. “She didn’t—”

“She didn’t,” Zuko cuts in, raising his head enough to catch Sokka’s eye. “Sokka, she didn’t.”

Good. Fucking…good, and Spirits, Sokka hates that he even thought it. That he even had *reason* to think it. “Someone taught Katara that,” he finally says, trying to pick back up the thread of the nice Zuko-is-so-great conversation he was attempting to have.

“…Huh,” Zuko says after a moment, looking like he’s deliberately deciding to set that aside to think about later.

“That’s two people, Zuko,” Sokka points out. “Which makes you three. Out of how many benders in the world? If that doesn’t meet your standards for being a Master, then I don’t know what does.”

“Usually there’s a test,” Zuko says after a long beat.

Sokka snorts. “I can assure you that no one around here except maybe Aang ever passed any tests. So if that’s the standard…”

“…Oh,” Zuko says, thoughtful this time, and after another moment he snuggles back down against Sokka’s chest. He doesn't say anything more, but his silence is more a thinking one than anything else, and after a moment Sokka finally settles back too. All Sokka can ask is that Zuko thinks about it, and he's vaguely aware that Zuko is still awake when Sokka finally drifts off himself, still thinking. But Sokka's surrounded by gentle, absent loops of heat, so he doesn’t think Zuko is thinking anything bad.

## Chapter 28: The Path Ahead

### Notes

#### Chapter Notes

No particular warnings in this one!

### Text

Sokka is having a truly amazing time wave whomping. He still isn’t entirely sure what wave whomping is, but the conditions are apparently just right, and Suki’s been trying to teach them all morning, and everyone is having a truly excellent time. And if Sokka is feeling a pang of guilt that Aang is stuck in firebending training because Zuko is as much of a stickler for a training schedule as he was for uniform regulations? Then Sokka is consoling himself that there’s always next time. And that maybe next time they’ll know what they’re actually doing enough to be able to get Aang and Zuko up to speed quickly. Suki's looking bemused by their collective inability to comprehend what they’re supposed to do, but she’s gamely demonstrating again and again, and Sokka’s feeling good that they’re going to have it figured out soon.

Though Sokka definitely doesn’t have it figured out *now*. He can feel the wave rising up under him as it’s about to break, and Suki is screaming for him to paddle, and Katara and Toph are screaming in general, but instead of being pushed forward like Suki demonstrated Sokka more…gets flipped. He yelps, clamping his mouth shut a second before he goes under, his world briefly the rushing of water and scrape of sand and sting of saltwater in his eyes before he pops back up, the surf nearly knocking him off his feet with another wave as he laughs and sputters and claws his shirt back down and tries to blink his eyes clear.

Sokka grins at the others' laughter, slicking his hair back from his face and pausing with his hands at the crown of his head when he catches sight of Zuko standing at the edge of the water. Sokka’s immediate burst of warm surprise and happiness begins to cool, though, as he takes in the way Zuko is rubbing at the back of his neck and shifting his weight on the damp sand.

“What’s up,” Sokka calls, beginning to wade toward the shore, sloshing through thigh-deep water and throwing out his arms for balance when an incoming wave shoves him forward.

Zuko flicks a quick glance toward the others. “…I think I broke the Avatar.”

“…What?” Sokka pauses to give his head a good shake. There must still be water in his ears.

“Aang’s just—sitting? With his face in his hands?” Zuko sends look up the beach where he must have left Aang, face caught between confusion and worry. “I don’t—he’s not talking.”

Sokka is still taking that in when Toph suddenly notices Zuko, calling out, "Sparrowkeet!" and towing Suki behind her as she moves to shallower water to get her feet more firmly on the sand. “Is firebending done already? Come whomp!”

“It was actually supposed to last a few more degrees,” Zuko sighs as he does that sun-reaching check of his.

“Did Aang finally wear you down?” Suki grins, obediently shadowing Toph through the water and setting a steadying hand on her shoulder as a wave breaks against Suki's back.

“Um.” The look Zuko sends him is questioning, silently seeking whatever context Sokka might have to give. “I don’t *think* that’s what he’s doing?”

“…Let’s go see?” Sokka suggests, finally moving toward shore again. Because this is weird enough that Sokka's pretty sure he doesn't have any to offer.

“Yes,” Zuko says immediately, shoulders relaxing, looking back over his shoulder again as Sokka slogs out of the water, trotting the last bit through the shallows until he’s at Zuko’s side. Sokka wrings out the bottom of his tunic as they walk, Zuko clearly holding back his pace for Sokka to sort himself out, and Sokka shoots him a quick, searching look. Zuko must be even more worried than he's showing not to take advantage of the opportunity to dry Sokka off like he usually likes to do.

“I don’t know what happened,” Zuko says, uncertainty furrowing his brow. “I—I think I said something?”

“What were you talking about?” Sokka asks, frowning. Aang doesn’t usually react that poorly to just words, and he can't think of anything Zuko could say that would make Aang truly upset. Even if they were talking about the Air Nomads, Zuko probably knows the most out of all of them except for Aang himself to be able to have a meaningful conversation about it.

“I was explaining being able to firebend in uncontrolled conditions,” Zuko says, “Like being able to still generate and control a flame during rain.” Sokka blinks. He…supposes that *would* be harder, not that Zuko's ever seemed to have an issue with it. “And I was talking about the old traditions, because Aang usually likes that, and how they used to make you test for Mastery in monsoon season, and he just kind of…”

They crest the rise of the beach to see Aang sitting, utterly still and ramrod straight except for his face in his hands, not even moving as Momo anxiously turns around his shoulders.

“…Did that,” Zuko finishes, huffing out a breath somewhere between frustrated and concerned.

“…Is it a Spirit thing?” Sokka asks, sharing a worried look with Zuko. Aang usually isn’t quite so…*emotive* during those, but…

“He’s not glowing,” Zuko says, edging a half-step backward like he doesn’t entirely trust that assessment.

Sokka runs a quick hand up Zuko’s spine—reassurance for himself as much as for Zuko— before stepping carefully toward Aang, making sure to make lots of noise and be extra obvious as he crouches down next to him on the sand, ignoring the way the dry sand clings uncomfortably to his damp skin. “Hey buddy,” Sokka says, keeping his voice easy. “Is ah—is something going on?”

Aang nods, infinitesimally, and Zuko looks relieved over his shoulder, so alright, that must be progress.

“Want to tell us about it?”

Another infinitesimal response, shaking his head.

“…Should I get Katara?”

Aang makes a choked noise then suddenly slumps, going from alarmingly stiff to folded over himself in a gesture worryingly reminiscent of…rocking back and forth? Sokka casts Zuko a wild look, absolutely not reassured that Zuko looking openly concerned.

“Aang?”

“Monsoon season,” Aang gasps out, sounding like he has to force the words out.

“…What about it?” Zuko asks, face twisting in confusion.

“Monsoon season,” Aang repeats, sounding on the edge of laughing and not at all in a good way, “It happens in the Fire Nation.”

“…Yeah,” Zuko confirms, silently gesturing that he has no idea why weather patterns are suddenly so upsetting in response to Sokka’s searching look. “Every year.”

“Every *summer*.”

Sokka goes still, feeling the cold edge of premonition even as Zuko starts to edge toward exasperated in his confusion.
