Whoever decided they should have lunch before convening an official meeting between the team and the Grand Lotus—Spirits, is it weird to think of Iroh that way—was an idiot. Which Sokka never thought he would think.

Sure, a meal is good, important talks over empty stomachs never end well. But couldn’t they have all just had a snack? Talked over food? Sokka is starting to feel jittery with waiting, like he gave Zuko all his calm and took all Zuko’s fidgets in return. He just wants to get it fucking over with. Time is wasting, but when Sokka pointed out the coming Comet all the old men had just nodded and acted like it was no big deal, which had boggled Sokka’s mind. What kind of international secret society was this *passive*?

But then, maybe that’s how you stayed secret in the first place. People noticed the things that cause the big waves.

Sokka can tell that the others are starting to get nervous as the meeting time approaches and they no longer have training to distract themselves with. The conversation gets a little more disjointed, the responses a bit tighter, people getting lost in their thoughts more and more.

“So, Bumi,” Katara tries to rally, since some of them aren’t even halfway done with their food yet. Sokka is so nervous he feels like he could eat the entire pot of jook by himself. “How did you escape Omashu?”

Zuko makes a little ‘ah’ sound, like he’s finally figured out who Bumi is, and Sokka takes a brief moment to admire Zuko’s selective ability to just go with the flow and not sweat the details he decides he doesn't care about.

“Oh, it was wonderful,” Bumi grins. “I was getting so bored, you know? And just when I was deciding I would really rather get on with things, the solar eclipse happened!” Sokka’s glad that he already finished his food because he’s pretty sure he would be choking on it otherwise, as Bumi details a truly insane story of earthbending with his face—Toph perks up at that—and riding the mail shoots and plowing through firebenders and Sokka can only gape, wondering how any of it could be true. Except the man is here, so…part of it must be.

“Really, it was time,” Bumi concludes. “Firebenders without their fire are such bores, you know.” He grins at Jeong Jeong, who lets out a long-suffering sigh that Sokka has no sympathy for.

“That’s…wow,” Katara says, struggling for a reply. “That’s…with your face?”

“Oh yes, it has so many muscles you can use! It’s all about that—” He gives a full-face wink that has everyone except Toph flinching, booming out a cackle when nothing happens. “What about you all? Did you do anything interesting when the fire was out?”

“Uh,” Sokka says, sharing a wide-eyed glance with Katara.

“Um,” Zuko offers.

Suki makes a considering noise, scraping up the last of her jook. “I started a prison riot. That was pretty cool.”

&#45;-

They finally all settle into the grand tent of the Grand Lotus, and Sokka can practically see the lever flip as Iroh goes from loving Uncle reunited with his long-lost nephew to leader of an international group of mystery. His yellow eyes sweep the table, assessing, and Sokka thinks they’d be foolish to forget that it’s also the Dragon of the West they’re dealing with.

“Now, much as I am delighted to see you all again—” Iroh starts, and Sokka thinks that’s probably directly mostly at Toph and Zuko. “—I imagine you have come here, now, for a reason.”

Before Sokka can even think about where to begin Zuko straightens into a formal seiza, back rigid and eyes direct, face settling into an expression of cool, scowling neutrality. Prince, Sokka thinks. This is Zuko being the Crown Prince, and taking his place at the Council table. “We want your help defeating the Fire Lord.”

A beat of silence, then, “That is the Avatar’s place.”

“Aang is missing,” Katara says, with a quick glance to Bumi, who looks utterly serene to hear it. “Gone.”

“Nevertheless,” Iroh says. “The winding path through the forest may seem obscure and random to the untrained eyes of man, but to the rabbaroo it is as clear and direct as any road.”

“…Come again?” Suki says, glancing around the table.

“We have faith that the Avatar will play his role when the time is right,” Pakku translates. Or adds, or—Sokka isn’t really sure which. “That is his destiny.”

“Aang isn’t some Spirit you pray to,” Sokka protests. “He’s a person.” They can’t just leave it all to *chance.* “And the Fire Nation is planning to burn down the Earth Kingdom with the Comet!”

“We know,” Jeong Jeong says, eyes flicking to Zuko. “You aren’t the only one with an ear in the Council chamber.”

Sokka isn’t sure what, exactly, the implication there was, but Zuko’s nostrils flare, his eyes narrowing on Jeong Jeong a moment before pointedly cutting away. Oh, Zuko did *not* like that. And Piandao’s expression is flickering toward a scowl, and Spirits, Fire Nation honor is so confusing when you get down into the details. They’re both deserters on the same side, what issue could Jeong Jeong have to take with Zuko’s conduct?

“If you know of the Fire Lord’s plan,” Zuko finally says, voice more spiky than frosty but every inch the Prince again. “Then what are you doing about it?”

Bumi throws his hands up in enthusiasm. “Liberating Ba Sing Se from Fire Nation rule!”

“…And what about the rest of the Earth Kingdom,” Sokka asks into the silence. “Leave that to a bunch of kids?”

Iroh gives him a deceptively mild glance before addressing the rest of the table. “We can offer support, against the airships.” Yes, then. The answer is clearly yes. Sokka fucking *hates* adults, and right now he really hates Iroh in particular. Though he supposes it’s too much to ask a man who has spent his whole life doing nothing to suddenly act just because now they really need him to.

“Support against the airships,” Zuko repeats, everything about him carefully neutral except for the fists Sokka can see him making beneath the table. “Is that all?” Zuko is pissed too. Sokka doesn’t know whether to be relieved or even more upset about it.

“We cannot leave Ba Sing Se in Fire Nation hands and hope to have peace,” Iroh says.

“So instead we leave the Fire Lord unaccounted for, and expect peace to follow?” Zuko challenges, a hint of heat coming into the words.

“The Avatar will account for him,” Iroh replies, somehow both serene and implacable.

“So,” Sokka breaks in, giving Zuko a moment to gather his thoughts and find his calm if he wants it, “We just…hope that Aang is going to come back before the Comet comes?”

“Patience is never a waste of time, and hope is a flame that shines its light on the path forward.” He glances toward Zuko, his countenance softening. “And Nephew—I do not know that I could, at this point in my life.”

Zuko grunts, scowling. “You’re a better bender than he is.”

Iroh looks briefly rueful. “Raw power does, at times, trump skill. And I do not know if that is true, Zuko. Your father—”

Zuko’s glare is immediate.

“—The Fire Lord has spent years focused solely on combat bending.”

“And so you won’t face him in case you lose,” Zuko says, slowly flattening his fists out against his knees and sounding grim enough about it that Sokka is pretty sure it isn’t actually a question.

“It is the place of the Avatar to face that struggle,” Iroh confirms.

Sokka bites back all the protests that want to break three as Zuko takes one deep breath, then another, head briefly bowed before he straightens, eyes suddenly intent on Iroh. “And will you make a bid for the throne, then? Once the Avatar has fulfilled your hopes?”

Sokka jolts, staring at Zuko a moment before turning to look at Iroh. Not just the Grand Lotus and Dragon of the West, but former Crown Prince Iroh, who was Prince Iroh still until not too long ago. Who should have been the Fire Lord if his brother hadn’t stolen the throne. Sokka…hadn’t even considered the possibility. But Zuko clearly had.

“…What?” Katara asks, cutting through a silence so thick Sokka feels like he can barely breathe through it.

“Someone needs to sit on the Dragon Throne and lead the nation,” Zuko answers without looking away from Iroh, his face unreadable. “The war doesn’t just end because Ozai is dead. There will be another Fire Lord.”

Katara frowns, eyes flicking between Zuko and Iroh, and Toph shifts her, head tilting as she listens to whatever her feet are picking up, face speculative. “So we need someone on the throne who wants to end the war.”

Zuko doesn’t take his eyes off his uncle. “Ideally.”

“I have no desire to light the Eternal Flame,” Iroh finally says, words quiet, focused only on Zuko. “That is no longer my path.”

A long moment, then Zuko nods, a bare inclination of his head, almost like the confirmation isn’t worth acknowledging. But Sokka is close enough to see the minute ways Zuko relaxes at Iroh’s words, which…is interesting. Sokka can already tell this is going to be an especially long afternoon. They’ve barely even started and already his mind is bursting with questions he won’t ask in front of this crowd.

&#45;-

All of them disperse for some much-needed space when the first break comes, Sokka silently praising whoever decided to pre-schedule them at regular intervals. Sokka hesitates for a moment over where, exactly, to set himself in public. Zuko is being all Prince-y and prickly, and he’s not exactly signaling a need for distance, but Sokka has a feeling that there’s as much going on with perceptions at the Grand Lotus’ table as there are with words. But they aren't so much in public right now, not really. And it’s not like Iroh and Piandao and everyone else doesn’t already know…

He catches Zuko’s eye and Zuko raises his brow in return, questioning, and Sokka mutters a sharp, “Fuck it,” under his breath and throws himself down where he wants to be—leaning against a crate of supplies next to Zuko, pressed together shoulder to thigh, one hand holding a mug of tea and the other resting on Zuko’s leg. It’s maybe more than a little possessive, but after who even knows how long sitting at the table and wearing his Battle Planning face and forcing himself to be as wholly objective as he can be, Sokka wants the tangible reminder that cool and objectie isn't all there is, that they’re fighting for more than just fate or destiny or whatever it is the White Lotus seem so concerned about. And fuck what anyone else might think about it.

Even though Sokka knows even saying that to himself shows that he does, in fact, care what other people think. Dammit.

“You okay?” Zuko murmurs, a low question just for his ears.

“I can’t believe we’re actually making a plan around the assumption that Aang’s going to come back and take out the Fire Lord,” Sokka mutters, dropping his head back with a sigh.

“It’s not *entirely* unlikely,” Zuko says after a moment.

Sokka cracks open an eye. “You suddenly sharing Iroh’s thoughts about destiny?”

Zuko snorts. “No. Definitely no.”

“He’s just so…adamant,” Sokka grumbles. Sokka’s all for having convictions, but Iroh’s had really shut down any conversation around the kind of contingency planning Sokka would really like to engage in, just to be thorough.

“Yeah,” Zuko sighs, “It’s…”

“Inconvenient?”

“I was going to say really fucking annoying.”

Sokka lets out a surprised bark of laughter, leaning a bit more into Zuko’s shoulder as he tries to let the bright flash of levity settle in his chest. “So are we just going to go with it anyway?”

Zuko hums, thinking. “…We can work with it.”

Sokka isn’t so sure. “How?” How could anything possibly end with Ozai still around?

“…If the airships are downed, he would be separated from most of his resources. He would go ahead on his own,” Zuko says with total certainty. “So at most he’d just have the one ship left. And if they’re supplied for a quick battle, and if Ba Sing Se and Omashu are freed…”

Zuko glances over and Sokka shrugs after a moment, trying to line all the pieces up in his mind. If they can lean on the White Lotus like Iroh seems to have suggested they can… “That seems doable enough. The supply situation is a bit out of our hands at this point, though.”

“We’d have to take down his ship too,” Zuko decides after a moment. “But then he’d be effectively stranded in the Earth Kingdom, at least for however long it takes him to get to a port in the Colonies. So if we can take the Fire Nation…”

“Take the *Fire Nation*?”

“The throne,” Zuko corrects himself.

“…You want to take his throne out from under him?” Sokka asks, not entirely sure if shock or awe is the appropriate response to the places Zuko’s mind is going, to his ability to see his goal so clearly still in between everything else.

“The systems are set up to work regardless of who’s at the top,” Zuko says, frowning as he starts tracing the edge of Sokka’s hand on his thigh. “If we go in fast enough, and if it takes him long enough to get back…”

“We can consolidate power?”

“Something like that,” Zuko sighs. “Its…perception stuff again. A Fire Lord returning at the back of a fallen army, on the heels of a failed invasion…There’s an opportunity.”

“But—” Sokka cuts himself off, searching for more delicate words.

“How?”

“Yeah, I mean…You’re…” Sokka still doesn’t have the delicate words.

“An exile and accused traitor to the throne?”

Zuko apparently doesn’t have time for delicacy, today. “…Yeah.”

“I’m not the only heir,” Zuko points out quietly. “Azula’s always wanted a throne.”

Well…shit.

Sokka picks his words with care. “And we…trust that she would agree with that particular plan?”

Zuko eyes him for a moment. “It aligns with *her* plan rather well.”

“And she.. wouldn’t pursue the war?” Because that’s what they need, right? Someone on top who would be willing to consider peace, which is…not generally how Sokka pictures Azula, even with all Zuko's been sharing about her. Moreinclined to drive her enemies into the ground so that they can never get back up again.

Zuko’s hesitation is long enough for worry to start to burrow in Sokka’s gut. “She’d do the thing that put the Fire Nation in the best position,” Zuko finally says, watching his own finger follow the veins along the back of Sokka’s hand. “And…it might take convincing. But maybe not as much as you’d think.”

“Ah.” Sokka clears his throat. “Well then. If you’re sure?”

Zuko shrugs. “As much as you ever can be, with her.”

Right. “We…can make that work, I guess.” Contingency upon contingency is already spinning loose in his brain, shifting and realigning around how to make this work because *maybe not as much as you’d think* feels like a pretty fucking large margin of error. But Spirits, is Sokka hoping that they won’t need any of them. Zuko might have faith in his sister, might clearly think it makes far more political sense for Azula to take the throne of the two of them. But Sokka didn’t miss that Zuko wasn’t able to speak with anything like certainty about what she might do once she has it.

&#45;-

Sokka’s head is full of plans and counterplans and backups to his backup plans by the time the break ends, which is maybe why he fails to entirely anticipate that just because he and Zuko can work with the idea of Azula on the throne, other people might have issues with the concept. And Zuko might be able to be the cool, controlled Prince about some topics, but it’s clear that his little sister is *not* one of them. He’s getting more and more prickly, his comments dripping with more and more acid, his flares of hot anger lasting longer and longer the more the argument drags on.

“I don’t really know if I can trust that Crazy Blue is going to end the war,” Toph is saying. “It doesn’t seem her style.”

“She would,” Zuko grinds out between his teeth. “If it’s what is best for the Nation, she would.”

“Would she do it in time, though?” Jeong Jeong wonders. “I have heard of the Lightning Princess. For one so young to have cold fire…” He trails off, looking disturbed, and Zuko bridles at whatever implication is in those words. Sokka eyes his tight outrage, once again dying to understand what’s going on beneath the surface of all this Fire Nation inference and suggestion, feeling like a whole second conversation is happening right in front of him that he can't understand.

“Extending the war could be in her favor,” Suki points out reluctantly. “In a time of instability, a new leader coming to power, rallying a nation around an external enemy…”

“She can be brought around,” Zuko insists.

“Princess Azula is not known for her…openness to counsel,” Iroh says delicately.

“It makes sense for it to be her,” Zuko says doggedly. “The people love her. She’s the best firebender of her generation. She’s already consolidated power among a significant portion of the Council and she knows how to bribe or blackmail enough of the rest to get a majority.” Wait, what? “She’s *there—*”

“But does she have the temperament?” Iroh breaks in, giving Sokka a moment to process the fact that Zuko’s fourteen-year-old sister already has what sounds like over half the Council behind her bid for power.

…Sokka can see why the Fire Lord might want to eliminate an heir like that.

Zuko frowns, the scowl on his face going from frustrated to confused. “When has temperament ever mattered for being Fire Lord?”

Piandao shifts, drawing Zuko’s attention. “Is that the kind of question that got us here in the first place?”

Sokka…can agree with that sentiment.

“Well, if it’s not going to be Azula, and it’s not going to be Uncle, then…” Zuko runs a hand through his hair, looking like he’s doing some kind of quick math. “You’d have to go all the way to the *fourth* cousins to find a bender of Agni’s blood who could do more than light a candle.”

Sokka is familiar enough with Zuko’s opinions on other people’s firebending to think that that’s probably a slightly uncharitable assessment, but Jeong Jeong’s face is sour like it isn’t wholly wrong. “Agni’s line ran weak.”

“Agni’s line got *pruned*,” Zuko bites back, harsh enough to make the man clamp his mouth shut.

Katara glances around the table. “…Am I missing something?”

“Oh, I think we all are,” Bumi says cheerfully.

“Master Katara raises a good point,” Iroh says evenly, ignoring Bumi with an ease that says long practice, which…Spirits, when would Iroh and Bumi even have had the *time?*

“And what’s that,” Sokka asks when Iroh doesn’t elaborate, not bothering to hide his eye roll that Iroh is forcing someone to ask. Zuko's hand is already twitching beneath the table from refusing to be the one to break the silence, and Sokka doesn’t see why anyone would want to rile him *more.* Sokka can’t help but wonder if Iroh even realizes when he does these little power games, or if they’re just so ingrained that they’re pure instinct.

“Princess Azula and I are not the only other Children of Agni.”

Zuko stares a moment before his eyes widen a fraction with realization, barely visible but enough that Sokka can see. “No.”

Iroh continues like Zuko hasn’t even spoken. “No one has ever denied that you have the blood.”

“Yeah, because Father made the Sages *prove* it,” Zuko snaps, the words full of fury and something Sokka hopes only he’s hearing as pain. “Which should be all you need to know about why it can’t be me!”

Sokka hazards a question. “And, ah—why is that, again?” He throws up his hands when Zuko’s glare snaps around to him. “Just asking. Just…trying to figure out what’s going on.”

Piandao is the one to answer. “To ask the Sages to prove that Crown Prince Zuko was of the Blood implies that there were doubts.”

“Okay…” Sokka kind of got the sense of that, but he feels like he’s missing why questions within a family would—

“The ceremony to resolve such doubts is traditionally quite public.”

“…Oh.”

Piandao transfers his stare to Zuko. “But those doubts were thoroughly laid to rest, as your uncle has pointed out.”

“But people don’t forget! And, besides, I’m in *exile*. Like I have been for the past four years! Legally I can’t step into Fire Nation territory, which is where the throne is!”

Suki clears her throat. “Can the Fire Lord *be* exiled? I feel like you could overturn that for yourself.”

“And it’s worth pointing out,” Iroh puts in, “That my brother did not, necessarily, reinstate your order of exile after he lifted it this winter.”

“Just the price on my head!”

Pakku waves a dismissive hand. “No one will pursue a bounty they won’t get paid for. And if you are Fire Lord, you certainly won’t pay it.”

Zuko gapes, mouth silently working, and Sokka isn’t sure if Zuko’s choked by disbelief or anger but either way his firebender needs a moment to find his voice. “I think Zuko still has a valid point, though,” Sokka says, stepping tentatively, aware that he doesn’t fully understand the lay of this land. “I get that it’s a hereditary monarchy with limited options to take the throne, but public sentiment has to matter at least a bit, right? And Azula *is* there.”

“Zuko is the firstborn,” Iroh says, shaking his head. “It is his rightful place, to take the throne.”

“Like *that’s* ever mattered,” Zuko spits.

“Traditions matter,” Iroh replies, mild despite what Sokka knows was a potshot against him.

Zuko’s shoulders are stiff. “What’s the saying again—the strong and mighty have little need to pay attention to those who lack both?”

“Might makes right,” Suki murmurs, face pinched, and Zuko nods.

“I’d say that’s mattered a bit more than *tradition* when it comes to the throne,” Zuko says, words hard.

Iroh raises his eyebrows. “And possession is nine-tenths of the law, as they also say.”

Zuko clamps his mouth shut, sucking in a slow breath between his teeth and Sokka sits up a little straighter, glancing around because whatever Iroh said well and truly landed to hit like that, but the other Fire Nation citizens don’t seem any more enlightened.

“Unless you got up to some very interesting things during the Day of the Black Sun—” Iroh pauses delicately and Zuko flushes and looks away. “—I believe the heir’s crown is still yours.”

“The one that has been missing for years?” Jeong Jeong asks, jerking upright.

“For four years,” Iroh confirms, looking serene except for the slight narrowing of his eyes on Zuko. “Give or take.”

Jeong Jeong turns an incredulous look on Zuko. “The *kid’s* had it?”

“Well it’s *mine*, as you all keep insisting,” Zuko snaps, glaring at the former General before scowling back at Iroh. “Not that it matters. The Fire Lord’s crown is sitting on the Fire Lord’s head right now. We aren’t fighting to be *heir*.”

Sokka doesn’t know whether to be proud on Zuko’s behalf or sad for him at the silence that stretches out after that, until finally Katara shifts, leaning forward to grab Zuko’s attention from where he’s glaring at the untouched cup of tea in front of him. “Zuko. How would you describe Azula?”

He frowns at her. “What?”

“When you think of her as a person,” Katara says. “And as a leader. How would you describe her?”

Zuko is silent, maybe looking for the trap—Sokka thinks he can see it—but Katara’s face is earnest, and when Iroh goes, “I can offer my thoughts,” Zuko is quick enough to jump in that Sokka’s pretty sure Iroh knew exactly what would prompt Zuko to speak.

“She’s a prodigy,” Zuko says, not seeming to know where to go next and looking uncertain when Toph makes an encouraging noise. “She’s…brilliant. Powerful.”

The look Katara is giving Zuko is very gentle, and Sokka can feel the way Zuko braces himself against it. “What does she care about?”

Zuko goes motionless, maybe seeing the trap too, and Sokka for a moment can’t help but feel anything but sad for whatever it is that’s between the royal siblings, whether it’s what Zuko thinks it is or what Sokka fears or something in between.

“Does she care about the Fire Nation?” Katara presses, keeping her voice even, withholding judgment except for the question itself.

“The Fire Nation isn’t hers to care about yet,” Zuko protests immediately, and Sokka can’t help tripping a little bit over how smoothly that ‘yet’ came out.

Toph taps her fingers on the table to get Zuko’s attention. “What about the people in it? Not as subjects or vassals or whatever, but as people.”

Zuko’s silence is telling even if Sokka wasn’t already fairly sure the number of people Azula personally cares about these days from the Fire Nation can be counted on one hand with four fingers left over.

Katara stretches her hand forward, almost like she wants to reach for Zuko, to clasp his hand, her face earnest. “When we think about what comes next, after the Comet and the war. Do we want a Fire Lord who can just be talked into calling a truce? Do we want someone who needs to win in order to stop fighting? Or do we want a Fire Lord who genuinely wants peace?” She searches his face, expression heavy, and Sokka aches to be having this conversation anywhere else, any place where he could pull Zuko into his arms so Zuko didn’t have to bear himself up alone to hear this. “Zuko, you—you’d end the war because it’s the right thing to do. Because you *care*. Not just about the world or the Fire Nation or the big stuff, but because you care about your people, too.”

“I can’t—I’m not—”

“You would make a good Fire Lord, Nephew,” Iroh observes, the Grand Lotus falling away for a moment.

“*No,”* Zuko snarls, and Sokka startles to hear a note of genuine revulsion in his voice, to see wisps of smoke curling from his fists beneath the table before he forces them open.

“You *are* the Crown Prince, Sparrowkeet,” Toph points out after a beat.

“No, it’s—it’s not supposed to be me,” Zuko says, voice verging toward something desperate. “It was never supposed to be me.”

Piandao raises an eyebrow. “’Supposed to be’?”

Zuko swings a glare onto him, all spiky-edged hostility that Sokka can tell is covering something dangerously close to panic.

Pakku leans forward, face twisted in annoyance. “Whatever scheme you might have cooked up in Caldera, boy, circumstances have changed. Inflexibility suits no one.”

Sokka nearly chokes on his own air, at *Pakku* saying that, but before he can find words for his outrage, or at hearing Pakku call Zuko *boy,* Zuko stills, his face going cold in a way that has Sokka’s skin prickling with wariness, in a way that's all Azula.

“Who are you,” Zuko says with a biting kind of softness, “To tell the Fire Nation who to put on the throne?” Pakku freezes, expression pinched, slowly sitting back at whatever he sees on Zuko’s face. “Does the Order of the White Lotus seek to control the Fire Nation from behind the throne?” Zuko asks, not looking at Iroh in a very pointed way as his voice goes hard, harder than Sokka’s ever heard it. “Because the Fire Nation does not consent to relinquish its sovereignty to another.”

“The White Lotus seeks balance in the world,” Pakku finally says, a tinge of wariness on his face as he looks a Zuko. Like he’s maybe seeing exactly the kind of Fire Lord he would get that he’s been pushing for.

“Of course,” Zuko says, sharp-edged. “The balance of hiding behind walls until it’s too late to act and your hand is forced by another.” Katara sucks in a breath across the table, eyes going wide, and it takes everything in his power for Sokka to keep his face still. Pakku might not have had Zuko’s measure, but Zuko has apparently known exactly who Pakku is and exactly what he did and did not do.

“The White Lotus is not in the business of empire-building and politics,” Iroh cuts in before Pakku can master his outrage enough to reply, voice firm and without even a hint of irony to be the one saying it. “The choice will be yours, Nephew,” Iroh says, eyeing his fellow Lotus members in a way that clearly signals them to drop the matter before he brings his gaze back to Zuko, as unreadable as Sokka’s ever seen it. “I trust you to choose wisely.”

&#45;-

Sokka lets out the quiet groan he’s been holding back when they break for the end of the day, closing his eyes and finally giving in to the urge to thunk his head, once, solidly onto the table.

“Come on, Snoozles.” Toph gives the back of his head a solid and surprisingly accurate poke, then a gentle pat. “Is it really as bad as that?”

“I can *feel* Zuko glaring at everything,” Sokka mutters into the table.

“Turning yourself into an earthbender?”

“Into a jerkbender, maybe,” Sokka mumbles, then, “Wait, no, I didn’t—”

“Too late,” Toph says, absolutely delighted. “*Way* too late.”

Sokka groans and gives his head another solid thunk as she makes her way out of the tent, calling Suki’s name. Spirits, how Toph still has the energy after an entire afternoon of arguing is scary impressive. But then, Toph wasn’t trying to walk the fine line of planning what amounts to a coup which happened to simultaneously involve trying to support your boyfriend as he very publicly worked through some shit about his father.

Sokka flails in surprise when his not-thinking is suddenly interrupted: “Master Sokka. Perhaps you would care for some tea?”

Sokka startles upright, eyes darting around and going tellingly wide as he realizes that everyone else has already left and somehow, he’s made the mistake of allowing himself to be alone in the tent with Iroh. Then he catches the glint in Iroh’s eye and slowly settles back as he realizes that it maybe wasn’t a mistake at all.

“Tea?” Iroh repeats. It’s not actually a question.

“I should…”

“Dinner is being prepared by the White Lotus tonight,” Iroh says evenly, already setting out cups and saucers and all the little implements that accompany his ritual of teamaking. The movements are familiar, incongruous next to Sokka’s slowly gathering dread over the conversation he thinks they’re about to have.

“Tea, then,” Sokka agrees belatedly, trying to cling to the semblance that it’s his choice to stay. But fuck, given a real choice, Sokka would *not* do this in a tent with its more suggestion of privacy than any actual reality of it. He isn’t entirely sure what Iroh wants to say to him— he has plenty of guesses—but Sokka’s acutely aware that Zuko’s desire for a relationship with Iroh sometimes feels like a thin restraint on the things Sokka wants to say to the man. Sokka doesn’t want to fuck this up for Zuko anymore than it's already fucked, but Sokka also can’t just ignore the fact that the more Sokka learns about Zuko’s past the more he struggles with Iroh’s role in it.

Iroh has chosen the time and place and Sokka learned from the General during more pai sho games than he can count the importance of choosing the battleground, so as Sokka accepts his tea he makes the first move. “Are you going to ask me about my intentions again?”

Iroh pauses in the act of setting the teapot back on its stand. “I will admit that it did surprise me, somewhat, to see my nephew with the Avatar’s companions.”

“Why?” Sokka asks bluntly.

Iroh gives Sokka a level look “My nephew had not previously shown a significant interest in *joining* the Avatar.”

“Maybe he just didn’t think it was an option before,” Sokka says, aware of the multiple requests he himself made for Zuko to join them. Requests that he knows Zuko was never truly in a position to accept, that were more his own painful hopes than any real choice to extend to Zuko with all Zuko would have been walking away from and all that Sokka could offer in return. Requests that he’s fairly sure Iroh doesn’t even know about, anyway, or else the man might have signaled in some way to Zuko that it was okay for him to accept.

“And it is an option now?”

“He’s here, isn’t he?”

“With the Avatar?” Iroh delicately sets his teacup down. “Or with you?”

Sokka feels wariness prickle across his shoulders. “I’m with Aang, so.”

Iroh’s silence somehow manages to perfectly convey the fact that Sokka says he’s with Aang, but Aang isn’t currently here, which just—ugh. Aang *was* here, and so was Zuko, and Sokka feels the sharp bite of frustration that Iroh would think *Zuko* of all people would lose track of his mission when it mattered. And then another flare of annoyance as he considers that maybe implying it is the whole point, to see what Sokka does.

“Why does it matter?” Sokka asks, trying not to let his irritation show, knowing he’s being baited into it and doing it anyway.

“My nephew holds you in high regard.”

Like they’re fucking work colleagues. Sokka holds back an eyeroll. “I think he’s pretty great, too.”

“That is good,” Iroh says, and his careful composure breaks for a moment enough for Sokka to see he actually means it. “I think my nephew would do many things, because you ask him to. Because of that regard.”

Sokka suppresses the urge to tap a restless finger against the edge of his cup. “We covered this in Ba Sing Se,” he points out. “He would do the same for you.”

“Indeed,” Iroh agrees. “And just as I imagine you have an interest, as a result, in what I would ask of my nephew, I find that I feel the need, as well, to ask what it is, exactly, that you would have him do on your behalf, or at your request.”

Sokka frowns as he sorts through the convoluted phrasing, uncomfortably aware that Iroh knows far more about his and Zuko’s sex life than Sokka will ever be comfortable with. Please, don’t let this be what the General is probing at, because no part of Sokka is interested in breaking down the types of things he can and cannot ask of Zuko. “I don’t see how it’s any of your business.”

“I care for him,” Iroh says simply. “I want what is best for him. I do not want to see him held back.”

Sokka is aware of his hands whitening tellingly around his teacup. “You think I’m holding Zuko back?” *Iroh*, who wanted Zuko to leave behind his bending and his swords and all his overwhelming caring for his nation to be a *teashop server?*

Iroh’s face is neutral-but-watchful, noting Sokka’s every reaction. “You do not think my nephew should be Fire Lord.”

“I didn’t say that,” Sokka immediately pushes back, scowling. “I didn’t say anything.”

“Yes. I noticed.”

Sokka snaps his mouth shut on a reply.

“Zuko thinks highly of your opinions,” Iroh continues. “He listens to your words. And to your silences. I am aware that it can be hard to be…objective, when one is young, and feels themselves to be in love.” Sokka fucking *feels himself* flush with a rush of mingled anger and embarrassment. “But these kinds of things are not just matters of the heart, they—”

“What is it, exactly, that you’re trying to say,” Sokka cuts in, deliberately setting his teacup down because he’s worried the thin porcelain is going to snap under his grip. “Just spit it out, Iroh.”

The General considers him a moment, calculating, assessing. “I cannot help but notice that it would be harder for someone like you to be with the Fire Lord than with a Prince in exile.”

Sokka takes a deep, careful breath. “Someone like me?”

“Not of the Fire Nation. Not willing to put the good of the Nation above all else. Not wanting to be of the aristocracy, yet too politically powerful among the nations to be a common citizen. All fine things.” Iroh takes a sip of his own tea, eyes never leaving Sokka. “But difficult for a consort to the throne.”

Sokka is glad he already set his teacup down as he fumbles for a response, feeling more than a little off-balance to hear himself described as some kind of international political power and absolutely sure that the General did it on purpose. Fuck, feeling off-balance to hear himself attached to the word *consort*, when Sokka only newly has words for Zuko other than ‘mine.’

“And then suddenly there is this talk of Zuko not becoming Fire Lord, or being unfit for it—”

“That’s all Zuko,” Sokka interrupts, finding his footing again. “That is all him.”

“Forgive me if I find that hard to believe,” Iroh says quietly, “Given that Zuko is the Crown Prince. This is not a new thought. Fire Lord is what comes next.”

Sokka gives the former Crown Prince of the Fire Nation a pointed look. “Not always.” From what Sokka can tell Fire Lord often *isn’t* the next step, considering the fates of their last few Crown Princes. And besides, Zuko spent far more of his life *not* being next in line for the throne.

Iroh tilts his head in something that could be acknowledgment. “The path of destiny is rarely a straight line, yet we must set our steps upon it nonetheless.”

Sokka…has no idea if that’s agreement or not, but he knows exactly what Zuko would think of Iroh talking about his destiny. “Why’s it so hard for you to believe that Zuko makes his own choices here? I just want Zuko to be happy. If he wants to go off and become an actor, I’ll support him. If he wants to rule a country, I’ll support him. If he wants to *not* rule one, I’m not going to be the one who tells him he has to. And if you don’t like Zuko’s choices, that’s your problem, not mine. And not his.”

Iroh’s eyes are slightly narrowed, assessing. “You act as if you are some objective, neutral arbiter, Master Sokka. Is that a place you can truly claim for yourself?”

“I could just as easily say the same of you,” Sokka snaps, giving up on the job of hiding his annoyance. He hasn’t exactly been succeeding at the effort so far. “I’m sure the White Lotus would find it pretty useful to have a Fire Lord on the throne who’s amenable to their ends.”

Iroh is already shaking his head. “The White Lotus has no interest in ruling nations.”

“What about the Dragon of the West,” Sokka challenges. “Because you seem interested in this one.”

“As a member of the royal family,” Iroh insists, a slight furrow cracking his neutral mask. “As an uncle.”

“And you can just separate out being an uncle from being Grand Lotus?” Sokka lets his disbelief color his words. “Because it would have been mighty convenient for Grand Lotus Iroh when Zuko got exiled and had to travel around the world.”

Iroh’s face goes cold, someplace between neutral and angry. “Nothing about that was convenient.”

“No, it wasn’t,” Sokka bites out, aware that his restraint is wearing thin, that the kinds of things he knows better than to bring up to Zuko without Zuko raising it first are pressing against his lips. “Not for him when he was hurt and scared and alone, and you were the only one he had, and he fucking knew it. And from what he’s said it sure as shit seems like you knew it, too.”

Iroh slowly, deliberately sets down his tea. “Are you accusing me of something, Master Sokka?” Cold, cold, cold fire in his voice, but Sokka’s pent-up frustration and swirling anger on Zuko’s behalf has finally found itself a target.

“You sit there and you say you care about him, but where was your care before he was useful to your secret little society? Where was your care when he was just a kid?” Sokka shoves his hands through his hair, unable to keep still with all this bursting out of him. “Do you even know how many scars he has? How many of them are from his *family*?” It makes Sokka’s chest feel hot and tight sometimes, just thinking about it. “Where was your care during his Agni Kai? Someone who cared would have *protected him*. But the way I see it? You left him to the viper wolves until he was useful to you.”

Sokka should maybe take the visible tightening of Iroh’s fists as a warning sign, but he can’t seem to stop now.

“You didn’t do *shit* when it mattered. You didn’t even *try* until it was already too late,” Sokka spits. “And now you act like you have the right to sit there and tell me to back off? When I’m here where you didn’t want to be, trying to step up and help and be on his side? You already had your chance,” Sokka says, feeling his chest heaving, his fists pressed against the table. “I think he’s had enough of your *caring*.”

Sokka’s words hang loud in the silence between them, Iroh deliberately uncurling his fists in a gesture shockingly reminiscent of Zuko. Sokka nearly trembles thinking of Zuko being left all on his own and scrambling like the bare crumbs of concern Iroh tossed his way were worth his devotion, feeling a sharp stab of something that might be guilt in his chest. Sokka hasn’t always gotten it right, not even close, and Spirits, that some of his misses have been truly spectacular. But at least he can fucking *admit* it, can fucking listen to Zuko and ask and pay attention and try to do *better*, try to give Zuko everything his firebender deserves and wants and needs and more and—

“I have not always been able to act as I would have wanted,” Iroh finally says, voice soft and tightly controlled. “I will confess to having been blinded by my grief, and by my duties to the crown that did not always allow me to be present in Zuko’s life. But do not *dare* to suggest that I do not love my nephew. Do not *dare* to imply that I would voluntarily see him hurt. He is like a son to me.”

Sokka hasn’t heeded Iroh’s warning signs yet and he can’t seem to start now, not over this. “Is he? You have a funny way of showing it. It’s great that you didn’t *mean* to neglect him. I’m sure that makes it so much better that it was just *accidental* neglect.”

Iroh’s nostrils flare. “I have cared for Zuko through more than you know—”

“I know *plenty*,” Sokka hisses. “I know the fact that you were with him for four *years* and he still feels like he needs to earn your love. That he feels like he can’t have it unless you think he’s worthy. That’s on *you*. That’s *all* on you.”

“Zuko has always sought to please others before himself,” Iroh snaps back. “If you haven’t learned that by now—”

“Did you ever take even one fucking second to look at how he grew up and ask yourself if pleasing others wasn’t the only fucking way he had to survive?” Sokka grips the edge of the table, trying to pull his volume back below a shout. “Did you ever even *try* offering him anything unconditionally? Or are you so deep in it yourself that you can’t even comprehend just *giving* your approval away.”

Iroh pauses, hesitating on a reply like he isn’t entirely sure what Sokka means, and Sokka can’t help the way that makes him just want to sag. Spirits, Sokka just…feels exhausted, needing to explain things that he never thought someone could not understand. Feels exhausted, wondering how much of a leg he has to stand on. to be the one explaining it when it comes to Zuko.

“If the only way Zuko could feel safe and loved with you was to show that he was worthy of it first, then I don’t see how he ever had either,” Sokka says, words quieter but still rough in his throat. “Not when he had to be a good enough bender, or join in music night, or adopt your worldview, or whatever you wanted in order to feel like he could breathe. He was tying himself into fucking knots trying to be good enough for you, and the whole time you were just there sending letters to your secret friends and—”

“You were not there, Master Sokka,” Iroh cuts in, voice suddenly hard and eyes flashing hot with anger. “You have much to say, but at the end of the day you do not know what it was like.”

“Zuko told me—”

“Zuko knows what it was like for *himself*,” the Dragon of the West says, voice terribly cold. “He does not know what it was like for the rest of us. And I pray that he never knows. To sit and watch one you love be burned, because if you try to interfere then his father might have grounds to kill him and call it an accident? To try to nurse him back to health and see him get worse and worse every day because he can’t bring himself to be still, he can’t allow himself to *rest* because he feels so driven to prove himself even on his sickbed? To still be able to hear on quiet nights the sound a person makes when they have a burn that bad and they fall and they are still too weak to—”

Iroh cuts himself off, closing his eyes. “Zuko was on the edge of death for—” A deep breath like he can’t even bring himself to say it, his hands going tight. “—And every day he slipped further and further away. And the harder we tried to hold him the faster he went, because the more he felt he had to prove he was fine.” His eyes snap back open, yellow and boiling and pinning Sokka in place. “It is a *miracle* that he found his way back to Agni’s light. A blessing from the Spirits, one that I give thanks every day for, with all my heart.

“And that was just the start,” Iroh continues before Sokka can even think about formulating anything approaching a response. “To try to guide him after? To be a safe place for him when he was on the verge of doing something terrible because he didn’t have eyes for anything else? To try to help him recreate his world when everything he knew was upended? Do you even know what it means, for a firebender of Agni’s line to be branded like that?” Sokka’s stomach lurches at the word, the one Zuko never uses. “What that tells people who see him? Zuko knows, and still I couldn’t keep him out of ports. He was on the edge of bolting *even* *when we were at sea*. For *years* the only reason we posted a night watch was because we didn’t know that he wasn’t going to try to go over the edge in armor.”

Sokka bites back a small noise at the thought, feeling almost numb under the force of Iroh’s anger and grief, the flow of words more honest and raw than anything Sokka’s ever come close to hearing from the man.

“So do not—” Iroh takes a deep breath, composure falling back over his face like a mask. “— try to tell me how it should have been, when you were not *there.”* He gives Sokka a warning look, but Sokka for once manages to hold his tongue. “You might disagree with how I went about it, Master Sokka. But I will never regret anything that allowed my nephew to be here, now, alive.”

Sokka licks his lips, hands clumsy as he takes a sip of lukewarm tea to relieve his suddenly dry throat, to give them both a moment to breathe. Spirits, Sokka feels like he is going to need an entire week just to start fully comprehending everything Iroh just said. But he still can’t bring himself to stop pushing now. “Just because he made it here doesn’t mean what happened to him was right,” Sokka finally says quietly, not quite sure where to put his eyes. “It’s good, it really is, that you gave him all those things. I’m not saying it’s not. But Spirits, what would it have taken to give him a hug? Some support? Maybe he wouldn’t have been on the edge of bolting if he felt like he had a place where he was wanted.”

Iroh sighs, sadness settling around the curve of his mouth. “You say you know my nephew? Then you know how he is when he is feeling cornered. You do not keep a feral spider cat by chasing it. You let it come to you.”

Sokka shakes his head, protest rising hard and fast in his throat. “Zuko isn’t some animal. He’s a person, with feelings. He didn’t need to be tamed or brought to heel or whatever. And if he really felt that cornered for that long, maybe you need to ask yourself if you were part of the reason. Because you’re supposed to know Zuko better than anyone, and it’s like you don’t even *see* him most of the time.”

Iroh is looking at him with something like…pity? “Who my nephew is now is not who he was back then.”

Sokka eyes him, wondering if they’re talking about the same nephew. “Always willing to fight because he’s always a little bit scared, no tolerance for feeling coddled, trying to do the best he can with what he has regardless of what he has to sacrifice of himself in the process?”

Iroh looks patient now, and Sokka abruptly feels like he doesn’t quite have his footing anymore the way he thought he did in the face of that look. “And what did my nephew have, back then?”

Sokka doesn’t understand. “…What?”

“He had a mission to capture the Avatar and return him in chains to the Fire Lord, to be forever imprisoned, putting the balance of the world out of each for decades more, potentially. That was not something I could support, even to help my nephew.” Iroh glances down at his teacup, face shadowed with regret. “I tried to help him see that there were other paths, but…”

But Sokka knows exactly how Zuko would have taken that—as doubt, as judgment on his competency, as commentary on his abilities. Spirits, Iroh just…makes it so hard to hate him, but so hard to like him at the same time. “Then you should have supported him in some other way,” Sokka says, shoving a hand through his hair. “Did you ever ask what he wanted and then actually try to help him with it? Like fuck, helping him with his bending? You do know he thinks he’s a terrible firebender, right?”

Iroh’s face briefly flickers with surprise, and Sokka doesn’t know if that’s good or bad, that Iroh apparently didn’t.

“Or if you didn’t want to do that, you could have helped him get some sword training. Or helped him actually find old scrolls so he didn’t have to steal them.” Iroh looks openly startled at that, and Sokka snaps his mouth shut and bites his tongue before he gives away any more of Zuko’s secrets. Hopefully that was a little one.

“It is easy to say all those things with distance,” Iroh finally says. “Hindsight is always the clearest of vision.”

“Except you’re still doing it,” Sokka says quietly, watching as Iroh pauses. “You have this— *idea* of Zuko,” he tries to explain, already knowing that the words are going to fall short. “Zuko the teashop server or Zuko the Prince or Zuko the potential Fire Lord you definitely won’t be trying to influence for your secret society from behind the throne.” Iroh frowns, and Sokka hurries on. “It’s like you interact with the idea of him, not the person actually in front of you. Zuko *isn’t* who he was back then, but you’re still treating him like a kid.”

“He is seventeen.”

Sokka wants to laugh, that Iroh says it like that matters. Aang is *twelve*. “He’s old enough to rule a country, according to you,” Sokka says instead, the words coming out tired instead of combative. “Just—try, for once, actually listening to him? Instead of projecting your assumptions onto him.” Sokka pauses, but Iroh doesn’t speak, so he keeps going. “He went back to Caldera for a reason, he joined the Avatar for the same reason, and the fact that you can’t see that *hurts* him.” Sokka thinks, belatedly, that this might be another of Zuko’s secrets. “You’re always talking about how pai sho is all about reading your opponent as much as the board—how do you think it makes him feel that you can’t read him?”

Iroh doesn’t reply, face still in a way Sokka doesn’t understand, and Sokka eventually closes his eyes, knuckling roughly at them and refusing to be the one to break the silence this time. Finally, Iroh stirs, and Sokka straightens back up when he realizes Iroh is studying him again. “You are very protective of my nephew.”

“Someone has to be,” Sokka says immediately.

“Indeed. I am as well. In a different way, maybe, than you would want me to be.” Iroh raises his eyebrows and Sokka doesn’t deny it. “But I want what is best for him too. Regardless of how much you believe that.” Regret shades the edges of his expression. “And I know from personal experience that what you might think is best for yourself is not always the case.”

Sokka sighs. “Zuko doesn’t need someone to tell him what to do, or how to think.” Zuko has enough people second-guessing him. He needs someone validating him, supporting him, someone he can trust to be a sounding board, someone who can help give him the confidence to stand behind his own choices.

“No,” Iroh agrees, thankfully. “But he needs to know that options are available, beyond just what he sees in front of him. That he does not have to limit himself in life to just what he is offered.” Sokka wonders if his tea had cactus juice in it, for Iroh to be the one saying this. “That he can do amazing things for this world, if he gives himself the chance.”

“Yeah,” Sokka finally says. “He does.” He wonders how he and Iroh can both share that belief while holding such wildly different understandings of what to do about it.

&#45;-

Zuko waits for Sokka, his inner flame flickering with as much quiet anxiety as he has the energy far. He’d slipped out of the tent without Sokka at Uncle’s quiet urging, but now he’s wondering…well, Zuko isn’t entirely unaware of the tension between Sokka and Uncle, even if he doesn’t wholly understand it. He trusts them both, but he also knows the day has been long for everyone.

Maybe he should have lingered, or pulled Sokka with him, or waited at their tent along with the others like Toph suggested instead of asking Katara to send Sokka after him. But Agni, Zuko had just needed space, and separation, and the knowledge that he was alone, even from the warm concern the rest of the crew is offering. He just…spent far too long today being watched and trying to pretend he didn’t see the judgment on so many of the faces around him. More concern isn’t what Zuko wants right now.

Besides, Zuko doesn’t know that he can really participate in any more conversation after the day. His throat feels hoarse from all the talking, and his mind still feels like it’s spinning in too many directions at once, plans trying to rearrange themselves in his head to the sound of Uncle’s quiet insistence and Katara’s careful questions, and Zuko is doing everything in his power to hold them firm. Things don’t *need* to be different, no matter what everyone else thinks. Sokka, Uncle’s happiness, the future of his nation—those things don’t have to be in conflict. Zuko can still see the path ahead, can still see between his ideas and Sokka’s where he needs it to go.

“Oh thank the Spirits, you have food.”

Zuko jerks his eyes open at the sound of Sokka’s voice, giving him a quick once over and letting his heat curl out in greeting as Sokka makes his way over to Zuko’s spot against the convenient little wall of supply boxes that rises high enough that he isn’t visible from inside the camp as long as he doesn’t stand. Zuko holds out the second bowl of noodles he’s been keeping more, his breath hitching a little when Sokka grabs it with a murmured thanks, throwing himself down onto the grass opposite Zuko like everything is normal even though he's looking wrung out around the edges, eyes on Zuko like he’s an oasis in the Si Wong Desert, which…Zuko supposes isn’t actually *not* normal, but, “How’d it go?”

Sokka huffs, giving him a sideways little look. “Oh, so you left me there on purpose?”

Zuko shrugs. Yes. “Uncle looked like he wanted to talk to you.”

Sokka snorts. “He sure did.”

“And,” Zuko prompts, wondering if he needs to gather the energy to go yell at Uncle. “How’d it go?”

“Fine,” Sokka mumbles around a mouthful.

Zuko eyes the lingering tension around Sokka’s mouth, the flyaway pieces of hair that have escaped their tie. “Hm.”

Sokka sighs, stretching out a foot to give Zuko’s knee a gentle, reassuring kind of nudge. “We just…might always have some different opinions on certain things.”

Zuko was already aware of that. “Am I a ‘thing’?”

Sokka freezes for a second, chopsticks halfway to his mouth, then pulls a little face like he knows he just gave the answer away. “We both gave each other some stuff to think about,” Sokka finally says, shoving his free hand through his hair and pulling more hair out of his wolf tail, face briefly shadowed. “Just…a lot of things.”

Zuko pokes carefully at his own bowl, turning that over, trying to think of all the things Sokka and Uncle might have to say to each other, and which ones might have Sokka looking so tight at the edges and so relieved to have found Zuko.

Though that’s how Zuko’s been generally feeling about the past few days, and he doesn’t think Sokka’s been feeling all that different.

“Zuko,” Sokka says, slurping up a noodle and giving his knee another nudge. “You look like you want to ask something.”

“…Did Uncle say anything more about the Fire Lord?”

Sokka sighs. “Just about you doing it.”

Zuko grunts again, stabbing his chopsticks into his bowl. Fuck. That’s…campaigning. Trying to gather support, on Zuko’s behalf. Dammit.

Sokka hesitates, leaning a bit to catch Zuko’s eyes. “You want me to tell him to shut his face about it?”

Zuko snorts out a surprised laugh. “No, it’s fine.” Sokka would probably end up drinking an entire pot of tea listening to Spirit tales in response. “He probably couldn’t stop even if he wanted to, once he gets going. Not if he thinks it's destiny or whatever.”

Zuko sighs, that brief flash of levity already leaving him. Agni’s balls, he wishes Uncle didn’t have the excuse of destiny to hide behind, to shield his ideas from needing to be defended. Uncle’s confidence and surety are nice, but…not when you don’t agree with them.

“I’m sure we could come up with a way,” Sokka says, rather darkly, and Zuko eyes him again. Maybe those different opinions on certain things between Sokka and Uncle are deeper than Zuko realized.

“It’s fine,” Zuko repeats.

“It’s making you all twitchy.”

Zuko is immediately conscious of the way he’s fiddling with his chopsticks. “It’s nice that he believes I could do it,” Zuko offers.

Sokka raises his eyebrows. “But?”

Zuko sighs. “It’s just…different.” He glances up to see the question on Sokka’s face and tries to find the words. “Before, Uncle wanted me to learn well and be ready for my duty to the Fire Nation. And then I was Crown Prince, and—well, Lu Ten was dead, and it took Uncle… a while.” Sokka shifts, but thankfully stays silent. Zuko’s aware that Sokka has thoughts on that, and doesn’t particularly want to touch them right now. “And then after the Agni Kai, he wanted me to move beyond the Fire Nation, I guess. And then he wanted me to be a tea server. And now he wants me to be Fire Lord. I just…don’t know who he wants me to be.”

“Maybe just yourself?”

Zuko thinks that’s a ludicrous idea. “I think there’s always been too many parts of me, for him.”

Sokka frowns, setting aside his empty bowl and shifting closer. “How so?”

Zuko mimics Sokka’s cross-legged position so they can sit knee-to-knee, looking at those points of contact instead of Sokka’s face, needing the delicate balance of distance and support. “Like…he says I get tunnel vision. But *he* gets so fixated sometimes, and…I can’t strip parts of myself away and add them back on again. Be the good Prince and set aside all the things I’m not supposed to care about, and then just overnight, care about all that other stuff instead and leave the Prince behind. And then flip it again. I don’t…work like that.”

Sokka is quiet, tracing a slow finger over Zuko’s knee, which is nice and relaxing and a good thing to focus on instead of waiting for a reply. Finally, Sokka taps his leg, capturing his attention. “Did I ever tell you about the time I got abducted into the Spirit world? Actually tell you about it?”

Zuko blinks, trying to follow the connective thread. It feels like a tangent, but Sokka is looking serious, and hates talking about Spirit stuff and is bringing it up anyway, so Zuko goes with it. “You wrote to me about it.” It had been a terrifying letter to receive, enough to drive him to Uncle for answers and reassurance. Agni’s tits, Zuko had been…so fucking happy to get a reply back. Fuck, they must have been so obvious, even back then.

“When I was there, there was this…thing. This Spirit, I guess. That acted like it was trying to help me. It wanted me to see all the ways I was in disharmony, it said. To look at all the distance between what I told the world I was, and what I actually was.”

Zuko…already thinks he hates everything about this.

“The thing took all these…really difficult memories, and it made them different. Worse. It was trying to make me doubt myself, I guess. Like, found every little thing that voice in the back of your head whispers and tried to make me think that they were true.”

Zuko’s chest lurches at that, that anyone would try to make someone as wonderful as Sokka believe that he’s anything less than he is. “Sokka…”

“And it really did make me doubt myself, is the worst thing,” Sokka says in a rush, like he can’t stop for whatever Zuko would say now that he’s started. “It…everything was so realistic, you know? So close to how it actually was, with Aang and Suki and you and my dad and Katara.”

“…Me?” It was before Roku’s Island melted….Zuko was already that prominent in Sokka’s thoughts? To make an appearance in some kind of…what, redo of Sokka’s greatest failures and hurts? Zuko feels an unsettling combination of pleased and sick over it, even as Sokka shrugs.

“I mean, none of it was—it’s whatever.” He shifts a little, looking uncomfortable, and Zuko reaches for his hand, the tightness in his inner flame unwinding when Sokka immediately moves to lace their fingers together. “It just took a grain of truth and made things up, you know? Kind of like that play. Close enough that you wonder.”

Zuko doesn’t like the idea that he would be part of that for Sokka even in concept, that some…fake version of himself, or whatever, would be involved in something that Sokka so clearly hates to remember. Fuck, and Zuko thinks this might be contextualizing more than a few nightmares he’s overheard…

“But that’s not the point,” Sokka says, and Zuko jerks his attention back up. “The thing was all about the ‘real’ me, you know? Like there were all these parts and we had to break away all the ones that were no good.”

Ah. Zuko has the thread again.

“And…I guess it stuck with me, after,” Sokka frowns, eyes flicking up quickly to Zuko’s face. “And maybe I didn’t realize how much it got to me. Because I used to talk about there being a real you, too. All that pretense stuff. Like you could take Crown Prince Zuko and Water Tribe Sokka and set that aside and just be two people which…” Sokka shrugs, face drawn. “It was a nice thought, sometimes. But. The spirit was trying to convince me that I wasn’t good enough. It was trying to cut me down. And…I guess this is my really longwinded, self-centered way of saying that I get it.” Sokka catches Zuko’s eyes, gaze earnest and edged with worry. “I get how it hurts, even if it's well-intentioned. How it makes you feel like you aren’t good enough. Like you need to change in order to deserve something.”

Zuko nods, squeezing Sokka’s hand a little tighter, throat clogged. He hates that Sokka has felt this way too, but…Agni, it’s a relief to know that someone else has felt it.

“And Zuko—” Sokka waits for Zuko to meet his eyes again, expression intense now. “I’m so, so sorry for doing that to you, too. Especially when I know how much it hurts. I didn’t think about it and that’s not—I don’t want to not acknowledge it or start listing excuses, I don’t want to be like your uncle, I don’t want—” Sokka presses his lips together, taking a deep breath, before continuing, voice low and urgent, “Zuko, you don’t need to be anyone but you, okay? No matter what you’re trying to do. You don’t need to change unless you want to, not for me, not for anyone.” Zuko’s breath catches, his inner fire stilling as Sokka’s words ring through him like a bell. “All of you. The whole you. That’s what I want, as my friend and my partner and just—And if there are sides of yourself that you haven’t felt comfortable showing yet, I want to learn those too when you’re ready, because it’s all just *you*. It’s all just you in different situations, not—not multiple masks you need put take on and off, or whatever. Not parts to cut away.”

Oh. Oh, that hit, deep and hard, punching the air right out of his lungs until Zuko can feel heat prickling behind his eyes as he tries to breathe around this thing he didn’t even know he needed to hear.

“And just in case it needs saying?” Sokka squeezes his hand, Zuko blinking furiously before pulling his gaze back up to Sokka’s face. “Zuko, I love you for who you are. Not in spite of it. And if I’ve made you feel like you had to earn that from me, like you aren’t worth it just for being you, I will apologize in every way I can because you deserve so *much*,” Sokka says, eyes fierce and bright. “And I don’t know if you’ve ever gotten that, and I know I’ve messed up, that I’ve been part of that, and—Spirits, I don’t even know how to say how much I want better for you. How much I want to *do* better for you.”

“You are,” Zuko says hoarsely, clearing his throat, words still coming out raspy and thick. “You—I asked, and you listened, and—you’re there for me, and you give me space when I need it, and you *do* things, the things you say you’re going to do, and…” Zuko trails off, holding tighter to Sokka's fingers, trying to impart everything clamoring in his brain through touch before he's so unprepared with the words for this. Agni’s tits, what did Sokka and Uncle *talk* about?

“That’s good,” Sokka says, laughing a little, the words coming out more than a bit wet. “Because you’re so important to me, and being able to be part of your life is so important to me, and I wake up every day and just—I want to show you that, and how amazing I think you are, and Spirits, you care for me so well and I’m just…so impressed by you. From the very beginning and every day since and I think—I think I didn’t always show it well, but fuck, Zuko you’re just—I know I’m going to be impressed by you every day for the rest of my life and it just—it makes me so proud to be able to stand by your side.”

Zuko can feel his eyes too wide, his face too open, a stunned disbelief fighting with a warm, curling kind of delight in his chest. He silently works for words, finally getting out an unsteady, “Thank you.”

“You don’t need to thank me for it,” Sokka says, equally shaky, offering a wobbly smile. “Being allowed to love you is…a gift. A privilege. And I don’t ever want to forget it. I want to earn it every day. I want to be good for you, Zuko. I—” Sokka takes a deep breath, hand squeezing Zuko’s. “—Iroh said some things and hearing them, and hearing *myself*, I just—the idea that you’ve felt alone because of me, that I—that I was just another person treating you like everything was conditional, like your choices don’t *matter*—and they do, so much, and you deserve so much, you—you deserve *everything*. And Spirits, Zuko, I want to do everything I can to help give that to you—”

Sokka’s words cut off in something close to a squeak as Zuko lunges forward, catching the rest of them against his lips, overfull and overwhelmed, his inner fire spinning as he tries to pour every bit of emotion and feeling he has into the kiss because he doesn’t—he doesn’t have *words* for this. Sokka makes another surprised noise before all at once relaxing into it, hand trembling a little as he brings it up to cup Zuko’s jaw, and Zuko's feeling more than a little shaky himself, his inner fire straining, his entire body stretched at the edges. But not in a bad way, not like he needs to hold himself back. No, it's like there’s so much inside himself ready to spill out, so much of himself that he wants Sokka to know that Zuko can’t waste time trying to find the words to begin.

“You didn’t let me finish,” Sokka whispers against his mouth, laughing a little. “I—I was going to write it down but then—”

“You said—more than enough,” Zuko says, his inner fire feeling almost more bright than he knows what to do with as he cards his fingers through Sokka’s hair, distantly aware of the hair tie falling down the back of his hand. “Tell me,” he demands, brushing his palms up Sokka’s undercut to cradle his head. “Tell me.”

“I love you,” Sokka says, his smile brushing against Zuko’s cheek.

“Again.”

“I love you.”

“Again.”

“I lo—”

Zuko catches those words too—Sokka *definitely* squeaks this time—tasting them real and sweet and, for a moment at least, the only thing he needs to care about.
