“Katara, do you know where Zuko is?” Sokka asks as he shoulders open the door to their collective room, because he’s searched everywhere he knows to look and it’s been most of the day, and he *knows* Zuko is in the building somewhere, but Sokka *still* hasn’t managed to get his hands on him yet today. “I can’t—oh.”

Zuko startles on the bed where he’s propped up against the headboard, then winces as he jostles…whatever’s going on beneath the crisp white bandage Katara’s winding back around his chest. But he gives Sokka a shy little smile, and the pink tinge to his cheek looks…really good on him in the afternoon sunlight, especially against the expanse of the sheets, and so does the spread of pale skin, touched almost gold by the light, and—

“I’ll just give you guys some space then,” Katara huffs, giving Sokka an exasperated look as she pointedly sets Zuko’s shirt down next to him before slipping out toward the courtyard.

Sokka walks slowly over, hesitating at the edge of the bed because the bandage is so *large*, and it wraps right around Zuko’s torso, and Spirits, if this is what it’s *still* like—

Zuko clears his throat and scoots over on the bed, a clear invitation to sit.

Still, Sokka can’t tear his eyes away from all that white linen as he settles on the edge of the bed, fingers hovering over the bandage. “This looks like it hurts.”

“Not so much anymore,” Zuko says quietly, gently pressing Sokka’s hand down onto his chest to demonstrate.

It’s a *very* light touch, so Sokka’s not entirely convinced, but whatever expression is on his face makes Zuko let out a breath of laughter that he doesn’t seem to regret, so maybe it really isn’t all that bad.

“*Sometimes* it hurts a *bit*,” Zuko corrects, lips still tilted as he gives Sokka’s hand a little tug. “Can I have a hug anyway?”

“Always,” Sokka breathes, shifting further onto the bed and leaning in as Zuko twists around. They fumble a moment, trying to slot together and not sure entirely where it’s okay to touch, before finding their fit and sinking down onto the pillows, Sokka melting into it, into the heat of Zuko’s skin and the strength of his arms, burying his face in Zuko’s hair and breathing in his smoke and spice scent and hearing his breaths and feeling how *alive* he is.

“Can I..?” Zuko’s fingers slide down Sokka’s chest, hovering over his sternum, and suddenly Sokka wants nothing more.

“Yes,” Sokka says, nearly before Zuko voices the question. Then he’s sucking in a sharp breath, letting it out on a shaky exhale as he feels Zuko’s bending wrap around the thing in his chest.

Sokka can immediately tell that it’s the firebender way of doing this. From the lack of motion, sure, but mostly from the way it feels like Zuko is tight against him and wrapped around him and reaching inside him to drape him in warmth all at the same time, just a shade more intense than the distance of the waterbending forms, and Sokka shudders at the feeling of being held and cradled inside and out, love and safety and…Spirits, this might be the first time Sokka’s truly felt safe, truly felt like he can breathe, since that morning on the beach when they all realized just how little time they had left.

“Are you okay?” Zuko eventually asks sometime later, slowly pulling his bending back, wrapping Sokka in nothing but the strength of his own body now which is just as nice, Zuko’s hand tracing a wandering pattern over Sokka’s back. “I mean—I know.” A deep breath. “I got the reports. On the airships.”

Sokka feels himself freeze a little, bracing almost before he’s even registered the words, heart climbing into his throat in anticipation of…what?

“I know it’s not what you wanted. What you’d hoped. Are you—you can talk about it. If you need to. If…I know the North is still…”

Sokka lets all his breath out in a rush when he realizes that Zuko isn’t looking for an explanation or a reason or a rehash of everything that happened, the guilt and reproach that have been lurking at the back of Sokka’s mind shuddering under the comfort Zuko is offering. It’s different, somehow, coming from Zuko instead of Aang and Toph and Suki. Zuko, who doesn’t know exactly what Sokka did but who has never needed to in order to care. Zuko, who knows more than Sokka ever will about making hard choices.

Still, Sokka can’t entirely ignore the voice whispering that hard choices in the abstract are different than hard choices someone makes against your own people. And telling Katara not to second guess is one thing, but holding onto that in front of Zuko, when Sokka wanted so much to be able to show Zuko’s people even a fraction of the care Zuko holds for them, turns out to be so much harder. “You don’t…”

“What?” Zuko prompts, gently shrugging the shoulder Sokka’s resting against to nudge him to speak.

“Blame me?” Sokka’s voice cracks over the question, fear tightening his throat. “So many people died, even with the naval boats and the White Lotus getting there so fast. And if I’d just been able to figure out *something.*” That’s maybe the hardest part, feeling the echoes of the Day of the Black Sun, sitting with the knowledge that the misstep came far before the first ship took off. That maybe things were never in any of their control in the first place. “Aang figured it out, why couldn’t—I should have been able to. I could have asked more questions, different ones. I could have—”

“Hey, hey, hey,” Zuko says, giving Sokka a little shake to break into the flood of his words, Zuko’s hands soft but insistent as he eases Sokka back enough to search his face, and Sokka can barely meet Zuko’s eyes when he’s feeling so stripped open and raw and tight all over, when he’s feeling so much like he let Zuko down. “Sokka, no one blames you.”

Sokka snorts.

“*I* don’t blame you,” Zuko says, a correction. A significant one, though. Something Sokka can finally wrap his hands around and cling to against the clamor of ‘what if’s’ bouncing around his thoughts. “I knew the plan, and I would have said something if I thought there was something better. And we all agreed, Sokka. It wasn’t just you.”

“I just—” Sokka swallows around the lump in his throat. “I did the thing you have *nightmares* about. *I* did that, all over again, and how can you—I don’t want you to—” Spirits, he doesn’t know if he could handle it, if Zuko were scared of him, too.

Zuko looks startled, and more than a bit alarmed when he ducks his head down to catch Sokka’s eyes. “Sokka,” Zuko says slowly, shaking his head, skimming a slow touch along his jaw. “That’s not the nightmare.”

Sokka chokes on something like disbelief.

“It’s not, I promise it’s not. The ships and the water are there but it’s not really *about* that. It’s —” Zuko shakes his head again, face twisting before he shoves away whatever it is. “I’ll tell you later.” His fingers are gentle but insistent as he keeps Sokka’s face tilted up. “Look, we can’t all be the Avatar and have a spirit come along and give us a new choice when we need it. Sometimes all the options suck and we just have the choices we have, and we do the best we can.”

“Pick the one you can live with?” Sokka says, chest aching and just—*needing* the reassurance.

“And the ones that let you look the people you care about in the eye after,” Zuko finishes softly, gold eyes earnest and intent as he holds Sokka’s gaze. “The one where you kept your people safe and tried to minimize the bad stuff and do the most good with what you had.” “I *tried*,” Sokka says, feeling his eyes sting and refusing to look away from Zuko’s gaze to hide it. “I don’t—I’m not sure if I succeeded. But I tried, I really did. I really wanted it to be…”

“I know,” Zuko murmurs, letting out his own shaky breath and tucking Sokka close as his tears finally spill over. “Me, too. Me, too.”

Sokka buries his face against Zuko’s shoulder, finally letting all the fear and anger and a worry so deep and intense that Sokka doesn’t even have words for it crash through him, ricocheting off his ribs and tangling around his lungs as Sokka tries to let himself believe what Aang and Toph and Suki and Katara and now Zuko are all offering him, that this thing Sokka doesn’t know if he’ll ever be able to view as anything other than a tragedy might have truly been the best they could have done.

Zuko keeps up a steady, soothing hum in the back of his throat as Sokka gasps and almost-sobs and manages to breathe out a fraction of the tension inside him with every shuddering exhale, Zuko's arms solid and strong and his hand gentle as he cradles the back of Sokka’s head, running slow fingers over his undercut.

Somehow they end up forehead to forehead, Sokka brushing the wetness from his face and Zuko brushing barely-there kisses over his skin as Sokka shudders into a post-storm kind of calm, the quiet after the clamor of wind and rain sweeps through as he matches his breathing to Zuko’s deep inhales and exhales and concentrates on the feel of Zuko’s fingers tracing the hollow of his throat.

“You always look at me there,” Sokka whispers.

“Hm?”

“Here.” Sokka gently taps the back of Zuko’s hand. “You always look there.”

“Oh.” Sokka cocks his head at the edge of embarrassment in that one word. “I can see your heartbeat there,” Zuko finally says, one finger pressing lightly to demonstrate. “Your pulse.”

“…Spirits,” Sokka says, pulling back enough to look at Zuko and smiling at the way he’s going pink around the edges, feeling his own cheeks going hot. “You’re secretly a total sap, aren’t you?” He quiets Zuko’s grumbling protest with a kiss, sweet and gentle and teasing until he can feel the curve of Zuko’s smile pressed against his own.

Sokka is content to just be with Zuko, their hands gently skimming each other’s bodies with no intent beyond assurance and reassurance, counting the beats of Zuko’s always-fast heart as it gradually slows. At some point Sokka manages to undo Zuko’s partial topknot—collateral damage in his quest to find the good spot on Zuko’s scalp that makes him purr—and Zuko eventually returns the favor, and it’s in the quiet curtain of their hair that Sokka finally asks Zuko back.

“Are you okay? It seems like things aren't *bad.* But—I know you hoped that Azula...” Sokka trails off, fiddling with the end of one of Zuko’s fuzzed-out braids, not quite sure how painful it might be to bring up any specific one of Zuko’s hopes for his sister.

“It’s…not good now,” Zuko sighs, eyes sad, but he thankfully doesn’t tense up, doesn’t pull away. “She’s…” Zuko shakes his head. “But she’ll be better.”

That…wasn’t exactly as informative as Sokka was hoping, but if that’s what Zuko is worried about then he supposes he knows the important piece of it, at least in part.

“You should meet her, at some point,” Zuko suddenly suggests. “Soon.”

Sokka blinks. “What?”

“Azula.”

“…Zuko. I’ve met Azula before.” And Sokka can’t say he ever particularly enjoyed the experience.

“For real, though,” Zuko says, sounding like he’s really warming to the idea, which…Sokka *understands*, intellectually, even if he’s currently struggling to see a world where this isn’t a thousand times worse than having to go talk to Iroh after getting walked in on. “I think she’d like to meet you.”

Sokka is sure of no such thing, but before he can find the words to offer his agreement—if it’s important to Zuko then Sokka’s going to do it regardless of how much it makes the bottom of his stomach drop to the floor—Zuko goes abruptly stiff against him.

“Wha—?”

“Shh,” Zuko breathes, body tense and alert as he stares over Sokka’s shoulder.

Sokka goes immediately still, readying himself to turn and lunge, his adrenaline spiking. There are weapons in the room, but none within easy reach of the bed which suddenly seems like a huge tactical oversight. Zuko can move, but he must be limited by his injury even if he can still firebend, so Sokka shouldn’t rely on Zuko’s usual flippiness, he should—

“Very slowly,” Zuko whispers, eyes still fixed and intent beyond Sokka. “And very quietly. Turn around.”

Sokka nods and slowly shifts, holding his breath to minimize as much noise as he can control and not quite sure what he’s expecting. Zuko has the kind of focused stillness that Sokka associates with fights and dangerous conversations, but his hand is still curved loosely over Sokka’s hip, moving on him but not falling away as Sokka turns to see—

Sokka lets out a whoop loud enough even through the glass of the courtyard-facing windows that Katara and Aang startle away from each other, breaking off from their kiss, Katara glaring through her blush and Aang going crimson all the way to the crown of his head even as he grins.

“I told you to be quiet,” Zuko says, exasperated and amused behind him.

“You know I can’t do that,” Sokka fires back. “Spirits, *finally*,” he calls as Katara and Aang slip back inside. “It’s about time.”

“It’s the perfect time,” Aang smiles, reaching out to clasp Katara’s hand and it’s disgusting and saccharine and beneath the blush his little sister looks so happy she doesn’t know what to do with herself.

“There’s no need to make a big deal out of it,” Katara starts, lifting her chin and trying to muster some composure.

“Oh, there is *every* need,” Sokka grins. “Do you remember the big deal you made out of me and Zuko the first time? And the second time? And the third?” He transfers his grin to Aang, who gulps. “Do you remember the *meddling*?”

“We weren’t meddling,” Aang protests. “We were…”

“Involving yourselves?” Zuko suggests dryly.

“Well, the jokes on you,” Katara sniffs. “Because Aang and I aren’t going to be as dumb about it as you two were. So we aren’t going to *need* any meddling.”

Zuko bursts into laughter and Sokka can’t hold back a giggle-snort as Katara pulls herself up with outrage. “Oh, baby sister. My sweet, little, baby sister.” He thinks his expression might be worthy of Toph. “You have so much to *learn*.” He looks over his shoulder at Zuko. “Isn’t the confidence and naivete of youth refreshing?”

“Very,” Zuko agrees, mock-serious.

“Very,” Sokka echoes, annunciating extra clear for Katara. “I cannot *wait* until Toph starts telling you about everything she learned from the Earth Rumble.”

Aang frowns. “Toph already shows me what she learned there,” he says, glancing down at his own hands uncertainly.

“Oh, pure Avatar. Pure Air Nomad child. You have no *idea*.”

Katara sniffs. “Well at least *we* know enough not to start something in the middle of the day in a shared room with the windows open and the doors unlocked.” She gives them a prim look before marching for the door, Aang happily in tow. “You might want to put your shirt back on before anyone else comes looking for you, Zuko,” she calls over her shoulder, and Sokka doesn’t even care that she got in the last word because this is going to be so much *fun*.

Zuko is actually considering sending for some tea. Not because he *wants* to drink it, but because he thinks the caffeine might be necessary right about now. And it must be getting late, for him to be thinking things like that instead of just breathing up a curl of his sparking inner fire to put a bit more alertness back into his body.

Apparently, his inner flame is just as tired as his body is, though. Zuko has enough self-awareness to know he really should find his way to bed when he’s feeling like this, especially considering he now wakes *before* the sun.

And he will. He just needs to get through these reports first. Which would be easier to do if Zuko could rope one of the servants into acting as a secretary—apparently all the actual secretaries were banished—but Zuko can’t ask them to work into the night like this, now when it’s Zuko’s own decision to leave this for the hours when Azula does well so that he can be available during the daylight when she doesn’t.

It does a little, shameful bit, make Zuko wish he was the type of person who could just ignore the work. Even with no technical Fire Lord there’s still the Fire Lord’s input and sign-off needed, and Zuko doesn’t have it in him to just *not* do it. Especially when it’s just the little things that no one cares enough about to really take issue with who’s the one doing it, like reassessing the taxes on non-Fire Nation-owned businesses in the Colonies, and maybe reassessing the prison terms of nonviolent ideological offenders, too, as long as they’re in the mood for reassessment.

The big stuff, the things that will be a fight, like dismantling the power structure that allowed the airship fleet to take off in the first place when no one in their right mind could have possibly thought an all or nothing gamble from a position of strength was actually a sound strategy—those things Zuko can’t touch, not quite yet. But soon.

Zuko is so deep in his work—or tired, maybe—that it takes him a moment to snap to attention when someone brushes the edge of his heat sense out in the hall, only relaxing when he recognizes the familiar feel. Sokka yawns as he pokes his head into the room, glancing around half-curious as he makes his way over to Zuko with only a bit of a hitch in his stride that Zuko thinks might be more habit than actual pain.

“Is this what the Fire Nation does with its offices these days?” Sokka asks, leaning up against Zuko’s chair and running an absent hand through Zuko’s loose hair, which feels *amazing* after all day having it up in a top knot. He’s going to need to get used to that again.

Zuko glances around the dining room he’s repurposed, most of its surfaces covered in papers and ink and scrolls that are varying degrees of official. “Not exactly,” he says, rueful. Zuko didn’t want to take the step of using the Fire Lord’s study for his own yet, with all the statements that would make to anyone who cared to notice. Though Zuko didn’t want to use it at all, to be honest. Not before sending in a whole crew of contractors to change everything about the space, at least.

Sokka hums an acknowledgment, poking curiously at the papers in front of him. “What’s all this?”

“Just…things that need to be seen to,” Zuko says, kicking out a chair for Sokka to sit. The work of a whole Council full of people, and Zuko the only technical member of the Council left in Caldera as far as he can tell, or at least the only one willing to admit to it.

And Azula, but, well. She never had much patience for paperwork.

“Now?”

Zuko shrugs. He wouldn’t mind taking a break—the fact that Sokka and the rest of the crew are all here, finally, has been a constant drumbeat in the back of his mind and a welcome bit of solidness to stand on—but Zuko isn’t unaware that the Fire Nation has a history of crowning who is convenient rather than who is right. Zuko is aiming to make himself very convenient, right now. “A nation doesn’t run itself.”

Sokka doesn’t look entirely sold on that idea as he pages through the reports and proposals and memos spread across the table. “Someone has to read all this?”

“*I* have to read all this,” Zuko says, half-smiling when Sokka shoots him an appalled look.

“Don’t you have people?” Sokka mutters, somewhere between fascinated and aghast as he takes in the sheer volume of paperwork again. “Spirits, this is like Ba Sing Se. When do you have to have it done by?”

“Yesterday.”

Sokka stares, waiting for the joke. Zuko raises his eyebrow. Sokka will be waiting a very long time.

“So, what I’m hearing,” Sokka finally says, “Is that you’re not coming to bed any time soon.”

Zuko sighs, hearing the open longing in the sound. “Not yet,” he says, not trying to hide the regret in his voice. “I just have a few reports left to get through.”

Sokka’s eyes narrow on the pile of papers in that way he does when he’s working through a plan. “Do you have to actually read the reports? Or can you read notes?”

Zuko gives him a sideways look. “Who’s taking the notes?”

Sokka eyes him back. “…Give me that brush. And that paper. We’re going to bed in an hour, okay? *Okay*?” He adds when Zuko opens his mouth to protest that he really does need to at least get through the tariff reports before tomorrow. “Don’t make me go to bed alone, Zuko. It’s very big and very strange.”

“There are like, three other people sleeping in it.”

“Two,” Sokka corrects easily. “It’s still very cold. Who knows, I might catch a chill in the night.”

Zuko can feel his lips curling in a smile despite himself. “I can see you sweating.”

“Burr,” Sokka says, giving a single dramatic shiver. “Feel that breeze coming on?” He flops back in his chair, casting longing eyes toward the ceiling. “Whatever will I do, without my own personal space heater?”

“Whatever will you do, indeed,” Zuko says dryly, rolling his eyes. “Fine. An hour.”

“Deal,” Sokka grins, immediately straightening again, and Zuko doesn’t mind that he technically lost the negotiation when it has Sokka sounding so pleased with himself and settling in to work beside him.

The silence that falls around the room is a comfortable one, just the rustle of paper and barely-audible glide of an inked brush, the nighttime sounds of the palace and the familiar rhythm of Sokka’s breathing. Zuko lets his heat wrap gently, lightly around Sokka, and Sokka is angled in his chair so his boot just rests against Zuko’s ankle beneath the table, a spot of connection Zuko isn’t entirely sure Sokka is aware of maintaining.

It's nice and relaxing even if it’s happening in the midst of paperwork. And unfortunately, it’s just distracting enough—or Zuko’s just tired enough, maybe, his focus worn thin after the past days—to persistently grab at his attention. And the words Zuko has been clinging to like a talisman to jolt him back into focus when exhaustion claws at his edges, suddenly much more of a distraction when Sokka is sitting right next to him.

Zuko keeps having to reread the same passages over and over because he keeps getting caught up in the way Sokka sticks his tongue out as he concentrates, or in watching those hands Zuko’s so familiar with form characters up close, seeing the angle of finger and wrist and the flex of forearm that results in Sokka’s distinctive slanted hand, and—

“You know, I didn’t want to work alone either, not just go to bed alone,” Sokka suddenly says, Zuko jolting as he finds himself looking into a pair of teasing blue eyes. “I *do* value you for more than just your space heating.”

“Sorry,” Zuko mutters, feeling himself flushing as he ducks his head back toward his report, trying to find his spot on the page and suddenly hyperaware of the way one of his braids swings forward with the motion.

“It *is* late,” Sokka says, giving Zuko’s ankle a gentle tap. “It’s okay if you’re too tired for this. We said an hour, but maybe we just go to bed and in the morning we—”

“Katara said something to me,” Zuko blurts out before he even realizes he’s thinking about saying it, the object of his distraction shoving to the front of his thoughts and spilling right out into the open.

Sokka gives Zuko a sharp look, relaxing at whatever he must see on Zuko’s face even as his eyes stay intent, searching. “What?”

“I don’t know if she knows I heard her,” Zuko says slowly, hedging a bit. He’s almost positively she didn’t, actually. He’s barely even sure he heard it himself half the time between the buzzing in his ears as he surfaced briefly to consciousness and the pain in his entire chest and Azula’s ragged screaming. Except that Zuko would never imagine something like this. “It was when she was healing me. Right after the Agni Kai.”

Sokka’s face goes serious, his body shifting toward Zuko as he carefully sets his brush down, and it feels like a lot, like so much, to get the words out with Sokka giving him his whole focus. But Sokka is quiet and waiting and not pushing, and it’s not like Zuko doesn’t *want* to tell him, it’s just—it’s a lot, and—

Zuko takes a deep breath and goes for it. “She said that I was her future brother-in-law.”

Sokka chokes on air, and Zuko gives him a moment because she said a lot more than that. She said that she’d already lost one part of her family and let part of it leave and she wasn’t going to lose another, which is more than Zuko thinks is his to share. And she said it determined and angry and scared and Zuko’s spent the past however many days—and he knows it’s not a good thing, that he’s lost count—spending whatever scarce moments of free time he has being stunned by the fact that his family might have shrunk down to three, but somehow with him barely noticing it’s maybe grown to…he doesn’t even know how many.

“And I just—I don’t know if you said something to her?” Zuko picks back up, feeling like that lump of metal is suddenly burning a hole in his pocket even though Zuko isn’t sending a bit of heat toward it. The pendant that’s not even half done, that’s nowhere near where Zuko would want it to be even if there weren’t so many things that Zuko needs to do first, for himself *and* for his nation, before he can contemplate that.

“Not…about that,” Sokka says, voice faint.

“Because I—um—”

“Zuko,” Sokka starts, the stunned look on his face starting to give way to something more like quiet panic.

“You remember that I can’t get married until I’m twenty-five, right?” Zuko breaks in, trying to parse the shock and urgency and worry flitting over Sokka’s face.

“Yeah,” Sokka nods. “But Zuko, I didn’t—you don’t have to—”

“Good, because I—yeah. But.” Zuko forces himself to meet Sokka’s eyes. “I know that’s a long way off. Even next year feels like it’s forever, and eight years is…” Half a lifetime. Nearly, for Zuko, and just about, for Sokka.

“Zuko, it’s not—I didn’t say anything to her,” Sokka says, starting to look flustered. “I wasn’t trying to pressure you—”

“But I like the idea that we could be…family, before then,” Zuko says on top of Sokka, watching the way he clamps his mouth shut. “I like being your boyfriend, I don’t want that to stop,” Zuko continues, slower now that Sokka is staring at him with wide eyes. “But I like the idea of being your family, too. And if Katara can say that now, then…maybe being family doesn’t have to wait?”

Sokka opens his mouth and nothing comes out, so Zuko just…keeps going.

“Like, maybe she can still be my other sister before I’m twenty-five.” Before Sokka’s twenty-five? Zuko’s going to need to get some scribes to look into precedent there for international marriages. He’d rather avoid having to bring it to the Sages first. “And, you know, if her and Aang work out, Aang could be my brother, and Toph could—”

“Zuko,” Sokka finally interrupts, words shaky and every line of his body intent. “I would like nothing better than to be your family. Your friend, your boyfriend, your family, your— whatever you need. And I mean—something official is probably a bit—at least until—but instead, we could—”

“That’s good,” Zuko says, inner flame relaxing as he realizes that he and Sokka are on the same page with this, that they both hear the idea and think ‘yes, but not yet.’ “Because I, um. I love you, so that—I’d like that.”

Sokka stares a moment, Zuko’s heartbeat going too fast for him to count. Then Sokka lunges over so fast he nearly tips out of his seat, catching himself on the arms of Zuko’s chair and more crashing their mouths together than kissing, deep and overwhelming and gasping and like he wants to find a way to crawl inside Zuko and never come out and—yes. This. This is what Zuko feels, what thrums through his veins, through his inner flame, what words never seem able to encompass.

“You know you don’t have to say it, right?” Sokka finally whispers, pulling away just enough to grab breath, words and kisses blurring together. “I already know. The way you care for me and listen to me and help me be strong and push me to be better—”

“I know,” Zuko murmurs back, finally registering that at some point Zuko must have hauled Sokka over the chair arm and into his lap. He’s going to need to get bigger chairs for this room.

“You say so much with what you do,” Sokka says, near reverent, thumbs stroking gently over Zuko’s cheeks.

Zuko hums, pulling Sokka back in. “But words are nice sometimes, too.”

&#45;-

Sokka stirs when Zuko’s weight and warmth ease off his side, the strangeness of sleeping in a bed again—or maybe the residual stress and sense that they might be attacked at any moment and it would definitely happen in the night—still preventing him from dropping so deeply into sleep that he doesn’t wake with Zuko’s leaving.

“Zuko? It’s too early,” Sokka mumbles, brain automatically cataloging that everyone else is in the room where they should be. He can tell from the light that it’s before sunrise, even with how late it takes for morning to crest Caldera’s high walls. “Where ‘re you going?”

“Shh,” Zuko whispers, giving Sokka’s shoulder a quick squeeze. “Go back to sleep. There’s something I have to do.”

Sokka blinks, a little more alert now. “What is it? Do you need help?”

Zuko hesitates. “I don’t *need* help.”

“…Do you want help?”

Zuko opens and closes his mouth a few times, getting weirdly shy about it considering it's just the two of them awake and Sokka has no idea what they’re talking about. “You can come. If you want.”

“Sure,” Sokka yawns, gently untangling his arm from Aang’s octopus cat tight hold.

“But we have to hurry,” Zuko adds with a glance toward the east. “We don’t have much time.”

&#45;-

Sokka trails Zuko through the halls, awake enough to be pleased that Zuko seems quietly happy Sokka is with him and enough to hope that there will be breakfast wherever they end up. It’s way too fucking early to be up and about without food.

Then they stop outside the only door in the entire corridor with guards posted on either side of it and Sokka suddenly is feeling wide awake. The guards are nodding to Zuko as if he’s expected, and Zuko’s nodding back and going inside the doors they open and Sokka can’t just stand here so he follows, and—

“…It’s really good to know when we’re doing important things, buddy,” Sokka sighs, resisting the urge to check that his wolf tail is neat and actually put together. “And maybe get some food first.”

“Zuko has never been good at using his words,” Azula says, her voice acid as she slowly straightens in an armchair half in the shadows.

“Good morning, Azula,” Zuko says mildly, giving Sokka a little shrug. “May Agni shine bright upon your day.”

“May he burn everlasting,” Azula says, all sarcasm, never taking her eyes off Sokka, which really does more to bring Sokka to full wakefulness than food would have. “Why is he here?”

“I thought it would be good for you two to meet,” Zuko says, with what Sokka would like to say is far too much serenity.

“We’ve met,” Sokka reminds him, yanking his hand down when he realizes it's drifted toward his side. Not before Azula catches the motion, though, her smile a razor-sharp flash.

“Have you changed your mind, Brother?” She asks, expression sweet but tone savage. “Are you *trying* to tempt me?”

Zuko gives her a level look. “I think that’s all rather settled, don’t you?”

Azula makes a low noise—Sokka has understood…less than half of what’s going on—and shoves out of the chair fast enough that Sokka openly startles. She shoots him a single withering glance before she starts…prowling around the room, is the only way Sokka can think to describe it.

He wants to pivot, to keep distance and line of sight, but Zuko isn’t reacting and Sokka doesn’t quite know what to do with what he’s seeing. Here she is, dressed in soft clothes instead of armor, her face makeup-free, in some kind of slipper instead of her usual boots. It all makes her seem so much younger—she’s only fourteen, he reminds himself. Maybe fifteen, now—which makes the fact that she’s still just as terrifying like this all the more unsettling.

“We will see how settled it is when you decide to try to pass that off as the Flame Consort,” she bites, flicking an annoyed little bolt of lightning into the fireplace. Zuko doesn’t jump— Sokka does—so maybe that’s just…a thing she does.

And wait. Sokka plays her words back, belatedly realizing that he’s the ‘that’ in her statement, which… “Wait. As the what?”

Azula gives him a flat look for the interruption, then flicks Zuko one of disgust. “You didn’t even tell him you were being crowned?”

“Um.” Zuko shifts on his feet, shooting Sokka a look that’s some mix of guilty and apologetic and surprised, which means it’s *true*, which means it’s a very fucking pertinent detail. “I kind of just…forgot.”

“You *forgot*,” Sokka says, the words climbing more than a few octaves in his disbelief. What, the tariff reports were so fascinating last night that Zuko *forgot*?

“I had other things on my mind,” Zuko says, shrugging and shooting Sokka a warm little sideways glance that shuts him right up.

“Agni’s breath,” Azula mutters, so low Sokka isn’t sure that he is hearing her right. “Only you.” She gives Zuko an annoyed look, opening her mouth and then freezing.

It must be sunrise because Zuko visibly pauses, inhaling deep and slow and shivering a little on his exhale. It’s a familiar gesture, one that Sokka usually feels pressed against him rather than sees. And he can also see the way Azula flinches, ever so slightly.

“Breathe,” Zuko says, voice low and steady, pitched for calm, which seems to be exactly what Azula doesn’t want.

“I know how to *breathe*, I’m not an incompetent like *you* who needs to be *taught*,” she spits, prowling the room again, her steps closer to agitated pacing and Sokka can’t hold back any longer the need to slide and adjust as she moves to keep her in his sight. “Just like I don’t need to be *taught* not to bring a two-headed rat viper into my bed for a *cuddle*.”

“Hey,” Sokka protests, insulted, or…is that actually a compliment? Is it good to be a two-headed rat viper if Azula is the one saying it?

“You think you haven’t already made it hard enough for yourself?” Azula is saying, her eyes hot on Zuko. “Exile, tarnished honor, taking a throne in questionable circumstances, *dear* Uncle Iroh conveniently in the Earth Kingdom, an ally—no, *teacher*—to the Avatar who destroyed Father.” She glares, tawny eyes blazing before pulling a mask of composure over herself so suddenly that Sokka flinches from it. “That’s quite a bit of nation-building you did there, Brother. So if you don’t *actually* want the crown, just give it to me instead of setting yourself up to be deposed.”

“Or maybe I’m trying to set myself up to be happy,” Zuko says, with such quiet genuineness that Sokka’s finally able to tear his eyes off Azula to stare at Zuko instead as something warm and soft bursts through his chest.

The warmth lasts for about half a second as Azula lets out a disgusted snort in response, raking Sokka with a glance so sharp it makes him feel completely hollowed out and found to be thoroughly wanting. “Happy. See how long your *happiness* lasts when the lion vultures come out. When the *love*—” she spits the word like a curse. “—turns to resentment when you realize that the peasant—”

“Azula,” Zuko says, a low warning.

“—is nothing but a weight around your neck. Every single step is going to be harder if he’s there. Is that what you want?” She pivots toward Sokka, eyes narrowed. “To make things worse?”

“It was never going to be easy, Azula,” Zuko says, grabbing her attention back, determined in the face of her glare. “It was never going to be safe.”

The siblings stare at each other for a long moment, so much that Sokka doesn’t understand passing between them in that look before Azula finally, slowly, shakes her head. “Not this way,” she says, voice jarringly soft. “Not for you. Happiness has never been for us, Brother. That was the first lesson you failed to learn.” Her eyes flick to Sokka. “But pain will be your teacher, I suppose.”

“Things change,” Zuko says after a moment, matching her softness and surreally steady in the face of whatever picture Azula is painting for him. Sokka doesn’t understand it all and *he* feels knocked back on his heels. “Time will tell.”

&#45;-

“…So. Meeting Azula,” Sokka says after they’ve gone through a few corridors and he finally feels like his head has stopped spinning enough for him to form words. That’s the first time he’s really seen them interact as themselves, as a pair of siblings and not hunter and prey, and…even knowing all that he does, that she loves Zuko in her messed-up way because Zuko says it and believes it, that Zuko so clearly loves her back—it still doesn’t sit comfortably with him. Being willing to hurt those you care about to protect them skates far too close to just being willing to hurt those you care about for Sokka’s comfort. Spirits, could Zuko have turned out this way too, if he’d been the one left behind and Azula went off with Iroh?

“I think it went okay,” Zuko says, looking thoughtful. Sokka blinks.

“It…I suppose it could have been worse,” Sokka says slowly. There were no *overt* death threats this time, at least. “She seemed…tense?”

“She worries,” Zuko sighs, some of the evenness he showed Azula giving way to a quiet, persistent kind of concern.

“Right,” Sokka says after a moment. “She worries.” She…certainly seemed very worried. Sokka wonders at the difference between worrying for Zuko and worrying about her opportunity to sit on the throne.

“She’s been prepping to be Fire Lord more than I have, really. She knows how hard it’s going to be.”

Sokka frowns, gently bumping Zuko to grab his attention. “You’re prepared too, Zuko.” “I know,” he shrugs. “I’ll do my best.” Like Zuko doesn’t give everything his best, every bit he has inside of him.

“They’ll be lucky to have it. To have you.”

Zuko flashes him a quick smile, and Sokka finally recognizes the hallways they’re in as they turn the corner. They’re making their way toward the room with all the papers in it. And since it's technically, he thinks, a dining room, hopefully it will also include breakfast, which somehow is being pushed down his list of priorities again.

“So about that thing she said,” Sokka starts slowly, glancing around the empty hallway and wondering just how careful they need to be in the Fire Nation about being visibly together. Zuko hasn’t seemed particularly concerned in the time they’ve been here, but Zuko also wasn’t particularly concerned with sharing the laws in the first place.

Zuko cuts him a dry look. “Which one.”

Sokka will appreciate Zuko’s playfulness in a moment. “I don’t want to make things harder for you.”

Zuko slows to a stop, tugging Sokka around and *not* letting go of his hand, searching Sokka’s face and seeming to choose and discard a number of replies before firmly, quietly saying, with all his earnestness, “Being with*out* you would be harder, Sokka. Unless you want to go.”

“No,” Sokka says immediately. “Or at least—not like that.” Not permanently, not *leaving* leaving, just…leaving.

“I didn’t even ask if you were staying,” Zuko frowns.

“Of course I’m staying,” Sokka says. “I mean, I need to go home eventually. There’s a lot to do in the South. But a new Fire Lord needs to, you know…build diplomatic ties or something. Right?”

Zuko’s smile is slow and sweet. “Strengthening relations with the Southern Water Tribe is of the utmost importance to the Fire Nation,” he confirms, sealing the sentiment with a gentle, hot kiss.

“Oh,” Sokka says dumbly when he finally pulls away. “Good.” Then he manages to marshal half his brain enough to remember where he is and take a big step back—though he can’t bring himself to let go of Zuko’s hand just yet. “And I mean, obviously we’ll be together. But you know, with the laws and stuff, if we need to keep it a secret, or keep it quiet, I’m okay with that.”

Zuko hums. “It’s probably good to keep quiet to start, at least in public. But remember that whole perceived power thing?”

Sokka snorts. “I don’t know if I can forget.”

“I have a lot of it now,” Zuko says, with the hint of a satisfied smile at the corners of his mouth. “Or I will. After the coronation.”

Sokka blinks, trying to sort that into his understanding of everything Zuko ever wrote about Fire Lord infallibility or implied about the shifting web of power based on collective belief. “So…basically no one will call you on it? Once you have a strong enough power base?”

“They’d need to be ready with a new Fire Lord,” Zuko says, tugging Sokka back forward and nuzzling along the line of his jaw which is…a very persuasive argument. “And stability becomes very attractive very quick.”

“But if they do,” Sokka finds the wherewithal to get out as Zuko’s *teeth* briefly catch onto his earlobe. Apparently this part of the palace counts as fucking private. “Regime change is unstable, and you said Azula made more sense politically before and—” He cuts off on a gasp when Zuko’s tongue swirls in the hollow behind his ear.

“Laws can change,” Zuko murmurs. “Especially ones that have only been around a century.”

Sokka stills, pulling back slightly to search Zuko’s face. “That’s a lot of political capital,” he says, trying to get his breathing back under control even though Zuko is clearly feeling some kind of way about their sudden privacy. Spirits, there are so many things that Zuko’s going to need to do and fix, so many big things. And fuck, Sokka knows how hard social change is, just look at the North.

Zuko just smiles, though, and says, “Some things are worth it,” and Sokka can’t find it in himself to do anything but give him another kiss.

&#45;-

Zuko pops his head into their collective room, which is enough of an anomaly during the day that everyone looks over with interest.

“I just got word that the Chief of the Southern Water Tribe is expected to arrive on Caldera’s shores tomorrow.”

Sokka pauses. “As part of a delegation? For the coronation?” The words come out more than a little hopeful.

“It better not be for the war,” Katara says, scrubbing her hands over her face.

Sokka gives her a sideways look, where she’s looking quite cozy with Aang at the moment. “Maybe it’s so he can be formally introduced to Aang as your suitor.”

The squawking and panic and annoyed “*Sokka”* that follows is definitely worth it.

&#45;-

It’s Sokka’s last healing, but definitely not Katara’s last, and it’s nice to just sprawl back on the bed after and let their dual healing-induced tiredness lull them into quiet and not have to worry about what has to happen next, at least for now. Sokka is pretty sure that everyone is going to have to get their own room, eventually, if everyone is sticking around, even if Sokka is still taking far too much reassurance in being able to actually see everyone safe and close to voice the suggestion just yet.

Maybe they can all migrate to Zuko’s room—Sokka knows he has one from comments Zuko’s made, and he’s quietly dying of curiosity about it after seeing the Ember Island room. Though maybe he doesn’t want the whole team in Zuko’s rooms every night. The more Sokka silently repeats that to himself the more it sounds like a bit of a self-created trap.

Though on the topic of couples and lovers and alone time…

“So,” he says, giving Katara a gentle elbow. “How’s Aang?” He doesn’t even try not to smirk when she glares at him.

“So,” she says pointedly, elbowing him much less gently back. “How’s being the future *Flame Consort*.”

“Shut up, that’s not a thing,” Sokka protests, then again when she laughs. “It’s not a thing!”

“Yet,” Suki adds on as she shoulders her way cheerfully into the room and throws herself cheerfully down onto the bed.

“Well then why are we talking about something that’s a ‘yet,’ when Katara and Aang are a thing *now*?”

Katara sniffs primly, somehow managing to raise her nose in the air without moving, which Sokka is half-certain she picked up from Li Ty. “Because it’s rude to butt into a person’s private business.”

“But not *mine*?”

“Brothers don’t count as people,” Katara says sweetly, sticking out her tongue and diving out of tickling range.

Sokka is still sputtering when Aang walks in. “Why is Sokka choking,” he asks, sounding way too calm about it. “Is Sokka choking?”

Suki gives Sokka a poke. “Just on the weight of all his life choices.”

“Oh, good,” Aang says. “As long as it’s nothing serious.” He climbs up onto the bed too, giggling as his wiggling to make room catches Suki in a ticklish spot, and her flinch gets Sokka, and Katara preemptively plants a foot in his side to keep him away.

“What?” Toph asks from the doorway. “Are you guys polar puppy piling on the bed? You know I can’t feel you when you’re all up there, why didn’t anyone tell me. At least do it on the floor.”

“It was impromptu,” Aang shrugs from where he’s somehow managed to squeeze himself under Suki, who’s now draped diagonally over everyone.

“It’s still rude,” Toph grumbles, stomping over to the bed and shoving free a spot for herself with complete disregard for other people’s limbs or sensitive areas.

“How would we even tell you,” Sokka grunts, pulling up his thigh just in time to avoid catching a wayward elbow to the balls. Spirits, *definitely* separate rooms.

“I don’t know, send a servant, *Flame Consort*.”

“How did everyone find out about that,” Sokka complains. “*I* just found out about it. And for the last time, the Flame Consort thing is *not a thing*.”

“Yet,” everyone choruses, just as an “Um,” comes from the doorway and Sokka wants to just smother himself in a pillow right now.

“I can come back?” Zuko says, rubbing the back of his neck.

“No need,” Aang says, ignoring any potential awkwardness like a champ and wiggling to open up a few inches of room.

“The bed looks pretty full…” Zuko says, still hovering in the doorway.

Aang stretches out an arm and beckons. “Almost.”

“It’s really probably meant for two…”

“And yet we can fit so many more,” Aang says, beckoning harder.

“Get over here and cuddle with us, Awkward Lord,” Toph orders, and Zuko blushes but finally comes over, gingerly setting himself on a few free inches of space at the edge of the bed and then yelping when Aang gets a grip on his over robe and tugs him back into the tangle of limbs, setting off another round of squawking and grumbling and poking and shifting that ends with Zuko blinking in surprise at Sokka’s face from inches away, Toph draped over them both, Aang using Zuko’s back as a nice rest for his head, and Katara and Suki somehow woven in toward where Sokka can’t see.

“How you doing, buddy?” Sokka asks, amused by Zuko’s frozen tension, squirming one hand free to find one of Zuko’s.

“Uh.”

“The idea,” Katara says firmly, digging a finger into Zuko’s back somewhere that makes him yelp again and twitch, “Is to relax.”

“Like this,” Aang calls, helpfully plastering himself along Zuko’s back.

“…Okay…” Zuko says, and Sokka laughs as Zuko’s confusion eases into a tolerant bemusement, as his breathing slows when there’s no more tickling and the relaxation finally manages to get a hold on all of them. Sokka hums, happy to feel it, happy to have all his people here, safe and together and their mission miraculously accomplished. There’s still so much left for them all to plan, to do—damage to assess and recoveries to start and power to consolidate—but for once it fills him with eager excitement instead of grim resolve. For once it doesn’t *have* to be his problem—not right now, at least, and not unless he wants it to be.

Sokka smiles and watches as Zuko dozes off. A few others are napping or zoning out between the quiet drifts of conversation, but Zuko’s solidly out, and it’s been too long since Sokka’s been able to see the way he goes loose and soft with sleep.

“So, Snoozles,” Toph murmurs.

“Hm?”

“Loverboy.”

Sokka cranes his head up to give her a wary look, holding back a gulp when her face splits on a slow, wicked grin.

“How’s that carving coming along again?”

“Shut up,” Sokka mutters, flushing and ducking his head back down next to Zuko’s. But his thoughts are already turning to the type of stone that would look best at Zuko’s throat, and he knows his heartbeat, if she decides to listen, is beating to the rhythm of Zuko’s breaths, saying yes, yes, yes.

#### Chapter End Notes

People, we did it! The actual end! (I'm not crying, you're crying.)

I can't believe we're actually here! And I cannot thank you all enough for going on this journey with me and coming along for the long haul. Thank you for all your support, I'm truly blown away by how this little (massive) story of mine has been received.

And for those of you like me who have trouble letting go, stay tuned! I'll be participating in Zukka week in May, and I've got a few slice-of-life ideas in my head for this AU and ideas for scenes that didn't get covered in this fic. I'm also working on a multi-chaptered post-canon story (featuring, in part, everyone's favorite pendant), and there are lots of other ideas kicking around in my head :)
